en: No penalty and no precautionary or reformatory measure shall be imposed for an offence for which the law had not provided at the time of its commission. The acts that constitute the offence and the acts of principal or accessory participation committed by the defendant before the law provided for this offence shall not be held against him.

No offence shall be punished by a penalty or a precautionary or reformatory measure if it is abolished by a new law. And penal judgments that have been rendered shall no longer have any effect, provided that the prosecution and punishment of every offence committed in breach of a temporary law during the period of its application shall not cease after the expiry of the said period.

Every law that amends the conditions of incrimination by an amendment that benefits the defendant shall apply to the acts committed before its entry into force, unless a final judgment has been rendered in respect thereof.

Every law that amends the right of prosecution shall apply to offences prior to it if it is more favourable to the defendant. If the new law sets a time limit for exercising the right of prosecution, this time limit shall run only from the day of the entry into force of the law.

And if the law amends a time limit previously established, it shall run in accordance with the old law, provided that its duration shall not exceed the time limit of the new law calculated from the day of its entry into force.

If a law amends the period of limitation for an offence, this period shall run in accordance with the old law, provided that its duration shall not exceed the period set by the new law calculated from the day of its entry into force.

The Memorandum of Understanding for Cooperation in the Agricultural Field between the Government of the Lebanese Republic and the Government of the State of Qatar, signed in Beirut on 28/4/2010 and attached hereto, is hereby ratified.
The environmental laws and regulations in force shall apply to the projects arising from the Memorandum.

(As amended by Article 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

If the five years following the first deposit expire and the depositor has requested neither the publicity of the deposited object nor the extension of the secret deposit, the Director of the Office shall open the box, and if the depositor does not request its recovery during the following month, the designs and models which may be utilised shall be distributed among the industrial establishments in Lebanon which are able to benefit therefrom (schools of arts and crafts), and the name and address of the depositor shall remain inscribed upon the objects; and that same distribution shall take place for the designs and models the renewal of the deposit whereof has not been requested after the expiry of the period of twenty-five years, as well as the designs and models which become the property of the public after the lapse of fifty years thereon.

(As amended by Resolution 170 issued on 6 December 1937):

Whether publicity is requested or not requested upon deposit, the first deposit

provided for in Article 53 shall entail the payment of the following fees:

1- A fixed fee of twelve Lebanese pounds, and there may not be deposited

more than one hundred designs or models in a single application. This fixed fee shall be reduced to six Lebanese pounds if the same person submits at one time several applications for the deposit of designs and models which he has created or of which he is the owner, provided that he shall always pay for the first application the fee of twelve pounds; whereas a person who submits numerous applications for deposit at one time for different commercial establishments or persons shall not benefit from this reduction.

2- A fee of fifty Lebanese piastres for each deposited design or model. This fee shall be reduced to thirty piastres if the number of deposited designs and models exceeds one hundred, and to twenty piastres if the number exceeds two hundred, and this reduction shall apply successively.

For example, if a person deposits four hundred and fifty typographical models

for the account of a single establishment, he must pay the following fees:

1- A fixed fee of twelve Lebanese pounds--------12

Four fixed fees of six Lebanese pounds each-------24

2- One hundred fees of 50 Lebanese piastres each-----------------50

One hundred fees of 30 Lebanese piastres each-------------30

And two hundred and fifty fees of 20 Lebanese piastres each--------------50

-------------------------

Making a total of 166 Lebanese pounds 166

If publicity is not requested upon deposit, but is requested at another time during the five years following the deposit, the application for publicity must be accompanied by the following fees, failing which the application shall be - null and void

1- A fixed fee of 12 Lebanese pounds.

2- A fee of one Lebanese pound for each design or model intended to be published if the number of designs and models does not exceed fifty, and fifty Lebanese piastres for what exceeds fifty.

An application for secret deposit submitted upon the expiry of the first period of five years following the first deposit shall be subject to the following fees:

1- A fixed fee of 12 Lebanese pounds.

2- A fee of 3 Lebanese pounds for each design or model remaining secret.

An application for public deposit submitted upon the expiry of the first five years following the first deposit shall be subject to the fees mentioned in the preceding paragraph regarding keeping the deposit secret.

Finally, an application for the extension of the deposit for a new period of twenty-five years after the expiry of the first twenty-five years shall be subject to the payment of the following fees:

1- A fixed fee of 18 Lebanese pounds.

2- A fee of 6 Lebanese pounds for each deposited model or design.

The publicity given to a design or model prior to deposit, even if such publicity occurred by reason of the sale of the product, shall not entail the forfeiture of the protection granted pursuant to this Resolution.

There shall be considered as marks of manufacture or trade names written in a form that distinguishes them from others, denominations, emblems, seals, letters, imprints, reliefs, vignettes, and numerals, and in general every sign whatsoever intended, for the sake of the benefit of the consumer and the benefit of the factory owner or merchant, to distinguish objects from others and to show the identity and origin of the merchandise and the industrial, commercial and agricultural product, or the products of forests or mines.
The mark is optional unless there are legal provisions to the contrary.

A mark may be individual or collective, and associations of literary professions, regional companies, and agricultural or industrial companies licensed by the Government shall have the right to possess a collective mark whereby to safeguard the quality of manufacture of their merchandise or its origin or their products, and the members of these companies alone shall have the sole right to use this collective mark or "label", independently of the individual mark which each one of them may possess.
There must neither be represented in the mark national or foreign decorations, nor be mentioned therein any word, sign, or emblem that is revolutionary or contrary to public order or to good morals.

No claim may be brought for the individual ownership of a mark unless such mark has been previously deposited with the Protection Office in accordance with the provisions of Article 79 and the articles following it.
If any person claims priority of use of a mark that has not been deposited, written proof must always be produced in such circumstances.

(As amended by the First Article of Resolution 84 issued on 30 December 1926)

If a legally deposited mark has not given rise to an objection recognised as well-founded within the period of five years following the deposit, no objection may thereafter be raised against the first depositor regarding the right of ownership of this mark by reason of priority of its use, unless it is proved by means of written instruments that the depositor was not unaware, when effecting the deposit, that the mark belonged to the person who used it first.

(As amended by Article 2 of Resolution 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

Every person who proves, after the expiry of the period of five years mentioned in the preceding Article, that he has made free and continuous use of the mark prior to the deposit may retain this right of use, but for a period of fifteen years only commencing from the date of the deposit, and this right of use may be transferred together with the transfer of the commercial establishment.

The holder of this right, in order to safeguard his right, may bring a civil action in the matter of unlawful competition.

(As amended by Article 3 of Resolution 84 issued on 30 December 1926 and by Resolution 170 issued on 6 December 1937):

A deposited mark may be transferred by way of inheritance, sale, or assignment for value or gratuitously, with or without the commercial establishment.

For every transfer of a deposited mark to be invoked against third parties in accordance with the text of this Resolution, a declaration thereof must be submitted to the Office, and for each registration of transfer a fee of 5 Lebanese pounds shall be paid if the purchaser of the mark requests the registration within a period of one month commencing from the day on which the sale took place (the statutory periods prescribed for distance of places shall not be included in this Article). Every delay in requesting registration shall entail the payment of an additional fee of 3 Lebanese pounds for every two months.

(As amended by Articles 11 and 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

All marks drawn upon merchandise sold, offered for sale, or manufactured in the territories situated in Lebanon may be deposited. The owner of the mark shall not be compelled to reside in Lebanon in order to benefit from the provisions of this Resolution. A foreigner who wishes to deposit a mark must appoint to represent him a person residing in Lebanon who shall act as his representative in carrying out the deposit formalities.

(As amended by Article 4 of Resolution 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

The duration of the deposit shall be fifteen years. It may always be renewed for new successive periods of fifteen years, subject to the payment of the fees mentioned below.

(Amended by Article 5 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926

and supplemented by Article 10 of the Law of 31 January 1946): and pursuant to Decision 245 dated 23/2/83

The owner of the mark or his agent shall send a written application on stamped paper to the Director of the Office, and the following explanations must be stated in the applicant, failing which the application shall be null and void:

1- The name, title, surname and nationality of the depositor and his place of residence.

2- Where necessary, the same instructions regarding the agent.

3- The type of commerce or industry carried on by the depositor.

4- A very brief description of the mark.

5- The products or goods on which that mark is affixed and a statement of their numbers in the International Classification of Goods and Services to which distinctive marks pertain.

6- There shall be stated, where necessary, the previous deposits of the same mark in

foreign countries.

7- There shall be stated, where necessary, the date of the power of attorney pursuant to which is identified the agent of

the depositing person.

The application must be accompanied by the following documents and shall not be null and void:

a- Two copies of the model of the mark with mention of the colour and size where

necessary.

b - The original copy of the power of attorney pursuant to which the agent is identified

c- The copperplate (cliché) of the mark

There shall be appended to the application, if possible, a copy of the certificates of deposit that may have been given for this mark abroad or certificates of temporary admission at exhibitions or trade fairs.

(Supplemented by Article 6 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

No application for deposit whatsoever shall be accepted unless the depositing person pays the fee provided for in respect of the first fifteen years at least, and if the depositor wishes to secure for his mark the protection of thirty, forty-five or sixty years or for any other period, he must make a clear declaration to that effect in his application and pay the fees corresponding thereto.

(Amended by Article 6 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

The Director of the Protection Department shall receive the application and the attached documents and examine whether it is possible to accept the registration of the distinctive commercial or industrial mark pursuant to the provisions of Article 71; in the event that it is not possible to accept its registration, the Director shall refer the file to the Minister of Commerce and Industry, attaching to the registration a decisive report, and the Minister may declare his acceptance or rejection by a decision issued by him within a period of fifteen days, and this decision shall be subject to opposition, in the event of rejection, before the Council of State within a period of thirty days from the date of its notification to the applicant for registration.

(Supplemented by Article 10 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

And by Decision 245 dated 23/2/83, if it appears that the mark is lawful, its deposit shall take place and the Director of the Office shall enter in the register of deposit of marks the following explanations:

1- The serial number of the mark.

2- The year, month, day and hour of the deposit.

3- The duration of the deposit.

4- The name, surname, nationality and place of residence of the depositor.

5- There shall be stated, where necessary, the name, surname and place of residence of the agent.

6- The specification of the classes of the International Classification covered by the mark

or to which pertain the goods or services listed in

the application for deposit and on which the mark will be affixed, with a statement of their numbers

in detail.

7- There shall be stated, where necessary, the previous deposits made by the depositor

abroad.

Thereafter, one of the two copies of the mark submitted with the application shall be affixed in the register in a column specially set aside for that purpose, and opposite it shall be stated all the explanations that clarify the form of the mark, what it is designated for, and the manner of its use.

After the completion of these formalities, the Director of the Office and the

depositing person shall sign the register.
The certificate of deposit must be delivered within a period of fifteen full days starting from the date of its entry in the register provided for in Article 82

(Supplemented by Article 10 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

and amended pursuant to Decision 245 dated 23/2/83

There shall be stated in the certificate of deposit delivered to the depositor or his agent:

1- The number of the deposited mark.

2- The date and hour of the deposit.

3- The duration of the deposit.

4- The name, surname, nationality and place of residence of the depositor.

5- There shall be stated, where necessary, the name, surname and place of residence of the agent.

6- The classes of the International Classification to which pertain the goods and services on which the mark is affixed.

7- The deposits that may have previously taken place abroad.

The second copy of the mark submitted with the application shall be affixed on the certificate

in a column set aside for this purpose and shall be stamped with the seal of the Office.

Paragraph added pursuant to Decision 245 dated 23/2/83

8 - Each of these fees shall be levied for each class of the International Classification to which pertain the goods and services on which the mark is affixed; if the mark exceeds the goods or services of a single class of that Classification, the levying of the fee shall be multiplied in proportion to the number of classes of the Classification to which pertain the goods or services on which the mark is affixed..

(Amended by Article 7 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

The copperplate (cliché) shall be kept in the Protection Department for the publication of the distinctive commercial or industrial mark in the Official Gazette, provided that the dimensions of this copperplate do not exceed 10 centimetres in length by 10 centimetres in width.

(Amended by Decision 170 issued on 6 December 1937):

The fees payable upon the first deposit or upon an application for

renewal have been fixed as follows: (1)

Individual mark--------------------Lebanese Pound

First deposit for a period of 15 years--------------15

First deposit for a period of 30 years--------------30

First deposit for a period of 45 years--------------45

First deposit for a period of 60 years--------------60

As for renewed deposits, 15 Lebanese Pounds shall be paid thereon for each

period of 15 years

Collective marks--------------------Lebanese Pound

First deposit for a period of 15 years-------------40

First deposit for a period of 30 years-------------60

First deposit for a period of 45 years-------------80

First deposit for a period of 60 years------------100

As for renewed deposits, 40 Lebanese Pounds shall be paid thereon for each period of 15 years.

(Amended by Article 9 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

If it is desired to renew the deposit, the applicant for renewal shall submit an application to that effect to the Director of the Office, and the application shall be drawn up as though it were an application for deposit and shall be accompanied by the same documents, and the renewal fee must, on pain of nullity, be paid in advance as fixed in Article 86

(Supplemented by Article 10 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

The Director of the Office shall proceed, after verification where necessary, to make the statutory entries in the register of specified deposits and shall mention the renewal opposite the first deposit, and shall deliver to the applicant within a period of fifteen days from the date of this application of his the certificate of renewal, and shall return to him at the same time the certificate of the first deposit submitted by the applicant with his application in accordance with Article 87

: (Amended by Article 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Inventions eligible for certificates, factory and trade marks, and designs and models may be protected temporarily at trade fairs and exhibitions held in Lebanon and abroad if Lebanon has officially held those exhibitions and fairs or has officially participated therein, subject to the completion of certain formalities mentioned hereinafter: Furthermore, the holding by Lebanon of the fairs and exhibitions or its participation therein must be an official holding or participation in order for this Decision to be applicable.

(Amended by Article 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

At fairs or exhibitions officially held abroad and where Lebanon officially participates, a person who wishes to protect an object exhibited by him therein shall submit a written application to the official officer of the Government of Lebanon in which he states the nature of the object (an invention eligible for a certificate, a mark, a design, a model, etc.) and shall compulsorily attach to it a certificate from the commissioner of the fair or exhibition proving that that object is actually exhibited.

(As amended by Decision 170 issued on 6 December 1937):

Upon receipt of these documents, the commissioner of the Government of Lebanon shall register them in a register designated for this purpose and shall deliver to the exhibitor a certificate of their registration against payment of a flat fee of 5 Lebanese pounds, and the exhibitor shall be granted a period of three weeks from the date of the day on which the object that he wishes to protect is exhibited to submit the application for its protection.

(As amended by Article 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Upon the conclusion of the exhibition, the official commissioner shall send the special register that was in his possession to the Protection Office in Lebanon upon presentation of a certificate granted as mentioned in Article 91, and the person who has obtained temporary protection may convert it into final protection within one year starting from the date of the closing of the fair or exhibition, and the commencement of actual protection shall then be from the day of the opening of the exhibition or fair - the applicant for final protection shall submit his application in accordance with the provisions of this Decision in the articles relating to the protection of the various rights pertaining to commercial industrial property, etc...

(As amended by Article 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

In fairs and exhibitions that are officially held in Lebanon, announcement shall be made in a special decision taken prior to their opening of the formalities that exhibitors must complete in order to secure for their products the temporary protection which they may thereafter convert into final protection if they deem that useful.

(As amended by Article 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

The holders of this temporary protection shall be granted the same rights as are given in Lebanon under this Decision to inventions for which certificates are granted and to deposited marks, designs and models, etc.

Every person who wishes to use an industrial or commercial award must, when mentioning this award, specify its nature and specify precisely the certificate of the exhibition or the official authority that granted it and the date on which the award was given with complete accuracy.

A person who holds an award in a personal capacity shall alone have the right to benefit from it, and he may not transfer it to another with his business; on the contrary, an award granted to one of the products shall pass with the product, and upon assignment of the commercial establishment, the assignee may avail himself of it. The same method shall also be followed where the award is granted to a commercial or industrial establishment, for the assignee of the establishment may avail himself of it because it follows the establishment; whereas an award granted to a person in his capacity as an assistant may not be availed of by this assistant unless he mentions the name of the establishment in which he was employed.

- The following shall be deemed unlawful competition:

1- Every violation of this Decision that lacks one of the conditions enabling the application of the penalties provided for in Title Six below.

2- Every act which the courts have discretion to examine and which appears to them to constitute unlawful competition.

(As amended by Article 11 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

Acts of unlawful competition may only give rise to an action requesting the cessation of the competition or of the harmful act and an action claiming damages, except in circumstances where such acts constitute offences punishable under the penal laws or this Decision.

(As amended by Article 12 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926 and Article 13 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Every person who indicates in any form or manner whatsoever that a mark is deposited when it is not deposited.

And every person who knowingly imitates or uses a deposited mark without being authorised by the owner of the mark, even if he adds to the mark words such as type, kind, compound, emulated from, emulation of, etc., in a manner so as to deceive the buyer.

And every person who places on his products or on the articles of his trade a mark belonging to another person, and every person who knowingly sells or offers for sale a product bearing an imitated mark or one resembling the original mark with a resemblance intended to defraud.

And every person who delivers a product other than that requested of him under a specified mark.

Shall be punished by a fine of fifty to five hundred Lebanese pounds

and by imprisonment from three months to three years, or by either of these two

penalties alone.

(1) (As amended by Article 13 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Every person who makes a mark resembling another mark with intent to defraud, but without imitating it, having instead made it in a manner so as to deceive the buyer, or who uses a mark made to resemble another with intent to defraud. And every person who uses a mark bearing indications calculated to defraud the buyer as to the nature of the product requested, and every person who knowingly sells or offers for sale a product bearing a mark resembling another mark with intent to defraud or indications calculated to defraud the purchaser as to the nature of the product.

Shall be punished by a fine of fifty to two hundred and fifty Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from two months to two years, or by either of the two penalties alone.

The courts shall assess the importance of the imitation and the emulation with intent to defraud by examining the imitated or emulated object from the standpoint of the consumer and by taking into account the overall resemblance rather than taking into account the differences in details existing between the genuine mark and the mark that is the subject of the action.

(As amended by Article 13 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Every person who fails to affix to his products a mark declared compulsory to be affixed.

And every person who sells or offers for sale a product that does not bear the mark compulsory for this type of product.

And every person who depicts on any mark symbols that violate the provisions of Article 71 of this Decision.

And every person who violates the provisions of Article 69 of this Decision.

Shall be punished by a fine of fifty to five hundred Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from two months to two years, or by either of these two penalties alone.

Upon repetition of the offence with respect to the violations punishable under the preceding Articles 105, 106 and 108, the penalty may not be less than the maximum limit specified in these Articles nor more than double the maximum limit, and in addition thereto, the offender must be sentenced to imprisonment for a period of two months to five years; as for the repetition of the offence, its determination shall be in accordance with Article 103 of this Decision.
The usurpation of a trade name shall be punished by the same penalties mentioned in Articles 105 and 109 of this Decision.

(As amended by Article 13 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Every injury knowingly caused to rights guaranteed under this Decision for industrial designs and models shall be punished by a fine of 25 to 250 Lebanese pounds, and if the offender is an assistant or has assisted in the past in any capacity whatsoever the person whose rights have been infringed, he shall mandatorily be punished, in addition thereto, by imprisonment from two months to six months.

(As amended by Article 13 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

If the act that necessitated the bringing of the action relates to a pharmaceutical product, the penalty imposed may not be less than fifty Lebanese pounds.

(As amended by Article 13 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

If the offence is repeated, and repetition is as mentioned in Article 103 of this Decision, the penalty mandatorily imposed may not be less than two hundred and fifty Lebanese pounds nor more than five hundred pounds, and the offender may, in addition thereto, be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

(As amended by Article 13 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

No act prior to the deposit shall give the aggrieved party a right to bring any action arising out of this Decision. And for every act that occurred after the deposit but was prior to publication, the action arising from Article 111, even if civil, may not be brought by the aggrieved party except on condition that he establishes proof of the bad faith of the accused.

If seizure, the taking of samples, inventory, etc... is carried out through the Protection Office, the Office shall collect the two fees mentioned below:

Inspection, taking of samples, and seizure for the protection of commercial, industrial, artistic, literary, and musical property,

- The fee due for a detailed description of an object, its identification, or the taking of samples thereof: /4,600,000/ L.L.

- The fee due for seizure there shall be added each of these two fees a special allowance for drawing up the record in the amount of: /2,300,000/ L.L.

If the Office acts upon a complaint from the aggrieved party, the aggrieved party shall advance these fees, which shall be refunded to him if judgment is rendered against the party against whom the action is brought; whereas if the Office acts directly and without a complaint, the party against whom the action is brought shall pay these fees if judgment is rendered against him.

Even in the event of the acquittal of the party against whom the action is brought in the criminal court, the court may issue a judgment for the seizure of the articles and goods in which suspicion lies and their sale either for the benefit of the aggrieved party or for the benefit of the Office.

(As enacted by Article 3 of Decision 164 issued on 8 December 1938):

Every judicial decision taken pursuant to the provisions of this Decision must be notified by the court that issued the decision to the Protection Office within a period of eight days at most.
(Repealed by Article 4 of Decision 164 issued on 8 December 1938)

As from the putting into execution of this Decision, all previous laws, decrees, enactments, and decisions relating to these matters are repealed, in particular the laws mentioned below. They are the Ottoman Law issued on 9 March 1880 concerning patentable inventions, the Ottoman Law issued on 11 May 1888, the Ottoman Kararname issued on 8 October 1888 concerning factory and trade marks, Decision No. 769 issued on 19 March 1921 concerning the temporary protection of the rights of persons exhibiting at the Beirut Fair, Decision No. 865 issued on 27 May 1921 concerning the protection of factory and trade marks, and Decision No. 1136 issued on 5 December 1921 modifying the preceding Decision, etc. This enumeration does not preclude the existence of decisions other than these that are repealed by this Decision.

(As amended by Article 15 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926 and by Article 12 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Factory or trade marks deposited in Lebanon under the regime of the provisions of Decision 865 and Decision 1136, which have been repealed, shall benefit without carrying out further formalities from the provisions of this Decision while retaining their date and rank of registration. Marks that were not legally deposited in accordance with the text of these Decisions shall be deemed validly deposited as from the putting into application of Decision 2385.

This Decision repeals all previous statutory provisions to this effect, in particular the Ottoman Law issued on 11 September 1872 on privileged works and the Printing Presses Law issued on 10 January 1888 insofar as it was contrary to this Decision.

(As amended by Articles 11, 14, and 15 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

This Decision shall apply in Lebanon, subject to the reservation of the provisions of international conventions existing and that will exist, as from the day of its publication in the Official Gazette.

(As enacted by Article 16 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926 and amended with respect to the fee by Decision 170 issued on 7 December 1937):

Every issuance of a duplicate copy or a certificate by the Office entails the collection of a fee in the amount of two Lebanese pounds.

Pursuant to the first Article of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, this Chapter was repealed and replaced by the following text:

The census and delimitation of real properties and immovable properties in the districts and governorates shall be carried out by the justices of the peace of the district. Where necessary, a surveyor shall be placed at the disposal of the justice of the peace.

The text of the second Article was amended pursuant to Law No. 392 dated 13/2/2002 to read as follows:

Single Real Estate Judges shall carry out the operations of census and delimitation of real properties and immovable properties in the districts and governorates.

The surveyor entrusted with carrying out the operations of provisional census and delimitation of real properties and estates, assisted by the auxiliary personnel necessary to him, shall perform the function of clerk to the Single Real Estate Judge throughout the duration of such operations.

This surveyor shall be appointed by the Director of Real Estate Affairs upon the proposal of the Head of the Survey Department, and after the conclusion of the operations of provisional census and delimitation, the surveyor shall be replaced by a registrar appointed by the Director of Real Estate Affairs, and the operations of census and delimitation may be assigned to specialised offices operating under the supervision of the Single Real Estate Judges, provided that the specifications of such offices and the conditions for assigning the operations to them are determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The Ministry of Finance - Directorate of Real Estate Affairs - may also contract with sworn surveyors and draughtsmen who fulfil the conditions provided for in Decree No. 2148 dated 14/1/2000 (Special Conditions of Appointment for Technical Positions in the Directorate of Real Estate Affairs) to assist the Single Real Estate Judges in the operations of delimitation and census and the supervision of such operations, provided that the contracting period does not exceed five years from the effective date of this Law, and the contractor shall enjoy all the powers and obligations without the rights enjoyed by employees of the permanent cadre.

The Ministry of Finance - Directorate General of Real Estate Affairs - may also contract with sworn surveyors and draughtsmen who fulfil the conditions provided for in Decree No. 2148 dated 14/4/2000 (Special Conditions of Appointment for Technical Positions in the Directorate General of Real Estate Affairs) to assist the Single Real Estate Judges in the operations of delimitation and census and the supervision of such operations, provided that the contracting period does not exceed five years, and the contractor shall enjoy all the powers and obligations without the rights enjoyed by employees of the permanent cadre."

The contracting with the surveyors and draughtsmen assigned to the operations of delimitation and census of real estates shall be extended.

In the event that the operations of delimitation and census are not completed within the period specified above, the Minister of Finance may extend the contracting with the surveyors and draughtsmen whose contract terms expired on 12/1/2007 under the same previous conditions, for an additional period according to the requirements of the work, and he may also contract for this additional period with the necessary number of surveyors and draughtsmen, until such time as there is no longer a need for them as a work team entrusted with the operations of delimitation and census.

Pursuant to the first and second Articles of Decision No. 141/L.R. dated 5/7/1939, Article 3 was repealed and replaced by the following text: Single Real Estate Judges shall be appointed, in Lebanese territory, by a decree of the Head of State. They shall take the oath and be installed in their functions in accordance with the formalities prescribed in the judicial regulations in force, and they shall be deemed assimilated to the judges belonging to the judicial cadre of the State, having the same duties and enjoying the same prerogatives as the latter, and in the exercise of their judicial functions they shall be subject to the supervision of the General Supervision of Justice.

As regards the coordination of the technical, administrative, and judicial operations relating to census and delimitation, they shall be subject to the supervision of the administrative authority to which the Real Estate Departments belong, and the Real Estate Judges shall be selected from among the candidates holding the qualifications required to assume a judicial post of the rank of peace judge. They may be promoted, while remaining in their functions, to a hierarchical rank higher than their rank, up to the rank of counsellor at the Court of Appeal, and they shall be subject to the regulations governing the selection, promotion, and discipline of judges, in the same manner as all other judges belonging to the judicial cadre of the State, pursuant to the first Article of Law No. 98 dated 18/6/1999, paragraph 5 of Article 3 was amended to read as follows:

Additional Real Estate Judges may be appointed and entrusted either with acting in the place of the original Single Real Estate Judges when the latter are unable to exercise their functions, or with undertaking, upon the request of the Real Estate Registrar, the interpretation of decisions issued by the Single Real Estate Judges during the census and delimitation of real properties which have acquired the force of res judicata, or with carrying out land consolidation operations, or with determining the amount of the shares of each co-owner in the real properties registered in the names of multiple co-owners without specification of the amount of the undivided shares pursuant to the minutes of delimitation and census, in the event that the co-owners fail to amicably agree on determining the amount of the share of each of them.

Additional Judges shall be deemed assimilated to the Real Estate Judges in all respects, and the Ministry of Justice shall place the Single Real Estate Judges at the disposal of the Ministry having authority over the Real Estate Departments. Real Estate Judges may be promoted to a hierarchical rank higher than the rank of justice of the peace in the annexes notwithstanding the provisions of the decisions in force relating to the appointment or determination of the number of judges of each category.

The judicial jurisdiction of the justice of the peace in matters of delimitation and census shall extend to the boundaries of the district or governorate, whereas the judicial jurisdiction of the Single Real Estate Judge shall extend to the places designated by the decision establishing this judicial authority or by subsequent decisions.

The justice of the peace acting in the place of the Permanent Committee, and likewise the Single Real Estate Judges, shall undertake the operations of census and delimitation under the supervision of the Director of the Real Estate Departments and shall be under his authority throughout the duration of such operations; the authority vested with the right of supervision may adjudicate upon any dispute arising out of the operations of delimitation and census in all cases where the law does not provide that recourse must be had to the judiciary, and it may report any infringement or negligence committed by the justices of the peace or by the Single Real Estate Judges, and the Ministry to which those officials belong may impose upon them, where necessary, the penalties provided for by law, after consulting the Director of the Real Estate Departments.

The operations of census and delimitation shall proceed village by village in each district or governorate, and zone by zone in the cities. The surveyors entrusted with such operations shall be placed under the supervision of the justice of the peace or the Single Real Estate Judge, provided that they shall report exclusively to the Survey Department with respect to the technical aspect and the supervision of topographical operations, and prior to commencing the exercise of their functions, the surveyors shall take an oath before the justice of the peace or the Single Real Estate Judge to perform them with diligence and fidelity, and the judge shall draw up a record of such oath.

(As amended by Article 11 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Special provisions shall be issued hereafter regulating the conditions of international protection for patents of invention applicable in Lebanon.

Every creator of a design or model, or his successor in title, shall alone have the exclusive right to exploit such design or model, to sell it, offer it for sale, and authorise its sale, provided that such design or model has previously been deposited.

Designs and models possessing the dual characteristics of novelty and originality, that is to say, comprising external features which give them a distinctive appearance differentiating them from designs and models hitherto known, may be deposited.

Accordingly, pursuant to the definition set forth in Article 49, deposits may be made of fabrics bearing printed or woven designs, illustrated papers for decorating walls, new models of caftans, coats (Manteaux), hats and headwear for men and women, dress accessories such as belts, garters, footwear, corsets, wrappers for flasks, bottles, and vessels for wines, alcoholic beverages, drinks, syrups, and perfumes, etc..., cardboard boxes and wrappers used for pharmaceutical products, and the external form of goods or of any product whatsoever, etc.. The foregoing enumeration shall not preclude the possibility of depositing other similar articles not mentioned therein.

If the new model may be considered an invention eligible for a patent, it must be protected in accordance with the provisions of Chapters I and II of the Law on Patents of Invention. However, if the elements which render such model new are separable from the invention itself, the inventor may, upon his request, benefit from the dual protection arising from the patent and from the deposit, subject to the payment of the fees relating to each of these two procedures.

Deposit alone shall not confer ownership of a design or model, but creates a presumption of ownership (1) in favour of the depositor; actual ownership, however, shall only be acquired through the use of the designs or models.

(As supplemented by Article 10 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

The creator of the design or model, or his officially recognised agent in that capacity, shall submit the application for deposit to the Director of the Protection Office, and this application must contain the following particulars, under pain of nullity:

1- The forename, surname, nationality, and domicile of the creator of the article sought to be deposited.

2- Where applicable, the same particulars concerning the authorised agent.

3- The number and nature of the articles sought to be deposited, provided that such number shall not exceed one hundred in a single deposit, and each of these articles must be designated by a number from 1 to 100.

4- The term of protection requested.

5- Where applicable, the articles of which publication is requested shall be indicated, and these articles must be designated by their serial numbers.

The application must be accompanied by the following, under pain of nullity:

1- The amount of the fees prescribed in Articles 65 and 66.

2 - Where applicable, the power of attorney by which the agent is officially recognised.

3- Two specimens or copies of each article sought to be deposited, which must bear the number of that article.

4- Two copies of the descriptions relating to each of the deposited designs and models, and each of the descriptions must bear a number as explained above and be signed by the person making the deposit. These descriptions shall be written on paper the dimensions of which shall be prescribed elsewhere, and shall state all necessary particulars concerning the article to which they relate, particularly where they relate to a model reproduced on a reduced or enlarged scale, in which case the scale of dimensions used for that purpose must be stated.

5- An impression of the seal used to seal the boxes in which the depositor has placed the articles sought to be deposited together with their descriptions.

The legal dimensions of the boxes, models, and descriptions referred to in Article 54 shall be determined by special instructions to be issued hereafter, and the provisions of those instructions must be observed under pain of nullity of the application.

The Head of the Protection Office shall enter the declaration of deposit in a register kept for that purpose, stating therein the date, hour, and serial number of the deposit, and the same particulars shall be inscribed upon the sealed box submitted by the depositor.

As stated in the fifth paragraph of Article 53, the depositor shall have the right to request the publication of all or part of the articles he has deposited at the time of deposit without paying an additional fee, and he shall retain this right during the first five years following the deposit; in the latter case, however, the request for publication shall entail the payment of the fee prescribed in Article 66. So long as the depositor does not request the publication of the articles he has deposited, the secrecy of the deposit shall be strictly preserved.

A depositor who wishes to publish the whole or part of the articles he has deposited shall submit an application to that effect to the Director of the Office, accompanied by a specimen of each of the articles he wishes to have published. Thereupon, the Director of the Office shall open the sealed box, remove therefrom the article or articles requested, and verify their conformity with the specimen submitted; one of the two specimens extracted from the box shall then be stamped, dated, and delivered to the depositor, while the second specimen shall bear the same endorsements and remain at the Office at the disposal of any person wishing to inspect it, and the remaining articles which are not to be published shall be returned to the box, which shall be resealed.

(As amended by Decision 170 of 6 January 1937).

As stated in Article 58, the public may inspect the copy of the published design or model remaining at the Office free of any charge upon an application submitted to the Director of the Office; furthermore, the depositor, his successors in title, and any person who proves that he is party to legal proceedings relating to the published design or model may obtain a photographic copy of that design or model against payment of the costs thereof as well as a fee of two Lebanese pounds.

If the publication of the deposited articles is not requested during the five years following the deposit, the sealed box shall be placed at the disposal of the depositor, who may then maintain the deposit in force for the whole or part of the articles contained in the box, whether he wishes the deposit to be secret or public, in accordance with the same procedure as set forth in Article 58, the sole difference between the two deposits being that the articles for which deposit is no longer requested shall be returned to the depositor.

If, upon the expiration of the first period of five years, the depositor requests that the deposit be kept secret, the Director of the Office shall open the sealed box, extract from the box the duplicate copies requested together with their descriptions, and place them all in a sealed envelope after certifying each of the two copies, and the box shall then be resealed to be returned, where applicable, to its depositor.

A public or secret deposit requested to be made before or upon the expiration of the first five years shall remain in force for a period of twenty-five years commencing from the date of the initial deposit provided for in Article 53, and the depositor or his successors in title shall have the right, upon or before the expiration of those twenty-five years, to request the renewal of the deposit for a further period of twenty-five years.
At the commencement of the second period of twenty-five years, the deposit shall be made public in accordance with the rules prescribed in Article 58 et seq.

(As amended by Article 13 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

There shall be punished by a fine of five pounds to two hundred and fifty Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment of three months to two years, or by one of the two penalties only, without the fine imposed being less than fifty pounds if a sentence of imprisonment is not passed, persons who fraudulently attributed to themselves awards or claimed fictitious awards and used them publicly, such as by placing them on trade badges, on merchandise wrappers, on commercial papers and in the writing of signboards, etc.

And persons who attempted to convince the public that they are holders of an award which they do not in fact hold.

And persons who contravened in any manner whatsoever the provisions of Articles 95 and 96 of this Decision.

Even in the case of acquittal, judgment must always be passed ordering the seizure of the objects which harmed or were used to infringe the rights guaranteed under this Decision, and the court shall likewise in all cases order the destruction of the marks, symbols, badges and inscriptions contrary to this Decision.

In the case of failure to affix an obligatory mark, the court shall order its affixing on the product mandatorily subject to having it affixed, or shall order the confiscation of the product and its sale for the benefit of the aggrieved party or by way of a fine.

Every judgment passed in any misdemeanour whatsoever provided for in this Decision or in a matter relating to unlawful competition shall always entail as ancillary penalties:

1- Adjudging the convicted person disqualified from being elected a member of chambers of commerce, associations, study committees, syndicates, cooperative societies and, in general, of any elective assembly.

2- Posting the judgment in the places designated by the court and publishing it in two newspapers, one issued in the Arabic language and the other in the French language, designated by the court which passed the principal judgment.
Even in the case of acquittal of the misdemeanour, the court may award damages to the aggrieved party.

(As enacted by Article 16 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

The Public Prosecution shall institute the public right action either of its own motion or upon the complaint of the civil party or the complaint of the Head of the Protection Department.

Whether the aggrieved party has lodged a complaint or has not lodged one, the Public Prosecution shall be entitled to proceed with the identification of the suspected objects or goods, instruments and utensils, their detailed inventory and their taking, and the Director of the Protection Office shall have the same right.

(As completed by Article 14 of Decision 84 issued on 30 December 1926):

The persons designated below have the requisite capacity to proceed with the identification of the suspected objects, their detailed inventory and the taking of samples thereof as mentioned in Article 121, namely police commissioners, special police commissioners for railways and ports, customs and octroi officers, employees of the Protection Office sworn for this purpose, and officers appointed by the Director of the Office for localities other than Beirut and who are sworn for this purpose.

These officers shall act pursuant to an order or authorisation issued by the Public Prosecution or the Director of the Protection Office, and they must inform the Protection Office of all contraventions of the provisions of this Decision that they witness.

Sworn officers of the Office shall have the capacity of judicial police officers in all that relates to the enforcement of this Decision.

The identification of suspected objects, their detailed inventory and the taking of samples thereof may take place in the places mentioned hereinafter, namely warehouses, shops, factories, vehicles (trucks) used in trade, depots, slaughterhouses and their appurtenances, covered markets Halles, public markets, and departure and arrival stations and ports.

(As completed by Article 10 of the Law of 31 January 1946):

Every taking of a portion of samples and every identification or inventory thereof must be recorded in a report in which there shall mandatorily be mentioned:

1- The name, surname, capacity and place of residence of the officer drawing up the report.

2- The authority which gave the order and the date of the order which it gave to the officer.

3- The date, hour and place of the occurrence of the operation.

4- The name, family name, house or place of residence and nationality of the person at whose premises the operation takes place, and his profession.

5- If the operation took place in transit, there shall be mentioned in the report the name, place of residence and nationality of the persons mentioned in the waybills Lettres de voiture or declarations in their capacity as consignors or consignees.

6- A brief explanation of the circumstances in which the operation took place and an enumeration of the persons who attended it, etc.

7- The signature of the person in whose possession the articles or goods were found, and if he refuses to sign, his refusal shall be mentioned.

8- The signature of the officer who drew up the report.

The owner of the goods shall in addition be entitled to mention in the report all instructions and reservations which he deems useful.

The officer drawing up the report is not obliged to inform the holder of the goods of the authorisation given to him before carrying out his mission, and he may in particular, when he is requested to verify the delivery of a product in place of another product requested under a specific mark or a deposited design or model, not produce to the holder of the goods the order in his possession until after he has received the product, and the officer may be accompanied by an expert appointed by the authority which gave the authorisation and the expert shall be mentioned in the authorisation.

The officer shall deliver to the holder of the goods, at the time he deems appropriate, a copy of the order pursuant to which he is acting, and upon the conclusion of the operation the holder of the goods shall in addition receive a copy of the report and of the inventory list of the articles or goods in respect of which the operation took place if a separate list thereof was drawn up.

The civil or criminal action must be brought before the competent court within fifteen full days starting from the date of the report, failing which the operation which took place shall be void, and there shall be added to this period one day for every distance of fifty thousand metres between the place of the occurrence of the operation and the place of residence of the party against whom the action is brought or his representative.

The action instituted within the periods specified in Article 127 shall be brought before the competent court having jurisdiction over the place of residence of the prosecuted party, and if there is no court there, it shall be brought before the court having jurisdiction over the place in which the operation was carried out. The court shall be entitled, upon the request of the complaining party and before ruling on the action, to issue an order for the attachment of the whole or part of the articles mentioned in the report and the inventory list, and it may in this case order the complainant to pay prior to the attachment into the fund of the Protection Office a security which the court shall fix in proportion to the value of the articles intended to be attached. There shall be designated in the order the officer charged with carrying out the attachment, and there shall preferably be chosen the officer who wrote the report and carried out the initial operation of inventorying the articles or taking a part thereof as provided in Article 121 if that took place. There may also be mentioned in the order the place in which the proceeds of the attachment are to be placed and the judicial custodian charged with preserving them.

The person whose articles are attached must receive copies of the documents mentioned below, failing which the attachment shall be void:

1- The order of attachment.

2- The instrument proving the deposit of the security at the Office, if the deposit of such security was required.

3- The inventory list of the attached articles.

4- The report of the attachment.

The officer who carried out the attachment operations must forthwith draw up a report thereof in two copies, one of which shall be delivered to the person whose articles are attached. This report shall be drawn up in the manner of the same model explained in detail in Article 124 and shall be accompanied by the inventory list of the attached articles. The person whose articles are attached shall sign these two papers, and if he refuses to sign or if he is unable to sign, his refusal or his inability shall be mentioned in the two papers in the place of the signature.

Objections or claims submitted by way of oral or written declaration shall be received by the clerk and concisely recorded by him in the record of proceedings. The aforementioned oral or written declarations must include mention of the rights, and the deeds or documents supporting the application, and the designation of an elected domicile in the cadastral area or at the seat of the district; written applications must be signed by the party concerned, and must be accompanied by all evidentiary documents; likewise, statements recorded in the record of proceedings as a result of oral declarations must be signed by the maker of the declaration, and if he is unable to sign his name he must affix to them the print of the first phalanx (joint) of the thumb of his right hand.

No objection whatsoever or application for registration shall be accepted after the expiry of the thirty-day time-limit appointed in Article twenty; furthermore, an objection or application for registration shall be struck off ipso jure if the intervening party does not produce, during the same time-limit, the deeds, documents or means mentioned by him in support of his claim, provided that he may have recourse to the ordinary courts in accordance with Article thirty-one.

Pursuant to the first Article of Order No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, Chapter Four (Articles 22 to 34) was repealed and replaced by the following text:

As soon as the thirty-day time-limit granted to objectors and claimants of rights expires, the justice of the peace or the real estate judge shall issue an order definitively closing the operations of demarcation and census; this order shall be posted on the door of the courtroom, brought to the knowledge of the interested parties through the mukhtars, notified to the courts of the area, and published in the Official Gazette.

Thereupon, the justice of the peace or the single real estate judge shall proceed to a preliminary examination of the records of provisional demarcation pertaining to each cadastral area, in accordance with the order of entry of the properties in the provisional census schedule, and shall verify that the formalities provided for in the provisions of the orders in force have been completed; he shall homologate the operative part of the records of proceedings and order the registration of the real property rights in rem in the Land Register if he finds that no objection or application whatsoever has been submitted in respect thereof or that the objections or applications submitted must be struck off pursuant to the provisions of Article 21 of this Order.

The decision of the judge shall be enforceable without any service or publication whatsoever, and copies of the original records of proceedings bearing this decision shall be sent forthwith to the head of the Land Registry Office in whose area the property is situated.

The justice of the peace or the single real estate judge shall draw up a consecutively numbered list of the properties in respect of which objections or applications have been submitted, following therein the order of the provisional census schedule. The interested parties shall have a time-limit of fifteen days starting from the date of posting of the closing order to bring a statement of withdrawal of the objections or applications for registration or a declaration attesting their acceptance thereof; if the party concerned succeeds, in this manner, in removing the objections and applications for registration, whether by proving their withdrawal or by acquiescing therein, the justice of the peace or the single real estate judge may order the registration of the real property right in rem in the Land Register in the name of the holder of that right, and homologate the contents of the record of proceedings in accordance with what has transpired.

Article 23: Objections or applications shall be adjudicated in accordance with the order followed in the provisional census schedule of properties for each cadastral area, and the judge shall appoint of his own motion or upon application the place, day and hour at which the actions are held.

This decision shall be served upon the interested parties at their elected domicile, and if they have no elected domicile, by way of posting it on the door of the place where the judge sits; in every case, the decision shall be posted on the door of the courtroom and the mukhtars shall be given notice thereof. During the fifteen days preceding the trial, the judge shall investigate the action, and may ipso jure or upon the application of the interested parties proceed to the site of the property to carry out the application of a deed or an investigation.

In this case, the judge shall act with the assistance of a surveyor-engineer and in the presence of the mukhtar and the intervening parties in the case, the latter having been notified of the inspection through the mukhtars; if the interested parties fail to appear, their presence shall be dispensed with and the work shall be commenced as if they were present, and a formal record of this operation shall be drawn up in due form. In addition, the judge may direct the plaintiff to submit his pleading or briefs before the eighth day of the time-limit; this pleading or these briefs shall be served upon the defendant, who may inspect them in the clerk's office and copy them without removing them from the office, and he must submit his reply brief before the expiry of the fifteen-day time-limit provided for in this Article. Upon the commencement of the trial, the statements contained in the records of proceedings shall be read out, and where necessary, the results of the investigations which the judge may have conducted at the disputed sites, and the pleadings or briefs of the interested parties, shall also be read out; the latter shall furthermore be entitled to request the reading out of any evidentiary document joined to the case file; thereafter, the statements of the interested parties or their representatives and the testimonies of the witnesses summoned by the judge shall be heard, following which judgment in the case shall be delivered either forthwith or after deliberation. The judge may not grant the interested parties any time-limit whatsoever, with the exception of public administrations, nor shall any excuse for adjourning the action be accepted save that resulting from force majeure proven with conclusive certainty to have occurred.

In the event of an application for the recusal of the real estate judge, the deputy real estate judge shall rule upon this application; if his recusal is also applied for, the Director of the Land Registry Departments shall appoint a single real estate judge or a deputy judge to rule upon the application or applications for recusal. An application for the recusal of the real estate judge appointed by the Director of the Land Registry Departments shall be deemed null and void; the judge shall disregard it and shall in all cases decide to dismiss the application.

Article 24:

If the plaintiff fails to appear at the hearing without an acceptable lawful excuse, the objection shall be deemed null and void and shall be struck off ipso jure in the record of demarcation. Every objection on the submission of which more than five years have elapsed starting from the date of the definitive closing of operations without being pursued and without being placed on the roll of hearings shall also be struck off. These provisions shall apply to all objections, whether prior or subsequent to this amendment; in all cases provided for in this Article, the objector shall retain the right to avail himself of the provisions of Article 31 hereinafter mentioned. This Article shall enter into force after the expiry of six months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

The Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Estate Judge shall give final judgment not subject to any recourse:

1- In every action falling within the jurisdiction of the Justice of the Peace, even if the judgment is subject to appeal under the laws in force. 2- In actions relating to rights existing over boundaries or pertaining to neighbourhood (such as party walls, and easements of view from windows, drainage of water, right of way, etc...).

He shall adjudicate at first instance, save where the provisions of Article 172 of the Code of Civil Procedure apply, in all other actions brought in respect of disputes concerning the existence or extent of the right of ownership or a real right over immovable property, or disputes concerning the position of the boundaries of the real property. Where the action falls within the jurisdiction of the Sharia Court, the judge may, if he deems it useful, obtain the opinion of the Sharia Judge before ruling on the merits of the right or on an incidental objection.

The Real Estate Judge shall have authority to impose a pecuniary fine and to rule on claims for damages where trespass and bad faith in the objection become apparent to him, subject to the reservation of the right of appeal. In such case, the objector may be sentenced to a pecuniary fine of twenty-five Lebanese-Syrian pounds in addition to the damages sustained by the injured party, and furthermore the costs of the objection (such as costs of inspection, travel, etc..) shall be borne by the objector, and in all cases the costs of additional investigation shall be borne by the party requesting the investigation, unless the judge has carried it out of his own motion.

The judge shall rule on the question of the costs incurred, and shall specify in the body of the decision the amount of the expenses and costs and the party liable for those costs, and recovery thereof shall take place in accordance with the legal provisions in force for the recovery of judicial costs, without non-payment thereof resulting in a delay in the execution of the decision.

An appeal against judgments rendered during judicial proceedings must be lodged at the same time as the appeal on the merits of the action is lodged. Furthermore, an appeal against decisions rendered by the Single Real Estate Judge must, on pain of inadmissibility, be lodged with the Court of Appeal of the region within a period of 15 days from the date of service effected in accordance with the conditions prescribed in Article 32 below. This shall be recorded in the minutes of the proceedings, and accordingly the clerk of the Court of Appeal must serve, within the twenty-four hours following the date of filing of the petition of appeal, the notice of appeal upon the Real Estate Judge who rendered his decision in the action, all on pain of a pecuniary fine of five Lebanese-Syrian pounds in addition to the damages which the said clerk may be liable to pay to the injured party, and the appeal shall be determined in accordance with the ordinary procedure, provided that the Court of Appeal shall be bound to appoint a reporting judge charged with conducting the investigations and, where necessary, proceeding to the locus in quo for the investigation, and when so proceeding the reporting judge shall be assisted by the clerk of the registry of the Court of Appeal and a surveyor appointed, at the request of the President of the Court of Appeal, by the Director of the Land Registry Services of the State, upon the proposal of the surveying contractor, and the investigation shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions laid down in Article 23, and the decision of the Court of Appeal shall be final, provided that an opposition may be lodged under the ordinary procedure against a judgment rendered in default.

An appeal shall not stay the registration of the real property in the Land Register and the entry shall be made in accordance with the decision at first instance, provided that the lodging of the appeal shall be noted in the Land Register in the column allotted for that purpose on the folio. In all cases, and without awaiting the entry of the real property in the Property Register, the real property shall become subject to the provisions of Decision No. 188 dated 15 March 1926, as soon as the decision at first instance is served in accordance with the provisions of Article 32 mentioned below.

The Single Real Estate Judge shall also adjudicate in every action referred to in Article 25 of this Decision where it has been instituted before the Court of First Instance, the Sharia Court or the Justice of the Peace, and judgment on the merits has not yet been rendered prior to the date of service of the decision opening the operations of census and demarcation in the region. For this purpose, as soon as the decision of the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Estate Judge opening the operations is served, the Court of First Instance, the Sharia Court or the Justice of the Peace before whom the action is brought must refer all the papers of the action to the competent Justice of the Peace or Single Real Estate Judge so that he may continue, in accordance with the provisions of this Decision, the proceedings previously commenced.

Judgments rendered by the Court of First Instance or by the Justice of the Peace in the actions referred to in Article 25, which have not become final at the date of service of the decision opening the operations of census and demarcation of real properties in the cadastral area, may not, with effect from that date, be subject to opposition, provided that they may be appealed against within a period of thirty days running from the date of service thereof upon the person of the judgment debtor or at his place of residence, and at the request of the interested parties the registry of the court shall serve these judgments, free of charge, upon the competent Single Real Estate Judge, who shall proceed to enter the particulars contained in the minutes of demarcation and census in accordance with those judgments, and the Single Real Estate Judge shall likewise be served ex officio with the appeals lodged against those same judgments so that they may be entered in the minutes of demarcation and census.

Appeals lodged in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article and appeals lodged prior to the date of the opening of the demarcation operations in the actions referred to in Article 25 shall be determined in accordance with the ordinary procedure.

Its text was successively amended by Decision No. 44 L.R. dated 20 April 1932, Decision No. 86/L.R. dated 17 April 1935, Decision No. 112/L.R. dated 17 May 1935 and Decision No. 135/L.R. dated 14 June 1935 as follows: Where an objection is lodged, and one of the interested litigants is subject to the jurisdiction of the Court of Foreign Actions, the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Estate Judge shall remain competent to hear the action brought before him and shall adjudicate thereon in accordance with the provisions of Decision 186 as amended by Decision No. 44/L.R. aforesaid, and in all the aforementioned cases, and notwithstanding the provisions of Article 25 of Decision No. 186 dated 15 March of the year 1926 concerning the census and demarcation of real properties and estates as amended by Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20 April of the year 1932, the decisions of the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Estate Judge shall be subject to appeal, and the appeal against the decisions of the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Estate Judge shall be brought before the Court of Appeal of Foreign Actions, and judgment thereon shall be given in accordance with the provisions of Article 26 of Decision No. 186 as amended by Decision No. 44/L.R. aforesaid. The Justice of the Peace and the Single Real Estate Judge shall also adjudicate in every action referred to in Article 25 of Decision No. 186 as amended by Decision No. 44/L.R. and brought before the Justice of the Peace of Foreign Actions where judgment on the merits of the action has not been rendered at the date of publication of this Decision, unless it has been referred for deliberation or is ready for judgment. For this purpose, immediately upon publication of this Decision, the Justice of the Peace must refer all the papers of the action to the competent Justice of the Peace or Single Real Estate Judge, who shall continue the proceedings previously in progress.

After the closure of the operations of census and demarcation, it shall remain open to bring any action whatsoever before the ordinary courts for objectors or claimants of a right, either those in respect of whose objection or claim no judgment having acquired the force of res judicata has been rendered, or, in the event of an appeal, those in respect of whom no final judgment has been rendered by the Court of Appeal granted in accordance with the provisions of this Decision. This right must be exercised, on pain of forfeiture, within the two years following the date on which the decision confirming the demarcation records, or the decisions of the Single Real Estate Judge, and, in the event of an appeal, the decision of the Court of Appeal rendered in accordance with the provisions of the present Decision, becomes enforceable.

The Magistrate or the Single Real Estate Judge shall confirm in his judgment the contents of the demarcation and census record and, where necessary, the judgment must include the reasons for the modifications or additions supervening upon the record, and he shall also confirm the plans drawn up by the surveying engineer attached to the court registry, by order of the judge, in rectification of the boundaries.

The decisions of the Magistrate or the Single Real Estate Judge shall be entered directly on the record, signed by the judge, and then transcribed onto the real estate census schedule. This schedule must always remain in conformity with the demarcation records, particularly as regards the annotations relating to the transfer of ownership and the real estate transactions effected before the judge prior to the issuance of the confirmation decision. The clerk of the judge shall be bound to transcribe these annotations on pain of a pecuniary fine of five pounds for each annotation omitted from transcription, in addition to damages that may be due from him to the injured party. Service of decisions shall be validly effected by posting them for a period of fifteen days on the door of the premises where the judge sits to administer justice; provided that, where a judgment in default is rendered, service shall be effected ipso jure through the judge at the elected domicile of the litigants, and if the litigants have not elected a domicile, service shall be validly effected by way of the posting aforementioned. In all cases, service upon public administrations shall be effected at the headquarters of such administrations and to the highest-ranking official therein. All formalities of service and notification to the interested litigants provided for by this Decision shall be effected in administrative form, and no nullity whatsoever shall result from the non-observance of the procedures prescribed by the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the execution of these formalities shall be established by the mere mention thereof directly on the record. The services provided for above shall be exempt from judicial fees and from stamp duties.

The rectification of boundaries and the drawing up of maps shall be carried out in accordance with the decisions of the Magistrate or the Single Real Estate Judge and, where necessary, under the same conditions, the measurement of the area of properties in unsurveyed regions shall be carried out.

Immediately upon the expiry of the time limit for appeal, the clerk of the Magistrate or the clerk of the Single Real Estate Judge or, where necessary, the clerk of the Magistrate's Court for Foreign Actions shall proceed, on his own responsibility, to transmit the demarcation records and the documents annexed thereto submitted by the litigants, with the exception of the files of judicial proceedings, to the Head of the Real Estate Office charged with keeping the Real Estate Register. In the event of an appeal of the action, only a copy of the records certified as a true copy of the original shall be sent to the Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office, under the same conditions, to serve as a basis for registration in the Real Estate Register.

As for the files of judicial proceedings relating to actions adjudicated by the Magistrate or the Single Real Estate Judge, they shall be deposited with the Directorate of Real Estate Services of the State, and as for the files of judicial proceedings relating to actions adjudicated before the Courts for Foreign Cases or the Courts of Appeal, they shall be kept in the registry of the court that rendered the judgment in first instance or on appeal.

The contractor for surveying works shall deposit with the local Real Estate Office, in accordance with this Decision, the final certified survey maps.

Pursuant to the third Article of Decision No. 141/LR dated 5/7/1939, the text of Article 35 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

In every real estate region, and in continuation of the operations of census and provisional demarcation being carried out on real properties and immovable property, and from the date of commencement of the census and demarcation fixed by decision of the Single Real Estate Judge until the date of the order or decision issued confirming the records, the Single Real Estate Judge shall act in the stead of the Defterkhaneh (Tapu) and the registration offices special to Mount Lebanon to authenticate and receive, in accordance with the provisions of the law, declarations or agreements containing sale and transfer (faragh), exchange, amicable composition of heirs (takharuj), or mortgage, and in general, the creation, modification, or extinction of all derechos in rem (real rights) or easements, and he shall also proceed, upon the request of the heirs and after examining the probative documents produced by their co-heirs, to determine the shares of each of them. Transactions conducted before the Magistrate or the Single Real Estate Judge may only cover rights established by a Tapu deed, by an entry in the registers of the Defterkhaneh, or by a contract legally authenticated in the registration offices in Lebanon.
