The Council of the faculty or institute shall nominate the examination committee for each subject, consisting of at least two members, one of whom shall be the instructor of the subject. The committee shall be appointed by a decision of the President of the University based on the decision of its Council founded upon the nomination of the Council of the faculty or institute.

The instructor or instructors of the subject shall, in agreement with the Head of the Department and the Dean or the Director, set the examination questions. The committee shall mark the written papers and conduct the oral examinations.

The University Council shall have the right to appoint, based on the recommendation of the Council of the faculty or institute, a person to substitute for the instructor of the subject on the committee, if it is impossible for him to participate in the examination operations.

The members of the committee, presided over by the Dean or the Director, shall examine the results of each examination, and the final results shall be submitted to the Council of the faculty or institute for ratification and approval.

The faculties and institutes shall grant official certificates in higher studies, and each certificate shall be signed by the President of the University and the Dean of the competent faculty or the Director of the competent institute.

As for the official university degrees granted by the University, such as the Licence and the Doctorate, their attestation shall be signed by the Minister of Education and Higher Education, the President of the University, and the Dean or the Director.

Every student who breaches his duties or commits an act incompatible with dignity or with the integrity of the university atmosphere shall be subject to disciplinary action. Disciplinary proceedings issued by the University shall be independent of judicial proceedings.

The following shall be deemed an act subject to disciplinary action:

- A criminal offence connected with university life.

- Disruption of security and order within the University and its faculties and institutes.

- Deliberate abstention from attending classes, lectures, and university works which university regulations require regular attendance at.

- Assault upon members of the teaching staff or employees of the University.

- Rebellion against the regulations of the University.

- Committing or attempting to commit cheating in an examination.

The following shall be subject to disciplinary authority:

- Students registered in the faculties and institutes attached to the University, as long as their registration subsists.

- Candidates from outside the University sitting for university degrees.

The disciplinary penalties are:

- Warning.

- Reprimand.

- Suspension from the University for a period ranging between one week and one month.

- Deprivation of the right to sit for University examinations for one or more sessions.

- Expulsion from the University for a maximum period of three years.

- Permanent expulsion from the University.

The bodies competent to impose penalties are:

- The Dean of the faculty or the Director of the institute in the first three cases, provided that the Dean or the Director obtains the approval of the Council of the faculty or institute in the matter of suspension if it exceeds one week.

- The President of the University, based on the decision of its Council, in all other cases.

Any forgery, cheating, or attempted cheating, upon registration or in examinations, shall expose the perpetrator to the cancellation of his examination.

If the student is caught in the act of cheating, he shall be expelled immediately from the examination hall and his examination shall be deemed void ipso jure; in all other cases, the annulment of the examination shall be issued by a decision of the Council of the faculty or institute.

The perpetrator of forgery, cheating, or attempted cheating, together with any accomplice therein, shall be referred to the Council of the faculty or institute, and the Council may issue, together with the decision to annul the examination, one of the penalties provided for in Article 61 of this Law.

A student against whom a disciplinary decision has been issued by the Dean, the Director, or the Council of the faculty or institute may appeal against it before the University Council within a period not exceeding two weeks from the date of his notification of the decision through administrative channels.

As for disciplinary decisions issued by the University Council, they shall not be subject to any recourse except in the two cases of temporary expulsion and permanent expulsion.

The University or some of its faculties or institutes may be closed if the necessity of preserving security and order so requires.

- The faculty or institute shall be closed for a period not exceeding three days by a decision of the President of the University based upon the proposal of the Dean or the Director, provided that it is submitted immediately to the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

- The University or one of its branches shall be closed for a period not exceeding two weeks by a decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education based upon the recommendation of the University Council or by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

- And the University or one of its branches shall be closed for a period exceeding two weeks by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers based upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education after consulting the opinion of the University Council.

The Equivalency Committee in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education shall examine the equivalency of degrees required for the appointment of members of the teaching staff and other technical personnel, provided that a representative of the competent faculty or institute is added to its members when examining the equivalency of a degree of one of the candidates for teaching in any of the faculties and institutes of the University.

If the position of President of the Lebanese University becomes vacant within ten years from the date of issuance of this Law and it is impossible to apply Paragraph A of Article 10 thereof.

An acting President of the University may be appointed from among three persons of the category of professors of higher education nominated by the University Council, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers based upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

If it is impossible to find candidates for the post of Deanship or Directorship from among the members of the teaching staff included in the cadre, the Government may conclude an agreement with a specialist to assume the Deanship or Directorship. In this case, the mission shall be entrusted to him pursuant to a decree adopted based upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education, provided that this proposal is accompanied by a draft contract for a period of three years stating the wages, allowances, and all other obligations of the two parties.
Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 37, it shall suffice during a period of three years to present a single candidate.

The salary scale of the teaching staff in the Lebanese University and other employees of the technical cadre shall be determined, and the current employees of the University shall be classified:

The President of the University, the members of the teaching staff, and other employees of the technical cadre by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers based upon the proposal of the University Council and after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board, within six months from the date of issuance of this Law.
The administrative cadre of the Lebanese University shall be determined in accordance with the table attached to this Law.

The conditions for the appointment of the instructor, head of laboratory, librarian, documentalist, workshop superintendent, assistant librarian, laboratory preparer, stenographer, investigator, book coordinator, mechanical worker, and other employees of the technical cadre shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.
The branch shall be managed by a Director and a Council.

The Branch Council shall be composed of at least five members:

1- The Director as Chairman.

2- A representative of the members of the teaching staff in the branch.

3- The heads of the academic departments in the branch. In the absence of departments, the Branch Council shall be completed by electing at most five members by the members of the teaching staff.

4- A representative of the students.

5- The secretary of the branch shall perform the function of secretary of this Council, and shall draw up the minutes of the sessions and keep them in due form after their signature by the Chairman and the members.

- The Council shall meet upon convocation by its Chairman once every two weeks, and it may also meet upon convocation by the Dean or whenever one-third of the members submit a reasoned written request.

- If the Dean attends, he shall chair the session.

- The sessions of the Council shall not be legal unless attended by two-thirds of the members at the first convocation or by an absolute majority at the second convocation. Decisions shall be taken by an absolute majority. In the event of a tie vote, the Chairman shall have the casting vote.

- The provisions governing the meetings of the Unit Council shall apply to the meetings of the Branch Council.

- On the appointment of the Branch Director:

1- The concerned Branch Council shall submit, to the Unit Council, a nomination list of five names of professors holding the rank of professor or assistant professor, or who have fulfilled the conditions for promotion to this rank, or a lecturer with at least ten years of experience in the cadre of the University or on a full-time basis.

2- The Unit Council shall select, from among the five names submitted to it by the Branch Council, three names which it shall in turn submit to the President of the University.

3- The President of the University shall appoint, by a decision issued by him, one of the three names submitted to him to be the Director of the concerned branch.

4- The term of office of the Director shall be three years, not renewable except after the expiry of a full term.

5- The Director shall be exempted from at most one-third of his teaching load at his request and by a decision of the University Council based upon the recommendation of the Unit Council.

6- The Director shall assume the management of business in the branch in both administrative and financial respects in accordance with the law and regulations of the University.

7- In the event of vacancy of the position of Director, the appointment shall take place according to the same mechanism. In the event of absence, the oldest member of the Branch Council shall replace him.

Functions of the Branch Council:

The Branch Council shall assume supervision over the academic, administrative, and financial affairs of the branch, coordination between its various departments, and follow-up of teaching performance and academic activities therein. Within this framework, the Branch Council shall perform the following functions:

1- Following up the implementation of the decisions of the Unit Council relating to the branch.

2- Recommending the establishment or amendment of teaching curricula and examination and evaluation systems in the faculty or institute.

3- Proposing the internal regulations of the branch.

4- Proposing the budget of the branch.

5- Proposing examining committees and examination committees.

6- Proposing the distribution of subjects and courses among the members of the teaching staff in the branch.

7- Submitting the applications of members of the teaching staff to benefit from the sabbatical year.

8- Nominating students to benefit from scholarships according to the ranking submitted by the concerned departments, and in accordance with the applicable scholarship regulations.

9- Determining the needs of the branch for members of the teaching staff for entry into the cadre, or full-time contracting, or hourly contracting.

10- Proposing the needs of the branch and submitting them to the Unit Council.

11- Discussing and approving the semi-annual report prepared by the Director on the academic, administrative, and financial affairs in the branch and submitting it to the Unit Council.

12- Studying the proposals and projects of the departments, following up the teaching work in the departments, and adopting recommendations regarding them.

13 - Reviewing and approving the results of the examinations of the branch before submitting them to the Unit Council.

Organization and management of the Department:

A- The branches of the University units shall be composed of academic departments.

B - The department shall be managed by a Head and a Department Council composed of six members elected from all the academic ranks present in the department. In the event that the number of members of the teaching staff in the department is ten or less, the Department Council shall be composed of a Head and three members elected from all the academic ranks available in the department.

C - Departments shall be established by a decision of the University Council, based upon the proposal of the Unit Council and based upon the proposal of the Branch Councils in the unit where both exist.

D- The department shall include the members of the teaching staff who teach its subjects. A group of subjects that constitute a single specialization, or closely related specializations, shall be considered a department.

The head and the council of the department shall take charge of the academic and educational affairs of the department.

A- The head shall take charge of:

1- Representing the department in the council of the branch or of the faculty if it has no branches.

2- Preparing the agenda of the council of the department, presiding over its meetings and following up on its recommendations.

3- Submitting a termly report to the council of the branch, after discussing it in the council of the department, on the conditions of the department.

4- Submitting an annual report, after discussing it in the department, on the needs of the teaching staff, the technical, administrative and academic works, and all other material requirements for improving academic performance.

5- Calling for regular and extraordinary meetings of the department and of the council of the department.

B- The dean or the director may call the department to meet whenever the need arises to deliberate on the academic affairs of the department.

C- The term of office of the head of the department and of the council of the department shall be two years, renewable once.

In the event of the absence of the head of the department, the member of the council of the department highest in rank shall deputize for him, and in the event of equality of rank, the highest in step.

If the position of head of the department becomes vacant for any reason whatsoever more than three months prior to the expiration of his term, the member of the council of the department highest in rank, and in the event of equality of ranks, the highest in step, shall deputize for him until new elections are held.

On the functions of the council of the department:

1- Proposing the distribution of subjects and courses among the members of the teaching staff according to specialization and teaching experience.

2- Proposing the programs of annual activities.

3- Determining the educational affairs in the department.

4- Determining the needs of the department in terms of members of the teaching staff.

5- Recommending the formation of examination committees.

6- Participating in the amendment of curricula and programs relating to the department.

7- Nominating those who have fulfilled the conditions for supervising postgraduate studies in the department.

8- Proposing the scientific content of the teaching subjects in the department, coordinating between them, the means of developing them, and the systems of study and examinations therein.

9- Determining the needs of the department and submitting them to the council of the branch.

On candidacy:

1- For the representatives of the members of the teaching staff in a single branch:

The candidate shall be required to be:

A- On the permanent staff of the Lebanese University or full-time in one of its faculties and institutes; in the event of the absence of permanent staff or full-time members, one of the hourly contractors may be elected, provided that his teaching load is not less than 200 hours and that at least five years have elapsed since he has been teaching.

B- Holding the general specialization of the branch or unit for which he runs as a candidate.

C- In the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, he shall be required to have the highest load, and in the event that the load is equal, he shall run as a candidate for the unit or branch closest to his specialization according to his degree.

2- For the heads of the academic departments:

The candidate for the headship of the department shall be required to be:

A- On the permanent staff of the Lebanese University or full-time in one of its faculties from the two highest ranks in the department, having spent at least ten years in university education; in the event of the absence of full-time members in the specialization, one of the hourly contractors from the parallel categories, namely the first or second category, may be elected, with a teaching load of not less than 200 hours and at least ten years having elapsed since he has been teaching.

B- Holding one of the main specializations of the department.

C- In the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, his candidacy shall be required to be where he has the highest load, and in the event that his load is equal with another department, he shall run as a candidate in the unit or branch closest to his specialization according to his degree.

3- For the members of the councils of the academic departments: The candidate for membership of the academic council of the department: shall be required to be:

A- On the permanent staff of the Lebanese University or full-time in one of its faculties, having spent at least five years in university education; in the event of the absence of full-time members in the specialization, one of the hourly contractors from the parallel categories, namely the first or second category, may be elected, with a teaching load of not less than 200 hours and at least five years having elapsed since he has been teaching.

B- Holding one of the main specializations in the department.

C- In the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, his candidacy shall be required to be where he has the highest load, and in the event that his load is equal with another department, in the unit or branch closest to his specialization according to his degree.

4- In the event that there are special cases in some faculties, such cases shall be submitted to the University Council to decide thereon, upon the recommendation of the council of the unit.

On election

A- Permanent staff and full-time professors shall have the right to vote; as for hourly contractors, the teaching load must not be less than 200 hours.

B- The contracted full-time member or the member on the permanent staff shall hold the general specialization and the highest teaching load in the unit, branch or department, and in the event that the load is equal, he shall vote in the unit, branch or department closest to his specialization according to his degree, and in the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, he shall be required to have the highest load.

- The candidate who has obtained the greatest number of votes shall be deemed the winner, and in the event of a tie, the highest in rank, then the highest in step, then the oldest in age.

- The results of the elections may be challenged before the University Council within three days from the date of their announcement, and the objection shall be decided upon within a period of ten days from the date of its submission. The decision of the University Council may be challenged in accordance with the provisions of Article 63 of the Statute of the State Council.

- The elections of the council of the unit and the councils of the branches shall be held upon a call by the dean and under his supervision.

- A copy of the results shall be notified to the Presidency of the University.

On the rules of student representation

Students shall be delegated to the University Council or to the council of the unit or to the council of the branch by their union in accordance with its own bylaws, provided that they are students of the second year or its equivalent and above.

The rights and obligations of students in the councils of the unit and the branch, in terms of attendance, voting and otherwise, shall be subject to the provisions set forth in Legislative Decree No. /115/ dated 30 June 1977, which determined the rules of student participation in the administration of the Lebanese University.

((Article 14 of Law 66 dated 4/3/2009 Official Gazette 12)

Upon the expiration of the term of office of any of the members of the academic councils provided for in this Law, they shall continue to exercise their functions until replacements for them are appointed or elected.

- All provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its content are repealed.

- This Law shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Gazette.)

An endowment (waqf) is of two types: charitable and family.

A charitable endowment is an endowment that is dedicated to charitable purposes from the time of its establishment, such as an endowment for mosques, hospitals, shelters and the poor.

A family endowment is one that is dedicated to the founder (waqif) himself and his descendants, or to such persons as he wishes to benefit, and the ultimate reversion of which is then assigned to charitable purposes.

An endowment may be partly charitable and partly family, such as where the founder dedicates his endowment on the condition that disbursements from its revenue begin with spending specified sums and charitable benefactions which he has designated, and the remainder is then spent on the beneficiaries in accordance with the condition laid down by the founder.

This Law governs the pure family endowment and the joint endowment shared between descendants and a charitable purpose.

As for the charitable endowment relating to religious institutes and charitable institutions, it is subject to the Sharia provisions and the applicable laws special to it, and to the decisions taken by its Supreme Council by way of addition or amendment to any of the articles of those laws as required by the Sharia ruling, and it includes all controlled (madbuta) and annexed (mulhaqa) endowments administered by the Directorate General of Endowments.

The rules relating to the establishment of charitable endowments, their validity, purpose, partition, lease and exchange (istibdal) are defined in the provisions of the laws and decisions special to them.

The establishment anew of a family endowment, its partition and its termination shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, with due regard to the laws and decisions relating to the Land Registry.

Sharia judges are prohibited from hearing an attestation to the establishment of a new family endowment if it is contrary to the provisions of this Law.

Every newly established family endowment that contravenes its provisions shall be deemed null and void with respect to the endowment, his descendants and third parties.

The founder may revoke his family endowment in whole or in part, and he may also alter its objects of expenditure and its conditions, provided that the alteration does not contravene the provisions of this Law.

A family endowment may not be made perpetual, nor may it be established for more than two generations (degrees).

The beneficiaries to whom the endowment is dedicated shall be deemed a single generation if the founder designates them by name at the time of the endowment; and if he does not designate them by name, each degree of descent (batn) shall be deemed a generation.
The founder shall not be counted in the calculation of the generations.

A family endowment terminates upon the extinction of the one or two generations, and the endowment reverts to the ownership of the founder if he is alive, and to his heirs of the first or second generation, as the case may be, if he is deceased.
If the founder leaves no heirs, the endowment shall revert to the Directorate General of Endowments, unless the founder stipulated a confirmed charitable purpose.
If an endowment is coupled with an invalid condition, the endowment shall be valid and the condition shall be void.
Every condition that restricts the freedom of the beneficiaries as to their marriage, their residence, or their borrowing of money without a preponderant interest shall be deemed null and void.
The founder may stipulate the ten conditions recognized under Sharia for himself or for another within the limits of this Law.
It is permissible to endow immovable and movable property, just as it is permissible to endow shares and stocks of companies that are exploited in a manner permissible under Sharia.

It is not permissible to endow an undivided share (musha') in an immovable property that is not capable of partition, unless the remainder thereof is endowed and united in the purpose to which it is dedicated.

The partition of a family endowment, and of a joint endowment shared between family and charitable purposes, as a binding partition is permissible upon the request of the beneficiaries or any one of them whenever it is capable of partition and there is no manifest, certain harm therein. The trustee (mutawalli) of the charitable share may request the partition in the exact same manner as one of the beneficiaries.

The shares of the beneficiaries to whom the endowment is dedicated shall be determined by reference to the deed of endowment, or to established practice accepted under Sharia, or to an enforceable judicial judgment.

If the founder assigns the revenue of his endowment to some of the beneficiaries and stipulates fixed allowances (murattabat) therein for others, the revenue shall be divided proportionally (by muhassa) between the beneficiaries and the holders of the fixed allowances according to the ratio between the fixed allowances and the remainder of the revenue at the time of the endowment, if the revenue was known at that time, provided that the fixed allowances shall not exceed what the founder stipulated.

If the revenue was not known at the time of the endowment, the revenue shall be divided between the holders of the fixed allowances and the beneficiaries such that the beneficiaries shall have the whole of the revenue and the holders of the fixed allowances shall have a share equivalent to the amount of their allowances; and if the founder stipulated shares (siham) for some of the beneficiaries and fixed allowances for the others, the fixed allowances shall be paid out of the remainder of the endowment after the shares, and if the remainder is insufficient to cover the fixed allowances, it shall be divided among their holders in proportion to them.

The fixed allowances shall be reduced in proportion to any reduction in the corpus (a'yan) of the endowment.

If the founder stipulates in his endowment permanent charitable benefactions or fixed allowances of a specified amount, or of an amount deemed as specified, and partition is requested, the court shall set aside a share the revenue of which guarantees what is due to the holders of these fixed allowances after estimating it in accordance with the preceding article on the basis of the average revenue of the endowment during the last five normal years.

Every person who holds a right of disposal (tasarruf) in an endowed immovable property by way of double rent (ijaratayn) or fixed ground rent (muqata'a) shall have the right to request the purchase of the bare ownership (raqaba) of the immovable property in return for a consideration equivalent to 30 annual installments.

Likewise subject to compulsory exchange (istibdal) are all endowed premises encumbered with rights of disposal in favor of third parties by way of long lease, whether they belong to controlled (madbuta), annexed (mulhaqa), or exempted (mustathna) endowments of all kinds.

The provisions of Decision No. 80 dated 29 January 1926 shall be observed in the transaction of exchange (istibdal) of immovable properties encumbered with rights of disposal in favor of third parties, as well as Order No. 3 taken on 22 December 1930 and ratified by Decision No. 156 dated 16 December 1931, and the decisions subsequent thereto.
The provisions relating to partition shall apply to the rights of double rent (ijaratayn) and long lease (muqata'a), and to the real rights relating to other leases registered in the Land Registry.

It is not permissible to conclude contracts of long-term ground lease (hikr), and if it appears necessary to establish double rent (ijaratayn) or fixed ground rent (muqata'a) on any endowed immovable property, its exchange (istibdal) shall be carried out in accordance with the Sharia regulations in force.

Operations for the partition of the real properties of family endowments (waqfs) that were carried out in accordance with the religious laws, statutes and provisions in force prior to the promulgation of this Law shall become final. All actions relating to the annulment of a partition carried out in accordance with the preceding provisions - brought by a beneficiary whose entitlement arose after the partition - shall not be admitted.

Upon the partition of a pure family endowment (waqf), the equivalent of fifteen per cent shall be set aside in return for the charitable object stipulated in the endowment, without which the endowment would not have been valid, and shall be delivered to the local Endowment Department to be expended on general charitable objects.
In partition proceedings, the provisions of the Law on the Partition of Immovable Property shall be followed.

Where the competent court partitions the endowment (waqf) in accordance with the preceding Article and a beneficiary has a segregated share, he shall be appointed trustee (mutawalli) over his share provided that he fulfils the conditions of trusteeship, and no regard shall be had to the stipulation of the endower (waqif). Here, the representative of the charitable entity shall be deemed one of the beneficiaries.
The Sharia Court must remove a trustee (mutawalli) of the endowment (waqf) who is not a beneficiary therein and appoint another from among the beneficiaries.

The Sharia Court may, while hearing any action relating to the endowment (waqf) whatsoever, dismiss the trustee (mutawalli) if it sees in his remaining a detriment to the endowment or the beneficiaries, and it may appoint a provisional trustee while hearing the action for dismissal until it is finally adjudicated.

Where the real properties of the endowment (waqf) fall into ruin and it is not possible to reconstruct that which has fallen into ruin or to exchange it in a manner that secures for the beneficiaries a share in the yield that is not negligible, the endowment therein shall terminate.

The endowment (waqf) shall be deemed terminated if that which the beneficiaries receive from the yield becomes negligible, and that in which the endowment has terminated shall validly become the property in full ownership of its beneficiary, or of the endower (waqif) if he is alive.

Where the termination of the endowment leads to the sale of the endowed real properties by public auction and it is impracticable to serve notice of the sale formalities upon all the beneficiaries owing to their large number, the absence of some of them, ignorance of his place of residence, or other reasons, the Execution Department may content itself with publishing the formalities in the Official Gazette and two daily newspapers, at the location of the real property, and on the door of the court.

The competent Civil Court shall decide the termination of the endowment (waqf) and the liquidation of the various rights incumbent thereon in accordance with the following rules:

- In pure family endowments, the endowment shall be liquidated upon the application of one of the beneficiaries, and the charitable share set out in Article 27 shall be reserved therein.

- In endowments wherein permanent charities or allowances of a fixed amount, or treated as fixed, are stipulated, the endowment shall be liquidated upon the application of one of the beneficiaries or of the charitable entity, and a share assessed by the court in proportion to the average annual charities or allowances to the total yield shall be reserved for such entity, in accordance with the provisions of the 20th Article of this Law.

In endowments shared between family and charitable purposes, the court may, upon the application of the religious or charitable authority or of the holder of the right from among the family parties, liquidate:

1- The spiritual rights incumbent upon family endowments, whether they pertain to the administration or the yield for the benefit of the living or the dead.

2- The family rights incumbent upon religious or charitable endowments. The court shall assess the value of these rights and specify the manner of their satisfaction so that the endowment becomes free thereof, and the court shall in all cases summon the representative of the religious authority.
Where the endowment (waqf) terminates and there is none of the descendants of the endower (waqif) owing to their extinction, the endowment shall revert to the local Charitable Endowments Department.
The endower (waqif) may endow all that he owns in favour of whomsoever he wishes if at the time of his death he has no descendants, spouses or parents.

An owner may endow not more than one-third of his estate in favour of whomsoever he wishes from among his heirs or others, or in favour of a charitable object, and one-third of the estate of the endower (waqif) shall be valued as at the time of his death.

The heirs from among the descendants of the endower (waqif), his spouse and his parents who are in existence at the time of his death must have an entitlement in the endowment (waqf) in respect of that which exceeds one-third of his estate, in accordance with the provisions of the Law of Inheritance. None of them may be deprived of all or part of the entitlement for reasons other than the following:

1- A beneficiary shall be deprived of his entitlement if he kills the endower in a manner of homicide that bars inheritance by law.

2- Where a wife endows an endowment in favour of her husband and stipulates that he be deprived thereof if he marries someone other than her or if he divorces her.

3- Where the endower has strong motives for depriving the beneficiary, the importance of which shall be assessed by the court.

The endower (waqif) may grant to the issue of any of his children who died during his lifetime an entitlement in the endowment (waqf) to the extent of that which would have accrued to his father had he remained alive.

Where a family endowment (waqf) is arranged by generations (tabaqat), no ascendant shall exclude the issue of another, and if anyone dies, that to which he was entitled or would have been entitled shall be paid to his issue. Where a beneficiary dies leaving his share and has no issue succeeding him in the entitlement, his share shall revert to the yield of the endowment in which he was entitled.

Where there is no one in his generation, the revenue shall be paid to the generation following it until someone from the members of that generation comes into existence, whereupon the entitlement shall revert to it.

Where the entitlement of a generation lapses, the revenue shall be paid to the generation following it.

The trustee (mutawalli) shall be deemed a fiduciary over the property of the endowment (waqf) and an agent for the beneficiaries, and his statement as to expenditure on the affairs of the endowment or upon the beneficiaries shall not be accepted save by voucher.

The trustee (mutawalli) shall be held liable for his gross negligence towards the real properties of the endowment (waqf) and its yields, and he shall be liable for his slight negligence if he receives remuneration for the trusteeship.

Where the trustee (mutawalli) is ordered to render an account of the endowment (waqf) and fails to submit it within the time limit fixed for him by the judge, or fails to execute the decision of the Sharia judge to produce the supporting documents, the latter may sentence him to a coercive fine not exceeding ten Lebanese pounds for each day of delay. This shall be subject to due regard for the measures which the judge is entitled to take in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article 31.
The decision of the judge in this regard shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse, provided that he may revoke it if the trustee (mutawalli) shows an acceptable excuse.

The provisions of this Law shall apply to all Christian and Israelite family endowments (waqfs) situated in Lebanese territory. A Special Court shall be constituted by decree, composed of a President of the rank of Appellate Judge (Counsellor) and two members, one of whom shall be from the community concerned and the other from among the beneficiaries of the endowments, to take the place of the Sharia judge or the Endowments Administration in matters falling within the jurisdiction of each of them pursuant to the provisions of this Law. The said Court must abide by the endowment deed and by the laws of the competent community in the event of a judgment for the liquidation of the endowment.

The decisions of the Special Court shall be open to opposition before it within three months from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette and in a widely circulated daily newspaper, and save for that shall not be open to any avenue of recourse.

The Execution Department shall execute the decisions of this Court.
All provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its provisions are hereby repealed, and it shall be published in the Official Gazette.
Every owner in an undivided real property in which amicable partition is impracticable may request the termination of co-ownership in accordance with the procedures specified in this Law.

The request for the termination of co-ownership shall be submitted to the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the real property or properties are located, in the form of a petition to be served upon all the co-owners and the holders of rights in rem, and upon the competent Land Registry Secretariat in order to enter a caveat thereof on the folio of the concerned real property or properties.

Service shall be effected in accordance with the procedures specified in Articles 353 and 355 of the Code of Civil Procedure. However, if it appears that the person to be served is of unknown place of residence pursuant to a certificate issued by the mukhtar of the locality, he shall be served by the exceptional method in the following manner:

- A copy of the petition shall be posted on the door of the vestibule of the court, and an abstract thereof shall be published in the Official Gazette and in two local newspapers designated by the President of the Court, at the expense of the petitioner, and these service measures shall be attested by a record drawn up by the clerk of the court under his responsibility, certifying that twenty days have elapsed since the carrying out of the two formalities of posting and publication.

- As for the service of the remaining documents and decisions, including the final judgment, it shall be effected by posting on the door of the vestibule of the court.

However, with respect to the final judgment, an abstract thereof shall also be published in the Official Gazette and in two local newspapers designated by the President of the Court at the expense of the party requesting service.

All the co-owners and the holders of rights in rem may submit their observations on the request for the termination of co-ownership by written submissions within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of service of the petition in accordance with what is specified in Article 3 of this Law.

They must elect a domicile within the jurisdiction of the court; failing which, all documents and decisions, including the final judgment, shall be served upon them by affixation on the door of the vestibule of the court.

If among the co-owners there are minors, incapacitated persons, or a waqf having no tutor or guardian, the court seized of the request for the termination of co-ownership may appoint a special tutor or guardian to represent them in the case, either of its own motion or at the request of the petitioner for the termination of co-ownership.

The Court of First Instance shall examine the case in the council chamber within a time limit of one week commencing from the date of expiry of the time limit for submitting observations specified in Article 4.

It may take the measures and steps conducive to making the case ready for judgment by virtue of decisions served within the time limits in accordance with the procedures specified above; such decisions shall include the time limits for their execution and shall not be subject to appeal except along with the final judgment.

The Court of First Instance shall issue in the council chamber its final judgment partitioning the real property in kind if it is susceptible of partition, and in the event that its partition in kind is impracticable, it shall decide to establish a real estate joint-stock company upon the request of co-owners owning at least fifty-one percent; if such majority does not concur on establishing a company, the real property shall be sold by public auction.

- If it is decided to establish the real estate company and there is among the co-owners who did not agree to its establishment one who owns a share that is susceptible of partition in kind and severance on the basis of the experts' reports, he may request the same, and his request shall be executed under the supervision of the court in accordance with the laws in force. The severance for the partition of the real property shall comply with all the conditions provided for in the Urban Planning Law issued on 24/9/1962 and its amendments, particularly Article 26 as amended thereof, and all the regulations adopted pursuant to its provisions, without contradicting the spirit of these texts.

- The decision of the court shall be served upon the interested parties in accordance with the procedures specified in Articles Two, Three and Four above, and the co-owner who wishes to avail himself of the right to partition and sever his share in kind must declare his wish in writing by a petition submitted to the court within a time limit of 15 days from the date of service, under pain of forfeiture of this right.

The decision ordering the conversion of the real property rights in rem into shares in a real estate joint-stock company must include the appointment of an expert or a committee of experts to appraise the elements of the real property and the rights in rem encumbering it, with a view to determining the value of the contributions in kind.

The expert or the committee of experts shall summon the parties by publication in two local newspapers to attend the physical inspection six days prior to the scheduled date and to submit their observations, and the expert or the committee of experts must complete their mission and submit the report to the court within a time limit of two months from the date of being notified of the decision mentioned in the preceding Article.

The report of the expert or of the committee of experts shall be deposited at the registry of the court, and the interested parties shall be summoned to submit their observations thereon within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of their being served notice of the deposit in accordance with the procedures specified in Articles Three and Four above, and every interested party shall be entitled to receive a copy of the report.

After the expiry of this time limit, the Court of First Instance shall issue its judgment whereby it shall determine the value of all the elements of the real property and the value of the contributions in kind pertaining to the co-owners and the holders of rights in rem, and shall summon them to hold a preliminary assembly presided over by the President of the Court of First Instance.

The judgment mentioned in Article Nine is subject to appeal within a time limit of thirty days from the date of its service in accordance with the procedures specified in Articles Three and Four above.

The appeal shall not stay the execution of the judgment unless the Court of Appeal decides to stay the execution.

The service procedures set out in Articles Two, Three and Four of this Law shall be followed before the Court of Appeal, and the Court of Appeal shall issue its decision in the council chamber; it shall be enforceable on its original minute and shall not be subject to challenge by any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

The quorum at the preliminary assembly provided for in Article 9 of this Law shall be deemed lawful with the attendance of co-owners representing at least twenty percent of the undivided shares in the real property, provided that their number is not less than three persons.

At this assembly, three founders shall be elected to draw up the articles of association of the company, including the designation of its name, its object, its head office, its duration, the amount of its capital, the number of its shares, the nominal value of the share, the manner of its management, the opening of subscription for shares in kind among the co-owners of the real property and the holders of rights encumbering it in proportion to their share in the real property and the value of their rights determined in accordance with the procedures appointed in this Law, and the opening of subscription for cash shares in the event of an increase of the capital and the designation of the bank in which the value of the subscription for cash shares shall be deposited, all in accordance with the procedures provided for in Articles 79 et seq. of the Code of Commerce relating to the incorporation of joint-stock companies, subject to the special texts specified in this Law; and each subscriber shall be delivered a provisional share certificate which shall subsequently be replaced by a final share certificate.

If among the co-owners and the holders of rights in rem there are absentees and an incapacitated person who has not come forward to receive the certificates of shares in kind pertaining to him, those certificates shall be deposited in trust in the chest of the court, which shall appoint a special curator to exercise the rights and obligations attaching to those shares and to represent them at general assemblies of all kinds, under the supervision of the President of the Court of First Instance.

Immediately upon the completion of the subscription for the entire capital of the company and the distribution of the provisional share certificates, the founders shall, under the supervision of the President of the Court of First Instance, set the agenda of the constituent assembly and convene it by publication in two local newspapers at least one month prior to the date fixed for its meeting.

The constituent general assembly shall be convened under the chairmanship of the President of the Court of First Instance or the person whom he delegates, and its deliberations shall not be lawful unless the number of shareholders of which it is composed represents at least two-thirds of the capital of the company. If a quorum is not reached, a new assembly may be convened pursuant to a notice published in accordance with the procedures set forth in the thirteenth Article, and the notice shall state the agenda of the previous assembly and the results to which it led, and the deliberations of this second assembly shall be lawful if the number of shareholders of which it is composed represents at least one-half of the capital of the company.

If this quorum is not reached for it, a third assembly may be convened, and it shall only be required at that time to represent at least one-third of the capital of the company.

The mission of the constituent general assembly shall be confined to verifying the validity of the subscription to the entirety of the shares of the company and the payment of their value in accordance with the articles of association, approving these articles of association, and ascertaining the final incorporation of the company, and to electing the members of the first board of directors, appointing a statutory auditor for the company, carrying out the formality of publication and registration and authorising whomever is required, approving the incorporation expenses and empowering the board of directors to pay them, and discharging the founders from liability.
The company shall be subject to its articles of association and to the provisions of the Code of Commerce relating to joint-stock companies for the regulations in force.

Upon submission of the application for the termination of co-ownership, a fixed fee shall be levied on this application, and if this application is accompanied by a final judgment ordering the incorporation of a real estate joint-stock company, the latter shall be required immediately upon the final completion of its incorporation to pay to the Lebanese Treasury a fee of three per cent of the value of its capital, and upon payment of the said fee, ownership of the contributions in kind made to the company shall be transferred to its name in the Land Registry Offices without any other financial or real estate fee being incurred by it.

Immediately upon the completion of the incorporation of the company and the election of its board of directors, the annotations of lawsuits pending among the owners shall be struck off ipso jure from the register sheet of the real property or real properties in kind, and the real estate joint-stock company shall be subrogated to their place in the disputes pending between them and third parties.

If it is impossible to complete the incorporation of the real estate joint-stock company for any reason whatsoever, the Court of First Instance which decided to establish the company shall have the right to revoke its decision and to decide to put the real property up for sale by public auction by a reasoned decision, and this decision shall be subject to appeal within a time limit of one month from the date of its notification by means of publication in two local newspapers.

All legal provisions contrary to this Law and which are inconsistent with its content are repealed. Lawsuits pending before Single Judges shall be referred administratively to the Court of First Instance.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The General Accounting Plan provided for in Article Three of Decree No. 4665 dated 26/12/1981 shall consist of a chart of accounts adopting the decimal classification.

This chart shall be divided into:

Nine classes of accounts numbered from 1 to 9. More detailed accounts shall branch out from each of these classes by adopting a numbering consisting successively of two digits, then three digits, then four digits, etc...

The classes of accounts referred to above shall comprise the following:

Class One - Permanent Capital Accounts.

Class Two - Fixed Assets Accounts.

Class Three - Inventory and Work in Progress Accounts.

Class Four - Third-Party Accounts.

Class Five - Financial Accounts.

Class Six - Charges Accounts.

Class Seven - Revenues Accounts.

Class Eight - Special Accounts.

Class Nine - Analytical Operating Accounts.

- Costs Attached to this Decision:

- The Accounting Framework .... (Annex No. 1)

- The List of Accounts .... (Annex No. 2)

- The Statement of Transition from the Accounting Result to the Tax Result .... (Annex No. 3)

- Implementing Provisions .... (Annex No. 4).

Accounts shall be recorded in the books in Lebanese currency; however, some of them may be recorded in another currency provided that their balances are converted into Lebanese currency upon closing the accounts of the financial period, in accordance with the exchange rate determined by the Bank of Lebanon on the date of closing.

If the items of the accounts listed in the General Accounting Plan are not sufficient to record the details of all operations, the enterprise may allocate additional subdivisions to these accounts.

However, if the details of certain accounts provided for in the Plan exceed the need of the enterprise, they may be grouped into a sub-account within the same classification, provided that this abbreviation does not hinder the operation of directly obtaining the financial statements.

In application of the provisions of Articles 2, 19 and 20 of Decree No. 4665 dated 26/12/1981.

A - Each of the following enterprises shall be subject to the obligation of submitting the detailed financial statements set out in Annexes 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the aforementioned Decree:

- Joint-stock companies without exception and companies subject to the system of statutory auditors.

- Other companies and sole proprietorships whose annual turnover exceeds two hundred and fifty million Lebanese pounds or that employ more than twenty-five employees.

B - Enterprises subject to assessment on the basis of actual profit - except for the enterprises set out in the preceding paragraph above - may use the abridged forms to submit the statements mentioned in Annex No. 5 of the aforementioned Decree, provided that they attach thereto the supplementary statements (Annex No. 3 of the Decree)

insofar as the contents of these statements apply to them, and these enterprises shall be exempted from submitting the special statement on the activities of the enterprise (Document Five of Annex No. 3 mentioned above) and the financing table of the financial period (Annex No. 4 of the Decree).

C - Enterprises subject to assessment on the basis of lump-sum profit, as well as other enterprises not mentioned in the two preceding paragraphs of this Article, may suffice with keeping cash-basis accounting consisting mandatorily of a journal in which receipts and expenditures are entered and of a register of fixed assets in accordance with the forms set out in Annex No. 6 of the aforementioned Decree, subject to any provisions that may be contained in other laws.

In the following special cases:

1- Assets acquired by the enterprise by way of barter for other assets shall be recorded in accordance with the certain market value of either of them.

2- Assets for the financing of which the enterprise has obtained subsidies shall be recorded in accordance with the cost of their acquisition or the cost of their production.

3- Assets acquired by the enterprise in consideration of a life annuity payment shall be recorded in accordance with the agreed value, and failing that, at their estimated value.

Items of assets and liabilities the value of which is affected by fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates shall be subject to valuation in the following manner:

First: Fixed assets:

Fixed assets located abroad shall be recorded at the cost of acquisition thereof.

Where such cost is denominated in a foreign currency, its value shall be converted into Lebanese currency at the prevailing exchange rate on the date of occurrence of the transaction.

The value in Lebanese currency shall be considered the basis for calculating depreciation and provisions for price decline, where necessary.

In all cases, the profit resulting from the change in foreign currency exchange rates shall not be considered realised, nor the loss arising therefrom finally incurred, except upon the exit of the fixed asset from the ownership of the enterprise, whereupon the result of such transaction shall be recorded within the relevant financial charges or revenues account.

Second: Receivables and payables:

As Paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 were amended pursuant to Decision 4779 dated 14/9/93.

1 - Upon the closing of accounts, current receivables and payables in foreign currencies, including short-, medium- and long-term credit loans, credit current accounts with banks and partners' credit accounts, shall be converted into their equivalent in Lebanese currency in accordance with the latest exchange rate.

2- Where the application of the exchange rate on the date of closing of accounts leads to the emergence of differences in the value previously calculated for receivables and payables in Lebanese currency, such differences shall be recorded in the results account for accounting and tax purposes.

3- Where there are short-, medium- or long-term liabilities in foreign currencies allocated for the purchase of a fixed asset, the valuation difference pertaining thereto shall be considered a cost on this fixed term, provided it is verified that these liabilities allocated to the fixed asset are actually in foreign currency and result exclusively from the acquisition of the fixed asset.

4- Paragraph 4 was repealed and was not replaced by another text pursuant to Decision 4779 dated 14/9/93.

5- The method by which exchange differences were calculated shall be stated in the supplementary notes, and the enterprise shall justify any subsequent change it introduces to the method of calculating such differences.

Third: Equity participation securities, other immobilised securities, investment securities.

Securities denominated in foreign currency and quoted only abroad shall have their value converted into Lebanese currency in accordance with the prevailing exchange rate on the date of acquisition of each of them.

Fourth: Inventory of goods:

At the end of the financial year, the value of the inventory of goods located abroad shall be converted into Lebanese currency by adopting the weighted average exchange rate method for each commodity, material or product on the date of purchase or entry into the warehouses. The enterprise may use another valuation method if difficulty appears in applying the average price method, within the limits that do not affect the results. The type of method adopted shall be indicated in the annexed supplementary statement. The enterprise shall establish a provision for decline in prices of goods if the current value of the inventory on the date of stocktaking in accordance with the prevailing exchange rate on that day is less than its book value.

Fifth: Cash and cash equivalents:

Available foreign currencies and liabilities that have fallen due upon the closing of accounts shall be converted into Lebanese currency in accordance with the latest exchange rate. Realised conversion differences shall be entered within the financial year results account.

1- For the purpose of applying the provisions of Article 18 of Decree No. 4665 dated 26/12/1981, any contract relating to the production of a set of goods or services the completion of which requires a period exceeding twelve months shall be considered a long-term contract.

Long-term contracts for which invoices may be issued for the services completed thereunder as at the date of closing of accounts shall not fall within this category.

2- Upon the closing of accounts, the revenues resulting from the executed works or rendered services shall be added to the turnover of the enterprise, and, correspondingly, the financial year shall be charged with the value of the expenses incurred for the progress of the works or services executed during the same year.

The provisions of Article 21 of Decree No. 4665 dated 26/12/981 shall be applied in accordance with the following:

1- The technique of preparing consolidated accounts requires replacing the value of the participating securities appearing in the balance sheet of one of the companies with a share equivalent thereto of the equity of the subsidiary or associated company:

a- Either by including in the balance sheet and the income statement of the parent company each item of the corresponding items in the subsidiary or associated company, which is known as full consolidation on a line-by-line basis. Exceptionally, these items may be taken in accordance with the percentage of the share of capital belonging to the parent company in the subsidiary or associated company, which is known as proportional consolidation.

b - Or by adopting the method of calculating the value of the equity belonging to the parent company. This is effected by replacing the net book value of the participating shares with the corresponding share in the net position of the subsidiary or associated company, which is known as consolidation on the basis of the net equity of the parent company. Subsidiary companies shall be subject to the full consolidation method; however, the method of consolidation on the basis of net equity may be applied to them in each of the following two cases:

- Where the activity of the subsidiary company differs to a large degree from the activity of the rest of the companies of the group, such that presenting its financial positions by means of separate statements, annexed to the consolidated financial statements, provides clearer information.

- Where the subsidiary company operates under strict and permanent restrictions on the transfer of funds, which weakens the control of the parent company over it. Associated companies shall also be subject to the method of consolidation on the basis of net equity. As for companies shared between several groups, they shall be subject to the proportional consolidation method.

2- Upon preparing the first consolidated accounts, any excess resulting from the lower purchase value of the participating securities in relation to the value of the share equivalent thereto in the equity of the subsidiary or associated company shall be considered as a "difference resulting from the first consolidation of accounts". This difference may be considered as goodwill.

3- The accounts being consolidated shall, in principle, be drawn up at a single date. The consolidation must also cover the accounts pertaining to the same financial year.

4- Uniform valuation rules shall be applied to the annual accounts included in the consolidated accounts. Any change or modification occurring to this valuation method must be indicated in the annexed statements, together with a statement of the necessary justifications and the effect thereof on the consolidated balance sheet and result. Any adjustments of a tax origin shall be excluded from the balance sheets and income statements of the companies, and the tax adjustments and their repercussions on the consolidated accounts shall be shown in the supplementary annexes.

5- The method followed in converting the items of the balance sheets and accounts of foreign companies into Lebanese currency shall be stated in the supplementary annexes. The method followed may not be modified from one year to another except in exceptional cases that are justified.

6- Transactions carried out between the companies whose accounts are being consolidated shall be excluded from the consolidated accounts.

7- The consolidated turnover shall consist of the following:

a - Sales carried out with third parties, realised by the companies whose accounts are consolidated in accordance with the full consolidation method, and transactions carried out between the companies of the same group shall be excluded from the sales.

b - The share of the parent company in the value of sales realised by the companies whose accounts are consolidated in accordance with the proportional consolidation method.

8- The consolidated financial statements shall consist of the following:

a - The consolidated balance sheet drawn up in accordance with the specifications of the General Accounting Plan, with the addition of the special items required by the consolidation of accounts.

b - The consolidated income statement drawn up in accordance with the model of the General Accounting Plan, with the addition of the special items required by the consolidation of accounts.

c- The supplementary annexes necessary to explain and facilitate the reading of the financial statements.

d- The consolidated financing table drawn up in accordance with the financing table of the company, with the making of the adjustments required by the consolidation of accounts.

Accounts of Class 9 relating to analytical accounting shall not have a mandatory character, and enterprises may resort to these accounts out of a desire to develop their management and evaluate certain account centres in their general accounting.
This Decision shall be published and notified where needed.

The Directorate General of Cooperatives may stay the execution of any resolution adopted by the General Assembly, the Board of Directors, or the Supervisory Committee in which it finds a violation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree, the decrees issued in implementation thereof, the articles of association, the internal by-laws, or any other law in force.

The management of the Fund shall have the right to appeal against such decision before the State Council within a period of one month from the date of notification thereof, and such appeal shall not stay the execution of the decision unless the State Council decides to stay execution.

The accounts of the Fund must be audited at least once a year by an auditor appointed by the Fund or by the General Union of Mutual Funds, whose nomination is approved by the Directorate General of Cooperatives.

The said auditor shall have the right to examine all the books, papers, and entries of the Fund and to audit its accounts, and the officials of the Fund must facilitate his task.

The auditors shall submit their reports to the Board of Directors and to the Directorate General of Cooperatives so that the necessary measures and actions may be taken in light of the findings thereof.

Assigned employees of the Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives - Directorate General of Cooperatives - shall have the right at any time to inspect all documents, registers, papers, and minutes of meetings of the bodies of the Fund and to audit the same.

A mutual fund shall be dissolved and liquidated by a resolution of the Extraordinary General Assembly at any time and for any reason which the latter deems to warrant dissolution.

A mutual fund shall also be dissolved and liquidated by a decision of the Minister of Housing and Cooperatives upon the proposal of the Director General of Cooperatives for the reasons and in the cases provided for in Article 49 of the Law on Cooperative Associations put into force by Decree No. 17199 dated 18/8/8/1964, as amended by Article 18 of the Law put into force by Decree No. 3508 dated 29/6/1972.

The authority that decides the dissolution is the one that appoints the liquidator or liquidators and determines their powers and their remuneration, and it holds the right to dismiss and replace them whenever it wishes.

The Directorate General of Cooperatives may name its own employees as liquidators in cases where it sees no grounds to have recourse to others, without their being entitled to any compensation out of the liquidation funds.

The final liquidation account shall be certified by the Directorate General of Cooperatives and published in the Official Gazette, and this account shall become final if no objection is lodged against it before the competent courts within two months from the date of publication.
The powers of the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Committee, and the General Assembly shall pass to the liquidator or liquidators immediately upon the issuance of the dissolution decision.
The rules, principles, and procedures determined by the articles of association drawn up in accordance with Article 12 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the liquidation operations.

From the moment of its issuance, the dissolution decision shall stop the running of interest on debts owed by the Fund in favour of members or third parties and shall cause unmatured debts to fall due.

Following the issuance of the dissolution decision, creditors must apply to the liquidator and prove their debts before him.
Mutual funds and their unions shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Article 58, as amended, of the Law on Cooperative Associations put into force by Decree No. 17199 dated 18/8/1964.

The penalties provided for in Articles 59, 60, and 61 of the Law on Cooperative Associations put into force by Decree No. 17199 dated 18/8/964 shall be imposed upon persons who commit the acts provided for therein in relation to mutual funds.

Mutual funds may establish among themselves a general national union or regional or specialized unions aimed at spreading, developing, defending, and representing the mutualist movement, training its members, and auditing their accounts, or for the purpose of carrying out acts and operations conducive to achieving the objectives set forth in the by-laws of their members.

The provisions of this Legislative Decree and the decrees issued in execution thereof shall apply to unions of mutual funds, and the latter shall operate in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association drawn up pursuant to Article 12 of this Legislative Decree.

The provisions of this Legislative Decree shall apply to mutual funds existing prior to its entry into force, and they must, without this necessitating their liquidation, amend their by-laws and regularize their status in conformity with its provisions within a period of two years from the date of publication of this Legislative Decree in the Official Gazette, failing which they shall be dissolved and liquidated by a decision of the Directorate General of Cooperatives.
Mutual funds and their unions may affiliate with the National Union for Cooperative Credit, benefit from the services and loans it provides, and deposit their funds with it.

Municipalities and public administrations and institutions may allocate to mutual funds and their unions operating in their areas halls and offices in the buildings that they own or occupy, as well as all possible financial and administrative assistance, in coordination and agreement with the Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives - Directorate General of Cooperatives.
Title Three of the Law on the Regulation of Insurance Bodies put into force by Decree No. 9812 dated 4/5/1968 is hereby repealed.
All texts contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Mutual aid funds are associations of persons founded upon the desire for solidarity and mutual assistance which do not seek profit, and whose object is to work in the interest of their members or their families through subscriptions paid by them, in order to achieve some or all of the following purposes:

1 - Compensation for the consequences of events and risks affecting the members or their families, whether in their person, their property, or their investments.

2 - Compensation for death, illness, and bodily accidents affecting them or affecting their families.

3 - Assisting members in cases of marriage, birth, and end of service.

4 - Encouraging education and specialisation in all its branches and providing aid, grants, and loans for this purpose to the members and their children only.

Associations and groups of persons that impose subscriptions upon their members in order to achieve one or more of the purposes specified in Article 1 above shall be deemed a mutual aid fund and shall be subject to the provisions of this Legislative Decree, with the exception of those established by a special law and with the exception of mutual aid funds in the Army - and the Internal Security Forces and General Security.
The operations of mutual aid funds may not extend to the interests of individuals other than their members and their families.

Mutual aid funds shall enjoy legal personality and shall be entitled to accept bequests, gifts, and grants, and shall also be entitled to own and invest the movable and immovable property necessary for the conduct of their operations or for the achievement of the purposes for which they were established.

They may also contract with insurance companies or with any other specialised institutions to carry out all or some of their objects or to invest their funds.

Every mutual aid fund shall have its own designation which shall mandatorily include the phrase "Mutual Aid Fund".

All agreements, contracts, correspondence, ledgers, papers, and publications of the fund must bear its full designation and its registration number at the Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives - the Directorate General of Cooperatives -.
The benefits of mutual aid funds shall not be subject to attachment or to prior assignment, even in part.
Mutual aid funds and their unions shall be established by a decision issued by the Minister of Housing and Cooperatives upon the proposal of the Director General of Cooperatives.

A special register shall be kept at the Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives - the Directorate General of Cooperatives in which mutual aid funds established in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall be registered free of any fee.

This register shall be organised, and its contents and the particulars which it must include shall be determined, by a decision of the Minister of Housing and Cooperatives upon the proposal of the Director General of Cooperatives.
The number of applicants for the founding of a mutual aid fund may not be less than fifty persons.

In addition to the active members who benefit from the benefits provided for in the by-laws in return for the subscriptions paid by them, persons who so wish may join mutual aid funds as honorary members who provide contributions, gifts, or grants without benefiting from any benefits. Minors may be members of a mutual aid fund subject to the approval of their guardians.

The conditions required for licensing the establishment and registration of mutual aid funds, as well as the procedures for submitting founding applications and the time limits for deciding upon them, the preparation, approval, and amendment of the basic and internal by-laws, the conditions of membership and affiliation and the forfeiture thereof, and the cases of expulsion from membership, shall be determined by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers.

The Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives - the Directorate General of Cooperatives shall draw up model basic by-laws the provisions of which shall be consistent with and inspired by the texts of this Legislative Decree and the decrees issued in implementation thereof.

The said Ministry shall determine the mandatory provisions of the aforementioned by-laws which mutual aid funds and their unions are obliged to adopt and abide by.

A mutual aid fund shall be managed by a board of directors the number of whose members, the qualifications they must possess, the manner of their election, and the forfeiture of their membership, as well as its powers and duties, the organisation of its work and meetings, and the term of its mandate, shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers.

The regularity of the conduct of work in the mutual aid fund shall be supervised by a supervisory committee the number of whose members, the manner of their election, and the conditions and forfeiture of their membership, as well as its powers and duties, the organisation of its work and meetings, and the term of its mandate, shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers.

The general assembly of the mutual aid fund shall be composed of all the members who have paid all the subscriptions and payments due from them provided for them of subscriptions and payments provided for in the basic by-laws.

It is the supreme authority in the fund, and its decisions duly adopted shall be binding upon all, including those present, those absent, or those abstaining from voting.

Every member in the fund shall have one vote regardless of the amount of his subscriptions and contributions.

The general assembly, the quorum, the majority, the manner of voting and representation therein, and the number, types, and powers of its meetings shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers.

A mutual aid fund shall have no share capital; rather, its financial resources shall consist of periodic subscriptions paid by the members and of aid, grants, gifts, bequests, and the proceeds of the investment of its funds.

The basic by-laws shall determine the amount of the members' subscriptions and the rates of the benefits and services from which they or their families benefit, as well as the conditions and cases in which they become due and the procedures and time limits for paying them to the beneficiaries.

The manner of constituting and using the reserve, as well as the methods of investing and using the funds available to the fund, and the procedures for drawing up and approving the annual budget and balance sheet, shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers.

The expenses of the fund must be limited to the necessary expenses and the cost required for the conduct of its operations, and no compensation or remuneration may be paid to the members of the board of directors or the supervisory committee unless the duties of these persons or of one of them require full-time or part-time dedication, and for whoever among them shall not be assigned to this work, subject to the prior approval of the general assembly, which, in order to be effective, must be coupled with the approval of the Directorate General of Cooperatives.

In the event that the fund incurs any deficit, an affiliated member may under no circumstances be required to pay more than twice the amount of his annual subscriptions in order to cover such deficit.

All financial and accounting operations of the fund shall be recorded in accounting and administrative registers and documents determined by the Directorate General of Cooperatives and initialled by it prior to their use.

Mutual aid funds may borrow from any source, and they may also lend their members the funds available to them, provided that this does not lead to a breach of their commitments and provided also that the loans are used for purposes provided for in the basic by-laws and within the limits set forth therein.

Subject to the legal provisions relating to mortgages and pledges, the debts owed to mutual aid funds and their unions by third parties and by members shall be deemed preferential debts in the event of their bankruptcy or in the event of execution against their property if the fund submits an application to join in the execution.
