Both the board of directors and the supervisory committee shall be subject to the supervision of the Directorate General of Cooperatives, which, if it detects negligence or default on the part of the board or the committee, may suspend their powers and appoint a provisional board or committee from among their members, the members of the fund, or its own employees to assume such powers; in such case, it must convene the general assembly within a period of three months at most to consider the dismissal and prosecution of all- or some of the members of the board or the committee and the election of replacements for them.

Registration shall take place at one of the ports mentioned in Article 8 on the basis of a declaration given by the owner after taking an oath before the harbour master and four witnesses. The form of the oath shall be as follows: I swear that I own the whole (or statement of the share) of the vessel of which I apply for the registration because I alone (or with my co-owners) built it at my own (or our) expense (or) because I purchased it from... pursuant to a deed dated ...

If the vessel is the property of a company, the representative of the company in that capacity shall make his declaration concerning it and take the oath as shown above. The declarant must substantiate his declaration of ownership thereof by producing all the supporting documents (such as the deed of sale, statements of account, etc...) or offer to the harbour master the hearing of witnesses (such as the building contractor, workmen, etc...) if the production of such documents or the hearing of such witnesses is necessary to prove his title.

A record of the foregoing shall be drawn up and signed by the declarant, the witnesses and the harbour master.

This record shall be posted on the special board at the registration offices, and thereafter a certified true copy of this record authenticated by the master of that port shall be sent to the other ports, which in turn shall post it on their special board upon receipt thereof.

It shall be a condition that this record state the particulars set forth in the aforementioned Article 11, and in every port the posting of the record shall be evidenced by another record signed by the master.

The registration may not be contested if a period of three months has elapsed from the date of the last posting and no claim or opposition has been made during that period; and after that date the injured party shall have only the right to bring an action for damages against the declarant.

Claims and oppositions lodged within this time limit of three months shall be received by the master of the port of registration, who shall transmit them after the expiry of this time limit to the registry of the Court of First Instance within the jurisdiction of which that port lies. The registry of the court shall in turn serve them upon the declarant through the bailiff within a time limit of fifteen days from its receipt thereof, and the declarant shall have a time limit of fifteen days to reply thereto; the president of the court shall then summon in the same manner all the litigants to a public sitting to adjudicate upon the said claims and oppositions.

A judgment rendered by the court in default shall be subject to no opposition whatsoever.

Appeal shall be the sole avenue of recourse whatever the rights in dispute may be, and resort thereto must take place within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of service of the judgment, and it shall be subject to all the rules of appeal laid down in Title Six of the Code of Civil Procedure. Retrial shall be admissible only in the cases referred to in items Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 of Article 537 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

Retrial shall be subject to the ordinary rules.

Vessels must be registered within fifteen days following their construction or purchase, and if "constructed or purchased abroad, within fifteen days following their entry into Lebanese waters. The presence of the vessel in a Lebanese port shall not be required in order to carry out the formalities of registration. A vessel purchased or constructed abroad shall be entitled, pending completion of its registration, to sail "flying the Lebanese flag under a permit granted by the representative of the Lebanese State at the place of sale and construction "on the basis of a declaration of purchase of the vessel supported by documents.

If the purchase takes place in Lebanon from an owner resident in a port other than the port of the purchaser, the latter must apply to the port of registration of the vessel for the transfer of the registration to the port of his residence, and "this transfer shall be effected after the transfer of ownership is registered on the folio of the vessel in the register book as will be set out hereinafter, and thereafter a copy of the folio "accompanied by a declaration from the former harbour master indicating the necessity of the transfer by reason of the change of residence shall be sent to the new port of registration.

A folio shall be opened for the vessel in the register of the new port of registration, and this folio shall bear a number corresponding to its place in the register, and the entries set forth in the folio shall be transcribed onto it

In the register of the former port the folio of this vessel shall be cancelled

The owner or co-owner of a Lebanese vessel who fails to perform the duty of registering it in accordance with the provisions of this Article shall be punished with imprisonment from two days to ten days and a fine from 25 to "500 Lebanese pounds, or with either of these two penalties, unless he proves that force majeure prevented "the carrying out of the registration.

If the vessel is sold to a foreigner, or if it is captured by the enemy, or if it is burned or perishes in any manner whatsoever, the owner in whose name it is registered must return its certificate of ownership to the office of the port of registration so that it and the folio of the register relating to the vessel may be cancelled.

This certificate must be returned within a time limit of fifteen days if the loss or sale took place in Lebanese waters, and if it took place abroad, within a time limit of three months.

Every contravention of these provisions shall render the owner of the vessel and its master liable to a penalty of imprisonment from two days to ten days and to a fine from 25 to 500 Lebanese pounds, or to either of these two penalties. In addition thereto, the vessel may be seized if seizure is possible.

Every unregistered Lebanese vessel which sails and is not proceeding from the port of its construction or sale to the port of its registration shall be detained at the first Lebanese port it reaches. If it is apprehended at sea, it shall be conducted to the nearest Lebanese port, where the harbour master shall seize it and draw up a record thereof. This record shall be transmitted to the competent courts and a copy thereof shall be sent to the Minister of Public Works.

If an intention on the part of the master to evade the formalities of registration for a correctional or criminal purpose is established, the court shall order the confiscation and sale of the seized vessel.

The proceeds of the sale shall be added to the revenues of the office of the port to which the registration of the vessel pertains, and a copy of the judgment shall be sent to the Minister of Public Works. In addition thereto, the master shall be liable to a penalty of imprisonment from three months to two years and to a fine ranging between 25 and 500 Lebanese pounds.

If, however, it is established that the matter involves nothing more than negligence or inadvertence, both the master of the vessel and its owner shall be liable to a fine ranging between 25 and 300 Lebanese pounds.

Every agreement and every contract, whether for valuable consideration or gratuitous, and every judgment having acquired the force of res judicata, and in general every act having as its object the creation, conveyance, declaration, modification or extinguishment of a real right encumbering a registered vessel shall have no effect even between the contracting parties until after its registration in the register book.

The right to register real rights encumbering vessels shall be acquired by virtue of the agreement, contracts, judgments or acts mentioned in the preceding paragraph. The obligation to deliver a vessel shall include the obligation to convey it in the register book.

Conveyance may be ordered judicially if one of the contracting parties refuses to perform his obligation voluntarily, without prejudice to the right of the injured party to damages, in particular if the conveyance of the vessel has been made to a third party.

Whoever acquires a right in a registered vessel on the basis of the entries in the register book and the graduations thereof shall be confirmed in his right.

However, a third party who, prior to acquiring a right in the vessel, had knowledge of defects or grounds for cancellation or deprivation may not invoke the force of the entries in the register book.

In all cases, the injured party shall be entitled to bring a personal action for damages against the person who caused the injury.

A person injured by reason of a registration, amendment or striking off effected without lawful cause may request the cancellation or amendment of those matters. If the cancellation or striking off does not take place by consent of both parties, a judicial decision must be obtained.

As for minor clerical errors, such as a discrepancy between the entries on the folio of the register book and the annotations in the journal book or the documents produced in support of the registration, the harbour master shall have the right to rectify them ex officio.

If an objection is made by one of the interested parties, the harbour master shall request the local justice of the peace to effect the rectification after noting on the folio the objection and the request for rectification.

The cancellation or rectification shall not be opposable to a third party who has previously registered his rights in good faith prior to the cancellation, the rectification or the registration of the objection.

Registration shall be effected pursuant to the declaration of the owner of the vessel or of the assignee of a right therein and the acceptance of the person in whose favour the registration is effected. Both the declaration and the acceptance shall take place before the harbour master of the port of registration, who shall draw up a record thereof, and they may take place before a notary public by an authentic instrument notified to the harbour master. The registration shall not be deemed final unless approved by the competent departments in the Ministry of Public Works. The declaration and the acceptance shall be required to contain:

1- A designation of the vessel covered by the registration by the number of the folio of the register.

2- The identity of the owner or the holder of the assigned right and of the beneficiary of the intended registration,

3- A statement of the nature of the right intended for registration,

4- A statement of the mode of purchase and the price, where applicable,

5- And, where applicable as well, a statement of the special provisions included in the agreement (the amount of the creditor's debt - the rate of interest - the commission - the money or currency stipulated and the manner of payment before maturity) or the restriction on the right of disposal or the annotations requested to be registered together with a statement of the principal right.

No declaration shall be required if the applicant relies on the law, or on a judgment that has acquired the force of res judicata, or on an instrument that confers the right of registration by operation of law.

The harbour master or the notary public who receives the instrument shall verify, on his own responsibility, the identity and capacity of the applicants. Such verification shall be mentioned in the record of proceedings or in the instrument.

As regards instruments executed abroad, the identity of the contracting parties shall be deemed verified if the signatures subscribed at the foot of the instruments produced have been authenticated, containing the annotations and certifications required by the laws in force, under pain of nullity.

If the contracting parties do not know how to sign or read, or are unable to do so, the acknowledgment of the contents of the record shall take place before the harbour master or the notary public in the presence of two witnesses enjoying civil capacity and able to sign.

The harbour master or the notary public shall certify the acknowledgment of the contents of the record of proceedings or the instrument and shall sign it together with the witnesses. If the harbour master or the notary public does not know the names of the contracting parties, their personal status or their domicile, these must be verified by two witnesses who know them and who fulfil the aforementioned conditions.

In all cases, the harbour master and the notary public must certify his acquaintance with the witnesses at the foot of the declaration.

The harbour master shall keep a daily register in which he shall enter, by consecutive numbers and in succession, the declarations and documents submitted to him. He shall deliver to the applicant an acknowledgment of receipt stating the number of the daily register in which his declaration is registered and the number and date of registration in that register. This date of registration shall determine the rank of priority.

If all the applications relating to a single vessel are submitted on the same day, the hour at which the application is lodged shall determine the rank of priority of the rights encumbering that vessel.

If several applications relating to a single vessel are submitted at the same time, that fact shall be mentioned in the daily register and the rights shall be registered as ranking concurrently.

Any person claiming a right in a registered vessel may apply for a provisional entry to preserve his right temporarily, and the application for a provisional entry must always be accompanied by an order from the president of the court of first instance having jurisdiction over the home port of the vessel, and the date of the provisional entry shall determine the rank for the subsequent registration of the right.

The effect of the provisional entry shall lapse upon the expiry of a period of one month.

This entry shall be struck off ex officio if no judicial action mentioned in the register book is brought within this period.

Registration and provisional entries may be struck off pursuant to any instrument or any judgment having acquired the force of res judicata which establishes, as against every party having an interest in a right duly published, the non-existence of the right to which the registration or provisional entry relates or the extinction of that right.

The provisions of Articles 21 to 27 relating to registration shall apply to striking off, save that the record of proceedings or the instrument of striking off must state:

1) The designation of the real folio of the vessel which the striking off is to cover.

2) A statement of the registration or provisional entry.

3) A statement of the ground for striking off or the instrument evidencing it.

The striking off shall be entered on the folio of the vessel, and the harbour master shall date and sign it under pain of cancellation.

The signature of the harbour master shall be accompanied by the official seal of the port of registration, and the grounds for the striking off shall be stated on the aforementioned folio.

Applications for the enforcement of an attachment levied upon a vessel and for the enforcement of a judgment determining a dispute over it shall be notified through the execution office to the harbour master of the port of registration of the vessel so that they may be registered on the folio of that vessel. Real actions must also be registered in the register book after notification of the writ of summons thereof to the harbour master of the port of registration, duly endorsed by the clerk of the court to which such writ of summons is submitted.

Notification shall be effected at the diligence of the interested party.

If a vessel is encumbered with a right in rem created inter vivos and an application for its registration is made after the death of the grantor thereof, such application may be granted upon production of a document permitting registration or an application signed by the grantor of the right, provided that his signature is authenticated in both cases.

If the signature is not authenticated and there is an objection from the heirs, the registration shall be decided by the judicial authority.

Rights in rem encumbering a vessel and arising from inheritance cannot be registered in the name of the applicants for registration, where the inheritance is intestate and not accompanied by a will, unless they produce, in addition to proof of the death of their decedent, legal certificates establishing the identity of each of them and his right to the inheritance.

Where, however, the inheritance is instituted pursuant to a will, the applicant shall produce the instrument of the will or the decision issued by the judicial authority competent for the execution of the will.

Every annotation made in the register book must, under pain of nullity, be accompanied by the signature of the harbour master. Such signature shall be accompanied by the seal of the port of registration.

The owner of the vessel alone, to the exclusion of any other person, shall be entitled to a full copy of the folio of his vessel. Such copy shall be nominative and the harbour master shall confer upon it authentic form by affixing his signature thereto and the seal of the port of registration, and the other holders of rights, such as mortgagees, shall receive only a certificate of the entry of their right.

Whenever an entry is registered on the folio, that entry must be registered on the copy thereof (the title deed). The harbour master shall refuse registration if this copy is not produced and the application relates to a right the creation of which presupposes the consent of the owner whose ownership is registered.

In all other cases, the harbour master shall effect the registration and notify it to the holder of the registered right.

No other registration may be requested with the consent of the holder of this rightuntil the conformity between the folio and the title deed has been completed. The harbour master shall certify the conformity of the copy with the folio whenever requested to do so.

If the harbour master establishes a new folio, he shall cancel the previous folio by signing the cancellation mark and affixing the seal of the port on all its pages. He shall cancel in the same manner the title deed and preserve it among his records.

The harbour master shall deliver to every interested party, upon his request, a general or special statement of the annotations registered in the register book and a copy or abstract of the documents.

If the title deed or the certificate of registration is lost or destroyed, the head of the port of registration shall replace them in the same manner to which the head of the land registry office resorts pursuant to Articles 92 to 94 of Decision No. 188 issued on 15 March of the year 1926 for replacing what is lost or destroyed of a title deed or a certificate of registration pertaining to any immovable property.

And the rules prescribed in the said articles shall apply in that case just as in this one.

The head of the port of registration shall be personally liable for damage resulting:

1) From his omission in the registers of a provisional entry, a registration, or a striking off duly requested.

2) From his omission in the certificates of registration or extracts signed by him of a provisional entry or entries, a registration, or a striking off entered in the register.

3) From a violation of the rules of procedure and the nullity of the provisional entries, the registration, or the striking off entered in the register.

4) From omissions and violations of the rules of procedure in the declarations and official reports that he accepts.

This is in addition to the legal provisions in force pertaining to the liability of public officials.

In all the cases mentioned above, the State shall be financially liable in the event of the inability of its officers to pay.

Every vessel registered in a Lebanese port must be in possession of the following papers in official printed forms:

A- Vessels intended for navigation on the high seas and coastal vessels:

1) The maritime title deed from the office of the port of registration within the jurisdiction of which the real or elected domicile of the owner of the vessel is located.

2) The crew list containing the latest changes occurring to the crew of the vessel and signed at the last port of call of the vessel by the head of the port or by the Consul of Lebanon abroad if present, and otherwise by the authority representing him.

3) The navigation licence for the current year. And for a passenger transport vessel: the safety certificate.

4) For each member of the crew, including the skipper or the master: a seaman's licence for the current year.

5) The clearance for departure from the head of the port.

6) The cargo manifest signed by the customs office at the last port of call of the vessel.

7) A bill of health signed by the quarantine office at the last port of call of the vessel.

8) A receipt for payment of port and lighthouse dues from the competent departments at the last port of call of the vessel.

B - For fishing vessels:

1) The maritime title deed.

2) The crew list.

3) The navigation licence for the current year.

4) The fishing licence for the current year from the port of registration of the vessel.

5) For each individual of the crew: a fisherman seaman's licence for the current year.

C- For pleasure vessels:

1) The maritime title deed.

2) The crew list in the event that seamen are employed on the vessel.

3) The navigation licence for the current year.
These papers must be produced upon every demand from the authorities charged with the supervision of navigation or fishing.

Article 43: his papers to the office of the port within a time limit of 24 hours commencing from the hour of his arrival at the port, under penalty of a fine from twenty-five to five hundred pounds for each period of delay of twenty-four hours.

The papers of the vessel shall be returned to the skipper or to the master upon the departure of his vessel after verification of the completion of the port and customs formalities. The provisions of this Article shall likewise apply to pleasure vessels and fishing vessels if their net tonnage is twenty-five tons and above.

Every vessel registered in a Lebanese port that is inspected at sea and is found not to be in possession of the legal papers set forth above shall be conducted to the nearest Lebanese port, where the port officer or its head shall detain it.

An official report thereof shall be drawn up, and this official report shall be referred to the competent courts.

If the intent to evade the provisions of this Law for a correctional or criminal purpose is established against the master or the skipper of the vessel, the master or the skipper of the vessel shall be sentenced to imprisonment from three months to two years and to a fine from 20 to 200 pounds, and the court shall order the confiscation of the detained vessel and its sale. The price of the sale shall be added to the revenues of the port office that effected the seizure.

If, however, it is established that there is nothing in the matter other than negligence or oversight, the master or the skipper of the vessel shall be sentenced to imprisonment from two days to ten days and to a fine from five pounds to one hundred pounds, or to one of these two penalties.

Every vessel in possession of forged papers or the papers of another vessel shall be seized and sold in accordance with the provisions of Article 45, and the skipper or the master shall be sentenced to the penalty provided for in the same Article.

There shall be treated on the same footing as the vessel's papers, with respect to the penalties to which the master or the skipper is exposed pursuant to the aforesaid Article 45, the identity papers that passengers are required to possess together with the signature of the General Security authorising embarkation on the vessel.

The following debts alone are privileged, and the rank of their privilege shall be determined according to the order in which they are listed:

1) Judicial costs and expenses paid in preserving the price in the general interest of the creditors

- Tonnage dues, lighthouse and port dues, and other public dues and charges of the same kind

- Pilotage dues and the expenses of custody and maintenance since the entry of the vessel into the last port.

2) Debts arising from the contract of engagement of the master, the crew, and the other persons employed on board the vessel.

3) The remuneration due for salvage and assistance, and for the contribution of the vessel in general average.

4) Compensation for collision and other casualties of navigation, and for damage caused to ports, docks, and navigable waterways, and compensation for personal injury to passengers and crew, and for loss of or damage to cargo and baggage.

5) Debts resulting from contracts entered into or operations carried out by the master away from the home port of the vessel by virtue of his statutory powers for an actual need required for the preservation of the vessel or the continuation of the voyage, whether the master is the owner of the vessel or not and whether the debt is owed to him or to victuallers, repairers, lenders, or other contracting parties.

6) Damages due to the charterers of the vessel.

7) The total insurance premiums contracted on the hull, tackle, and apparel of the vessel due for the last insured voyage where the insurance was contracted for the voyage, or for the last insured period where the insurance was contracted for a fixed term, provided that this total shall not in either case exceed the premiums for one year.

Privileged creditors must be ranked by voyage. The privileged debts of the last voyage, whatever their rank, shall have priority over the debts of previous voyages. However, debts resulting from a single contract for the engagement of seamen shall always be deemed debts of the last voyage even if they relate to a previous voyage.

Debts relating to a single voyage shall be ranked in the order prescribed in Article 48.

Debts of the same rank relating to the same voyage shall rank concurrently.

Every remuneration for assistance and debts incurred for the supply of provisions and repairs shall be ranked in the inverse order of the dates on which they arose.
Debts relating to a single maritime casualty shall be deemed to have arisen at the same time.
The privileges prescribed in the preceding Articles shall be established as from the constitution of the debt. They shall not be subject to any formality or to any special condition of proof.

Mortgage creditors whose debt is registered on the vessel shall rank in the order of their registration immediately after the privileged creditors mentioned in items No. 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 of Article 48.

The privileges shall attach to the vessel, to the freight of the voyage during which the privileged debt arose, and to the accessories of the vessel and its freight earned since the commencement of the voyage.

However, the privilege prescribed in Article 48, in its second paragraph, shall attach to the total freight of the vessel due for all the voyages carried out during the course of the same contract of engagement.

The following shall be deemed accessories of the vessel and its freight for the purpose of the application of liens:

1) Compensation payable to the owner of the vessel for material damage sustained by his vessel and not made good, or for loss of freight.

2) Compensation payable to the owner of the vessel for general average in so far as it constitutes either material damage sustained by his vessel and not made good, or loss of freight.

3) Remuneration payable to the owner of the vessel for assistance or salvage performed up to the end of the voyage, after deduction of the sums allotted to the master and other persons in the service of the vessel.

Passage money, and the lump sum to which the liability of shipowners may be limited, shall be assimilated to freight.

Compensation payable to the owner of the vessel under a contract of insurance, or by way of bounties, subsidies or other grants, shall not be deemed accessories of the vessel and its freight for the purpose of the application of liens.

All the liens enumerated in Article 48 shall be extinguished at the expiration of a period of one year by prescription, except the lien for claims arising out of supplies provided for in sub-paragraph 5, which shall be extinguished at the expiration of six months.

The period of prescription shall run, in the case of the lien for remuneration for assistance and salvage, from the day when the operations are terminated; in the case of the lien for indemnity for collision and other accidents and for bodily injuries, from the day when the damage was caused.

In the case of the lien for loss of or damage to cargo or baggage, it shall run from the day of the delivery of the cargo or baggage or from the date when they should have been delivered; and in the case of the lien for repairs and supplies and other cases specified in sub-paragraph 2 of Article 48, from the day when the claim originated.

In all other cases the period shall run from the enforceability of the claim. The claims of persons in the service of the vessel referred to in sub-paragraph 2 of Article 48 shall not be deemed enforceable until the end of the voyage, notwithstanding the right of such persons to demand advances or payments on account during the voyage.

The period specified above shall not apply where it has been impossible to arrest the vessel in Lebanese territorial waters, provided the creditor has his domicile or principal place of business in Lebanon, subject however to the period of prescription not exceeding three years from the time when the claim originated.

Apart from the general methods of extinction of obligations, liens shall also be extinguished:

- By judicial sale carried out in the forms prescribed in this Law.

- By any voluntary sale of the vessel under the following conditions:

That the transfer is effected in accordance with the provisions of Articles 21, 24 to 27, 33 to 35, and 37 of this Law.

That this transfer is made public by publication in the Official Gazette of the Lebanese Republic and in two daily newspapers appearing in the port of registry of the vessel, and by a notice affixed to the door of the registry office, provided that the name and domicile of the purchaser are necessarily stated in the publication and notice.

That no opposition has been served on the purchaser by the creditor within one month after the publication.

The creditor's right of preference on the purchase price shall subsist so long as the said price has not been paid, even after the expiration of this period, provided the creditor has made himself known to the purchaser before payment by a deed of opposition.

The opposition provided for in the two preceding paragraphs must be served on the creditor through the notary public.

Preferred creditors may register their lien in order to be notified of the putting up for sale of the vessel in accordance with the conditions laid down in Article 48 of this Law. Such registration shall not affect the rank of the lien.

The registration shall be entered on the sheet of the vessel in the register.

The foregoing provisions shall apply to vessels operated by a disponent owner who is not the owner thereof or by a principal charterer, except where the owner has been dispossessed by an unlawful act and when the creditor is not in good faith.
Vessels of a gross tonnage of two tons and upwards may be the object of mortgages, provided this is done by agreement of the two parties.

An agreed maritime mortgage contract must be drawn up in writing. It may be executed by an instrument under private signature.

The deed of mortgage may be made to order, in which case its negotiation shall entail the transfer of the mortgage right.

None other than the owner of the vessel or his agent holding a special proxy shall be entitled to contract a conventional mortgage on the vessel.

If the vessel has several owners, the managing owner may mortgage it for the needs of outfitting or navigation by virtue of an authorization from the majority of its owners, provided such majority holds at the same time three-fourths of the co-ownership interests. If the interests of the majority do not reach three-fourths, the co-owners may apply to the court with a view to obtaining judgment for the course most conducive to their general interest.

None of the co-owners may mortgage his undivided share in the vessel without the consent of the majority of the owners, provided such majority holds at the same time one-half of the co-ownership interests.

The mortgage must be registered in the register book in accordance with Article 21 and the following articles of this Law.

The registration of a mortgage secures, in addition to the principal, interest for two years in addition to the interest for the current year at the time of adjudication.

A mortgage contracted on a vessel or on a share therein shall extend to the whole of its hull and to the tackle, apparel, machinery and other accessories, as well as to the wreck thereof, unless otherwise agreed.

Such mortgage shall not extend to freight, nor to government bounties and subsidies. It shall, however, extend to compensation for damage, unless such compensation is applied to the repair and maintenance of the vessel.

Nor shall it extend to insurance indemnity; nevertheless, the insurance policy may contain an express delegation by the mortgage creditors of such indemnity.

Such delegation shall not be effective against the insurers unless they have accepted it or have been notified thereof.

A maritime mortgage may be contracted on a vessel under construction. In that case, the mortgage must be preceded by a declaration addressed to the harbour master within whose area the vessel is being constructed.

Such declaration shall state the approximate length of the keel of the vessel and its other dimensions, as well as its estimated tonnage; it shall also mention the place of its construction.
Where the mortgage contract is drawn up to order, its transfer shall be effected by endorsement of the certificate of registration.

Creditors holding a registered mortgage on a vessel or on a share therein may follow it into whatever hands it may pass, in order to have their claim marshalled in its order and to be paid according to the order of registration.

If the mortgage covers only a share in a vessel, the creditor may neither apply for arrest nor pursue the sale except in respect of the share assigned to him. If, however, more than one-half of the vessel is mortgaged to him, he may, after arrest, pursue the sale of the whole vessel, subject to summoning the co-owners to such sale.

Where at the sale by auction the vessel is adjudicated to one of the co-owners, or where after partition the vessel falls to his share, the mortgage shall remain after partition or sale as it was before them, even though such co-owner is not the one who contracted the mortgage on his undivided shares in the vessel. Where the sale by auction takes place before the court under the conditions laid down in Article 83 and the following articles of this Law and is adjudicated to a person who is not a co-owner, the right of creditors whose mortgage covers only a share in the vessel shall be limited to a right of preference on the portion of the price relating to the mortgaged interest.

Likewise, charges encumbering each share in the ownership of the vessel shall pass by operation of law to the share of the price representing the value of the share in the vessel.

Any person who purchases a vessel or a share therein and wishes to protect himself against the proceedings authorized by the preceding article must, after registering his purchase and before the institution of proceedings or within a period of fifteen days, serve a copy of the title deed of the vessel on all the creditors registered in this deed at the domicile elected in the original deed.

The purchaser shall declare in the same deed that he is ready to pay forthwith the debts secured by mortgage up to the value of the vessel, whether such debts are due or not.

The owner of the vessel shall not be liable except to the extent of the value of the vessel, its freight, and its accessories:

1) For compensation imposed in favour of a third party by reason of damage caused by the faults of the master, the seamen, the pilot, or any person in the service of the vessel, on land or at sea.

2) For compensation imposed by reason of damage sustained by the cargo handed over to the master for the purpose of its transport, and by all property and objects on board the vessel.

3) For obligations resulting from bills of lading.

4) For compensation imposed by reason of a fault in navigation committed during the performance of any contract.

5) For the obligation to raise the wreck of a sunken vessel or to repair damage sustained by the installations of docks, ports, or navigable waterways, and for the obligations relating thereto.

6) For remuneration for assistance and salvage.

7) For the share which he must contribute to general average.

8) For obligations arising out of contracts or acts entered into or performed by the master within his statutory powers, away from the home port of the vessel, for real needs required for the preservation of the vessel or the continuation of the voyage, provided that such needs do not result from an insufficiency or defect affecting the equipment or provisioning at the beginning of the voyage.

As regards the debts referred to in items Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, the liability resulting from the preceding provisions may not exceed the sum obtained by multiplying the number of tons of the vessel's tonnage by the official value of the ton, and such value shall be fixed by a decree issued in the week following the publication of this Law and shall be amended where necessary.

If death or injury is caused by the faults of the master, the seamen, the pilot, or one of the servants of the vessel, the liability of its owner towards the victims or their successors in title shall exceed the limit fixed in the preceding Article up to an amount equivalent to double thereof. The victims of the same accident, or their successors in title, shall participate together in the distribution of the sum imposed by way of liability.

If the victims or their successors in title are not compensated in full, they shall participate, as regards the balance, with the other creditors in the sums mentioned in the preceding Article, having regard to the liens.

The liability of the owners and operators of the vessel shall not be subject to any limitation towards the seamen.

The provisions of the first paragraph of the preceding Article relating to additional compensation shall not apply to any owner of a vessel that is not used for the carriage of passengers and the tonnage of which is less than three hundred tons. The limitation of liability prescribed in Articles 94 and 95 shall not apply:

1- To obligations arising from the faults of the owner of the vessel. However, if the master of the vessel is its owner or one of its owners, he may not invoke the limitation of liability in respect of his faults in navigation and the faults of the servants of the vessel.

2) Nor to the obligations provided for in the eighth paragraph of Article 94 where there is express consent or authorisation on the part of the owner of the vessel.

3) Nor to the obligations of the owner of the vessel arising from the employment of the seamen and the servants of the vessel.

The owner of the vessel who invokes the limitation of his liability to the value of the vessel, its freight, and its accessories must prove this value. The valuation of the vessel shall be based on its condition at the following times:

1) In the case of collision or other accidents, and as regards all debts connected therewith, even by virtue of a contract, which arise up to the arrival of the vessel at the first port it reaches after the accident, and likewise debts resulting from general average caused by the accident, the vessel shall be valuedaccording to its condition upon its arrival at the first port. If, prior to arrival at the first port, a new accident unrelated to the previous accident occurs and diminishes the value of the vessel, such diminution shall not be taken into account as regards the creditors whose debt arose from the previous accident. If the accidents occur during the stay of the vessel in one of the ports, the vessel shall be valued according to its condition while in the port and after the accident.

2) As regards debts relating to the cargo or arising from the implementation of the terms of the bill of lading, other than the cases provided for in the first paragraph of this Article, the cargo shall be valued according to the condition of the vessel at the port of destination of this cargo or at the place where the voyage is broken. If the cargo is destined for different places and the damage is attributable to a single cause, the valuation shall be effected according to the condition of the vessel at the end of the voyage.

3) In all other cases, the valuation shall be effected according to the condition of the vessel at the end of the voyage.

The various debts relating to a single casualty, and the debts which, independently of any casualty, require the valuation of the vessel in a single port, shall participate together in the sum to which the liability of the owner of the vessel extends in respect of these debts, after having regard to their rank of lien.

The freight referred to in the first paragraph of Article 94, including passage money, means a lump sum fixed for all accidents at ten per cent of the value of the vessel, whatever its type, at the beginning of the voyage, even if the vessel has earned no freight.

The accessories of the vessel referred to in Article 94 shall include:

1) Compensation caused by material damage not made good and sustained by the vessel since the beginning of the voyage.

2) And compensation caused by general average, where such general average consists of material damage not made good and sustained by the vessel since the beginning of the voyage.

However, indemnities paid or due by virtue of contracts of insurance, and bounties, financial subsidies, and other governmental subsidies, shall not be deemed to be accessories.

The tonnage of the vessel shall be determined as follows:

For steamships and other motor vessels, by their net volume plus the space occupied by the machinery or engines.

And for sailing vessels, by their net volume.
The principal charterer of the vessel and its operator who is not its owner shall benefit from the limitation of liability and from the provisions of the following Articles.

In the event of the institution of an action or the pursuit of execution for one of the causes set forth in the preceding Articles, the court shall be entitled to decide, upon the application of the owner of the vessel, to stay proceedings against property other than the vessel, its freight, and its accessories for a period sufficient to enable the sale of the vessel and the distribution of the proceeds among the creditors.

The President of the Court of First Instance, acting in his capacity as judge of urgent matters, shall rule on the amount of the security required to be furnished by the owner of the vessel in order to enable him to invoke the limitation of liability.

The owner of the vessel may at any time stay proceedings against himself by depositing the sum to which the extent of his liability reaches. The sum deposited shall be determined at the rate of exchange on the day of payment and is intended for the satisfaction of the rights of the creditors to whom the limitation of liability applies.

The distribution among the creditors shall be effected in the manner provided for in Article 794 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The operator of the vessel shall have the right to appoint and dismiss its master, subject to compensating him where necessary.

If the dismissed master is one of the owners of the vessel, he may renounce his ownership therein and demand payment of the value of his share.

The determination of this value shall be effected by technical experts appointed amicably or judicially, provided that this right of renunciation may not be exercised after the expiry of a time limit of thirty days commencing from the day on which his co-owners put him on notice; if he exercises this right within the prescribed time limit, his co-owners in the property must pay him his share within a time limit of thirty days commencing from the technical appraisal which has determined its value.

The opinion of the majority must be adopted in all matters relating to the common interest of the owners. The majority shall be determined by a share of the rights in the vessel exceeding half of its value. However, decisions falling outside the purpose of the operation of the vessel or contrary to the terms of its contract shall only be valid if taken unanimously.

Each co-owner of a vessel shall be liable only in proportion to his share in such ownership in respect of obligations which give rise to personal liability.

Moreover, he may at any time exonerate himself from the obligations resulting for him from an act of management to which he has refused to consent by abandoning his share in such joint ownership.

Such share shall be distributed among the other co-owners in proportion to the rights of each of them in the vessel.

The ship's husband entrusted by the owners of the vessel with its management and outfitting may not sell the vessel or effect insurance thereon unless they authorise him to do so by a special authorisation. However, chartering it falls within his general powers.

He shall represent the owners of the vessel before the courts in all matters relating to the outfitting and the voyage.

If the powers of the managing ship's husband have been restricted pursuant to special instructions from the owners of the vessel, such restriction may not be invoked against any third party who has contracted with him in good faith.
Every master or skipper entrusted with the management of a vessel or other craft shall be liable for damage caused to third parties by reason of fraud or fault during the performance of his duties.
The master must deliver the goods which he receives. His receipt thereof shall be proved by the bill of lading or by any other document.
The master must submit his vessel to survey in accordance with the requirements of the regulations.

The master shall form the crew of the vessel, conclude the necessary contracts and take all useful measures for the voyage. However, he may not perform these acts without the consent of the shipowner if the said shipowner or his representative happens to be present at the place where they are performed.

In all vessels, except those intended for pleasure (yachts), the master must keep a logbook, the pages of which shall be numbered and signed by the head of the port authorities. There shall be faithfully recorded in the logbook all supervening incidents, all decisions taken during the voyage, a list of the receipts and expenditure relating to the vessel, the daily observations concerning the state of the weather and the sea, a statement of the infractions committed by the persons employed on the vessel and the disciplinary penalties imposed, and the births and deaths which may occur on board the vessel.

In addition, in steamships and motor vessels, a daily engine logbook (machinery) shall be kept in which shall be recorded the quantity of fuel taken on at departure, the daily consumption of the vessel, and everything relating to the operation and servicing of the propelling machinery.

The master must have on board the vessel the papers establishing its nationality, the crew roll, the bills of lading, the charter-party, the cargo manifest (manifesto), the certificates of survey, the receipt for payment or for the provision of security to the customs, and the deed of ownership of the vessel.

The master is bound to exercise command in person and to be on board the vessel when it enters ports, roadsteads or rivers and when it leaves them.

He must not leave it during the voyage for any reason or danger whatsoever except with the agreement of its officers. In that event, he shall be bound to save the money, the ship's papers and the most valuable goods, if that is possible.

If a breach of the obligations imposed in the three preceding Articles occurs, the master shall be deemed liable for all accidents towards any third party having an interest in the vessel or in the cargo.

The master shall cease to be liable in the case of force majeure, and the burden of proving such case shall lie upon him.

The master shall be liable for all loss or damage caused to goods loaded on the first deck of the vessel, that is to say on its upper deck, unless he has obtained the consent of the shipper stated together with his signature on the bill of lading, or unless maritime usages permit such loading.

Every roofed shelter on deck, such as the crew's quarters or the like, shall be assimilated to the first deck if it is intended or fit to accommodate goods. However, this provision shall not apply in near coastal navigation.

If an urgent need arises during the voyage, the master may, after obtaining an authorisation granted in Lebanon by the President of the Court of First Instance and abroad by the Lebanese Consul, if there be one, and failing that after obtaining the approval of the local magistrate, borrow on the security of the hull of the vessel and its freight, and, if they are insufficient, on the security of the cargo as well.

If he is unable to borrow, he may, after obtaining the same authorisations, sell goods up to the amount of the necessary sum determined.

The shipowner, or the master of the vessel who represents him, must account to the owners of the goods sold for their value according to the current or estimated price for goods of the same kind and the same quantity at the place of delivery and at the time of the arrival of the vessel; and the shippers or holders of rights may oppose the pledging or sale of their goods and demand their discharge, provided that they pay the full freight therefor.

The master may not, under pain of nullity of the sale, sell the vessel without a special authorisation from its owner, unless it is legally and duly proved that the vessel is unseaworthy. In the absence of an authorisation or special instructions from the owner of the vessel, the sale shall take place by way of public auction once the unseaworthiness of the vessel has been proved as stated above.

A master who operates a vessel on the basis of being a partner in the profit arising from its cargo may not engage in any trade for his own account, save by a stipulation to the contrary.

If a breach on his part occurs in this respect, he shall be deprived of his share in the common profit and shall be liable for damages, if any have been incurred.

Upon his arrival at the port of destination or upon his entry into a port for temporary anchorage, and within a period of twenty-four hours at the most, the master must obtain thecertification of the logbook by the port authorities, and abroad by the Lebanese Consul, if there be one, and failing that by the competent maritime authorities.

If extraordinary events occur relating to the vessel, the cargo or the crew, the master must submit to the same authorities a sea protest stating the time and place of his departure, the course which he followed, the contingencies from which the crew and the vessel suffered, and all the circumstances of the voyage which ought to be set forth.

In the event of shipwreck, the survivors of the crew must attest the contents of this report.

Verification of the sea protest drawn up by the master shall be carried out either of its own motion, if the competent authority sees fit to order an inquiry to be held, or upon the request of the master or of any other person having an interest in the matter. The inquiry shall be conducted before the President of the Court of First Instance, and abroad before the Lebanese Consul, if there be one, and failing that before the competent judicial authority.

The members of the crew and the passengers shall be heard, and any other evidence shall be admitted.

Unverified reports shall not be admissible in defence of the master and shall not be valid as evidence before the courts.

Where the drawing up of a report is required, the master may not, save in a case of necessity or urgency, discharge any goods or open the hatches in the deck of the vessel until after he has submitted his sea protest.
Notwithstanding the presence of a pilot on board the vessel, and even if his presence is compulsory, the authority and liability of the master shall remain entire.
A seaman is every person employed on board a vessel to perform a sea voyage.

If the tonnage of the vessel exceeds five tuns, the contract of employment subsisting between a seaman and a shipowner or his agent shall be subject to the following provisions:

1) The clauses and conditions of the contract of maritime employment shall be entered in the crew roll. The seaman shall express his consent by affixing his signature or his fingerprint. Before the departure of the vessel, the authority in charge of navigation regulations shall inspect the entries in the crew roll in order to verify that all the seamen embarking on the vessel are employed under a contract. The conditions of the contract shall be read out and the two contracting parties shall be questioned in order to ascertain that they know its contents and accept it. The completion of this formality shall be mentioned in the margin of the roll.

2) If the contract of employment is not recorded in the crew roll, it may be proved by all means.

The following shall be stated in the contract of employment:

- Whether it is concluded for a definite period, for an indefinite period, or for a complete voyage.

- The service or function of the seaman.

- The date on which the service or function shall commence.

- The method of payment of the wages agreed upon between the contracting parties.

- The amount of the fixed wages or the basis for determining the profits.

- The date and place of conclusion of the contract.

The contract shall not be valid unless the seaman is free from any other employment.

The seaman shall report to board the vessel upon the first request of the master. Both on board the vessel and ashore, he shall be bound to obey the orders of his superiors in respect of the service of the vessel. He shall be bound to work for the salvage of the vessel and the cargo.

Neither the master nor the seaman may load any goods on the vessel for their own account except by permission of its operator.

If a violation occurs in this respect, the offenders shall be bound to pay for their goods the highest freight stipulated at the place and date of loading, in addition to the damages that may be due from them. The master may order the jettison of the goods into the sea if their loading was unlawful and if they are of a nature to threaten the safety of the vessel or to lead to the payment of fines or expenses.

The operator of the vessel shall employ only Lebanese seamen for coastal navigation from one Lebanese port to another Lebanese port and for fishing on the Lebanese coasts.

As for large vessels intended for long-range voyages provided for in paragraph 2 of the amended Article 2 and vessels intended for international coastal navigation, the Administration reserves the right to oblige their owner to employ up to one-fifth of Lebanese seamen or to train in navigation a number of persons equivalent to this proportion under conditions determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Works.

As for technical workers, the operator of the vessel may employ, in case of necessity, foreign masters, officers, or mechanical workers or (machinists) who prove that they hold licences or certificates at least equivalent to the licences and certificates required by the departments of the Ministry of Public Works from Lebanese masters, officers, or mechanical workers or (machinists).

Neither the operator of the vessel nor the master may employ cabin boys who have not completed the fifteenth year of their age.

Nor may they employ cabin boys who have not attained the legal age of majority unless they have obtained in writing the consent of their parents or guardian.

It is required in a contract of employment which provides that the whole or part of the seaman's wages shall consist of a share of the vessel's freight or of the profit that it specify the expenses intended to be deducted from the gross profit in order to obtain the net profit.

Compensation paid to the vessel by reason of the cancellation, shortening, or extension of the voyage, or by reason of the loss of profit or of the vessel's freight, shall be deemed to be included in the gross profit.

This provision shall not apply to insurance indemnities unless the seaman has contributed to the payment of the premiums since the commencement of the voyage.

Bounties and other government subsidies shall not be included in the funds subject to division unless there is an agreement to the contrary.
In the event of the extension or shortening of the voyage, the seamen shall receive wages in proportion to the duration of their actual service if their wages are paid to them by the month.

If the wages of the seamen are linked to the voyage, they shall not be subject to any reduction by reason of the intentional shortening of the voyage, whatever the cause of such shortening.

If the voyage is intentionally extended or postponed, the wages shall be increased in proportion to the duration of the extension or postponement.

If the seamen are employed on a share of the profit or of the vessel's freight, they shall not be entitled to any compensation by reason of the postponement, extension, or shortening of the voyage due to force majeure.

If the cause is the act of a third party or the act of the shippers, the seamen shall be entitled to a share of the damages awarded to the vessel.

If this cause is attributable to the act of the operator of the vessel or the master and the seamen have suffered damage, they shall be entitled, in addition to their share in the profit realised, to compensation determined according to the circumstances of the case.

Disputes raised concerning the payment of wages, and every dispute in general occurring between the master or operator of the vessel and the seamen, shall be submitted with a view to attempting a settlement thereof to the maritime authority entrusted with the regulation of navigation at the port of registry of the vessel or at the port of discharge.

If this authority is unable to reconcile the contracting parties, it shall draw up a record in which it shall enter the disputes raised by the two contracting parties and the amounts paid.

This record shall be transmitted at its request to the competent judge. No action shall be entertained before the courts unless this settlement procedure has been completed.

Every advance on wages shall be entered in the crew list if received by the seaman before departure, and in the logbook if received by him during the voyage.

The seaman shall affix his signature or his fingerprint. Every advance that does not fulfil these conditions shall not be taken into consideration. The total advances may not exceed one-fifth of the wages due at the time the advance is requested.
Advances may be allotted to the seaman's wife, his children, and his ascendants, to the exclusion of all others.

Unallotted advances, payments on account, and employment bonuses shall not be refunded to the operator of the vessel unless the termination of the employment occurs by the act of the seaman. Their refund shall not exempt from disciplinary penalties and compensation for damages.

Allotted advances shall in no case be subject to refund notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary.

The wages and profits of seamen shall not be subject to attachment and may not be assigned except for the following causes and up to the following amounts:

1) Up to one-fourth thereof:

By reason of a debt to the State or to provident funds.

And by reason of debts arising from the supply of food, clothing, or lodging.

And by reason of a debt to the operator of the vessel resulting from an undue payment occurring upon the settlement of previous wages, or resulting from an undue advance or payment, or damages.

2) And up to their second fourth by reason of a debt due in execution of a final judgment.

No seaman may be employed except after being subjected to a medical examination carried out by a physician appointed by the port authorities. The employment of seamen afflicted with contagious diseases is prohibited and shall have no effect.

The completion of this formality, together with the medical permit to board the vessel, shall be mentioned in the crew list under penalty of a fine ranging between 25 and 200 L.L., which may be doubled in the event of recurrence.

If a seaman is injured in the service of the vessel, his treatment shall be at the expense of the vessel. The same shall apply to one who falls ill after the vessel has left its port of registry. However, if insubordination, an inexcusable fault, or drunkenness is the cause or origin of the injury or illness, or if it is a matter of a hereditary disease such as insanity and epilepsy or a disease of syphilitic origin, the operator of the vessel shall advance the expenses of treatment, provided that he deducts them from the account of the injured or sick seaman.
The expenses of treatment shall cease to be due after the injury or illness becomes incurable.

A seaman who is injured or falls ill in the service of the vessel shall be entitled to his wages for as long as he remains on board. After he is landed ashore, he shall be entitled to an allowance equivalent in amount to the seaman's wages for a period of four months at most.

If his landing ashore takes place in a foreign country, a sum equivalent to the wages of the four months shall be deposited with the Lebanese consul or his representative.
The right to wages and to the allowance is a personal right; it shall lapse upon death, recovery, or when the incurability of the disease is established.

If the seaman's injury or illness is caused by insubordination or drunkenness, or originates from heredity or syphilis, the seaman shall be entitled to medical treatment and food for as long as he remains on board the vessel, and he shall have no right to wages or to the allowance.
If the seaman dies as a result of an illness or injury while in the service of the vessel, his burial expenses shall be borne by the vessel whatever the case may be.
The provisions of the Workmen's Compensation Law shall apply in respect of permanent disability befalling seamen while in the service of the vessel.

The shipowner shall repatriate the seamen who are transferred ashore during the voyage for any reason whatsoever, save those of them who were transferred ashore for a lawful cause pursuant to the order of the foreign authority, or by reason of an injury or an illness which are unrelated to the service of the vessel and the treatment of which cannot be ensured on board.

In the event of termination of the contract of employment by mutual consent, the expenses of repatriation shall be borne by the party designated by the agreement for such termination.

With respect to foreign seamen, their right to repatriation shall be limited to returning them to the port at which they were engaged unless it was stipulated that the seaman be returned to a Lebanese port. The right to repatriation shall include lodging and subsistence in addition to passage.

The contract of employment shall expire:

1) Upon the expiry of the period fixed therefor where it was concluded for a definite period.

2) Upon the completion of the voyage or the voluntary cancellation thereof where it was concluded for the duration of the voyage.

3) Upon the death of the seaman.

4) Upon the rescission of the contract by a judicial decision.

5) Upon the occurrence of a justifiable cause for dismissal.

Where the contract of employment was concluded for a definite period and its term falls due during a voyage and it contains no provision for its extension, its performance shall continue on board the merchant vessel or the fishing vessel until its arrival at a Lebanese port.

Where the seaman dies during the term of the contract and was engaged by the month, his wages shall be due up to the day of death. Where the seaman was engaged for the duration of the outward voyage alone and his wages consisted either of a lump sum or of a share of the profit or of the freight of the vessel, his full wages or his full share shall be due to him if he dies after the commencement of the voyage, and where he was engaged for a voyage both outward and homeward together, half of his wages and half of his share shall be due to him if he dies during the homeward leg of the voyage.

The decision of dismissal by the shipowner or the master of the vessel for a lawful cause shall not confer upon the dismissed seaman any right to compensation.

In ports other than Lebanese ports, the master may not disembark a seaman from his vessel for a lawful cause except with the permission of the Lebanese consul, if any, and failing that, of the maritime port authorities. Whatever the case in which the master of the vessel or its shipowner decides upon dismissal for a lawful cause, the date of such decision and the reasons therefor must be entered in the crew list.

Where this provision is not observed, the dismissal shall be deemed unlawful.

Where a seaman is dismissed without a lawful cause, he shall be entitled to compensation in respect of such dismissal. Such compensation shall be determined having regard to the nature of the service, the duration of the contract and the extent of the damage sustained. The contract of employment may fix such compensation at a lump sum, provided that such lump-sum determination shall not be deemed valid unless it does not conceal a waiver of the rights of the seaman.
The rescission of the contract of employment by the seaman without a lawful cause shall confer upon the shipowner a right to compensation.

The rescission of the charter of the whole vessel by the charterer thereof shall cause the rescission of the contract of employment of the seaman. A seaman engaged for a share of the freight of the vessel shall participate in the compensation which is awarded to the vessel: and his share of such compensation shall be in proportion to his share of the freight of the vessel.

Where the voyage becomes impossible by reason of force majeure, the rescission of the contract of employment shall not confer upon the seaman any right to compensation. However, if he was engaged by the month or by the voyage, he shall be paid wages for the days which he spent in the service of the vessel.

Where the continuation of the voyage after its commencement becomes impossible by reason of force majeure, the seamen engaged by the month or by the voyage shall be paid their wages up to the day on which their work ceased. Where the seamen were engaged for a share of the freight of the vessel or of the profit, they shall be entitled to the share fixed in the contract of the profit or of the freight of the vessel earned by reason of the performance of part of the voyage.

Where the vessel is captured, founders, or is declared unseaworthy, the courts may cancel the wages of the seamen or reduce them if it is proved that the loss of the vessel resulted from their fault or their negligence, or that they did not do everything in their power to save the vessel, the passengers or the goods, or to recover its wreck.

The seaman shall participate in the compensation which may be awarded by the administrative or judicial authorities in respect of the damage sustained where, by the operation of the two preceding Articles, he did not receive the whole of his wages to which he was entitled for the estimated duration of the voyage.

The remuneration of the master, with the exception of his fixed wages, shall be subject in its entirety to attachment for the sums due from him to the shipowner in his capacity as his agent. As for his fixed wages, they shall be subject to attachment for the causes and to the extent provided for in Article 143

The master, whatever the duration of his contract, shall have no right to rescind or annul such contract at his own will during the voyage. However, the shipowner shall have the right to dismiss the master at any time he wishes, provided that he compensates him in the event of dismissing him without a lawful cause.

The provisions relating to the payment of wages in the event of the delay, extension or shortening of the voyage shall not apply to the master where his personal fault was the cause of the alteration which occurred to the voyage.
After the expiry of one year from the end of the maritime contract of employment, the right to any action relating to such contract shall be barred by prescription.
The judge shall apply the custom of the place or the general customs in all matters not provided for by the agreement or the law.

Where the chartered vessel is designated by name in the agreement, the owner (lessor) thereof may not replace it with another vessel unless it perishes or becomes unseaworthy by reason of force majeure occurring after the commencement of the voyage.

The master, if he finds undeclared goods on the vessel, may order that they be put ashore at the place of their loading, or may fix double freight in respect of them, while reserving his right in respect of any greater damage he may sustain.

Where such goods are discovered during the voyage, the master may jettison the goods loaded without right if their nature is capable of causing damage to the vessel or to the rest of the cargo, or if their carriage would entail expenses exceeding their value or public fines, or if their sale and exportation are prohibited by law.

Whatever the case, the master shall set forth in the logbook the discovery of the goods loaded without right and the fate which befell them, and shall draw up a detailed report in this regard.

A time charterparty is a contract whereby the vessel is chartered for a definite period. The owner (lessor) of the vessel has the option either to leave or not to leave to the charterer thereof the right to appoint and dismiss the master, and he may assign to him the nautical and commercial management thereof, or its commercial management alone.

The charterer of the vessel who has the right to dispose of both its nautical and commercial management shall provide it with all provisions, maintenance repairs and all operating expenses, and shall bear the contribution to general average which is chargeable to the vessel and its freight, and the loss of the vessel and marine casualties, whatever their gravity, shall fall upon him unless it is proved that they resulted from the fault of the owner (lessor).

However, where the charterer of the vessel has only its commercial management alone, such loss and such casualties shall be chargeable to the owner (lessor) thereof unless the latter proves that they resulted from the fault of the charterer.

The hire (freight) of the vessel shall be due from the charterer thereof for the entire period during which the vessel is at his disposal. In the event of the capture, detention or loss of the vessel, its hire shall be due up to the date of such events.
Where the hire (freight) of the vessel is measured by periods of time, every period begun shall be due in its entirety.

The hire (freight) in respect of the vessel shall be due from the day it is placed at the disposal of the charterer thereof until the day it is returned to the disposal of the owner (lessor) thereof in a condition qualifying it to receive cargo.

Such hire shall be suspended for the entire period during which the charterer is deprived of the disposal of the vessel by reason of an act of authority, but it shall continue to run during the period of detention of the vessel by reason of accidents of navigation.

Where such detention results from the act of the owner (lessor) thereof, no hire whatsoever shall be due in respect thereof, and damages may moreover be claimed.

A contract of voyage charter of a vessel is a contract whereby the whole or part of a vessel is chartered for one or more specified voyages. A contract of carriage by sea is a contract whereby the carrier undertakes, in return for freight, to deliver luggage or goods to a specified place, provided that he carries them by way of the sea during the whole or part of the duration of the voyage.

The vessel must be ready to receive the goods at the appointed time and at the agreed or customary place of loading. The master must take the goods at the expense of the shipowner from under the tackle and must deliver them at the port of destination to the consignee under the tackle.

The chartering of the whole of the vessel shall not include the cabins and spaces assigned to the master and the seamen; nevertheless, neither the master nor the seamen may load any goods therein except with the consent of the charterer of the vessel.

If the vessel is chartered in whole or for a specified part thereof, the master may not carry in the vessel or in the chartered part thereof any other goods except with the permission of the charterer thereof.

In the event of a breach in this respect, the freight for the goods carried without right shall accrue to the charterer, who may also claim damages.
The lessor of the vessel shall be liable for all loss and damage sustained by the goods throughout the duration of their remaining in his custody unless he proves force majeure.

The lessor of the vessel must pay, for the goods which the master uses or sells during the voyage for the needs of the vessel, a price from which the expenses saved to the charterer thereof are deducted and which is calculated on the basis of the value of the goods at the port to which they are bound if the vessel reaches it safely, and otherwise on the basis of their actual sale price.

The lessor of the vessel shall have the right to retain the freight for all the goods the value of which he is bound to pay. If the shippers are not paid the price of their goods used for the needs of the vessel, the loss which they sustain as a result thereof shall be apportioned rateably over the value of those goods and over all the goods which reach the place to which they are bound or which are saved from shipwreck at a time subsequent to the casualties of the sea which compelled the sale or the pledge.

If no one appears to take delivery of the goods or if the person to whom they were consigned refuses to take delivery thereof, the master may apply to the judicial authority for the sale of the whole or part of the goods up to the amount of the freight of the vessel and for an order to deposit the unsold goods.

If the proceeds of the sale are insufficient to satisfy the amount of the freight, the master shall retain the right to claim the difference from the shippers.

If the shipper fails to bring under the tackle the agreed quantity of goods, he shall be liable for the freight for the entire voyage in respect of such shipment as well as the expenses incurred by the vessel as a result of this act, provided that the expenses saved to the vessel and three-quarters of the freight of the goods shipped in place of his goods are credited to him.

No freight shall be due for the vessel in respect of goods which have not been delivered to the consignee or which have not been placed at his disposal at the port to which they are consigned.

Nevertheless, the freight shall be due.

- If the non-delivery results from the negligence or fault of the charterers-shippers or of their successors in title

- If necessity during the voyage compelled the sale of the goods by reason of their deterioration, whatever the cause of such deterioration may be

- If the loss of the goods is reckoned as general average

- If the goods perished by reason of an inherent vice therein.

Freight shall also be due in respect of animals which die on the vessel for any cause whatsoever other than the fault of the shipper.

In all cases where no freight is due for the vessel, the master must return the advances paid to him before the voyage on account of such freight. However, he may retain them in full if he has paid the insurance premium thereon to the charterer of the vessel or to the shipper.

A charterer of the vessel or a shipper who wishes the goods to be delivered to him before their arrival at the place to which they are bound must pay the freight in full, even in the event of it being necessary to repair the vessel during the voyage by reason of a maritime casualty of force majeure.

If the vessel is detained during the voyage by order of a State or by an event which cannot be attributed either to the master or to the lessor of the vessel, the agreements shall remain in force and there shall be no ground for compensation or for an increase in the stipulated freight.

During the detention of the vessel, the shipper shall have the right to have his goods discharged for him at his own expense, provided that he reloads them or compensates the master.

If the vessel is unable to proceed to the port for which it is bound by reason of force majeure supervening after its departure, the shipper shall be liable only for the outward freight of the voyage, even if his charter was concluded for an outward and return voyage.

If the vessel is unable to enter the port of destination by reason of blockade or any other force majeure, the master shall have full discretion to act in the best interests of the shippers if he has not been furnished with instructions for such an eventuality.

The shipper may not discharge himself from the freight of the vessel by abandoning the goods, even if they have lost their value during the voyage or have suffered damage.

However, if casks containing liquids have leaked so as to have lost at least three-quarters of their contents, they may be abandoned in satisfaction of the freight of the vessel.
