Disputes arising out of the establishment of the easement provided for in the preceding paragraphs, the exercise of these rights, and the determination of the indemnities which may be due, where applicable, to the owners of the lower lands, shall be brought before the Justice of the Peace of the district; and this judge, in rendering his judgment, shall reconcile the interests of agriculture and industry with the respect due to the right of ownership.
Every owner of an immovable property has the right to enclose his property, unless such enclosure prevents the exercise of an easement established for the benefit of an adjoining immovable property.
Legal easements are established either for public utility or for the utility of private individuals.

Legal easements of public utility, whether designed to enable access to the sea-shores and the banks of watercourses, or designed to secure or facilitate the laying out, maintenance and use of public ways or works, and in particular works of land or naval military defence, are defined in the special laws and regulations relating thereto.

Every owner of an immovable property must construct the roofs of his building in such a manner that rainwater flows onto his own land or onto the public highway, unless the special regulations relating to highways apply to him in this respect; and he may not cause these waters to flow onto the land adjoining his.

Every owner of an immovable property who wishes to carry out on his land works calculated to injure the adjoining lands, such as boring, sounding, excavations, and the establishment of dangerous, inconvenient and insalubrious depots, must comply with the local regulations which prescribe the distance to be observed between him and the adjoining land or the intermediate works to be erected between them.

No owner of an immovable property may have openings giving a direct view over his neighbour, or windows, balconies or other similar projections overlooking the enclosed or unenclosed land of the owner of the adjoining immovable property, unless there is a distance of two metres between the wall in which such projections are made and the said land. In the absence of this distance, he may not open windows or lights except at a height of two metres and a half above the floor of the room intended to be lighted if it is on the ground floor, and at a height of one metre and ninety centimetres above the floor of the dwelling if it is on an upper floor.

No owner of an immovable property may have side or oblique windows over the enclosed or unenclosed land of his neighbour, unless there is a distance of fifty centimetres between the wall in which the windows are situated and the said land.
This prohibition arising from Articles 66 and 67 above does not apply to roofs or to windows opening onto the public highway.

The distance prescribed in Articles 66 and 67 is computed from the outer face of the external wall where the windows are situated, and, as regards balconies and similar projections, from their outer line to the dividing line between the two immovable properties.
Neither the buyer nor the seller may, during the term of the contract, assign the real property, lease it, or establish real rights over it without their express mutual consent.
It may be stipulated in the contract that the buyer has the right to enjoy the real property gratuitously or to enjoy a portion of its yield.

The buyer must attend to the maintenance of the real property and carry out the useful repairs necessary for it, unless there is an agreement to the contrary, and he may deduct from the yield of the real property the expenses arising from the maintenance and repair of the real property.

If the buyer takes delivery of the real property, he becomes liable towards the seller for the yield which he collects, unless there is a provision to the contrary, and each year the value of the yield shall be deducted from the principal of the debt after having subtracted therefrom, where applicable, the value of the yield which he collected for his personal account in accordance with the conditions inserted in the deed, and after having also deducted therefrom the expenses which he spent on the real property.

The purchaser is liable for the destruction of the real property which is in his possession and for its damage, under the following conditions:

The amount of the destruction or damage shall be deducted from the principal of the debt; if this value equals or exceeds the purchase price, the sale shall be rescinded ipso jure and the purchaser must pay the excess above that, unless the destruction or damage arose from force majeure.

If an insured real property is destroyed or damaged, the insurance indemnity shall be allocated with priority to the discharge of the creditor's debt, and an amount of the debt equal to the value of the indemnity shall fall due from the debtor.
Upon the death of the purchaser or the seller, the right to rescind the sale passes to their heirs.
The sale with right of redemption is indivisible, even if the debt is divided among the heirs of the purchaser or of the seller.

The creditors of the seller are not entitled, throughout the entire term of the contract and before they pay the price of the real property to the purchaser, to exercise any right whatsoever over this real property.
If the seller does not return the price of the real property, the creditor is entitled to demand the sale of the real property in order to satisfy his debt out of its price.

Pledge is a contract whereby the debtor places a real property into the possession of his creditor or into the possession of another person agreed upon by both parties, and this contract confers upon the creditor the right to retain the real property until his debt is paid in full, and if the debt is not paid, he has the right to pursue the expropriation from his debtor by legal means.
A pledge may not be allocated to secure the performance of an obligation relating to doing something or abstaining from doing it.
The validity of a pledge depends upon the existence of a legally established debt.
Every real property that may be sold may be pledged. Undivided shares in co-ownership may not be pledged.
The pledged real property may serve as security for the debt of another person other than the pledgor.
The entirety of the pledged real property secures every part of the debt; accordingly, the debtor is not entitled to claim the enjoyment of his real property before the discharge of his debt.
It may not be agreed that the pledged real property shall, in case of non-payment, become the property of the creditor.
The real property shall be under the supervision of the possessor, and it shall be at the risk and liability of its owner if the pledgee proves that the damage arose from force majeure.
A pledge does not prevent the exercise of real rights lawfully acquired (and subsisting) over the real property prior to the registration of the pledge in the Land Register.
The pledge encompasses all things that were or have become integral parts of the real property, or among its utilities, or among the accessories necessary for it.

The creditor is not entitled, without the consent of the debtor, to enjoy the pledged real property gratuitously, and he must exploit it to the extent that it can yield, and this yield shall be deducted from the secured debt even before the maturity of the debt, and it shall be deducted first from the interest and expenses and then from the principal.

The creditor must attend to the maintenance of the pledged real property and to carrying out the useful and necessary repairs for it; however, he shall take from the yield all the expenses expended for the maintenance and repair of the real property, or recover them with priority out of the price of the real property, and he is always entitled to relieve himself of these obligations by renouncing the right of pledge.

A pledge is indivisible even if the debt is divided among the heirs of the debtor or the heirs of the creditor; thus, the heir of the debtor, even if he pays the portion of the debt incumbent upon him, cannot demand the delivery of the pledged real property, and likewise the creditor heir, even if he receives his share of the debt, cannot deliver the real property to the debtor so as to cause prejudice thereby to his co-heirs whose shares have not been paid to them.

Neither the debtor nor the creditor may, without their mutual consent, dispose of the pledged real property, and every contract made over the real property contrary to these rules shall be null and void ipso jure.
The pledged real property which the pledgee creditor lends to the debtor or leases to him remains allocated to secure the discharge of the debt.

The pledge is extinguished by the payment of the debt at maturity, or by agreement between the debtor and the pledgee creditor, or by the mere will of the latter.

This extinction shall have no legal effect except after the cancellation of the entry recorded in the Land Register.

A real property privilege in real property matters is a real right which the creditor obtains by reason of the quality of his debt, rendering him preferred over all other creditors, even over the holders of mortgages themselves.

The sole privileged debts are three, namely:

1- The debt specified in Article forty-four of Decision No. 186 issued on 15 March 1926.

2- The judicial costs arising from the sale of the immovable property and the distribution of its price.

3- The duties and expenses of the transfer of ownership and the fines imposed on false declarations relating to sale prices.
These privileges shall be exempt from registration, contrary to the general principle established in Article 10 of the Decision establishing the Land Register.

A mortgage is a real right over immovable properties allocated to secure the performance of an obligation. It is by its nature indivisible and subsists in its entirety over the immovable properties allocated to it, over each immovable property thereof and over every part of these immovable properties, and follows them into whatever hands they may pass.

Mortgages may be contracted over the following things only:

1- Built or unbuilt lands capable of being sold and purchased, together with all their accessories deemed to be immovable properties.

2- The right of usufruct subsisting over these immovable properties and their accessories, for so long as it exists thereon.

3- The rights of Ijaratayn and Muqata'a.

4- The right of superficies.

A mortgage contracted by a co-owner in a jointly owned immovable property without the permission of his co-owners shall be transferred after partition to the share accruing to him, and the proceeds of the sums paid to the mortgagor by reason of differences existing in the values of the shares, or the sums accruing to him following the sale of the immovable property, shall be allocated to the payment of the mortgage sum.
An acquired mortgage shall extend to the buildings, plantations or improvements which take place after the contracting of the mortgage in the immovable property over which such mortgage subsists.

A creditor who has registered his debt, where such debt is a principal bearing interest or having matured instalments, shall have the right for the rank of the interest and mature sums (for the year due at the date of the application for execution and for the current year, provided that the total does not exceed the amount of two years' interest) to come in the rank of the mortgage and the rank of the principal, provided that this right arises from the same instrument, that it is registered, and that the rate of interest is specified.

Every mortgage legally registered in the Land Register shall preserve its rank and its validity without the performance of new formalities until the contract resulting from the discharge of liability is legally registered in the same register.
A mortgage is either compulsory or conventional, and in both cases it shall have no legal effect until after its registration.

Several mortgages may subsist over a single immovable property, and the rank of these mortgages, whether compulsory or conventional, shall be according to the date of their entry in the Land Register.
A conventional mortgage may only be contracted by the person who has the right to sell the immovable property or to sell the right which he offers for mortgage.

A mortgage may not be effected over the rights of persons lacking capacity, minors and interdicted persons save for the causes specified in the law applicable to their personal status and in the manner appointed therein.

As for the rights of absent persons, so long as the taking of possession thereof is provisionally authorised, no mortgage may be effected over them save by judicial authorisation.
A mortgage may not be effected over property which it is hoped to acquire in the future.

A compulsory mortgage is a mortgage which is registered by operation of law in the cases appointed below, whether with the consent of the owner of the immovable property or without his consent, and such mortgage shall only be specific. The rights and debts for the preservation of which a compulsory mortgage is contracted are:

1- Such of them as pertain to minors and interdicted persons: the compulsory mortgage is contracted over the property of their guardians.

2- Such of them as pertain to a married woman: the compulsory mortgage is contracted over the immovable properties of her husband to secure her dowry (dot) or dower, her matrimonial rights, and the indemnity accruing to her from the obligations of the husband which she performs.

3- Such of them as pertain to the State, municipalities and public administrations: the compulsory mortgage is contracted in this respect over the immovable properties of accounting officers.

4- With respect to the vendor, the exchanger and the co-partitioner: the mortgage is contracted over the immovable property sold, exchanged or partitioned when there is no conventional mortgage to secure payment of the price and the differences of exchange or partition.

5- With respect to creditors and legatees of an estate: the mortgage is contracted over the immovable properties of the estate to secure the separation of the estate of the deceased from the property of the heir.
A compulsory mortgage must always be specified with respect to the sums secured and the immovable properties over which the mortgage subsists.

The basis of the compulsory mortgage relating to minors and interdicted persons, its substance and its conditions shall be determined by the authority charged, in accordance with the laws in force, with supervising the administration of guardians.

The basis of the mortgage relating to a married woman, its substance and its conditions may be determined by an express provision in the marriage contract drawn up before the competent authorities and in accordance with the form and conditions appointed in the laws in force.

If there is no marriage deed, or if the deed is devoid of the provisions necessary to determine the compulsory mortgage, the Civil Court in the place of residence of the two parties shall determine it.

If it appears that the mortgage guarantees given to minors and interdicted persons or to a married woman are insufficient, the authority appointed in Article one hundred and thirty-three shall have the right to extend them with respect to minors and interdicted persons, and the Court shall have the like right with respect to a married woman. If it appears that the mortgage guarantees given to minors and interdicted persons or to a married woman are excessive, they may be reduced within the conditions appointed in the preceding paragraph.
The mortgage contracted over the immovable properties of accounting officers shall be determined in a decision by the Minister of Finance or by the official acting in his stead.

The vendor, the exchanger and the co-partitioner of immovable real property shall have the right to demand, in the instrument of sale, the instrument of exchange or the deed of partition, from those who purchase from them, exchange with them or partition with them, a mortgage over the immovable properties sold, exchanged or assigned to secure payment of the price in its entirety, or to secure payment of a part thereof, or to secure payment of the differences resulting from the exchange or partition.

If there is no provision relating to a conventional mortgage, the vendor, the exchanger or the co-partitioner shall have the right, pursuant to a judgment issued by the Civil Court in the locality of the immovable properties, to obtain a compulsory mortgage contracted over those immovable properties.

Creditors and legatees shall have the right to preserve their rights in the separation of estates one from another by means of a compulsory registration effected during the six months following the commencement of the opening of the estate.

If the registration does not take place within the aforesaid period, this right shall have no effect with respect to the immovable properties.

The registration shall be effected pursuant to a judgment in the council chamber of the Court without the meeting of the two parties, upon the application of the interested parties in the matter and after hearing the Public Prosecution, and the rank of this entry shall only be appointed as from the day it is mentioned in the Land Registry Office, unless the provisional entry provided for in Article 139 one hundred and thirty-nine has been effected in this respect.

The mortgage, whether registered by one of the creditors of the deceased or by one of the legatees, or by several of them applying at the same time or one after another, shall enure to the benefit of all the creditors and legatees; however, this shall not preclude the obligation to observe the causes of preference or priority of some of them over others previously existing amongst them, and this registration shall not create new causes of preference or priority, and this registration shall be effective against the creditors of the heir himself just as it shall be effective against the creditors of the deceased and the legatees who did not submit an application for registration before the expiry of the period appointed in the first paragraph of this Article.
Ijaretayn shall include all that the immovable property yields and all that is united with it as an accessory thereto, whether such union is natural or artificial.

The holder of the ijaretayn may, with a permit from the administrator of the waqf, plant in the immovable property whatever plantings he wishes and erect thereon whatever buildings he wishes, provided that he observes the regulations of the police, roads, expansion and planning.

He may also carry out excavations therein to whatever depth he wishes and, subject to reserving the provisions of the laws and decisions relating to mines, quarries and ancient antiquities and the regulations of the police and roads, he may extract from these excavations whatever building materials he wishes, to the exclusion of other extractions.

The provisions of Article 215 of this Decision and the articles following it shall apply in all cases in which the holder of the right of ijaretayn has erected buildings or planted plantings without a permit obtained in advance from the administrator of the waqf.

The holder of the right of ijaretayn shall be liable for any decrease occurring in the value of the immovable property on his account, and he must also pay the expenses of maintaining the immovable property and the taxes and fees due thereon, and he shall not be entitled to claim the expenses which he has spent on the immovable property or the improvement which he has made therein.

The holder of the right of ijaretayn is bound to pay the perpetual annuity, and if he does not pay this annuity or does not pay the indemnities and other expenses due, expropriation against him may be pursued by legal means.

The right of ijaretayn shall remain on the waqf in the event of the extinction of the heirs of its holder, except that it reverts to the waqf, and the right of ijaretayn shall lapse from its holder for non-use of the immovable property for a period of ten years.
The right of ijaretayn shall not lapse by the destruction of all the buildings or plantings, but shall remain on the bare ownership.

Long lease is a contract whereby its holder acquires, in return for a consideration which he pays, the right to erect whatever buildings he wishes and to plant whatever plantings he wishes on an immovable property constituted as waqf, and he may furthermore acquire ownership of these buildings or plantings as his own exclusive property within the conditions specified in Article One Hundred and Ninety-Six.
The contract of long lease shall only be permitted by way of muqata'a (for a fixed annual consideration) to the exclusion of any other.

The consideration shall consist of a specified sum of money equivalent to the value of the right assigned, in addition to the creation of a perpetual annuity whose value equals two and a half per thousand of the value of the immovable property as determined in the assessment made for the collection of the immovable property tax.

Rights arising from contracts of long lease other than the right of muqata'a existing prior to the promulgation of this Decision shall be subject to the right of redemption by purchase in accordance with the provisions of Decision No. 80 issued- on 29 January 1926
The holder of the muqata'a shall enjoy the right to acquire the ownership of the immovable property at any time whatsoever, and the sale price shall be the equivalent of thirty annual instalments.
A permit from the judge must be obtained in advance for the permissibility of concluding a deed of muqata'a.

The holder of the right of muqata'a is the owner of all the buildings erected and the plantings planted on the immovable property constituted as waqf; he uses them, enjoys them and disposes of them with full freedom as though they were his mulk property, and he may in particular, within the limits of his right, assign them for consideration or without consideration, pledge them, constitute a mortgage thereon, constitute them as waqf, or establish thereon any other real rights or easements.

The land constituted as waqf shall be deemed an accessory to the buildings erected and the plantings planted on the bare ownership, and accordingly this land shall be included in the totality of the buildings and plantings upon their assignment unless there is an agreement to the contrary.
The right of muqata'a may be transferred by way of inheritance, intestate or testamentary, in accordance with the provisions applicable to mulk immovable property.

The holder of the muqata'a shall forfeit his right if there is not the slightest trace of the building or of the plantings on the land, or if he does not restore these buildings or plantings to their former state after a formal notice from the administrator of the waqf, or if he does not pay for a period of three years the perpetual annuity due.

The forfeiture of his right in these two cases shall be decided by a decision of the judiciary.

The right of muqata'a shall lapse either by the merger of the two capacities in a single person, or following the forfeiture by its holder of his right, or by the extinction of the heirs, and in these three cases this right shall revert to the waqf.
The provisions relating to co-ownership and partition shall apply to the rights of ijaretayn and long lease (muqata'a).

Real rights shall be acquired and transferred by means of their entry in the Land Register, and the right of ownership and the right of tasarruf shall also be acquired by way of accession in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Two of this Title; anyone who acquires an immovable property by inheritance, by expropriation or by a judgment of the court shall be the holder of such immovable property prior to its entry, provided that such acquisition shall have no effect until after its registration.
The effects of registration are specified in the provisions of Article 11 of Decision No. 188 relating to Land Registration.
Alluvion, that is to say the earth which accumulates successively and imperceptibly on the land adjacent to a watercourse, shall be the property of the owner of such land.

Lands which are displaced from their locations by reason of a sudden event of force majeure onto land lower than them may, if they are recognizable, be claimed by their owner during the year following the unforeseen event, and if the year expires he shall no longer have a right to claim.
Large and small islands which form naturally in the beds of rivers or watercourses shall form part of the private domain of the State.
Large and small islands and alluvion which form within lakes, as well as the alluvion of lakes and of the sea, form part of the private domain of the State.

A waqf property may not be sold, nor may it be assigned either gratuitously or for valuable consideration, nor may it devolve by way of inheritance, nor may it be pledged or encumbered with a mortgage; however, it may be exchanged (istibdal) or subjected to a double lease (ijaratayn) or a fixed perpetual ground rent (muqata'a).
A waqf shall not prevent the exercise of real rights lawfully acquired and preserved over the property prior to the entry of the waqf in the Land Register.
A waqf shall have no legal effect save from the day of its entry in the Land Register.
A waqf shall comprise all things which were or have become integral parts of the property, or its appurtenances, or its necessary accessories.
No right whatsoever may be acquired by prescription over waqf properties used as a mosque, church, synagogue, hospital, or educational institution, or dedicated to public use.

The rules relating to the constitution of waqfs, their validity, their object, their partition, their leasing, and their exchange (istibdal) are prescribed in the provisions of the special laws governing the same.

Double lease (ijaratayn) is a contract whereby a person acquires in perpetuity the right to use and enjoy a waqf property in consideration of the payment of its price. This price shall consist of a fixed sum of money serving as an advance rent and equivalent to the value of the assigned right, to which shall be added the creation of a perpetual annuity the rate of which shall be fixed in the proportion of 3 per mille of the value of the property as determined in the assessment made for the collection of the property tax.
The holder of a double lease (ijaratayn) shall have the right to purchase the bare ownership of the property at any time in consideration of a sum equivalent to 30 annual instalments.
Prior authorisation from the judge must be obtained after the deed of double lease (ijaratayn).

The holder of a double lease (ijaratayn) shall have the right to use and enjoy the property as a true owner; he may enjoy it himself or lease it out, and he may dispose of his right with full freedom, particularly with respect to assigning it for valuable consideration or gratuitously, pledging it, effecting parts of a mortgage thereon, or encumbering it with all real rights
The right of double lease (ijaratayn) may devolve by intestate or testamentary succession in accordance with the provisions applicable to amiri properties.

The owner of a party wall may not raise it or build upon it without the permission of his co-owner.

However, he may, on the side of his immovable property, place upon the party wall or rest against it beams, constructions or other things up to the limit of what half the strength of the wall can bear.

No one shall be compelled to waive to his neighbour his joint right in the wall. However, if one of the co-owners in common increases the height of a wall, with the permission of the other party, that party shall be entitled, if he has not borne any part of the expense, to acquire the right of co-ownership in the newly constructed part of the party wall, provided that he pays half of such expense and pays also, where applicable, half the value of the land used to increase the thickness of the wall.

Where the storeys of a house belong to different owners, repairs and renewals in the building shall be subject to the following provisions, unless there are contrary conditions mentioned in the title deeds:

- The cost of the main walls and roofs shall be borne by all the owners of the immovable property, each in proportion to the value of the storey that he owns.

- The owner of each storey shall bear the cost of the floor of the storey upon which he walks.

- The owner of the first storey shall bear the cost of the stairs leading to that storey, and the owner of the second storey shall bear the cost of the stairs leading to it starting from the first storey, and so forth.

The owner of an immovable property may have large and small trees near the boundary of his neighbour's land, provided that the owner of the adjoining land shall be entitled to cut the branches that overhang his land.

Large and small trees of any kind whatsoever may be planted adjacent to the dividing wall between two immovable properties on either side thereof without leaving any distance whatsoever between the wall and the plantings, provided that the trees may not exceed the top of the wall.

Where the wall is not a party wall, its owner alone shall have the right to rest his plantings against it.

Every owner of an immovable property which is enclosed on its sides and has no outlet to the public road shall be entitled to claim a passage over the adjoining lands, provided that he pays compensation assessed in proportion to the damage that he may cause. The same right is recognised for the owner of an immovable property who has only an outlet that is insufficient for the agricultural or industrial exploitation of his immovable property.

The passage must by law be taken on the side where the distance of the passage from the enclosed land to the public road is shorter than it is on the other sides, provided that the place of passage must be designated at the spot where passing through it causes the least damage to the person who granted permission to open the passage on his land.

Where the land becomes enclosed on all its sides by reason of its subdivision following a sale, exchange, partition or any contract whatsoever, the creation of a passage may only be claimed over the lands upon which such transactions took place.

However, if it is impossible to open a sufficient passage over the partitioned lands, Article Seventy-Four shall apply.

Every owner of an immovable property who wishes to use for the irrigation of his land the natural or artificial waters of which he has the right to dispose may obtain the passage of such waters over the intermediate lands between them and his land, provided that he pays in respect thereof compensation in advance.

The owner of the said immovable property shall also be entitled to obtain, in return for the payment of compensation in advance, a passage for the waters flowing from his land irrigated in this manner over the lands that are lower than it.

Subject to the reservation of the regulatory provisions relating to water intakes, every owner of an immovable property adjoining a watercourse may, if he wishes to use the waters for the irrigation of his land, obtain, in return for the payment of prior compensation, the right to rest the necessary technical constructions upon the land adjoining the watercourse opposite his land.

Where the owner of the immovable property upon whose land it is requested to rest the technical constructions requests to use the dam in common, he must bear half the expenses of construction and maintenance, and furthermore he shall have no right in this case to the slightest compensation for resting the dam upon his land, and if compensation had been paid to him in respect thereof, he must refund it.

Every owner of an immovable property who wishes to improve his land by draining its waters or by any method of drying whatsoever may conduct such waters, in return for fair compensation paid in advance, underground or on the surface through the lands separating his land from one of the watercourses or from any channel whatsoever for the flow of water, with the exception of houses, canals, pleasure gardens, orchards and gardens adjoining dwellings.

The owners of the adjoining immovable properties or of those crossed by the waters shall be entitled to use the constructions created in accordance with the preceding Article for draining the waters of their lands, and in this case they shall bear the following:

1- A share of the expenses of the constructions in proportion to the benefit that they derive therefrom.

2- The expenses resulting from the alterations that may have to be made to the channel in order to be able to exercise this right.

3- The share that will fall upon them in the future of the expenses of maintaining these constructions which become common.

Disputes arising from the creation of the easement in question, from the exercise thereof, from the determination of the place of passage of the waters, from the construction of works relating to the improvement of lands by draining their waters by means of canals or relating to the drying of lands, and from compensation and the expenses of maintaining the place of the easement, shall be brought before the Justice of the Peace of the district. In rendering his judgment, the said Justice must reconcile the interests of the easement with the respect due to the right of ownership.

The owners of immovable properties may create over their immovable properties or for the benefit of their immovable properties such easements as they see fit, provided that such rights are not imposed upon a person or for the benefit of a person, but upon the land or for the benefit of the land, and provided that they are not contrary to public policy.

The exercise and extent of these rights shall be determined in the instrument creating them, and in the absence of an instrument, they shall be determined by the following rules.

Whoever creates an easement implicitly grants whatever is necessary to enable the exercise of that right.

Thus, the right to draw water from a spring necessarily entails the right of passage over the land on which that spring is situated.
The owner of the dominant immovable property shall have the right to construct upon the servient land all the constructions necessary for the exercise and maintenance of that easement.
The expense of the constructions necessary for the exercise and maintenance of the easement shall be borne by the owner of the dominant land.

Where the dominant land is subdivided, the easement shall remain for each of its parts, provided that this does not entail an increase in the burden of the easement upon the servient land.

For example, where the easement consists in a right of passage, all the co-owners of the immovable property must use the same passage.

The owner of the servient immovable property may not do anything that diminishes the exercise of the easement or makes its exercise more difficult than before. Consequently, he cannot alter the condition of the premises or transfer the easement to a place other than the place originally designated for it. However, if the place originally designated has become more burdensome to the owner of the servient immovable property or if it prevents him from making useful repairs to the immovable property, he shall be entitled to offer to the owner of the dominant immovable property a place as convenient as the first place for the exercise of his rights, and the latter may not refuse. Likewise, whoever has an easement may only exercise it in accordance with his instrument, and he cannot make, either upon the servient land or upon his own land, the slightest alteration that increases anything in the burden of the easement upon the servient land.

Easements are extinguished by striking off.

Striking off takes place by the effect of agreements or in accordance with judgments rendered by the courts, and the judge shall be entitled to order the striking off when the easement is of no utility or when its exercise is impossible.

A sale with right of redemption (vente à réméré) is the sale of an immovable property on condition that the seller shall be entitled at any time upon the expiry of the stipulated period to recover the thing sold in return for refunding the price, and that the buyer shall be entitled to claim the recovery of the price upon returning the thing sold.

Every immovable property capable of being sold shall be capable of being sold with right of redemption, and it may be stated in the deed of sale that the seller shall continue to occupy the immovable property in the capacity of a lessee (sale with leaseback).

The right to effect registration in the Real Estate Register is acquired, in respect of immovable properties and rights not registered in the Real Estate Register, by a person taking possession of the immovable property or of the real estate right by a peaceful, public, continuous possession as if he were the owner of the immovable property for a period of five years, by himself or through a third party on his behalf, provided that the possessor holds a valid title; and if he does not hold a valid title, the period shall be fifteen years.

Possession is deemed continuous from the time it is manifested by the ordinary and regular exercise of the right taken into possession. Whoever claims prescription is entitled to rely upon the possession of the person from whom the immovable property devolved to him. Neither the sharecropper, nor the usufructuary, nor the depositary, nor the borrower, nor their heirs may claim prescription.
Possession proved at a certain given time and present possession create a presumption of possession in the interval between those two dates, unless proof to the contrary is established.

The right to register the right of disposal (tasarruf) in Amiri lands not subject to the administration of State Property is acquired by the lapse of ten years from the date of possession, with or without title, provided that the possessor is cultivating the land.
No person may acquire by prescription a real right against his own particular title or against the title of his predecessors in title by inheritance.
The right of prescription may not be waived in advance, However, every person having the capacity to dispose of his rights may waive a right acquired by prescription.
If prescription is interrupted, the period of possession prior to the occupation of the immovable property shall not be counted.
Prescription is interrupted when its holder loses his possession, even if this is due to the act of another person.
The same shall apply if the owner of the immovable property claims his right by instituting a judicial action, provided that he does not allow his action to lapse.
Prescription in respect of immovable property does not run against absent persons or persons lacking legal capacity pursuant to the law.

The right to register real rights in immovable property is acquired by the effect of contracts.

The provisions relating to sale and gift shall apply to Amiri immovable properties and to real rights that are the subject of a sale or a gift

The undertaking to give an immovable property entails the obligation to transfer (faragh) the immovable property in the Real Estate Register and to preserve it until the transfer, under penalty of paying damages to the creditor.

Undertakings to transfer (faragh) an immovable property in the Real Estate Register are subject to the provisions governing sale, privileges, and mortgages, as well as to the provisions of Decisions No. 188 and 189 issued on 15 March 1926 establishing the Real Estate Register

The protection and development of the natural water resource, within the framework of preserving the environment and the balances of nature, shall be deemed to be at the core of public utility.

The Ministry of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources.

The Ministry of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources shall assume, in the water sector, the following powers and duties:

1- Observing, monitoring, measuring, enumerating and studying water resources, and estimating the needs for water and the fields of its use in all regions.

2 - Monitoring the quality of surface and ground water and determining the standards thereof.

3 - Drawing up the draft general design for the allocation and distribution of water resources for drinking and irrigation at the State level, drawing up the draft general master plan for water and sanitation, updating it continuously, and submitting it through the Minister to the Council of Ministers.

4 - Designing, studying and executing major hydraulic installations such as dams, mountain lakes, tunnels, the rectification of river courses, water networks and others, and putting them into exploitation.

5 - Carrying out the artificial recharge of groundwater aquifers when necessary, and monitoring the exploitation of the quantities extracted therefrom.

6 - Working to protect water resources from waste and pollution by laying down texts and taking the necessary measures and procedures to prevent their pollution and to restore them to their natural quality.

7 - Granting permits and licences for prospecting for water and using public water and public riverine domain, conducting all transactions relating thereto, and granting them in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

8 - Conducting hydraulic, geological and hydrological studies and research, collecting technical data in the field of water, and preparing technical maps therefor and updating them regularly.

9 - Exercising supervision and trusteeship over public establishments and all other bodies operating in the field of water in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the texts and provisions pertaining to each of them.

10 - Enhancing the performance of Public Water Exploitation Establishments, and monitoring such performance on the basis of the indicators set out in the work programmes duly approved.

11 -Laying down the standards to be adopted in the studies of Public Exploitation Establishments and the execution of their works, the conditions and regulations for the exploitation of surface water, groundwater and wastewater, and the standard regulations for water quality and the monitoring thereof"

12 - Completing expropriation transactions pertaining to the Ministry and to the Public Water Exploitation Establishments subject to its trusteeship in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

13 - Giving an opinion on licences for mines and quarries in terms of their impact on water resources.

14 - Ensuring public relations with citizens and informing them of all that concerns them in water affairs and the rationalisation of its use.

Public Water Exploitation Establishments.

The Public Water Exploitation Establishments, the names and headquarters of which are indicated as follows, shall be established:

- The Beirut and Mount Lebanon Water Establishment, having its headquarters in the city of Beirut.

- The North Lebanon Water Establishment, having its headquarters in the city of Tripoli .

- The Bekaa Water Establishment, having its headquarters in the city of Zahle.

- The South Lebanon Water Establishment, having its headquarters in the city of Sidon.

The aforementioned Establishments shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy, and the scope of their exploitation shall be determined in accordance with the map annexed to this Law.

1 - Each of the Water Establishments shall assume, within the scope of its exploitation and competence:

a- Studying, executing, exploiting, maintaining and renewing hydraulic projects for the distribution of potable and irrigation water, and collecting, treating and disposing of wastewater in accordance with the general master plan for water and sanitation or subject to prior approval from the Ministry for the use of public water sources or for the locations of wastewater treatment plants or new outfalls for the disposal of wastewater.

b - Proposing tariffs for potable and irrigation water services and wastewater disposal, provided that general social and economic conditions are taken into consideration.

c - Monitoring the quality of distributed drinking and irrigation water and the quality of wastewater at the outfalls and outlets of treatment plants.

2- The Water Establishments shall operate in accordance with their own regulations. The aforementioned Establishments must contract with an auditing firm whose mission shall be defined as drawing up a report on the financial statements, final accounts and internal control system adopted in the Establishment.

The management of the Establishment shall be assumed by a Board of Directors composed of a Chairman and six members who shall be appointed and their remunerations determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water, and they must hold university degrees recognised in Lebanon in the disciplines of law, water and environment - medicine - engineering - economics, accounting or business administration.

- The term of office of the Board of Directors shall be determined in its decree of appointment, and its services may be terminated at any time in accordance with the same procedures.

The Chairman of the Board of Directors shall perform the duties of Director General of the Establishment, and shall be assisted by an executive body of employees subject to his authority.

- The Board of Directors of the Establishment shall draw up all the regulations pertaining to it, and they shall be approved by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources.

The Public Water Exploitation Establishment shall be subject to the ex post audit of the Court of Accounts in accordance with a system agreed upon with the Court, and to the supervision of the Central Inspection, and shall not be subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board.

 A committee for evaluating the performance of Public Water Establishments shall be established at the Ministry of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources, which shall be formed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources, of:

- The Minister of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources, as Chairman.

- The Director General of the Ministry of Finance, as Member.

- The Director General of Exploitation at the Ministry of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources, as Member.

- The Director General of Hydraulic and Electrical Equipment at the Ministry of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources, as Member.

- An engineer in hydraulic affairs having at least six years of experience, as Member.

- A holder of a degree in economics having at least six years of experience, as Member.

- A holder of a degree in law having at least six years of experience, as Member.

- A holder of a degree in accounting or business administration having at least six years of experience, as Member.

- A civil servant of at least the second category in the Directorate General of Exploitation, as Member-Rapporteur.

The duties and working procedures of this committee shall be determined by a joint decision issued by the Ministers of Finance and of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources, and it may seek the assistance of such experts as it deems fit to carry out its work.

By way of exception to the provisions of the first Article of this Law, the National Authority for the Litani River, established pursuant to the Law issued on 14/08/1954, shall continue to manage and exploit irrigation water within the scope of its exploitation (South Bekaa and South Lebanon), and this Authority shall be subject to paragraph 2 of the fourth Article and to the sixth Article of this Law.

The autonomous authorities and committees currently existing for the management and exploitation of potable and irrigation water shall continue to exercise their works until they are merged into the Water Establishments mentioned in the third Article of this Law gradually, provided that this is completed within a period not exceeding two years from the date of entry into force of this Law.

The details of implementation of this Law shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources.

Implementing decree for this Article
The Public Water Establishments shall not be subject to any other legislative and regulatory texts that are contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Preparation and Training Department established in the Civil Service Board pursuant to Legislative Decree No. 114 dated 12/6/1959 is hereby repealed.

A public institution known as the "National Institute of Administration" shall be established, having legal personality and enjoying financial and administrative autonomy, hereinafter referred to by the word "the Institute", and shall be subject to the tutelage of the Civil Service Board and to the law of its establishment and its regulations, and shall undertake:

1- The preparation of employees for the public administrations at the level of the categories of the general administrative cadre: the Second, the Third, and the Fourth, first rank, provided that each category shall have a special section of its own in the Institute in accordance with the following:

- The Special Higher Degree for the positions of the Second Category.

- The Higher Degree for the positions of the Third Category.

- The Intermediate Degree for the positions of the Fourth Category, first rank.

2- The training of employees of public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities covered by the powers of the Civil Service Board.

3- Liaison with institutes of public administration in Arab and foreign States that are bound with the Lebanese State by agreements for the exchange of culture information.

4- The holding of meetings, seminars, research, and studies in the various branches of public administration.

5- The issuance of bulletins, books, journals, and all other publications of interest to public administration and addressing its problems.

The administration of the Institute shall be undertaken by a Board of Directors composed of a Chairman and five members appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the Board of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

The budget of the Institute shall be secured from a special item provided for in the Chapter of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, Section of the Civil Service Board, in the General Budget under the title "Contribution of the National Institute of Administration".

The Board of Directors of the Institute shall lay down, pursuant to decisions issued by it after the approval of the Civil Service Board, the regulations of the Institute, in particular the distribution of powers and functions among its various bodies and the methods of exercising them, its cadre, the scale of ranks and salaries, the conditions for appointing the Board of Directors and the employees therein and their special allowances and all other provisions governing their affairs, and the manner in which the tutelage authority exercises its powers over the acts of the Institute, and these decisions shall become effective after their ratification by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.

Provided that the Preparation and Training Department and the National Institute of Administration and Development shall continue to exercise their functions and powers in the Civil Service Board until the issuance of the texts mentioned in this Article.

In addition to its basic functions and in cooperation with the Institute, the Personnel Department in the Civil Service Board shall conduct the special competitive examinations for preparation in the National Institute of Administration for the positions mentioned in the Second Article of this Law, and shall also conduct the selective competitive examinations for the preparation and training of employees abroad for certain specialisations not available in the Institute in accordance with the principles determined in the laws and regulations in force, provided that the rules of the said cooperation shall be determined in the texts that will be issued in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article.

The Research and Guidance Department created in the Central Inspection pursuant to Legislative Decree No. 115 dated 12/6/1959 shall be transferred and attached to the Civil Service Board.

Provided that the said Department shall continue to exercise its functions and powers in the Central Inspection Administration until the end of the functions of the Preparation and Training Department in the Civil Service Board.

And all texts in force on the date of entry into force of this Law shall continue to be applied in the said Department, and the expressions "Central Inspection", "Board of the Central Inspection", and "President of the Central Inspection" shall be replaced by the expressions "Civil Service Board", "Board of the Civil Service Board", and "President of the Civil Service Board".
The appropriations allocated in the General Budget for the Research and Guidance Department shall be transferred to the budget of the Civil Service Board.

The Board of the Civil Service Board shall be amended, effective from the issuance of the regulations provided for in the Fifth Article of this Law and the transfer of the Research and Guidance Department, and shall become as follows:

- The President of the Civil Service Board (Chairman).

- The Head of the Personnel Department (Member).

- The Head of the Research and Guidance Department (Member).

The Board of the Central Inspection shall be amended, effective from the transfer of the Research and Guidance Department to the Civil Service Board, and shall become as follows:

- The President of the Central Inspection (Chairman).

- The Financial Inspector General (Member).

- The Educational Inspector General (Member).

The employees of the Preparation and Training Department shall be distributed among the various public administrations and shall be appointed to positions in the same category in which they were, in accordance with the rules determined in the laws and regulations in force.

In addition to the provisions contained in Article /11/ of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/06/1959 (Personnel Regulations) and its amendments, positions of the Second Category in the general administrative cadre may be filled from among the graduates of the Preparation Branch, Special Higher Degree, in the Institute.

The paragraph added to the first paragraph of Article /11/ of the Personnel Regulations pursuant to the draft law promulgated by Decree No. 58 dated 15/12/1982 is hereby repealed and replaced by the following paragraph:

"And the Board of the Civil Service Board may exempt from the condition of the said training course employees who have successfully completed a training course in administrative affairs of a duration of not less than six continuous months at one of the institutes of public administration abroad and who were delegated to these institutes on specialisation scholarships in accordance with the rules, provided that this exemption is coupled with the approval of the Council of Ministers ".

 Exceptionally, by a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, graduates of institutes of public administration abroad may be appointed to one of the positions referred to in the preceding Article, provided that they have spent therein a period of at least nine months of continuous study in administrative affairs similar to the study programme adopted at the Institute of Public Administration in Lebanon, which combines theoretical and practical training.

The details of implementation of this Law shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers and after the approval of each of the Presidents of the Civil Service Board and the Central Inspection, each within his competence, and after the approval of the Civil Service Board within the scope of its powers.

The provisions of this Law shall apply to pending lawsuits that have not been finally adjudicated.

And all general and special legislative and regulatory texts contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its provisions are hereby repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

In all cases of compulsory mortgage, the President of the Court shall have the right, where urgent causes exist, to order upon an application submitted to him the effecting of such precautionary registrations or provisional registrations as may be necessary, and these registrations shall have effect only until the issuance of the final judgment which is required to be registered. If the final judgment orders the maintenance of all the registrations or the maintenance of a part thereof, the mortgage as defined in the judgment shall then acquire its rank starting from the date of the precautionary entry.

A mortgagee creditor may not assign his right to another except with the express consent of the debtor, unless the contract contains an express provision empowering him to do so (as where it is mentioned, for example, in the contract that the mortgage deed is "to order")

The assignment shall take place either by its entry in the Real Estate Register or the Register of Mortgages, or by the endorsement of the certificate of entry; and in this latter case, the signature of the endorser must be authenticated within the conditions prescribed in Articles 59, 60, and 61 of Decision No. 188 issued by the High Commissioner of the French Republic on 15 March 1926

Creditors holding a mortgage running on an immovable property shall have the right to follow it into whatever hands it may have passed, in order to enter their debt in its rank and recover it in accordance with such entry.

The debtor or the holder in possession shall have the right to dispose with full freedom of the mortgaged immovable property, and he may, in accordance with the rules prescribed below, discharge his obligation before its maturity without permission from the mortgagee creditors.

If the debtor sells the mortgaged immovable property or right after the conclusion of the mortgage contract, the holder in possession newly entering into the matter shall have the option either to pay to the pursuing creditor the principal of his debt in full, together with interest and costs, or to become subject to the compulsory expropriation proceedings which the creditor applies to have carried out.

If the mortgaged immovable property or properties perish or sustain damage such that they become insufficient to secure the creditor, this creditor shall have the right to demand immediately the recovery of his money after obtaining a decision to that effect from the judiciary, or to obtain an additional mortgage.

Insurance indemnities shall in principle be allocated to the restoration of the immovable property, provided that they are sufficient to return it to its former state. The restoration shall be carried out and the money expended under the supervision of the mortgagee creditor or creditors within the conditions agreed upon jointly between them and the debtor, and if no agreement is reached in this respect, the judge shall decide thereon.

If the insurance indemnities are insufficient, or if the debtor waives his right to restore the immovable property, payment shall be made to the holders of privileged debts and the mortgagees, each according to the rank of his debt, out of the amount of the insurance indemnities, and there shall fall due from the debtor out of the debt an amount equivalent to the value of the indemnity.

If the holder in possession effects an alteration in the substance of the mortgaged immovable property, the damages which occur by reason of him or which arise from his negligence and cause prejudice to the mortgagee creditors shall entitle them to bring an action against him claiming compensation; as for him, he shall have the right to claim the expenses which he was compelled to expend for the maintenance and care of the immovable property.

A mortgage shall be extinguished by its striking off.

Striking off is obtained:

1- By the extinction of the obligation which the mortgage secures.

2- By the creditor's waiver of his right.

Registrations shall be struck off by the consent of the two parties having the necessary capacity therefor, or pursuant to a final judgment or a judgment having acquired final status; provided that they may be struck off without the consent of the creditors where the amount of the debt is deposited after a real tender thereof has been made to the creditors and they have refused to accept it.

This deposit, which takes place after the making of a real tender of payment of the debt, shall discharge the liability of the debtor and shall stand, in so far as concerns him, in the place of payment if the tender was made in a lawful manner. As for the amount or thing deposited in this manner, it shall be at the charge and responsibility of the creditor.
