1 - Pursuant to the provisions of this Decree, the rules for the management and safekeeping of materials, the procedures for keeping their accounts, and the scope of liability of those in charge of their affairs shall be determined in each of the public administrations, municipalities, and public institutions affiliated with the State or with municipalities.

2 - These provisions shall cover materials within Lebanese territory and in Lebanese missions abroad, with the exception of:

a - Documents, publications, and collections of national museums, which are subject to special rules.

b - Documents of historical and administrative archives, library publications, and technical information publications, which are tracked in indexes in accordance with conditions determined by special instructions issued by the President of the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister.

c - Machinery or equipment fixed in a specific place which have become immovable property by destination or a part thereof, such as heating and cooling installations, cold rooms, elevators, etc...

3 - These provisions shall not apply to the materiel of armies in active service, nor to the materiel used in maritime and aerial vessels.

In this Decree, the following terms shall mean:

- By the word "materials": all equipment, supplies, requisites, and items belonging to public administrations, municipalities, or public institutions affiliated with the State or with municipalities, as defined in Article One of this Decree..

- By the word "accountant": the materials accountant in public administrations, municipalities, or public institutions affiliated with the State or with municipalities indicated in the preceding paragraph of this Article, and this expression shall include the principal accountant and the secondary accountant in accordance with what is provided for in Article 17 of this Decree.

- By the word "Head of Administration": the head of every unit directly linked to the Minister, provided that it is at the level of a Department (Maslaha) or above.

Basic classification of materials:

1 - Classification of materials into two categories:

a - The category of consumable materials, which comprises the following items:

- Stationery.

- Printed matter.

- Supplies.

- And others.

b - The category of fixed assets, which comprises the following items:

- Machinery

- Equipment

- Installations

- Furniture

- And others

2 - The entries for each of the two categories above shall be recorded as follows:

a - The first category shall appear as materials in stock.

b - And the second category shall appear in two statuses:

- Materials in use.

- Materials in stock.

Numbering:

- Serial numbers shall be adopted to identify materials and classify them according to their nature or according to their belonging to groups intended for common use.

- A series of numbers shall be allocated to identify consumable materials, and another series of numbers shall be allocated to identify fixed assets.

- The series of numbers shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance and shall be adopted in all administrations to facilitate the preparation of consolidated statements.

Materials in stock:

1 - Materials in stock shall include the following items:

a - Stock of consumable materials present in the main and/or branch warehouses. These materials shall be considered as current or deferred assets and shall be recorded under expenditures upon their withdrawal from stock.

b - Materials in transit expected to be received when payment of their value falls due.

c - Materials removed from custody due to their condition.

2 - A decision by the Director General shall periodically determine the types of materials that are considered consumable materials, the minimum and maximum limits thereof that must be available in stock, and the indication of the condition of the materials that must be classified as outside custody pending their destruction and removal from stock.

Fixed assets:

1 - Fixed assets shall include the following components:

- Machinery

- Equipment

- Installations

- Furniture - etc...

2 - Fixed assets shall be considered non-current assets and are in the nature of capital expenditures that are depreciated annually on the basis of the depreciation rates determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

3 - The purpose of considering fixed assets as capital expenditures shall be defined as:

- Providing permanent control over the existence, soundness, and value of the components of these assets.

- Keeping special accounts for the State's capital expenditures throughout the period of use of the fixed assets and until the date their value is written off.

4 - The purpose of the annual depreciation of fixed assets shall be defined as knowing the true cost of the State's administrative expenditures and evaluating the extent of the administration's effectiveness in production by calculating the cost of services.

5 - The accounting of fixed assets shall be kept on the basis of their true cost if known, or on the basis of their estimated cost, or on the basis of their market value in respect of donations, and the depreciation accounts of fixed assets shall be kept in a manner that ensures the existence of an accumulated expropriation (depreciation) account corresponding to each type of these assets.

Materials in use:

1 - Materials in use shall include depreciable materials and non-depreciable materials in the possession of the administration and intended for the execution of its mission.

These materials are brought from supplies or from the vendor directly, and in the latter case, the delivery of the materials must be preceded by the prior receipt provided for in Article Nine of this Decree.

2 - Materials in use shall be determined and distributed among the units in the administrations pursuant to a schedule of allocations drawn up by a decision of the Director General or whomever he delegates for this purpose from among the Grade Two employees.

The task of supervising the work of materials accountants and following up on the movement of materials in each administration shall be entrusted to the head of one of the Grade Two units subordinate to the Director General, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister.

Movement orders:

The operation of bringing in and taking out materials in the administration shall take place pursuant to an order issued by the Director General or whomever he delegates for this purpose upon the request of the unit concerned.

Such materials may not be moved unless prior receipt in respect thereof has taken place by a committee appointed in accordance with the bases determined in Article 139 of the Public Accounting Law, and receipt shall take place pursuant to serially numbered minutes signed by the recipient and containing a description of the condition of the materials, their quantity, and the date of their receipt.

Transport:

1 - The provisions of Articles 683, 684, 685, and 687 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts shall apply to the transport of materials which takes place by one of the following methods:

- Administrative transport, which is that carried out by the administration by its own means or by the means of another administration.

- Commercial transport, which is that carried out by other than the means of the administration and through private carriers.

- Joint transport, which is that carried out by other than the means of the administration and under the supervision of its employees.

2 - And in each of the aforementioned methods of transport:

- The carrier shall take charge of the materials delivered to him after verifying their soundness upon receipt and shall be liable for them until their receipt by the consignee.

- The consignor shall remain liable for shortage, loss, and damage which is shown upon delivery to have resulted on his part.

- The consignee shall only take charge of the materials actually delivered and which fulfill the conditions of final receipt, and he shall be liable for shortage, loss, and damage which he did not duly indicate upon receipt.

Lease, Assignment, and Loan of Materials:

1 - Materials may be the subject of lease, assignment, or loan.

2 - The rental fee shall be on the basis of prices for the materials determined in accordance with the rules and procedures provided for in Articles 47 to 50 of the Public Accounting Law. The cases in which materials are leased and the conditions of leasing shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

3 - Assignment without consideration between public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities shall be by a decision of the two competent Ministers or those acting in their stead according to the provisions of the forty-ninth Article of this Decree.

4 - Loan shall be gratuitous and shall be limited to public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities.

The loan shall take place by a special contract comprising the authorisation for the borrowing body to possess the loaned materials in the capacity of a custodian, with the obligations and responsibilities entailed by this capacity, and shall be approved by a decision of the Minister concerned with respect to public administrations, and by a decision of the tutelary Minister with respect to public institutions and municipalities.

The said contract shall be concluded by the Director General or whoever he delegates for that purpose in the administration owning the materials, and shall be subject to the approval of the tutelary Minister if the borrowing party is a public institution or a municipality.

Sale and Destruction:

Materials shall be placed for sale or destroyed when necessary by a decision of the competent Minister upon the proposal of a special committee formed by a decision of the Director General comprising at least three members, among whom is the Chief Accountant, to which a specialist expert member shall be added when necessary.

Inventory:

1 - An annual comprehensive inventory of materials shall be conducted at the end of the year, and comprehensive or partial inventories by way of spot-checking shall also be conducted when necessary at the request of the Head of the Administration or the Central Inspection Administration.

2 - The inventory shall be conducted by the accountants under the supervision of the Head of the Administration or whoever he delegates for that purpose. As a result of the inventory, a record shall be drawn up and submitted to the Head of the Administration to take the necessary measures regarding it, and a copy thereof shall be referred to the Court of Audit.

3 - The Head of the Administration shall review and evaluate the inventory, identify the obsolete and slow-moving items thereof, and take the appropriate measures regarding them. The inspectors of the Central Inspection Administration may conduct an inventory of materials upon a complaint or on the occasion of the periodic and surprise inspection tours which they undertake, and they shall record the results of the inventory in their report.

4 - A copy of the records and reports of conducting the inventories and their results shall be communicated to the Minister through the Head of the Administration in the administration and to the Court of Audit, provided that any discrepancy in the entries or violation falling under penalty of the sanctions provided for in the Law on the Organisation of the Court of Audit is explicitly indicated.

Objectives and Foundations of Accounting:

Materials accounting aims to:

- Show the assets and their movement.

- Determine the responsibilities resulting therefrom.

This accounting is based on:

- Permanent documents of the current status.

- And supporting documents of the movement.

Accounting Operations:

Materials accounting consists of the following basic operations:

a - Taking materials into the custody of the competent employee.

b - Preserving and using the materials.

c - Executing the movements ordered by the competent authorities.

d - Keeping and centralising the entries.

e - Submitting the accounts.

Registers Required to be Available:

1 - With respect to materials in stock.

a - The accountant of the concerned administration shall keep:

- Individual cards bearing the numbering determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance, showing the movement of incoming and outgoing materials in terms of quantity and value, in the following manner:

- Date.

- Description.

- Incoming quantity.

- Unit value.

- Total value.

- Outgoing quantity.

- Unit value.

- Total value.

- Quantity in stock.

- Average unit value.

- Total value of stock.

- A subsidiary general ledger account for each group of materials in which the movement of quantity balances is registered pursuant to entry vouchers to which the supporting documents and special approvals regarding them are attached.

b - Periodic comparisons and reconciliations shall be carried out by the accountant of the administration between the quantities appearing on the cards kept in the accounting office and those kept in the warehouses.

As for the warehouses and depots, individual cards shall be kept by quantities only.

2 - With respect to fixed assets:

a - The accountant of the concerned administration shall keep a subsidiary general ledger account for the subdivisions of the items of fixed assets with respect to the estimated cost, showing the current movement on these accounts pursuant to entry vouchers, corresponded by special accounts for depreciations.

b - As for the materials management unit, individual cards shall be kept for each of the components of the fixed assets bearing serial numbers within a general framework determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

In these cards shall be recorded, in particular, the following information:

- Description.

- Date of purchase.

- Cost.

- Place of its location.

- Name of the employee who uses it.

- Rate of depreciation.

- Annual depreciation.

- A column designated for maintenance.

- Date of disposal.

- Method of disposal.

- Value of sale or disposal.

c - The resources management unit shall prepare at the end of each year a detailed schedule of the fixed assets the total of which must match the balances of the subsidiary ledger accounts kept by the accountant of the administration.

Responsible Employees:

1 - The operations of materials accounting as defined in the preceding Article 15 shall be undertaken by accountants and custodians.

2 - Accountants are of two types:

Chief and secondary.

- The Chief Accountant is the one who performs the accounting operations and undertakes the keeping and unifying of materials entries at the level of a single administration.

- And the Secondary Accountant is the one who performs the accounting operations at the level of one or more units in the administration and is subordinate to the Chief Accountant.

3 - Custodians are those who preserve or use the materials and are of two grades:

- Custodians of the first grade who draw up the inventory at the end of the year and upon conducting the handover and takeover operation, and keep the accounts of the materials placed in their custody.

- And custodians of the second grade, who are those who use the materials and are responsible for them.

4 - The Chief Accountant or the Secondary Accountant may at the same time be a custodian of materials in service and materials in reserve in the cases determined by a joint decision issued by the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister.

5 - The mission of Chief Accountant shall be entrusted to one of the employees of the third category in the concerned administration holding a degree in business administration or in informatics, or the Technical Superior Diploma.

- Audit and Accounting Expertise branch who have occupied a financial post of the third category for a period of at least five years.

6 - The capacity of Secondary Accountant shall be granted by a decision of the competent Minister upon the proposal of the Director General to one of the employees of the fourth category in the concerned administration. And the capacity of custodian of the first grade shall be granted by a decision of the competent Director General to one of the employees of the fourth category in the concerned unit.

7 - In selecting accountants and custodians, consideration shall be given to their being of good conduct and their holding of academic qualifications or experience in accounting not less than the Technical Baccalaureate certificate (commercial accounting branches).

8 - Accountants must preserve the registers and supporting papers relating to materials accounts in tightly locked fireproof safes and they must maintain the confidentiality of the work and not disclose it to anyone other than their hierarchical superiors and the oversight bodies.

9 - The mission of the Chief Accountant, the Secondary Accountant, and the custodian of the first grade shall be terminated in the manner prescribed for granting them this capacity. 10 - Whoever undertakes the operations of materials accounting without having the capacity of an accountant shall be deemed a de facto accountant responsible for his acts like the official accountant and subject to the obligations of the latter.

Prohibitions:

1 - The office of Accountant may not be combined with any office or duties related to the purchase, lease, sale, storage in warehouses, removal therefrom, and disposal of materials, or participation in preliminary acceptance operations provided for in the laws and regulations governing public procurement, subject to the provisions of Articles Twelve and Twenty-Three of this Decree.

2 - The Accountant and the Custodian are prohibited from engaging in any work or activity that conflicts with their duties.

Security:

1 - Both Principal and Secondary Materials Accountants, as well as First-Class Custodians, are under an obligation to provide security, the value of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

2 - The security may be in cash deposited with one of the public treasuries, or a bank guarantee, or real estate security.

3 - By a decision of the Minister of Finance, the cash, bank, or real estate security may be replaced by considering the salaries and end-of-service indemnities accruing to each of the Principal and Secondary Materials Accountants and First-Class Custodians as a guarantee for any unjustified shortage in the materials placed in their custody, provided that two of the following three conditions are met:

a - The years of service of the employee concerned have reached at least twenty years.

b - The monthly income of the employee concerned from the office has reached at least three times the minimum wage in force at any given time.

c - The annual turnover of materials in the administration concerned does not exceed two hundred times the minimum wage in force at any given time.

Handover and Takeover of Duties:

1 - The handover and takeover of duties between Accountants shall take place in the presence of the immediate superior pursuant to a report drawn up as a result of the inventory and signed by the two Accountants concerned. In the event of a discrepancy between the actual inventory and the accounting records, the provisions of Article Thirteen of this Decree shall apply.

2 - The handover and takeover of duties between Custodians shall take place in the presence of their immediate superior and under his responsibility, and the results shall be recorded on the special inventory or on the inventory summary. In the event of a dispute between the Custodians, the immediate superior shall draw up an inventory report in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph of this Article.

Absence, Inability, Suspension from Duty, Disappearance, and Death:

1 - In the event of the absence of the Accountant, whether Principal or Secondary, on administrative leave, the leave decision shall designate the employee who shall replace him to carry out his duties as Accountant throughout the period of his absence.

2 - In the event of the absence of the Principal Accountant on sick leave, the highest-ranking Secondary Accountant among the Secondary Accountants subordinate to him in the central administration shall deputize for him, and shall carry out his duties throughout the period of his absence, or until a successor is appointed in accordance with the applicable rules in this regard.

3 - In the event of the absence of the Secondary Accountant on sick leave, the highest-ranking First-Class Custodian among the Custodians subordinate to him in the central administration shall deputize for him, and shall carry out his duties throughout the period of his absence, or until the capacity of Secondary Accountant is conferred upon another employee.

4 - In the event that the Accountant is unable to perform his duties, or in the event of his suspension from duty, disappearance, or death, the Director General shall assign the highest-ranking subordinate of the Accountant to carry out his duties on a temporary basis until the Accountant or his successor is able to exercise these duties. The assigned employee shall, throughout the period of performing the duties set forth above, be deemed an Accountant and shall bear the obligations and responsibilities prescribed for the Accountant, and the process of his taking over his duties shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of Article Twenty of this Decree, provided that the predecessor Accountant is represented by a delegate from the administration concerned appointed by the Director General.

5 - The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply to the First-Class Custodian, provided that his duties are carried out by the next highest-ranking employee after him.

6 - The assigned employee shall, throughout the period of performing the duties set forth in items 1, 2, and 3 above, be held responsible for the performance of the duties assigned to him in the same manner as the responsibility of the incumbent employee.

Execution of Movement Orders:

1 - Movement orders shall not be executed until they have been endorsed by the Accountant.

2 - The Accountant must categorically refuse endorsement and return the transaction to its source, stating the reasons therefor, if the order pertaining to it was issued by an incompetent authority; and he must refuse endorsement and return the transaction to the authority competent to issue the order, stating the reasons for refusal, in the following cases:

- If the order pertaining to it does not fulfill its regulatory requirements, other than having been issued by an incompetent authority.

- Or if the prescribed documents are not attached to the order

- Or if the content of the order is inconsistent with the particulars stated in the attached documents. If the said authority confirms the order in the aforementioned cases, the Accountant must execute it and notify the Public Prosecution at the Court of Accounts and the Central Inspection Administration by means of a certified copy of the transaction, the reasons for refusal, and the confirmation of its execution.

Unity of Management in the Principal Accounting Office:

Ordinary operations of final entry and exit of accounts shall be conducted and their records entered in the Principal Accounting Office, with the exception of the following two cases:

- The case of conducting an entry operation by direct delivery from outside the Principal Accounting Office.

- And the case of conducting an adjustment entry operation based on a report establishing the occurrence of a shortage upon conducting a handover and takeover operation.

- Where the Principal Accountant or his duly authorized representative is the secretary of the acceptance committee in the first case, and is a rapporteur in the second case.

The Secondary Accountant may not conduct any final entry or exit operation in his accounts except pursuant to supporting documents issued or certified by the Principal Accountant.

Unity of Management in the Warehouse:

In the case where the quantity of supplies requires several warehouses or a group of warehouses placed in the custody of several employees, these employees shall work under the supervision of the Principal Accountant or the Secondary Accountant, who shall be responsible for keeping the unified records and for their accuracy and control from the time they are taken into custody until the submission of the accounts.

Warehouses:

The process of materials accounting shall take place within the scope of warehouses classified as follows:

a - Principal warehouses (central or general warehouses) operating across the scope of a single administration, for which the Principal Accountant is the accountant, and in principle there shall be only one principal warehouse in each administration.

b - Secondary or regional warehouses, for which the Secondary Accountant is the accountant.

c - Permanent or temporary auxiliary warehouses, according to their status, role, and importance, in which the First-Class Custodian is responsible for the materials, and which are attached to the nearest principal or secondary warehouse.

Tenure of the Accountant:

The tenure of the Accountant encompasses the operations he performs in his accounting office from the first of January until the 31st of December of the year, or during the period in which he performs his office if such period is less than one year.

Account of the Accountant's Tenure:

1 - The Secondary Accountant shall draw up "in his own name and under his own responsibility" a tenure account of the operations of his tenure, which he shall lodge with the Principal Accountant to whom he is subordinate. The Principal Accountant shall consolidate the tenure accounts of the Secondary Accountants subordinate to him, and shall draw up therefrom, and from the operations of his own tenure, a consolidated tenure account which he shall lodge in his own name and under his own responsibility with the Court of Accounts in accordance with the conditions provided for in the regulations governing the submission of accounts to the said Court, and shall send a copy of this account to the Directorate of Public Accounting at the Ministry of Finance.

2 - The Principal Accountant shall propose to the Director General the settlement of the tenure accounts of the Secondary Accountants subordinate to him and the discharge or holding liable of their accounts in respect of these accounts.

And the Court of Accounts shall settle the consolidated tenure account of the Principal Accountant and discharge him or hold him liable in respect of this account.

Professional Secrecy:

Accountants and the employees subordinate to them shall be bound by professional secrecy and it shall be prohibited for them, under penalty of the sanctions provided for by law, to issue any statements on the statuses of materials in their custody or to give any information relating to the service to persons other than those who have the right to inspect them.

Supervision, Inspection and Oversight:

1 - The principal accountant and the employees subordinate to him, including secondary accountants and custodians, shall be subject to the supervision of the Court of Accounts and the Central Inspection in accordance with the legal provisions relating to the supervision of central and local accountants.

2 - In addition to the supervision and inspection carried out by the competent bodies, the administration must conduct permanent oversight over its administrative units with respect to the existence of the materials belonging to it and their status, condition and maintenance.

Principles:

1 - Materials accounting shall be kept in accordance with the provisions of these regulations and the accountant shall retain the supporting documents.

The entries shall be based on quantities such that the units of account are the units set forth in the codification: item, metre, kilogram, litre, etc... and the identification and classification of materials in the entries shall always be carried out on the basis of the codification.

2 - The accounting period shall be annual, extending from the first of January until 31 December of the year.

Movement Documents:

1 - Every operation relating to the movement of materials or their preservation must be the result of a prior written decision issued by the competent authority in which the quantity (in figures and in words) and the type of movement are stated. Every movement modifying the total existing quantities must be based on a supporting document bearing matching attestations from the two parties concerned with delivery and receipt and referring to the decision ordering the execution of the movement.

2 - The supporting documents substantiating the inventory shall be registered with the accountant according to the order of their chronological sequence in a daily register numbered and initialled by the authority charged with administrative supervision over the accountant. This register shall be closed on 31 December of the year or on the date of carrying out the operation of handover and receipt of duties between accountants in the event that this operation is carried out before 31 December of the year.

3 - The documents provided for in this Article shall be determined in the implementing instructions provided for in Article 43 of this Decree, and their form and contents shall be designated in the same manner so as to permit the keeping of accounts on the basis of quantity and, where necessary, on the basis of value.

The Central Card Index and Inventories:

1 - The custodian of the second class shall draw up an inventory summary of the materials that he uses.

2 - The custodian of the first class shall keep a special inventory in which are cross-checked the inventory summaries belonging to the custodians of the second class subordinate to him for accounting purposes, the materials placed in his custody, and those that he uses personally.

3 - The secondary accountant shall keep a general inventory comprising:

- Materials in use, on the basis of the special inventories of the custodians of the first class.

- Materials in reserve, which are tracked by the custodians by means of cabinet labels and storage cards.

4 - The principal accountant shall keep the central card index in which are cross-checked the general inventories belonging to the administration to which he is subordinate.

5 - The special inventory, the general inventory, and the central card index shall consist of loose-leaf cards opened according to the codification number, and must always indicate the total holdings and their distribution.

6 - Every movement that modifies the quantity of the holdings, their status, and their distribution must be recorded in the inventory at the same time in which its execution takes place, and the time limit for recording must not exceed forty-eight hours.

7 - The duration of use of inventory cards is unlimited; however, a prominent distinction must be made between the operations belonging to each year.

Prices:

The unit prices of materials shall be stated in the supporting movement documents from which a financial operation results.

The rules determined in the implementing instructions provided for in Article Forty-Three of this Decree shall be adopted in determining these prices.

Audit and Closing of Entries:

1 - The audit of entries must be carried out locally during the year by the supervisory authorities, and in particular on the occasion of the inventory and supervision carried out pursuant to Articles Thirteen and Twenty-Nine of this Decree.

2 - The holdings shown in the inventories on the date of 31 December shall be carried forward to the subsequent inventory on the date of the first of January.

The inventories shall be closed before 31 March with respect to value, and the results shall be shown separately for materials in reserve on the one hand and for materials in use on the other hand.

General Summaries and the General Account:

1 - The value of the result of the annual inventories for each directorate general shall be calculated in a general summary before 30 June of the following year.

This general summary shall be drawn up such that materials in reserve are distinguished therein from materials in use.

2 - On the basis of the general summaries, and before the first of September of the year, a general account of the administration shall be drawn up comprising the value of materials in reserve on the one hand and the value of materials in use on the other hand on the date of 31 December of the past year and on the date of 31 December of the year preceding it.

Keeping of Entries and Documents: Entries and documents shall compulsorily be kept in ink and may not be kept at all in pencil, nor may scraping, interlineation, erasure, or overwriting be made therein; however, any error that may occur therein may be corrected, provided that this correction is carried out by the competent authority in a visible manner in figures and in spelled-out words and in ink of a colour different from the colour used in the original, and that it is accompanied by the date and the signature of the person making it, his name, and his capacity.

Impossibility of Producing Entries and Documents:

If force majeure circumstances prevent the accountant from producing the prescribed entries or documents, they shall be replaced by special minutes drawn up in accordance with the conditions determined in the implementing instructions provided for in Article Forty-Three of this Decree.

The Director General shall decide upon the effect to be given to the minutes within the limits set forth in Article Thirteen of this Decree.

Principles:

Subject to the provisions of Article 216 of the Public Accounting Law, and in addition to the civil obligations and penal and disciplinary sanctions that may be imposed by the competent authorities, every person who assumes the management of materials, his assistants, materials accountants, and custodians thereof shall be liable within the limits set forth in the following Articles.

Persons Assuming the Management of Materials and Their Assistants:

Persons assuming the management of materials shall be considered among the persons assuming the management of public funds, and their assistants shall be considered among the interveners and participants in the management of public funds provided for in the Law Organizing the Court of Accounts, and shall be liable for their acts in accordance with the provisions of the said Law and all other laws and regulations in force.

Accountants:

The accountant shall be liable within the scope of the accounting office that he assumes in general for his duties determined in this Decree:

1 - Administratively for:

- The accuracy of his entries.

- The preservation of the documents belonging to his entries.

- The supervision and audit of the accounts kept by the accountants and custodians subordinate to him, where they exist.

2 - Financially for:

- The existence of the materials placed in his custody and the preservation, use, and maintenance of these materials.

- The validity of the movement orders that he has put into execution.

Custodians:

1 - The custodian of the first class shall be liable:

a - Administratively for:

- The accuracy of his entries.

- The preservation of the documents belonging to his entries.

b - Financially for:

- The existence of the materials placed in his custody and the preservation, use, and maintenance of these materials.

- The conformity of execution with the movement orders.

2 - Custodians of the second class shall be financially liable for the existence of the materials placed in their custody and for proving their condition.

A foreigner shall not be granted the right of real property inheritance, whether by will or without a will, unless the laws of his country grant the like to Syrians and Lebanese. The real property estate of a foreigner, whether by will or without a will, shall be subject to the provisions of the laws of his country.
The provisions of the local laws relating to gifts shall apply to foreigners.
The right to establish pious endowments (waqfs) and the form of the instrument establishing them are determined by the provisions of the local laws.

The occupation of a place confers upon the first person who occupied it under a legal licence from the State a right of preference over others to acquire the right of disposal (tasarruf) over vacant escheated (mahlul) real properties.

If the holder of the right of preference proves, after the expiry of the period of three years, that he has revived land, built buildings thereon, planted trees therein, or arranged it within the conditions specified in the special regulations governing State domains, he shall acquire free of charge the right to register the right of disposal (tasarruf) over the portion which he has revived, planted, built buildings upon, or arranged, provided that he shall lose the right of disposal if, after registration and within the period of ten years following registration, he ceases to exercise his right for a period of three consecutive years.

The occupation of a place shall not confer the acquisition of any right whatsoever over a real property registered in the Land Register or under the administration of State domains, nor over forests and dedicated (marfuqah) or protected (mahmiyah) public-use (matrukah) real properties.

If a treasure is found in the land, three-fifths thereof shall belong to the owner of the land, one-fifth to its finder, and the last fifth to the Public Treasury, subject to observance of the conditions provided for in the laws in force and the special regulations governing mines and antiquities.

Pre-emption (shuf'ah) is a right which entitles its holder to take the sold real property from the purchaser in the cases and under the conditions provided for in the following Articles:

The right of pre-emption shall apply to full-ownership (mulk) real properties and to State-owned (amiri) real properties. The rights of priority (rujhan) and tapu provided for in the Ottoman Land Code shall remain repealed.

The right of pre-emption is established:

1- For the owner of the bare ownership, if the right of usufruct is sold, whether the sale covers the whole of the right or part thereof.

2- For the co-owner in undivided ownership, if one or more shares in the undivided real property are sold to a person other than the co-owners in undivided ownership.

3- For the holder of the right of usufruct, if the bare ownership is sold, whether the sale covers the whole of the bare ownership or part thereof. Every other right of pre-emption which arose before the entry into force of this Law and has not yet been exercised shall lapse.

If pre-emptors of different classes compete, the exercise of the right of pre-emption shall be in accordance with the order provided for in the preceding Article 239. If pre-emptors of the same class compete, the right of each of them shall be in proportion to his share, and if one or some of them relinquish his or their right, the remaining ones shall exercise this right in proportion to their shares.
The right of pre-emption belongs to the persons mentioned in Article two hundred and thirty-nine of this Decision whose title is prior in date to the title of the purchaser.
The right of pre-emption passes upon the death of its holder to his heirs, and it may not be assigned to another person.

The right of pre-emption may only be exercised against the purchaser or against the donee for consideration. In the latter case, the right of pre-emption shall be subject to the same grounds of nullity, voidability, and revocation applicable to the gift itself. An action for pre-emption shall not be heard in a real property exchange or in a sale taking place between spouses, or between ascendants and descendants, or between brothers and sisters.

The right of pre-emption is indivisible and may neither be exercised nor waived except in its entirety. If there are several pre-emptors equal in class and one or some of them waive his or their right to pre-emption, the remaining ones must claim pre-emption or waive it in its entirety. However, if there are several purchasers, the pre-emptor may take the share of one of them only.

The right of pre-emption shall lapse:

1- If the pre-emptor does not exercise it within the statutory period set forth in the following two Articles.

2- If the pre-emptor expressly waives it prior to the registration of the pre-empted property in a written instrument having a certain date containing a statement of the name of the purchaser, the price, and the conditions, and the date of which does not go back- to more than six months prior to registration.

3- If the pre-emptor was the agent of the seller in the sale or a witness to the contract and affixed his signature without reservation.

4- If the pre-emptor waives his right after registration expressly or impliedly. However, such waiver is not permissible after the filing of the action for pre-emption except with the consent of the purchaser.

The purchaser may, after the registration of the contract, notify the pre-emptors of the registration through the Notary Public for those residing in Lebanon, and in accordance with Article 362 of the Code of Civil Procedure for those residing in foreign countries, provided that he states in the notification the sold real property and its description, the date of registration, the names of the contracting parties and their place of residence, the price and its accessories, and the conditions of the contract. The pre-emptor must claim the right of pre-emption within the ten days following the notification, after adding the distance time-limit, on pain of forfeiture.

If the notification set forth in the preceding Article does not take place, the right of pre-emption shall lapse after the expiry of one year from the date of registration of the contract in the Land Register. This period shall run against incapacitated persons and absent persons. The period mentioned in this Article and in the preceding Article shall only be interrupted by the filing of an action claiming pre-emption before the competent court of the place where the real property is inventoried (situated) according to the price stated in the contract.

The right of pre-emption may only be exercised on condition that its holder fully indemnifies the purchaser.

This indemnification includes:

1- The price of the sold property, which must be tendered and actually deposited on the day of filing the action for pre-emption at the latest, unless the registered contract stipulates the deferment of payment.

The tender and actual deposit shall be made into the treasury fund of the court competent to hear the action for pre-emption.

2 - The expenses of the contract, which include the official registration fees and the brokerage fee, provided that such fee does not exceed the fee specified by the statutory tariff.

3 - The value of the improvement supervening upon the real property by the act of the purchaser, without regard to economic appreciation resulting from the fluctuation of prices.

If the pre-empted property is assigned to a third party who records it in the Land Register prior to the filing of the action for pre-emption, pre-emption may only be taken from the second purchaser and under the conditions upon which he purchased.

If a dispute arises over the amount of the price of the pre-empted property between the purchaser and the holder of the right of pre-emption, the court shall determine the true price regardless of the value of the pre-empted property. A claim by the purchaser that this price exceeds the price stated in the registered contract shall not be heard.

The right of pre-emption is established and the pre-emptor acquires the right of registration, either by his taking delivery of the pre-empted real property with the consent of the purchaser after paying the price and its accessories specified in Article 249, or by a judgment rendered in favour of the pre-emptor.

The pre-emptor shall be deemed to have purchased from the purchaser, and pre-emption shall have between them the effects of the sale itself; the pre-emptor shall not be entitled to benefit from the term stipulated in the contract in favour of the purchaser for payment of the price, unless the court deems fit against the guarantees which it considers necessary. Save in the case of the term stipulated in the contract, the court may not grant the pre-emptor a grace period for payment.
There is no pre-emption for a pious endowment (waqf), nor in a sale taking place by public auction through the administration or the judiciary.

Prescription (passage of time) shall not run against the following real property rights, nor shall ownership thereof be acquired by adverse possession:

1 - Rights recorded in the Land Register.

2 - Properties belonging to the State in accordance with the provisions of Article 2 of Decision No. 275 dated 25/2/1926, whether they have been ascertained, delimited, and censused or have not yet been subjected to these operations.

3 - Private properties of municipalities.

4 - Common lands (musha') owned collectively by villages. The courts hearing real property ownership cases, including the Real Property Judges, must of their own motion join the Directorate General of Real Property Affairs - Service of Immovable Private State Domains, and the municipalities concerned as a party in every action or application to establish a right of ownership claimed on the basis of adverse possession, prior to rendering their judgments or decisions on the merits of the action.
Not the slightest right over public-use (matrukah), protected (mahmiyah), and dedicated (marfuqah) real properties shall be acquired by prescription (passage of time).

Absence of Liability:

Liability resulting from loss or damage shall not be extinguished except in the cases provided for in the Code of Obligations and Contracts.

General Implementing Instructions:

1 - The detailed rules for implementing the provisions of this Title shall be determined by general instructions issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - Specific detailed rules within the scope of each administration may be determined by special instructions issued by the competent Minister, in a manner not inconsistent with the provisions of this Decree and the general implementing instructions pertaining thereto.

Principles:

1 - The provisions of Title One of this Decree shall apply to materials in municipalities subject to the Public Accounting Law, subject to the special provisions set forth in the following articles.

2 - A special regime issued by a joint decision of the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Municipal and Rural Affairs shall apply to materials in municipalities that are not subject to the provisions of Title One of this Decree as set forth in Paragraph 1 of this Article.

Functions of the Minister and the Director General:

1 - The Municipal Council shall exercise, subject to the oversight of the administrative oversight authority, the functions of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance provided for in Articles Three to Forty-Two of this Decree.

2 - And the Governor, with respect to the Municipality of Beirut, and the President of the Municipality with respect to all other municipalities, shall exercise the functions of the Director General set forth in the articles mentioned in the preceding paragraph.

Sale of Materials:

By way of exception to the provisions of Article Twelve of this Decree, materials in the municipality shall be sold in accordance with the provisions of the financial regulations adopted by it, and in the absence thereof, in accordance with the provisions of the Public Accounting Law relating to the sale of materials in public administrations.

Appointment of the Accountant and Termination of His Mission:

By way of exception to the provisions of Paragraphs 5 and 6 of Article Seventeen of this Decree, the principal accountant and the secondary accountant in the municipality shall be appointed by a decision of the Governor with respect to the Municipality of Beirut and of the President of the Municipality with respect to all other municipalities after the approval of the Minister of Municipal and Rural Affairs, and his mission shall be terminated in the same manner.

Principles:

Materials in public institutions affiliated with the State or with municipalities shall be subject to the provisions of Title One of this Decree, subject to the following special provisions.

Functions of the Minister and the Director General:

1 - Subject to the oversight of both the administrative tutelage authority and the Ministry of Finance, where applicable, the decision-making authority in public institutions shall exercise the functions of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance set forth in Articles Three to Forty-Two of this Decree.

2 - The head of the executive authority in the public institution shall exercise the functions of the Director General set forth in the articles mentioned in the preceding paragraph.

Sale of Materials:

By way of exception to the provisions of Article Twelve of this Decree, materials in the public institution shall be sold in accordance with the provisions of the financial regulations adopted by it, and in the absence thereof, in accordance with the provisions of the Public Accounting Law relating to the sale of materials in public administrations.

Appointment of the Accountant and Termination of His Mission:

By way of exception to the provisions of Paragraphs 5 and 6 of Article Seventeen of this Decree, the capacity of principal accountant and secondary accountant shall be conferred by a decision of the head of the decision-making authority, and his mission shall be terminated in the same manner.

Materials Accounting in Public Institutions of an Operating Nature:

By a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Ministers of Tutelage and of Finance, public institutions of an operating nature may be subjected to keeping general accounting and analytical operating accounting for materials in accordance with the principles of a general chart of accounts, and in such case, the rules of such accounting shall be determined by a joint decision of the Ministers of Finance and of Tutelage in all matters that conflict with the provisions of this Decree.
This Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force as of the beginning of the year following the year in which it is published.

a - The head of the school may contract for a period of two years at most, and under special conditions, with persons holding academic qualifications the minimum of which is the qualification that entitles them to appointment to the permanent establishment, and their salary shall be, at the very least, in proportion to their working periods calculated on the basis of the statutory salary in the permanent establishment. Upon the expiry of the period of two years, the head of the school must either dismiss them or confirm them in the category and grade that correspond to their academic qualifications, provided that this contractual service is taken into consideration with respect to promotion upon confirmation, and in the event of dismissal or confirmation, the provisions of the second and third paragraphs of Article 12 of this Law shall apply to them."

b- If a member of the teaching staff transfers to another school, without interruption from teaching, after the expiry of at least the two years, he shall enter by operation of law into the permanent establishment and his services shall be combined in the Indemnity Fund, subject to the provisions of the new Article 39 of the Law. This school must pay him at least the minimum salary equivalent to his qualification in the permanent establishment, provided that he retains with respect to the Indemnity Fund the previous rank and grade; whereas if he returns to the same school, he shall enter by operation of law into the permanent establishment and his salary in the school shall be equivalent, as a minimum, to the salary he was receiving on the day he left the school to which he returns, subject to the provisions of the new Article 39 of the Law.

c: The provisions of this Article shall not apply to the category of teachers in free schools whose status is governed by the provisions of the third Article of Law No. 32/65, dated 11/6/1965.

Persons who teach in the last three years of the secondary education stage or its equivalent in vocational or technical education shall have the right to contract with one school or several schools, provided that the total of their working hours per week in the various schools does not exceed 30 hours or periods.

The head of the school shall also have the right to contract under special conditions with qualified persons:

1- To teach languages and cultural subjects related thereto

2- To teach artistic subjects not included in the curriculum that are approved by a decision of the Director General of National Education.

Such persons shall not enter into the permanent establishment unless agreement thereon is reached between the two parties.

Members of the teaching staff contracted with more than one institute and not included in the permanent establishment of a specific institute shall not benefit from the provisions of the texts relating to family allowances and promotion.

Whereas if they are included in the permanent establishment of one of the institutes, they shall be treated in that institute like the rest of the members of the teaching staff included in the permanent establishment.

The salary scale prescribed in the permanent establishment of the teaching staff of public schools shall apply to members of the teaching staff included in the permanent establishment. As for members of the teaching staff not included in the permanent establishment, they shall receive their wages in accordance with special contracts.

The minimum monthly salary for members of the teaching staff in the free schools mentioned in the third Article of this Law and who do not hold the academic qualifications that entitle them to enter into the permanent establishment shall be fixed at one hundred and forty-five Lebanese pounds /145/ L.L. and they shall be given the family allowance prescribed in the Labour Code, and the salary shall be increased every two years by fifteen /15/ pounds at least. Whereas if they are holders of these qualifications, the rules relating to members of the teaching staff included in the permanent establishment shall apply to them.
All private educational institutions in Lebanon, and all members of their teaching staffs, shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

A private educational institution means any non-governmental institution for upbringing and education of whatever kind, licensed to individuals, associations, or religious or civil bodies.

In this Law, the word "institute" is used to denote any private educational institution.

Schools are divided into free schools and non-free schools. A free school means a day primary school in which the following conditions are met:

1- That it is licensed to religious bodies or to legally recognised institutions or associations among whose objectives is the dissemination of education, provided that such schools operate for non-profit purposes.

2- That it is licensed to individuals before the first of October of the year 1964, or that the applications of individuals were registered at the Ministry of National Education before the first of October of the year 1964 fulfilling the required conditions.

3- That it provides education at its primary level in accordance with the prescribed curriculum, and the owner of this free school may attach to it, under conditions to be determined by decree, a nursery that does not benefit from the financial contribution of the State.

4- That it neither imposes nor charges per single pupil fees of whatever kind exceeding sixty pounds per academic year, provided that in any case their general average in the academic year does not exceed twenty-nine /29/ pounds in relation to the total number of pupils during the academic year; and the owner of the free school is permitted to charge an additional amount up to a maximum of five pounds annually for each pupil to cover the expenses of school medical care, insurance, and heating, and is also permitted to charge a transportation allowance, where applicable, in addition to the fees due.

That it forms a unit independent of any non-free school in its teaching staff, classes, and financial affairs.

Members of the teaching staff in the institute mean anyone who performs teaching, supervision, or educational administration therein. The members of this staff are divided into two categories:

A - A category included in the cadre.

B- A category not included in the cadre that receives its wages pursuant to special contracts.

The school year shall be deemed twelve months commencing on the first of October and ending at the end of September of the following year, provided that the date of the beginning and the end of the academic year for the various levels of pre-university education shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports.

A- The cadre of the teaching staff consists of four categories:

- The category of kindergarten mistresses

- The category of teachers, who work in the classes of the primary level or the kindergarten, or in both together.

- The category of teachers, who are in the classes of the primary or intermediate level, or in both together.

- The category of secondary education professors, who work in the classes of the intermediate or secondary level, or in both together.

The conditions of appointment of kindergarten mistresses, the rules governing their work, and their salary scale shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers. The transitional provisions relating to those working in kindergartens as of the date of its issuance shall also be determined by the same decree.

B - Holders of diplomas working in kindergartens as of the date of entry into force of this Law shall be confirmed de jure in the cadre at the grade corresponding to their diplomas, provided that at least two years have elapsed in their work at the kindergarten level.

As for the instructors at this level for whom two years have not elapsed in their work at this level, they shall be confirmed or dismissed from service immediately upon the expiry of this period.

Those confirmed in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph shall retain their rights with respect to salary and shall benefit from the children's rules provided for in the preceding paragraph (A) if they meet the conditions stipulated in the said rules.

Any increase occurring in the salary by reason of this Law shall take effect only as from the beginning of the school year following the issuance of this Law.

The conditions provided for in the laws and regulations relating to the teaching staff in public schools, with the exception of the two conditions of age and examination, shall apply to the members of the teaching staff included in the cadre with respect to their appointment.

For the appointment of an instructor in vocational or technical primary schools, it is required that he hold at least a diploma from a recognised institute in the branch or branches which he is entrusted to teach.

For the appointment of a teacher in vocational or technical education at the secondary level, it is required that he hold at least a higher diploma from a recognised institute in the branch or branches which he is entrusted to teach.
Holders of university degrees shall be appointed at the rank of teacher of the sixth grade.
Members of the teaching staff shall be appointed as probationers for a period of two years at most.

The instructor, teacher, or secondary education professor shall be confirmed or dismissed from service after the expiry of the period of his appointment.

In the event of his confirmation, the probationary period shall be added to his services and the deductions provided for in the second paragraph of Article 21 shall be levied thereon. In the event of his dismissal from service, the institute shall pay him an indemnity at the rate of one month for each year.
The conditions of promotion provided for in the laws relating to State civil servants shall apply to the members of the teaching staff in private institutes included in the cadre.
A family allowance similar to the allowance received by State civil servants pursuant to the laws in force shall be added to the salary fixed in the cadre.

Members of the teaching staff included in the cadre must perform actual teaching actual teaching per week:

- Throughout the school hours in kindergartens with respect to those working at the kindergarten level.

- At least 24 periods and at most 30 periods at the primary level

- At least 20 periods and at most 24 periods at the intermediate level

- At least 15 periods and at most 18 periods at the secondary level.

A period shall be deemed to be between 45 and 60 minutes.

When participating in teaching at more than one level, the working periods shall be deemed the periods of the level at which he works more.

Members of the teaching staff included in the cadre shall not be entitled to work in more than one school at the same time; however, those who perform teaching at the secondary education level or its equivalent in vocational or technical education and who are included in the cadre of one of the schools may contract with another school or schools, provided that the total of their working hours per week does not exceed 30 periods or hours.

1- The salaries of the members of the teaching staff in private schools shall be paid at the end of every month throughout the twelve months of the school year

2- Paragraph 2 was repealed pursuant to Law 5 dated 15/5/2025

3- The school's contribution to feeding the Indemnity Fund shall be set at a rate of six percent of the total salaries of the members of the teaching staff included in the establishment by operation of law, to which shall be added, until the issuance of a new law fixing the scale of ranks and salaries for members of the teaching staff in private schools, the additional wages and allowances granted to the members of the teaching staff as compensation for the collapse of the Lebanese currency.

4- The head of the school or the person acting in his stead shall pay the deductions and the school owners' contribution in accordance with the rules to the Indemnity Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools provided for in Part Five of this Law pursuant to detailed schedules for each of those included in the establishment once every three months, namely in the second half of January, March, June and September of every year. Where payment is not possible within the specified time limit, the school administration shall send a letter to the administration of the Indemnity Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools stating the reasons for the postponement, and in all events all amounts due must be settled within a maximum time limit of the end of the school year to which they pertain, on pain of taking the measures provided for in paragraph (6) of this Article.

5- For one time only and on an exceptional basis, all schools shall be granted a time limit of six months (this time limit is extended for a period of six months starting from 10/2/2005 pursuant to Law 669 dated 4/5/2005, Official Gazette 6 dated 10/2/2005) from the date of issuance of this Law to submit an application to settle their financial status towards the Indemnity Fund, and the schools that submit the settlement application shall be exempted from all fines accrued on the amounts due from them towards the Fund.

The schools that submit the aforementioned application shall also be granted a time limit of eight years starting from the expiry of the six-month time limit to pay all the financial obligations and dues to the Indemnity Fund accrued up to 30/9/2001 in equal quarterly instalments, and the failure of the concerned schools to submit the settlement application and/or the failure to pay any of the quarterly instalments mentioned in this paragraph shall result in all of them falling due in a single lump sum, in which case the measures set out in paragraph 6 of this Article shall apply

6- Every violation of the provisions of this Article shall subject the violator to the following measures:

A- A written warning issued by the Board of Directors in the person of its Chairman requiring payment within a maximum time limit of two months from the date of notification

B- Upon expiry of the time limit, the Board of Directors may impose a late fine at a rate of 2% (two percent) for each month of delay, provided that the value of the fine shall not exceed the amount of the sums originally owed

C- In the event that the violation is repeated, the Board of Directors shall have the right to submit to the Minister of Education and Higher Education a list of the names of the violating schools requesting him to adopt the appropriate measures

D- If the Minister of Education and Higher Education deems it necessary to close the school for a specified period or permanently, he shall submit the matter to the Council of Ministers

E- In the event that a decree of permanent closure is issued against the school, it shall bear the full indemnities due to the members of the teaching staff working therein, and these due indemnities shall be considered privileged debts ranking after the debt of the State

F- Debts resulting from contributions, deductions and fines due in favour of the Indemnity Fund shall be considered privileged debts ranking after the debt of the State, and the administration of the Fund shall be authorised to collect them in accordance with the rules for the collection of State debts

G- It is prohibited to invest the funds of the Indemnity Fund except in Lebanese Treasury bonds and in Lebanese commercial banks that occupy the first twenty positions in terms of balance sheet size or volume of deposits. Investment in commercial banks shall be made in Lebanese pounds or in any other currency or currencies, provided that the percentage that may be invested in Treasury bonds and in foreign currencies shall be determined by a decision of the Board of Directors of the Fund

H - In the event of a deficit in the Indemnity Fund, such deficit shall be covered by increasing the rate of both the deductions owed by the members of the teaching staff and the contribution of the school owners, provided that this is approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education and following the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

Members of the teaching staff shall remain bound to the administration of the institute during one month of the summer vacation designated for them by the administration before the end of the academic year, and they must comply with every summons addressed to them during this month within the limits of their professional duties and within the time limit it sets for them, provided that it does not assign them to actual teaching.

Every member of the teaching staff shall have the right to be absent with permission and on full salary for a period of one week in the event of his marriage and for a period not exceeding 4 days in the event of the death of his spouse or one of his ascendants, descendants, brothers or sisters.

Female members of the teaching staff in private institutes shall be granted maternity leave (pregnancy and childbirth):

A - For a period of two months on full salary.

B - For a period of another month on half salary.

Any member of the teaching staff shall have the right to obtain sick leave under the following conditions:

If he is absent for health reasons, he must inform the head of the institute immediately and of the reasons that called for the absence. The head may, if he wishes, verify the truth of the matter through a physician who shall give a report on the facts.

If it appears from the report that the period of absence does not exceed thirty days, the health leave shall be granted on full salary.

And if it appears that it exceeds the aforementioned period, the leave shall be extended on half salary for up to two further months, provided that the person concerned shall, after the expiry of two months of his illness, be referred to the Medical Committee for State Employees at the Ministry of Public Health.

And the head of the institute shall have the right to dismiss him from service if the Medical Committee deems that his return to work is not possible two months after his examination.

If one of the members of the teaching staff neglects his duties in maintaining order, teaching and upbringing, or commits any violation of the provisions of this Law, or is absent without a legitimate excuse, or behaves in a manner that harms the reputation of the school or the regularity of work therein, he shall be subject to one of the following penalties:

1- Written warning.

2- Reprimand.

3- Deduction of salary for a period not exceeding ten days during a single school year.

4- Deduction of salary for a maximum period of one month during a single school year.

5- Delay of advancement in step for a maximum period of two years.

6- Dismissal from service with indemnity.

7- Dismissal from service without indemnity, in which case the person concerned shall recover the deductions withheld from his salary and paid into the Indemnity Fund.

The head of the school shall impose the aforementioned penalties and notify them to the person concerned, reasoned, by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, and the person concerned shall have the right to object to the third to the seventh penalties inclusive before the Disciplinary Board provided for in the Law Regulating the Teaching Staff in Private Schools dated 15/6/1956 and its amendments within a time limit of twenty days from the date of notification of the letter to the person concerned directly against his signature of receipt on a certified true copy of this letter in lieu of registered mail. The Disciplinary Board shall have the right to approve the penalty, replace it or annul it.

The provisions of this Law relating to classification, salary, promotion, family allowance and severance indemnity shall be deemed to pertain to public policy, and any contravention thereof shall be null and void ipso jure.

The provisions of Articles 461 and 462 et seq. of the Penal Code shall apply to any statement or entry in the registers of the institute that does not conform to reality. Any person who knowingly uses such statements or entries shall be subject to the same penalties.
The holder of the licence of the institute and its director shall be jointly and severally liable for the application of the provisions of this Law.

Any contravention of the provisions of this Law or of the laws on the adjustment of salaries and wages, following a prior written warning from the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts, shall be punishable by a fine ranging between /10000/ ten thousand and /50000/ fifty thousand Lebanese pounds.

In the event of recurrence, the fine shall be from /50000/ fifty thousand pounds to /500000/ five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

If the contravention recurs anew, the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts shall be entitled to close the school for a specified period or permanently. In such case, the school shall bear the full severance indemnities due to the members of the teaching staff.

Contraventions shall be established by official reports drawn up by the inspectors of the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts in the presence of the representative of the institute, approved by the Director General of that Ministry.

Indemnities relating to services prior to the date of 1 April 1951 shall be borne by the private institutes, whether free or non-free, and shall be paid to those entitled thereto upon their dismissal from service at the rate of one month for each of the first five years and half a month for each year of the remaining period.

The Fund shall bear the other half-month in the cases provided for in Articles 31 and 35 of this Law, and the school shall bear this other half in cases other than those provided for in those two Articles. The average of the monthly salaries received by the person concerned during the last two years shall be taken as the basis for calculating these indemnities in free schools, and the Indemnities Fund shall bear the difference resulting from this adjustment.

As for the indemnities relating to the services of members of the teaching staff in free and non-free schools for the period subsequent to 1 April 1951, the provisions of this Law shall apply thereto, provided that all deductions due pursuant to the provisions of the second paragraph only of Article 7 of Legislative Decree No. 113 dated 12 June 1959 in respect of members of the teaching staff admitted to the establishment and benefiting from the provisions of this Law are paid to the Fund for this period, within a time limit of three years from the date of promulgation of this Law, under penalty of forfeiture of the right in respect of any period of service for which the deductions are not paid in full.

Members of the teaching staff shall retain their acquired rights with respect to salaries and promotion. The head of the institute shall, within one month from the promulgation of this Law, classify each of them in the rank and step the salary of which equals his current salary, or to which his academic qualification entitles him where his salary is less than the salary fixed for such qualification in the establishment.

Members of the teaching staff who have practised teaching in the last three years of the secondary education stage for a period of ten consecutive years in the same institute and who do not hold academic qualifications shall be classified in the last step of the rank of secondary education teacher if their current salary is less than the salary fixed for that step.

Where their salary exceeds the last step, they shall be classified in the step that equals it, or that immediately exceeds it if there is no corresponding step in the establishment.

If the head of the institute refrains from applying the provisions of this Article, the person concerned shall be entitled to leave the service and receive the full severance indemnity from the institute on the basis of the provisions of this Law.
With respect to the salary increase resulting from classification, the provisions of the preceding Article shall apply with effect from 1 October 1956.

The State shall contribute to the financial burdens resulting from the application of the provisions of this Law to free primary schools, and this contribution shall be distributed among them in the amount of 135 pounds for each pupil in proportion to the number of eligible pupils in each of them, on the basis of written statistical statements submitted by these schools in accordance with special forms drawn up by the Ministry of National Education and within a time limit fixed by it for that purpose.

A committee shall be appointed by decree, composed of:

A judge of the first or second category ... Chairman

A representative of the Ministry of National Education ... Member

A representative of the Ministry of Finance ... Member

Its mission shall be to adjudicate disputes arising between the Government and the administration of private institutes with respect to their right to obtain the contribution provided for in the preceding Article.

The committee shall adjudicate disputes upon a written application by either party, and it may dispense with ordinary rules of procedure.

The decisions of the committee shall be subject to appeal before the State Council.

The details of implementation of this Law shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education.
All provisions that contravene this Law or that are inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed, in particular Legislative Decree No. 212 dated 31 August 1942 and the Law of 27 March 1951.
Subject to the provisions of Article 61, this Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

No member of the teaching staff in private institutes shall be entitled to any dismissal indemnity.

1- If he is dismissed for disciplinary reasons pursuant to item 7 of the new Article 26.

2- If he resigns or leaves work in cases other than those specified in Article 31 of this Law. He shall only be entitled to recover all deductions that were withheld from his salaries.

3- If he practises any profession other than the teaching profession.

The rights of members of the teaching staff shall be liquidated upon their dismissal from service or his resignation. A person who is dismissed from service for a non-disciplinary reason or who resigns therefrom shall be entitled, in the event of his return to the practice of teaching, to request that his previous services be combined and included in the calculation of his new indemnity, provided that he submits his application to the Compensation Fund and returns to the Fund in a single lump sum the indemnity that he received or the deductions that he collected or that were due from him, within a period of three months from the date of his resumption of service under penalty of forfeiture of the right.

This rule shall apply to those who were dismissed from service and resigned, and returned to the practice of teaching prior to the promulgation of this Law, provided that they submit an application for combination and return the indemnity that they received or the deductions that they collected or that were due from them, within a period of three years from the date of promulgation of this Law under penalty of forfeiture of the right.

The Compensation Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools established by the Law of 27 March 1951 shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy. Every dispute arising between the Fund and the concerned parties shall be adjudicated by the ordinary courts. The dismissal indemnities provided for in Article 36 of this Law shall be paid from this Fund to the members of the teaching staff mentioned below:

1- Members of the teaching staff whose names are registered in the Compensation Fund as at the date of promulgation of this Law.

2- Members of the teaching staff who are in service prior to the promulgation of this Law and whose names are not registered in the Compensation Fund, provided that they submit an application for registration in the Fund within a period of three months from the date of promulgation of this Law under penalty of forfeiture of the right.

3- Any person who practises teaching after the promulgation of this Law, subject to submitting an application for the registration of his name in the Fund within six months from the date of his commencement of work under penalty of forfeiture of the right in respect of all previous service.
