Except for these cases, every member of the teaching staff shall be deemed to have entered service, with respect to the dismissal indemnity, from the date of registration of his name in the Compensation Fund.

The indemnities and pensions of retirees shall be covered from the deductions paid to the management of the Compensation Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools and if the result of any given year is a deficit and an inability to pay the indemnities, the pensions of retirees and the operating cost, they shall be covered by a parallel contribution appropriated in the budget of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, upon the request of the Board of Directors of the Compensation Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools accompanied by a detailed statement issued by the management of the Compensation Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools and based on such documents as the Ministry of Education deems appropriate for that purpose in its capacity as the supervisory authority over the public utility represented by the Compensation Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools.

The management of the Fund shall be undertaken by a Director assisted by an accountant and the necessary number of employees. The Director and the accountant shall be appointed by a decision of the Minister of National Education upon the recommendation of the Board of Directors and the proposal of the Director General, and the employees shall be appointed by a decision of the Board of Directors of the Fund upon the proposal of the Director.

The management of the Fund shall be supervised by a Board appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education for a term of three years renewable and composed of:

- The Director General of Education... Chairman

- A representative of the Ministry of Justice... Member

- Four representatives of the owners of private schools (chosen by the holders of the ten licences contributing the most to the funding of the Fund during the three years preceding the appointment pursuant to a report drawn up by the management of the Fund for this purpose)... Members

- Four representatives of the members of the teaching staff in private schools chosen by the Council of the Syndicate... Members

The Board shall undertake the supervision of the management of the Fund and in particular the following matters:

1- Establishing the cadre of the employees of the Fund and approving its internal regulations.

2- Monitoring the work of the Director and the accountant.

3- Investing the funds of the Fund.

4- Approving the annual budget.

5- Examining all matters relating to dismissal indemnities in accordance with the provisions of this Law and taking decisions thereon.

The Board shall draw up internal regulations for itself provided that such regulations shall not be deemed effective until after their approval by the Ministries of National Education and of Labour and Social Affairs.

The allowances of the Chairman and members of the Board shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Ministry of National Education. The salaries and allowances of the employees of the management of the Fund shall be determined by a decision of the Board of Directors.

The management of the institute shall, on its own responsibility, undertake the withholding of the deductions provided for in the second paragraph of Article 21 of this Law and shall pay them to the management of the Fund once every six months pursuant to a detailed statement in accordance with a special form containing the name of the concerned party, his monthly salary, and the deductions withheld from the salary, signed by the concerned parties and certified by the head of the institute.

Untrue statements or statements contrary to fact shall subject the management of the institute to the penalties provided for in Articles 461 and 462 et seq. of the Penal Code.

Applications for the dismissal indemnities provided for in Article 36 shall be submitted to the Board of Directors of the Fund within a period of two years from the date of dismissal or death, under penalty of forfeiture of this right.

The Board of Directors shall rule thereon by a reasoned decision within a period of three months from the date of their submission.

This time limit is extended for a period of six months starting from 10/2/2005 pursuant to L. 669 d. 4/2/2005) from the date of their submission.

For each application, a special record shall be drawn up showing the name of the beneficiary, the duration of his service, and the amount of the indemnity due to him.

This record shall be drawn up by the accountant, audited by the Director, and approved by the Board of Directors of the Fund.
The decision of the Board of Directors of the Fund may be appealed before the Court of Appeal within thirty days from the date of its notification.

The provisions of this Law shall not apply:

1- To administrative employees in the institutes, to whom the Labour Law shall apply.

2- To members of the institution owning the institute or entrusted with its management who undertake administrative work or practise teaching therein without receiving a salary therefor.

3- To members of the teaching staff who practise teaching in higher institutions in branches where the level of education exceeds the level of secondary education.

Heads of institutes are prohibited from admitting any non-Lebanese person into the teaching staff before verifying that he holds a permit issued by the Ministries of National Education and of Social Affairs.

The head of the institute shall notify the management of the Compensation Fund provided for in Part Five of this Law before the end of December of each year of the names of the members of the teaching staff belonging to his institute, both those included in the cadre and those not included therein, and shall attach thereto information regarding their certificates, the number of their weekly working hours, the subjects they teach, the classes in which they work, their ranks and their salary, and copies of the contracts concluded between him and the members of the teaching staff not included in the cadre, as well as all other information that it may request from him.
Syndicates of members of the teaching staff in private schools shall be subject to the regime of syndicates provided for in the Labour Law.

In the event that the company violates the provisions of Article 2 of this Legislative Decree, this company shall become subject, in respect of the financial year in which the violation occurred, to the income tax applicable to joint-stock and limited liability companies (capital companies) operating in Lebanon on the entirety of its net annual profits derived from all its activities, to which shall be added a fine of 50 per cent of the amount of the tax due from it.
All provisions stipulated by the laws in force shall apply to the companies provided for in this Legislative Decree in all that does not conflict with its provisions.
The details of the application of this Legislative Decree shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force as of the day following its publication in the Official Gazette.

In application of the provisions of the laws promulgated on 24 November 1931 and 19 December 1931, a committee shall be formed in every seat of a Governorate or Qaimaqamiyya, called the (District Census Committee), which shall undertake the matter of the census in that area.

A town, village, or locality shall be considered a census area, and the area shall consist of subdivisions, provided that each subdivision consists of twenty-five houses, and provided that the local government shall, where necessary, have the option to decrease or increase this number in order to secure the attainment of the result within the period specified in Article (2) and paragraph (c) of the fourth Article of the Law dated 24 November 1931. No subdivision of a neighbourhood or village may be added to another neighbourhood or village; as for the census of the inhabitants of farms, it shall take place within the jurisdiction of the Mukhtar to whom it belongs.

The division of villages and neighbourhoods into subdivisions shall take place through the agency of the Mukhtars, the Council of Elders, and the Compulsory Body under the supervision of the Governors and Qaimaqams; as for the towns and villages in which there are municipal councils or committees, such councils and committees shall participate in this work, and the Governor or Qaimaqam shall issue a special decision on the division, publish it at least three days prior to the commencement of the census, and send a copy thereof to the Ministry of the Interior

The District Census Committee shall be composed of:

The Governor or Qaimaqam .... as Chairman

A member of the Administrative Council .... as Member

A member of the Municipal Council .... as Member

The Civil Status Clerk .... as Rapporteur (and in his absence, the Clerk of the Qaimaqamiyya)

The Village or Locality Census Committee shall be composed of:

The Mukhtar ..... as Chairman

The Council of Elders.... as Members

A Clerk

A committee shall be composed in each subdivision of the villages or localities of:

Two members from among the notables of the locality.

A Clerk

These committees shall be appointed by a decision of the Governors or Qaimaqams, a copy of which shall be sent to the Ministry of the Interior.

Subject to the provisions of the law, the Minister of the Interior shall have the right to:

1- Appoint the date on which the census shall take place.

2- Appoint all the officers and clerks necessary to conduct the census in all its branches, from preliminary preparations to final completions.

3- Authorise the Governors and Qaimaqams to appoint the clerks and workers necessary for the census operation, whether from among the persons mentioned in Article (3) of the Law dated 24 November 1931 or from outside.

4- Lay down the instructions necessary to conduct the census and communicate them to the relevant authorities.

There shall be formed in the Ministry of the Interior a (Higher Census Committee) composed of:

The Minister of the Interior ... as Chairman

The Director of the Interior .... as Member

The Public Prosecutor before the Court of Appeal and Cassation, or a representative on his behalf ... as Member

A representative of the Ministry of Finance .... as Member

The Head of the Civil Status Department .... as Rapporteur

There shall be added to it a clerk appointed by the Chairman, and the function of this committee shall be restricted to the following:

1- Supervising and auditing the census operations.

2- Auditing and certifying the schedules received from the committees.

3- Drawing up a general schedule of the number of inhabitants of the Republic and another of the number of emigrants, announcing the final result.

4- Drawing up a special schedule of foreigners detailing the number of nationals of each foreign State.
Lebanese nationals and foreigners residing in Lebanese territory and emigrants shall be enumerated in accordance with the instructions given in this regard by the Ministry of the Interior.

Householders shall be obliged to fill in the declarations distributed to them in accordance with the explanations mentioned therein and to sign them, and these declarations must be certified by the subdivision committees and then by the Mukhtars; however, if the householder is illiterate, the clerk of the committee shall fill them in and the householder shall affix his thumbprint thereon, and after the subdivision committee inspects the members of the family person by person, it shall record its attestation to the accuracy of the declaration.

Monks and nuns living in monasteries, and orphans, lunatics, the infirm, and foundlings present in asylums. And orphanages, pupils who board in schools and colleges, patients present in hospitals, and persons present in inns, hotels, prisons, and all other institutions shall be enumerated where they are; and the superior, mother superior, director, and proprietors of inns, khans, hotels, and the like shall be obliged to fill in the declarations, mention their names as well at the head thereof, and sign them, and likewise for ships and vessels.
As for nomadic tribes, none of them shall be counted as Lebanese except the tribes that reside each year for more than six months in the territory of Lebanon.

Refugees from Turkish territories, such as Armenians, Syriacs, Chaldeans, Greeks, and all other persons who are of Turkish origin and who were present on 30 August 1924 in Lebanese territory, shall be counted as Lebanese in accordance with the provisions of High Commission Decision No. 2825 dated 30 August 1924; in order to be counted as Lebanese, they shall be required to produce civil status certificates to the committees, and in this manner the registration of those who acquired Lebanese nationality in accordance with Decision (S) 15 dated 19 January 1925 shall take place; as for those who took refuge in Lebanese territory after that date and did not acquire Lebanese nationality, and those who are unable to prove their presence in Lebanese territory on the aforementioned date, they shall be counted as foreigners and registered as stateless.

When all the schedules and declarations reach the Civil Status Department, it shall proceed to transcribe the information contained therein into the registers established on a family basis; the transcription shall be carried out by clerks specially appointed by the Ministry of the Interior for this purpose, and sufficient space must be left on each page of the register to allow for the registration of personal status events pertaining to each family, such as birth, marriage, divorce, death, change of place of residence, and others; as for emigrants, they shall be registered in a special register of their own.

Upon the arrival of the schedules at the Ministry of the Interior (the Higher Census Committee), there shall be sorted out from among the emigrants the persons who opted for Lebanese nationality and those who emigrated after 30 August 1924, and they shall be registered with their families, and all others shall be registered in the special register of emigrants.

After the registration of the schedules and census declarations is completed, the Civil Status Department shall proceed to draw up identity cards (civil status certificates); these cards shall then be sent to the civil status offices in the districts to be delivered to their holders through the Mukhtars against a receipt showing the number of cards and the names of their holders.

The Civil Status Department shall draw up a statement of the amount that must be collected from each person in each district and each village as the price of the identity cards; the statements shall then be sent to the Ministry of Finance for the collection of their value through the tax collectors together with the fees and taxes at the same time.

Every Lebanese national is obliged to obtain an identity card, whereas foreigners shall have the option to do so. The value of the card has been fixed at five Lebanese piastres in paper currency, and if the card is lost, a copy thereof may be obtained for the same fee. If there are persons who are unable to pay this fee, they must submit to the Qaimaqams or Governors a petition requesting their exemption therefrom, and this petition shall be exempt from stamp duty; after the aforementioned officials verify the poverty of the petitioners, a statement of their names and send it to the Ministry of the Interior to grant them cards free of charge. Photographs of male persons who have reached the eighteenth year of age and above must be affixed to their identity cards.

Old cards shall be cancelled upon the delivery of the new cards.

"The carrying of an identity card is compulsory for every Lebanese national who travels outside his place of residence"

A Lebanese who is temporarily absent from Lebanese territory at the time of the census and whose name was not mentioned in the statement submitted by the head of his family shall be required, within the first month of his return, to submit his declaration to the Personal Status Office in his place of residence for his registration in the census registers.

Furthermore, even after the conclusion of the census, the name of every person whose name was not entered for any reason in one of the statements must also be recorded, provided that this shall not preclude the penal prosecutions provided for in Article (7) of the Law of 24 November 1931.

A Lebanese emigrant after the date of 30 August 1924 who has not been recorded in the census registers may, after the date of his emigration is verified, be recorded in the aforementioned registers pursuant to an application submitted to the Central Census Department by an attorney-in-fact of his to whom he has granted legal authority for this purpose.

Every Lebanese who is not in possession of a new identity card and does not have an acceptable excuse for failing to obtain it shall be deemed in default of the obligations of the census and liable to the penalty provided for in the seventh Article of the aforementioned Law.

Nothing entered in the registers may be rectified except pursuant to a judgment of the Peace Court issued in the presence of the Civil Status Officer or his delegate, with the exception of circumstances subject to change, such as occupation, sect, religion, change of place of residence, and the like, which shall be rectified by the Civil Status Departments without any need for a judgment of a court.

The Head of the Civil Status Departments may strike off entries entered without right after conducting an investigation and obtaining the approval of the Minister of the Interior. The civil courts shall remain competent to hear the nationality of the person whose entry was struck off administratively.

All inhabitants of the Republic and persons staying therein are prohibited from leaving their homes during the period of 24 hours designated for conducting the census, and whoever violates this shall be punished under the provisions of Article 254 of the Penal Code as amended pursuant to Decision No. 1047 dated 11 January 1922.

Every person who is proven to have defaulted on the census, either by refusing to submit the statement pertaining to him or by concealing his true identity, or who is proven to have submitted and caused another to submit false information concerning the members of his family or concerning their ages, shall be punished in accordance with Article (7) of the Law of 24 November 1931.

Every worker in one of the census committees who intentionally violates the provisions of the Census Law, or deliberately submits false information, or defaults on accepting the statements, or takes duplicate information, or alters the statements of the inhabitants, shall be punished in accordance with Article (6) of the aforementioned Law.

Every person who commits during the census operations an act leading to disturbance, rebellion, or riot shall be referred to the court of competence for his punishment in accordance with the specific articles of the Penal Code.

After the conclusion of the census, the Ministry of the Interior shall send a sufficient number of inspectors to the districts and necessary localities to examine whether the census operations have proceeded along their regular course.
The civil authorities, the gendarmerie, and the police must comply with the requests of the census officers and assist them at all times and promptly.
The Ministers of Justice, the Interior, and Finance are charged, each insofar as concerns him, with the execution of this Decree.

No person whomsoever may open a racecourse unless he obtains a licence to open it.

Every company or every individual holding a licence to open a racecourse, or having concluded an agreement with a company or with an individual holding such licence, may operate exclusively within the racecourse betting and all forms of wagering on races, provided that a special licence is obtained and that the conditions set forth in this Law are observed.

The licences provided for in Article One shall be granted and revoked pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, and the licence may be revoked at any time upon the infringement of the provisions of this Law.
The operator may retain for himself an amount which may not exceed nine and one-half per cent of the gross total of bets.

No person may practise the profession of intermediary inside or outside the racecourse between bettors and the person or company holding a licence to operate betting, whether for his own account or for the account of the said person or the said company.

Permanent admission tickets shall indicate the year during which they are valid, and a fixed annual fee of five Lebanese-Syrian pounds shall be levied on these tickets, and permanent complimentary invitations shall be exempted from this fee, the number of which must not exceed a figure determined by the Minister of Finance at the beginning of each season upon a proposal submitted by the operator accompanied by the statement of reasons.

A schedule of these tickets or invitations shall be drawn up showing all alterations occurring therein daily and shall be submitted to the Ministry of Finance within a period of fifteen days commencing from the date of publication of this Law or from the date of occurrence of the alteration in the schedule.

A fee of two and one-half per cent shall be levied for the account of the Treasury from the gross total of bets in addition to the amount levied by the operator for his own account in accordance with Article Three.

The amounts which must be paid to the Treasury pursuant to Article Six of this Law shall be paid directly into the Central Treasury Fund in Beirut within eight days from the date of the meeting in respect of which these amounts are levied and in accordance with a schedule drawn up by the betting operator.

Where the operator is a company, it shall be incumbent upon the chairman of that company or the person delegated by the chairman or the partners to perform this task to draw up the said schedule.

All betting transactions and in general all financial and accounting transactions relating to individuals or companies holding a licence to open racecourses or to operate betting in these racecourses shall be placed under the supervision of the Ministry of Finance, and the individuals or companies mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall keep double-entry books in the commercial manner in which they shall enter completely and in detail all their transactions, observing therein Articles 3 to 9 of the Commercial Code.

Their financial year shall be annual, commencing on 15 October, and they shall also submit to the Ministry of Finance before the first of January of each year a detailed schedule of their accounts for the elapsed financial year, and after the Ministry of Finance completes the audit of these accounts, it shall grant them a discharge in respect thereof if necessary.

The application of the provisions shall commence as from the 1931-1932 season, and the officials appointed by the Ministry of Finance may inspect at any time the registers, accounting papers, and accounting or non-accounting documents of all kinds relating to these transactions, and they may also closely supervise the issuance of admission tickets and betting.

Subject to the provisions of Article One, there shall be punished by a pecuniary fine ranging between one pound and fifty Syrian pounds, and in the event of a repetition of the offence by imprisonment from one month to six months:

First: Any person who offers in any place and in any manner whatsoever, or takes or gives a bet on horse racing, whether through an intermediary or directly.

Second: Any person who operates in any place or in any manner whatsoever betting on horse racing, or acts as a betting intermediary by selling tickets for betting on races or by any other means.

Third: Any person who sells tips on the chances of success of competing horses for the purpose of betting, and any person who publicises by advertisements, leaflets, and other means of publication the existence of establishments, agencies, or individuals selling such tips, whether in Lebanon or abroad.

Fourth: Any owner or manager of premises open to the public if he turns a blind eye to the operation of betting on his premises.

Fifth: Any person who contravenes the provisions of Article Four of this Law; as for the betting funds, they shall be seized in the event of tampering with the law and the judge shall order their confiscation for the benefit of the Treasury.

Every intermediary or professional practitioner of the game of paroli or similar games shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine of two hundred pounds to one thousand Lebanese-Syrian pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

If there are stated in the schedules drawn up in accordance with Article Seven of this Law amounts which are less than the amounts actually due to the Treasury in accordance with Article Six thereof, a fine equal to three times the shortfall incurred shall be imposed on the operator, and the shortfall amount shall be claimed from him, and where necessary, the licence shall be withdrawn from him in accordance with Article Two.

In the event of the occurrence of contraventions other than the contraventions mentioned in Articles Nine and Ten of this Law, a pecuniary fine determined by the Council of Ministers shall be imposed in respect thereof, provided that its amount does not exceed one thousand Lebanese-Syrian pounds.

All amounts due to the Treasury in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall be collected by the administrative method in accordance with the procedures followed in the collection of public funds.

Individuals or companies currently operating a racecourse or betting premises and who have not previously obtained an operating licence from the Government must request from the Minister of the Interior, before the expiration of fifteen days from the publication of this Law, the licences provided for in Articles One and Two thereof; if they do not submit the application within the specified period, or if they submit the application and do not obtain the decree of authorisation within two months from the date of the application, they must cease operation, failing which the provisions of Article Nine of this Law shall apply to them.
This Law shall enter into force as from the first of January of the year 1932.
The Minister of the Interior, Health and Public Assistance and the Minister of Finance are charged with the execution of this Law, which must be published in the Official Gazette.

Lebanese joint-stock companies which engage, exclusively, in the following activities shall be subject to this Law:

1 - Negotiating and signing contracts and agreements concerning transactions and deals that are executed outside Lebanese territory and pertain to assets located abroad or in customs free zones.

2 - Managing companies and institutions whose activity is restricted outside Lebanon, operating out of Lebanon, and exporting professional, administrative and organizational services and information technology services and software of all kinds to institutions resident outside Lebanon and at the request of such institutions.

3 - Tripartite or multilateral foreign trade transactions taking place outside Lebanon; for this purpose, offshore companies may conduct negotiations, sign contracts, ship goods, and re-issue invoices for business and transactions outside Lebanon, or from and to the customs free zones in Lebanon, and this includes using the facilities available in the customs free zones in Lebanon to store imported goods for the purpose of re-exporting them.

4 - Carrying out maritime transport business and activities.

5 - Owning shares, stakes, bonds and participations in non-resident foreign institutions and companies, and lending to non-resident institutions in which the offshore company owns more than 20% of the capital.

6 - Owning and/or benefiting from rights pertaining to agencies for materials and goods and representation of foreign companies in foreign markets.

7 - Opening branches and representative offices abroad.

8 - Building, operating, managing and owning all economic projects with the exception of the prohibitions set forth in the second Article of this Law.

9 - Opening credits and borrowing to finance the transactions and activities referred to above from banks and financial institutions resident in Lebanon or abroad.

10 - Leasing offices in Lebanon and owning the real property necessary for their activity, with due observance of the Law on the Acquisition by Foreigners of Real Property Rights in Lebanon.

The companies provided for in this Legislative Decree shall be prohibited from engaging in insurance operations of various kinds and the operations and business carried on by banks, financial institutions and all institutions subject to the supervision of the Bank of Lebanon, and they shall also be prohibited from carrying out in Lebanon business other than that referred to in the first Article of this Law.

They shall likewise be prohibited from earning any profit, return or revenue from movable or immovable property located in Lebanon, or as a result of providing services to institutions resident in Lebanon, except for the revenue of their bank accounts and the revenues resulting from subscribing to and trading in Lebanese Treasury bonds.

Related text: Determining the business in which offshore companies are prohibited from engaging

These companies shall be subject to the provisions to which joint-stock companies are subject in all matters that do not conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

1 - The articles of association of the company must provide that it is not permitted to engage in any activity other than the activities provided for in the first Article of this Legislative Decree.

2 - All bank accounts of these companies shall be subject to the provisions of the Law promulgated by Decree No. 9976 dated 1/4/1975 and the regulatory texts issued pursuant to the provisions thereof. Their accounts may be in Lebanese pounds.

3 - The capital of the company may be denominated in a foreign currency provided that it keeps its accounts in the same foreign currency.

4 - The members of the board of directors may be non-Lebanese, and the chairman of the board of directors or the person authorized to sign on behalf of the company shall not require a work permit if he is a non-Lebanese not resident in Lebanon, and the chairmanship of their boards of directors and the membership of these boards shall be exempted from the maximum limit provided for in Article 154 of the Code of Commerce.

Foreign employees working in Lebanon shall be exempted from the obligation to obtain a work permit provided that the annual balance sheet of the company is not less than one billion Lebanese pounds, under pain of forfeiture of this right.

5 - The company shall not be subject to the obligation provided for in Article 62 of the Law Regulating the Legal Profession, except in the event that its capital exceeds fifty million Lebanese pounds or the total of its annual balance sheets exceeds the equivalent of five hundred thousand US dollars.

6 - The company must appoint, at least, one principal auditor resident in Lebanon and holding Lebanese nationality, and he may be appointed for a term of 3 years.

The company shall be exempted from the obligation to appoint an additional auditor.

7 - The company shall be registered in the Public Commercial Register in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Commerce, and a special register for the companies provided for in this Legislative Decree shall be established at the Court of First Instance in Beirut in which these companies shall be registered and in which the statements and information that the law requires joint-stock companies to publish shall be entered.

8 - Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 101 of the Code of Commerce, the company may suffice with publishing the balance sheet of the financial year and the names of the members of the board of directors and of the auditors in the special register referred to in the preceding paragraph above.

9 - The company shall be subject to the obligation to keep accounting records, draw up annual financial statements, submit returns and pay the taxes due by it to the competent financial department for income tax, in accordance with the legal provisions relating to joint-stock companies in all matters that do not conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

A fine in the amount of 50000 L.L. fifty thousand Lebanese pounds per month shall be imposed on the company when it delays in submitting the statutory return, in addition to the taxes due.

Implementing decree for this Article

The company shall be exempted from income tax on profits and shall instead be subject to an annual lump-sum tax in the amount of fifty million pounds (50.000.000 L.L.), and this tax shall apply to the company starting from the first financial year regardless of its duration.

This text shall take effect starting from the 2022 financial year.
Contracts and all documents signed by the company in Lebanon and relating to its business outside Lebanon shall be exempted from fiscal stamp duty.

Dividends distributed by the companies shall be exempted from the tax on revenues from movable capital, and the companies shall be exempted from the tax on movable capital payable on their revenues and returns resulting from the investment of their funds outside Lebanon and that payable on the interest they pay to legal or natural persons resident abroad; the company shall likewise be exempted from the tax on the amounts it pays to legal or natural persons outside Lebanon in consideration of services performed abroad, and it shall also be exempted from the tax on salaries and wages of employees working abroad, and the shares of the company and its shareholders shall also be exempted from all transfer and inheritance taxes and the duties connected therewith of whatever kind.
The capital gain resulting from the company's disposal of its fixed assets in Lebanon shall be subject to the tax provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law.

The salaries and wages of employees working in the company shall be subject to the tax under Title II of the Income Tax Law. 30% of the basic salary of a foreign employee working in the company shall be deemed a representation allowance not subject to the tax on salaries and wages.

The taxes due by the company shall be paid in a single payment upon the declaration of business and within the time limit specified therefor. In the event that the company violates its tax obligations, the fines provided for in Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 (Tax Procedures Law) shall apply.

Effect and consequences of appointment:

1- No person shall be appointed save to a vacant post in the cadre, for which a special appropriation has been allocated in the budget, and in accordance with the procedures prescribed by law.

2- Appointment shall be made at the last grade of the category, save in cases where the law provides otherwise.

3- The effect of the appointment shall take effect from the date of commencement of work. It shall not be permissible for it to have any retroactive effect.

4- Instruments of appointment shall be notified to the Civil Service Board and the Court of Audit.

5- If an appointment is made to a post that is not vacant in the cadre or to a post for which no special appropriation has been allocated in the budget, both the liquidator and the authorising officer shall be prohibited from liquidating and disbursing the expenditure resulting therefrom, even if they receive a written order to that effect. The authorising officer shall report the matter to the Minister of Finance and to the Civil Service Board in order to work towards the annulment of the instrument of appointment.

6- If the appointment is contrary to legal procedures, it shall be deemed ineffective, and no acquired right shall accrue to the party concerned by reason thereof until he obtains from the competent judicial authority a final and binding decision as to its legality.

Duties of civil servants:

A civil servant shall, in general:

1- Be guided in his work solely by the public interest, and ensure the application of the laws and regulations in force without any transgression, violation, or negligence.

2- Submit to his immediate superior and execute his orders and instructions, unless such orders and instructions are explicitly and clearly contrary to the law. In such case, the civil servant shall draw the attention of his superior in writing to the violation that has occurred and shall not be bound to execute such orders and instructions unless the superior takes them upon himself in writing, and he may send copies of the correspondence to the Central Inspection Administration.

3- Bear personal responsibility for the orders and instructions which he gives to his subordinates.

4- Complete the transactions of interested parties with speed, accuracy, and good faith within the limits of his competence.

5- Relinquish completely, in the event of his affiliation with political parties, bodies, councils, or associations, or confessional ones of a political nature, any mission or any responsibility in such parties, bodies, councils, or associations.

Prohibited acts:

A civil servant is prohibited from performing any act forbidden by the laws and regulations in force, and in particular:

1- Delivering or publishing, without written permission from the head of his administration, speeches, articles, statements, or publications on any matter whatsoever."

2- Joining professional organisations or syndicates.

3- Striking from work or inciting others to strike.

4- Practising any commercial or industrial profession or any other remunerated profession or trade save in the cases explicitly provided for by special laws, or being a member of the board of directors of a joint-stock company or a partnership limited by shares. Or having a direct material interest, or through a third party, in an enterprise subject to his supervision or to the supervision of the administration to which he belongs.

5- Combining his post with parliamentary, municipal, and mukhtar elective offices as set forth in the special laws governing those offices.

6- Performing any remunerated work that demeans the dignity of the post or is connected therewith.

7- Soliciting or accepting any recommendation whatsoever, or soliciting or accepting, directly or through an intermediary, by reason of the post which he occupies, gifts, gratuities, or grants of any kind whatsoever.

8- Disclosing official information of which he became aware during the performance of his post, even after the termination of his period of service, unless his ministry authorises him in writing to do so.

9- Organising collective petitions relating to the post or participating in organising them, whatever the reasons and motives may be.

General provisions:

1- Each grade shall have a salary determined by law.

2- Salaries and their accessories shall be liquidated monthly when they fall due. All months, without exception, shall be calculated as thirty days starting from the first day thereof.

3- No advance on salaries shall be permissible before they fall due.

4 - No person may receive the salary of a post unless he is legally appointed thereto and is actually performing the duties thereof, subject to the special cases provided for by law.

Immediate superiors shall be deemed personally responsible for the payment of the salaries of civil servants who do not actually perform the duties of their posts.

5 - No person may combine two salaries.

Conditions of entitlement to salary:

1- The salary of a new civil servant shall fall due starting from the date of his commencement of work.

2- If the seat of the post is outside Lebanon, the salary of the civil servant shall fall due from the date of his departure from Lebanese territory for the seat of his post pursuant to the instructions given to him, unless he has been temporarily retained in the central departments by a decision of the Minister to perform a specific work during a period not exceeding two months, in which case the salary shall fall due starting from the date of his commencement of that work.

3- The new salary of a civil servant advanced in grade shall fall due starting from the first of the month following the month in which the advancement in grade took place.

4- The new salary of a civil servant promoted from one category to another category shall fall due starting from the date of issuance of the decree or decision ordering his promotion.

5- The new salary of a civil servant sentenced to reduction in rank or grade shall fall due starting from the date the judgment becomes final and binding.

Cases in which half salary is paid:

1- A civil servant suspended from work shall receive half of his salary starting from the day following the date on which he is notified of the decree or decision ordering his suspension from work, or starting from the date of his actual cessation of work if he ceased work prior to being notified of the decree or decision. The other half shall not be paid to him unless the Disciplinary Board acquits him or sentences him to a penalty of the first degree, or if the administration reverses its decision to refer him to the Disciplinary Board after the lapse of fifteen days from the date of his suspension from work.

2- A civil servant placed under judicial preventive detention shall receive half of his salary, and the other half shall not be paid to him unless his trial is barred, or he is acquitted, or he is sentenced to a penalty other than imprisonment.

Cases in which salary is discontinued:

1- Salary shall be discontinued for a civil servant placed outside the cadre or on availability, and for a civil servant suspended from work by a judgment of the Disciplinary Board, or dismissed from service, or placed on retirement, or who has resigned, or who has been removed from office, starting from the day following the date on which he is notified of the decree or decision, or from the date of his actual cessation of work if that occurred prior to notification being effected.

2- Salary shall be discontinued for a diplomatic or consular civil servant serving abroad, in the cases referred to in the preceding paragraph, starting from the date of his return to Lebanon, provided that he returns within a period of one month from the date of his being notified of the decree or decision. This period may be extended by a second month by a decision of the Minister.

3- Salary shall be discontinued for a civil servant who is deemed to have resigned pursuant to the provisions of the law starting from the day on which he ought to have returned to his post.

4- Salary shall be discontinued for a civil servant who reaches the legal age limit, starting from the day following his reaching that age, even if no decree or decision ordering his termination of service has been issued.

The Government may, in exceptional circumstances and cases the assessment of which rests with it, take certain special measures relating to the discontinuation of the salaries of civil servants, the wages of employees, and the allowances of contractors, and all other workers in public sector administrations, whether wholly or at varying rates.

The special measures set forth above shall be implemented whenever necessary by a decision taken in the Council of Ministers.

Travel Allowance and Transport Fares:

1- Civil servants travelling outside their duty station by reason of office shall receive a daily travel allowance, the amount and conditions of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

2- This allowance shall also accrue to members of the security forces and members of the customs in special exceptional circumstances, if they are detained for continuous deployment pursuant to a special order from the High Command addressed to each of them.

3- The travel allowance may be replaced by a lump-sum monthly allowance, the amount of which shall be determined by decree and which shall be allocated to the civil servant who is compelled by virtue of his office to travel frequently, provided that it does not exceed his rate set for the daily allowance.

4- The State shall provide means of transport for civil servants who travel outside their duty station by reason of office, or reimburse them for the transport fares they have incurred on the occasion of a mission with which they were officially entrusted, subject to conditions determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers. The State shall not be liable to compensate for damage caused to means of transport of whatever kind.

5- A civil servant may be granted an advance on the travel allowance and transport fares that may accrue to him.

Miscellaneous Allowances:

1- A civil servant may be granted a cash-handling responsibility allowance, or a car allowance, or a representation allowance, or a night-hours allowance, or an expatriation allowance, or a housing allowance, or an allowance to cover expenses incurred by him on the occasion of a public mission with which he is entrusted, or other allowances provided for by law.

2- The amount and conditions of these allowances shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

Cash Rewards:

A civil servant who performs a specific act meriting appreciation may be granted a cash reward determined by a decision of the competent Minister within the appropriations allocated for this purpose in special items of the budget, provided that the acts that warranted the reward are stated in the decision.

See Article Ten of Decree 3379 dated 11/7/2000 regarding the annual reward)

Maximum Limit of Allowances:

1- The total allowances and wages of whatever kind, and the rewards and proceeds that a civil servant receives from the State budget or from the budgets of public and private institutions and autonomous agencies, during a single financial year, may not exceed seventy-five per cent of the total of his monthly salaries in the same year.

2- There shall not be included in the calculation of this total the proceeds of tax collectors and prosecuting bailiffs, the travel allowances and transport expenses provided for in paragraphs 1 and 4 of Article 24, family allowances, representation allowance, night-hours allowance, acting allowance, and wages for teaching hours outside official working hours.

3- The provisions of the two preceding paragraphs shall not apply to diplomatic and consular civil servants and to military and technical attachés actually serving abroad.

Material Losses:

1- A civil servant may be granted compensation for a material loss sustained by him while performing an official mission, if it resulted from force majeure to which he was exposed by reason of office.

2- Compensation shall not be granted if the loss occurred by reason of the civil servant's negligence or a fault committed by him.

3- The injured civil servant must submit an application for compensation within fifteen days from the date of occurrence of the damage. If force majeure prevented the submission of the application within this time limit, it must be submitted immediately upon the cessation of such circumstances. The civil servant's right to compensation shall lapse if he does not comply with these conditions.

4- The compensation shall be granted by decree based on the opinion of a committee appointed by the competent Minister consisting of a delegate from his ministry, a delegate from the Ministry of Finance, and a delegate from the Central Inspection Administration. The committee shall conduct its investigations by all means it deems fit.

Sickness Grants:

1- The State shall bear the expenses of treating a civil servant if he contracts an illness or an infirmity resulting from the performance of his office.

2- A civil servant may be granted, in the event he contracts an illness or an infirmity not resulting from the performance of his office, or in the event a member of his family, namely a father, mother, children, spouse, or brothers and sisters who are his dependants, contracts the same, financial assistance determined by a decision of the Minister within the appropriations allocated for this purpose in special items of the budget.

3- The rules that must be adopted in granting sickness grants shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Civil Service Council.

4- The provisions of this Article shall continue to apply until social security benefits that provide this assistance are organised.

Family Assistance in the Event of the Civil Servant's Death:

1- If a civil servant dies as a result of an accident sustained by him by reason of office, his family shall be granted financial assistance equivalent to his salary at the date of death for a full year, provided that it is not less than five thousand and does not exceed ten thousand pounds.

2- If a civil servant dies for a reason unrelated to office, his family shall be granted financial assistance equivalent to his salary at the date of death for five months, provided that it is not less than two thousand and does not exceed four thousand pounds.

3- The assistance in both cases shall be distributed in equal shares among the members of his family, namely his father, mother, children, and spouse, and his brothers and sisters who were his dependants prior to death.

4- This assistance shall be granted by a decision of the competent Minister.

5- The provisions of this Article shall continue to apply until a cooperative scheme for civil servants that provides this assistance is established.

Assistance to the Civil Servant in the Event of the Death of a Member of His Family:

1- A civil servant shall be granted by a decision of the Minister, in the event of the death of one of his parents, children, or spouse, or in the event of the death of one of his brothers or sisters who were his dependants, financial assistance equivalent to his salary for one month at the date of death, provided that it is not less than five hundred pounds and does not exceed one thousand pounds. 2- If there are multiple persons who may benefit from the assistance, it shall be granted to the eldest of them.

3- The provisions of this Article shall continue to apply until a cooperative scheme for civil servants that provides this assistance is established.

Advancement in Step:

1- Every civil servant who has spent thirty months in a single step or in a step equivalent thereto since the date of his assumption of duties after his appointment or the date of his obtaining an increase in his salary shall acquire by operation of law one step within the category.

2- The Minister may, upon the proposal of the Director General or the President of the Central Inspection Administration, defer the date of advancement in step for a period of six months if it is established that the civil servant breached his duties. This measure may not be taken except after addressing a reprimand to the civil servant twice consecutively within a year, and after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Council.

3- The ceiling shall be opened in all categories, and a civil servant who has reached the ceiling in his category shall continue to benefit by operation of law and in accordance with the provisions governing advancement in step, from an increase in his salary equivalent to one step every two years in accordance with the scale of steps of the corps to which he belongs, provided that he remains in his category, and this increase shall be calculated as part of the basic salary. The salary due as a result of opening the ceiling shall be paid starting from the date of entry into force of this Law. This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.

4- Only the period of actual service for which the civil servant received his full salary shall be included in the calculation of the period of advancement in step.

Advancement:

1- Advancement brings forward the due date of the step increment by six months.

2- Every ministry or administration shall send to the Civil Service Board before the end of the month of June of each year a list of the names of the civil servants whom it proposes to advance, provided that their number does not exceed ten per cent of the total civil servants of the ministry or administration whose step increment due date falls in the following financial year, and that this number is distributed, as far as possible, among the various categories according to the percentage.

3- The list shall be accompanied by a statement of the marks and the justifying reasons for advancement in accordance with the forms established by the Directorate of Personnel at the Civil Service Board.

4- The Directorate of Personnel shall take a decision before the end of the month of October of each year regarding the lists received by it.

5- The Directorate of Personnel may approve the lists or reject them in whole or in part. Whatever it approves shall be deemed effective. Whatever it rejects shall be returned to the competent ministry or administration with a statement of the justifying reasons for rejection. The competent ministry or administration may submit before the end of the month of November new proposals or statements supporting its previous proposals. The Board of the Civil Service Board shall take the final decision regarding these proposals and statements before the end of the month of December, and if it does not take a decision by this date, the proposals and statements shall be deemed effective as received by it.

6- The advancement shall take effect starting from the date specified for it in the decision of the Directorate of Personnel or the Board of the Civil Service Board, or on the date specified for it in the lists and statements received from the ministries and administrations if the Board of the Board does not take a decision by the specified date.

7- If it is not possible to disburse the advancements from the appropriations allocated to them in the budget, they shall be disbursed from the surplus resulting in the salary appropriations.

Promotion:

1- It is the transfer of the civil servant from one rank to a higher rank within the same category and from one category to another category.

2- A civil servant shall not be promoted from one rank to another rank unless he is in the first step in his rank and his name is listed on the promotion roster. This is subject to the provisions of paragraph 4 of this Article.

3- Every ministry or administration shall draw up a promotion roster and send it to the Civil Service Board before the first of October of each year and include therein the names of the civil servants whom it nominates for transfer from one rank to another rank in the same category, or from the third category to to the second and from the second to the first, and shall attach to the roster the justifying reasons, and the Civil Service Board shall make a final determination on this roster before the end of the first of January, and it may seek the opinion of the Central Inspection Administration before taking its decision. If it does not take its decision by the specified date, the roster shall be deemed effective as received from the competent ministry or administration.

4- Engineers shall be promoted from one rank to another rank if they are in the top three steps in their rank and their name is listed on the promotion roster, in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 3 of this Article.

"1- A civil servant is entitled, after the expiry of one year from his appointment, and in each subsequent year he spends in actual service, to benefit from an annual leave on full salary for a period of fifteen days. One day shall be added to this period for every 5 years of actual service. Excluded from this are civil servants who benefit from judicial and school holidays".

This Article shall take effect as of the year 2020.

2- Leaves may accumulate for a maximum period of three years.

3- Each department shall schedule the dates of the leaves of the civil servants subordinate to it, in a manner that ensures the continuity of work therein. The leave decision must mention the name of the civil servant who replaces the civil servant on leave throughout the period of his absence and acts on his behalf in all his powers and responsibilities.

4- Dismissal from service or placement on retirement shall not take effect until after the expiry of the period of administrative leaves to which the civil servant is entitled.

Family leaves:

A civil servant is entitled, in addition to his annual leave, to be absent with permission and on full salary, for a period of one week at most, in the event of his marriage, or the death of his spouse or one of his ascendants or descendants or his brothers or sisters

Leaves without salary:

A civil servant may be granted for private reasons, and upon his request, a leave without salary not exceeding three months which may be extended for another three months, provided that the total of private leaves does not exceed six months during five consecutive years

Maternity leaves:

A pregnant female civil servant shall be granted a leave on full salary called "maternity leave" for a maximum period of ten weeks. Maternity leave shall not be included in the calculation of administrative leaves nor in the calculation of sick leaves.

1 - Maternity leave shall be granted all at once without division when the applicant therefor is about to give birth.

2 - In order to be granted maternity leave, the female civil servant must submit a special request containing:

a - The start date of the leave and its end date.

b - The approximate date of delivery according to the physician's report.

3 - A female civil servant who has been granted maternity leave is not entitled to submit medical sick reports during the period of maternity leave, nor is she entitled to divide this leave.

Health leaves:

1- A civil servant who is absent for health reasons is entitled to receive his full salary for a period of one month at most, provided that he informs his superior immediately of his current address and of the reasons calling for absence, and that he sends to him a medical report stating the nature of the illness and specifying the period of absence approximately.

If the civil servant refrains from sending the medical report, he shall be subject to disciplinary penalties, and the administration shall be entitled to send a physician to examine him at his own expense, and the expense required therefor shall be deducted from the salary of the civil servant. If the period of absence exceeds ten days, the superior shall request the Ministry of Public Health to delegate a physician to examine the absent civil servant and draw up a report on him.

2- If the absence exceeds one month without interruption, or one month over several stages within three months, the leave on full salary shall only be granted based on the opinion of the Official Medical Committee and for a maximum period of three months renewable, provided that the total of leaves does not exceed nine months during a full year or eighteen months during five consecutive years.

3- The Medical Committee referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be composed of three physicians in each governorate, appointed by a decision of the Minister of Public Health. A reserve panel of three other physicians shall be appointed in the same decision. The civil servant may, if he wishes, be assisted when appearing before it by a physician of his choice. If it is impossible for him to travel, the Committee shall travel to the place of his presence at the expense of the administration.

4- If the absence exceeds a period of nine months during a year or eighteen months during five consecutive years, the civil servant shall be referred at the end of the period to the Medical Committee to look into his case. If he is curable within a period of two years, he shall be granted a leave on half salary for a period of one year at most and then placed on availability without salary for a period of another year, and he shall not thereafter be returned to his work except based on the opinion of the Medical Committee.

If he is not curable within a period of two years, or if the Medical Committee deems during this period or at the end thereof that he is unable to resume his work, he shall be dismissed from service or placed on retirement in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

5- A civil servant residing outside Lebanon by virtue of his function, or legally absent therefrom, is entitled to obtain a health leave or request the extension of a previous health leave, within the conditions referred to in paragraphs (2) and (4) of this Article, based on medical reports certified by the head of the Lebanese diplomatic or consular mission or certified by the local health departments where there is no Lebanese mission.

The authority vested with the right to grant leaves:

1- Administrative leaves, whatever their duration may be, family leaves, maternity leaves, and sick leaves the duration of which does not exceed one month, shall be granted by a decision of the Director General.

2- Sick leaves the duration of which exceeds one month, and leaves without pay, shall be granted by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

Transfer from one corps to another:

1- A civil servant may be transferred from one corps to another after the approval of the Civil Service Board if he satisfies all the conditions of appointment in the corps to which his transfer is intended, including the condition of a competitive examination.

2- The transfer shall be effected by a decree or by a decision issued by the authority vested with the right of appointment.

3- It is a condition for the transfer that the post to which the civil servant is intended to be transferred be vacant in the cadre and have a special appropriation allocated to it in the budget. 4- The transferred civil servant shall retain the seniority acquired in his previous corps, unless his transfer results in an increase in his salary equivalent to at least one step.

Transfer from one administration to another within the same corps:

1- A civil servant may be transferred from one administration to another administration within the same corps after the approval of the Civil Service Board.

2- The conditions stipulated in paragraphs (2) and (3) of the preceding Article shall apply to the transfer from one administration to another, within the same corps. The transfer shall not result in an increase in salary.

Transfer within the same corps and the same administration:

1- A transfer from one post to another post, within the same corps and the same administration, shall be effected after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board:

a- By a decree for civil servants of the Second Category.

b - By a decision of the Minister for civil servants of the Third Category.

c- By a decision of the Director General for civil servants of the Fourth and Fifth Categories.

The transfer of members of the official teaching staff shall be exempted from seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

2- The transfer must be based on considerations derived from the interest of the service and a reasoned decision must be issued in respect thereof.

Conditions for the appointment of an acting civil servant:

1- An acting civil servant is a civil servant temporarily assigned to occupy a post other than his original post.

2- The authority that appoints the titular incumbent shall appoint the acting civil servant, and it may temporarily relieve him of the duties of his original post or keep him therein.

3- An acting civil servant may only be appointed to a vacant post or to a post in which the titular incumbent is absent.

4- The acting civil servant must be from the corps of the titular incumbent. If that is not possible, he may be appointed from another corps from among the civil servants of the same Ministry.

5- The acting civil servant must satisfy the conditions prescribed for appointment to the vacant post, with the exception of the two conditions of age and competitive examination.

6- An acting civil servant may not be appointed for a period exceeding one year.

- The acting appointment may be renewed in the same manner.

7- A civil servant may not be appointed to more than one post.

8- Where necessary, and by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, common rules may be laid down for acting appointments to the various posts of the public administrations.

Rights and duties of the acting civil servant:

1- The acting civil servant shall exercise all the powers of the titular incumbent and shall be bound to carry out all his responsibilities and duties.

2- The acting civil servant shall receive the permanent allowances allocated to the post which he occupies in an acting capacity. If permanent allowances are allocated to him in his original post, he shall receive the higher allowance.

3- The acting civil servant shall have no vested right to appointment to the post which he occupies in an acting capacity.

4- The acting civil servant shall receive an acting allowance equivalent to half the difference between his salary and the salary of the lowest step of the category of the post which he occupies in an acting capacity; however, if his salary is equal to or exceeds the salary of this step, he shall not be entitled to any acting allowance. The allowance shall be due ipso jure, even if it is not expressly mentioned in the instrument of appointment.

5- The acting allowance shall be disbursed from the appropriations allocated to salaries or from the appropriations allocated to miscellaneous allowances.

6- A civil servant who is appointed in an acting capacity outside his place of residence shall receive the relocation allowance stipulated in Article (24).

Definition of secondment:

A seconded civil servant is one who has been temporarily relieved of the duties of his original post and assigned to another mission while retaining the right to receive his salary and his right to step advancement, promotion, advancement in category, and retirement in his original administration.

Cases in which secondment is permissible:

1- A civil servant may be seconded for specialization in one of the branches in which the administration needs new specialists.

The conditions for secondment for specialization shall be laid down by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

2- A technical civil servant may be seconded from one Ministry to another Ministry, after the approval of the two competent Ministries. The authority vested with the right of appointment shall decide upon the secondment.

Decree 7366 dated 18/8/1961 stipulated the necessity of obtaining the approval of the Civil Service Board for the application of the provisions of paragraph 2 above.

Status of the seconded civil servant

1- A seconded civil servant shall be subject, from the disciplinary standpoint, to the administration to which he is seconded.

2- The post of the seconded civil servant shall remain vacant in the cadre of his original administration, and he shall return to it immediately upon the expiry of the period of secondment.

Prohibition of other statuses:

With the exception of the statuses of titular incumbency, acting capacity, and secondment, no other status for active civil servants, such as placement at the disposal of a Minister or of any administration, shall be considered lawful, except for the other cases stipulated by law.

Conditions for placement outside the cadre:

1- A civil servant may be placed temporarily outside the cadre for the purpose of attaching him to one of the public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, international institutions, or States.

2- A civil servant placed temporarily outside the cadre shall cease to receive his salaries, and shall retain his right to step advancement in his cadre and his right to a retirement pension or dismissal indemnity.

Civil servants placed outside the cadre for the purpose of attaching them to a public administration, a public institution, a municipality, or a Lebanese mixed-economy company shall not be entitled, upon the termination of their service therein, to receive any retirement pension or dismissal indemnity from its budget in respect of their services therein.

The provisions of the second sub-paragraph of paragraph 2 of Article 50 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959, added pursuant to Article Eight of this Law, shall apply to employees of municipalities and employees of public institutions placed outside the cadre or in any similar status for the purpose of attaching them to a public administration, a public institution, a municipality, or a Lebanese mixed-economy company. (Article 16 of L.D. 58/1982).

3- A civil servant of the Third Category and below shall be placed temporarily outside the cadre at his request by a decision of the Minister after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Board, in which the duration of the placement outside the cadre shall be specified. The administration shall have the right to revoke this measure at any time in the same manner. As for civil servants of the First and Second Categories, their placement outside the cadre shall be effected by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Board.

4- The civil servant shall receive the salary of the new post to which he has been attached or the allowance allocated thereto.

5- The civil servant shall continue to pay the pension deductions on the basis of his original salary.

6- If the duration of the placement of the civil servant outside the cadre exceeds one full year, his original post shall be considered vacant, and the administration shall have the right to appoint a successor to him therein, provided that it notifies him of its intention to do so and gives him the choice between returning to his original post or remaining outside the cadre.

Return of the civil servant after the expiry of the period:

A civil servant placed outside the cadre shall be reinstated to his original post, if it is still vacant, by a decision of the authority vested with the right of placement outside the cadre, after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Board; if this post is not vacant, a post of an equivalent category shall be assigned to him by the authority competent to appoint, or a lower post shall be offered to him while retaining his original salary. If he refuses this latter post, he shall be placed on retirement or dismissed from the service.

Conditions of Placement on Inactive Status:

1- A civil servant shall be deemed to be on inactive status when he is placed ex officio or upon his request outside the cadre, whereby his salary is discontinued, and he loses his right to step advancement and retirement calculation throughout the period he spends outside the cadre.

2- A civil servant of the Second Category and below shall be placed on inactive status by a decision of the Minister following the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council. As for civil servants of the First Category, their placement on inactive status shall take place by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers following the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

3- A civil servant may be placed on inactive status upon his request if he suffers a grave accident, or in the event of the illness of his spouse or one of his descendants, or for the purpose of his undertaking studies from which the Administration seeks a public benefit, provided that the period of inactive status does not exceed one year renewable twice.

4- A civil servant may be placed on inactive status ex officio in the cases provided for by law.

5- The competent Administration shall verify that the civil servant placed on inactive status upon his request does not violate the purpose for which he was placed on inactive status. It may at any time revoke its decision approving the request for inactive status.

Termination of Inactive Status:

The provisions of Article (51) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the civil servant at the end of the period of inactive status. If the civil servant was placed on inactive status for the purpose of his undertaking a study from which the Administration seeks a public benefit, his original position shall remain vacant and he shall mandatorily be reinstated to it.

Disciplinary Liability:

A civil servant shall be deemed liable from the disciplinary standpoint and shall be subject to disciplinary penalties if he intentionally or negligently breaches the duties imposed upon him by the laws and regulations in force, and in particular the duties provided for in Articles 14 and 15 of this Legislative Decree, and disciplinary prosecution shall not preclude the prosecution of such civil servant, where applicable, before the competent civil or criminal courts.

Disciplinary Penalties:

Disciplinary penalties are of two degrees:

First Degree:

1- Reprimand.

2- Salary deduction for a period of fifteen days at most.

3- Deferment of step advancement for a period of six months at most.

Second Degree:

1- Deferment of step advancement for a period of thirty months at most.

2- Suspension from work without salary for a period not exceeding six months.

3- Reduction by one step or more within the same rank.

4- Reduction of rank.

5- Termination of service.

6- Dismissal.

The Authority Vested with the Right to Impose Disciplinary Penalties:

1- The Head of Department has the right to impose the penalty of reprimand and the penalty of salary deduction for a period not exceeding three days.

2- The Director, the Head of Service, and the Kaymakam have the right to impose the penalty of reprimand and the penalty of salary deduction for a period not exceeding the year days upon the proposal of the immediate superior of the civil servant.

3- The Director and the Muhafiz have the right to impose the penalty of reprimand and the penalty of salary deduction for a period not exceeding ten days upon a written proposal from the immediate superior of the civil servant.

4- The Minister, upon the proposal of the Director General or the President of the Central Inspection Administration, has the right to impose upon the civil servant any penalty of the First Degree, provided that the third penalty thereof shall not be imposed except after addressing two consecutive reprimands to the civil servant within one year.

5- The Disciplinary Council has the right to impose any penalty of the Second Degree penalties, and it also has the right to impose any penalty of the First Degree if it appears to it that the civil servant does not deserve a more severe penalty.

6- Each of the authorities mentioned in the first three paragraphs of this Article, after having taken the penalty falling within the scope of its competence, has the right to propose to the authority superior to it the adoption of a more severe penalty.

(Implicitly repealed pursuant to Article 13 of Law 54/1965)

Composition of the Disciplinary Council:

1- Disciplinary Councils are three:

A Council for civil servants of the First and Second Categories and for Inspectors General and Inspectors affiliated with the Central Inspection Administration, a Council for civil servants of the Foreign Service of whatever category they may be, and a Council for other civil servants of any service and any category, with the exception of cases in which the law provides for special disciplinary councils.

2- The Special Disciplinary Council for civil servants of the First and Second Categories, and Inspectors General and Inspectors affiliated with the Central Inspection Administration, shall be composed of the Board of the Civil Service Council, of a judge of at least the Second Category delegated by the Ministry of Justice, and of a civil servant of the rank of the civil servant referred to the Disciplinary Council delegated by the President of the Council of Ministers, and the President of the Central Inspection Administration shall perform the function of Government Commissioner if the Disciplinary Council is trying a civil servant of the First Category; however, if the Council is trying a civil servant not of the First Category, an Inspector General delegated by the President of the Central Inspection Administration for this purpose shall perform this function.

3- A special disciplinary council for trying civil servants of the Foreign Service shall be appointed by decree.

4- The Disciplinary Council for all other civil servants shall be composed by decree for a period of one year upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Council, of a president who is a judge of the Second Category delegated by the Ministry of Justice, three civil servants of the Second Category, and a civil servant of the rank of the civil servant referred to the Disciplinary Council. It shall have two panels, regular and alternate. The President of the Central Inspection Administration, or an Inspector General or an Inspector whom he delegates for this purpose, shall perform the function of Government Commissioner before it.

5- If several civil servants from different categories are referred to the Disciplinary Councils on account of a single case, the Council competent to try the highest of them in category shall try the rest.

6- A clerk from the Central Inspection Administration delegated by its President shall be attached to each Disciplinary Council.

Manner of Referral to the Disciplinary Council:

1- A civil servant shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council by a decree or by a decision from the authority vested with the right of appointment. He shall also be referred by a decision from the Central Inspection Board.

2- The decree or decision providing for referral to the Disciplinary Council may provide for the suspension of the civil servant from work. The civil servant shall remain suspended until the Disciplinary Council rules on his matter or the authority that referred him to discipline revokes the referral decision.

3- The Minister has the right to suspend from work civil servants of the Second Category and below prior to referring them to the Disciplinary Council, for a period not exceeding fifteen days. If they are not referred to the Disciplinary Council at the end of this period, their salaries shall be restored to them in full.

Procedure before the Disciplinary Boards:
