1- The Government Commissioner shall examine the case file, request from the civil servant all clarifications which he deems necessary, and then prepare an opinion which he shall transmit with the file to the President of the Disciplinary Board within one month from his receipt of the file.

2- The President shall convene the Disciplinary Board to meet within one week from the date of his receipt of the file.

3- The meetings of the Disciplinary Board shall be confidential, and shall not be deemed valid unless attended by all members, provided that an absent member shall be replaced by a member of the alternate panel, or vice versa.

4- The civil servant shall have the right to inspect all documents relating to him, to make copies of such documents as he deems necessary for his defence, and to be assisted by one lawyer or one civil servant of his rank during his appearance before the Board.

5- The civil servant must attend the hearings in person, and if he is absent he shall be notified a second time. If he fails to attend, the Board shall examine the case on the basis of the investigation and its decision shall be deemed rendered inter partes.

6- The Board must decide the case within two months at most from the date on which the opinion of the Government Commissioner is lodged with its President.

7- A decree or decision referring a matter to the Disciplinary Board may not be revoked after the Government Commissioner has referred the file to the President of the Board.

8- Not more than one penalty may be imposed on the same civil servant in the same case unless the second penalty is issued by the Disciplinary Board or by a higher superior, in which case the first penalty shall be annulled.

9- The Board shall adopt reasoned decisions by a majority of votes.

10- Resignation shall have no effect on the disciplinary prosecution of the civil servant.

Effect of Decisions Issued by the Disciplinary Boards:

1- Penalties imposed by the Disciplinary Boards shall be executed immediately without a decree or decision.

2- No pardon may be granted in respect of penalties imposed by the Disciplinary Boards.

3- A civil servant sentenced to dismissal from service or removal from office may not be reinstated into service in any department of the State, municipalities, or public institutions.

1 - A civil servant shall be referred to the criminal courts where it appears that the acts attributed to him constitute an offence punishable under the Penal Code and other laws in force.

2 - Where the offence arises out of the office, the civil servant may not be prosecuted criminally except with the approval of the administration to which he belongs.

Public prosecution shall not be initiated by way of a personal claim.

3 - The Public Prosecution shall submit to the competent authority determined by law a request seeking its approval to prosecute the civil servant, accompanied by the file. The competent authority determined by law shall decide upon the request, by a reasoned decision, within a period of fifteen working days following the receipt of the request by the administration, and the expiry of this period without a decision thereon shall be deemed an implicit approval thereof.

The decision of the competent authority granting leave to prosecute shall not be subject to any form of appeal.

4 - If the competent authority determined by law refuses the request of the Public Prosecution to grant leave to prosecute, the Public Prosecution may, within a period of fifteen days from its notification of the decision of refusal, refer the matter to the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, who shall decide thereon by a reasoned decision notified to the concerned parties within a similar period, and the expiry of this period without a decision on the approval shall be deemed an implicit approval of the prosecution.

5 - The President and the two members of each of the Board of the Civil Service Council, the Central Inspection, and the Higher Disciplinary Board shall remain subject to the special legal provisions applicable to them.

6 - The public prosecution is independent of the disciplinary action, and the institution of a public prosecution shall not preclude the institution of a disciplinary action, the proceeding therewith, and the rendering of judgment therein.

Civil Liability:

If a civil servant commits an act harmful to a third party during the exercise of his office or by reason of his exercise thereof, the State shall be liable towards the third party for the act of the civil servant, and the State, in the event that damages are awarded against it, shall have a right of recourse against the civil servant if it appears to it that he committed a gross fault that could easily have been avoided.

Cases in which Service Terminates:

The service of a civil servant shall terminate and he shall permanently leave the establishment in each of the following cases:

1- Resignation.

2- Dismissal from service or placement on retirement.

3- Removal from office.

Resignation upon the Request of the Civil Servant:

1- A civil servant may submit his resignation in writing to the administration to which he belongs. He must continue to perform his duties until the administration decides upon his request.

2- The authority vested with the power of appointment shall decide upon the request for resignation. If it does not refuse the resignation within two months from the date of its submission, it shall be deemed accepted by operation of law.

3- A decree or decision accepting the resignation may not be revoked or amended after its issuance.

4- A resigning civil servant shall not benefit from his rights to a retirement pension or dismissal indemnity, but shall be paid the retirement deductions withheld from his salaries.

5- A resigned civil servant may not be reinstated into service unless he fulfils all the conditions for appointment with the exception of the age requirement. In such case, he shall be reinstated to his former rank and step, provided that he refunds in a single lump sum to the Treasury the full amounts he received pursuant to the preceding paragraph.

Cases in which a Civil Servant is Deemed to Have Resigned:

1- The following shall be deemed to have resigned:

A- A civil servant who is appointed or transferred and fails to assume his duties without a legitimate reason within fifteen days from the date of his notification of the decree or decision appointing or transferring him.

B - A civil servant who absents himself from his work without legal leave and fails to resume his work within fifteen days from the date of his absence from work.

C- A civil servant who fails to resume his work after the expiry of fifteen days from the date of the termination of his leave.

D- A civil servant who goes on strike from work.

In this case, a replacement may be appointed in his stead from among those who fulfil the conditions of appointment for the position which he occupied, with the exception of the condition of competitive examination.

2- Resignation in the aforementioned cases shall be formalised by a decree or decision issued by the authority vested with the power of appointment.

3- The provisions of paragraphs 3 and 4 of the preceding Article shall apply to a civil servant deemed to have resigned.

A civil servant deemed to have resigned may not be reinstated into service unless he fulfils all the conditions for appointment, with the exception of the age requirement, provided that the difference, in all events, between his age and the retirement age prescribed for the position for which he is a candidate shall not be less than the minimum period required for entitlement to a retirement pension. A civil servant deemed to have resigned who is reinstated into service shall be appointed to the last step of the last rank in the category.

Placement on Retirement and Dismissal from Service:

1- Placement on retirement is the termination of the civil servant's service and his final removal from the establishment, provided that a retirement pension is allocated to him, and this measure shall apply to civil servants who have reached a specified age and have spent the statutory period in service in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force.

2- Dismissal from service is the termination of the civil servant's service and his final removal from the establishment, provided that he is granted a dismissal indemnity, and this measure shall apply to civil servants who do not receive a retirement pension, either because they are not subject to the retirement system, or because they do not meet the prescribed conditions to obtain a retirement pension, despite being subject to the retirement system.

3- A civil servant shall be placed on retirement, or dismissed from service, by a decree or by a decision of the authority vested with the power of appointment. His service shall be deemed terminated ipso jure upon his reaching the statutory age or on the day following the notification to him of the decree or the decision or from the date of his actual cessation of work where his service terminated prior to his reaching the age limit.

4- A civil servant may not be reinstated into service, even temporarily, if he was dismissed or placed on retirement by a judgment of the Disciplinary Board or for reaching the statutory age. He may be reinstated in other cases provided that he meets the conditions of appointment with the exception of the condition of age, whereupon he shall be reinstated to his former rank and grade, and if he had received a dismissal indemnity, his previous services shall not be added to his new services unless he returns the dismissal indemnity, in a single lump sum, to the Treasury prior to assuming his new post. However, if he was receiving a retirement pension, the payment of this pension to him shall be suspended.

5- If a retired civil servant is appointed to a public institution attached to the State or the municipalities, he may receive from this institution only the difference between the retirement pension and the salary of the post to which he is appointed. Where the civil servant has benefited from a dismissal indemnity instead of the retirement pension, he may receive from the aforementioned institution only the difference between the retirement pension calculated on the basis of the services in respect of which he received the dismissal indemnity and the salary of the post to which he is appointed.

Grounds for Dismissal from Service and Placement on Retirement:

A civil servant shall be dismissed from service or placed on retirement in the cases provided for by law, or by a decision of the Disciplinary Board, or in each of the following cases:

- Reaching the statutory age.

- Abolition of the post.

- Professional incompetence.

- Reorganisation of departments.

1- Every civil servant who has completed sixty-four years of age shall be placed on retirement or dismissed from service ipso jure.

2- As for those who perform work requiring unusual physical exertion, they shall be placed on retirement or dismissed from service ipso jure upon completing sixty years of age; these posts shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Civil Service Board within six months from the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree, and they shall be placed on retirement or dismissed from service ipso jure if forty years have elapsed since the date of their entry into service for those appointed after 13 January 1955, and forty-two years for those appointed prior to this date

For the purpose of placement on retirement ipso jure by reason of completing the period provided for in Article 68 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959, account shall be taken of the date of the civil servant's entry for the first time into the service of public administrations, whether such service was by way of permanent or temporary appointment, employment, or contracting, even if such services are not counted for the calculation of the retirement pension or the dismissal indemnity.

3- Placement on retirement or dismissal from service shall be effected by a decision of the Board of the Civil Service Board, after consulting the competent administration and the Ministry of Finance.

4- A civil servant whose service has terminated by reason of reaching the statutory age or spending the statutory period in service shall cease work ipso jure. If he continues to work, no wage, salary, allowance, or remuneration shall accrue to him for the services he performs after reaching the age limit or the statutory period limit of service, and he shall be subject to criminal prosecution.

5- It shall not be permissible to contract with a civil servant placed on retirement or dismissed from service by reason of reaching the statutory age provided for in this Legislative Decree or spending the maximum period for the termination of service provided for in this Legislative Decree in service, nor shall it be permissible to employ him to work in any public administration, public institution, or municipality.

6- Excluded from the provisions of paragraph five are members of the teaching staff at the Lebanese University holding the rank of professor or who meet the conditions of the rank of professor and with whom the Lebanese University may contract to supervise the preparation of Lebanese doctoral dissertations in the various fields of specialisation therein, starting from their reaching the statutory age and until they complete sixty-eight years of age. This shall be subject to obtaining the prior approval of the Council of Ministers on the proposals of the Lebanese University.

See Articles 3 and 4 of Decree 7881 dated 27/7/1967

Voluntary Termination of Service:

"A civil servant whose actual services in the permanent establishments have reached at least twenty years may request his dismissal from service or his placement on retirement. The authority competent for appointment shall accept the request for termination of service after the approval of the Civil Service Board. In the event that the Civil Service Board rejects the request, the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers to take the appropriate decision thereon, and in the event that it rejects it, the Government may, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, grant the civil servant the right to collect 50% of the value of the dismissal indemnity due to him on the date of submitting the request, provided that:

1- The amount is allocated for the acquisition of one or more real properties or for the construction or completion of a building.

2- The exercise of the civil servant's right to collect the aforementioned portion of the dismissal indemnity is restricted to a single time.

3- A first mortgage annotation is placed on the real property in favour of the State in preservation of its rights towards the civil servant.

The mortgage annotation shall lapse ipso jure upon the settlement of the full amount or after the lapse of one year from the date of termination of the civil servant's service and the collection by the administration of its full rights.

Abolition of the Post:

If a post in the establishment is abolished and the appropriations allocated to it in the budget are deleted, the civil servant who occupied it shall be transferred to another vacant post in his corps, rank, and salary, in the administration to which he belongs or in another administration, provided that he meets the conditions of appointment with the exception of the conditions of competitive examination and age. If there is no vacant post in his corps and rank or if he does not meet the conditions of appointment thereto, a post lower than it in his corps shall be offered to him. If he accepts it, he shall retain his salary and the right of priority in appointment to a post of his rank. If he does not accept it, or if there is no vacant post in his corps, he shall be dismissed from service or placed on retirement.

Compensation:

1- No severance pay shall be due to a temporary employee who has resigned, is deemed to have resigned, or has been dismissed.

2- A temporary employee who is discharged, or whose term has expired, or whose work has ended, or who has reached the statutory age, shall be entitled to severance pay equivalent, for each year of actual service, to a rate of 85% (eighty-five per cent) of the last basic monthly salary he received. A month shall be calculated as one-twelfth of a year and a day as one-thirtieth of a month.

3- It shall be a condition for granting severance pay that the temporary employee has continued in service, each time, for a period exceeding one year. No intermittent service prior to the terminated service shall be taken into account.

4- A month shall be calculated as one-twelfth of a year, and a day as one-thirtieth of a month.

5- Any service performed by a temporary employee before reaching the age of twenty or after completing the statutory age shall not be included in the calculation of the compensation.

6- If a temporary employee dies before the expiration of his period of service, the members of his family shall be granted the severance pay as follows:

A- The full compensation to which he would have been entitled, to the spouse and children, and the father and mother within the conditions specified in the Retirement Law.

B - If the employee dies unmarried and the conditions prescribed in the Retirement Law are not met by his parents, they, or whichever of them is alive, shall be granted half of the severance pay.

In the absence of both parents, half of the compensation shall be granted in equal shares to his brothers and sisters whom he supported before his death.

7- An application for compensation shall be submitted to the Ministry of Finance within two years from the date of termination of service. The right shall lapse upon the expiration of this time limit.

8- The compensation shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance. Receipt of the compensation shall not preclude challenging the decision.

Rights of the temporary employee:

There shall apply to the temporary employee the provisions of Articles 16, 17 and 19 (paragraphs 3 and 4) relating to salaries, the provisions of Articles 21, 22, 23, 24, 26 and 29 relating to allowances and financial assistance, the provisions of Articles 35, 36, 38 and 39 relating to leave, the provisions of Article 37 relating to leave without pay, and Article 68 relating to termination of service, provided that he shall be discharged from service if the duration of his sick leave exceeds three months, and that the leave shall in no case exceed the term of appointment,

Duties of the temporary employee:

1- The provisions of Articles 14 and 15 relating to the duties of the permanent employee shall apply to the temporary employee.

2- If a temporary employee breaches his duties, there shall be imposed upon him, by a decision of the Minister or the Director General, the penalty of reprimand or deduction of salary for a period not exceeding ten days, or there shall be imposed upon him, by a decision of the Minister, the penalty of discharge from service.

3- The provisions of Article 61 relating to criminal liability and Article 62 relating to civil liability shall apply to the temporary employee.

4- A temporary employee shall be transferred by a decision of the Minister or of the employee delegated by the Minister for that purpose, even if the transfer requires a change in the place of work.

The Minister shall contract with Lebanese nationals for a specified period and to perform a specific work requiring special knowledge or qualifications, within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose and within the scope of the number specified therein, pursuant to a competitive examination conducted by the Civil Service Board in accordance with the rules.

Contractors shall be granted severance pay calculated in accordance with the bases specified in the preceding Article 83 relating to the severance pay of temporary employees. The prior services of contractors who are in service on the date of issuance of this Law shall be taken into account, whether as contractors or as permanent, temporary or daily-paid employees.
Wage earners shall be employed in each public administration in accordance with the special regulations prepared by that administration and approved by the Board of the Civil Service Board.
The statutory provisions relating to work emergencies shall apply to wage earners.
Wage earners shall be discharged in accordance with the provisions of the regulations to which they are subject.

Lebanese wage earners working in the service of the State and permanently attached to its administrations shall be entitled to receive severance pay, if they meet the following conditions:

1- That they are assigned to the work entrusted to them in accordance with the legal rules specified in the regulations applicable to each category of them.

2- That the duration of their service is not less than five hundred days of actual work.

3- That the average number of days of their actual work during the period of their service is not less than one hundred and eighty days in a single year.

4- That they have not absented themselves from work of their own accord, or failed or declined to comply with work requests addressed to them by the administration without a legitimate reason among the reasons provided for in the regulations of the category to which the wage earner belongs.

5- That they have not been discharged for any of the reasons set forth in the following Article.

A wage earner shall not be entitled to severance pay in each of the following cases:

1- If he commits an intentional act or omission aimed at causing harm to the interests of the administration.

2- If he commits serious violations of the instructions of the administration to which he belongs or of the regulations in force therein.

3- If he commits a felony or an intentional misdemeanour at the workplace or during the performance of work.

4- If it is established that he accepted a bribe or embezzled State funds, deposits entrusted to him, or materials handed over to him.

A wage earner shall be entitled to request his discharge from service in each of the following cases:

1- If the days of his actual work in a year fall below one hundred and eighty days for a reason attributable to the administration.

2- If he reaches the age of sixty.

3- If he suffers an infirmity or illness that prevents him from performing service.
In the appointment of employees, the provisions of Article 95 of the Constitution shall be observed.

If a disagreement arises between the Civil Service Board and the competent ministry regarding the application of the provisions of this Legislative Decree, the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers for determination.

An employee shall be prohibited, during five years after leaving service, from working in an establishment that was subject to his supervision in the administration to which he belonged, or that customarily supplied materials to that administration, or performed works on its behalf while the employee belonged to it. He shall be prohibited during the same period from having an interest in such establishment, or representing it, or undertaking its defence before the courts in disputes brought by it against public administrations and public institutions.

An employee who violates these provisions shall be punished by forfeiture of the right to benefit from a retirement pension. If he does not benefit from a retirement pension, he shall be punished by a fine not exceeding one thousand pounds, which shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

Surplus Posts:

1- If the number of civil servants working in any administration exceeds the number of posts specified for this administration in the numerical cadres, it shall draw up, within a period not exceeding three months commencing from the date of the text determining the cadres, a list of the names of civil servants whose number equals the number of surplus posts. Any natural person who is not of Lebanese nationality shall be deemed a foreigner within the meaning of this Law.

Subject to the provisions of international conventions and special laws, foreigners shall be subject to the provisions of this Law with respect to their entry into Lebanon, their residence therein, and their exit therefrom.

Members of the diplomatic and consular corps shall be exempted from this Law.

As for honorary consuls, they shall only be exempted from the special provisions concerning residence, entry, and exit.
A foreigner holding a transit visa, a residence visa, or a residence card shall have the right to move about in Lebanon, with the exception of places excluded by the competent authorities.

No non-Lebanese may enter Lebanon except through the posts of General Security and provided that he is equipped with the legal documents and visas and holds a travel document bearing a transit visa or a residence visa from a representative of Lebanon abroad, from the authority entrusted with looking after the interests of Lebanese nationals, or from General Security.

- No Lebanese may enter Lebanon except through one of the posts of General Security.

- As for non-Lebanese persons exempted from travel documents, the departments of General Security at the borders shall regulate their entry into Lebanon, and the details of the application of this paragraph shall be regulated by a decision of the Minister of Interior.

- A foreigner wishing to enter Lebanon to practice a profession or work must obtain prior approval from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, unless he is an artist, in which case he shall obtain this approval from the Directorate of General Security.

Nationals of certain countries arriving for tourism for a maximum period of three months shall be exempted from transit and residence visas by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.
A transit visa entitles its holder to Lebanon once and to reside therein for a maximum period of fifteen days.
The Directorate of General Security may, in exceptional cases, grant a person entering on a transit visa a residence visa.
A residence visa may be for a single journey or for several journeys for a maximum period of six months from the date of granting the visa.
The Directorate of General Security may extend a residence visa time after time for a maximum period of one year starting from the date of entry into Lebanon.

The Directorate of General Security shall grant foreigners wishing to reside in Lebanon for a period of one year and above annual residence cards or permanent residence cards valid for a period of- three years, renewable.

Annual or permanent residence cards permit their holder to return to Lebanon.
For the application of this Law, an artist means any person who performs an artistic show in places that serve alcoholic beverages by retail, present shows with music, and serve or do not serve food.

The following shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior:

A - The conditions of entry, residence, and work of foreign artists, and the fees imposed on them.

B - The conditions of operation of artists' employment offices (impresario).
The Directorate of General Security may require foreigners, in cases relating to State security, to obtain an exit visa.

Leaving Lebanese territory shall not be permitted except through the posts of General Security.

A special regime shall be established by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior in order to facilitate and regulate the movements of the inhabitants of the villages adjacent to the Lebanese-Syrian borders within an area to be determined in the same decree.

A foreigner shall be expelled from Lebanon by a decision of the Director of General Security if his presence constitutes a threat to public security and safety, and the Director of General Security must or immediately deposit a copy of his decision with the Minister of Interior.

Expulsion shall take place either by notifying the person concerned of the obligation to leave Lebanon within the period fixed by the Director of General Security, or by deporting him to the borders through the Internal Security Forces.
The Director of General Security may, with the approval of the Public Prosecution, detain a person whose expulsion has been decided until the formality of his deportation is completed.

The Director of General Security may grant foreigners who do not hold any travel document a laissez-passer to the countries to which they are bound in the two following cases:

A - If the foreigner is a refugee or of undetermined nationality.

B - If the foreigner holds the nationality of a State that has no representative in Lebanon.
A laissez-passer shall be valid for a maximum period of three years at the discretion of the Directorate of General Security.
A laissez-passer shall not entitle its holder to return to Lebanon unless it is accompanied by a return permit.
The fee due on a Lebanese passport shall be levied on a laissez-passer.
A joint laissez-passer may be drawn up for the head of the family, his wife, and his children who have not completed fifteen years of age.
A laissez-passer shall cease to be valid if its holder enters the territory of a country in which there is a representative of the State to which he belongs.

A foreigner who is not an artist is prohibited from engaging in any work or profession in Lebanon unless he is authorized to do so by the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

Every foreigner who is the subject of prosecution or convicted of a political offence by a non-Lebanese authority, or whose life or liberty is threatened for political reasons, may apply to be granted the right of political asylum.

Articles 196 and 197 of the Penal Code shall apply for the definition of a political offence. The provisions of Articles 30 to 36 of the General Penal Code relating to extradition shall remain in force.

The right of asylum shall be granted by a decision issued by a committee composed of:

- The Minister of Interior, as Chairman

- The Directors of Justice, Foreign Affairs, and General Security, as members

- In the event of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have the casting vote.

- The decision shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse, including recourse for annulment for abuse of power.

Any person granted the right of political asylum shall be issued a special card by the Directorate of General Security in which his full identity and the conditions imposed upon him, where applicable, shall be recorded.

The Committee may refuse to grant the right of political asylum or may revoke it and thereby order expulsion, or subject it to conditions such as residence within a specified area and other conditions.
No person granted the right of asylum shall be entitled, throughout his residence in Lebanon, to engage in any political activity.
If it is decided to expel a political refugee, he may not be deported to the territory of a state where his life or liberty would be at risk.

In implementation of the provisions of Article 19 of the Constitution, a council named the Constitutional Council is hereby established, whose task is to review the constitutionality of laws and all other texts having the force of law, and to adjudicate disputes and challenges arising from presidential and parliamentary elections.

The Constitutional Council is an independent constitutional body of a judicial nature.

The Constitutional Council shall consist of ten members.

The Chamber of Deputies shall appoint half of these members by an absolute majority of the number of members of which it is legally composed in the first round, and by a relative majority of the votes cast in the second round, and in the event of an equality of votes, the eldest shall be deemed elected.

The Council of Ministers shall appoint the other half by a majority of two-thirds of the number of members of the Government.

The members of the Constitutional Council shall be selected in accordance with the following:

1- Ten members from among honorary judges who have practised in the judicial, administrative or financial judiciary for a period of twenty-five years at least, or from among higher education professors who have taught a subject of law, political science or administrative science for a period of twenty-five years at least, or from among lawyers who have practised the profession of law for a period of twenty-five years at least.

2- A member of the Constitutional Council is required:

A - To have been Lebanese for ten years at least, enjoying his civil rights and not convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour.

B - To be not less than fifty years of age and not more than seventy-four years of age.

C - Anyone who wishes to be a member of the Constitutional Council and meets the conditions of membership must submit his candidacy by means of a declaration to which he attaches his detailed curriculum vitae and which he lodges with the registry of the Constitutional Council against a receipt.

D - The time limit for candidacy shall begin ninety days before the date of expiry of the term of office of a member of the Constitutional Council and shall end thirty days after its commencement. In the event of a vacancy in the seat of one of the members, the time limit for submitting a candidacy shall be ten days from the date of the announcement of the publication of the vacancy of the seat in the Official Gazette.

- Exceptionally, declarations of candidacy for membership of the Constitutional Council shall be submitted within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of entry into force of this Law.

Declarations of candidacy submitted previously which still meet the conditions for candidacy to the Constitutional Council shall remain valid.

F - At the end of the six years fixed for the term of office of a member of the Constitutional Council or upon the termination of membership by drawing lots, a member other than higher education professors working in the public sector and anyone subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Law shall be entitled to an indemnity equivalent to two months' emoluments for each year of service in the Constitutional Council, calculated on the basis of the allowances of the last month. This indemnity shall be paid in full to the member or to his heirs if he does not complete his term of office by reason of physical incapacity duly established or by reason of death.

The member shall forfeit these rights in the event of resignation.

As for higher education professors in the public sector and members subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Law, they shall be deemed seconded by operation of law and shall return to the practice of their work at the university upon the end of their membership in the Constitutional Council, and the period of their work shall be counted for them as actual service and they shall retain their right to advancement in step, subject to compliance with the retirement and dismissal from service regulations.

The term of office of the members of the Constitutional Council is six years, non-renewable, and the term of office of any of them may not be shortened.

- The calculation of this term shall begin from the date of taking the oath by all the members.

- In the event of a vacancy in the seat of one of the members by reason of resignation, physical incapacity, death or for any other reason, the Council shall declare the occurrence of the vacancy and the termination of the term of office in due form, and the President of the Council shall notify the same within one week to the authority that selected the member whose seat became vacant so that it may take note and appoint a replacement member.

- That authority shall appoint the replacement member within one month from the date of taking note, in the same manner in which the original member was appointed and for the remainder of his term of office.

The rule of non-extension shall not apply to the replacement member if the remainder of the term of office of the original member is less than two years, and absence from attending three consecutive sittings without a legitimate excuse shall be deemed a resignation.
