2 - Unlicensed cultivation or planting an area exceeding the areas provided for in the licence carried out by persons licensed to cultivate tobacco (Article 7, 8 and 10) if the seedbeds are not destroyed, there shall be imposed:

- A monetary penalty of 5 to 25 L.L.S., and the entire crops shall be confiscated or destroyed at the expense of the cultivator.

3 - Refusal to submit to the inspection of the crops (Articles 14 and 39).

- A monetary penalty of 15 to 50 L.L.S., and confiscation or destruction of the planted crop on the account of the planter.

4 - Failure to submit the declaration of the crop (Article 15)

- A fine of 5 to 100 L.L.S. with confiscation of the undeclared tobacco, or either of these two penalties.

5 - Failure to destroy the stalks and roots (Article 19) there shall be imposed upon him:

6 - Mixing the tobacco placed in sacks with prohibited substances (Articles 20, 27, 30, 32 and 40 Section One - or Section Two - h) confiscation of the sacks in which the mixing is verified.

7-

a- An unjustified shortage exceeding ten per cent between the declaration of the crop or the final assessment and the weight (Articles 21, 27 and 40 Section One- a) a monetary penalty of two pounds to five Lebanese pounds for each kilogram or fraction of a kilogram of the difference exceeding the tolerated rate.

b - An established shortage that has not been justified between the declaration of the crop or the final curing and the weight if the weighing took place after the curing of the tobacco

(Article 40 Section Two - e) a monetary penalty of two pounds to five Lebanese Syrian pounds for each missing kilogram or fraction of a kilogram.

c- An established shortage that has not been justified appearing in the accounts of the planter or the curers (Article 40 Section Two - d, h and Section Three a, b, c, d)

Furthermore, in the cases provided for in paragraphs b and c above, if the matter relates to the curers, the Monopoly Administration shall seize a quantity of the tobacco in his possession the value of which is equivalent to the monetary penalty assessed by the Monopoly Administration as a guarantee for the recovery of the said penalty.

8 - Failure to submit the declaration relating to loss or theft (Articles 23 and 40 Section Two - d) a fine of 5 to 25 Lebanese and Syrian pounds.

9 - Failure to deliver the tobacco to the warehouse within the specified time limit (Articles 24 and 40 Section One- e and Section Two - h) a fine of 2 to 10 Lebanese Syrian pounds for each kilogram, or fraction of a kilogram, with confiscation of the tobacco if it is not delivered to the warehouse before the rendering of the judgment.

The value of the fines and monetary penalties provided for in paragraphs 10/11/13/15/16 of Article 80 of Decision 16 dated 30/1/1935 (Tobacco and Tombac Monopoly) and everything relating to the smuggling of (non-national) tobacco and tombac and tobacco products wherever mentioned shall be increased.

The value of these fines shall be fixed at a rate of double the increase that has occurred or may subsequently occur to the minimum wage applied on 1/1/1961, amounting to 125 L.L., which is considered a fixed basis for every determination operation, pursuant to Law 175 dated 22/12/1992, Official Gazette 53 dated 31/12/1992.

10- Failure to obtain a selling licence (Article 41):

11- Selling at prices differing from the fixed price (Article 49):

12- Transporting leaf tobacco without a licence (Articles 17, 24 and 40 Section One b and Section Two f- and Article 57)

A fine of 5 Lebanese Syrian pounds for each kilo or part of a kilo with confiscation of the transported tobacco and seizure of the means of transport.

13- Acts of smuggling or acts considered as such Articles 22, 36, 48, 55, 59, 61 and 62:

And if the offender is one of the sellers of the Monopoly, there shall be imposed upon him - regardless of the penalties mentioned above - a fine of 300 Syrian pounds and the licence he holds shall be cancelled.

14- Secretly manufacturing tobacco (Article 63) a fine of 100 to 1000 Lebanese Syrian pounds with confiscation of the tools. As for the confiscated tobacco, it shall be subject to the penalties provided for in the aforementioned paragraph 13.

Upon repetition of the contravention, a penalty of imprisonment from 8 days to six months shall be imposed regardless of the penalties provided for in the preceding paragraph.

15- Manufacturing, using, or possessing counterfeit marks or stamps of the marks and stamps of the Monopoly Administration, or cigarette paper and tubes of the paper and tubes of the said Administration.

As for the judgment that will be rendered in the penal matter, it must also determine the amount of compensation that the offenders must pay to the Monopoly Administration in return for the losses and damages that they have caused to it as a result of their acts.

16- Manufacturing or possessing items - such as cigarette paper or boxes - where it appears from their mark and the writings mentioned thereon that they are intended for the manufacture of cigarettes or for placing manufactured products in boxes or packets regardless of their shape:

A fine of 150 Lebanese Syrian pounds and confiscation of the seized items.

17- Contraventions committed against the tobacco regulations and not referred to in the aforementioned penal provisions:

A fine of 10 to 50 Lebanese Syrian pounds

18- If it is established that some planters have committed the following acts:

- Failure to declare the planting (Article 8)

- Planting by unlicensed persons (Article 7)

- Failure to destroy the nurseries (Article 13)

- Failure to declare the crop (Article 15)

- Failure to destroy the seedlings and roots (Article 19).

- Mixing the tobacco placed in sacks with prohibited substances Articles 20, 27, 30, 32 and 39).

- An established and unjustified shortage of 10 per cent between the declaration of the crop, the final assessment, and the weight (Articles 21 and 27).

- Failure to declare the loss or theft of the crop (Article 23).

- Transporting tobacco leaves without a licence (Articles 17, 24, 39 and 57).

And they have furthermore committed, during or on the occasion of the inspection of these contraventions against them, a subsidiary contravention such as resisting or beating the officers of the Monopoly or

the officers referred to in Article 66 charged with assisting the officers of the Monopoly, the judge shall rule to prohibit them from engaging in the cultivation of tobacco for a period of one year or three years, and this shall not preclude the application of the provisions of this Article and the provisions of Article 82 below.

19- Failure to submit the declaration of origin or submitting a declaration contrary to the truth (Article 40 Section Two - c, e)

A monetary penalty of 5 to 100 Lebanese Syrian pounds with confiscation of the tobacco that was not declared or was declared in a manner contrary to the truth, or either of these two penalties only.

20- If it is established that a planter or a curer has committed the following acts:

- An established shortage that has not been justified appearing in the accounts of the planters or the curers (Article 40 - Section Two - g, h and Section Three - a, b, c, d).

- Failure to submit the declaration of origin or submitting it in a manner contrary to the truth (Article 40 - Section Two - c, e).

- Acts of smuggling or acts considered as acts of smuggling (Articles 61 and 62)

- Refusal to submit to the inspection of curing (Article 40 - Section Two b) mixing the tobacco placed in sacks with prohibited substances (Article 40 Section One-a- and Section Two - h)

- Failure to submit the declaration relating to loss or theft (Article 40 Section Two d)

- Failure to deliver the tobacco to the warehouse within the specified time limit (Article 40 Section One - e and Section Two h).

And if he has furthermore committed, during or on the occasion of the inspection of these contraventions, a subsidiary misdemeanour such as resisting or beating the officers of the Monopoly or the officers referred to in Article 66 charged with assisting the officers of the Monopoly, the judge shall rule to prohibit him from engaging in the cultivation and curing of tobacco for a period of one year to three years, and this shall not preclude the application of the provisions of this Article and the provisions of Article 82 of this Decision.

2 - In the cases referred to in the aforementioned paragraphs 18 and 20, if the offender (the planter or the curer) is at the same time a recognised exporting merchant, the judge shall rule to strike his name from the list of recognised exporting merchants for a period of one year to three years, and this shall not preclude the application of the provisions of these two paragraphs and the provisions referred to therein.

Subjecting the Accounts of Public Institutions and the Accounts of State-Affiliated Institutions and Utilities to the Internal Audit System and to Independent Auditing by Auditing and Accounting Firms.

1- In addition to the supervision of the Ministry of Finance and the supervision of the Court of Accounts provided for in the laws and regulations in force, the accounts of public institutions, and the accounts of State-affiliated institutions and utilities, which enjoy financial and administrative autonomy, shall be subject to the internal audit system and to an independent audit by an accredited auditing and accounting firm.

2- a- The internal auditor shall be appointed by a joint decision of the Minister of Finance and the supervisory Minister in a contractual capacity for a renewable term of one year, as a result of a call for tenders conducted by the institution or utility concerned, participation in which shall be restricted to accounting experts who meet the criteria and specifications determined by the Ministry of Finance.

b- The accredited auditing and accounting firm shall also be appointed by a joint decision of the Minister of Finance and the supervisory Minister, under a contract for a renewable term of one year, as a result of a call for tenders in which participation is restricted to auditing and accounting firms that meet the criteria and specifications determined by the Ministry of Finance.

3- The criteria and specifications that must be met by each of the internal auditor and the auditing and accounting firm shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance, taking into consideration in determining these criteria and specifications with respect to:

a- The internal auditor.

- Academic degree

- Practical experience

b- The auditing and accounting firm.

- The number of working auditors and accounting experts, their academic degrees, their practical experience, its duration and the names of the firms in which it was acquired, the number of companies and institutions whose accounts the firm has previously audited and the turnover of each of them.

4- The auditing and accounting firm shall exercise its duties in accordance with the generally accepted auditing and review standards adopted in auditing the accounts of private sector enterprises.

And the internal auditor shall exercise his duties in accordance with the principles of internal auditing, which includes in particular the internal control procedures adopted in the institution or utility.

5- The reports of the internal auditor shall be submitted to the Ministers of Finance and of supervision and to the board of directors of the institution or utility concerned, and the reports of the auditing and accounting firm shall be submitted to each of the Minister of Finance and the supervisory Minister, and copies thereof shall be sent to each of the Central Inspection and the Court of Accounts, with respect to public institutions and utilities subject to their supervision, and to the board of directors of the institution concerned or the utility concerned, and to the Annual Control Committee on Public Institutions at the Court of Accounts with respect to public institutions subject to its supervision, and a copy thereof shall also be sent to the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies.

6- In addition to the report of the financial controller, with respect to public institutions subject to his supervision, the reports of the auditing and accounting firm may be relied upon to show the financial position and economic results of the operations of the public institution or utility during the year covered by the report.

As for the reports of the internal auditor, they shall include observations relating to internal control procedures, the internal control system and the violations committed, along with a proposal for the corrective measures to be adopted.

7- The institution or utility concerned shall bear the expenses payable to each of the internal auditor and the auditing and accounting firm accredited to audit its accounts.

8- The details of the implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister.

Regularisation of the Status of Motor Vehicles Brought into the Border Zone During the Period of its Israeli Occupation

First: Notwithstanding any other text, in particular Law No. 150 dated 6/5/1992 and Law No. 368 dated 1/8/1994 as amended by Law No. 432 dated 15/5/1995, the Government is authorised, for a period of six months from the entry into force of the provisions of this Law, to regularise the status of motor vehicles brought into the border zone during the period of the Israeli occupation without the need to submit the documents customarily required in normal cases for bringing in motor vehicles and putting them into circulation within Lebanese territory, and it shall suffice to produce:

- A certificate issued by the International Theft Prevention Bureau of the Judicial Police proving that the motor vehicles requested to be placed into consumption are not the subject of prosecution to date.

- A certificate issued by the Internal Security Forces proving that the motor vehicle requested to be placed into consumption is not being pursued by them domestically.

- An undertaking by the owner of the motor vehicle to return it to its rightful owner or owners should it subsequently transpire that it is stolen, and to bear all resulting legal liabilities.

Second: The customs duties payable on these motor vehicles shall be levied, and they shall be exempted from any fine resulting from their importation into Lebanon in violation of the laws in force.

Publication of the Law

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
This Law governs the office of the notary public and the functions thereof and prescribes the rules for the practice thereof.

A notary public is a public officer entrusted, within the limits of his jurisdiction, with performing the acts set forth in this Law and in other laws and the acts which the interested parties request to be authenticated; he is attached to the Ministry of Justice and receives no salary or allowance from the State, and receives his fees from the interested parties in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The number of notaries public, the place of residence of each of them, and his territorial jurisdiction shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers; positions of notaries public may also be created in the regions that are in need thereof pursuant to decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.
Notaries public are trainee notaries public and tenured notaries public.

Conditions of Appointment:

A trainee notary public shall be appointed as a result of a competitive examination:

A candidate must:

1- Be a Lebanese national for at least ten years

2- Have completed the twenty-fifth year of his age and not have exceeded the forty-fourth year as at the date of commencement of the competitive examination, and his age must be stated in the decree of his appointment, and no subsequent amendment to such age shall be given effect regardless of the reasons therefor.

3- Be free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from discharging the duties of the office of notary public, and he must submit a certificate from the Official Medical Committee proving the same.

4- Enjoy his civil rights and not have been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour. The offences of theft, fraud, breach of trust, issuing a cheque without funds, embezzlement, bribery, forgery, use of forged documents, perjury, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code, and narcotic offences shall be deemed disgraceful.

5- Hold the Lebanese Licence in Law.

1- The Minister of Justice shall lay down the regulations of the competitive examination and shall determine the legal subjects in which it shall be held, provided that they shall not be fewer than five subjects.

2- The Ministry of Justice shall fix the date for holding the competitive examination and shall announce the same in two local daily newspapers and on the official Radio Lebanon at least one month prior to the date fixed therefor.

3- The Minister of Justice shall appoint a committee of judicial and administrative judges to decide on the acceptance of applications for candidacy for the competitive examination after conducting a personal interview with each candidate, and the decisions of this committee shall not be subject to any means of review, including an application for annulment for excess of power, and this committee shall perform the functions of the examining committee.

4- Applications for candidacy for the competitive examination shall be submitted to the Ministry of Justice, which shall give the candidate a receipt proving his submission of the application within the time limit fixed for accepting such applications.

5- Holders of a State Doctorate degree in Law who pass the competitive examination shall be awarded four marks, which shall be added to their total marks when drawing up the ranking of successful candidates.

A candidate who passes the competitive examination shall be appointed as a trainee notary public pursuant to a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice. The trainee notary public shall undergo a training course for a period of six months during which he shall be attached to one of the offices of a tenured notary public without the need to issue any instrument.

Notaries public shall not assume their functions until after:

a- They take before the Court of Appeal in Beirut the following oath:

"I swear by Almighty God to preserve the secrecy and ethics of the profession of notaries public, to perform the duties thereof with honesty, to abide by the laws and regulations thereof, and to conduct myself in all my acts in a manner that inspires confidence and respect".

b - They deposit specimens of their signatures and their addresses with the Directorate General of the Ministry of Justice, which in turn shall deposit the same with all competent authorities.

c - They furnish to the Ministry of Justice a guarantee the conditions of which shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Justice and Finance.

d - Each of them establishes premises for his office within the scope of his territorial jurisdiction determined in the decree of his appointment, and the provisions governing lease contracts for liberal professions shall apply in respect of the lease contract of these premises.
The functions of a notary public shall terminate ipso jure upon his completion of the sixty-fourth year of his age.

The Minister of Justice shall, by a decision issued by him, grant a notary public:

1 -

a - An administrative leave not exceeding thirty days per year upon his request, which he must submit at least one week in advance; however, in case of necessity, he may be granted leave for an additional period to be determined by a reasoned decision issued by him.

b - A sick leave the duration of which shall be determined in the decision granting it.

2 - The Minister of Justice shall assign one of the retired notaries public affiliated with the Council to carry out the functions of the tenured notary public during his absence on administrative or sick leave or in the case of permanent vacancy or absence without a legitimate excuse, or as a result of his temporary suspension from work and in the cases of permanent vacancy or absence without a legitimate excuse, or temporary suspension from work. Provided that he shall not be assigned more than twice.»

a - In addition to the general conditions required for the profession of notary public, the assigned retired notary public must fulfil the following conditions:

1 - That he shall not exceed the age of seventy up to the end of the period of his assignment, and that he enjoy the civil and legal capacity required to practise the profession of notary public.

2 - That no disciplinary decision has been issued against him by the Disciplinary Council during the period of his practice of the profession of notary public as a tenured notary public, with the exception of the penalties of warning and reprimand, and that he be of good conduct.

3 - That his assignment take place within the scope of the Governorate (Mohafaza) in which he was serving upon the termination of his functions or in a Governorate in which he practised the profession as a tenured notary public for more than ten years.

b - Where it is not possible to assign a retired notary public, the Minister of Justice may, after perusing the opinion of the Judicial Inspection, assign one of the permanent employees on the establishment of the Ministry or one of the judicial assistants or legal assistants holding the Lebanese Licence in Law for more than five years, to perform the functions of the notary public on a temporary basis during the absence of the notary public on leave.

Those mentioned in this paragraph must hold a certificate from the Council of Notaries Public proving their attendance of a training course conducted by the Council of Notaries Public.

The aforementioned course shall be accredited after the approval thereof by the Minister of Justice and shall become mandatory for assignment after the expiry of one year from the date of publication of this amendment.

No assignment to the functions of a notary public may be made for any of those mentioned above for a period exceeding six intermittent or consecutive months in a single year, and the person assigned must specifically and mandatorily state on the transactions he handles the following phrase: Temporarily assigned to the functions of the Notary Public in... (the region).

In the case of permanent vacancy or the absence of the notary public without a legitimate excuse or as a result of his temporary suspension from work, the person assigned to his functions from among the retired notaries public shall receive 50% fifty per cent of the fees collected, and a proportion of 25% twenty-five per cent shall accrue to the Treasury and 25% twenty-five per cent to the Mutual Aid and Retirement Fund for Notaries Public.

A person assigned from among the permanent employees on the establishment of the Ministry of Justice shall not benefit from the benefits of the Mutual Aid and Retirement Fund for Notaries Public. In all cases, the person assigned shall be subject to all the obligations incumbent upon the tenured notary public.
Notaries public may not be transferred or exchanged among one another without a written request from them, and the transfer and exchange shall be effected pursuant to a decree

Notaries public shall be subject to administrative and financial inspection by one or more judges, provided that their number does not exceed three, seconded for this purpose by the Minister of Justice from among the judges attached to the Ministry of Justice, and the inspection may be carried out by employees on the establishment of the Ministry of Justice of at least the third category under the supervision of the Director General of the Ministry of Justice.

They shall be assigned by a decision of the Minister of Justice. The Minister of Justice may request the Central Inspection Board to assign financial inspectors to carry out financial inspection at the offices of the notaries public. All inspection reports shall be submitted to the Ministry of Justice.
The judge delegated for inspection shall receive the allowances received by the inspector at the Judicial Inspection Board.

The Minister of Justice shall decide, after reviewing the inspection reports, and based on the gravity of the violations contained therein, either to impose one of the first three penalties provided for in Article Fifteen of this Law, or to refer the notary public to the Disciplinary Council for Civil Servants, and in the latter case the Minister of Justice may decide to suspend the notary public from practising his work for a period not exceeding six months.

The disciplinary penalties are the following:

1- Warning.

2- Reprimand.

3- Suspension from work for a period not exceeding six months.

4- Suspension from work for a period ranging between one year and three years.

5- Permanent prohibition from practising the profession of notary public.

The notary public shall be prosecuted judicially before the competent courts for every violation of the rules of the office, and in particular for every negligence occurring in the drawing up of deeds, in the keeping of accounts, or in the collection of fees.

He shall be punished in these cases by a fine from one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds to five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds; however, if the notary public commits the violation intentionally, he shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine from five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds to two million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

This shall not preclude the prosecution of the notary public by a claim for compensation by the injured party for damages resulting from fraud or error, nor shall it preclude the disciplinary prosecution of the notary public. The criminal prosecution of the notary public in respect of acts arising out of the exercise of his duties shall be subject to an authorisation from the Minister of Justice.

The office of the notary public shall consist of the notary public and of clerks and employees appointed by the notary public and of clerks and employees appointed by the notary public, whose wages and allowances he shall bear.

The clerks and employees are required to be Lebanese of full age, not convicted of a felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour.

The notary public must notify the Ministry of Justice of the names of these clerks and employees upon their appointment and upon their leaving his service.

The notary public shall be civilly liable for every fault committed by these clerks and employees during the performance of their work with him.

A mutual aid and pension fund for notaries public shall be established whose mission is to distribute medical, cultural, social and housing assistance, and to allocate a retirement pension according to what the management committee of the fund decides.

The mutual aid and pension fund shall be managed by a committee composed of six members, four of whom are incumbent notaries public, and two of whom are retired notaries public, chosen by the Minister of Justice, who shall name a president from among them provided that he is one of the incumbent notaries public.

The revenues of the Notaries Public Mutual Aid Fund shall consist of:

1- A monthly subscription fee determined by the committee of the fund after the approval of the Government Commissioner and the ratification of the Minister of Justice.

2- Donations which the committee of the fund decides to accept.

The notary public shall undertake:

1- Drawing up and authenticating the deeds provided for in the Code of Obligations and Contracts and, in general, every deed which the law does not prohibit or which does not fall exclusively by virtue of a special text within the competence of another public official, keeping the original thereof, and giving copies thereof to the concerned parties.

2- Accepting and keeping deeds, documents and deposits in kind, and delivering to the depositors a certified copy of the statement drawn up by him containing the conditions of deposit and the description of the deposit.

3- Drawing up the protest and serving it through a process server to establish refusal of acceptance or payment of bills of exchange, drafts and promissory notes in accordance with the laws in force.

4- Placing a date certain on the instruments presented to him.

5- Serving all notices and formal warnings through the process server and accepting actual tender and deposit in accordance with the provisions of Articles /822/ et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure.

6- Drawing up and authenticating wills in accordance with the provisions of the Law of Inheritance for Non-Mohammedans issued on 23/06/1959.

7- Authenticating the signature of the translator of instruments from one language into another.

8- Numbering the pages of the books and registers of merchants and members of the liberal professions in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Code of Commerce.

9- Taking fingerprints, keeping them, and authenticating the identity of their holder.

10- Seeking the assistance of process servers and members of the Internal Security Forces in order to carry out all notifications issued by his office.

The notary public may:

1- Transfer the seat of his office within the scope of its territorial jurisdiction after the approval of the Ministry of Justice.

2- Perform all acts falling within his competence outside official working hours and on official holidays.

3- Send monthly schedules to the Central Bank of the protests made on commercial papers relating to banks.

4- Carry out notification himself within his office at the request of the concerned parties or one of them, and in this case the rules of notification provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply.

The notary public must not draw up or authenticate any deed before verifying the identity of the contracting parties.

- If the notary public knows the contracting parties personally, he shall state that on his responsibility in the deed; otherwise, he must verify their identity:

- Either from their identity cards to which a personal photograph is affixed, or from their passports or their residence permits, or from the military card to which a personal photograph is affixed in respect of persons whom the law requires to carry this card, or by the testimony of two adult Lebanese witnesses known to the notary public or holding two identity cards to which their personal photographs are affixed, provided that they are not relatives of the contracting parties up to the fourth degree and are not afflicted with the infirmity of muteness and deafness. The notary public shall verify the capacity of the contracting parties and their acceptance to contract of their own free will, and shall also verify the capacity and authority of the guardian, the proxy, the partner and the representative of the legal person, as well as every person who takes the place of the party concerned, and shall state the place of residence of each of them and record all these matters in the body of the deed.

The notary public must keep a copy of the document that proves the capacity of the guardian, the proxy, or the representative of the legal person and everyone who takes the place of the original contracting party if the document produced is issued abroad; however, if the document is issued in Lebanon, the notary public must state that he has reviewed that document.

The notary public must read out to the contracting parties, the witnesses, and the translator, where applicable, the deed which he has drawn up and state that in the authentication clause, and all those present must sign at the bottom of the clause; then the notary public shall affix his seal to the deed, date it, and sign it.

If the notary public does not know the language of the contracting parties, he shall receive their declarations through a sworn translator, and the translator shall sign the deed in which he participated in this capacity.

If one of the contracting parties declares that he does not know how to sign his signature, the notary public shall require him to place the print of one of his fingers on the deed and shall indicate that in the authentication clause; however, if the concerned party is afflicted with an infirmity that prevents his ability to express his will in a natural manner, the notary public shall receive his declaration in the presence of two witnesses and the mukhtar of the locality, or the person with the infirmity shall name a person to the notary public in the presence of the two witnesses and the mukhtar of the locality whom he commissions to sign on his behalf on the deed, provided that the notary public states that in the authentication clause.
The probative force of the deeds drawn up by the notary public is the same force inherent in official deeds within the conditions provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure.

An instrument prepared for signing and authentication shall be drawn up in the Arabic language in clear handwriting or in print, stating therein the name of the concerned party, the names of both his parents, his nationality, the place and date of his birth, his place of residence, his civil status register number, the year, month and day on which the instrument was drawn up or authenticated, the name of the Notary Public, the place of completion of the act, the name of the translator and the witnesses, and the value of the fees collected, provided that they are written together with the date and numbers in words in a clear manner. Every deletion, addition or interlineation shall be indicated by a note in the margin signed by the Notary Public, the contracting parties, the witnesses and the translator, under penalty of the deletion and addition or interlineation being deemed null and void. The pages of the instrument shall be numbered and the number of sheets bound together shall be stated in words at the foot of the last page, and beneath this statement the contracting parties, the witnesses, the translator and the Notary Public shall sign, under the responsibility of the latter.
The Notary Public shall not consider the translation of a produced document as a probative document unless it is accompanied by the original or by a duly certified copy thereof.

The Notary Public shall draw up a detailed statement of the fees due to the Treasury and the remuneration he charges for every transaction falling within his competence and shall post it in a prominent place in his office.

The Notary Public must keep in an orderly manner registers of a uniform format approved by the Minister of Justice, and these registers shall consist of:

1- The daily register.

2- The register of deposits.

3- The register of correspondence.

4- The alphabetical index register.

5- The register of wills.

These registers shall be numbered and certified by the President of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction his office is located prior to commencing their use. In the daily register shall be recorded the daily operations carried out by the Notary Public according to their dates, and therein shall also be recorded a summary of the instruments, the names of the contracting parties, and the value of the fees and remuneration collected. The register of deposits shall be allocated for recording commercial bills of exchange, and the alphabetical index register for facilitating supervision, wherein the names of the contracting parties shall be stated in alphabetical order together with the date of their transactions, and the register of wills shall be allocated for keeping the wills drawn up and authenticated by the Notary Public.

6- The registers of the Notary Public shall not be removed outside his office except pursuant to an order issued by the judicial authority.

1- The Notary Public must collect for the account of the State and in accordance with the procedures stipulated in Decree No. 730 dated 13 July 1936 the Notary Public fees detailed in Schedule "A" annexed to this Law, and he must also affix the fiscal stamps due by law and cancel them. The copies retained by the Notary Public in his office in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall be exempted from all fees including the stamp duty.

2- In addition to the fees mentioned in Schedule "A" annexed to this Law, the Notary Public shall collect his remuneration at the rate of (30 %) thirty percent of the amount of the fees collected in accordance with Clause /1/, and he shall also collect for drawing up and drafting each page, regardless of the number of its copies, the amount of /7000/ L.L. seven thousand Lebanese Pounds, as well as /1500/ L.L. one thousand five hundred Lebanese Pounds for typing each original page regardless of the number of copies. A page shall be deemed to consist of twenty lines and a line of fifteen words as a minimum, and a single or last incomplete page shall be deemed as a full page. He shall also collect a rate of 001/0 one per thousand on contracts registered with him that are prepared for registration in the Land Registry offices and in the Commercial Register.

3- In the event that the Notary Public travels at the request of one of the interested parties, he shall collect an allowance in the amount of twenty thousand Lebanese Pounds if he travels within the jurisdiction of his office, and an amount of thirty-five thousand Lebanese Pounds if he travels outside the jurisdiction of his office.

4- The Notary Public shall be required to place a detailed schedule of the fees due to the Treasury and the remuneration he charges for every transaction falling within his competence in a prominent place in his office where it is easy to see and read.

5- The Notary Public must record on every transaction a detailed and clear statement of the fees and remuneration collected and give a detailed receipt for the amounts collected in accordance with the provisions of Article 191 of the Public Accounting Law, provided that the procedures of collection shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance. A Notary Public who violates the provisions of any of the preceding paragraphs of this Article shall be subject to the penalties stipulated in the first paragraph of Article (15) fifteen of this Law.

In Beirut

Offices of Notaries Public:

In the administrative centers of the Governorates

Time limit for payment:

Twice a week at the rate of once every three working days.

Offices of Notaries Public:

In the administrative centers of the Districts and dependencies

A Notary Public who fails to remit the fees after a period of three working days beyond the time limits specified above shall be subject to a delay fine in the amount of

(1%) one percent for each day of delay.

The Collection Audit Department affiliated with the Directorate of the Treasury at the Ministry of Finance shall undertake the matter of supervising the collection of fees and their remittance to the Treasury, and shall submit reports in this regard to the Director of the Treasury, who shall hear the concerned Notary Public and impose, if the violation is established, the delay fine, and the Director of the Treasury must notify the Ministry of Justice thereof.

Paragraph added pursuant to Law 326 d. 28/6/2001

1- The Notary Public shall have the right to request the payment by installments of the fines due from him within a time limit of one month from the date he is notified of the collection order, provided that he includes in his request the reasons justifying the request for payment by installments.

Payment by installments shall take place with the approval of the Director General of Finance upon the proposal of the Director of the Treasury and Public Debt, provided that the Notary Public pays a rate of (25%) twenty-five percent of the fine and that the remainder of the fine is paid in three quarterly installments with interest equivalent to the interest on six-month Treasury bills on the date the installment arrangement is made.

2- The amounts arranged into installments shall become due and payable in full if the Notary Public delays in paying one of the installments on its due date, and a delay fine shall be imposed at the rate of (2%) two percent monthly calculated from the due date of the unpaid installment until the date of payment.
Notary Public fees shall be determined pursuant to Schedule (A) annexed to this Law.

Unless Schedule (A) annexed to this Law stipulates otherwise, the fees shown in this Schedule shall be levied for each signature, and signatures signed in the name of a company or a juristic person shall be deemed a single signature.

However, an agent, testamentary guardian, curator or legal guardian who acts in the interest of several persons shall be required to pay the fee for each person on whose behalf he signs.

The Notary Public is prohibited from:

1- Drawing up or authenticating instruments falling exclusively within the competence of another authority pursuant to a special legal text.

2- Drawing up or authenticating instruments falling exclusively within the competence of another authority pursuant to a special legal text.

3- Keeping more than one register for the same type of transactions at the same time.

4- Drawing up instruments pertaining to his ascendants, descendants or relatives up to the fourth degree.

5- Disclosing professional secrecy relating to transactions initiated before him or conducted with him.

6- Transferring his office and its registers except after the approval of the Ministry of Justice.

A notary public is prohibited from:

1- Resorting to a strike, under pain of the disciplinary and criminal liability relating to public servants

2- Combining the office of notary public with:

- Public offices

- All remunerated professions and occupations, and commercial, industrial and journalistic activities, with the exception of teaching outside official working hours

- Membership or chairmanship of the board of directors of a company

- Parliamentary representation and ministerial office. Where a notary public assumes any of the offices, occupations or professions set forth above, he shall be deemed by operation of law to have permanently ceased his functions as a notary public, and his post shall become vacant and shall be declared as such by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice

3- Leaving Lebanese territory, closing his office, absenting himself or refraining from receiving clients, except after obtaining written approval from the Ministry of Justice; however, in cases where it is impossible to obtain such prior written approval, such as cases of illness or the death of a relative, the notary public must notify the Ministry of Justice of the matter on the day following his absence and specify the duration of his absence.

A notary public may not issue certified true copies or deliver the contents of instruments except to the concerned parties, their heirs or their successors in title, and if he delivers to the concerned parties a first executory copy in accordance with the conditions laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, he may not thereafter issue to them anything other than duplicate copies.

A notary public whose registers have been destroyed or damaged for any reason whatsoever, or whose registers have been stolen, must immediately report the matter to the Ministry of Justice, which shall urgently delegate a person to carry out an inspection, describe the condition and draw up a detailed report thereon in the presence of the notary public; the original thereof shall be kept at the Ministry of Justice and a copy thereof shall be delivered to the notary public.

Every interested party may attach the security guarantee furnished by the notary public, such that if execution is levied thereon, the notary public must reconstitute the security guarantee required by law under pain of being barred from practising and the office of notary public.

All texts contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content are also hereby repealed.

Where necessary, the detailed rules for the application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the Minister of Finance.
This Law shall enter into force upon the expiry of thirty days following its publication in the Official Gazette.

Establishment of the Council:

1 - A Council of Notaries Public in Lebanon (hereinafter referred to as "the Council") is hereby established, which shall be of a professional nature and shall enjoy legal personality.

2 - The Council shall be composed of two bodies: the General Assembly and the Bureau of the Council (hereinafter referred to as "the Bureau").

3 - All tenured notaries public in the Lebanese Republic shall be deemed affiliated to "the Council" by operation of law.

4 - Retired notaries public who so wish may also affiliate to the Council.

The application for affiliation of retired notaries public shall be submitted to the Bureau.

Functions of the Council:

The functions of "the Council" shall be defined as follows:

1 - Working to safeguard the affairs of notaries public, develop the profession and elevate its standing.

2 - Cooperating with international organisations that have a similar activity.

Its powers and functions:

A - The General Assembly shall be composed of all tenured notaries public and of the affiliated retired notaries public.

B - Subject to what is stated below with respect to the first meeting held by the General Assembly after the enactment of the present Law, the General Assembly shall hold its ordinary meeting on the first Sunday of the month of November of each year. Where a quorum is not reached, it shall be adjourned by operation of law to the third Sunday of the same month.

C - The General Assembly shall also hold an extraordinary meeting whenever "the Bureau" deems it necessary or where a request therefor is submitted to it by one quarter of the number of tenured notaries public entitled to participate in such meeting.

D - A meeting of the General Assembly, at the first sitting, shall be deemed valid if attended by more than half the number of notaries public entitled to participate in the General Assembly. If such quorum is not met, a second sitting shall be held two weeks later and shall be deemed valid regardless of the number of those present.

E - The General Assembly shall be chaired by the President of "the Bureau" and, in his absence, by the Vice-President, and then by the oldest among the members of "the Bureau" present.

F - Decisions shall be taken by a relative majority.

G - The business of the annual ordinary General Assembly shall cover:

1 - Electing the members of "the Bureau".

2 - Determining the annual subscription fee payable by tenured notaries public

in favour of "the Council", provided that the subscription fee payable by affiliated retired notaries public shall be equal thereto.

3 - Approving the accounts of the preceding financial year and adopting the budget of the following financial year.

The financial year shall begin on the first of January and end on the thirty-first of December.

As for the first financial year, it shall begin on the date of election of the first "Bureau" and end on the thirty-first of December following.

4 - Matters which the Bureau decides to submit to the General Assembly.

Decisions relating to the preceding items 1, 2 and 3 shall be taken by an absolute majority of the number of notaries public participating in the General Assembly.

H - Adopting the internal regulations of "the Council" prepared by the Bureau, provided that such regulations shall not become effectiveuntil after the approval thereof by the Minister of Justice.

I - The internal regulations shall determine the manner of operation of "the Council" and "the Bureau", including the powers of each of the President, the Vice-President, the Secretary and the Treasurer, and the rules for conducting elections as well as the procedural rules. They shall designate the location of the permanent seat of the Council.

J - The legal quorum required for convening the General Assembly relating to the adoption or amendment of the internal regulations shall be at least two thirds of the number of notaries public entitled to participate in this General Assembly at the first sitting.

Where a quorum is not reached, the legal quorum for convening the second sitting shall be the absolute majority of the number of notaries public entitled to participate in this sitting.

Decisions with respect to the adoption and amendment of the internal regulations shall be taken by a majority of two thirds of the notaries public present.

The General Assembly must convene to adopt the internal regulations within a period of six months from the date of election of the first "Bureau".

K - After the annual subscription fee is determined, a notary public shall not be entitled to participate in the General Assembly unless he has paid his subscription fee prior to the sixteenth of the month of October of each year.

Elections of the Bureau:

1 - The "Council" shall be managed by a bureau composed of eight members elected by the General Assembly from among the incumbent Notaries Public (hereinafter referred to in this Law as the "Bureau").

2 - The General Assembly shall also elect two persons, from among the retired Notaries Public affiliated with the Council, who shall join the "Bureau". They shall have the right to debate without the right to vote, and shall not be counted towards the quorum of the "Bureau".

For the purposes of the first electoral process referred to hereinafter, the incumbent Notaries Public shall be deemed affiliated with the Council, and the retired Notaries Public who have submitted an application for affiliation to the Ministry of Justice at least one week prior to the date set for convening the first meeting of the General Assembly which shall be called to elect the first Bureau shall also be deemed affiliated therewith.

3 - The term of office of the members of the "Bureau" shall be three years, renewable once. Running for re-election shall not be permissible save after the expiry of a full term.

4 - The process of electing the members of the first "Bureau" shall take place on a Sunday within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, by virtue of a call addressed by the Minister of Justice and published in two local newspapers and in the Official Gazette, which shall include setting the date of the first and second sessions for the election as stated below.

5 - The first electoral process shall take place in the courtyard of the Palace of Justice in Beirut.

6 - The quorum required in the first session for the election is the absolute majority of the incumbent Notaries Public in Lebanon. If the quorum is not met, a second session for the election shall be held two weeks after the date of the first session, and the quorum shall be legal with those in attendance.

7 - The first electoral session shall be held under the chairmanship of the oldest of those present, and two of the youngest Notaries Public from among those present shall perform the duties of Secretary and Vote Teller, and all of these shall certify the minutes of the election session.

8 - In the event that the first electoral session is not convened within the period of six months mentioned above for any reason whatsoever, the session shall be deemed convened by operation of law in the courtyard of the Palace of Justice in Beirut on the first Sunday following the expiry of this period, and shall remain in session until the election of the members of the first "Bureau" of the "Council".

9 - The election of the members of the "Bureau" by the General Assembly shall take place by secret ballot, and the candidate who obtains the largest number of votes shall win, and if the votes are equal, the one most senior in the profession shall win membership of the "Bureau", and in the event of equality, the oldest.

10 - It is always required that a member of the "Bureau", on the date of his election, has been a Notary Public for at least seven years, including the traineeship period.

11 - The oldest member of the "Bureau" shall call the remaining members to a session to be held within a period of three days from the date of their election, in order to elect each of the President, the Vice-President, the Secretary, and the Treasurer by secret ballot and in succession. The incumbent Notary Public who obtains the largest number of votes shall win the post, and in the event of an equality of votes, the one most senior in the profession shall win the post, and in the event of equality, the oldest.

12 - In the event that the session is not convened within the period of three days mentioned above for any reason whatsoever, the "Bureau" shall be deemed in session by operation of law as of the fourth day until the elections referred to above are conducted.

13 - The year shall be defined as the period extending between the date set for the convening of the General Assembly in a given year and the date set for its convening in the following year. As for the first year, it shall extend from the date of the convening of the first General Assembly until the date set for the convening of the General Assembly in the following year.

14 - The members of the "Bureau" shall not receive any fees or allowances in return for their membership and their performance of the duties entrusted to them.

Meetings of the "Bureau"

1 - The "Bureau" shall hold periodic meetings and whenever the need arises, at the headquarters of the "Council", upon a call by its President or by three of its members in the event that the President fails to address the call.

2 - The President shall chair the sessions, or his Vice-President in the event of his absence, or the oldest of the members in the event of the absence of the President and the Vice-President.

3 - The sessions of the "Bureau" shall not be legal save in the presence of the absolute majority of its members from among the incumbent Notaries Public.

4 - The decisions of the Bureau shall be issued by a majority, and if the votes are equal, the President's vote shall be deemed a casting vote.

5 - If one or more seats of the members of the Bureau become vacant, the Bureau shall continue its work composed of the remaining members until the convening of the first General Assembly during which those who shall fill the vacant seat or seats are elected. The successor shall replace his predecessor for the remainder of the term of his membership.

6 - However, in the event that the "Bureau" loses half of its members from among the incumbent Notaries Public or more for any reason whatsoever, the Bureau in the entirety of its members shall be deemed resigned and as having had its term of office expired. In this case, and notwithstanding the expiry of its term of office, the "Bureau" must, within a period of two weeks, call the General Assembly to convene within a period of two months at most from the date of the call to elect a new Bureau. If the "Bureau" abstains from addressing the call, the Minister of Justice shall address the call within a period of ten days following the expiry of the period of two weeks referred to above.

7 - The "Bureau" shall continue to conduct caretaker business until a new "Bureau" is elected.

8 - In the event of the temporary absence of the President of the "Bureau", the Vice-President shall replace him during the period of his absence. In the event of the permanent vacancy of the seat of the President of the "Bureau", the Vice-President shall replace him for the remaining period of his term of office.

9 - In the event that the Vice-President assumes the post of President permanently, the "Bureau" shall elect a Vice-President within a period of fifteen days from the assumption by the Vice-President of the presidency of the Council.

10 - Every member of the "Bureau" who absents himself from its meetings three consecutive times without an acceptable excuse shall be deemed resigned by operation of law.

Powers and duties of the "Bureau":

The Bureau shall work to attend to the affairs of notaries public, oversee the proper performance of their duties, and undertake that which enhances the role of their profession, in particular:

- Expressing an opinion on all matters relating to the affairs of the profession, including draft laws, proposed laws, and decrees.

- Establishing a code of ethics for the profession of notary public and the conduct of notaries public, to be approved by the Minister of Justice.

- Endeavouring to resolve professional disagreements and disputes among notaries public amicably.

- Representing the "Council" vis-à-vis public authorities and third parties and before the courts.

- Accepting donations, bequests, and grants following the approval thereof by the Minister of Justice.

- Expressing an opinion, within a time limit not exceeding ten days, on complaints and judicial prosecutions against notaries public arising from the exercise of their duties which the Minister of Justice may refer to it.

- Submitting proposals on all matters relating to the affairs of the profession and the proper performance of notaries public.

- Expressing an opinion regarding the establishment of new notary public offices or the abolition or transfer of existing offices.

- Organising training courses for tenured and trainee notaries public and seeking the assistance, for this purpose, of retired notaries public when necessary.

- Holding seminars and conferences with the aim of enhancing the profession and improving the performance of notaries public.

- Maintaining permanent coordination with the various bodies of the State in all matters relating to the affairs of the profession, and providing advice upon request.

- Coordinating with unions of notaries public in the various countries of the world, exchanging expertise, participating in national and international conferences and meetings, and strengthening the international relations of Lebanon in this field.

- Preparing and executing the annual budget.

- Convening the General Assemblies and executing their resolutions.

- The possibility of contracting with an insurance company to establish a collective insurance policy covering the professional civil liability of notaries public.

Revenues of the Council:

The revenues of the Council of Notaries Public shall consist of:

1 - Subscription fees of notaries public.

2 - Donations, bequests, and grants which the "Council" decides to accept in accordance with what is set forth above.

The successful bidder or lessee by mutual agreement may have a personal agent who must be approved in advance in writing by the forestry officer to whom his exploitation reports, and must furthermore take the oath before the magistrate of the locality. If the coupe or coupes which this agent is charged with supervising are situated within the boundaries of several magistrate courts, the taking of the oath that took place before one of the judges shall be registered in the registry of each of these magistrate courts. This agent may draw up seizure reports and carry out all inspections of misdemeanours within the boundaries of the coupe and outside it in a zone extending to a distance of one hundred metres therefrom. These seizure reports shall be subject to the same formalities to which the seizure reports drawn up by the officers of the Forestry Department are subject and shall be deemed authentic until proof to the contrary of their contents is established.

No produce whatsoever of forestry produce may be removed from any of the worksites or depots legally approved by the Administration to be transported outside the boundaries of one of the coupes without being accompanied by a carrying or transport permit issued by the officer of the Forestry Department authorised therefor, and this permit must be produced upon every demand by the officers of the public force or the forestry officers, and the latter must affix their endorsement thereon with mention of the kind of quantity of the produce the transport of which they have inspected.

The removal of forestry produce of whatever kind and origin outside the boundaries of woods and forests is prohibited between sunset and sunrise, provided that the officers of the Forestry Department may grant night transport permits solely to legal exploiters the location of whose coupe is very far from the ordinary places of sale and from the places of deposit so that they may be able to transport it during a single day.

Produce of any kind whatsoever originating from the forests, if transported without a permit, shall be seized and placed under guard, as well as the wrappings in which it was contained and, where necessary, the vehicles, draught animals and pack animals used for its transport. This seizure and, where necessary, the sale of the produce shall be carried out in accordance with the procedures prescribed in Articles 128, 129, 130 and 131 of this Decision.

The storage of forestry produce and trading therein shall be subject to obtaining a prior licence. The conditions of "granting this licence as well as the manner of supervision by the Forestry Administration shall be regulated by local decisions or decrees, and if a contravention occurs in this regard, the provisions of Articles 128, 129, 130 and 131 referred to in the preceding Article shall apply.

Traders in forestry produce may not oppose the supervisory officers of the Forest Department, the administrative authorities and all judicial police officers in visiting and inspecting their stores and depots.

An inspection of every coupe shall be carried out during the three months following the day of expiry of the periods prescribed for clearing the coupes. After the expiry of these three months, the successful bidder or lessee by mutual agreement shall not be liable for the obligations of the exploitation if the Administration has not carried out the inspection within this period, provided that whoever has completed the exploitation and cleared the coupe before the prescribed periods may notify the Administration to carry out the inspection by a registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt sent to the Forestry Administration, and thereby becomes non-liable if this operation is not carried out within a period of three months starting from the date of the acknowledgment of receipt of the registered letter.

The successful bidder or lessee by mutual agreement must attend the inspection and shall be notified thereof by a registered letter at least 15 days before the date fixed for this operation, and if he does not attend at the coupe or does not appoint someone to represent him, the inspection report shall be deemed adversarial.

During the period of thirty days following the closure of the report, the Administration or the successful bidder or the lessee by mutual agreement may apply for the annulment of the report before the courts for a defect in form or for erroneous information therein, and if the report is annulled, the Administration may within a period of thirty days starting from the date of the annulment order the drawing up of a new report in place of the annulled report, and if the time limits prescribed in the preceding Article expire and the Administration has not raised the slightest objection, the successful bidder shall become released from the obligations of the exploitation.

The recognition of usufructuary rights over State woods and forests shall take place concurrently with the operations of placing the boundaries of these forests and delimiting them as prescribed in Articles 13, 14 and 15 of this Decision through the diligence of the Delimitation Commission. An officer of the Forestry Department shall represent the Administration in these operations. The substance of these rights shall be determined in a local decision or decree in accordance with the decisions of the Commission. No usufructuary right whatsoever may be created over the forests or woods subject to delimitation after the promulgation of the decree or decision provided for in the preceding paragraph.

In application of the preceding Article, usufructuary rights over State woods and forests may only be recognised solely in favour of communities, the villages neighbouring the woods and forests or contiguous to these villages neighbouring them.

Usufructuary rights which may be recognised in accordance with the preceding Article shall only apply to the following things: 1) collecting dry firewood and minor produce b) supplying the firewood necessary for the need of every house of the houses of the village c) supplying timber intended for making agricultural implements or for constructing or repairing dwellings d) exercising the right of pasture of flocks unless there is a prohibition issued by the local governments in the interest of afforestation, and in any case these rights shall only be exercised if they do not prejudice the possible exploitations determined in advance and at fixed periods by the Forestry Administration, and in particular, whatever the age or kind of the woods, the holders of the right of pasture may only exercise this right of theirs in the places which the Forestry Administration has declared to be defensible. No land may be declared to be defensible before the expiry of a period of ten full years starting from the day on which felling or fire, even partially, occurred therein, unless this felling was carried out by the Administration to thin the density of the trees.

Official instruments shall be drawn up in respect of usufructuary rights, the extent of which may be proved by the means provided for in Articles 37 and 38 of Decision No. 186 issued on 15 March 1936.
Notwithstanding the preceding provisions, the local governments may designate the kind of forestry produce which may be ceded free of charge.

The determination of the usufructuary rights running over certain State woods and forests in their capacity as wooded lands left for public use or assigned for common use (baltalik), as well as the final official recognition of these rights, shall take place within the conditions and in accordance with the procedures prescribed in the preceding Articles 48 and 49.

Provided that if a dispute arises over the basis of rights of this kind or their substance, the community concerned may refer the dispute for review to the State Council or the judicial body acting in its stead, and these two bodies shall rule finally on the dispute. Recourse to this review may not be had after the expiry of a period of one year starting from the date of the impugned administrative act.

If the usufruct running over the wooded lands left for public use or assigned for common use (baltalik) is an object of trade in favour of the community concerned, this community may be subjected to the payment of a fee to the Treasury the amount of which shall be fixed in a local decree or decision.

The designation of the place over which the usufructuary rights recognised in favour of the communities are exercised, as well as the designation of the conditions for the exercise of these rights, shall be effected through the diligence of the Forestry Administration within the limits of what the forest can bear and the limits of the plan established for its exploitation. This operation shall be carried out as a whole for each place or parcel of a forest of which a given exploitation unit is composed, and an overall allocation shall be decided therein for the community benefiting from the usufructuary right, and this allocation shall then be distributed among its members.
The distribution of rights among the members of the communities concerned shall take place in accordance with custom.

With the exception of the gathering of dry firewood lying on the ground or accessible by hand and gathered without the use of a sickle, saw, axe or other tools, and the gathering of acorns that have fallen naturally, the right of usufruct shall be subject to the granting of a special permit by the Forestry Administration.

Local decrees or decisions shall determine the conditions for the exercise of rights of usufruct recognised in favour of communities, as well as the penalties applicable to contraventions in this regard.

Areas of the forests of the State domain over which rights of usufruct are exercised may be the subject of consolidation or restriction operations. Rights of usufruct may also be bought out, in which case their value shall be paid either in kind or in cash, and their price shall be determined by the Forestry Administration, without prejudice to the right, in the event of a dispute, to apply to the judicial authority designated in the provisions of Article 54.

All the provisions of this Decision relating to the conservation and administration of woods forming part of the State domain shall apply to the undivided or disputed woods mentioned in Article 1 of Title I. The conditions for the administration and exploitation of these forests shall be determined by local decrees or decisions.

Woods and forests which villages own in full ownership in a private capacity shall be administered by the municipalities concerned and, where there are no municipalities, by the village committees under the supervision of the Forestry Administration, in implementation of the special regulations provided for in Title I, Chapter I of this Decision. The ownership of these woods may not be subjected to any partition whatsoever among the inhabitants of the village itself.
The organisation of the villages mentioned in the preceding Article 62, their functioning and their detailed powers shall be determined by local decrees or decisions.

Villages may appoint private guards and provide them at their own expense with what they require to ensure the conservation and exploitation of their woods and forests. The number of these guards and their appointment shall be made by the president of the municipality, provided that this is approved in advance by the Forestry Administration.
The Forestry Administration may suspend these guards from their duties or dismiss them.

The private guards of village woods shall be treated as guards of State forests in all matters relating to the investigation, ascertainment and suppression of forestry misdemeanours; they shall take the oath in the same form, and the official reports drawn up by them shall be authoritative under the same conditions, whether they relate to misdemeanours committed in the woods entrusted to the custody of the village guards or to misdemeanours committed in all other public or private woods.

Village woods and forests may only be maintained in accordance with the special regulations establishing a plan for their exploitation, and a prior special authorisation from the Forestry Administration must be given in each separate matter, whether such matter relates to primary produce, secondary produce or the exercise of the right of pasture. The sale or exploitation shall be carried out through the diligence of the municipal council or the village committee after the file relating thereto has been approved by the Forestry Administration under the conditions determined by local decrees or decisions. The provisions on incapacity and prohibitions laid down in Article 24 shall apply to presidents of municipalities or village committees and to mukhtars.

Any sale, exploitation or grazing carried out unlawfully by order or with the participation of a representative of the municipal council in contravention of the preceding Article 67 shall be punishable by compelling that representative to pay a fine of 25 to 250 Lebanese-Syrian pounds, without prejudice to a claim for damages against him by the injured community; furthermore, a sale carried out in this manner shall in all cases be deemed null and void.

Villages may not clear (Defricher) the woods and forests belonging to them without a special authorisation from the Head of State granted by decree or decision following a prior inquiry by the Forestry Department and after the approval of the Director of Agriculture. Any unlawful exploitation, or uprooting of tree stumps, or permanent grazing of new growth in a recently felled plot carried out in contravention of the special regulations relating to the exploitation plan and capable of leading to the disappearance of the wood shall be deemed to be land clearing and shall be punishable by the same penalties.

Those who knowingly and under their responsibility order or permit the clearing of land, or carry it out in a village wood without a permit, or order, permit or carry out an abusive exploitation that may be deemed to be unauthorised clearing, shall be punishable by the penalties set out in Article 81 of this Decision relating to misdemeanours of the same kind committed in private woods and forests; if these operations are carried out by order or with the participation of a representative of the municipal council, the maximum penalty shall always be applied to that representative.

Markings carried out by officers of the State Forestry Department on behalf of villages, as well as the execution of all preparatory or subsequent formalities relating thereto and all operations of supervision or administration of village woods by those officers, shall all be free of charge.

One third of the net proceeds from the sale of the produce of village forests and the leasing of village pastures shall be compulsorily retained in the reserve funds through the diligence of the president of the municipality or the president of the village committee, who shall be personally responsible for the execution of this measure. This third shall be used under the supervision of the Forestry Administration for afforestation works carried out on the lands of the village itself under the conditions laid down in Article 93 of this Decision.

Any distribution that may take place among the inhabitants of the village of certain produce in kind, in particular for burning in homes, from the woods and forests of the village after they have been lawfully exploited under the supervision of the village administration shall be carried out in accordance with custom and usage, unless there is an instrument to the contrary, and such distribution shall be performed by the municipal council or the village committee. The municipal council or the village committee may decide not to distribute the produce among the inhabitants, but to sell it for the benefit of the community.

Where the woods and forests of a village are encumbered with rights of usufruct distinct from the right of exploitation belonging to the community that holds the bare ownership, the recognition, delimitation and exercise of those rights shall be subject to the provisions of Title II, Chapter IV of this Decision relating to the rights of usufruct belonging to neighbouring inhabitants over State woods and forests.
Private individuals shall exercise over their woods all the rights arising from ownership, subject to compliance with the restrictions set out in the following articles.

No private individual whomsoever shall have the right to uproot or clear his woods except after submitting a written declaration to that effect to the Forestry Department at least three months in advance, and during this period, which shall run from the day on which the Administration receives this declaration, the said Administration shall be entitled to notify him of its provisional opposition to the clearing. The declaration must state an elected domicile in the administrative district in which the woods are situated. An officer of the Forestry Department shall inspect the condition and location of the woods and draw up a detailed official report thereon. After examining this report, the Forestry Administration shall, where appropriate, notify the declarant of its provisional opposition to the clearing, in which case it shall serve the official report on the interested party, who may submit his observations on the decision of opposition; the report, accompanied where appropriate by the observations of the interested party, shall then be forwarded to the Head of State, who shall maintain or lift the opposition.

Objection to clearing may only be made in respect of woods the preservation of which is deemed obligatory 1- for the conservation of soil on mountains or on slopes 2- for the protection of the land against erosion by large and small rivers and torrents and their encroachment upon it 3- for the conservation of springs or watercourses 4- for the protection of dunes on the seashores and inland dunes against the invasion of sands 5- for public health 6- for the preservation of a natural landscape pertaining to a designated summer resort centre, and in this latter case the objection to clearing or the partial expropriation shall give rise to a right for the owner of the wood to compensation, and if the objection is final, the owner of the property shall have the right to demand expropriation

Only a declaration shall be required to be submitted where the matter relates to the clearing of land: 1- in young woods during the first twenty years after their sowing or planting, unless their density is sufficient to form a wood covering the land, except where they were established in replacement of cleared woods 2- in walled parks and gardens or those adjoining dwellings

Unlawful exploitations in sloping lands and grazing after exploitation, felling or fire which lead to the destruction of part of the forest or to its destruction in its entirety, or which constitute a danger to the retention of soil on slopes or to the protection of the land against erosion, shall be deemed to be a clearing of the land, and those who ordered their execution, permitted them or carried them out without right shall be punished by the penalties provided for in the following Article 81

Communities or public establishments may not carry out any clearing of land whatsoever in their woods and forests, whatever their location may be, without an express authorisation from the Head of State. Those who ordered the carrying out of such clearing or who knowingly permitted it shall be punished by the maximum penalties provided for in Article 81 imposed upon individuals for contraventions of the same kind
