In the event of a disagreement between the Minister and the Minister of Finance, the Board of Directors may request the Minister to submit the disagreement to the Council of Ministers, whose decision shall take the place of the opinion of the two Ministers.
The Institution may contract with the Housing Bank or with other banks in order to deposit its funds and collect instalments.

Notwithstanding any contrary text, the Institution, the Housing Bank, and the administrations and institutions that undertake the execution of housing projects or housing lending must exchange lists of the names of beneficiaries, every six months, in order to prevent a beneficiary from obtaining more than one loan or dwelling.

The Board may delegate some of its powers to its Chairman, and the Chairman, in his capacity as Director General, may delegate some of his powers to one or more of the staff members directly subordinate to him who hold their posts in a permanent capacity.

By a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Housing and Cooperatives and of Public Works and following the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, housing complexes that were established in accordance with the provisions of previous housing and reconstruction laws and regulations may be exempted from certain regulations relating to subdivision in order to facilitate the housing of beneficiaries.

1- The Government shall be granted exceptional authority for a period of one year starting from the date of entry into force of this Law, to issue a special pardon having the effects of a general amnesty pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, in respect of any person convicted of or prosecuted for the offences excluded from the amnesty, committed against the internal or external security of the State and perpetrated prior to the date of 28 March 1991. That shall be within the following rules: a- Personal damages, civil obligations and precautionary measures shall be excluded from the pardon. b - The pardon decree may stipulate the condition that the beneficiary of the pardon leave the country and specify the duration of his stay outside it, in respect of offences in which no judgment has been rendered until now. The beneficiary of the pardon shall leave the country within a time limit of forty-eight hours from the date of issuance of the pardon decree, and the provisions of Article 47 of the Penal Code shall apply to him. 2- Any person who, after the issuance of the pardon decree, proceeds to do the following shall forfeit the grant of pardon: a-Violating the condition of leaving the country and staying outside it. b - Undertaking throughout the period specified for staying abroad: - Any political activity inside or outside the country, whatever the nature, means and purposes of this activity may be. - Any act likely to prejudice order or the security of the State. - Any act likely to undermine national unity or the fundamental interests of the country, or aimed at inciting sedition or disturbing harmony among the elements of the nation. 3- If the offences covered by the pardon decree have been referred to the Judicial Council, the referral decree shall remain in force and the proceedings in the action shall continue with respect to personal damages, civil obligations and precautionary measures. Prosecution with respect to the public right action shall also be resumed upon the forfeiture of the grant of pardon without any need for the issuance of a new decree of referral to the Judicial Council.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.
A general amnesty is granted for offences committed prior to the date of 28 March 1991, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

A full amnesty is granted for the following offences: 1- Contraventions 2- Misdemeanours, except those wholly or partially excluded pursuant to this Law. 3- The following offences: a- Offences against the internal security of the State, except those excluded pursuant to this Law. b - The offences provided for in the Law of 11 January 1958, amending certain articles of the Penal Code. c- Political offences or those bearing a general or local political character, including offences of homicide for political motives, provided that they were not committed for a personal purpose or benefit, it being for the competent judicial authority seized of the action to rule on the matter, and the decision shall be deemed to be by way of ruling on formal defences and shall be subject to the avenues of recourse provided for in the Code of Criminal Procedure. d- The offences provided for in Articles 107 to 171 of the Military Penal Code No. 24/68, as amended pursuant to the draft law put into force by Decree No. 1460/71, and by Legislative Decree No. 110/77, provided that the serviceman has reported to or requested to report to his duty station, or requested his discharge, or his service has ended for any reason whatsoever in accordance with the rules prior to the date of entry into force of this Law, with the exception of the offences of capitulation, treason, and espionage on behalf of the enemy. e- The offences provided for in Articles 72, 73, 75, 76, 77, and 78 of the Weapons and Ammunition Law, provided that the perpetrator of the offence surrenders his weapon and ammunition within one month from the date of entry into force of this Law. f- The offences provided for in items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 7 of Article 569 of the Penal Code. g- Offences perpetrated in consummation of the offences mentioned in this Article or in fulfilment of their purposes, or which accompanied them or resulted therefrom. The grant of amnesty shall lapse in respect of the perpetrators of the offences mentioned in this Article if they are of the nature of continuing or successive offences, and their perpetrators continued to commit them or resumed committing the like thereof after the date of enforcement of this Law, and prosecution shall thereupon resume from the point at which it ceased by effect of the amnesty.

The following are excluded from the provisions of this Law: 1- Offences against the external security of the State provided for in Articles 273 to 300 of the Penal Code. 2- Offences referred to the Judicial Council prior to the date of entry into force of this Law. 3- Offences of assassination or attempted assassination of clerics, religious scholars, political leaders, and Arab and foreign diplomats. 4- Offences of fraudulent bankruptcy and the offences provided for in the Code of Money and Credit and all other laws and regulations relating to banks. 5- Offences of counterfeiting and falsifying national and foreign currency or circulating the same and undermining the financial standing of the State, and forging passports and documents and registers of personal status and official departments 6- Offences relating to antiquities. 7- Offences of selling real property to foreigners without a licence. 8- Offences of encroachment upon public or private funds and properties belonging to the State or municipalities, and upon the funds and properties of public institutions, and upon communal lands, and upon the real properties of individuals, including the offence provided for in Article 738 of the Penal Code (as amended), provided that the amnesty shall cover the penalty of imprisonment only in respect of this latter Article. 9- The offences provided for in the laws on customs and the tobacco and tumbak monopoly and in the financial laws, and offences relating to the manufacture of and trafficking in narcotics. 10- The offences provided for in the building laws, provided that the amnesty shall cover the penalty of imprisonment only.

Penalties for all other offences not provided for by this Law shall be reduced as follows: 1- The death penalty shall be commuted to life hard labour. 2- Life hard labour shall be commuted to temporary hard labour for a term of ten years. 3- Other felony penalties shall be reduced by up to one half. 4- The penalty in the following misdemeanours shall be reduced by up to one quarter, namely: theft - fraud - forgery and knowing use of a forged instrument embezzlement - breach of trust - trading in influence - bribery - illicit enrichment - cheque without funds, and the offences provided for in Articles 138, 141, and 143 of the Military Penal Code.

Notwithstanding any contrary provision, the court may apply the rules of discretionary mitigating circumstances to the offences covered by this Law, committed prior to the date of 28 March 1991, and if the minimum penalty is three years, the court may sentence, by a reasoned decision, to imprisonment for one year at least.

There is excluded from the provisions on the suspension of time limits provided for in Legislative Decrees No. 12/83, No. 66/83, and No. 18/85, and Law No. 50 dated 23/5/91, the suspension of the limitation period for felonies committed prior to the date of entry into force of this Law. The provisions on suspension shall remain in force in respect of the civil right arising from the felony in accordance with the provisions on suspension applicable to civil rights and in force in the aforementioned Legislative Decrees and in Law No. 50/91.

Jurisdiction to hear civil claims arising from an offence covered by the full amnesty or limitation shall remain vested in the criminal courts if the public prosecution was brought directly before the criminal authorities or referred to them prior to the enforcement of this Law. As for other civil actions arising from a criminal offence covered by the full amnesty or limitation, they shall be adjudicated by the competent civil or administrative courts, and the laws on fees in force for civil actions before the criminal courts shall apply thereto. Upon execution of the judgment for compensation rendered by the criminal or ordinary courts, the claimant shall be entitled to request the imprisonment for debt of the convicted person, pursuant to Article 446 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Article 997 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and Article 146 of the Penal Code.

Notwithstanding any other provision, all offences of assassination or attempted assassination of clerics, religious scholars, political leaders, committed on or before the date of 28 March 1991, shall be deemed as of the date of their commission to be referred by operation of law to the Judicial Council.

A transfer duty shall be imposed on all movable and immovable rights and property that devolve upon third parties, with the exception of the State and municipalities, by way of inheritance, will, gift, waqf, or by any other means without consideration equivalent to their true value, and estates relating to events that occurred before the date of 13/10/1994 shall be exempted from the transfer duties, and the competent judicial authorities shall be permitted to issue judgments of determination of heirs and execute wills for the concerned parties without their producing the licence required from the competent departments at the Ministry of Finance in respect of deaths that occurred before the date of 13/10/1994

Explanatory notice for this Article: Exemption of estates occurring before 13/10/1994 from transfer duties

The duty shall fall due on the date of death or of the judgment declaring the death of the absent person, or the taking effect of the gift or waqf, or the termination of the waqf. The factor of prescription shall not run except from the date on which the competent financial departments are notified of the final judgments relating to the determination of heirs or to the execution of the will, gift, or waqf, or to the termination of the waqf.

The duty shall cover:

A - All movable and immovable property located in Lebanon and transferred from a Lebanese or a foreigner, whatever his place of residence.

B - All movable and immovable property located abroad and transferred from a Lebanese resident in Lebanon.

C - All movable and immovable property located abroad and transferred from a foreigner resident in Lebanon.

Double duty on the property mentioned in paragraph (C) of this Article may be avoided by international agreements.

Movable and immovable property which the decedent gives by way of gift or disposes of during the two years preceding his death, whether directly or through a nominee, to a person who became his heir by a cause existing at the time the gift or disposition took place, shall be deemed, for the purpose of assessing the duty, as if it had been transferred with the remaining elements of the estate on the day of death, provided that the registration or transfer duty that may have been paid on the said property shall be deducted from the duty due on the estate; and if the disposition took place for consideration paid by the concerned party out of his own funds, he shall be entitled to file an objection before the judiciary and prove the payment of such consideration, whereupon the amount unduly collected shall be refunded to him.

Financial instruments found in the possession of one of the heirs which, up to one year prior to the death of the decedent, were deposited in his name at a bank, a company, or elsewhere, or the income of which was collected by the decedent or collected for his account, shall be deemed, with respect to the collection of the duty, to be part of the estate, unless the person in possession of these instruments proves that they were legally transferred to him for a consideration equivalent to their true value.

All sums and financial instruments deposited at a bank or institution or with individuals for a joint account or for the account of a group of joint and several persons shall be deemed, with respect to the collection of the duty, to be the property of the depositors in equal shares and shall be included in the estate of each of them in this manner, unless the contrary is proved.

All sums, financial instruments, and other items deposited in a safe deposit box jointly rented by several persons shall be deemed, with respect to the collection of the duty, to be the property of the depositors in equal shares, unless the contrary is proved, and sealed envelopes and closed boxes deposited with a bank, money-changers, or others who customarily accept deposits of such items shall also be deemed to be the property of the depositors in equal shares, unless the contrary is proved.
The duty shall be chargeable on the share of each heir, and if the share is encumbered with charges, then on its net value after deducting the value of the charges

The following shall be exempted from the transfer duty:

1- Retirement pensions, refunds of pension deductions, dismissal indemnities, and any other indemnities or allowances granted on the occasion of dismissal.

2- Financial instruments exempted from the said duty pursuant to legal provisions

3- Portraits and statues of the deceased and members of his family

4- Collections of antiquarian books, medals, and other collections and furniture located in the dwelling house of the decedent, up to a maximum limit of forty million pounds; scientific and literary books, however, shall be exempted in full from the duty.

5- There shall be exempted from the duty the portion of the net hereditary share that does not exceed:

a - For each of the descendants, spouses, and parents: six hundred million pounds.

b - For each of the ascendants other than the parents, and a brother and sister: two hundred and forty million pounds.

c - For each of the remaining heirs: one hundred and twenty million pounds.

There shall be added to the value of the exempted portion of the children's hereditary share:

- Three hundred and sixty million pounds when the child suffers from a permanent disability that prevents him from working.

- Twenty-four million pounds for each year or fraction of a year separating the minor child from the eighteenth year of his age.

- Two hundred and forty million pounds when the heir has a dependent husband or wife, and one hundred and twenty million pounds for each child who has not exceeded the age of eighteen, provided that the total of these additions does not exceed the limit of six hundred million pounds.

To benefit from the additions enumerated in this paragraph, it is required that the cause that gave rise to the right thereto be existing on the date of the decedent's death.

6 - Estates of martyrs of the Lebanese Army and the other armed security forces who fell as martyrs, if they have not been paid on the date of entry into force of this Law”.

The obligation to file a declaration shall remain incumbent upon the heirs before the competent financial units in order to grant them the required licence to obtain the judgment of inheritance and to grant them the transfer certificates in accordance with the rules.

Transfer duties paid on these estates shall be deemed a right of the Treasury and may not be refunded.

7- Heirs of Lebanese who perished as a result of the Beirut Port explosion on 4/8/2020, on all movable and immovable rights and property relating to the estates of their decedents, provided that they submit, up to 31/12/2020, the declarations and supporting documents to the competent financial units to grant them the required licence to obtain the judgment of determination of heirs and to grant them the transfer certificates in accordance with the rules.

The following shall be excluded permanently or temporarily from the estate:

1- Debts owed to the decedent by bankrupt persons.

2- Bad debts or uncollectible debts.

3- Disputed rights and the right of recourse against third parties.

In these cases, every heir must claim before the judiciary, within a period of six months, the rights and debts designated to him by the financial departments. If the appointed time limit expires and the heir has not instituted the necessary lawsuits or has shown negligence in pursuing them, the said rights and debts shall be included in the valuation of his hereditary share.

The factor of prescription shall not run, with respect to the duty, on the debts and rights temporarily excluded from the estate and which may be collected subsequently, except from the date on which the financial departments officially take cognizance of the fact of collection.

All debts and liabilities encumbering the estate shall be excluded therefrom if they are established by documents that can be invoked against the deceased before the judiciary, and funeral expenses shall be deemed liabilities of the estate.

The heirs must submit the documents relating to the said debts and liabilities within the period fixed for them by the competent financial departments, under penalty of rejection.

Funeral expenses may be accepted when it is impossible to prove them by documents, provided that their total does not exceed one per cent of the gross value of the estate.

The financial departments shall be entitled to inspect the documents that prove the liabilities and obligations owed by the estate. They may disregard, provisionally or finally, any debt owed by the estate that appears to them to be fictitious or insufficiently established, and in particular:

1- Every instrument or acknowledgment of debt issued by the decedent during the year preceding his death for the benefit of a person who became an heir to him for a cause existing at the time of the acknowledgment of debt, whether such acknowledgment took place directly or through an intermediary.

2- Every debt acknowledged by the decedent in his will for which the creditor has not proved a lawful cause; and the heirs shall be entitled, in all these cases, to sue the administration to recover the duties unlawfully collected from them.

The financial departments shall disregard the following debts:

1- Debts and obligations barred by prescription, even if the heirs do not invoke it.

2- Debts incurred abroad until a judgment in respect thereof is rendered by the Lebanese judiciary or a judicial judgment in respect thereof is rendered abroad and acquires exequatur in Lebanon, with the exception of commercial debts that are sufficiently established.

3 - The text of paragraph 3 was repealed pursuant to Article 2 of Law 374 dated 14/8/1994

The duty shall be payable on the value of the gift, and where the gift is encumbered with charges, on its net value after deducting the value of the charges.

For the purpose of assessing the duty, all gifts accruing to a single person from a single donor within two years shall be deemed a single gift.

The Transfer Duty Department alone shall undertake the assessment of the duty payable on any gift in Lebanon.

Article 15

- The sum provided for in life insurance contracts shall not be deemed a gift and shall not be included among the assets of the estate. The beneficiary thereof shall be assessed a duty in the amount of (5%) five percent of the insurance sum according to the currency specified in the insurance contract and according to the manner of collection of the sum provided for from the company, without any exemption, and no surcharge shall be added thereto.

This text shall apply to events that have not been assessed and for which the value of the duty has not been paid as at the date of issuance of this amendment.

All aids, subsidies, and grants paid out of public funds shall be exempt from the duties, and every gift whose value does not exceed fourteen million four hundred thousand pounds shall also be exempt. Where it exceeds that, the duty shall be levied on the excess, unless the donee is a charitable institution or an athletic, cultural, artistic, charitable, or religious association, including religious endowments (waqfs), in which case the exemption shall cover an amount of nine hundred million pounds.

The provisions of Articles 14, 15, and 16 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to property and rights bequeathed to a person who is not an heir; whereas if the property and rights are bequeathed to a person who is an heir, the preceding provisions relating to the bases of the duty on estates shall then apply.

The duty shall be payable by the beneficiaries of the endowment (waqf), with the exception of the founder (waqif) himself, and shall be imposed on the value of the entitlement estimated in accordance with the third paragraph of Article 36 of this Legislative Decree after deducting an amount of one million six hundred thousand pounds from the value of the share of each beneficiary.

The duty shall be levied upon the death of the founder (waqif) and its assessment shall be renewed upon the renewal of the entitlement; on the first occasion, the degree of kinship of the beneficiaries shall be determined in relation to the founder (waqif), and thereafter in relation to the person whom they succeeded.

Upon the termination of the endowment (waqf), the duty shall be payable on two-thirds of the value of the property and shall be imposed on the value of the share of each right holder after deducting an amount of one million six hundred thousand pounds.

The mukhtar shall notify the financial departments of the death of any person in his area within a time limit not exceeding 30 days from the date of occurrence of the death, provided that the notification clearly includes the available information regarding the type and place of business or businesses of the deceased and the names and addresses of the heirs.

The mukhtar shall be rewarded with an amount of (25) twenty-five Lebanese pounds for each notification, and shall be punished for every violation of the provisions of this Article by a fine of up to two hundred Lebanese pounds.

Where there are multiple mukhtars for a single area, the fine shall be imposed on the mukhtar who drew up a certificate of death for the civil status departments.

A new time limit of six months shall be opened for the mukhtars concerned by this Article to notify the financial departments of deaths that have occurred and have not been declared up to the date of entry into force of this Law.

In this case, the mukhtars shall benefit from the reward specified above.

The Minister of Finance may extend this time limit for a period not exceeding 31/12/1986 by a decision issued by him upon the proposal of the Director General of Finance.

This fine shall not be payable in the event that the heirs make a declaration within the statutory time limit

The heirs, donees, beneficiaries of an endowment (waqf), and executors of wills and endowments (waqfs), or their legal representatives, shall submit to the competent financial departments, within 90 (ninety) days from the occurrence of the death, gift, execution of the will or endowment (waqf), or judgment declaring the death of an absent person, a declaration containing the name of the decedent, donor, founder (waqif), or testator, the names of the heirs, donees, legatees, beneficiaries of the endowment (waqf), and executors of the will or endowment (waqf), together with the place of residence of each of them and the particulars of the transferred property of various kinds, in addition to the place where it is situated and its true sale value.

The concerned parties shall attach to the declaration the documents substantiating it (the death certificate, family civil status extracts for the deceased and the heirs, title deeds or real estate certificates, the instrument of the will or the contract of gift).

The concerned parties mentioned above shall also submit the remaining documents and proofs relating to their declaration within a period of six months at most from the date of occurrence of the event giving rise to the duty (death, will, gift, endowment (waqf), termination of the endowment (waqf)).

The probative documents required to be submitted for each type of event giving rise to the duty shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

The competent department shall complete the file of the estate and issue the collection order relating thereto within a maximum time limit of three months from the date of submission of the documents and proofs relating to the declaration. In the event of failure to submit the declaration and documents, the competent department shall resort to direct assessment as at the date of death, provided that it completes the file of the estate and issues the collection order for the tax and the applicable fines within a time limit of six months from the date of expiry of the time limit for submitting the documents.

Re-assessment of the estate of the deceased upon the request of a beneficiary of contracts concluded by the decedent prior to his death in favor of a third party or concluded by him two years prior to the date of his death in favor of a person who became an heir

The time limit for submitting the declaration or the time limit for submitting the remaining documents and proofs shall not run against the heirs, donees, legatees, and beneficiaries of an endowment (waqf) with respect to any estate, gift, will, or endowment (waqf) that is the subject of a judicial dispute, except as from the date of issuance of the final judgment in the dispute.

The declaration shall be incumbent upon each right holder individually. However, the declaration of one of the right holders may suffice, without the fine being incurred by the others, when the transfer of the property and rights to them arose from a single event (the death of the decedent, the testator, or the founder (waqif)) or from the execution of the contents of a single instrument (the instrument of the will or the gift).

The competent financial department may extend the time limit for submitting the declaration for a period not exceeding one year in respect of taxpayers obliged to submit it, if they were outside Lebanon on the date of the death, will, gift, or endowment (waqf), or if the causes of the transfer of the property to them occurred outside Lebanese territory.

If, at any time after submitting the declaration and in any manner whatsoever, the concerned parties become aware of new information necessitating the amendment of what was stated in the declaration, they must submit a supplementary declaration within a time limit of thirty days from the date on which they became aware of such information.

The provisions of prescription shall not run against the right of the administration to have recourse against the taxpayers liable for the duty with respect to property and rights not declared by every person obliged to make a declaration.

Every debtor to an estate for funds, bonds, shares, or any other rights, and every person with whom anything of this kind is deposited or who holds possession thereof, must declare the same to the competent financial department within two months from the date of his knowledge of the death of the owner of the estate or his notification thereof. Such debtors may not hand over anything that they owe or that is in their possession to the concerned parties until the latter produce a certificate from the competent financial department proving that the duty has been paid or is not due.

However, the aforementioned debtors may deposit what they may owe or hold in their possession in the Treasury fund or in any bank designated for them by the competent financial department or by the concerned parties with the approval of this department, and such deposit shall discharge them of their liability without prejudice to any rights that they or the concerned parties may have.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply to banks subject to the Law dated 3/9/1956 relating to banking secrecy.

If any of the persons mentioned in the preceding Article hands over anything in his possession contrary to the provisions of that Article, he shall be held liable towards the Treasury for the duty due on what he relinquished, in addition to being charged a fine equivalent to the value of the said duty. If the estate is not subject to the transfer duty, a fine of three hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on the offender.

Contrary to the provisions of the two preceding Articles and the subsequent Article 51, the financial departments have the right, in the event of delay in assessing and collecting the duty, to authorise the concerned parties to dispose of a portion of the estate's assets, provided they pay double the maximum rate of the duty relating to the portion covered by the authorisation.

This excess payment shall be settled when the duty is finally imposed on all the elements of the estate.

Those who customarily lease safes or iron boxes and have a safe leased in whole or in part to a person who has died must inform the competent financial departments of the matter within a week from the date of their knowledge of the death.

As of the date of death, it is prohibited to open the safes or boxes without the presence of a representative from the aforementioned departments.

The offender shall be punished with a fine from fifty thousand pounds to five hundred thousand pounds and shall be held jointly and severally liable with the taxpayers for the duties due on the assets deposited in those safes or boxes.

A creditor of the estate or anyone who holds a registered or unregistered right against it must submit to the competent financial departments, within three months from the date of his knowledge of the death, a statement of the original and current amount of the debt, its nature, its origin, and its terms, as well as the documents, deeds, and apparent or concealed mortgages in his possession.

If the creditor fails to submit the said statement within the specified time limit, a fine equivalent to the value of the duty that may fall due on the heirs as a result of not deducting this debt from the base of the estate shall be imposed on him.

If the estate is not subject to the transfer duty, a fine of three hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on the offending creditor.

The inventorying of estates may only be carried out in the presence of a representative from the competent financial departments, and the concerned authorities must invite him for this purpose.

The competent financial departments have the right to proceed with re-inventorying any estate and to impose a fine on the offending inventorying officer equivalent to fifty percent of the total duty that may fall due on the difference between the two inventories.

This fine shall range between twenty thousand pounds and one hundred thousand pounds if the estate is not subject to the transfer duty.

The competent financial departments may, when necessary, take precautionary measures to safeguard the rights of the Treasury, including attachment, affixing seals, and establishing judicial receivership.

If a dispute arises over the capacity of an heir and there is a judicial receivership, the highest duty shall be imposed in the name of the heirs and collected from the judicial receiver, provided that the final duty is settled when the dispute is adjudicated, regardless of the factor of prescription.

The same provisions shall apply in the absence of a judicial receivership, in which case the duty shall be collected from the heirs, who shall be considered jointly and severally liable therefor.

If the concerned parties neglect to submit the declarations and their attachments or neglect to submit the remaining documents within the time limits specified in Article 21 of this Legislative Decree, or delay in submitting them, they shall be punished for each of these two offences with a fine equivalent to five percent for each offence for each month of delay or fraction of a month of the value of the duty due on the assets, rights, or values not declared within the specified time limits, provided that the fine for each of these two offences does not exceed the value of the duty on the basis of which it is imposed, and that it is not less, even if no duty falls due, than one hundred and twenty-five thousand pounds for each of these two offences for each incident, including incidents occurring prior to the issuance of this Law for which the duty due thereon has not been liquidated.

Whoever intentionally conceals a part of the assets covered by the duty or makes false declarations regarding the debts or rights relating to the estate, gift, will, or waqf shall be punished with a fine from one million pounds to five million pounds.

If the offender is one of the taxpayers subject to the duty, double the duty shall be imposed on him in respect of the concealed assets, in addition to the lump-sum fine provided for in the first paragraph, without his having the right to invoke the factor of prescription.

Petitions, statements, and papers submitted to the competent financial departments for the purpose of imposing the duty are exempt from fiscal stamp duties.

The competent financial departments may suffice with copies of the documents produced to them after verifying their conformity with the produced original which is returned to the concerned party, provided that they are endorsed as being specific to the transfer duty and that they may not be used for any other purpose.

The values of transferred property and rights shall be taken as the basis for assessment according to the prices prevailing on the date of:

- 31/12/2006 in respect of events occurring up to this date.

- The entry into force of this Article in respect of events occurring from 1/1/2007 and up to its entry into force.

- The occurrence of the event in respect of events occurring from the date of entry into force of this Article.

In the event of doubt regarding the declaration, the competent financial departments may amend it in accordance with the following bases:

1 - The value of immovable property shall be assessed taking into consideration all the elements that affect the true value of the real property, such as the price of the land in relation to its location, the cost of construction, the annual revenue, etc...

2 - The right of usufruct in relation to the full value of the ownership shall be assessed based on the age of the usufructuary in accordance with the following table:

Age of the right holder Ratio of usufruct to the value of the real property or to the value of the movable property

Up to 30 years 6/10

From 30 to 40 years 5/10

From 40 to 50 years 4/10

From 50 to 60 years 3/10

From 60 to 70 years 2/10

From 70 and above 1/10

The same principle shall apply with respect to the usufruct of movable property. Where the duration of the right of usufruct is fixed, such right shall be assessed on the basis of one-tenth of the value of the real property for each period of ten years without taking into consideration fractions of such period.

No duty shall be due in the event that the right of exploitation is merged with the bare ownership of the real property, whether this results from the death of the exploiter or from the expiry of the period fixed for exploitation.

3 - A life annuity, if it comprises an annual or monthly stipend, shall be assessed based on the age of the right holder in accordance with the following table:

Age of the right holder Multiple of the annual stipend

Up to 20 years 15 times

From 20 to 30 years 12 times

From 30 to 40 years 10 times

From 40 to 50 years 8 times

From 50 to 60 years 6 times

From 60 to 70 years 4 times

From 70 and above 3 times.

4 - An entitlement in a waqf shall be assessed as though it were a right of usufruct; however, if the waqf deed provides for granting the beneficiary a fixed sum annually or monthly, the entitlement in the waqf shall be assessed in accordance with the table set out at the end of the preceding paragraph.

5 - Financial instruments shall be valued and foreign currencies shall be converted into Lebanese currency according to their average prices during the month preceding the death or the gift.

6 - In all other cases, the competent department shall undertake the assessment, after examining the documents and statements submitted by the interested parties, and it may, where necessary, conduct additional investigations and appoint experts.

The provisions of this Article shall apply to cases subject to the duty that have not yet been submitted to the special valuation committees.

The head of the competent financial department shall undertake the amendment of declarations on the basis of the reports of the controllers, and may refer the case with his reasoned opinion to the Head of the Revenue Department, who shall take a binding decision thereon. The competent controller shall notify the taxpayers concerned or their representatives of the amount of this amendment and the reasons therefor, together with the notice of assessment of the duty, by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.

Each of the taxpayers concerned may object to the issued assessment if he finds an error or an overcharge therein. Objections shall be accepted within two months from the date of notification of the interested parties and the notice provided for in the preceding Article 37, and an objection submitted by some of the interested parties shall benefit the remaining co-owners.

If the financial departments find that the objection submitted within the legal time limit is well-founded, they shall proceed to correct the assessment by means of monthly reduction orders. However, if the department does not agree with the viewpoint of the objector, it shall notify the taxpayer thereof by registered letter and refer the objection, accompanied by its report, to the committee provided for in the following Article.

There shall be formed by decree in each governorate a committee of first instance to examine and adjudicate objections, composed of:

- A judge (appointed upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice) as President

- A Category Three civil servant in the Revenue Department at the Ministry of Finance as Member

- A property owner in the governorate (selected by the Minister of Finance upon the proposal of the Director General of Finance) as Member

- The head of the competent financial department or his representative as Rapporteur

A controller from the competent financial department shall be attached to each committee in the capacity of clerk.

The Rapporteur shall notify the decision of the committee to the competent financial department and to the taxpayer within 15 days from the date of its issuance, and each of these two parties shall have the right to appeal this decision before the State Council within twenty days from the date of notification.

Petitions of appeal shall be submitted directly to the State Council.

The admissibility of an appeal submitted by the taxpayer shall be conditional upon the deposit of a security equivalent to five percent of the duties imposed, and if the petition of appeal is not accompanied by a receipt proving payment of the said security, it shall be dismissed in form.

This security shall be paid together with the judicial fees into the approved fund at the State Council and within the time limit fixed for appeal.

If the decision of the State Council is in favour of the taxpayer, he shall be entitled to recover the value of the security referred to in the preceding paragraph, and if it is in favour of the Treasury, the said security shall become a vested right thereof.

The transfer duty shall be imposed on the net hereditary share of estates and the net share bequeathed to an heir in accordance with the rates specified in the table annexed to this Legislative Decree after making the deductions provided for in the preceding Article 9.

The transfer duty shall be imposed on gifts, waqfs, and bequests made in favour of a non-heir and on other transfers effected without consideration in accordance with the rates specified in the table annexed to this Legislative Decree and after making the deductions provided for in the preceding Articles 16, 18, and 19.

In addition to the transfer duties specified in the table annexed to this Legislative Decree, a flat transfer duty of five per mille shall be imposed on all movable and immovable rights and property that devolve upon third parties, with the exception of the State and municipalities, by way of inheritance, bequest, gift, or waqf, or by any other way without consideration equivalent to their true value.

This flat additional duty shall be due on the portion of the gross total value of the transferred rights, property, and values that exceeds two hundred million Lebanese Pounds, and it shall be considered among the debts and liabilities encumbering the total of the said elements.

Upon the request of the interested parties, this duty may be distributed in accordance with the ratios of the shares of the heirs and without considering it among the burdens of the estate, notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding paragraph of this Article.

The duty shall be due on what devolves upon charitable institutions and upon athletic, cultural, artistic, or charitable associations by way of gift, waqf, bequest, or the like, after the deduction set out in the preceding Article 16 and according to the rate prescribed for the Third Category in the table annexed to this Legislative Decree.

If the property of a deceased person is transferred to any person by way of inheritance, gift, bequest, and waqf simultaneously, or by some of these ways, the total property that has devolved upon him shall be taken into consideration in determining the rate of the duty.

Income tax shall cover:

1- Profits of industrial, commercial and non-commercial professions.

2- Salaries, wages and retirement pensions.

3- Income from movable capital.

The tax shall cover the profits of commercial, industrial and craft professions and establishments, the profits of liberal professions, and the profit of any work generating revenue not subject to another tax on income. No income shall be exempted from the tax except by an explicit provision in the law.
The tax shall be imposed in the name of natural and legal persons, residing in Lebanese territory or abroad, on the total profits that they realise in Lebanon.

There shall be deemed among the taxpayers subject to this tax:

A - Companies, whatever their type and object.

B - Natural or legal persons:

1 - Who act as intermediaries in the purchase or sale of real property and commercial establishments and who undertake the purchase thereof in their own name and the sale thereof for trading.

2 - Who lease out a commercial or industrial establishment equipped with the furniture or tools necessary for its operation, whether the lease covers all the intangible elements of which the establishment consists or covers part thereof, or does not cover them at all.

3 - Who benefit from the proceeds of the exploitation of substances located in the subsoil.

C - Brokers, commission agents and intermediaries, and in general any natural or legal person who acts as an intermediary in the purchase or sale of all kinds of property.

D - Any natural or legal person who has obtained a profit from a work generating revenue not subject to another tax on income.

There shall be exempted from the tax:

1 - Educational institutes.

2 - Hospitals, orphanages, shelters, which admit patients free of charge and similar nursing and relief institutions, within the limits of their net profits derived from public or private funds and subsidies.

As for hospitals, orphanages, shelters, homes for the elderly, dispensaries, sanatoriums and similar nursing and relief institutions, which are owned or operated by institutions, associations or bodies that do not seek to realise a profit, they shall be exempted from the tax on the entirety of their profits.

3 - Mental hospitals and tuberculosis sanatoriums.

4 - Consumer cooperative societies, syndicates, and agricultural cooperatives, if they do not have a commercial character.

5 - Agricultural operators, unless they display the produce of their lands and the livestock that they raise therein and the produce of such livestock in premises designated for sale or sell them after transformation.

6 - Air and maritime navigation enterprises, and subject to reciprocity for foreign enterprises belonging to countries in which Lebanese enterprises operate.

7 - Public services that do not compete with private enterprises, and by this is understood public establishments and autonomous services of an industrial or commercial character.

8 - Fees that mukhtars are permitted to collect pursuant to Article 17 of the Law on Mukhtars, the remuneration provided for in Article 20 of the Law promulgated by Decree No. 146/59 and its amendments (transfer duty), and the allowances that the State may disburse to mukhtars.

The duty shall be paid in a single lump sum in accordance with the provisions relating to the collection of direct taxes and similar duties, whenever the share of the taxpayer liable therefor includes cash and marketable financial instruments whose value exceeds the amount of the transfer duty due from him.

If the taxpayer's share is devoid of cash or financial instruments marketable at such value, the Directorate General of Finance may, upon the request of the concerned parties, within a period of two months from the date on which they are notified of the duty, proceed to divide the imposed transfer duties into five equal annual instalments, the first of which shall fall due three months after the date of notification of the payment order, and an annotation of the payment by instalments shall be entered on the real estate register folio.

No interest shall be due for the first two years of the instalment period, and interest at the rate of interest on five-year Treasury bonds shall be due for the remaining years of the instalment period.

The instalments shall fall due in full upon failure to pay or an instalment of the instalments on its due date.

In the event of disposal of any of the transferred property, the consideration shall be allocated to the satisfaction of the deferred duties unless the rights of the Treasury are secured by an amount equivalent to at least twice their value.

The provisions relating to prescription shall not apply where payment is made by instalments.

In the event of default in paying the instalments on their due dates, all the instalments shall fall due and shall bear annual interest at the rate of 12%.

For the purpose of calculating interest, a fraction of a month shall be deemed a full month.

The administrator of the waqf shall pay the duties due from the beneficiaries out of their share in the revenue within two months from the date of notification mentioned in the preceding Article, and such revenue shall be subject to attachment in favour of the Treasury whatever its value may be.

Provided that the instalment paid by the administrator of the waqf in satisfaction of the duties shall not exceed the revenue of the share of the beneficiaries if they belong to the first or second category set out in the Schedule annexed to this Law, nor the fiftyf of the share if they belong to another category.

The Treasury shall have a priority right over the property transferred to each taxpayer by the measure of the duties imposed on him, and with respect to real property this priority right shall be exempt from registration in the Real Estate Register and shall rank after the three priority rights provided for in Article 118 of Decision No. 3339 dated 12 November 1930

The financial offices shall undertake the imposition of the fines provided for in this Legislative Decree. Such fines and the duties imposed pursuant to this Legislative Decree shall be collected in accordance with the Direct Taxes Collection Law.

The competent judicial authorities are prohibited from issuing a certificate of succession before the concerned parties obtain a special authorisation from the competent financial offices.

The said offices shall have the right to exercise the rights of the heirs and to request directly from the competent authorities the issuance to them of the certificate of succession pertaining to any estate whatsoever free of charges.

The competent judicial authorities, both religious and civil, shall also file with the Ministry of Finance (Revenue Department) monthly nominal lists of all certificate of succession transactions issued by them.

Notaries public, employees of the real estate offices and all public employees are prohibited, under pain of disciplinary penalties, from drawing up, recording, authenticating or registering contracts, declarations, rights and all other transactions relating to an estate or to rights devolved upon their holders by way of inheritance, bequest, gift, waqf or by any other gratuitous way unless the concerned parties obtain a special authorisation from the financial offices. And twice its maximum limit in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall not be granted.

Every person whose office, powers or competence requires him to intervene in the imposition of the duties instituted pursuant to this Legislative Decree, or in their collection, or in the examination of objections submitted in respect thereof, shall be bound by professional secrecy in accordance with the provisions of Article 579 of the Penal Code and shall be subject to its provisions.
The methods of implementation of this Legislative Decree shall be determined by decree.

The previous transfer duties set out in Legislative Decree No. 20 dated 18 December 1939 and on immovable property subject to the transfer duty provided for in this Legislative Decree shall not be levied.

No registration fee shall be levied on motor vehicles transferred by way of inheritance upon their registration in the names of the heirs.

Estates, bequests, gifts and waqfs in respect of which transfer duties have not been paid in accordance with the previous laws in force up to 26 December of the year 19fifty-one, the date of application of the provisions of the Law of 21 December 1951, shall remain subject to the fines due.

The Minister of Finance shall have the right to effect a settlement in respect of the fines, provided that it does not cover more than half of such fine.

First:: Industrial establishments may cover, with a specified portion of their net annual profits, the amounts they allocate starting from the year 1980 for their self-investments, under the following conditions:

1- The investment must be made in order to achieve any of the following purposes:

a - Establishing new industrial equipment capable of increasing the establishment's productive capacity in quality or quantity, and no account shall be taken of investment made in equipment or constructions of a temporary nature, such as those erected for a specific workshop and which cease to exist upon its cessation, nor in equipment and supplies imported under the temporary admission regime .

b - Based on dwellings to house salaried employees and wage-earners working in the establishment in accordance with the provisions of the Housing Law and the regulations emanating therefrom, provided that:

- The dwellings remain the property of the establishment for a period of not less than 12 years.

- They are not used at any time for a purpose other than that for which they are intended.

- The annual housing consideration collected per single dwelling does not exceed 15% of the total annual salaries and wages and their permanent supplements of the salaried employee or wage-earner.

c - And the provisions of the exceptional rent laws shall not apply to these dwellings.

2 - Industrial establishments wishing to benefit from the provisions mentioned above must notify in writing the competent financial department of this wish at least one month prior to commencing the investment, and must specify the year in which they wish to begin the deduction from their profits, and must attach to the notification detailed statements of the investments they wish to undertake, under penalty of losing their right to benefit from the exemption.

The execution by the establishment of any financial transaction arising from its final commitment with third parties in implementation of the purpose of the investment shall be deemed a commencement of the investment .

3 - Where the conditions mentioned above are met, the amounts invested in each transaction shall be covered successively by deducting an amount not exceeding a maximum limit of fifty percent of the profits of the year in which the financial investment takes place and the three subsequent years. This percentage shall be raised to 75 % as a maximum limit if the investment takes place in one of the regions that the Government wishes to develop and which are determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

4 - The percentage deducted from the net annual profits and used to cover self-investments in accordance with the provisions set out above shall be exempted from income tax, provided that the deduction does not exceed the limits of the four years mentioned above for each investment transaction .

5 - The competent financial departments must, regardless of how much time has elapsed, add the amounts deducted for investment purposes to the profits of any subsequent year and subject them together therewith to tax assessment with a fine equivalent to 1% per month starting from the year following the financial year from the profits of which the deduction was made to cover the investment , in the event of failure to complete the investment and breach by the establishment of any of the conditions set out above.

Second:

1 - The profits of industrial establishments established in Lebanon starting from the year 1980 shall be exempted from income tax for a period of ten years as a maximum limit starting from the date of commencement of production if all the following conditions are met by these establishments and within the maximum limit set out in paragraph "d" below:

a - That the factory is established in one of the regions that the Government wishes to develop and which are determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

b - That the establishment aims to produce new goods and materials that were not produced in Lebanon prior to the first of January 1980, and new goods and materials mean those that were not previously produced in Lebanon, and they include what results from converting raw materials into semi-manufactured products or finished products, or converting semi-manufactured products into finished products, as well as new goods and materials produced by mounting or assembly industries by completing the manufacture of unfinished materials or goods imported from abroad.

c - That the value of the fixed assets owned by the new establishment in Lebanon and allocated by it to the production of new goods and materials is not less than five hundred million Lebanese pounds.

d - That the total profits exempted from income tax throughout the entire years of exemption do not in any case whatsoever exceed the value of the fixed assets prior to depreciation invested up to the date of commencement of production.

2 - Industrial establishments wishing to benefit from the provisions mentioned above must notify in writing the competent financial department thereof prior to commencing production, and must attach to the notification the detailed documents and statements relating to the value of their fixed assets and the specifications of their production.

3 - The exemption shall be granted by decree upon the proposal of the Ministries of Finance and of Industry and Petroleum.

4 - The establishment benefiting from the exemption provided for in this Law must submit to the competent financial department, within the time limit specified for submitting returns on annual business results, all the returns and documents required by the Income Tax Law.

It must also keep all the registers and documents relating to its accounting for the exemption period throughout the period provided for in the Code of Commerce.

5 - The competent financial department shall exercise permanent supervision over the establishments benefiting from the provisions of this Law with a view to verifying their compliance with the imposed conditions.

Third:

1-- Industrial establishments shall benefit from a tax discount equivalent to 50% of the tax due on the profits of their industrial exports of Lebanese origin. In the event of transferring the funds resulting from exportation to banks operating in Lebanon for their investment in Lebanon, or in the event of proving their use in full for the purposes of the industrial activity carried on in Lebanon

The percentage of the tax discount shall be raised to seventy-five percent (75 %) for five years starting from the year in which this Law is published.

The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - The certificate of origin duly certified shall be adopted as a primary means of proof in order to consider exports as being of Lebanese origin in accordance with the tenor of the Law.

3 - Customs declarations shall be adopted to prove the value of industrial exports holding the certificate of origin, along with the statements prepared by the Ministry of Finance for this purpose.

4 - Entities benefiting from the exemption shall be bound to include in their profit accounts submitted to the competent financial units at the Ministry of Finance the statements referred to above.

5 - Companies and establishments that exploit underground resources shall be excluded from this exemption, as well as whatever may be excluded pursuant to decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Industry.
The tax shall be imposed on the net profit realised in the year preceding the year of assessment, even if the source of the profit ceased during the year of assessment or prior thereto.

Dividends obtained by Lebanese capital companies as a result of holding shares and quotas in other Lebanese capital companies shall be deducted in their full value from their revenues subject to the tax provided for in this Title, provided that upon their redistribution they shall remain subject to the tax provided for in the new Article 72 bis of the Income Tax Law.

For the purpose of determining the net profit subject to tax, every taxpayer obliged to keep commercial books pursuant to the Code of Commerce must submit a declaration of his actual profit or of his total revenues, and in the second case the Administration shall determine the net profit subject to tax on a lump-sum basis at a specific rate applied to the total revenues.

As for taxpayers who are not obliged to keep commercial books, their profits subject to tax shall be assessed in accordance with the provisions of Sub-section "C" of Chapter Three of this Title.

Where the taxpayer is the practitioner of a non-commercial and non-industrial profession, he must submit a declaration of his total revenues, unless he requests to be assessed on the basis of actual profit in accordance with the provisions of Sub-section (A) of Chapter Three of this Title.

A partner having legal capacity in general partnerships or limited partnerships, as well as the guardian of every minor partner to whom the partnership devolved pursuant

to the provisions of Article 66 of the Code of Commerce, shall be personally liable for submitting the declaration relating to him, and the limited partnership shall remain liable for submitting

a global declaration of the shares of the remaining limited partners in the profits and losses.

The declaration of actual profit is compulsory for the following categories of taxpayers, namely:

1 - Partnerships and capital companies, as well as consumer cooperative societies, syndicates and agricultural cooperatives of a commercial nature.

2 - Branches of the establishments set out in the preceding item when their head office is abroad.

3 - Factories, plants and all other industrial establishments that permanently employ more than four persons, except for those among them that are artisanal establishments.

4 - Banks, bankers, moneychangers and persons who engage in discounting operations or banking business.

5 - Exporters, importers, wholesale and semi-wholesale merchants, commission agents, brokers, and agents of factories and commercial houses.

6 - Retail merchants who employ in their work more than four persons.

7 - Owners of warehouses of pharmaceutical and chemical materials.

8 - Operators of betting establishments (horse racing, pigeon shooting, etc...).

9 - Operators of hotels of the first and second classes according to the official classification.

10 - Operators of theatres and cinemas of the first and second classes. According to the official classification.

11 - Publishing houses and printing presses that permanently employ in their work more than four persons.

12 - Mills operated other than by water and wind that permanently employ more than four persons.

13 - Lessors of equipped establishments.

Categories not mentioned in the preceding Article shall be assessed on the basis of lump-sum or estimated profit; however, every person shall have the right to request to be assessed on the basis of actual profit, provided that he submits an application to that effect before the end of January of the year of assessment.

A person who has chosen the method of assessment on the basis of actual profit may not request to revert in subsequent years to the lump-sum or estimated method of assessment.

The declaration of actual profit shall be submitted to the competent financial offices before the first of April of each year, and before the first of June with respect to capital companies, and there shall be attached thereto a copy of the balance sheet, an abstract of the profit and loss account and a statement of the expenses and charges to be deducted pursuant to the provisions of Article 7, whereas the auditors' report and the explanatory statements relating thereto in companies subject to the system of auditors under the provisions of the Code of Commerce shall be submitted before the first of September of each year. The auditors must comply within the shortest possible time limit with every request for information or clarifications addressed to them by the financial office competent for income tax regarding the audit they conducted, under pain of application of the provisions of Article 108 of the Income Tax Law.

As for taxpayers other than practitioners of commercial and industrial professions for whom it is impossible to submit a balance sheet, they must attach to their declaration

a schedule showing their total gross revenues, the total expenses of their profession, the deductible charges and the amount of their net profit during the preceding year. As for establishments which, in closing their accounts with the approval of the competent financial offices, follow a financial year other than the calendar year, they shall benefit from the time limit set out in this Article (three months or five months), provided that this time limit begins from the date of the annual closing of accounts.

The Administration may extend the aforementioned time limits by one month if it finds substantial grounds warranting the extension.

A lump-sum fine of 2.000.000 L.L. shall be imposed on anyone who fails to submit the auditor's report within the statutory time limit. This fine shall be reduced by half in partnerships, limited liability companies and establishments subject to the system of submitting an auditor's report.

The profit that must be declared is the actual profit realised during the preceding year, or during the period of twelve months on the results of which the last balance sheet was based (where such period differs from the calendar year), and in the case of commencement of a new business, the profit realised between the date of commencement of the business and the end of December of the year preceding the year of assessment must be declared.

If it appears that establishments affiliated to establishments situated outside Lebanon, or supervising establishments situated abroad, transfer part of their profits abroad either by increasing or decreasing purchase or sale prices or by any other means, the profits transferred in this manner must be added, when imposing the tax, to the profits shown in the accounts.

If sufficient evidence is not available to determine the actual profit, the profits of similar establishments shall be taken as a basis for comparison and for determining the profit, in addition to external signs and the information of the competent financial offices.

If a deficit occurs in a specific year, such deficit shall be considered among the charges of the following year and shall be deducted from the actual profit that may have been realised during the said year, and if such profit is insufficient to cover the deficit in full, the balance of the deficit shall be deducted from the profits of the second year, and if anything remains thereof, it shall be deducted from the profits of the third year. This deficit or its balance may not be carried forward beyond the third year following the year of its occurrence.

The amount of the deficit must be declared within the time limit specified for declaring the actual profit, and in the same manner.

As for the employees, workers and wage earners referred to in the preceding Article, as well as the employees personally obliged to pay the tax on salaries and wages and to declare the same, and the non-profit institutions, associations and bodies having no more than five employees which fail to submit the annual declaration, the competent financial departments shall assess the tax upon them directly together with a lump-sum fine of fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds, and upon repetition of the infringement within three years the fine shall be raised to double its amount without being subject to settlement in any case; and if the employers referred to in Article 51 fail to keep the register provided for in the said Article, or refuse to produce it or to produce the documents necessary to determine the true taxable revenues, or refuse to allow the competent officials to inspect them, they shall also be assessed directly for the tax and the fine on the basis of the revenues estimated by the competent financial departments.

Every employer obliged to keep the register of wage earners provided for in Article 51 shall, when he ceases work or assigns his establishment or premises before the end of the year, submit the declaration provided for in Article 52 within one month from the date of cessation of work or assignment of the establishment or premises, failing which the fine provided for in the preceding Article 54 shall be imposed upon him.

The same provisions shall apply to judicial receivers and trustees in bankruptcy in the event of bankruptcy, in which case the said one-month time limit shall run from the date of issuance of the decision appointing them. The taxes imposed in accordance with the provisions of this Article shall fall due in full immediately.

When calculating the tax, any taxable profit below ten Pounds shall be disregarded.

This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall take effect starting from the operations of the year 1977.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 88 dated 30/6/77 - Official Gazette No. 20.

The tax shall be imposed on the net annual revenues determined in accordance with the provisions of Articles 48, 49 and 50 of the Income Tax Law after deducting therefrom, for each natural person among the taxpayers, the family deduction in accordance with the provisions of Article 31 of the Income Tax Law under the same conditions, in addition to deducting an amount of ten million Lebanese Pounds from the basis of the retirement pension for pensioners.

If the limit [one] of the taxpayers subject to the tax instituted under this Part simultaneously engages in work subject to the tax of Part I, he shall only benefit from the deduction provided for in Part I.

A- The tax rate in respect of salaries and wages is fixed as follows:

2% (two per cent) on the portion of net taxable revenues not exceeding /360.000.000/ L.L. three hundred and sixty million Lebanese Pounds.

4% (four per cent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /360.000.000/ L.L. three hundred and sixty million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /900.000.000/ L.L. nine hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

7% (seven per cent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /900.000.000/ L.L. nine hundred million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /1.800.000.000 L.L. one billion and eight hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

11% (eleven per cent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /1.800.000.000/ L.L. one billion and eight hundred million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /3.600.000.000/ L.L. three billion and six hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

15% (fifteen per cent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /3.600.000.000/ L.L. three billion and six hundred million Lebanese [Pounds] and not exceeding /7.200.000.000/ L.L. seven billion and two hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

20% (twenty per cent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /7.200.000.000/ L.L. seven billion and two hundred million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /13.500.000.000/ L.L. thirteen billion and five hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

25% (twenty-five per cent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /13.500.000.000/ L.L. thirteen billion and five hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

The deduction from the basis shall be calculated at an amount equivalent to 1.500.000 L.L. one million and five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds per day for wage earners and hourly workers who receive daily wages regardless of their family status.

Taxpayers,Whatever the method of their assessment for the tax, as well as establishments exempted from the tax on profits, and the employee, worker and wage earner who simultaneously holds a post or employment in several establishments or premises, shall calculate the tax on salaries and wages due in accordance with the laws in force, pay it to the Treasury and take care of [declare] it in accordance with the provisions of Chapter III of this Part, without the need to issue basic assessment rolls therefor.

If the financial departments find grounds for modification when auditing the accuracy of the submitted declarations, they shall notify the taxpayer of the amount of such modification and the reasons therefor, together with a notice of the additional tax or surcharge, by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.

The tax shall be imposed by virtue of annual assessment rolls and collection shall be effected in accordance with the rules for the collection of direct taxes and similar fees, subject to the provisions of the following Article 62.

A personal notice detailing the tax assessed upon him shall be sent to each taxpayer through the employer or through the institution that pays him the retirement pension or life annuities, with the possibility of replacing such personal notices with abstracts of the assessment rolls drawn up for each employer separately.

The employer shall withhold the tax from the salaries and wages that he pays to the employee and shall remit the withheld amounts to the Treasury in the same currency in which such salaries and wages were paid every three months on a date not later than the fifteenth of the month following the three-month period concerned.

For the purpose of calculating and paying the tax due on salaries and wages paid in foreign currencies, the salaries and wages shall be converted into Lebanese pounds in accordance with the provisions of Article 35 of the Law enforced ipso facto No. 10 dated 15\11\2022, and then the calculated tax shall be converted into the foreign currency in which the salaries and wages were paid according to the exchange rate determined by the Bank of Lebanon..

This text shall not apply to the calculation of end-of-service indemnities for the period preceding 31/12/2023, provided that they are addressed in a special law and after a revaluation of all end-of-service indemnities accrued during that period.

This obligation shall be incumbent upon individuals, establishments, companies and associations that pay retirement pensions or life annuities, and those who do not remit to the Treasury within the time limit indicated above the amounts for which they are liable or remit them short shall be deemed personally liable for the unpaid amounts in addition to a fine of three per cent (3%) for each month of delay, a fraction of a month being counted as a full month.

Where it is established that the employer decided to pay or paid additional amounts to employees (such as a balance sheet bonus) at a date subsequent to 15 January of each year in respect of the business year preceding it, such amounts shall be exempted from the late payment fine on condition that the tax due thereon is remitted within the statutory time limit prescribed for submitting the annual declaration.

The text of this Article shall take effect starting from the business operations of the year 2003 and the details of its application shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

All employers, regardless of the method of their assessment for income tax, shall be required to submit the periodic statement of salaries and wages for each quarter when the tax falls due for the quarter concerned within the statutory time limit prescribed for each of the quarterly payments.

Anyone who contravenes the provisions of this paragraph shall be subject to a fine of five per cent 5% of the value of the tax due, provided that such fine shall not exceed two million (2.000.000) Lebanese pounds and shall not be less than two hundred thousand 200.000 Lebanese pounds for each quarter in respect of which the tax fell due and the periodic statement pertaining thereto was not submitted.

As for employees personally required to remit the tax on salaries and wages and to declare it, and establishments, associations and bodies that do not seek to realise profit and where the number of employees therein does not exceed five, a flat fine of fifty thousand (50.000) Lebanese pounds shall be imposed in the event of a contravention.

The Administration may extend the time limit mentioned above by ten days if it finds substantive grounds necessitating the extension.

The provisions of this Title relating to keeping the register of employees, declaring their revenues, withholding the tax therefrom, and remitting it to the Treasury shall apply to autonomous services, public establishments and major municipalities, as well as other municipalities and bodies determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The tax due from civil servants, officials, employees, workers, and other wage-earners and pensioners of all categories, who receive their salaries, wages and allowances from the State, shall be withheld monthly from the income of the taxpayer during the month in which it fell due.

The provisions of this Title relating to the obligations of employers and to the manner of drawing up assessment rolls, and paying the tax, shall not apply to the State.

The salaries of diplomats appointed to Lebanese missions abroad shall be subject to the tax on the basis of the salary.

The details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined, where necessary, in a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.
