Whoever is liable for remitting the tax on behalf of a principal taxpayer shall have the right to recover what he has paid out of the principal of the amounts that he receives or holds for the account of that taxpayer, provided that he benefits from the priority enjoyed by the Treasury.
All correspondence between the financial departments and the taxpayers subject to this tax shall take place through the employer or the establishment that pays retirement pensions or life annuities.

All the rights and obligations of the non-resident employer, provided for in this Title, shall be transferred to the resident taxpayer, and in particular with regard to submitting declarations and paying the tax.

First: Notwithstanding any other text, the following shall be subject to the provisions of the Income Tax Law (Legislative Decree No. 144/59 and its amendments) and to the tax of Title III thereof at the rate of seven per cent (7%):

1 - All interest, yields and revenues of credit accounts of all kinds opened with banks, including savings accounts, with the exception of accounts opened in the name of the Government, municipalities and public establishments and deposited with the Bank of Lebanon, and the accounts of foreign diplomatic and consular missions in Lebanon.

2 - Interest and yields of deposits and all other banking commitments in whatever currency, including those pertaining to non-residents.

3 - Interest, revenues and yields of fiduciary and asset management accounts.

4 - Yields and interest of certificates of deposit issued by all banks and debt debentures issued by joint-stock companies

5 - Interest and revenues of Lebanese Treasury bonds.

Second: Where such interest, yields and revenues are included within the profits of banking, financial or commercial establishments pursuant to Articles 8 and 70 of the Income Tax Law, they shall remain subject to the tax provided for in paragraph (First) above, and the value of the tax paid thereon shall be deducted from the tax on the profits of practising the profession.

Third: Amounts deposited with the Bank of Lebanon and investments with the Government by foreign States or institutions affiliated thereto or international institutions shall be exempted from the tax.

Fourth: The provisions of this Article shall not apply to Lebanese Treasury bonds issued on a date prior to the publication of this Law. The details of the application of this Article shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

Interest, yields, profits and revenues resulting from the practice of the profession shall be subject to the tax of Title I.

Apart from these, the tax on income from movable capital shall cover every capital profit, revenue or income not subject to another tax on income.

Nothing shall be exempted therefrom except what is exempted by an express text in the law.

The following shall be exempted from the tax:

1 - (Repealed)

2 - Amounts paid for the reimbursement of the funds of creditors and shareholders, if they are taken other than from the profit and loss account or the reserve.

3 - Repayments of the funds of shareholders and creditors in concessionary companies, even if deducted from the reserve or the profit and loss account, when the reason for the repayment arises from the obligation to hand over the installations to the authority upon the expiry of the term of the concession without consideration.

4 - Interest on amounts entered in savings passbooks, on condition that the value of such interest does not exceed one thousand pounds per year.

5 - Interest and yields of all current accounts opened with banks.

6 - Revenues of bonds on the Lebanese Treasury.

The rate of the tax on movable capital income is fixed at ten percent (10%) of the gross revenues and no surcharge shall be added to the principal of the tax.

Notwithstanding any other text, the tax on movable capital shall be paid upon filing the declaration for the income subject thereto. This tax shall be imposed pursuant to collection orders, and such orders may be drawn up by way of settlement.

The details of application of this paragraph shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

Distributions of Lebanese capital companies shall be subject to a proportional tax of ten percent (10%) under all circumstances, even if the company is exempt from the tax of Title One pursuant to Articles 5 and 5 bis, and no surcharge shall be added thereto.

Every increase of capital taken from profits that were previously subjected to the tax of Title One or

were exempt from this tax pursuant to Articles 5 and 5 bis shall be excluded from the tax on distributions.

Profits realised prior to the operations of 1980 that were subjected to the progressive tax provided for in

Title One of the Income Tax Law or in the Built Property Tax Law shall also be excluded from the tax on distributions.

As for foreign capital companies operating in Lebanon, their profits shall be deemed distributed in full and shall be subject to the tax provided for in this Article after

deducting therefrom the following:

- The tax of Title One due on the profits.

- The reserve of 10% provided for in Article 133 of the Code of Money and Credit put into force by Decree No. 13513 dated 1/8/1963.

(Implementing text for this Article: Decree 1460/2017)

The tax rate that capital companies are required to apply to the distributions they make as from the date of 27/10/2017

The taxable income or yield in respect of Lebanese shares and debt securities shall be determined as follows:

1 - In respect of shares of various kinds, founders' shares, and amounts deducted by Lebanese joint-stock companies from profits and what they distribute with the reserve.

The income shall be determined on the basis of the statements of the auditors, the resolutions of the general assemblies of shareholders and boards of directors, and other similar documents.

2 - In respect of debt securities:

It shall be based on the interest or the income distributed during the year.

3 - In respect of lottery prizes.

It shall be based on the amount of the prize itself stated in Lebanese currency.

4 - In respect of redemption premiums:

It shall be based on the difference between the amount paid upon redemption and the issue value of the security.

The gain from the disposal of shares shall be excluded from income tax.

5 - The gain from the disposal of shares realised by natural persons upon disposing of their shares in one of the following joint-stock companies shall be subject to a tax equivalent to the real estate transfer and devolution fee:

- Companies whose sole or principal object is the ownership of built and unbuilt real property.

- Companies engaged in the trade of built unbuilt real property or real estate development activity.

- Companies in which the value of their fixed assets consisting of real property exceeds 50% of their total fixed assets.

The taxable gain shall be determined as the difference between the cost of acquisition of the share and the actual disposal price thereof.

The transferor shall benefit from a tax deduction at the rate of 50% when the disposal takes place between the shareholders themselves or between ascendants and descendants.

The gain realised by these persons upon disposing of their shares in the remaining joint-stock companies shall be excluded from the tax.

Any shareholder may carry out an exceptional revaluation of his shares once only and within a time limit ending on 30/6/2023.

The revaluation operation shall be carried out through one of the experts affiliated with the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants.

Positive differences resulting from the revaluation operation shall be subject to a new proportional tax at the rate of 1% (one percent) of the value of these differences.

The transferor is required, within a time limit of two months from the date of the disposal, to declare the disposal operation and to pay the tax due pursuant to special forms prepared by the Ministry of Finance for this purpose, and the transferor and the transferee shall be jointly and severally liable for the payment of the tax due on the disposal operation.

Where necessary, the details of application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

The tax shall fall due within twenty days from the end of the quarter during which the profits, interest, royalties or other revenues of shares and founders' shares accrued.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

Every company, institution, or public or private body shall advance the tax to the Treasury within the period set forth in the preceding Article, provided that it recovers it subsequently from the holders of the shares or securities, and it must submit upon payment the following documents:

1 - For shares: extracts of the statements of the auditors, and of the resolutions of the general assemblies of shareholders or boards of directors, and in general, of every resolution relating to the distribution of yield or reserve.

2 - For debt securities: a schedule containing the number of securities, the nominal value of the security, the rate of interest, and the maturity date.

3 - For lottery prizes and redemption premiums: a certified true copy of the minutes of the draw, and a schedule showing the number of securities redeemed in each draw, the issue value, the amount of prizes due and the taxable amount.

Natural and legal persons who fail to pay the tax within the legal time limit, in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article, or who pay it short, shall be held directly liable for the unpaid amounts, to which shall be added an assessment fine of three percent for for each month of delay, a fraction of a month being considered a full month, provided that it does not exceed (100%) one hundred percent of the value of the unpaid amounts.

All foreign shares and private and public foreign debt securities owned by natural or legal persons residing in Lebanon, whether foreigners or Lebanese, shall be subject to the tax.

Any natural or legal person who undertakes in Lebanese territory the payment of the yield of the said shares and securities shall withhold the tax for the account of the Treasury.

Whoever engages in the profession of collecting, paying or purchasing coupons, or other financial securities designated for the payment of profits, interest, royalties and prizes of securities or the financial securities set forth in the preceding Article, must submit a declaration thereof to the competent financial departments within one month from the date of commencing his work, failing which he shall be punished by a fine ranging between two hundred thousand pounds and five hundred thousand pounds.

All persons referred to in the preceding paragraph are prohibited from collecting, paying or purchasing the coupons or other financial securities mentioned above, or trading therein, without immediately withholding the tax, unless it is proven to them that another intermediary had previously withheld it.

The persons referred to in the preceding Article shall draw up, upon every payment they make, a schedule in two copies in which the following particulars shall be entered:

1 - The name of the payer, his business address, and his profession or trade.

2 - The type of coupons or other financial securities presented to him collection, their number, and their unit value in Lebanese currency at the time of payment.

3 - The total gross amount in Lebanese currency.

4 - The amount of the tax due.

5 - The registration number in the register provided for hereinafter, the date, the signature of the payer, and the name, address and signature of the payee.

One copy of the schedule shall be given to the party who collected.

The second copy shall remain in the possession of the party who paid, and in the event of failure to draw up these schedules, a fine ranging between two hundred thousand pounds and five hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on the offender.

The persons themselves shall keep two registers numbered and signed by the Financial Departments, in which they shall enter, day by day, without blanks or interlineations, the transactions of payment, sale, or purchase of coupons or other securities from which the tax must be withheld.

In these two registers shall be recorded the particulars included in the schedules provided for in the preceding Article.

Register No. (1) shall be allocated to payment transactions that required the withholding of the tax by the person directly entrusted therewith.

Register No. (2) shall be allocated to sale and purchase transactions that did not require the withholding of the tax because another intermediary had previously withheld it.

In the event of failure to keep these two registers, a fine ranging between two hundred thousand pounds and five hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on the offender.

The withholder of the tax shall draw up, at the end of each half-year, an abstract of Register No. (1), total it, certify it, and send it with the tax withheld, and this tax must be paid within the month following the half-year, and the provisions of Article 76 shall apply to the offender

Holders of financial and foreign shares and bonds, or the beneficiaries of their yield, residing in Lebanon, if they transfer their dividends, interest, royalties, or other revenues abroad, or collect them abroad, whether directly or through an intermediary, shall submit to the Financial Departments, before the first of March of each year, a statement in which they mention the total of these dividends, interest, royalties, and revenues collected during the preceding year, and in the event of failure to submit this statement, a fine of ten percent of the amount of the tax imposed on him for each month of delay shall be imposed on the offender, provided that a fraction of a month shall be considered a full month and that the amount of the fine shall not exceed fifty percent of the amount of the said tax.

In the event of repetition, the fine shall be raised to an amount equal to the tax, and no settlement may be made in respect of these fines .

This tax must be paid before the first of April of each year, and in the event of delay in payment, a fine of 3% for each month of delay shall be added to the unpaid amounts, provided that a fraction of a month shall be considered a full month.

The tax shall be imposed on interest, royalties , commissions , reinvestment indemnities , prepayment indemnities, and other revenues from secured debts, whatever their designation and the manner of their payment, and all these revenues have been designated in this Chapter by the name "interest".

By secured debt is meant every debt (loan , bond, etc...) secured by real property situated in Lebanon, whatever the type of security or its designation, (hypothec, mortgage, sale with right of redemption, sale with right of repurchase, antichresis etc...) or secured by movable property the registration of the security of which is provided for by law, such as motor vehicles, vessels, and others.

All gross interest resulting from the security, whether nominal or actual, and whatever the date on which it arose, shall be subject to the tax. For the calculation of the interest, the rate mentioned in the instrument of security shall be adopted, if it is not less than the customary level , and otherwise the legal rate .

In all cases, the competent Financial Departments may recover the concealed rights of the Treasury from the tax up to the third year following the year during which the release of the security took place, and assess the creditor with a fine equal to three times the recovered tax. The collection of the said tax and fine shall be effected in accordance with the Direct Taxes Collection Law.

If the principal of the debt or a part thereof is collected before its interest, the tax shall be calculated as if the payment had been made in respect of the interest first.

The said tax shall be reduced in proportion to the loss affecting the original capital if the creditor has exhausted the legal means of execution, and the subject of the security has not devolved upon him in any case.

If the debtor, or any successor in title after him, pays the tax due on the interest, he shall benefit by operation of law from set-off, by deducting the amount paid from the interest due to the creditor, and otherwise from the principal of the debt.

No one shall be entitled to obtain a total or partial striking off of a mortgage or security registered as a guarantee for a debt producing interest, unless he obtains a prior approval from the competent tax departments.

In the event of execution of the mortgage or security through the Execution Departments, these departments shall undertake to withhold the tax from the amounts collected and pay it to the Treasury.

Shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article, notwithstanding any other text, transactions for the striking off of a mortgage or security relating to private passenger cars, vehicles intended for agricultural work, and residential units owned by their owners who are natural persons by virtue of loans, in the event that the interest resulting therefrom in favour of the creditor entity is subject to the tax on the profits of this entity.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

The tax on the interest of secured debts shall be collected by virtue of collection orders issued by the competent department, upon the request of the party concerned, whether he is the creditor or to a debtor or represents them.

The tax shall cover the gross amount of interest, royalties, and other revenues set forth in paragraphs 9 and 10 of Article 69, and shall be incumbent upon the creditor notwithstanding any stipulation to the contrary , provided however that the debtor is obliged to withhold it and pay it to the Treasury unless it is proven to him that it was previously paid by the creditor. The tax shall be collected pursuant to collection orders issued by the competent Financial Department, and a declaration must be made of the name of the creditor (or the number of his account where naming is prohibited) and the value of the interest and the debt, and the date on which it arose and its maturity.

The debtor shall submit this declaration, together with the declaration due on the result of his operations subject to the tax of Title One, or before the first of March, if he is not subject to the said tax. The Execution Departments shall undertake, upon initiating the execution of the various debts, to withhold the tax due to the Treasury and the tax shall then be calculated for the entire period falling between the date on which the debt arose and the date of its payment, regardless of the provisions on prescription.

In the event of execution of the debt through the Execution Departments, these departments shall undertake to withhold the tax from the amounts collected and pay it to the Treasury.

Any violation of the provisions of this Article shall entail the imposition of the fines provided for in Article 82 on the creditor and the debtor, who shall be jointly and severally liable for paying them together with the tax to the Treasury.

Fifty percent of what lapses by prescription of the amounts and securities set forth below shall accrue definitively to the State:

1 - Dividends of shares and bonds issued by commercial and civil companies and Lebanese bodies, whether public or private, and their interest, royalties, and revenues.

2 - Shares, founders' shares, debt bonds, and other securities issued by the same companies and bodies.

3 - Cash deposits, and in general, all cash funds deposited in banks, credit and lending institutions, and other institutions that accept funds in the form of deposits or current accounts.

4 - Shares, bonds, and all securities deposited in banks or in other institutions that accept them in the form of deposits or in any other form.

5 - Amounts paid by way of security deposit, whatever its cause, to commercial and civil joint-stock companies and to private or public Lebanese bodies, or to public administrations, and the taxpayer shall have the right to recourse against the Treasury, subsequently, if a judgment is rendered against him in favour of the owner of the funds, and within the limits of this judgment.

The companies, banks, establishments, public and private bodies, and public administrations referred to in the preceding Article are required to declare to the financial offices, before the first of June of each year, all the sums or securities that have lapsed by prescription during the preceding year, half of which accrues to the Treasury, and they must attach to this declaration the value of the sum payable to the Treasury.

In the event of a violation of the provisions of this Article, the violator shall be required to pay the full sum lapsed by the said prescription, together with a fine equal to half of this sum.

Every taxpayer shall have the right to object to the taxes imposed upon him pursuant to this Legislative Decree, if he finds an error or an overcharge therein. Objections to these taxes shall be submitted to the competent financial offices within two months:

1 - Either from the date of the announcement in the Official Gazette of the placing of the basic assessment rolls into collection, when the assessment that is the subject of the objection is included in those rolls.

2 - Or from the date of notification of the personal notice, where there are additional assessments, additions, or reductions independent of the basic rolls.

If the objection submitted in accordance with the preceding Article satisfies its formal conditions and the grounds contained therein are well-founded in fact and in law, the competent office shall proceed to rectify the assessment by means of monthly rolls and shall notify the summary thereof to the concerned party by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.

However, if the competent financial office finds that this objection is unfounded, it shall inform the concerned party thereof and refer the objection, accompanied by its opinion, to the special committee provided for in the following Article for examination and adjudication.

In all cases, the head of the competent office must decide on the objection, or refer it together with his opinion to the said committee, within six months at the most from the date of its submission.

There shall be formed by decree, in each governorate, one or more committees of first instance to examine and adjudicate the said objections, composed of:

- A judge appointed upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice --- Chairman

- An employee of the Ministry of Finance belonging to the third category at least (selected by the Minister of Finance) -- Member.

- A representative of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry (appointed upon the proposal of the President of the said Chamber) or a representative of the Governorate Council or the Municipal Council (selected by the Governor and appointed upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior where such Chamber does not exist) ----- Member.

- The Head of Finance of the Governorate or the head of the competent tax office ---- Rapporteur.

A tax inspector (first grade) from the competent office shall be placed at the disposal of the said committee in the capacity of secretary, who may deputise for the rapporteur when necessary, provided that neither he nor the rapporteur may participate in the voting.

In the stages of litigation before this committee, the rules of procedure followed before the administrative courts relating to the exchange of pleadings, time limits, and notification shall be observed, with the exception of those relating to the Government Commissioner.

The rapporteur must notify the decision of the committee to the competent financial office and to the taxpayer within 15 days from the date of its issuance, and both the financial office and the taxpayer shall have the right to appeal this decision before the State Council within twenty days from the date of notification.
Applications for appeal shall be submitted directly to the State Council.

The admissibility of the appeal submitted by the taxpayer shall be conditional upon the deposit of a security equal to five percent of the amount of the contested tax, and every application for appeal not accompanied by a receipt proving payment of the said security shall be dismissed as to form.

This security shall be paid, together with the judicial fees, into the approved fund at the State Council, and within the time limit prescribed for the appeal.

If the decision of the State Council is wholly in favour of the taxpayer, he shall be entitled to recover the value of the security referred to in the preceding Article, and if it is wholly in favour of the Treasury, the said security shall become a vested right thereof.

However, if the judgment is partially in favour of the taxpayer, the refund of the security shall only be in proportion to the tax that the judgment ordered to be discharged from the said taxpayer.

Income inspectors shall have the right to inspect, at the premises of taxpayers or the persons responsible for paying the tax, all registers and documents, and everything that may assist in the assessment of the tax.

No natural or legal person, nor even official offices, may invoke professional secrecy if the competent finance employees request to inspect the documents and records relating to the assessment of income tax.

The financial offices may request the Public Prosecution to inspect the file of any lawsuit brought before the courts, and the judicial authority must inform the said offices, through the Public Prosecution, of any information in its possession that gives reason to suspect that one of the taxpayers has defrauded the financial offices or attempted to defraud them in matters relating to income tax, whether the lawsuit is civil, commercial, correctional, or criminal, even if it ended in a decision of dismissal of proceedings.

Every natural or legal person in Lebanon, including those subject to the Banking Secrecy Law, is required to allow the inspectors of the tax administration, upon request, to inspect all registers, documents, and information in his possession that assist in determining the bases of the tax that may be due from him or from other taxpayers.

Every person whose office, powers, or competence requires him to intervene in the assessment of income tax, or in its collection, or in the examination of objections submitted in respect thereof, shall be bound by professional secrecy and shall be subject to the provisions of Article 579 of the Penal Code.

However, professional secrecy may not be invoked in lawsuits affecting the interests of the administration, or during the exercise by the offices of assessment control, collection, or financial inspection of their administrative duties. Income inspectors and assessment and collection inspectors must take the oath before the competent judicial authority prior to assuming their duties.
Taxpayers or their agents may not request certificates or extracts from the assessment files except in relation to the declarations and documents that they have previously submitted.
All statements and correspondence relating to income tax that are exchanged by the employees of the administration or sent by them to taxpayers shall be placed in sealed envelopes.

Whoever obstructs the exercise of the right of inspection provided for in Chapter Two of Part Four, or refuses to give the administration the information it requests, shall be punished by a fine ranging between one million and five million pounds.

The fine shall be imposed by the competent financial offices. Payment of the fine shall not preclude the requirement for the taxpayer to fulfil his basic obligations nor his prosecution, in accordance with the legal provisions in force, in the event of his failure to fulfil these obligations.

Every violation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree or of the regulations subordinate thereto, not expressly provided for therein, shall render its perpetrator punishable by a fine of two hundred thousand pounds and five hundred thousand pounds.

The competent financial offices shall undertake the imposition of the fines prescribed pursuant to this Legislative Decree, and these fines shall be levied and collected in accordance with the rules for the collection of direct taxes and similar fees.

As for the penal sanctions and fines provided for in Article 108, they shall be adjudicated by the competent courts, upon the request of the Ministry of Finance, without any need for prior notice to the taxpayer to rectify his declaration.

The rights of the Treasury in respect of assessment may be recovered by means of supplemental or annexed assessment rolls drawn up until the end of the third year following the year during which the undisclosed or concealed income ought to have been assessed, in addition to the penalties to which the taxpayer, or the person liable for payment of the tax, is subject.

Assessments cancelled wholly or in part due to a defect in their non-essential formalities, or in the type of tax stated therein, or in the designation of the taxpayer subject thereto, may be recovered, and they may also be rectified and the tax imposed on any profit or income proven to have been realised by virtue of a judicial judgment, an arbitral award, or the inventorying of an estate, until the end of the calendar year following the year in which the judgment, award, or inventory was issued, in addition to the time limit provided for in the preceding paragraph.

Every person wishing to leave Lebanese territory permanently shall obtain, prior to his departure, a certificate from the Ministry of Finance proving that he has paid the income tax due from him.

The competent departments are prohibited from endorsing the passport of any person wishing to leave Lebanese territory permanently before the production of the certificate provided for in the preceding paragraph.

Provided that the aforementioned certificate shall be required of non-residents wishing to leave the country even on a temporary basis.
Returns, objections, statements, and other papers and documents submitted to the Ministry of Finance in connection with income tax shall be exempt from fiscal stamp duties.
Persons who provide information relating to concealed income shall be granted a reward ranging between 10 and 30 per cent of the value of the fines collected by virtue of the said information.

A - Every taxpayer who commences a new activity shall notify the financial departments thereof within a period of two months from the date of commencement of the activity, and anyone who violates the provisions of this paragraph shall be fined a penalty determined as follows:

- Three million Lebanese pounds for joint-stock companies.

- Two million Lebanese pounds for limited liability companies and partnerships limited by shares.

- One million Lebanese pounds for partnerships and taxpayers mandatorily assessed on the basis of actual profit.

- Five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for other taxpayers.

The detailed rules for proving the date of commencement of the activity shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

B - Concealed taxpayers who file a declaration within a period determined by the Minister of Finance, provided that it does not exceed the date of 31/12/1997, shall be exempted from the fine for failing to declare the commencement of the activity within the period specified in Paragraph -A- above.

All natural and legal persons enjoying special exemptions or exceptions from income tax, as well as all commercial companies enjoying a permanent exemption pursuant to the Fifth Article of this Legislative Decree, shall submit annual returns and statements to the competent financial departments and allow the competent officials, upon request, to inspect every entry or document related to the determination of the operations and profits or losses relating to them or to third parties dealing with them.

In the event of delay or refusal, a fine of two hundred thousand pounds to five hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on the offender.

Taxes, fines, and other sums due to the State pursuant to this Legislative Decree shall enjoy a general lien of the first rank over all the property of the taxpayers subject thereto or of the persons liable for their payment to the Treasury.

This lien shall apply even in the event of preventive composition, judicial liquidation, or bankruptcy.

Subject to the provisions of the Code of Commerce, and for the purpose of applying the provisions of the income tax, the registers and documents necessary to prove the accuracy of the entries and returns must be retained for a period of five years following the basic year of assessment.

For the purpose of applying this Legislative Decree, the following words and expressions shall be equivalent in their general meanings:

- Tax on industrial, commercial, and non-commercial profits: the tax of Title I.

- Tax on salaries, wages, and pensions: the tax of Title II.

- Tax on income from movable capital: the tax of Title III.

- Income: Profit - Revenue.

- (Taxpayer - Employer) Every natural or legal person subject to the tax.

- Establishment: Commercial establishment - Industrial establishment - Non-industrial establishment - Public or private establishments - Profession of whatever kind - Craft - Work.

- Profit: Income from movable capital whatever its designation - Interest - Royalties - Revenues.

The expressions and words contained in this Legislative Decree shall be interpreted in accordance with the public interest and so as to preserve the rights of the Treasury, and the detailed rules for its application shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.

This Legislative Decree shall enter into force as from the beginning of the year 1960, and as from that date all laws, legislative and ordinary decrees, and regulations contrary to it or inconsistent with its content, whether general or special, shall be repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall be published and communicated wherever needed.

Article 3 of Order No. 15/S issued on 19 January 1925 concerning Lebanese nationality, completed by Order No. 160/L.R dated 16 July 1934, is repealed. The effect of this repeal shall commence from the day on which the Lebanese Law issued on 27 May 1939 concerning nationality enters into force by its publication in the Official Gazette of the Lebanese Republic.

Active service in the Special Troops of the Levant, when its duration is two years or more, may be considered exceptional services within the meaning of Article 2 of the Lebanese Law issued on 27 May 1939 concerning nationality.

This Order shall be published in the Official Gazette of the Lebanese Republic at the same time as the Lebanese Law issued on 27 May 1939 is published, and shall become mandatory under the conditions provided for in Article 2 of Order No. 96/S dated 14 April 1925.
The Secretary-General of the High Commission is charged with the execution of this Order.

The felling, exploitation and processing of all resinous trees of the species of stone pine, Aleppo pine, Lebanon cedar, juniper,cade juniper, cypress, fir and all other resinous trees located within forests owned by the State or owned by municipalities and villages or owned by individuals shall be prohibited, and the application of Article 132 of the Forests Law shall be suspended, and public works projects carried out by public administrations and institutions and licensed construction projects shall be exempted.

Firewood, timber and trees felled, transported or processed in violation of Article- 1 of this Law shall be confiscated and sold at public auction for the benefit of the Treasury - the General Reforestation Fund - and offenders shall be sentenced to imprisonment from one month to three years and to a fine ranging between 20 and 80 thousand Lebanese pounds for each tree felled or uprooted according to its size, and to one hundred pounds for each kilogram of timber or firewood, and to two thousand Lebanese pounds for each manufactured crate, and to one thousand Lebanese pounds for each kg of other- manufactured wooden materials.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.

No foreign association may be established, nor may it carry on its activities in Lebanon or Syria, unless it obtains prior authorisation from the Delegate of the High Commissioner. It may not have establishments in Lebanon or Syria save pursuant to a special authorisation for each of such establishments.

The authorisation may be granted on a temporary basis or be subject to periodic renewal.

It may be made subject to certain conditions. The authorisation may be withdrawn at any time by an administrative order from the High Commissioner or from his Delegate.

Foreign associations existing at the time of publication of this Decision shall be required to apply, within one month from the date of such publication, for themselves and for each of their establishments, for the authorisation prescribed in Article 1.

Groups having the characteristics of associations and having their principal office abroad shall be deemed to be foreign associations, whatever the form under which they may be disguised as the case may be.

Associations having the characteristics of associations and having their office in Lebanon or Syria which are affiliated with foreign associations or groups, or which are in fact managed by foreigners, or which have either foreign board members or at least one quarter of their members consisting of foreigners, shall also be deemed to be foreign associations. For the purposes of the application of this Decision, associations which, even though Lebanese or Syrian, pursue a political objective extending beyond the Syrian or Lebanese sphere and are linked in their activities to foreign elements shall be deemed to be assimilated to foreign associations.

In order to ensure the application of the preceding Article, the Delegates of the High Commissioner shall be entitled at all times to require the directors of every group or every establishment in Syria or Lebanon to submit to them in writing within one month all information sufficient to determine the principal office to which such groups or establishments belong, their true objective, and the nationality of the members of their board and of their de facto directors.

It shall be a condition for the admissibility of applications for authorisation that there be stated therein the name of the association or establishment, its objective, its place of operation, the name, profession, place of residence and nationality of its members and of the persons who are charged in any capacity whatsoever with carrying out the management of the association or establishment, and its financial resources. Such applications must be accompanied by two copies of the articles of association and internal regulations of the association.

Every amendment to the articles of association or the internal regulations must be authorised in advance by the Delegate of the High Commissioner.

Every change of place of residence and every modification in the composition of the bureau of the association occurring following a resignation, death or any other cause must be notified to the Delegate of the High Commissioner within eight days.

Save for the exceptions provided for in Article 1 of Decision No. 215/LR issued on 14 September 1935, foreigners residing in Lebanon or Syria who join the association must hold the identity card issued to foreigners.

Foreign associations whose authorisation has been refused or withdrawn must immediately cease their activities and proceed with the liquidation of their assets within a period of one month from the date of notification to them of the decision refusing or withdrawing the authorisation.

Foreign associations, whatever the form under which they may be disguised as the case may be, shall be dissolved by operation of law if they fail to apply for authorisation within the conditions specified above. Such dissolution shall be established by an administrative order from the Delegate of the High Commissioner.

The liquidation of the assets of foreign associations whose dissolution is established by the administrative order provided for in the preceding Article shall take place before the court, and the same shall apply to the liquidation of the assets of foreign associations whose authorisation has been refused or withdrawn if such liquidation is not completed within the period specified in Article 9.

The judicial authority shall proceed with the sale of the assets of the groups deemed dissolved pursuant to Article 10, and the proceeds of the sale shall be paid to the charitable associations designated by the authority which decided the dissolution of those groups. As for the case provided for in the second paragraph of Article 11, as well as in the case of dissolution of the association pursuant to its own wish or pursuant to its articles of association, its assets shall be disposed of in accordance with those articles of association, and if there is no provision therein in this respect, they shall be disposed of in accordance with the decision of the general meeting of the members of such association, provided that the assets of the dissolved association may not, pursuant to those articles of association or the decision of the general meeting, be disposed of save for charitable purposes.

Every person who in any capacity whatsoever manages or continues to manage foreign associations or establishments that have not obtained an authorisation, and every person who fails to comply with the order addressed to him in application of Article 5 or who makes false declarations, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from five to three hundred Lebanese or Syrian pounds, or by one of these two penalties only. Every person who, although not carrying out the management of the associations and establishments referred to above, has nevertheless participated in their activities, and every person who in any manner whatsoever contravenes the provisions of this Decision, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from two pounds to one hundred pounds, or by one of these two penalties only.

Offences provided for in this Decision and all other offences relating to the activities of foreign associations shall fall within the jurisdiction of the courts having cognisance of foreign cases, whatever the nationality of the perpetrators of such offences.

This Decision shall apply neither to foreign associations whose sole objective is the performance of religious acts nor to religious associations. The provisions of the Law of 3 August 1325/1909 relating to associations shall apply to foreign associations where they are not contrary to this Decision.

The provisions of Decisions No. 146/LR and 172/LR dated 4 July and 3 August 1934 which are not contrary to this Decision shall likewise apply to foreign youth associations established for the practice of sports activities.
The Secretary-General of the High Commission is charged with the execution of this Decision.

1 - Medical laboratories are institutions that carry out laboratory tests and analyses contributing to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of human diseases.

2 - The work of medical laboratories is divided into branches and is based on the following clinical laboratory sciences:

a - Pathogenic microbiology (bacteria, parasites, viruses, and fungi).

b - Clinical biochemistry.

c - Clinical immunology.

d - Haematology and blood coagulation.

e - Immunohaematology and blood banks.

f - Diseased tissues and cells (pathology).

g - Radioisotope analyses.

3 - A general medical laboratory means a laboratory that carries out the work relating to branches "a - b - c - and d" and a specialised laboratory means a laboratory that carries out the work relating to one of the branches "e - f - g" mentioned in the second paragraph above.

A licence to manage medical laboratories shall be granted only to Lebanese physicians and pharmacists in accordance with the following conditions:

1 - Physicians:

a - That they have completed all the conditions required to obtain the title of specialist in clinical laboratory sciences or in pathology, or in both together, or in nuclear medicine provided for in the Law on the Practice of the Medical Professions, and that they have registered their specialisation with the Ministry of Public Health (hereinafter referred to as the Ministry) and with the Order of Physicians.

b - A physician specialised in clinical laboratory sciences may manage a blood bank in addition to a general laboratory if his specialisation covered that branch, and a physician specialised in clinical laboratory sciences and in pathology may simultaneously manage a general laboratory and a laboratory specialised in diseased tissues and cells, and in both cases the two laboratories must be in one place.

c - A blood bank or a laboratory for diseased tissues and cells may only be managed by physicians specialised in the laboratory sciences relating to these branches.

2 - Pharmacists:

a - Prior to specialisation and during pharmaceutical studies, a pharmacist who wishes to specialise in medical laboratory sciences must have enrolled in a special study programme qualifying for specialisation in these sciences at a university recognised by the Lebanese Government and belonging to a country in which the texts permit pharmacists who are its nationals to manage medical laboratories.

b - After obtaining a pharmacy degree in accordance with the programme mentioned in the preceding paragraph, the pharmacist must pursue specialisation studies in medical laboratory sciences from the theoretical, practical, and clinical aspects for a period of at least four years in an integrated (Integre) university programme recognised by the Lebanese Government and covering branches "a" to "d" mentioned in the second paragraph of Article One of this Legislative Decree.

c - The pharmacist shall register his specialisation with the Ministry in accordance with the conditions followed in the registration of the specialisation of physicians and provided for in the Law on the Practice of the Medical Professions.

d - The pharmacist shall register his specialisation with the Order of Pharmacists after registering it with the Ministry.

e - A specialised pharmacist shall not be permitted to manage a general medical laboratory unless he is registered with the Ministry.

3 - A specialised physician or pharmacist may manage, in addition to a general medical laboratory, a laboratory for testing water, a laboratory for testing toxic substances, or a laboratory for testing foodstuffs if his specialisation covered these branches or one of them, provided that all of these laboratories are in one building.

A private medical laboratory may not be opened except with a permit. The permit shall be granted by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

The categories set out below shall be entitled to submit an application to open a private medical laboratory:

a - Lebanese physicians and pharmacists licensed to manage a medical laboratory, provided that they work full-time in this work, and none of them may own or manage more than one laboratory except as stated in paragraph b (item 1) and item 3) of Article Two of this Legislative Decree, and in all cases no laboratory work may be carried out other than that covered by their licence.

b - Private hospitals, provided that they have contracted with a physician or pharmacist licensed to manage a medical laboratory who works full-time at the hospital.

The laboratories of private hospitals may not carry out laboratory work not covered by the specialisation of their director. In all cases, the licence shall be suspended if the hospital fails to contract with a full-time medical director. The hospital must notify the Ministry immediately in the event of a change of director.

c - Non-profit bodies and institutions, to which the conditions of contracting with a full-time laboratory director shall apply as they do to private hospitals.

d - A partnership of physicians or pharmacists each of whom is licensed to manage a medical laboratory, provided that each one works full-time in the partnership, which shall be entitled to open one laboratory.

Giving lessons only at one of the recognised universities shall not preclude considering the physician or pharmacist as working full-time, provided that the hours of the lessons do not conflict with the working hours at the laboratory. In addition to the name of the responsible director, the address and location of the laboratory shall be stated in the application, and an architectural drawing of the laboratory at a scale of 1/100 shall be attached thereto.

1 - The area of a general medical laboratory must not be less than one hundred square metres within which the spaces necessary to perform the following tasks are available: receiving patients and taking samples from them, the licensed analyses and tests provided that bacteriological analyses are carried out separately from the rest of the analyses, sterilisation, and preparation of the materials used, and the sanitary facilities necessary for patients and for the workers in the laboratory. The technical and sanitary conditions shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

2 - All laboratories licensed prior to the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree must comply with the provisions set out in the first paragraph of this Article within a period not exceeding two years from the date of its entry into force, under pain of revocation of the licence granted to them and their permanent closure, which shall be effected by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

The licence to open a private medical laboratory shall be granted by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry in the name of the person concerned, and this decision shall be recorded in the special register of private medical laboratories.

A permit to open a private blood bank shall only be granted within a medical laboratory in a hospital and solely for the needs of its patients, with the exception of blood banks belonging to the Ministry and public utility institutions specialised in the matter.
It shall not be permissible to open branches for the laboratory work of a licensed laboratory.
The licence holder must notify the Ministry of the date of opening of the laboratory within one month from the date of commencement of its work.

It is prohibited to carry out any laboratory analysis outside officially licensed laboratories, with the exception of:

First - Physicians who, in the course of their medical work, personally and in their clinics carry out certain laboratory work that is considered part of medical work and for which they are not entitled to charge any fee or issue any report.

Second - Official and private health centres licensed by the Ministry, where it is permitted to carry out certain simple routine analyses determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry, provided that they are carried out by a laboratory technician working full-time at the health centre and registered with the Ministry, and that these analyses are free of charge.

Those responsible for medical laboratories shall:

1 - Acquire a numbered register or its equivalent in modern electronic means, in which they record all the examinations they perform, stating the name of the patient, the name of the physician who requested the examination, and adequate instructions regarding the requested examination and its result, and this register shall be kept with the owner of the laboratory and the legal provisions relating to medical secrecy shall apply to it.

2 - Give the written result of the requested examinations pursuant to a report on special printed forms bearing:

a - The name of the laboratory, its address, and the responsible director with his academic titles.

b - The number and date of the license.

c - The number and date of the report.

d - The signature of the responsible person with his name clearly stated.

Those responsible for medical laboratories shall directly notify the treating physician and the Ministry of cases of diseases that they diagnose by means of a laboratory examination and which must be reported in accordance with the list issued by the Ministry.

Those responsible for medical laboratories that include branches of pathogenic microbiology and laboratories that use radioactive isotopes shall take all necessary measures to protect the persons working in these laboratories from infection or exposure to radioactive materials, and they shall also take all measures to prevent the leakage of contamination into sewers, repositories, waste, persons, animals, and objects outside their laboratories in accordance with the conditions determined by the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

The Minister of Public Health shall have the right to close urgently, pursuant to a decision issued by him, any laboratory whose operations result in any danger to public health, and the resumption of work in these laboratories shall not be permitted until after verifying the cessation of this danger.

When a medical laboratory that includes branches of pathogenic microbiology breeds test animals, the room designated for injected animals must be completely independent from the room designated for such breeding.

Physicians exclusively shall have the right to perform on the human body procedures of puncture, incision, and catheterization to obtain a substance for examination or analysis, and other qualified technical persons working in medical laboratories and nurses shall have the right to perform the following acts exclusively:

1 - Taking blood from the arm vein, from the fingers, and from the earlobe.

2 - Taking pus from an abscess open to the outside.

3 - Taking hair and skin scales.

4 - Taking substances from the eyelid, the lower part of the nose, the tonsils, and the external ear.

A licensed laboratory may have a center for collecting samples intended to be examined in any village or town in which there is no laboratory, and it is prohibited to acquire any equipment or devices for analyses, just as it is not permissible to conduct any analyses in this center, and it is not permissible for this center to be within a pharmacy or a physician's clinic, and the opening of a sample collection center shall be subject to an authorization from the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

A person authorized to open a medical laboratory may, during his absence, assign one of his authorized specialist colleagues to supervise his laboratory under his responsibility for a period not exceeding three months after notifying the Ministry thereof. If the period of absence exceeds three months, he must assign a specialist physician or pharmacist who meets all the conditions set forth in this Legislative Decree to carry out the aforementioned task, after obtaining permission therefor from the Ministry, provided that the assignee works full-time. In the event of the death of the owner of the laboratory, his heirs shall have the right to operate the laboratory for a period of three years at most from the date of death, provided that they entrust its management, for the first six months, to an authorized specialist in accordance with the conditions set out in this Legislative Decree, and for the remaining period, to a specialist who does not own or manage a laboratory and who devotes himself full-time to this work, after the approval of the Ministry, and if the deceased owner of the laboratory has an heir who has commenced the study of medicine or pharmacy with a view to specializing in medical laboratory sciences, the Minister of Public Health shall have the right to approve the assignment of an authorized part-time pharmacist or physician to carry out the task of managing the laboratory for the period remaining to complete his study, and this assignment shall be renewed annually.
Anyone who closes his laboratory for a period exceeding six months or permanently, and anyone who changes the address of his laboratory, shall notify the Ministry thereof.

All owners of medical laboratories existing prior to the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree shall notify the Ministry of the address of their laboratory within a period not exceeding three months as of the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree.

The provisions of the first and second articles of this Legislative Decree shall not apply to persons licensed to open a medical laboratory prior to the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree, provided that they are specialist physicians or pharmacists or holders of a doctorate degree in one of the medical laboratory sciences.

Non-Lebanese shall have the right to open and manage a medical laboratory if they meet the conditions stipulated in this Legislative Decree, provided that they are nationals of countries that permit Lebanese to open medical laboratories under the same conditions, and that reciprocity is applied in inverse proportion to the numerical population ratio in Lebanon and in the country to which the license applicant belongs, and that reciprocity is established by an agreement between the Lebanese State and the State concerned, after obtaining a license therefor from the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry, and provided that they are registered as laboratory directors with the Ministry and with the Order of Physicians or of Pharmacists.

Anyone who opens or manages a medical laboratory without meeting the legal conditions shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years or by a fine from five thousand to twenty-five thousand Lebanese pounds, or by one of these two penalties, and the laboratory shall be closed permanently.

The Minister of Public Health shall, by a decision issued by him, without delay, close the laboratory temporarily pending the issuance of the court's decision in this regard.

Every violation of the provisions of the eighth and seventeenth articles of this Legislative Decree shall punish its perpetrator by imprisonment from three months to one year or by a fine from two thousand to ten thousand Lebanese pounds, or by one of these two penalties, in addition to closing the laboratory permanently.

In the event of recidivism, these penalties shall be doubled.

The Minister of Public Health shall, by a decision issued by him, close the laboratory temporarily pending the issuance of the court's decision in this regard.

Every other violation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall punish its perpetrator by a fine from one thousand to five thousand Lebanese pounds. In the event of recidivism, this penalty shall be doubled.

The license to open a laboratory may be withdrawn temporarily or permanently by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry and after hearing the concerned party in this regard, in the following cases:

1 - Loss by the license holder of one of the legal conditions.

2 - Declaration of bankruptcy of the owner of the laboratory, and the license shall be restored to him if the bankruptcy ends with a final composition agreement.

3 - Issuance of a criminal judgment against him on account of an act of his profession that harmed the health of others.
All texts contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Instruments upon which the contracting parties wish to confer, or upon which the law requires to be conferred, the authentic character attached to instruments of public authority shall be authenticated in the territory of the Lebanese Republic by public officers charged with certifying the date thereof, preserving them and issuing copies thereof in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree. Those public officers attached to the Courts of First Instance and to the Magistrates' Courts shall exercise their functions in the capacity of notaries public; they shall not receive from the State any salary or allowance and shall be entitled only to the fees specified in the fifteenth Article of this Legislative Decree. The attached Schedule "A" determines the number of notaries public, their place of residence and their territorial jurisdiction.

Any Lebanese who has attained the age of 25 years, is of good morals and has had no judgment rendered against him may be appointed a notary public by a decision of the Secretary of State. Where applicants for this office do not hold a Licence degree in law, they must sit the special examination for the appointment of judicial assistants provided for in Article 65 of Decision No. 324/L.R. dated 22 November 1939.

Notaries public shall be subject to the disciplinary regime applicable to judicial assistants. Notaries public shall not assume their functions until they have furnished security under conditions to be determined hereafter by decree and have sworn before the President of the Court of First Instance that they will not swerve, in the discharge of the duties of their office, from the path of integrity and honour. A specimen of the signature of the notary public shall be deposited with the registry of the Court of First Instance and with the Directorate of Finance.

Notaries public may not continue to exercise their functions after having attained the full age of sixty, and they may not be transferred or effect an exchange among themselves except after the approval of the Disciplinary Council.

A table of the names of the notaries public, comprising their place of residence, the date of their appointment and the limits of their territorial jurisdiction, shall be posted each year at all seats of the courts and municipalities.
The office of notary public may not be combined with any other judicial or administrative office or any remunerated employment or commerce of any kind whatsoever.

The notary public shall have competence: 1- to authenticate instruments falling within the scope of the Code of Obligations and Contracts and, in general, any instrument not prohibited by law or not falling by virtue of a special provision within the competence of another public officer or official, and to draw up such instruments; 2- to receive all instruments and documents which the two interested parties wish to deposit with the notary public for preservation or for the issue of copies thereof; 3- to establish through the bailiff the refusal to accept payment of bills of exchange and promissory notes and to draw up a protest (protesto) in accordance with the laws in force. 4- to serve all notices through the bailiff and all extrajudicial formal warnings or actual tenders and applications for deposit in accordance with the provisions of Articles 850 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure; 5- to legalise signatures affixed to instruments under private signature and to affix a certain date to deeds presented to him; 6- to instruct bailiffs and officers of the public force to ensure the effecting of all services of process and notices within the scope of his area of jurisdiction or outside it; 7- to receive and register wills drawn up in accordance with the Law of 7 March 1929 and to authenticate them.

The notary public shall not draw up any instrument before verifying the identity of the contracting parties appearing before him. Where the notary public knows the contracting parties personally, he shall state that fact in the instrument; otherwise he must require them to produce their identity cards or passport or the testimony of two known adult witnesses enjoying their civil rights, provided that they are neither spouses, nor servants, nor ascendants, nor descendants of the contracting parties, and that they are not afflicted with the infirmity of muteness and deafness. All of this shall be noted in the instrument. The notary public shall verify the capacity of the contracting parties and their consent given of their own free will, as well as the authority and capacity of the proxy, the heir, the partner, and the representative of a company or association, as well as every person acting in the place of the interested party, and shall state all of this in the instrument.

Where the notary public does not know the language of the contracting parties, he shall receive their declarations through an adult interpreter who shall take an oath before him that he will translate the declarations faithfully, and the interpreter shall sign the instrument in which he participated in that capacity.

The instrument shall be written in Arabic or in French in a clear hand without erasure, addition or interlineation; words struck out for the purpose of cancelling them, as well as words added to the body of the instrument, shall be noted in the margin of the instrument, and such note shall be certified and signed by the notary public, the contracting parties, the witnesses and the interpreters.

The given name, surname, status, profession and place of residence of the contracting parties, of the witnesses certifying identity and of the interpreter shall be stated in the instrument, provided that dates and numbers are written out in full in words.

The notary public shall read out to the contracting parties and the witnesses the instrument which he has drawn up and shall state that fact in the attestation clause, and the notary public, the contracting parties and the witnesses shall affix their signatures at the foot thereof, and the instrument shall then be sealed with the seal of the notary public. Where the instrument is written on several sheets, the number of such sheets fastened to- each other shall be stated in full in words at the foot of the last page and this shall be certified by the contracting parties- and the notaries public, and the same signatures and the same seal shall be placed at the foot of each sheet. Beneath the signature of the notary public, the duties and fees collected shall be stated in detail.

Where one of the contracting parties declares that he does not know how to affix his signature, the notary public shall require him to affix his fingerprint to the instrument and shall note that fact in the attestation clause.
The probative force of instruments drawn up by the notary public shall be the same force as that attached to authentic instruments under the conditions laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure.

The notary public shall collect for the account of the State and in accordance with the procedures laid down in Decree No. 730 dated 13 July 1936 the "notarial duties"; these duties are detailed in Schedule B attached to this Law and constitute the tariff currently in force. These duties do not include the fiscal stamps required to be affixed to instruments. The fees of notaries public for each instrument shall be levied at the rate of twenty per cent of the amount of the duties collected, not including fiscal stamps.

The notary public shall keep in a regular manner registers of a uniform model approved by the Departments of Justice, and these registers shall be supplied successively to the notary public at his own expense whenever the need arises. These registers shall consist of: 1= a daily register = 2 = a register of deposits = 3 = a reference register = 4 = a register of correspondence. In the daily register shall be entered the daily transactions effected by the notary public according to their dates, and therein shall also be entered an abstract of the instruments, the names of the contracting parties and the amount of the duties collected. The register of deposits shall be assigned to the registration of commercial bills of exchange. The purpose of the reference register is to facilitate inspection; therefore the names of the contracting parties shall be entered therein in alphabetical order= the surname, then the given name, then the date of their transactions. The President of the Court to which the notary public is attached shall number and initial the pages of the daily register, the pages of the register of deposits and the pages of the reference register.
The Departments of Finance shall exercise permanent supervision over the keeping of the registers with respect to the supervision and collection of duties.

The notary public is bound to preserve professional secrecy; he must neither disclose the content of the instruments or the names of the contracting parties nor the content of the agreements concluded in his presence, and he must neither accept nor draw up instruments in which he has a personal interest or which contain provisions in the interest of his ascendants howsoever high, his descendants howsoever low, his brother, sister, wife, brother-in-law or son-in-law, or servant, and it shall not be permissible for the notary public to hand over the original copy of any instrument or document delivered to him by way of deposit unless he is ordered to do so by a judicial decision or order, and it shall not be permissible for him to give certified true copies or hand over the content of the instruments except to the interested parties or their heirs, and if he has handed over to the interested parties a first certified true copy in accordance with the conditions provided for in the articles of the Code of Civil Procedure, he may not give them thereafter anything other than duplicate copies (Duplicatas).

The notary public shall be fined a pecuniary fine from ten to fifty Lebanese pounds for every inadvertence or negligence occurring in the drafting of instruments, in the keeping of accounts, and in the collection of fees, and this shall not preclude his prosecution before the judiciary on a claim for compensation for the damages that may have resulted by reason of his fraud or gross fault and the infliction of disciplinary penalties upon him for a serious breach of the duties of the profession. The fine shall be imposed by a decision of the Secretary of State taken upon the proposal of the inspection departments, and the fine shall be collected by the methods followed in the collection of direct taxes.

Notaries public shall not have the right to employ clerks until after the Public Prosecution has investigated their competence and their morals and after the approval of the Secretary of State. The clerks whose admission is approved by the Secretary of State are alone those who may participate in the clerical work of the notary public.

The current notaries public who are practising as of the date this Legislative Decree is put into execution shall remain in their posts to practise within the jurisdiction of the court to which they are appointed, with the exception of those who have reached the age of sixty or upon whom a disciplinary penalty affecting their dignity has been inflicted. The posts of the notaries public who remain in their posts in excess of the number fixed pursuant to this Decree shall be abolished gradually whenever a vacancy occurs in the establishment of notaries public.

The Secretary of State shall have the right to take all measures for the execution of this Legislative Decree, which repeals all previous provisions contrary to it or inconsistent with its provisions.
The execution of this Legislative Decree is entrusted to the Secretary of State.

The owner of the entire built real property may register in the records of the Land Registry Departments the constructions standing on his real property, divided into each unit separately, in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree, whereupon the land of the real property and all the elements and parts, and everything intended for common use, shall be common parts among the owners, and each part intended for private use shall be the property of the person to whom it belongs, subject to the special provisions specified in this Legislative Decree.
The ownership of each part shall be deemed to consist of 2400 shares.

The word building, wherever it appears in this Legislative Decree, shall mean a single building or a group of buildings standing on the real property. The word "real property" shall mean a single real property or a real property complex in accordance with the provisions of the Building Law. In this latter case, the real property unit shall be identified by the smallest number among the numbers of the real properties of which it consists. A building erected on a group of real properties deemed to be a real property unit after the issuance of this Legislative Decree shall not benefit therefrom, unless there is a legal impediment preventing the amalgamation of the real properties of which the unit consists, wholly or partially, with one another to become a single real property.

Each part shall be given a specific number, added to the number of the real property, and a special supplementary real folio shall be assigned to it, on which the entries relating to it shall be recorded in due form.

- The land of the real property and the parts, elements, installations and everything intended for common use among all the owners of the real property shall be deemed a common part among all of them, and shall always be given the number 1.

- The parts, elements, installations and everything intended for common use among a specific group of the owners of the real property shall be deemed a common part among this group, and shall always be given the number 2.

- The parts, elements, installations and everything intended for common use among the group of owners of a single building shall be deemed a common part among this group, and shall always be given the number 3.

- The remaining parts shall be deemed private parts, and shall be numbered consecutively starting from the number 4.

In the case of multiple buildings, each of them shall be identified by a consecutive letter of the Latin alphabet, starting from the first letter, added to the number of the real property and followed by the numbers of the parts from the number 2 upwards in each building as the case may require, in accordance with what is stated in the preceding Article.
Constructions may not be registered as parts unless they are in conformity with the provisions of the building laws.

Common parts shall be such either by their nature or by their allocation:

A- Common parts by their nature shall include, in a particular and mandatory manner:

1- The land of the real property.

2- The structure of the building, the foundations, the supports, the columns and the walls that bear the building or bear the ceilings.

3- The entrances, the facades, the stairs and their shafts.

4- The ventilation ducts and shafts and the chimneys.

5- The elevators.

6- The top roofs in accordance with the provisions of the building laws.

B - And common parts by their allocation shall include everything intended for common use, and in particular the following elements:

1- Tunnels, cavities and garages.

2- Roads, courtyards, open spaces, gardens, passages and walkways of all kinds.

3- Sports and tourist installations, installations intended for recreation and the like.

4- Conduits and installations of all kinds.

5- Doorkeepers' rooms. And all equipment and appliances that provide common services and the places in which these things are located.

These elements shall be distributed among common parts 1, 2 and 3 in the real property management regulations provided for hereinafter according to the situation and as the case may require - and it is prohibited to register the common part in the Land Register otherwise.
Partitions or walls that separate two or more parts, and which are not deemed to be part of the structure of the building, shall be common between the parts that they separate from one another.

The elements of each private part must be connected to one another, and if there exist for this part constructed elements annexed to it, which are however separate from it, they may be registered as independent parts whose ownership follows the ownership of the private part, and they cannot be disposed of or have rights established over them independently of the principal part.

The ownership of the common parts shall be deemed ancillary to the ownership of the private parts, and consequently they are not susceptible of division or partition and no rights can be established over them independently of the private parts to which they are annexed.

For the purpose of regulating the use of the unconstructed common part, the Owners' Association alone may designate this by indicating it on a copy of the map of the common part which shall be annexed to the regulations as an amendment thereto and noted therein.

Each owner shall have the right, within the conditions of the regulations, to use the common part for that for which it was intended, provided that this does not prevent the use by the remaining owners. And no owner may carry out any act likely to threaten the safety of the building or to alter its shape or external appearance.

No modification may be made to the common part, even upon renovation of the building, and to anything that is necessary for the harmony and uniformity of the building, even if it is of the non-common parts, such as entrance doors, windows, balconies and others, except by a decision issued by the Association by a majority of at least 75% of the votes of the owners.

Where the number of private lots is three or more, and likewise in the case described in Article 15 of this Legislative Decree, there shall be attached to the application for registration by-laws for the management of the property, consisting of the following documents, duly authenticated before a Notary Public:

A- A schedule showing the following matters in a separate column for each:

1- The number of the property.

2- The cadastral district.

3- The numbers of the lots in sequence.

4- The designation of the building in which the lot is situated, where applicable.

5- The floor, where applicable (the designation shall be taken from the building permit).

6- The contents of the lot, its appurtenances, and the lots dependent thereon, in accordance with what is set forth in Articles 9 and 10.
