Where a person is prosecuted simultaneously for an offence falling within the jurisdiction of the Military Court and for another offence falling within the jurisdiction of the ordinary courts, he shall be referred first before the court competent to hear the offence carrying the more severe penalty, and where the two offences are punishable by the same penalty, the accused shall be tried first for the offence falling within the jurisdiction of the Military Court. The court hearing the offence for which he is tried last shall pronounce all the penalties or their merger.

The Military Court shall rule only on the public prosecution, save that it shall be entitled to order the restitution of seized items and incriminating items to their owners where such items are not required to be confiscated pursuant to the law. The action for personal damages shall be brought before the civil courts, and judgment in such action shall not be rendered until after judgment has been rendered in the public prosecution.

Where it is necessary to designate the competent authority to hear a case, upon the occurrence of a negative or positive conflict of jurisdiction between the Military Courts and the ordinary courts, the matter shall be referred ex officio by the Public Prosecution to the First Chamber of the Court of Appeal, which shall decide thereon in council chamber after hearing the submissions of the Public Prosecution and without the presence of the two parties. The decision issued in this respect shall not be open to debate before the designated authority.

A complaint or denunciatory notice relating to offences committed by a serviceman against a serviceman shall be submitted to the Supreme Commander of the Army, who must refer it to the Government Commissioner together with the authorisation to prosecute. That shall be without prejudice to the disciplinary penalties imposed by the military authorities. In all other cases, the complaint or denunciatory notice shall be submitted directly to the Government Commissioner.
In the case of an offence committed in flagrante delicto, the Government Commissioner shall be entitled to take cognisance of the case, whoever the perpetrators of the offence and the victims may be.

The Government Commissioner shall inform the Supreme Commander of the Army as soon as possible of all cases of which he has taken cognisance directly or pursuant to a complaint or denunciatory notice.

The unit commander or the head of service shall attach to the complaint or denunciatory notice: 1- A detailed report on the circumstances that accompanied the incident. 2- The service record 3- A list of administrative disciplinary penalties.

In the case of default in reporting for duty, the complaint shall be drawn up by the officer who is head of the recruitment service. This officer shall attach to the complaint: 1- A copy of the enlistment contract 2- A copy of the travel order and of the return of service thereof. 3- A copy of the documents showing that the defaulting person did not arrive at the appointed time at the place assigned to him. 4- A statement of the circumstances that accompanied the default. 5- The description sheet.

In the case of desertion, the complaint shall be drawn up by the commander of the unit or detachment to which the deserting serviceman belongs, and there shall be attached to the complaint, in addition to the matters set forth in Article 58: 1- A schedule of the weapons, kit, military items and animals that are the property of the Army and that the deserter took with him, indicating, where applicable, what has been returned of those items. 2- The investigation records drawn up after the declaration of desertion. 3- The record showing, where applicable, the return or arrest of the deserter.

Where the offender is a serviceman, a person assimilated to military personnel, or a civil employee in the Army, the Government Commissioner shall inform the unit commander or the head of service of the decision to file without further action, the decision to prosecute, the warrants issued, the decisions of release on bail, the decisions of dismissal of proceedings, and the final judgment. This shall be effected through the Supreme Commander of the Army.
The Government Commissioner shall be entrusted with the prosecution of accused persons referred before the Military Courts.

Where a preliminary investigation has been conducted in the case, the Government Commissioner shall forthwith serve the order of committal upon the accused persons and shall likewise serve upon them the bill of indictment in felony matters.

The Government Commissioner shall serve the summonses to appear upon the accused persons at least three days prior to the sitting; there shall be entered in the summons to appear the legal provisions and the names of the witnesses called by the public prosecution.
The accused shall submit, at least one day prior to the date of the sitting, a list of the names of the witnesses whom he requests the court to hear.

Where the Public Prosecution and the accused request the hearing of witnesses who have not been designated in accordance with the manner set forth in the preceding Articles, such witnesses may only be heard with the approval of the President of the Court.
Summonses to appear and all other documents set forth in the preceding Articles shall be served through process-servers, the Gendarmerie and all other officers of the public force.

The trial before the Military Court shall be public, on pain of nullity. Nevertheless, the Court shall be entitled to decide to conduct it in camera in accordance with the ordinary law, but the judgment shall in all cases be pronounced in public. The Military Court may prohibit the publication of the proceedings of the sittings or a summary thereof where it deems that the case requires such a measure. Paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 6 of Article 420 and Article 421 of the Penal Code shall apply before the Military Courts.
The President of the Court shall maintain order during the sitting.
Accused persons released on bail in felony matters shall surrender themselves into custody at the registry of the Military Court prior to the hour appointed for the opening of the sitting.

The President shall order the accused to be brought in, and he shall attend the trial free and unfettered, guarded by a sufficient force and accompanied by his counsel. The accused must raise his objection as to jurisdiction and the nullity of prior proceedings as soon as he is interrogated, on pain of inadmissibility.

The President may order that the accused be removed from the sitting and returned to prison if he causes an uproar or commits any other act liable to disturb the peace of the sitting and obstruct the course of the trial, and the sitting shall proceed as though the accused were present.

The President shall order the clerk to read out the order of committal, the bill of indictment and all other documents that he deems necessary for the Court to examine. Each member of the Court shall be given a copy of the order of committal and of the bill of indictment in all felony cases, and in misdemeanour cases which the Government Commissioner deems to call for such a measure by reason of their importance or difficulty. Thereafter, the Court shall examine, where applicable, the objections raised in accordance with the provisions of Article 71 as to jurisdiction or the nullity of proceedings.

The trial shall be conducted in accordance with the rules of procedure provided for in the ordinary law for felony cases if the offence is a felony, and for misdemeanour cases if the offence is a misdemeanour.

As soon as the President declares the trial closed, he shall state the questions that will be put to the judges ex officio or at the request of the Public Prosecution or the defence, whether such questions are drawn from the indictment decision or from what emerged during the trial. The Government Commissioner and the accused or his counsel may submit such observations as they see fit regarding the questions stated.

The judges shall retire to the deliberation room, whereupon they shall, in principle, neither communicate with any person nor separate before the judgment is rendered, and they shall deliberate and vote in the absence of the Government Commissioner and the clerk after carefully examining the documents of the case. However, they shall not be entitled to rely upon documents that have not been submitted to public debate.
In important or complex cases, the Court may adjourn until the next day the continuation of deliberation and the rendering of judgment.

The President shall put the questions regarding each of the accused in accordance with the following order: 1- Is the accused the perpetrator of the act attributed to him? 2- Did the act occur under one of the circumstances that constitute an excuse pursuant to the law? 3- Are there aggravating circumstances? If the accused has attained the age of eighteen years, the President shall put the following question: Did the accused commit the act with awareness and discernment? Voting on these questions shall take place by secret ballot. Each of the members shall express his opinion by placing in the ballot box a slip bearing one of these two words: "Yes" or "No", and the result shall be taken by a majority.

If the accused is declared responsible for the offence attributed to him, the President shall ask whether there are mitigating circumstances. Thereafter, the Court shall deliberate on the determination of the penalty. Each of the judges shall be called upon to express his opinion, beginning with the youngest judge, and the President shall express his opinion last. The penalty shall be determined by a majority, and if no penalty obtains a majority, the penalty shall be determined by taking the middle limit of the penalties proposed by the majority that is in favour of the accused. The Court may, after determining the penalty, decide to stay the execution thereof in accordance with the provisions of Articles 169 and 170 of the Penal Code and under the conditions provided for in the said Code.

In the case of material concurrence of offences and in the case of recidivism, the penalties handed down by the Military Courts shall be deemed equivalent to the penalties handed down by the ordinary courts.
The President shall read out the judgment in a public sitting in the absence of the accused.
The judgment rendered shall be enforceable forthwith, except in the case of a sentence of death.

All formalities required by law shall be mentioned in the judgment, and neither the answers of the accused nor the testimonies of the witnesses shall be included therein. The judgment shall contain the operative part of the judgments rendered regarding jurisdiction, nullity, and other defences and incidental pleas, and shall set forth therein: 1- The names of the judges and their ranks 2- The name of the accused, his nationality, his surname, his age, his occupation, and his place of residence 3- The misdemeanour or felony for which he was referred before the Military Court. 4- The taking of the oath by the witnesses 5- The submissions of the Government Commissioner 6- The questions put and the decisions taken in accordance with the provisions of Articles 78 and 79 7- A mention of the articles relied upon, without there being a need to set out the text thereof: 8- That the sittings were public, or a mention of the decision ordering that they be held in camera. 9- That the judgment was read out publicly. The President, the members, and the clerk shall sign the judgment forthwith.

The clerk shall read out the judgment to the accused by order of the Government Commissioner and in his presence and the presence of the guard under arms. He shall draw up a record of all the foregoing, which shall be signed by him and by the Government Commissioner.

If the accused appears at the beginning of the sitting and thereafter fails to attend, the trial shall be deemed adversarial with respect to him unless there is an established force majeure preventing his attendance.
Judgments rendered in absentia by the Permanent Military Court in felonies and misdemeanours shall have the effects provided for in the ordinary law.
Opposition to such judgments shall be subject to the rules of procedure provided for in the ordinary law.
The rules of procedure provided for in the ordinary law shall apply to applications for retrial submitted regarding judgments rendered by the Military Courts.
The Minister of National Defence shall be vested with the powers vested in the Minister of Justice regarding retrial.

Every person who commits the offence of default of appearance set forth in the Conscription Law shall be punished in time of peace by imprisonment from one month to one year, and in time of war by imprisonment from two years to five years. If the offender is an officer, he shall, in addition thereto, be punished by dismissal, in time of war, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and these penalties shall not preclude the application of the special provisions provided for in the Conscription Law.

There shall be deemed a deserter within the country in time of peace: 1- Every serviceman who absents himself from his unit or detachment without leave and six days have elapsed from the date of verification of his desertion. However, a serviceman who does not have three months in service shall not be deemed a deserter until after an absence of one month. 2- Every serviceman who travels from one unit to another, or from one post to another, or whose leave expires and who does not return to his unit or detachment within nine days from the date fixed for his return. A serviceman, a person of equivalent status to servicemen, or a civilian employee in the Army who deserts within the country in time of peace shall be punished from six months to five years. If the offender is an officer, he shall be punished by this penalty and, in addition thereto, by the penalty of dismissal. The penalty shall not be less than one year in any of the following circumstances: 1- If the deserter takes with him a piece of his weapons, or an item of equipment, clothing, gear, or animals, or anything belonging to the Army. 2- If he deserts during hours of duty or in the presence of insurgents. 3- If he has previously deserted before. In time of war, two-thirds of the periods provided for in this Article shall be reduced, and the penalty may be increased up to double.

Every serviceman who crosses the Lebanese borders without leave, or leaves the unit to which he belongs and joins a foreign country, after the lapse of three days from the verification of his desertion, shall be deemed a deserter to a foreign country in time of peace. This period shall become one day in time of war. A serviceman who deserts to a foreign country shall be punished by imprisonment from two years to five years. If he is an officer, he shall be punished by temporary detention, and if he is granted mitigating circumstances and is punished by imprisonment, he shall, in addition thereto, be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal. The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased up to ten years if the serviceman deserts to a foreign country under the following circumstances: 1- If the deserter takes with him a piece of his weapons, or an item of equipment, clothing, gear - and animals, or anything belonging to the Army. 2- If he deserts during hours of duty or in the presence of insurgents. 3- If he has previously deserted before 4- If he deserts in time of war, or in a territory in a state of war, or in an area in which martial law has been declared. If the deserter is an officer, he shall be punished by the maximum penalty of temporary detention, and if he is granted mitigating circumstances and is punished by imprisonment, he shall, in addition thereto, be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal.

Every serviceman who commits the offence of desertion to the enemy shall be punished by death with military degradation. If the desertion takes place before the enemy, he shall be punished by temporary detention. If the deserter is an officer, he shall be punished by temporary hard labour and shall, in addition thereto, be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal in all cases.

Every desertion committed by two or more servicemen after their agreement thereon shall be deemed desertion by conspiracy. The leader of the conspiracy to desert to a foreign country shall be punished by temporary detention. If he is an officer, by temporary hard labour. The leader of the conspiracy to desert within the country shall be punished by imprisonment from five to ten years. The other offenders shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to five years if the desertion is within the country, and if it is to a foreign country, the penalty shall be doubled. In time of war, there shall be punished by death with military degradation: 1- Whoever deserts by conspiracy before the enemy. 2- The leader of the conspiracy to desert to a foreign country. If the deserter is an officer, in addition to the penalties provided for in this Article, he shall be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal even if the penalty imposed does not include military degradation. A serviceman who has engaged the enemy, who is about to engage him, or who is exposed to his attacks shall be deemed "before the enemy".

If a judgment in absentia is issued against a deserter to the enemy or a deserter in the presence of the enemy, or against a deserter or a defaulter who has joined a foreign country and remained therein in wartime in order to evade his military duties, the court shall rule in favour of the Treasury for the confiscation of all his property of whatever kind, present and future, movable and immovable, undivided and divided. The judgment ordering confiscation shall be sent forthwith to the President of the Civil Court having jurisdiction over the convicted person's last domicile or last place of residence. The President of the Court shall issue a decision appointing a custodian for the confiscated property to undertake its preservation and administration under the supervision of the President. During the custodianship, an allowance may be granted to the needy wife or wives, children, and parents of the convicted person. The allowance shall be granted by a decision of the President of the Civil Court. If six months elapse from the date of the declaration of the end of the war and the convicted person has not appeared, all his property shall be sold in accordance with the procedures prescribed for the sale of State property. ' Schedule of Weapons of War First Category Weapons, ammunition, and equipment manufactured and intended solely for land, sea, or air warfare A- Weapons, ammunition, and equipment manufactured and intended solely for land, sea, or air warfare which are included or which shall be included in the future in the armament of the armed forces of any State, or the use of which has been discontinued, provided that they remain capable of military use and are not used for any other purpose. Weapons, ammunition, and equipment to which the above definition applies, but which fall within another category, shall be excluded. These weapons, ammunition, and equipment are divided into the following sections: 1- Rifles and carbines. 2- a- Machine guns, automatic rifles, and submachine guns of all calibres. b - Machine gun mounts. c- Interrupter gears for firing through a propeller. 3- Projectiles and ammunition specific to the weapons mentioned in numbers 1 and 2 above. 4- Gun-sighting apparatus, including aerial sights for firing and bomb-dropping, and fire-control apparatus. 5- a- Long and short cannons and howitzers of a calibre of less than 15 centimetres (5.9 inches) b - Long and short cannons and howitzers of a calibre equal to or exceeding 15 centimetres (5.9 inches) c- Mortars of all models d- Gun carriages, rifle mounts, recoil mechanisms, and accessories for mounting the same. 6- Projectiles and ammunition for the weapons mentioned in number 5 above. 7- Apparatus and appliances for throwing bombs, torpedoes, depth charges, and other types of projectiles. In the cases set forth in the first paragraph of the preceding Article, neither the public prosecution nor the penalty imposed shall be subject to limitation of time.

All persons who conceal or embezzle, or participate in concealing or embezzling, the property of the convicted person shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine from 100 to 500 Lebanese pounds, or by one of these two penalties. Without prejudice to the rights of third parties acting in good faith, all contracts and acts executed in violation of the provisions of this Article shall be null and void. If any of these acts are committed by the custodian entrusted with preserving such property, the penalty shall be doubled and he shall be ordered to restituate what he had concealed or embezzled.

Every person who incites to desertion or facilitates the same, whatever the means used by him, and whether or not his act has produced an effect, shall be punished by the penalty prescribed for the deserter in the cases set forth in this Law

Every person who conceals a deserter or performs any act calculated to prevent the conduct of legal prosecutions, having knowledge of the matter, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.
The penalties prescribed for the offence of desertion shall apply to a deserter belonging to an allied army fighting against a common enemy.

The following shall be deemed to be in a state of mutiny: 1- Military personnel under arms who assemble to the number of at least four and, acting in concert, refuse to obey the orders of their superiors upon the first warning. 2- Military personnel who assemble to the number of at least four, take up arms without permission, and act contrary to the orders of their superiors. 3- Military personnel who, to the number of at least four, engage in violence while using arms and refuse the call of their superiors to disperse and return to order. Mutinous military personnel shall be punished by imprisonment from two to five years in the circumstances set forth in the first paragraph, by imprisonment from three to five years in the circumstances set forth in the second paragraph, and by imprisonment from five to ten years in the circumstances set forth in the third paragraph. Instigators of mutiny and the military personnel highest in rank shall be punished by temporary hard labour in the first case, and by the maximum penalty of temporary hard labour in the other two cases. Furthermore, the penalty of dismissal shall be imposed upon officers convicted pursuant to this Article, even where military degradation does not result ipso jure from the penalty imposed. If the mutiny takes place in a territory in a state of war or in an area in which martial law has been declared, the maximum penalty of imprisonment must always be imposed. If the mutiny takes place in the presence of the enemy and in the case set forth in the third paragraph of this Article, the penalties prescribed in the second and third paragraphs of the following Article shall be imposed.

Every military person who refuses to obey his superiors and to execute the orders he receives, where no force majeure prevents the execution thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years. Every military person who refuses to obey when ordered to march against the enemy, or to perform any other service ordered by his superior in the presence of the enemy, shall be punished by death with military degradation. Every military person who refuses to obey in the presence of rebels shall be punished by temporary detention, and furthermore the penalty of dismissal shall be imposed upon an officer even where military degradation does not result ipso jure from the penalty imposed.

Every military person who, while armed, commits violence against a sentry or a lookout with intent to prevent him from fulfilling the mission entrusted to him shall be punished by temporary hard labour. If the violence is committed while he is unarmed, but accompanied by one or several persons, he shall be punished by imprisonment from one to five years. If he commits the violence while alone and unarmed, he shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to five years. The maximum penalty prescribed in each of the three cases set forth above shall be imposed if the violence takes place in wartime, or in a territory in a state of war, or in an area in which martial law has been declared, or if it takes place inside an arms or ammunition depot or a fortress, or on the approaches to such places. In addition to the penalties set forth in this Article, the penalty of dismissal shall be imposed upon a convicted officer even where military degradation does not result ipso jure from the penalty imposed.

Every serviceman who intentionally and by any means whatsoever sets fire to, demolishes, or destroys buildings or edifices, or railways, or telegraph and telephone lines and centres, or aviation centres, or ships, vessels, and boats, or any immovable property belonging to the Army or used in national defence, shall be punished by death with military degradation. Moreover, an officer shall in all cases be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal if the convicted person is granted mitigating circumstances and is sentenced to a penalty other than death.

Every serviceman who intentionally attempts to burn, demolish, or destroy, in time of war or in the presence of insurgents, buildings, edifices, railways, telegraph and telephone lines, ships, vessels, boats, and any immovable property belonging to the Army or used in national defence, shall be punished by hard labour for life. If the offence takes place other than in time of war or in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be temporary hard labour. If an officer is sentenced to imprisonment as a result of being granted mitigating circumstances, he shall, in addition, be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal.

Every serviceman who, for a criminal purpose, by himself or through another, destroys means of defence, war materiel, weapons, ammunition, provisions, equipment, clothing, and any movable property belonging to the Army or used in national defence, shall be punished by temporary hard labour. If the destruction occurs in time of war or in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be hard labour for life. If an officer is sentenced to imprisonment as a result of being granted mitigating circumstances, he shall, in addition, be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal.

Every serviceman who intentionally destroys, breaks, or disables weapons, materiel, equipment, clothing, animals, and any property belonging to the Army, whether entrusted to him or to another, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years.

Every serviceman who intentionally destroys, burns, or tears up registers and other official papers belonging to the military authorities shall be punished by temporary detention in a fortress. If the offender is an officer and is sentenced only to imprisonment as a result of being granted mitigating circumstances, he shall, in addition, be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal or loss of rank.

Every sentry or lookout who leaves his post before completing the mission entrusted to him shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to one year. If the sentry or lookout is in the presence of insurgents, he shall be punished by temporary detention in a fortress. If he is in the presence of the enemy, he shall be punished by death. If the offence occurs in a territory in a state of war or in an area in which martial law has been declared, but not in the presence of the enemy or in the presence of insurgents, the offender shall be punished by imprisonment from two years to five years.

Every serviceman who sleeps while performing the duty of guard and lookout shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to six months. If the offence occurs in the presence of the enemy or in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be from two years to five years, and if it occurs in a territory in a state of war or in an area in which martial law has been declared, and it is not in the presence of the enemy or in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be imprisonment from six months to one year.

Every serviceman who leaves the post of his duty shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to six months. The post of duty means the place where the serviceman is present pursuant to the order of his superiors to perform the mission entrusted to him. If the abandonment of the post occurs in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be imprisonment from five to ten years. If it occurs in a territory in a state of war or in an area in which martial law has been declared, the penalty shall be from two years to five years. If the abandonment of the post occurs in the presence of the enemy, the offending serviceman shall be punished by death. The maximum penalty shall always be imposed if the offender is the commander of the post.

Every serviceman who violates the general instructions given to his unit or the instructions the execution of which was entrusted to him personally, or rebels against the instructions given to another serviceman, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years. The penalty shall be raised to five years if the offence occurs in the presence of insurgents, or inside a fortress, a military unit, or a weapons or ammunition depot, or in a territory in a state of war, or in an area in which martial law has been declared.

Every serviceman who intentionally renders himself unfit for service, temporarily or permanently, in order to evade his military duties, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to five years. He shall be punished by death if he commits the offence while in the presence of the enemy, and by temporary detention in a fortress if he commits it while in a territory in a state of war, or in an area in which martial law has been declared, or in the presence of insurgents. An attempt shall be punished as the offence itself. Military accomplices shall be punished by the same penalty as the offender, and if they are doctors, physicians, medical officers, or pharmacists, the penalty of imprisonment and temporary detention in a fortress shall be doubled. In addition, a fine from 1000 to 3000 Lebanese pounds shall be imposed on offenders who are not servicemen or persons assimilated to servicemen. If the offender is an officer and is sentenced only to imprisonment as a result of being granted mitigating circumstances, he shall, in addition, be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal.

Every serviceman who is duly summoned to take part in the composition of the Military Court and refuses to do so without a legitimate excuse shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to six months.

Every commander of a military region who is referred to the court and is proved to have surrendered to the enemy the position entrusted to him without having exhausted all the means of defence at his disposal and without having done everything that duty and honour command shall be punished by death with military degradation.

Every commander of an armed unit who capitulates in the field of battle shall be punished: 1- By death with military degradation if the capitulation leads to the cessation of fighting, or if, prior to communicating with the enemy in writing or orally, he did not do everything that duty and honour command. 2- By dismissal in all other cases.

Every Lebanese serviceman, or serviceman in the service of Lebanon, who bears arms against Lebanon shall be punished by death with military degradation. Every prisoner of war who is captured anew after having broken his parole and borne arms shall be punished by death. Every Lebanese serviceman who is in the service of Lebanon and falls into the hands of the enemy, and regains his freedom from him on condition that he not bear arms against him thereafter, shall be punished by imprisonment from three to five years. If the offender is an officer, he shall, in addition, be punished by the penalty of dismissal. In all cases, deprivation of political and civil rights shall be imposed.

The following shall be punished by death with military degradation: 1- Every serviceman who delivers to the enemy, or in the interest of the enemy, the troops under his command, or the position entrusted to him, or the provisions of the Army, or the maps of military positions, factories, ports, and docks, or the password, or the secret of military operations, campaigns, and negotiations 2- Every serviceman who establishes relations with the enemy in order to facilitate his operations. 3- Every serviceman who participates in conspiracies intended to bring pressure to bear upon the decisions of the responsible military commander. 4- Every serviceman who incites to flight or prevents the rallying of fugitives.

The following shall be deemed a spy and punished by death with military degradation: Every serviceman who enters a military position, or a military centre and military establishment, or a military workshop, or a camp or bivouac, or any premises of the Army in order to obtain documents and information for the benefit of the enemy. 2- Every serviceman who gives the enemy documents and information liable to harm military operations or to prejudice the safety of positions, centres, and other military establishments. 3- Every serviceman who conceals, by himself or through another, while being aware of the matter, spies or enemies sent for reconnaissance.
Every enemy [literally: number] who enters in disguise into the places set forth in the preceding article shall be punished by death

The penalties prescribed in Book I, Title II of this Law relating to military felonies and misdemeanours shall apply to persons assimilated to military personnel and to civilian employees in the Army, with the exception of the provisions of Article 160, which shall apply solely to military personnel to the exclusion of all others.

The provisions of this Law shall apply to offences committed prior to its publication, provided that the penalty imposed shall not exceed the maximum penalty that should have been imposed under the previous laws.

The modalities for the application of this Law shall be regulated by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers

The Ottoman Military Penal Code is repealed, the last paragraph of Article 18 of the Penal Code is repealed, the Law issued on 12 October 1945 is repealed with the exception of Article 21 thereof, the provisions of which shall remain in force temporarily, and all other provisions contrary to this Law that are incompatible with its content are repealed.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette.

Any person who incites military personnel to join the enemy or the rebels, or knowingly facilitates the means for them to do so, or recruits in favour of a state that is at war with Lebanon, shall be deemed a recruiter in favour of the enemy and shall be punished by death. Where the offender is a member of the military, he shall, in addition, be punished by military degradation.

Every member of the military who publicly and without right wears a decoration, rosette or insignia of the Lebanese decorations, rosettes and insignia, or wears a uniform or attire of the Lebanese military uniforms and attire, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

Every member of the military who wears a decoration, rosette or badge of foreign decorations, rosettes and insignia without or being authorised to wear it in advance by the Lebanese authorities shall be punished by the same penalty.

The preceding Article shall apply in time of war to any person who publicly and without right uses, in combat zones, the insignia of the Red Cross, its flag or its emblem, or the insignia, flags and emblems assimilated thereto.

Military degradation is an accessory felony penalty to the penalty of death, hard labour, detention, banishment and compulsory residence imposed upon a member of the military in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and military degradation is an inevitable consequence of civic degradation and results in: 1- Loss of rank and the right to wear the attire and carry the insignia pertaining thereto. 2- Dismissal from the army and the other matters set forth in Article 49 of the Penal Code. 3- Permanent deprivation of every retirement pension and of every gratuity for prior services, which shall be deemed null and void and of no account. The right to recover deductions paid during prior services shall also lapse. Every judgment imposing military degradation shall be mentioned in the Order of the Day.

Removal from office is an accessory misdemeanour penalty that applies only to officers and entails the loss of rank and status and the right to wear the attire and carry the insignia pertaining to both. A removed officer forfeits his rights to every retirement pension and to every gratuity for prior services, which shall be deemed null and void and of no account, and he also forfeits the right to- recover deductions paid by him during his prior services.

Loss of rank is an accessory misdemeanour penalty to certain penalties exclusively specified by the law. Loss of rank has the effects of removal from office save that it does not deprive of the right to a retirement pension and to a gratuity for prior services. Loss of rank is entailed by a conviction of any holder of a military rank for a felony or for one of the misdemeanours provided for in Articles 471, 635 to 648, 649, 655, 665 and 670 of the Penal Code, whichever court rendered it, whether or not demotion and removal from office were ordered, and whether or not mitigating circumstances were granted. Loss of rank is also entailed by a conviction imposing a misdemeanour penalty of imprisonment with total or partial deprivation of political and civil rights.
A judgment imposing, under the circumstances set forth in the preceding Article, a penalty of imprisonment exceeding three years shall ipso jure entail dismissal from the army.

With respect to ordinary felonies and misdemeanours, whoever their perpetrator may be, the military courts shall apply the principal, supplementary and accessory penalties provided for in the Penal Code. With respect to military personnel, they shall apply the accessory penalties provided for in Chapter Twelve of Title One of Book Two of this Law.
With the exception of a sentence of death, judgments rendered by the military courts shall be enforceable forthwith.

In the event of a sentence of death, the case shall be submitted to the Office of the Presidency of the Republic through the Minister of National Defence with such observations as he sees fit, after consulting the opinion of the Standing Pardons Committee.
A penalty of death imposed by the military courts shall be executed by firing squad.
The Minister of National Defence shall decide where the penalties imposed by the military courts must be executed: in ordinary prisons or in special prisons.
The period of remand in custody in its entirety shall be included in the calculation of the penalty imposed.

The period during which a person was deprived of his liberty shall be deemed remand in custody, and the period during which a person was deprived of his liberty pursuant to a disciplinary measure taken against him for the same reason shall be included in the calculation of remand in custody.

Where the case results in a conviction, the period during which the convicted person was held in remand in custody or under disciplinary detention shall not be included in the calculation of the period of his military service.

The Minister of National Defence may decide to stay the execution of a judgment for reasons relating to the public interest and after the approval of the Council of Ministers. The stay of execution may cover the accessory penalties in whole or in part, and in such case this must be expressly stated in the decision ordering the stay of execution.
The Minister of National Defence may, after the approval of the Council of Ministers, revoke at any time his decision ordering the stay of execution.

The period spent by the convicted person in service during general mobilisation shall be deducted from the penalty imposed the execution of which has been stayed. The revocation of the decision ordering the stay of execution shall entail the execution of the remaining penalty.

Judgments imposing penalties provided for in this Law the execution of which has been stayed shall be deemed null and void and of no account if the convicted person is not sentenced anew to a penalty of imprisonment or a more severe penalty within a period of one year in contraventions, three years in misdemeanours and ten years in felonies starting from the date of the stay of execution.

The Government Commissioner shall notify, through the Supreme Commander of the Army, the commander of the unit or the head of the department to which the convicted person belongs of all decisions relating to the execution of judgments rendered against military personnel, persons assimilated to military personnel, and civilian employees in the army.
Every penalty of imprisonment exceeding three months imposed upon military personnel shall entail compulsory labour.

In all cases not provided for in this Law, the military courts shall apply the penal laws and the procedures provided for in the ordinary law or in special laws in all that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

When the provisions of the ordinary law and special laws are applied in accordance with the preceding Article, military personnel, persons assimilated to military personnel, and employees in the army shall be deemed as ordinary public servants with respect to offences committed by them and committed against them during the performance of duty or on the occasion of the performance of duty.

Where the acts provided for in this Law constitute, by reason of the circumstances in which they were committed or by reason of the consequences to which they led, an offence carrying a more severe penalty in the Penal Code, they shall be punished by the penalty provided for in the said Code.

An employer is any natural or legal person who employs a wage-earner pursuant to a written or oral contract of employment, in return for a wage, even if such wage is in kind or a share in the profits."

A wage-earner is any man, woman or juvenile who works for a wage with an employer under the conditions set forth in the First Article, on a full-time, part-time or seasonal basis, in person or remotely, and even if he uses his own equipment and fittings to perform the work."

Wage-earners are divided into salaried employees and workmen:

- A salaried employee is any wage-earner who performs clerical work or non-manual work

- And a workman is any wage-earner who does not fall within the category of salaried employees.

- As for temporary or daily-paid trainees, they are considered to be in the category of salaried employees if they perform work customarily entrusted to salaried employees,

- And in the category of workmen if they perform work other than that.

- And a trainee is any wage-earner who is still in the stage of training and has not yet acquired in his trade the experience of a full-fledged wage-earner.

A syndicate is a group of wage-earners or employers or craftsmen who belong to one of the categories provided for in the following Article and are united in an association whose conditions are defined in Title Four of this Law.

Syndicates are divided into four major categories:

1- Industrial syndicates

2- Commercial syndicates

3- Agricultural syndicates

4- Syndicates of the liberal professions

A workshop industry is any industry or profession in which its owner works by himself and without being under the management of another employer, whether he has wage-earners or not, provided that the number of these does not exceed fifteen wage-earners including the members of the family of the master of the workshop.

The following are exempted from the provisions of this Law.

1- Domestic servants in the homes of individuals

2- Agricultural syndicates that have no connection with commerce and industry, and special legislation shall be enacted for these syndicates.

3- Establishments in which only family members work under the management of the father, the mother, or the guardian.

4- Government administrations and municipal bodies with respect to daily-paid and temporary salaried employees and wage-earners who are not covered by the civil servants' regulations, and special legislation shall be enacted for them.

All employers and wage-earners shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, except those exempted among them by a special provision; and establishments with their various commercial and industrial branches, their annexes, and their national and foreign kinds, whether public or private, secular or religious, including national and foreign educational establishments and charitable establishments, shall also be subject to it, as shall foreign companies that have a commercial centre, a branch, or an agency in the country.

Every natural or legal person who employs under this Law any number whatsoever of wage-earners in one of the establishments referred to in the preceding Article must submit a declaration concerning them to the Department of Social Affairs within two months starting from the publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, and must attach to this declaration rules of employment for the wage-earners consistent with the provisions of this Law with respect to all enterprises that employ more than 25 wage-earners. A declaration must be submitted in advance regarding new establishments within a period of two months from the date of their foundation, and all establishments must also submit the declaration in the following cases:

1- If one of the establishments referred to in the preceding Article intends to employ any number whatsoever of wage-earners.

2- If an establishment ceases to employ wage-earners for a period of at least six months and then intends to employ them.

3- If the establishment that employs a number of wage-earners has replaced its operator.

4- If the establishment that employs a number of wage-earners transfers to another place or undergoes an expansion or change capable of bringing about a modification in the industrial and commercial activities that it carries on.

5- If the establishment that does not employ women or children under sixteen years of age intends to employ them.

6- If the establishment that does not use motive power or mechanical machinery comes to use them, its head must submit a declaration clarifying which of the cases mentioned above applies to him and stating the name and address of the declarant, the location of the establishment, and the nature of the industrial and commercial activities that it carries on, and stating, where applicable, whether he employs women or children under sixteen years of age or uses motive power or mechanical machinery.
No person who has not completed twenty-one years of age shall be entitled to employ trainees under sixteen years of age.

A person is prohibited from binding himself by any contract of employment for the whole duration of his life or from undertaking for life to refrain from working in any profession. Every contract, whatever its form, that leads to this result directly or indirectly is null and void ipso jure.

1 - An individual contract of employment is an agreement pursuant to which a wage-earner undertakes by virtue thereof to provide by his consent his work for the benefit of an employer and under his supervision and control in return for a wage regardless of the place of work.

2 - A written contract must be drawn up in the Arabic language and may be translated into a foreign language if the employer or the wage-earner is a foreigner who does not know the Arabic language."

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025 Official Gazette 22

In the event that the nature of the work so permits, agreement may be reached between the employer and the wage-earner to work according to a compressed working schedule, provided that the weekly working hours do not exceed 48 hours and without prejudice to the intermittent and continuous daily rest hours.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025 Official Gazette 22

1- Part-time work is considered to be work whose schedule is not less than one-third of the working schedule of comparable workers in the same establishment or company on a full-time basis or of wage-earners working in the same branch of activity where there are no comparable full-time workers in that establishment or company, and does not exceed two-thirds thereof.

2 - A part-time contract of employment shall be written or oral, and agreement shall be reached therein on the nature of the wage-earner's work, his working hours, the manner of their distribution during the week, the month, or the year, and the amount of his wage with a clarification of its elements.

3- Full-time working wage-earners affected by partial unemployment and by a collective and temporary reduction of their normal working hours, whether for economic, technical, or structural reasons or emergency circumstances in accordance with the provisions of this Law, shall not be considered part-time working wage-earners.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025 Official Gazette 22

The employer may, when the interest of the establishment so requires, request the part-time wage-earner to perform overtime working hours, provided that agreement is reached on the possibility of working overtime hours upon contracting or with the express consent of the wage-earner in the absence of prior agreement, provided that the wage-earner is notified at least three days in advance of the overtime working hours required of him and that the overtime working hours do not exceed ten percent of the part-time working hours agreed upon between the two parties unless the wage-earner consents to such increase; the wage for an overtime hour shall be paid with a fifty percent increase over the wage for a working hour of the part-time wage-earner.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025 Official Gazette 22

Written agreement may be reached between the wage-earner and the employer to transfer from a full-time working schedule to a part-time working schedule:

1- For a maximum period of two years for the wage-earner who wishes to pursue studies.

2- For a maximum period of one year after the end of maternity leave for a working woman.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025 Official Gazette 22

Wage-earners working on a part-time basis shall enjoy priority to transfer to the full-time working system, in the event that the required conditions are met, if the employer wishes to fill vacant or newly created full-time positions.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025 Official Gazette 22

Seasonal work is considered to be work which nature requires to be performed within a period of time not exceeding six months, and it is deemed to be in the nature of fixed-term contracts.
Working hours may be reduced in arduous or health-impairing work, and they may also be increased in certain cases, such as restaurant and café work, by a decision of the Minister of National Economy.

The provisions of Article 31 may be derogated from in emergency cases by making the working hours twelve hours, provided that:

1- The provisions of paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 23 are observed

2- The Department of Social Affairs is notified within twenty-four hours of the occurrence and of the time necessary to complete the work.

3- The wage for the overtime hours worked by the employee is 50 percent more than the wage for ordinary hours.

Whenever working hours exceed six for men and five for women, the employer must grant his employees at the middle of the working day a rest that may not be less than one hour.

The employee shall enjoy in every twenty-four hours a rest of nine consecutive hours, except in cases required by the circumstances of the work.

In industrial and commercial establishments, the employer or whoever represents him must post in a conspicuous place in his establishment a statement of the working hours for the various categories of employees, and notify a copy of this statement to the Department of Social Affairs.

The hours of work, opening and closing in establishments, businesses and professions of the same and similar nature, carried on by a group of natural and legal persons, shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs upon the proposal of the Director General, at the request of 60% of the members of this group within the scope of the Governorate, the city or the Qaimaqamiyya, or within the scope of a specific area, a village or a neighbourhood, and the bases that must be adopted in determining the percentages mentioned above shall be designated by a decision of the Minister.

Related text: Designating the bases that must be adopted in determining the percentages set forth in Law No. 48-66 relating to designating the hours of work, opening and closing in- establishments, businesses and professions of the same and similar nature

All employees must be granted a weekly rest of not less than 36 uninterrupted hours.

The employer may choose the day of this rest and distribute it among the employees according to the requirements of the work.

In the cases provided for in Article 33, the employees assigned to work shall be given the choice either of a rest equivalent to the weekly rest of which they were deprived, or of receiving a wage for the hours during which they worked.
Every employee who has lost his father, his mother, his spouse, or one of his children and grandchildren, or one of his grandfathers and grandmothers is entitled to a leave of two days with full pay.

Every employee is entitled to an annual leave of fifteen days with full pay, provided that he has been employed in the establishment for at least one year.

The employer may choose the date of these leaves according to the requirements of the service, and he may neither dismiss the employee nor serve him with a notice of dismissal during the leave.

If the employee contracts an illness other than the illnesses resulting from his service and the work accidents provided for in Legislative Decree No. 25/ET dated 4 May 1943, he is entitled to a sick leave determined as follows:

1- Half a month with full pay, and half a month with half pay for the employee who has spent in the service a period of three months or more up to two years.

2- One month with full pay and one month with half pay for an employee who has spent in the service more than two years up to four years.

3- A month and a half with full pay and a month and a half with half pay for the employee who has spent in the service more than four years up to six years.

4- Two months, with full pay and two months with half pay for the employee who has spent in the service more than six years up to ten years.

5- Two months and half a month, with full pay and two months and half a month with half pay for the employee whose service exceeds ten years.

Sick leaves shall be granted on the basis of a report from the physician who treated the employee or from the physician of the establishment. And the employer is entitled to entrust a physician of his choice with verifying the validity of the report submitted by the employee.

Sick leaves shall be renewed as necessary several times during a single year until they reach the maximum limit set forth in the preceding Article. And if they exceed one month, the employer is entitled to reduce the annual leave to eight days.
The employer may neither dismiss the employee from service nor serve him with a notice of dismissal during the sick leave.

Every agreement contrary to the provisions of this Chapter with respect to the duration of work and leaves is null and void by operation of law, and the employees may benefit from the agreements and regulations that are more favourable to them.

The minimum wage must be sufficient to meet the necessary needs of the employee and the needs of his family, taking into consideration the nature of the work, and it must not be less than the official minimum.
The determination of the minimum shall be undertaken by committees in which the Ministry of National Economy, the employers and the employees are represented.
The determination of the minimum wage shall be reconsidered whenever economic circumstances call for it.

Wages, if not in kind, must be paid in the official currency notwithstanding any contrary provision. And they must be paid at least once a month to salaried employees and twice to workers.

As for the wages for piecework that requires more than fifteen days to complete, the date of their payment shall be determined by mutual consent of the two parties, provided however that the worker is given payments on account every fifteen days and that his wage is settled within the fifteen days following the delivery of the work.

The payment of wages must take place on working days and at the workplace.

The salaries of employees for the last year are privileged debts and shall be ranked after the debt of the Treasury, judicial expenses and compulsory mortgages. This principle shall apply in cases of bankruptcy as well.

An employee who has in his possession a thing of his own making may exercise the right of retention within the conditions provided for in Article 677 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts.

Movable things delivered to an employee to be made, repaired or cleaned and which have not been reclaimed within two years from the date of their completion may be sold within the conditions and forms specified by Legislative Decree No. 46 dated 20 October of the year 1932 concerning the pledge of movable things, in order for the employee to obtain the consideration owed to him by the employer for the thing delivered to him.

a- Both the employer and the employee shall be entitled to rescind at any time the contract of employment concluded between them for an indefinite duration. However, in the event of abuse or excess in the exercise of this right, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to claim compensation assessed in accordance with the following principles:

- If the rescission emanates from the employer, the compensation shall be assessed on the basis of the nature of the employee's work, his age, the duration of his service, his family and health status, the extent of the damage, and the degree of abuse in the exercise of the right, provided that the compensation awarded shall not be less than the equivalent of two months' wages and shall not exceed the equivalent of twelve months' wages, in addition to any statutory indemnities to which the employee may be entitled as a result of his dismissal from service.

- And if the rescission emanates from the employee for reasons other than those permitted by law and it is established that he caused damage or embarrassment to the employer, the compensation for damages shall be assessed at an amount equivalent to one month's to four months' wages as the case may require, in addition to the compensation for notice provided for in paragraph c.

b - Whosoever invokes that the rescission occurred as a result of an abuse or excess in the exercise of the right must institute the action to that effect before the Arbitration Council within a time limit of one month from the date on which he was notified of the rescission, and he may prove the validity of his claim by all means of proof.

The Arbitration Council must adjudicate the case within a time limit not exceeding three months.

c- Both the employer and the employee must inform the other of his desire to rescind the contract, one month in advance if a period of three years or less has elapsed since the execution of the contract of employment, two months in advance if more than three years and less than six years have elapsed, three months in advance if more than six years and less than twelve years have elapsed, and four months in advance if twelve years or more have elapsed.

The notice must be in writing, and must be served upon the party concerned, and the latter shall be entitled to request clarification of the reasons for the rescission if they are not stated in the text of the notice. The party who violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be liable to pay compensation to the other party equivalent to the wages for the period of notice imposed upon him by law.

If the employee contracts with a new employer after rescinding the contract without fulfilling the obligations of notice, and the new employer was aware of the matter, the latter shall be jointly and severally liable for what is awarded in favour of the first employer.

Notwithstanding the provisions of this paragraph, if the employee is appointed on probation, he, as well as the employer, shall be entitled to rescind the contract of employment without any notice or compensation during the three months following his employment.

d- Dismissal shall be deemed to constitute an abuse or excess in the exercise of the right if it takes place in the following cases:

1- For an unacceptable reason or one unrelated to the employee's competence or his conduct within the establishment or to the good management and operation of the establishment.

2- For the employee's affiliation or non-affiliation with a specific professional syndicate or for his carrying out of a lawful syndical activity within the limits of the laws or regulations in force or a collective or special employment agreement.

3- For his standing for elections or for his having been elected as a member of the bureau of a syndicate or for the mission of an employees' representative in the establishment, throughout the duration of his performance of such mission.

4- For his submission in good faith of a complaint to the competent departments relating to the application of the provisions of this Law and the texts issued pursuant thereto, as well as his institution of a lawsuit against the employer pursuant thereto.

5- For his exercise of his personal or public liberties within the scope of the laws in force.

e- Notwithstanding the provisions of the first item of paragraph -a- and with the exception of the cases provided for in Article 74 of the Labour Law, the dismissal of members of syndicate councils duly elected, and throughout the duration of their term of office, shall be conditional upon recourse to the competent Arbitration Council. In this case, the employer must state all the reasons that led him to the dismissal and he may suspend the employee from work immediately until the issuance of the decision of the Arbitration Council on the merits of the case. The President of the Arbitration Council shall hold a special session to which he shall summon both parties for conciliation, within five days from the date of the recourse.

In the event of failure of the conciliation, the Arbitration Council sitting in plenary session shall examine the merits of the case, and shall adjudicate it within a time limit not exceeding one month. If it approves the dismissal, it shall order the liquidation of the employee's rights in accordance with the rules provided for in the Labour Law.

And if it does not approve the dismissal, it shall order that the employer be compelled to reinstate the employee in his work under pain of holding him liable to pay, in addition to the statutory indemnities to which the employee is entitled, an additional sum ranging between twice and three times the allowance provided for in paragraph -a- of this Article.

f- The employer may terminate some or all of the current contracts of employment in the establishment if force majeure or economic or technical circumstances necessitate such termination, such as reducing the size of the establishment or replacing one production system with another or ceasing work definitively. The employer must notify the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs of his desire to terminate those contracts one month prior to its execution, and he must consult with the Ministry to establish a final programme for that termination taking into consideration the seniority of work in the establishment, their specialisation, their ages, their family and social status, and finally the necessary means for their re-employment.

g- Employees dismissed from service pursuant to the preceding paragraph shall enjoy, for a period of one year commencing from the date of their leaving work, a right of priority (preference) in returning to work in the establishment from which they were dismissed if work therein returns to normal and it becomes possible to employ them in the newly created jobs therein.
During the notice period, the wage-earner may absent himself for one hour of the working hours per day in order to seek other employment.

Notice shall not be addressed:

1- To a pregnant woman.

2- To a woman on maternity leave.

3- To any wage-earner during ordinary leave or during sick leave.

However, the employer shall be released from these impediments if the wage-earner is employed in another place during those periods.
If the employer violates the provisions relating to notice, he must pay the wages for the days included in the notice period or the days during which he is not permitted to serve notice.

Until social security legislation is enacted, the employer must pay to the wage-earner dismissed from service for any reason other than those mentioned in Article 74 a dismissal indemnity equivalent to one month's wages for each year of service and half a month's wages if the period of service is less than one year.

The dismissal indemnity may not exceed ten months' salaries regardless of the number of years of service for wage-earners who work for practitioners of liberal professions, crafts, workshop industries, and the persons provided for in Article 10 of the Code of Commerce.

1- A wage-earner who has reached the age of sixty years or has twenty-five years of service in the same establishment may request his dismissal from service and benefit from the dismissal indemnity. The same wage-earner shall also have the right to continue to work until he reaches the completed age of sixty-four years, whereupon his subjection to the provisions of the Labour Law, and consequently to the system of dismissal indemnity, shall ipso jure terminate, unless the internal regulations of the establishment in which he works or the collective employment agreement allow him to work beyond the age of sixty-four.

2- If the wage-earner or salaried employee requests the payment of his indemnity upon reaching sixty years of age or after the expiry of twenty-five years of service in the same establishment, he shall not be entitled to any new dismissal indemnity from the employer in the event that he continues in service until the age of sixty-four.

The compensation referred to in the preceding articles shall be due to all employees, regardless of the category to which they belong, even if they are outside the permanent establishment, temporary, or daily workers, provided that they are bound to the enterprise by continuous service for at least one year.

The limitation period for legal actions relating to the compensation shall be two years from the date on which the compensation falls due.

The wage adopted for the calculation of the compensations provided for in the preceding article shall be the last wage paid prior to dismissal or prior notice of dismissal.

Wage shall mean the basic wage received by the employee on a time basis together with the increments, allowances, and commissions that have been added to the basic wage.

However, if the wage, in whole or in part, is calculated on a commission basis, account shall be taken of the average amount actually received by the employee during the twelve months prior to dismissal.

A hire of service entered into for a definite period by contract or by the nature of the work shall not be subject to the provisions of this Chapter relating to prior notice and dismissal compensation. Employees who have benefited from contracts for a definite period that have been renewed by contract or by continuing to work without interruption for a period of at least two years shall be governed, with respect to dismissal compensations, by the same rules as employees who benefit from contracts for an indefinite period.

Every provision in a hire of service contract and, in general, every agreement concluded between the employer and the employee before the work and during its term which purports to waive the provisions of Chapter Four relating to wages or to reduce the amount to which the employee is entitled pursuant to those provisions shall be null and void by operation of law. However, provisions contained in a special agreement or in general regulations for workers which purport to grant them conditions more favourable to them shall accrue to their benefit.

Foreign employees shall enjoy, upon their dismissal from service, the rights enjoyed by Lebanese workers, subject to reciprocity, and they shall be required to obtain a work permit from the Ministry of Labour. Exclusively exempted from the condition of reciprocity and from the fee for the work permit issued by the Ministry of Labour shall be Palestinian refugee employees duly registered in the records of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Directorate of Political Affairs and Refugees.

A female worker or female salaried employee who is compelled to leave service by reason of marriage shall also benefit from dismissal compensation, provided that she gives notice within the period specified in Article 13 and that she has more than one year of service, and such compensation shall not be payable until after the marriage has been verified.

If a change occurs in the legal status of the employer by reason of inheritance, sale, assignment, merger, or the like in the form of the establishment, or conversion into a company, all employment contracts in force on the day the change occurs shall remain in effect between the new employer and the employees of the establishment.

Subject to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 21 dated 22 July 1936 relating to dangerous, unhealthy, or inconvenient establishments, the provisions of the decrees and decisions adopted in implementation of the aforementioned Legislative Decree, and the provisions of Article 647 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts, the establishments provided for in Article 8 of this Law shall be kept clean at all times and shall fulfil the conditions of health and comfort necessary for the employees, and the establishment shall be equipped in such a manner as to ensure the safety of the employees.

As for machines, mechanical parts, transmission gear, tools, and implements, they shall be installed and maintained in compliance with the best possible conditions of safety.

There shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers after consulting the Department of Social Affairs:

1- The general measures of health protection and prevention applicable to all establishments subject thereto, in particular with respect to safety measures, lighting, ventilation, air renewal, potable water, lavatories, evacuation of dust and smoke, sleeping quarters for employees, and precautions taken against fires.

2- The special instructions relating either to certain trades or to certain types of work, according to necessity.

With respect to the application of the decrees referred to in the preceding article, the inspectors shall serve notice upon the heads of establishments requiring them to comply with those instructions before drawing up an official report against them.

This notice shall be drawn up in writing and entered in a register prepared for this purpose, and shall be dated and signed, and shall specify the concrete contraventions and a time limit for remedying such contraventions.

Every head of an establishment, director, manager, or foreman, and in general every person having authority over the workers and salaried employees, is prohibited from permitting the introduction or distribution of any alcoholic beverages in the establishments provided for in the eighth article of this Law for the purpose of their consumption by the employees at the workplace, and every head of an establishment, director, manager, or foreman, and in general every person having authority over the workers and salaried employees, is prohibited from permitting persons in a state of intoxication to enter the establishments referred to in the eighth article of this Law or to remain therein.

Every employer employing fifteen or more employees shall draw up regulations for the employees and for the organisation of work in his establishment.

These regulations must be approved by the Minister of National Economy.

The regulations provided for in the preceding article may include a schedule of fines applicable to salaried employees and workers when they commit a fault or negligence during work.

If the regulations do not include such a schedule, or if there are no regulations, the schedule shall be drawn up by decision of the Minister of National Economy. In drawing up the schedule, the matters set forth in the following articles shall be observed:

If an employee commits during work a serious fault or gross negligence, or contravenes the internal regulations of the establishment, the employer shall have the right to impose upon him, by way of penalty, a fine which may not exceed the deduction of three days' wage for a single act.

The fine shall not be applied after the expiry of fifteen days from the verification of the fault, negligence, or contravention.

If material damage to the employer results from the fault, negligence, or contravention of the regulations, he shall have the right to recover the value of such damage from the wage of the worker or salaried employee.
In all cases, the amount deducted may not exceed five days' wage in any single month.

Fines imposed by way of penalty must be allocated in their entirety exclusively to cooperative works established for the benefit of the employees in accordance with the general rules determined by decision of the Minister of National Economy.

If an employee is taken into custody by the judiciary, he shall be deemed suspended from work by operation of law. As soon as he is released, he shall be reinstated in the work he was performing or in similar work.

Penalties imposed upon employees shall be entered in a special register stating the name of the penalised employee, the nature and date of the contravention, the amount of the penalty, and the manner of its execution.

Labour inspectors may inspect this register at any time and request all necessary explanations regarding the penalties imposed.

The employer may terminate the contract without any compensation or prior notice in the following cases:

1- If the employee has assumed a false nationality.

2- If the employee has been engaged on probation and has not satisfied the employer within three months of his engagement.

3- If it is established that the employee has committed an intentional act or negligence aimed at causing damage to the material interests of the employer. Provided that, in order to invoke this ground, the employer must notify the Department of Social Affairs in writing of this violation within three days of verifying it.

4- If the employee, despite written warnings addressed to him, commits a serious violation of the internal regulations three times in one year.

5- If the employee absents himself without legitimate excuse for more than fifteen days in one year or for more than seven consecutive days. The employee must explain to the employer the reasons for the absence within twenty-four hours of his return. And the employer must on each occasion notify the employee in writing of the number of days counted against him as having been absent without legitimate excuse.

6- If the employee is sentenced to imprisonment for one year or more for committing a felony, or if he commits a misdemeanour at the workplace and during the performance of work, and if the employee is sentenced for the acts provided for and punishable under Article 344 of the Penal Code.

7- If the employee assaults the employer or the responsible person in charge of management at the workplace.

The employee is entitled to leave his work before the expiry of the term of the contract and without any prior notice in the following cases:

1- If the employer or his representative deceived him as to the conditions of work upon the conclusion of the contract, provided that the employee shall not be entitled to invoke this right after the lapse of thirty days from his entry into service.

2- If the employer does not fulfil his obligations towards the employee in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

3- If the employer or his representative commits an offence contrary to public morals against the person of the employee or a member of his family.

4- If the employer or his representative commits acts of violence against the person of the employee.
If the employee leaves his work for one of the reasons set out in the preceding Article, he shall be paid the dismissal compensation provided for in this Law.

There shall be established in the centre of each governorate, to hear the disputes referred to in the first Article of this Law, one or more Labour Arbitration Councils composed as follows:

- A judge of the eleventh grade and above - as President, appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council

- A representative of the employers and a representative of the employees

- Two members appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs; two alternate members shall also be appointed, one for the employers and another for the employees, each to replace the principal representative in the event of his absence or inability to attend, by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs.

- A Government Commissioner shall be appointed to the Council, chosen from among civil servants of the third category in the public administrations, provided that he holds a degree of Licence in Law.

The duties and powers of the Government Commissioner shall be determined by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs. The appointment of the Government Commissioner shall take place in the same manner.

Principal and alternate representatives of employers and employees are required:

1- To be Lebanese.

2- To have completed twenty-one years of age.

3- Not to have been convicted of a felony or a dishonourable offence.

4- To have practised their profession for a period of at least five years.

The Arbitration Council shall have jurisdiction:

1- To hear disputes arising from the determination of the minimum wage.

2- To hear disputes arising from work accidents provided for in Legislative Decree No. 25 issued on 4 May 1943.
