3- To hear disputes arising from dismissal from service, abandonment of work, and the imposition of fines, and in general all disputes arising between employers and employees from the application of the provisions of this Law.

The Arbitration Council shall hear the cases brought before it by way of summary procedure.

These cases shall be exempted from judicial fees, to the exclusion of expenses, which shall remain borne by the losing party.

Judgments rendered by the Labour Arbitration Councils shall not be subject to any means of recourse other than opposition, third-party opposition, and cassation in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure and in the Law on Judicial Organisation, subject to the special provisions set forth in Articles No. 6 to No. 10.
The members of the Arbitration Council shall receive a compensation to be determined by decree.
In each category of professions, employers and employees are each entitled to form a special syndicate which shall have legal personality and the capacity to litigate.

The object of the syndicate shall be restricted to matters aimed at protecting the profession, encouraging it, raising its standard, defending its interests, and working for its advancement in all economic, industrial, and commercial respects. Syndicates are prohibited from engaging in politics and from participating in meetings and demonstrations of a political nature.

No single syndicate may bring together persons belonging to different professions; rather, all its members must be persons practising one profession or similar professions.

As for the boundaries between similar professions and trades and the schedules of professions whose practitioners are licensed to form syndicates among themselves, they shall be determined by the Minister of National Economy by a decision taken by him upon the proposal of the Department of Social Affairs.
No syndicate of employers or of employees may be established except after authorisation from the Minister of National Economy.

The application for authorisation shall be submitted to the Ministry of National Economy - Department of Social Affairs, and this Ministry shall seek the opinion of the Ministry of the Interior thereon and thereafter take its decision of refusal or acceptance.

The syndicate shall not be considered legitimate until after the publication of the decision in the Official Gazette.

The application for authorisation must be submitted in three copies and be accompanied by three copies of the internal regulations and by the judicial record certificate of the founding members.

Revenue stamps shall be affixed to the first copy, which shall be returned to the applicants together with the approval decision. The second shall remain with the Ministry of the Interior and the third with the Department of Social Affairs.

Every syndicate must draw up internal regulations approved by the General Assembly by a majority of two-thirds of its members, and they shall not take effect until after their approval by the Ministry of National Economy.
Both the employer and the employee are free to join or not to join the syndicate.

A person wishing to join the syndicate is required.

1- To be of Lebanese nationality, enjoying his civil rights.

2- To be practising the profession at the time of the application.

3- To have completed eighteen years of age.

4- Not to have been convicted of a felony or a dishonourable offence.

Foreigners may join the syndicate if they fulfil the conditions set out in paragraphs 2, 3, and 4 of the preceding Article and are authorised to work in Lebanon.

Provided that foreign members shall not be entitled to vote or to be elected, though they shall be entitled to delegate one of their number in order to represent them and defend them before the Council of the Syndicate.

The application for membership shall be submitted to the Council of the Syndicate accompanied by an identity card and a work certificate certified by the Department of Social Affairs indicating that the applicant practises the profession of the syndicate.

The Council of the Syndicate must take its decision accepting or rejecting the application by secret ballot within a period of fifteen days.
The applicant is entitled to object to the decision of rejection before the Department of Social Affairs, which shall take the necessary decision thereon.
The Council of the Syndicate may expel any member who commits acts gravely contravening the object of the syndicate, or violates its internal regulations, or abstains from paying the subscription.

A member who is expelled from the syndicate for reasons he considers unlawful may object to the decision of expulsion before the Department of Social Affairs, which shall take the necessary decision thereon.

Municipalities in the capital of each governorate shall establish an employment office operating under the management of the head of the municipality and the supervision of the Ministry of National Economy - Department of Social Affairs.

Employment offices may be established in other municipalities by a decision of the Minister of National Economy.

- Private employment offices, even those free of charge, shall be subject to a licence from the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, and offices established prior to the issuance of this Law shall submit an application for the said licence within three months

- The Minister of Labour and Social Affairs shall have the right to revoke the said licence in the event that the owner of the employment office fails to abide by the purpose for which the office was established or causes harm to the interest of the concerned parties or the public interest. - Approval of the licence application shall be conditional upon:

1- If the applicant for the licence is a natural person.

a- That he has completed twenty-one years of age.

b - That he enjoys civil rights and has not been convicted of a felony, an infamous misdemeanour, or a narcotics offence .

2- If the person is a legal person.

a- That it is established in accordance with the laws in force.

b - That its bylaws permit it to practise this work

3- The conditions for establishing private employment offices shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs.

Employment offices shall be competent :

1- To accept employment applications and requests for labour in every profession among the professions of the syndicates provided for in this Law, and to classify, coordinate, and register them in a special register with the date of their receipt.

2- To facilitate finding work for the unemployed and to exert endeavours to this end.

3- To guide unemployed workers according to the economic needs of the country, according to their particular circumstances, and requests for labour, and to facilitate their transfer from one profession to another or from one region to another.

4- Organising statistics on the number of unemployed workers in each region and in each profession at the times designated by the Ministry of National Economy.

The provisions of this Law shall cover contracts in force on the date of its publication, and its provisions shall apply within three months from the date of its publication to all syndical bodies provided for in Articles 83 et seq. of this Law.

Lawsuits pending before the ordinary courts shall be adjudicated by the courts seized thereof.
The methods of applying the provisions of this Law shall be regulated by decrees enacted in the Council of Ministers.
All laws and regulations contrary to the provisions of this Law and inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
The provisions of these Bylaws shall apply to public kindergarten and basic education schools.

The following words and expressions used in this Decision shall mean:

- The teacher: Any person who undertakes teaching.

- The person in charge of the school: Any person assigned to manage the affairs of the school.

- Teaching staff: The person in charge of the school, the supervisors, the teachers, and the physical education teachers.

- The remaining staff of the school: Ushers, servants, and guards ...

- The guardian of the pupil: The person responsible for him.

For the admission of a pupil, it shall be required:

First: That he be Lebanese.

Second: That he be accompanied by his guardian to submit an application signed by him stating his name, surname, address, profession, degree of kinship to the pupil, and the curricular year in which the pupil requests to enrol, and attaching to the application the following supporting documents:

a - An identity card or a certified copy thereof, or an individual civil status extract proving that his age is not less than the minimum age specified in the public education curriculum. Pupils who have previously been registered in public schools and are still pursuing their studies therein shall be exempted from the age requirement.

b - A school certificate or report card from the school in which he spent the last academic year showing clearly the results of his schoolwork, provided that such certificate or report card is certified in accordance with the rules and records in particular whether the pupil:

 Completed his academic year successfully and was promoted to the following curricular year. Or failed at the end of the year and must repeat his class.

c - A health certificate and a vaccination card, both mandatory for a first-time applicant, provided that the certificate proves that he is free from contagious diseases.

The person in charge of the school must notify the local authorities and the Head of the Educational Region, within a period not exceeding ten days, of the names of the pupils who are rejected for this reason.

Third: That he pass an entrance examination for the curricular year permitted by his report card or his school certificate.

Fourth: That the school fees and other amounts due be collected from him in accordance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force.

All supporting documents shall be kept in the pupil's file.

Pupils wishing to enrol in the kindergarten stage and the first curricular year of the primary stage shall be admitted in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article, with the exception of the two requirements of the examination and the school report card.

Priority in enrolment in the curricular years shall be given according to the following order:

1 - Pupils of the school who have passed the school tests.

2 - Pupils of the school who have failed and are accepted to repeat their classes.

3 - New pupils.

Preparatory work shall begin on the morning of the first working day following the fifteenth of the month of September and shall continue until the end of the official working hours of the last working day thereof, and shall include:

1- Registration of returning pupils.

2 - Organisation of the entrance examination for new pupils.

3 - Organisation of all school affairs and work.

The registration of returning pupils shall take place and the fees due shall be collected from them during the period of preparatory work.

As for new pupils, they shall be finally registered, and the fees shall be collected from them after their success in the entrance examination and the securing of places for them in the curricular years.

 It shall be permissible to continue admitting pupils to fill the places that remain vacant until the fifteenth of November, and thereafter only pupils transferred from other schools shall be admitted, following the approval of the Head of the Educational Region if the transfer is within the same region and the approval of the Director of Primary Education if the transfer is from one region to another.

Lists of registered pupils:

The entrance examination for new pupils shall be held and its results announced during the period of preparatory work, and this examination shall include the following:

a - For candidates for the second cycle of the primary stage of basic education:

1- An examination in written communication in the Arabic and foreign languages.

2 - An examination in written communication in arithmetic problems.

b - For candidates for the intermediate stage of basic education:

1 - An examination in written communication in the Arabic and foreign languages.

2 - An examination in written communication in solving mathematical problems and in sciences.

c - Any person whose average of total marks is at least 10/20 shall be deemed to have passed the examination, provided that he has not obtained a zero in any of the subjects of this examination.

d- Vacant places shall be filled from among the successful candidates according to the order of their passing grades, and their marks shall be recorded in a special register.

e - Examination documents shall be kept in the file of the successful pupil.

As for the documents of pupils who are not admitted, they shall be kept in a special file for a period of at least one year.

First: The person in charge of the school and all its staff must attend the school on the days of preparatory work from eight o'clock in the morning until thirteen hundred hours in order to carry out the following tasks:

1 - Invigilating the entrance examinations.

2 - Marking the examination papers.

3 - Organising school and educational affairs.

Second: The person in charge of the school may organise in his school a shift schedule during the preparatory period, provided that at least half the number of the teaching staff attend.

Teaching shall begin on the morning of the first working day of the month of October and shall end at the end of the official working hours of the first working day following the twenty-first of the month of June of the following year.

The following printed forms shall be kept in the school in accordance with special models prepared by the Directorate of Primary Education:

1 - The annual registration register of pupils.

2 - The daily attendance register of pupils.

3 - The register of marks.

4 - The daily attendance register of the staff of the school.

5 - The register of outgoing and incoming transactions.

6 - The register of inspection and technical guidance.

7 - The register of minutes of the teachers' council.

8 - The register of minutes of the guidance and disciplinary council.

9 - The financial register.

10 - The school library register.

11 - The laboratory register.

12 - The register of school furniture and teaching equipment.

13 - The register of supervision of schoolwork.

14 - The health register.

15 - The pupil's personal card.

16 - The pupil's file, and in the event that the pupil transfers to a new school, a certified copy of this file shall be given to be joined to his new file..

17 - The school staff member's card.

18 - The school staff member's file, and in the event that the staff member transfers to a new school, the entire file shall be sent by registered mail to his new place of work.

19 - The incoming file, in which general decisions, circulars, and various administrative texts shall be kept.

20 - The outgoing file, in which copies of correspondence shall be kept.

21 - The archives file, in which schedules, internal correspondence, and all other archives of the school shall be kept.

22 - The file of expenditure invoices and financial documents. 23 All other registers, files, and books that are required to be kept.

The pages of the registers shall be numbered, and special indexes containing a statement of their contents shall be drawn up for the files.

Management:

It is the assignment of a member of the teaching staff to manage the affairs of a specific school and is not a permanent appointment that confers this capacity upon its holder.

The person in charge of the school shall be:

- A principal if the school comprises at least five teachers other than himself.

- A head teacher if the school comprises fewer than five teachers.

- A sole teacher if the school has a single teacher.
The assignment of the person in charge of the school shall be subject to the bases and criteria specified by Decision No. 686/3/99 dated 02/10/1999 attached to these Bylaws (Document No. 1).

In the exceptional cases in which the position of the person responsible for the school falls vacant and in other cases, such as death, incapacitating illness, absence exceeding six consecutive months, or cessation of work, and when it is impossible to find a person who meets the required conditions, a member of the teaching staff may be assigned temporarily to carry out the duties of the permanent person responsible for a non-renewable period not exceeding one year.

The supervisor most senior in rank within the cadre shall replace the person responsible for the school, in the event of his absence, and shall deputise for him in all his powers and responsibilities.

In the absence of a supervisor, the teacher most senior in rank within the cadre shall deputise for the person responsible for the school.

The person responsible for the school shall designate in writing the person who deputises for him in the two aforementioned cases.

The person responsible for the school is the immediate superior of all employees working therein, and he is prohibited from addressing any remark to them in front of the pupils and in front of others.

The person responsible for the school shall attend to all its affairs and in particular to the following matters:

1- Preserving the building with its sections, facilities, and contents of furniture, teaching tools, library, laboratory, and registers.

2 - Attending to general cleanliness and public health in the school and taking the necessary measures and means to ensure them.

3 - The solidarity of the members of the teaching staff and watching over their attendance and their performance of their duties.

4 - The technical organisation of teaching and school work in terms of knowledge and education.

5 - Taking the measures capable of ensuring the regularity of work and securing activity and discipline in all school work.

6 - Treating the teaching staff in a spirit of justice and equality in all school work, and particularly in matters relating to the organisation of school registers and the distribution of working hours including teaching, duty shifts, and free hours.

7 - Organising cooperation between the school and the parents of the pupils.

8 - The necessity of conducting physical education exercises in the playgrounds of the school.

The person responsible shall inspect at least once a month the lesson preparation notebooks, the grade notebooks, and the circulating notebooks, and he shall sign, stamp, and date them upon each inspection, record his remarks in the school work monitoring register, and communicate them to the teacher concerned in person.

The person responsible shall:

1 - Contribute to actual teaching if the need of the school so requires.

2 - Attend the lessons of each of the teachers of the school periodically at least once every two months, monitor the work of the supervisors, those assigned to daily supervision, the class tutors, the physical education teachers, and all other school activities, and record his remarks accurately on all of that in the school work monitoring register, provided that he communicates them to the persons concerned in person.

The person responsible for the school shall post, in the last week of the academic year and in a prominent place, an announcement of the dates of the commencement of registration and the entrance examinations that will take place during the preparatory period for an upcoming academic year.

The person responsible for the school shall preside over the teachers' committees, their council, the guidance and discipline council, the committees for school examinations and tests, the subject coordination committee, and the school activity committees that are formed under his patronage and supervision. He may assign, under his own responsibility, a person to deputise for him in the latter case when necessary.
The head teacher and the sole teacher shall have the same rights and powers granted to the principal, and each of them shall be subject to the same duties imposed upon him.

The person responsible for the school shall inform without delay his immediate superiors of the events that take place in his school and that relate to all its work and to the affairs of the employees working therein. He shall conduct the preliminary investigations, interrogate the persons concerned in writing, and submit a report in this regard without delay to the immediate superior, recording therein his remarks and proposals.

The person responsible shall in particular inform the Educational Region immediately of any decrease or increase occurring in the number of members of the teaching staff in his school, under pain of aggravated liability.

The person responsible for the school shall certify the payrolls and their annexes pertaining to the employees of the school, as a notice from him that these employees are attending to their school work in accordance with the provisions of these Internal Regulations, and it is not permissible to draw up payrolls for any employee who has discontinued his work except in the special cases provided for by law.

If the discontinuance occurs after the drawing up of the payroll, he shall immediately inform the Educational Region thereof. As for the payrolls of sole teachers, they shall be certified by the Head of the Educational Region.

The teaching staff shall assist the person responsible for the school in the educational guidance of the pupils and in supervision; to this end, the person responsible for the school shall designate a tutor for each class from among its teachers to monitor the behaviour of the pupils and help them solve their problems through guidance, advice, and educational measures, in cooperation with the teachers of the class and with the tutors of the other classes, provided that this mission of his does not exempt him from teaching or from other work.

The person responsible shall draw up at the beginning of the academic year a list of the class tutors.

Supervision and monitoring work in the school shall be secured as follows:

- One supervisor for each school containing between (75- 150) pupils at least.

- Two supervisors for each school containing between (151-300) pupils.

- Three supervisors for each school containing between (301 - 450) pupils.

- Four supervisors for each school containing between (451 - 600) pupils.

- Five supervisors for each school containing between (601 - 800) pupils.

The person responsible for the school shall assign in writing one or more teachers who possess educational and professional competence to carry out supervision work in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article, and he shall have the right to revoke the assignment if the interest so requires after the approval of the Head of the Educational Region.

The Director of Primary Education may reconsider the assignment of the supervisor or the revocation of this assignment whenever the need arises.

The person responsible for the school may assign one or more additional supervisors in either of the following two cases after the approval of the Head of the Educational Region:

1 - If the number of pupils exceeds 800 pupils.

2 - If the condition of the building so requires.

1- The supervisor shall secure supervision during breaks, as the supervisors shall secure it in periodic duty shifts while maintaining the regularity of work in all classes. In the absence of a supervisor, the supervising teachers shall secure supervision during these breaks in periodic duty shifts.

2 - The person responsible for the school shall assign the teachers to assist the supervisors in supervision work during breaks to maintain order and facilitate work in all aspects of school activity, provided that the assignment is in periodic duty shifts that do not prevent the assigned person from performing his school duties.

a - The number of pupils in a single class shall not be less than ten pupils at the intermediate level and the kindergarten level, and not less than fifteen pupils at the primary level, provided that the condition of schools located in remote areas and sole-teacher schools is taken into consideration. In principle, it is not permissible to divide a single class into two sections unless the number therein exceeds thirty pupils and a sufficient number of teachers and classrooms is secured. Where these two conditions are met, the division of the class becomes mandatory.

b - If the number of pupils of a single class falls below the minimum indicated in paragraph a, the pupils of the curricular year of this class may then be combined in one room with the pupils of another curricular year whose number is less than the aforementioned minimum, in which case priority shall be given to combining two curricular years that are close in level, and they shall be given such joint lessons as the nature of those lessons permits.

Every case that does not conform to the content of this Article due to special circumstances shall be subject to the prior written approval of the Director of Primary Education upon the proposal of the Head of the Educational Region.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025, Official Gazette 22

Remote work is work performed by the employee from any place of his choice other than the employer's workplace, on a full-time or part-time basis, in accordance with the directives and regulations of the employer.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025, Official Gazette 22

1-Part-time, seasonal and remote employees shall benefit from the same protection enjoyed by comparable permanent and on-site employees in the establishment or company with respect to the right to:

-Organisation and the right to collective bargaining.,

-Occupational safety and health.,

-Non-discrimination in employment and occupation.,

2-Part-time or remote employees shall benefit from the rights pertaining to comparable full-time or on-site employees in the establishment or company in accordance with the provisions of the Labour Law and the Social Security Law, provided that the principle of proportionality based on the number of working hours is adopted in calculating and determining their entitlements and rights.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025, Official Gazette 22

The employer must keep records showing the names of the employees, the type of their contracts, the number of their working hours, the types of their activity and the other conditions and terms of their work. The Labour Inspection, Prevention and Safety Body at the Ministry of Labour shall have the right to inspect them when necessary.

Added pursuant to Law No. 3 dated 9/5/2025, Official Gazette 22

The details of the application of the provisions relating to inspection to verify the extent of application of the provisions of the laws in force to remote workers shall be determined by decrees issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

The details of the rules governing the benefit of part-time and seasonal remote workers from social security benefits and the means of financing shall be determined by decrees issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund.

Every employee shall be given a booklet by the Social Affairs Service known as the employment booklet, containing the name of the employed person, a copy of his nationality certificate, the specification of his specialisation, the medical examinations, and the date of his entry into and exit from each establishment; as for his daily, weekly or monthly wage, it shall be recorded in the employment booklet if the employee so requests.
An employer, whether male or female, single, separated, divorced or widowed, shall not have the right to house with him a minor employed by him.

Persons sentenced to imprisonment for theft, forgery, use of forged documents, fraud, breach of trust, or for a felony or an offence against public morals shall not have the right to employ juvenile apprentices.

The disqualification resulting from the preceding Article may be lifted upon request by a decision of the Minister of National Economy when the convicted person resides in the same Governorate, after having served his sentence for one year without incurring any new penalty.

The employer must teach the apprentice progressively and completely the special art, profession or trade for which he was employed.

Upon the expiry of the training period, he shall be given a certificate proving the qualification of the apprentice.

After the expiry of the first two months of training, which are considered as a probationary period, the employer must pay the apprentice a wage the minimum of which is equal to one-third of the ordinary wage of the employee in the first stage, half of the wage in the second stage, and two-thirds of the wage in the third stage.

All provisions aimed at stating the necessity of the apprenticeship contract, its form and the end-of-apprenticeship examinations shall all be the subject of decrees taken in the Council of Ministers.

The labour inspectors are charged with supervising the execution of these decrees and ensuring the application of the provisions of this Law, and the powers of these officials affiliated with the Social Affairs Service at the Ministry of National Economy shall be determined by decree.
The employment of juveniles under eighteen years of age shall be subject to the provisions set forth in this Chapter.

It is absolutely prohibited to employ juveniles before they have completed the age of thirteen, and a juvenile must not be employed before undergoing a medical examination to ascertain his fitness to perform the work for which he is employed to perform.

Medical certificates are given free of charge by the Ministry of Public Health and are renewed annually until the juvenile completes the age of eighteen. They may be revoked at any time if it is subsequently proven that the juvenile is unfit to perform the work for which he was employed.

It is prohibited to employ juveniles in industrial undertakings and in arduous or health-impairing work set forth in Schedules No. (1) and (2) annexed to this Law before they have completed the age of fifteen. It is also prohibited to employ juveniles before they have completed the age of sixteen in work that is dangerous by its nature or that constitutes a danger to life, health or morals because of the conditions in which it is carried out.

Such work shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

It is prohibited to employ juveniles whose age is not less than eighteen for more than six hours daily, interspersed with at least one hour of rest if the daily working hours exceed four consecutive hours, and it is also prohibited to employ them during the period extending between seven o'clock in the evening and seven o'clock in the morning.

The juvenile must be granted a period of rest of not less than 13 consecutive hours between every two periods of work, and it is also absolutely prohibited to assign him overtime work or to employ him during daily and weekly rest periods, or during holidays and occasions on which the establishment closes.

Every juvenile has the right to an annual leave of twenty-one days with full pay, provided that he has been employed in the establishment for at least one year. The juvenile must benefit from at least two-thirds of the leave period at one time, provided that he benefits from the remainder of the period during the same year."

Verification of the age of children and juveniles takes place under the responsibility of employers, whatever the category to which they belong; they must require from every child his nationality certificate before employing him.

In institutions intended for teaching trades, the provisions of Articles 22 and 23 may be derogated from, provided that the age of the juvenile is not less than 12 completed years and provided that the curriculum of these institutions specifies the type of trades and the hours and conditions of work, and that it is approved jointly by the Ministry of Labour and the Health Departments.

The employer is prohibited from discriminating on the basis of sex between a male worker and a female worker with regard to the type of work, the amount of wage, recruitment, promotion, advancement, vocational qualification and clothing.
It is prohibited to employ women in the industries and work set forth in Annex No. 1 to this Law.

Working women in all categories set forth in this Law have the right to obtain maternity leave for a period of ten weeks, including the period preceding childbirth and the period following it, by producing a medical certificate indicating the probable date of childbirth.

The wage shall be paid in full to the woman during maternity leave. A working woman who has benefited from maternity leave with full pay remaining has the right to receive a wage for the period of ordinary annual leave that she will obtain during the same year, pursuant to the provisions of Article /39/ of the Labour Law.

It is prohibited to dismiss a woman from service or to serve her with notice during the period of maternity leave, unless it is proven that she was employed in another place during the said period.

The following shall be criminally liable for the execution of the provisions of this Chapter relating to the employment of children, juveniles and women:

1- Employers and their agents.

2- Parents or guardians who have employed or permitted the employment of their children or juveniles, or the children or juveniles in their custody, in violation of the provisions of this Law.

The maximum limit of work per week is 48 hours in the guilds set forth in the fifth Article, with the exception of agricultural guilds. As for children and juveniles, they shall be employed in accordance with the provisions of Article 22 to 25.

Distribution of Subjects:

Each member of the teaching staff shall organise, under the supervision of the person in charge of the school, and within the first week from the date of receiving his work schedule, the annual schedule for the distribution of the subjects which he teaches over the months of the academic year in a form and quantity that ensure the completion of the prescribed official education curriculum.

Posting of Schedules:

The person in charge of the school, with the assistance of the teaching staff, shall post at the beginning of the academic year, in a prominent place in each classroom:

1 - The annual schedule of study subjects distributed over the months.

2 - The weekly schedule of lessons and assignments.

3 - A list of the names of the pupils.

4 - The schedule for the distribution of monthly tests. The person in charge shall also post in the administration room or in the teachers' room:

a) A general schedule for the distribution of lessons and assignments across the teaching rooms.

b) A general schedule for the distribution of working and free hours among the teaching staff in the school, signed by them.

c) A schedule for the distribution of the duties of the supervisors.

d) A schedule of the names of the class homeroom teachers.

e) A comparative list of the names of the school textbooks, showing the name of the textbook adopted in the past year and the textbook currently adopted.

In the event of any change, the number and date of the approval transaction shall be stated in the remarks column.

Preparation Notebook and Grades Notebook: Each member of the teaching staff shall prepare his daily work and lessons practically and in writing before the beginning of the school working day. The teacher shall number the pages of his preparation notebook and include in its first pages:

1 - His name and a summary of his curriculum vitae in the service.

2 - The schedule for the distribution of lessons and assignments.

3 - The schedule of monthly tests.

4 - The monthly-annual schedule for the distribution of subjects. The preparation shall cover all types of daily school work in the classroom, including teaching, assignments, exercises, review, tests or correction, illustrative aids, or any other school work, and shall set out the elements of the subject, the stages of the work, and its means.

 The teacher shall record in a special notebook the grades of lessons, assignments, and tests, and his monthly remarks on the development of each pupil's conduct and diligence.

Teachers of experimental science subjects shall prepare their experiments and tests in the school laboratory before the official time fixed for giving the lesson, in cooperation and coordination with the laboratory preparer.

The Rotating Notebook:

The class teacher, or the teachers who participate in teaching a single class, shall take full care of the rotating notebooks, number their pages, and hand them each day to a pupil to write therein the exercises and written work given in the classroom, provided that three notebooks shall be allocated to each primary class:

One for the Arabic language and social studies, one for the foreign language, and one for sciences and mathematics; whereas in the intermediate classes, a rotating notebook shall be allocated for each subject or what is deemed equivalent to a subject. The rotating notebooks shall be kept with the school archives.

Subject Committees and Coordination:

The teachers of a single subject shall form a committee that meets under the supervision of the person in charge of the school in each academic term, and whenever the need arises, to examine the difficulties that prevent the pupils from comprehending the subject and to organise a coordinated work plan among the teachers of the subject in order to raise the standard of the pupils.

Where a sufficient number of teachers of a single subject is available, the person in charge of the school may select one of them from among those possessing competence and seniority to perform the duties of coordination.

The Coordinator:

a - His Selection:

The person in charge of the school shall assign one of the teachers of the subject to perform the duties of coordination. The Head of the Region may reconsider this assignment or cancel it whenever the need arises. The weekly teaching load of the coordinator shall be reduced at the rate of one teaching period for every fifteen periods of the total periods of each subject across all curriculum years in the school. And one period for every fraction exceeding one half, provided that the number of coordination hours for each subject does not exceed five periods weekly.

b - His Duties:

 Assisting the person in charge in supervising the organisation of the annual schedule for the distribution of the subjects which he coordinates. Agreeing with the teachers of the subject on the general steps for methods of teaching and evaluation. Monitoring assignments and the questions of tests and examinations and the bases for their correction. Attending lessons accompanied by the person in charge or alone pursuant to a written assignment from the person in charge, provided that he discusses his remarks with the teachers of the subject after the dismissal of the pupils or in a special meeting. Organising mutual attendance of lessons among the teachers of a single subject in consultation with the person in charge, with a view to exchanging expertise. Holding monthly meetings for the teachers of a single subject. Inspecting the preparation notebook of each of the teachers of the subject when the person in charge so requests. Organising a special register in which he records a summary of his work, including attendance of lessons, meetings, and proposals, provided that the person in charge of the school inspects it and signs it.

Excursions:

The school administration, upon the proposal of the subject teachers, may organise excursions or visits to technical institutions, factories, productive farms, or archaeological, tourist, and geographical sites outside school hours and after the written consent of the pupils' guardians to bear all liability arising from such visits or excursions.

 However, if circumstances require carrying out the visit or excursion during school hours, the said administration shall obtain the written consent of the pupils' guardians to bear all liability arising from such excursion or visit. In both cases, prior approval must be obtained from the Head of the Educational Region.

1 - The teaching staff shall rely upon the books and references available in the school library or elsewhere and shall encourage the students to read.

2 - Teachers of languages, literature, and social and applied sciences shall require their pupils, at least once every two months, to submit summaries of what they have read in reading books, which shall be discussed in the classroom, and the teacher shall express his remarks on each of them and return them to their owner.

The school textbook issued by the Center for Educational Research and Development shall be mandatorily adopted in the curriculum subjects and years.

Any other work which the school principal deems necessary to add shall be subject to the approval of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports after consulting the opinion of the said Center.

A teachers' council shall be formed in the school, composed of the person in charge as chairman and the rest of the teaching staff therein as members.

One of them, upon assignment by the person in charge, shall undertake the recording of the discussions and the organisation of the minutes, which shall be signed by the chairman and the members present and communicated to those absent from among them upon their return to work in order to be implemented and acted upon.

The teachers' council shall examine educational affairs, and it shall not be permissible for it to examine non-school matters or for anyone other than the teaching staff in the school to attend its sessions. Decisions shall be taken by majority vote, and the chairman shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie.

Administrative affairs, however, shall fall within the competence of the person in charge of the school alone. The teachers' council shall meet outside working hours in ordinary sessions at least once every month upon convocation by its chairman and prior to the date of holding the term school tests, and it shall meet in extraordinary sessions pursuant to a written request from at least one third of the members, or upon convocation by the person in charge of the school stating the date of this meeting and the agenda, and the convocation or request shall be kept in the school archives, provided that the convocation is communicated to the members at least two days prior to the date of the meeting, and in emergency cases the person in charge may convoke the teachers' council for an immediate meeting.

If the absence is partial for certain teaching hours, every five hours of absence shall be counted as one day of absence, and if the pupil is late by a few minutes without a legitimate excuse, he shall be permitted to enter the classroom provided that the appropriate penalty is imposed upon him.

In the event that the pupil violates the laws and regulations of the school and public morals, one of the following penalties shall be imposed upon him:

1- A verbal warning.

2 - A written warning, which consists of a deterrent caution.

3 - A written reprimand, which consists of a stricter deterrence of the pupil for persisting in the path of error.

4 - A registered notice by letter to the guardian of the pupil signed by the person in charge of the school, which consists of placing the pupil under close supervision.

5 - Temporary expulsion from the school, which is a threat of final expulsion, and the total temporary expulsion may not exceed fifteen days in the year.

6 - Final expulsion from the school.

7 - And the person in charge of the school may, in addition to the penalty, take educational measures that assist in rectifying the behaviour of the pupil, such as depriving him of participating in school activities.

The person in charge of the school shall impose:

- The penalty from 1 to 4 of the preceding Article and execute it, and the teaching staff members concerned with the pupil shall also impose and execute it after the approval of the person in charge. The person in charge shall undertake the recording of these violations in the pupil's file and notify his guardian of the penalty imposed and the reasons therefor.

- The Guidance and Discipline Council in the school shall impose any of the penalties set forth in the preceding Article, and the penalty of temporary expulsion for a period not exceeding three days shall be executed automatically.

As for all other cases of temporary and final expulsion, the penalty shall not become effective until after the approval of the Director of Primary Education, who has the right to amend it.

The pupil must be given, during the execution of one of the penalties of temporary expulsion, useful schoolwork that can be completed during the period of the penalty.

In organising school tests for the various curricular years, the provisions of Decision No. 208/M/2000 dated 22/04/2000 annexed to these Internal Regulations (Document No. 3) and subsequent decisions on the same subject shall apply.

The person in charge of the school must nominate for the official examinations for the Intermediate Certificate all pupils who are pursuing their studies in the class of this Certificate, and he may refrain from nominating for these examinations a pupil who fails to attend at a rate exceeding 20% of the total annual school days.

The doorkeepers, servants and wage-earners of the school shall obey the orders of the person in charge thereof or whoever deputises for him in whatever relates to the school, and in particular ensuring its cleanliness, preserving its furniture, guarding its entrances especially during the daily break periods, safeguarding the food of the pupils placed in their custody and their books and supplies deposited with them, as well as carrying official mail.

1 - The minimum working hours for permanent or daily-paid servants is 48 hours per week distributed over six working days in the week.

2 - The person in charge of the school shall organise the working hours of the servants and wage-earners assigned to carry out the cleaning of the school before, during and after official working hours according to a schedule which he shall post in the administration room and notify to the persons concerned.

3 - The servant shall refer to the person in charge of the school in everything that relates to the pupils.

4 - The person assigned to clean the school buildings must carry out the following:

a - Sweeping all rooms, halls, stairs and corridors daily after the end of official working hours.

b - Cleaning the rooms, halls, stairs and corridors with water and soap at least once a week and whenever the need arises.

c - Cleaning the drinking fountains and various facilities daily.

d - Cleaning the lavatories and sanitary fixtures daily while placing special disinfectants to prevent odours and germs.

e - Daily cleaning and wiping of tables, cupboards, seats, curtains and other furniture.

f - Washing the glass facades once every two weeks.

g - Weekly cleaning of doors, windows and banisters.

h - Cleaning the carpets daily.

i - Cleaning the lighting fixtures once a month.

j - Washing and cleaning laboratory instruments and equipment under the supervision of the science teachers and the persons in charge of the scientific laboratories.

k - Cleaning the playgrounds and roofs and tending to the gardens, saplings and everything related to the school.

l - Locking the doors and windows after finishing the cleaning.

5 - The permanent servant must, in addition to the duties mentioned above, inspect the school once a day during the short holiday and once a week during the summer holiday. He must inform the person in charge of the school of any emergencies that arise in the school.

6 - Doorkeepers of schools, servants and permanent workers therein are prohibited from engaging in commercial activities of buying and selling or assigning anyone to deputise for them therein.

The person in charge of the school is prohibited from holding public parties to which parents are invited except with prior permission from the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports, with the exception of Independence Day, Teacher's Day, Tree Day, sports events, exhibitions of drawing and handicrafts belonging to the pupils, and parties honouring successful and excelling pupils and the teaching staff in the school.
School staff members are strictly prohibited from conducting lotteries and selling books and school supplies of various kinds.

Teaching staff members are prohibited from going on outings or trips with the pupils on holidays without the written approval of their parents to bear all responsibility resulting therefrom and subject to the written approval of the person in charge therefor.

They are also prohibited, under penalty of liability, from assigning any of the pupils of their school to perform work unrelated to education or to render any private services inside or outside the school.
Teaching staff members may not at all bring into the school any book, bulletin, magazine or publication that is not closely related to the nature of their school work.

Public school staff members must abide by the following in all their correspondence:

1 - Following the rule of administrative hierarchy.

2 - Mentioning the subject at the top of the letter.

3 - Mentioning the place of work: the school, the district (Qada) and the locality.

4 - Mentioning the financial number.

5 - Writing the name clearly under the signature as it appears in the decree of appointment.

6 - Mentioning the date.

A staff member transferred from one school to another must lodge with the Regional Education Office a notice of commencement of work in which he mentions the number and date of the transfer document and attaches thereto a certificate of departure from the person in charge of his former school mentioning the date of departure, or from the Mukhtar of the village if he was a sole teacher, showing the date he left work. In the event of his transfer to a school in which there is another teacher or more, the person in charge thereof shall submit this notice of commencement.

As for the new sole teacher, he shall submit the notice of commencement of work after it is certified by the Mukhtar, mentioning therein the number of the decree relating to the appointment and the decision of assignment and their dates, and in the event of his assignment to a school in which there is more than one teacher, the person in charge thereof shall submit this notice of commencement.

Public school buildings, their playgrounds and their contents may not be used for anything other than official school work except in the special cases provided for in the laws and regulations in force and after the approval of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports therefor.

The persons in charge of public schools in which there are official communication devices (telephone, internet...) must refrain from using these devices for anything other than the interest of the service.

No staff member of the public primary and intermediate schools may leave Lebanese territory during school holidays before obtaining written permission from the Director of Primary Education, and in this case he must submit an application in accordance with the rules prior to the date of travel, mentioning therein the places to which he intends to travel and the reasons calling therefor.
Physical education teachers shall be subject to this Decision in all matters that do not conflict with the laws and regulations governing their affairs.

Teaching staff must attend to the health of the pupils, monitor their seating and their general conduct, and remain alert to pathological conditions that may spread among them, in order to take the necessary preventive and therapeutic measures.

The person in charge of the school shall supervise the execution of the various maintenance, sanitation, restoration and repair works decided upon for the school building, ensure their execution during weekly days off and school holidays, and refrain from suspending the school on working days except with prior permission from the Head of the Educational Region.

At the end of each academic year, the person in charge of the school shall draw up a report on the progress of work in his school, submit it to his superiors, and send a copy thereof to the Educational Inspectorate.

Paymasters in public schools may be absent from their workplace for two days per month after obtaining permission from the person in charge of the school, and such absence shall be recorded in the attendance register.

The provisions of this Decision shall apply to contracted teachers in all matters that do not conflict with the provisions of the special texts relating to them, regardless of the nature of such contracting.

If the guardian is unable to submit the pupil's identity card or civil status extract, any other evidentiary document, such as a mukhtar's certificate or a baptismal certificate, may be accepted for a period not exceeding one academic year, with the approval of the Educational Region.

Former pupils who wish to re-register themselves in the same school shall be exempted from submitting the school certificate or the report card, and the identity card or a certified copy thereof, provided for in Article 3 of these Bylaws.
In cases where vacant places remain in the school, non-Lebanese pupils may be admitted.
All texts that contravene the provisions of this Decision or that are inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Decision shall be published and notified where needed.

Scope of the Law:

This Law comprises the regulation of the telecommunications services sector in the Lebanese territory, and the rules for transferring it or transferring its management wholly or partially to the private sector, including the role of the State in this sector.

Definition of Terms:

The following words and expressions shall have the meanings assigned against each of them:

- "Minister" or "Ministry": the Minister or Ministry responsible for telecommunications, unless otherwise stated.

- "Authority": the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority in Lebanon established pursuant to this Law.

- "Members": the individuals appointed to the Authority by the Council of Ministers.

- "Company": LIBAN TELECOM.

- "Network": an integrated system of equipment used to provide one or more telecommunications services.

- "Radio Frequencies" or "Radio Frequency Spectrum": radioelectric waves propagating naturally along the radio spectrum and used to transmit and/or receive information.

- "Allocation": the allotment by the Authority of parts of the radio frequency spectrum for various uses and services.

- "Assignment": the designation by the Authority of specific radio frequencies that a Licensee is entitled to use in providing a telecommunications service.

- "Information": symbols, signs, writings, sounds, and other data.

- "License": the authorization granted by the Authority to provide telecommunications services and/or to use the radio frequency spectrum.

- "Person": a natural or legal person enjoying legal personality.

- "Service Provider": a person who provides telecommunications services, directly or indirectly.

- "Service Provider with Significant Market Power": a Service Provider who has the practical ability to affect the terms of subscription with regard to price and supply in a given market relating to a telecommunications service as a result of control over essential facilities, or the use of its position in the market; essential telecommunications facilities mean a public service or basic infrastructure that is exclusively or predominantly available from a single Service Provider or a limited number of them, and which cannot practically be substituted economically or technically in order to provide the service.

- "Licensee": a person who holds a valid License duly granted to him by the Authority.

- "Subscriber": a person who receives telecommunications services and pays a fee for a period of time and pursuant to an agreement concluded by him or the terms of which he accepts as set by the Service Provider.

- "User": any person who uses a telecommunications service, whether such person pays or does not pay consideration for this service.

- "Interconnection": the physical and logical linking between telecommunications networks, whether of one or more Service Providers, in order to enable the Users or Subscribers of one to communicate among themselves or with the Users or Subscribers of another Service Provider, and the linking of any service whatsoever with any other service across networks, whether locally or internationally.

- "Telecommunications Services": the transmission or routing of Information, or the combination of both functions, by wire, radioelectricity, optical means, electromagnetic systems, or any other means, and the provision of infrastructure relating to telecommunications for these purposes.

- "Public Telecommunications Network": a wholly interconnected and integrated telecommunications system consisting of various transmission and switching means and used to provide Basic Telephone Service and other Public Telecommunications Services.

- "Public Telecommunications Services": telecommunications services provided to the public or to a group of people so as to be generally available, including Basic Telephone Service.

- "Basic Telephone Service": the provision of a local telecommunications service for the purpose of transmitting a fixed, two-way or multi-directional, live voice telephone service over a Public Telecommunications Network.

- "Private Telecommunications Services": telecommunications services provided to specific groups of employees, whether within the confines of a single building or adjacent premises, or within the confines of non-adjacent buildings by connecting them through a Leased Line Service, for transmission and reception by a single person or by his employees, or by persons belonging to a single group or by their employees.

- "Local Telecommunications Services": telecommunications services provided within the Lebanese territory.

- "International Telecommunications Services": telecommunications services provided between Lebanon and abroad.

- "Leased Line Service": a telecommunications service during which the Subscriber uses, exclusively and for a specified period of time, infrastructure in addition to a specified capacity, provided that the Subscriber pays consideration therefor calculated on the basis of the full capacity rather than on the basis of the quantity actually used by him. Leased Line Service may be provided as a Private Telecommunications Service or a Public Telecommunications Service.

- "Value-Added Services":

a - Restructuring the form, content, code, protocol, or any aspect of the Information transmitted by a User or Subscriber via telecommunications, without changing its content.

b - Providing Information to a User or Subscriber, including restructuring Information transmitted by them.

c - Offering stored Information for interaction therewith by a User or Subscriber.

- "Telecommunications Equipment": equipment, including computers and software, with the exception of Customer Premises Equipment, used to provide telecommunications services.

- "Customer Premises Equipment": equipment used by a Subscriber benefiting from a Public Telecommunications Service or a Private Telecommunications Service to originate, route, or terminate telecommunications, including handsets whether for wired or wireless communications, facsimile machines, computer modems (Modem), modulation and detection mechanisms, and related equipment and wiring of the Subscriber at the premises where such equipment is installed.

- "Resale": the provision of a telecommunications service to Subscribers, for profit, through another Service Provider.

Any word or expression not given a definition pursuant to this Law shall be interpreted in accordance with the definitions adopted by the Authority on the basis of the international telecommunications treaties to which Lebanon is a party, without limitation, as well as the definitions provided by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).

Powers of the Minister:

A - The Minister shall exercise the following powers:

1 - Laying down the general rules for regulating telecommunications services in Lebanon, supervising implementation through the reports submitted to him by the Authority, and proposing draft laws and draft decrees relating to the telecommunications sector to the Council of Ministers.

2 - Representing Lebanon at official meetings held by international telecommunications organizations.

3 - Proposing the appointment of the Chairman and members of the Authority to the Council of Ministers in accordance with the provisions of Article Seven of this Law.

4 - Designating service providers to participate in international telecommunications organizations, satellite and submarine cable organizations, or other organizations arising from international treaties and agreements, and supervising them.

5 - Approving the decisions of the Board of Directors of the Authority as provided for in the provisions of Articles 10, 11 and 49 of this Law.

6 - Proposing fees for monitoring and managing radio frequencies, to be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.

7 - Proposing fees for the use of radio frequencies, to be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.

B - The Ministry shall be composed of:

- The Directorate General of Posts.

- The Directorate General of Telecommunications.

- The Joint Administrative Service.

- The General Control Service.

- The Directorate General of Telecommunications shall be composed of:

- The Economic Affairs Service.

- The Technical Affairs and Research Service.

- The International Relations Service.

- The Directorate General of Posts shall be composed of:

- The Postal Service.

- The Monitoring Service.

- The Financial Service.

Schedule No. (1) annexed to this Law determines the establishment of positions of the first and second categories.

Establishment of the Authority:

There shall be established pursuant to this Law an Authority enjoying legal personality and administrative and financial autonomy, which shall exercise the powers and functions set forth in this Law, and whose administrative and financial organization shall be determined, and whose Chairman and members shall be appointed, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

- This Authority shall not be subject to the provisions of the General Regulations for Public Institutions, but shall be subject to the ex post audit of the Court of Accounts.

Functions and Powers of the Authority:

1 - The Authority shall undertake:

A - Preparing draft decrees and regulations relating to the implementation of the provisions of this Law and referring them to the Minister, and giving an opinion on draft laws and draft decrees relating to the telecommunications sector.

B - Taking decisions and measures in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

C - Encouraging competition in the telecommunications sector.

D - Organizing tenders and issuing licenses, supervising their proper execution, monitoring them, amending them, enforcing compliance with them, suspending them and revoking them in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the decrees issued in implementation thereof.

E - Laying down interconnection rules and reviewing interconnection contracts upon the request of one or more telecommunications service providers or on the initiative of the Authority.

F - Laying down technical standards and rules for verifying compliance therewith, and establishing and managing the numbering plan.

G - Monitoring the tariffs of service providers with significant market power, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

H - Determining and collecting tariffs and fees in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

I - Implementing this Law within the powers granted to it and laying down the rules and regulations derived therefrom, including laying down the standards and procedures for examining and deciding on complaints and other applications that may arise from this Law.

J - Monitoring practices that restrict competition and ensuring market transparency.

K - Assisting educational and health institutions in implementing their programs through telecommunications and facilitating the access of persons with disabilities to telecommunications services.

L - Acting as a mediator and as an arbitral body to settle disputes arising from the implementation of the provisions of this Law between license holders.

2 - In discharging its responsibility, the Authority shall take into consideration the best international standards relating to the regulation and management of telecommunications service.

3 - The Authority shall adhere to the principle of developing service systems in the telecommunications sector in accordance with the latest technical means and regulatory principles.

To that end, it shall lay down rules for collecting and studying observations and proposals from telecommunications service providers and persons concerned with developing the systems, and resort when necessary to forming advisory committees in accordance with the provisions of Article 10 of this Law.

4 - The Authority shall prepare an annual report on its activities to be submitted to the Council of Ministers through the Minister within the three months following each financial year; this report shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall include a summary of the measures taken by the Authority in execution of the functions entrusted to it, and the extent of its contribution to achieving the objectives set forth in this Law.

Management of the Authority:

1 - The Authority shall be composed of a Chairman and four full-time members, appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister for a term of five years, not subject to renewal or extension, from among holders of a university degree in fields related to telecommunications, economics, business administration, law, finance, engineering or computers and who possess experience in these fields, and none of them may be dismissed or have his service terminated except for the reasons set forth in this Law.

2 - The Authority shall hold its meetings and take decisions by an absolute majority of the members of whom the Authority is legally composed.

Impediments to Appointment:

Subject to the conditions of appointment provided for in Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 dated 12/6/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations) with the exception of the conditions of age and competitive examination, the Chairman and members of the Authority may not be appointed from the following categories:

1 - Anyone who has a direct or indirect interest with any person who provides telecommunications services in Lebanon or to Lebanon, or supplies telecommunications equipment or private subscriber equipment in Lebanon or to Lebanon, or has a direct or indirect relationship with the telecommunications sector in Lebanon.

2 - Anyone who has been declared in cessation of payments or judicially declared bankrupt.

3 - Anyone against whom a disciplinary decision has been issued imposing a penalty other than a warning or a reprimand.

Termination of Membership:

1 - The term of office of each of the Chairman and members of the management of the Authority shall terminate upon the expiry of the term, death, resignation, termination of membership or dismissal.

2 - The term of office of the Chairman or a member shall be terminated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister in the event of gross breach of the duties of office or breach of the conditions specified in Article Seven above, after verification thereof, upon the request of the Minister, by a panel composed of the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the State Council, and the President of the Court of Accounts by a decision taken by it by majority.

3 - In the event of a vacancy in the post of the Chairman or of any of the members, the Council of Ministers shall fill the vacancy for the remaining period within a time limit of one month at most and in accordance with the rules of appointment specified in this Law.

- In the event of a vacancy in the post of the Chairman, the eldest member shall deputize for him.

Allowances:

Each of the Chairman and members of the Authority shall receive a lump-sum monthly allowance to be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Telecommunications and Finance.

Related text: Determining the lump-sum monthly allowance for the Chairman and members of the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority

Staff Regulations:

The Authority shall lay down special regulations for its staff, and it may, when necessary, enlist the assistance of Lebanese or non-Lebanese experts to carry out a specific assignment and for a specified period.

Budget and Financing:

First - Budget:

1 - The Authority shall enjoy administrative and financial autonomy, and shall only be subject to the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts. Its funds shall be managed through a special account opened with the Bank of Lebanon.

2 - The first Authority shall, within three months from the date of its formation, establish special regulations for the management of these funds, provided that they are approved by the Ministers of Telecommunications and Finance.

3 - The Authority shall establish, at least three months prior to the end of each financial year, the budget for the upcoming year and submit it to the Minister, who shall, within thirty days starting from the date of its registration with the competent department at the Ministry, either approve it or refer it to the Council of Ministers for determination.

4 - The Authority shall have the right, starting from the first of January and until the approval of its budget, to collect revenues and disburse expenditures on the basis of the provisional twelfth rule by reference to the figures of the budget of the preceding year.

Second - Financing:

1 - The sources of income of the Authority shall consist of the following revenues:

a - Fees collected by the Authority for licence applications, and annual fees paid by Licensees in consideration of monitoring, examining, supervising and enforcing licences and the Authority carrying out its functions, provided that the total fees collected are proportionate to the total actual cost of regulating the sector and, where necessary, to the total turnover of Public Telecommunications Services Providers.

b - Fees collected for the monitoring and management of radio frequencies, which shall be determined by decrees upon the proposal of the Minister and in accordance with the recommendation of the Authority based on studies demonstrating their proportionality to the actual cost of managing radio frequencies.

c - A percentage determined from the fees for the use of radio frequencies stipulated in Article 17 of this Law by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister, provided that it does not exceed ten percent of the total revenues from the use of these radio frequencies.

d - Unconditional grants and aid from sources that have no direct or indirect interest in the telecommunications sector, subject to the approval of the Council of Ministers.

e - Dues of the Authority held by the Ministry, which shall be transferred from the Treasury account to the special account of the Authority twice a year during the months of February and July.

2 - In addition to the revenues stipulated above, the Authority shall be financed exceptionally and for a maximum period of two years from the date of its establishment, through contributions allocated to it in the General Budget, provided that all operations and costs of the Authority after the expiry of the two-year period shall be financed in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph (1) of Item Second above.

3 - Revenues resulting from tendering shall not fall within the ordinary revenues of the Authority and shall be deposited in the Treasury account.

4 - Any realized annual deficit or surplus shall be carried forward to the budget of the following year of the Authority, provided that such carried-forward surplus does not exceed twenty percent of the budget of the preceding year.

It may provide in its budget for reserves appropriate for its own purposes, provided that such reserves do not exceed fifteen percent of its annual budget.

5 - The surplus of funds resulting from the exercise by the Authority of its functions shall be transferred to the Treasury account every three months.

6 - The accounts of this Authority shall be subject to an internal audit system and to independent auditing by auditing and accounting firms in accordance with the provisions of Article 73 of Law No. 326 dated 28/6/2001 (the 2001 Budget Law).

Publicity of Data:

1 - With the exception of matters affecting commercial secrecy and the principle of competition, the Authority shall make available to the public all data, documents, registers and statements.

Every person wishing to inspect them or obtain copies or reproductions thereof shall have the right to submit a written application, provided that the Authority determines the fee required therefor in proportion to the necessary cost.

2 - The Authority shall publish at the end of each financial year in the Official Gazette and in at least two local newspapers a statement on the status of its assets and holdings and a summary of its budget.

Decisions of the Authority:

The decisions of the Authority shall be subject to the principle of reasoning, and the Authority shall state in the recitals of the decision taken its reasons and objectives.

The decisions of the Authority shall only become effective from the date of their notification or their publication, with reasons, in the Official Gazette.

Methods of Recourse Against Decisions:

1 - Every interested party shall have the right to request a reconsideration of the decisions issued by the Authority within a period of two months from the date of their publication or notification.

The Authority may decide ex officio and within a period of two months from the date of issuance of the decision, or within a period of two months from the date of submission of the request for reconsideration, to revoke the decision, stay its execution, or take any provisional measure to preserve the status quo and prevent the occurrence of any damage until the decision is finally determined administratively or judicially.

2 - The State Council shall have jurisdiction to hear recourses relating to administrative decisions issued by the Authority, provided that the procedures and time limits followed before this jurisdiction are observed.

Disputes between the Authority and its employees, workers or contractors shall fall within the jurisdiction of the judicial courts.

Arbitration clauses, where present in contracts concluded with third parties, shall be observed.

Radio Frequencies:

1 - Radio frequencies are public property that may not be sold, and the leasing thereof or licensing for the use thereof shall be subject to the provisions of this Law. The Authority shall enjoy exclusive authority to manage, allocate and monitor the use of these frequencies.

2 - The Authority may establish an annual plan for the allocation of frequencies used in commercial telecommunications among Service Providers, radio and television broadcasting operations, and radiocommunications belonging to public administrations and public institutions, and other natural and legal persons and amateurs.

The use of radio frequencies for television and radio broadcasting services shall be subject to consultation with the Ministry of Information and/or the concerned administrations and councils pursuant to the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, and any dispute in this regard shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers for adjudication.

3 - The Authority shall publish the application for a licence to use radio frequencies at the expense of the concerned party, in the Official Gazette and in two local newspapers, and in the event that an objection is filed against it, the Authority shall grant the applicant a period of one month to reply.

The Authority shall issue a reasoned decision of acceptance or rejection stating the material facts and the legal grounds warranting the decision.

4 - The Authority may alter the frequencies for the use of which a licence was granted, provided that this does not affect the quality and efficiency of the service, and provided that this is preceded by a notice of not less than three months.

5 - The Authority may revoke the licence without any compensation if the licensed frequencies are not used for a period of six months within one year.

Licensing for the Use of Radio Frequencies:

1 - Whenever possible, and where the provision of a telecommunications service subject to a licence requires the use of the radio frequency spectrum, the Authority shall issue a single licence covering both the provision of telecommunications services and the use of the radio frequency spectrum required for such service.

2 - An application for a licence to use radio frequencies must include information relating to the financial, legal, and technical qualifications that the Authority deems necessary for the applicant to possess in order to establish and operate a station using radio frequencies. The Authority may request the provision of updated information during the period of examination of the application or the provision of additional information during the term of the licence or upon submission of a renewal application.

3 - In the radio frequency allocation plan, the Authority shall adhere to the general policy laid down by the Council of Ministers, the requirements of the sectors utilizing such frequencies, and the recommendations issued by the International Telecommunication Union or by any other competent international organization of which Lebanon is a member.

The Authority shall also take into account, in the exercise of its powers, the approved frequency allocation plans.

Collection of Special Fees for the Use of Radio Frequencies:

The fees for the use of radio frequencies shall be determined by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister and the recommendation of the Authority, and shall be collected directly by the Ministry.

Principle of Equality and Competition:

In order to ensure equality and achieve competition, licences shall be granted to providers of public and private telecommunications services, including basic telephone services, who meet the conditions and requirements determined by the Authority.
