A commercial representative is an agent who, by virtue of his customary independent profession, and without being bound by a contract of hire of services, undertakes negotiations to conclude operations of sale, purchase, lease or the provision of services and, where necessary, performs such acts in the name of producers or merchants and for their account.

A merchant who, for his own account, sells what he purchases pursuant to a contract that includes granting him the capacity of sole representative or distributor on an exclusive basis shall also be deemed a commercial representative.

Paragraph added by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 9639 dated 6/2/1975

Effective from the date of entry into force of this Law, and subject to the preservation of prior acquired rights and the observance of reciprocity which non-Lebanese commercial representatives are required to prove, a commercial representative must be Lebanese, and must have a place of business in Lebanon.

If the commercial representative is a company, it is required:

A - In partnerships and limited liability companies:

That the majority of the partners be Lebanese, the majority of the capital belong to Lebanese nationals, and the person holding the right to sign on its behalf be Lebanese.

B - In joint-stock companies:

That its shares be registered, the majority of its capital belong to Lebanese nationals, and two-thirds of the members of its board of directors, its general manager, or the person delegated by the chairman of the board of directors or the general manager for all or part of its management functions, all be Lebanese.

Every commercial representation contract concluded after the entry into force of this Legislative Decree must be in writing and may be for a fixed or indefinite term.

This contract may include a clause restricting the representation to a sole representative, or stipulating a guarantee by the representative for those with whom he contracts for the account of his principal (del credere), or a clause for the consignment of goods for the purpose of delivering them to customers.

A clause restricting representation shall not be enforceable against third parties unless the agent gives notice thereof by registering it in the Commercial Register, and it shall not apply to foodstuffs with the exception of items of special consumption which are determined by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of a committee formed of the Director General of Economy and Trade and a representative of each of the Syndicate Chamber of Commercial Representatives in Lebanon, the National General Federation of Cooperative Associations, the General Confederation of Lebanese Workers, and the Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

This committee shall be appointed by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers.

The applicability of exclusive commercial representation to foodstuffs may be restored by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the committee mentioned in the preceding paragraph when economic conditions so permit.

An annual fee of $500 shall be levied on every commercial representation contract registered with the Ministry of Economy and Trade upon initial registration, and $165 annually in the years following registration.

A commercial representative is independent in carrying out the acts of his agency and organising his customary commercial activity, and he shall be entitled in particular:

1 - To carry out commercial acts for his own account.

2 - To accept the representation of new principals without referring to his principal, provided that the subject matter of the new representation does not conflict with or compete with the first representation.

3 - To select sub-representatives for himself or employ employees whose commissions or wages he pays himself and whose relations are confined to him to the exclusion of his principals.

In such case, these sub-representatives shall be subject either to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or to the provisions of the Labour Law, according to their status.

A commercial representation contract shall be deemed concluded for the mutual benefit of the contracting parties.

Accordingly, its termination by the principal, without fault on the part of the representative or other legitimate cause, entitles the latter, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, to claim compensation equal to the damage sustained by him and his lost profit.

Likewise, the commercial representative shall be entitled, even in the event of the expiry of the contract upon the arrival of its term, and notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, to claim compensation to be assessed by the courts if his activity has led to manifest success in promoting his principal's trademark or in increasing the number of his customers and the non-consent of his principal to renew the representation contract prevented him from reaping the profit from that success.

Text added by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 9639 dated 6/2/1975

1 - A special register shall be organised at the Ministry of Economy and Trade for companies and establishments wishing to engage in commercial representation in Lebanon, in which they shall be obliged to register, and a folio therein shall be opened:

A - For every company whose representation contract has been registered by its agent in his special register effective from the date of entry into force of this Law.

B - For every company that is the subject of a lawsuit pursuant to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 34 dated 5/8/1967 and its amendment.

C - For every company against which a judgment has been rendered that has not been executed.

2 - The following two caveats may be entered on the folio of each company:

A - A caveat of a lawsuit brought against it under Legislative Decree No. 34 dated 5/8/1967 and its amendment, to be recorded immediately upon the filing of the statement of claim, a copy of which shall be served on the Ministry of Economy and Trade (the Special Register).

B - A caveat of a final judgment rendered against it under Legislative Decree No. 34 dated 5/8/1967 and its amendment.

3 - A new representative may represent a company that has a caveat of a lawsuit on its folio and register its agency in his special commercial register, provided that he shall be compelled, within three months from the date of issuance of a final and binding judgment against this company under Legislative Decree No. 34 dated 5/8/1967 and its amendment, to choose between:

- Executing the judgment on behalf of the judgment debtor company while reserving his right of recourse against the latter.

- Permanently waiving the representation of this company and accepting the striking off of its agency from his special register.

4 - A company against which a final and binding judgment has been rendered shall be prohibited from being represented in Lebanon unless it executes the judgment rendered against it itself or its new representative executes this judgment while reserving his right of recourse against it.

5 - A former representative shall be entitled, in the event that a caveat of a final and binding judgment under Legislative Decree No. 34 dated 5/8/1967 and its amendment is recorded on the folio of the company he used to represent, to notify the content of the judgment to the Customs Administration so that it does not permit the clearance of imported goods produced by the judgment debtor company except after the importer thereof produces a certificate proving the removal of the caveat from the company's folio.

Notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, the courts of the place where the commercial representative exercises his activity shall be deemed competent to hear disputes arising from the commercial representation contract.

This Legislative Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette and its provisions shall apply to representation contracts concluded prior to the date of its entry into force, whether in writing or established by other means of proof admissible under the previous legislation.

Clause 7 - Specifications of Classrooms

The specifications of a classroom shall be as set forth below, provided that these specifications are supplemented by the Guiding Manual issued by the Ministry of

Education and Higher Education, which shall serve as the reference for the general design of school buildings.

c - It is prohibited to make lighting openings facing the internal corridor of the school, except for upper openings for ventilation and lighting of the corridors.

Fiscal stamp duty is imposed on:

1- Instruments of whatever form, whatever the nationality of the signatories thereto, and whatever their place of residence. The duty is chargeable on the instruments themselves, and on all signed copies, transcripts, abstracts, and extracts taken therefrom. The duty is chargeable anew, where the law provides otherwise, upon the renewal of such instruments or the extension of their effect, whether the renewal or extension takes place expressly or impliedly.

2 - Writings which do not constitute instruments in themselves, but which are capable of being relied upon as evidence and as a means of claim or defence. The duty is chargeable on these writings only when they are produced as written evidence before an administrative or judicial authority.

3 - Other writings which this Legislative Decree or the Schedules annexed hereto expressly provide shall be subject to the duty.

4 - Instruments and writings executed abroad or at the premises of foreign embassies or consulates, when they are used in Lebanese territory outside such premises and consulates by individuals.

And they shall be subject to the duty pursuant to the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the Schedules annexed hereto.

For the application of the provisions of this Legislative Decree, instruments mean signed writings which constitute documents proving legal acts, whether such documents are official or under private signature, permanent or temporary, including, by way of example and not limitation:

1- Agreements and contracts.

2 - Undertakings and guarantees.

3 - Acknowledgments and waivers.

4 - Releases, receipts, and quittances.

5 - Instruments of bequest and gift.

6- Title deeds, and instruments creating real rights.

7- Commercial papers of various kinds.

8- Securities (shares and debentures).

9- Transport tickets of all kinds.

10- Invoices of various kinds.

In relation to instruments, an initial, a printed signature, a fingerprint, or the seal of an establishment, as well as any unsigned phrase indicating payment or discharge, is deemed equivalent to a signature.

Instruments and writings executed abroad or at the premises of foreign embassies or consulates are deemed to have been used in Lebanese territory when:

- They are produced for any reason before an administrative or judicial authority, or any official formality is carried out in respect of them to grant them an executory formula.

- They are dealt with by way of sale and purchase, exchange, acceptance, guarantee, warranty, transfer, or any other civil or banking transaction.

- Their execution, collection, placing into execution, or collection is commenced, whatever the form and means.

- Their texts, abstracts, or extracts taken therefrom are recited in an official document, or annexed to an official document for purposes of proof.

The following fall outside the scope of the duty:

1- Internal writings exchanged between the departments of a single establishment, or between its employees, or between it and its branches, for purposes of accounting or internal work organisation, provided that they do not bear the signature of those dealing with the establishment such as suppliers, agents, customers, or others.

2 - Tickets and cards subject to the entertainment tax.

3 - Writings which do not constitute instruments in themselves and do not fall within the categories of writings provided for in Article One of this Law.
Instruments and writings whose exemption is expressly provided for in the Schedules annexed to this Legislative Decree and in special laws are exempted from the fiscal stamp duty.

Unless the law provides otherwise, the duty falls due from the occurrence of the event giving rise to the right in accordance with the following provisions:

1 - Instruments, and their copies, transcripts, abstracts, and extracts taken therefrom within a time limit not exceeding five working days from the date of

their execution and signature.

Provided that this time limit shall apply to instruments and writings to which the State, municipalities, and public establishments are a party thereto as from the date of notifying the concerned party of the approval.

2 - Writings which do not constitute instruments in themselves and are produced as written evidence before an administrative or judicial authority - upon their production.

3 - Other writings submitted to or issued by an administrative or judicial authority - upon their submission to the authority or their delivery by

the authority to the interested parties.

4 - Instruments and writings executed abroad or at the premises of embassies or consulates - upon their use in Lebanon.

The date recorded on the instrument is relied upon to determine the date on which the right to the duty arises. Where the date is not recorded thereon, it falls to the competent department to determine it on the basis of the content of the instrument, its intended use, and the presumptions and evidence it gathers.

If that is not possible, the date of the day preceding the legal time limit for seizing the instrument is relied upon

The validity or utility of the instrument has no effect on the arising of the right to the duty, which remains due notwithstanding the nullity of the instrument or its being vitiated by a defect or devoid of utility.

Proportional duty is due on all commercial and non-commercial transactions taking place between Lebanon and abroad which are effected by telegraph, telephone, wireless, correspondence, or by any other means, and the fiscal stamp duty is levied on customs declarations relating to imported goods, commodities, and materials only, which are submitted to the Customs Administration for the purpose of taking delivery on the ground that they constitute in themselves proof of commercial agreements in all their forms, either by paying it in cash to the customs offices or by affixing the stamp to the declaration, according to the wish of the concerned parties, and in the case of cash payment the customs offices must open a special account for the amounts levied from the fiscal stamp duty and endorse the customs declarations to indicate its collection and its amount with mention of the number and date of the receipt.

As for the duty due on other transactions which are not executed by way of importation and customs declarations, the duty thereon is paid by affixing the fiscal stamp to the contracts relating thereto which remain in the possession of the party resident in Lebanon.

Contracts relating to the export and transit trade in all its forms, foreign currencies, gold and all other precious metals, raw jewellery, and fuels delivered to aircraft are exempted from the fiscal stamp duty.

And this Law shall enter into force as from the date of entry into force of Law No. 1/70 dated 19/1/70.

The fiscal stamp duty is of two kinds: proportional and fixed.

All instruments and writings that expressly or implicitly involve a specific sum of money shall be subject to the proportional duty, unless they are exempted or subject to the fixed duty in accordance with the provisions of the schedules annexed to this Legislative Decree.

- Notwithstanding any other text, the transactions of arbitration chambers in Lebanon shall be subject to the proportional duty.

1- Deposits and guarantees refunded to their owners.

2 - Advances and loans .

3 - Sums unduly collected that are refunded to those entitled thereto.

4 - Sums paid to a foreign state or to an international organisation by way of assistance, contribution, or subscription.

- Allocations of public authorities and salaries and wages of employees of the State, municipalities, and public institutions, and allowances, grants, bonuses, and assistance of whatever kind attached thereto, shall be exempted from the duty.

5 - Contributions paid by the State to public institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities, and other legal persons of a public nature and non-profit bodies.

Stamping machines must satisfy at least the following technical conditions and specifications:

Subject to the provisions relating to the methods of payment and collection of the duty, the fiscal stamp duty shall be due by the person from whom the chargeable event giving rise to the right emanated in accordance with the provisions of Article 7 of this Law.

In the event that the said event emanated from several persons, all of them shall be deemed jointly and severally liable for the payment of the duty and the fine, where applicable, without the multiplicity of signatures resulting in the multiplicity of the duty, unless there are duplicates or copies to which the provisions of the first Article of this Law apply. Any person who accepts or deals with instruments or writings that contravene the provisions of this Law shall remain jointly and severally liable with the offender for the payment of the duty and the fine.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding Article 55, the fiscal stamp duty shall be due:

1- On amounts paid by the State, municipalities, and public institutions to their creditors as set forth in Article 14, by the person entitled to the amount paid.

2- On agreements and contracts concluded by the State, municipalities, and public institutions with third parties, by such third party in respect of the copy or copies pertaining to him.

3 - On other instruments and writings issued by the State, municipalities, and public institutions and subject to the duty in accordance with the provisions of the schedules annexed to this Legislative Decree - by the person for whose benefit the said instruments and writings are issued.

4 - On insurance contracts and insurance premiums, by the insured persons through the insurance institutions.

5 - On receipts and discharges, by the persons to whom they are given.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply to conventions and contracts which the State, municipalities, and public institutions with international organisations, foreign governments, and institutions affiliated with them.

As for the agreements and contracts previously concluded by the State, municipalities, and public institutions with the aforementioned foreign entities and which are still under liquidation, they shall be exempted from the fiscal stamp duty on the copy or copies pertaining to these entities of the said agreements and contracts and on all other instruments and writings mentioned in this Article.

- Imposing an internal consumption duty on certain goods concurrently with the reduction of the customs duty and subject to not exceeding this reduction in accordance with the requirements of the Agreement to Facilitate and Develop Trade Exchange among Arab States to which Lebanon has acceded, and as required by the Association Agreement with the European Union Member States, and the Agreement of Accession to the World Trade Organization upon their ratification.

Officials of the State, municipalities, and public institutions who execute for the benefit of third parties instruments and writings subject to the proportional or fixed duty shall be personally liable for the non-payment of the duty or any part thereof and shall be obliged to pay the fine, while the duty remains due by the interested parties.

As for the makers of the instruments and writings provided for in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the preceding Article, they shall remain liable for the payment of the duty and the fine, where applicable, jointly and severally with those by whom the duty is legally due.

No official may receive by hand instruments or writings submitted to the State, municipalities, and public institutions unless the due stamps are affixed thereto or they bear an indication that the duty has been paid thereon.

Officials to whom instruments or writings contravening the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law are sent by mail shall forward them through their hierarchical superiors to the competent financial office, within a time limit not exceeding one month, for the collection of the duty and the fine.

The provisions of the preceding Article 58 shall apply to Notaries Public in respect of instruments and writings which they are requested to authenticate, or to reproduce the texts, summaries, or extracts taken therefrom in an official deed, or to annex thereto.

The competent fiscal stamp duty inspectors and their superiors shall have the right to inspect, at government departments, municipalities, public and private institutions, and individuals, all instruments, writings, accounting records, and registers in order to verify the implementation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

None of the aforementioned, not even government departments, may invoke professional secrecy so as to prevent the officials from exercising their right of inspection. However, the said officials may not inspect at banks instruments and writings the inspection of which would lead to a violation of the Banking Secrecy Law, to the exclusion of other instruments and writings.

The right of inspection may only be exercised by the competent officials during official working hours.

However, in emergency cases, an investigation may be conducted outside official working hours with the authorisation of the head of the competent unit.

The officials referred to in Article 60 may seize instruments and writings contravening this Legislative Decree which they may find with a private institution or individuals, provided that they give a receipt therefor or a certified copy thereof if necessary.

However, if seizure is impracticable due to the large number of documents, they shall be sealed with red wax, provided that an official report of the facts is drawn up.

If such instruments and writings are found at a government department, municipality, or public institution, the competent official shall suffice with taking cognisance thereof and shall draw up an official report to that effect, and the competent financial office shall officially request them in order to take the necessary measures in respect thereof.

The officials referred to in Article 60 shall be bound by professional secrecy in accordance with the provisions of Article 579 of the Penal Code. These officials shall be provided with special identity cards given to them after taking the legal oath before the competent judicial authority, and they must produce their cards before commencing to exercise the right of inspection.

Whoever knowingly uses, sells, or attempts to sell previously used fiscal stamps shall be punished by imprisonment from 15 days to two months and by a pecuniary penalty from 25000 to 100000 Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Whoever counterfeits or attempts to counterfeit the special die placed in the stamping machines provided for in Article 40 of this Legislative Decree, as well as whoever counterfeits or attempts to counterfeit the impression of that die, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 450 and 451 of the Penal Code.

Whoever counterfeits or forges, or attempts to counterfeit or forge, fiscal stamps, or knowingly uses counterfeited or forged stamps, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 450 and 451 of the Penal Code.

Whoever enters false or erroneous information in the register provided for in Article 32 or in Article 52 of this Legislative Decree, or omits to enter correct information that ought to have been entered, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 461 and 462 of the Penal Code.

Whoever forcibly prevents or attempts to prevent the officials charged with recording contraventions of this Legislative Decree from performing the duties of their office, or treats them with violence or severity, or subjects them to contempt, slander, or defamation in any manner whatsoever, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 381 and following of the Penal Code.
The officials charged with recording contraventions of this Legislative Decree are entitled to establish the misdemeanours and felonies provided for in this Chapter.

The fines imposed by the Administration may be combined with the penalties adjudicated by the courts in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Articles and the relevant provisions of the Penal Code.

The acquittal of the offender of the offence attributed to him in accordance with the provisions of Articles 83 and following shall not entail the revocation by the Administration of the fine imposed on him in accordance with the law.

The payment of the fiscal stamp duty by way of affixing stamps or by way of placing the stamp impression or the visa or by way of periodic payment shall be deemed final, and an application for the refund of the said duty shall not be accepted thereafter on the ground of the nullity of the instrument or writing, or its uselessness, or for any other reason.

Subject to the provisions of Article 91 of this Law, the fiscal stamp duty paid into the Treasury fund in advance on instruments or writings prior to their drawing up, or on transactions prior to their occurrence, may be refunded if it is established that those instruments and writings were not drawn up or that those transactions did not occur, and the rightful claimant submits an application for refund accompanied by the supporting documents prior to the expiry of one year from the date of payment of the duty.

Distributors licensed in accordance with the provisions of Article 23 are entitled to apply for the replacement of the fiscal stamps delivered to them with others if they are damaged on their premises for reasons beyond their control, or if it appears that they are unfit for use due to a defect in manufacture, an error in printing, or for any other similar reason. The application for replacement shall not be accepted unless accompanied by the stamps requested to be replaced, without the distributor being able to plead their destruction, loss, or any other reason for failing to deliver them.

By decision of the Director General of Finance, a committee of three officials shall be formed to inspect the stamps requested to be replaced with a view to verifying the seriousness and validity of the application and that the said stamps have not been used or begun to be used.

The Head of the Treasury Department shall decide on the application for replacement on the basis of the minutes of the said committee.
None of the members of the committee provided for in the preceding Article 94 may participate in the operation of destroying the replaced stamps.

Subject to the provisions of the following Articles, the fiscal stamp duty, together with the fines attached thereto, shall lapse by the passage of five years from the date the right thereto arose or from the end of the time limit legally prescribed for its payment into the Treasury fund in the cases where the law provides for its payment in cash.

The prescription provided for in the preceding Article 96 shall be suspended in respect of instruments that create a legal bond or a creditor-debtor relationship throughout the duration of the existence of the bond or relationship.

The prescription provided for in the preceding Article 96 shall be interrupted:

- By recording the contravention and establishing it in minutes with the knowledge of the offender.

- By notifying the taxpayer of his obligation to pay the duty and the fine.

- By pursuing the recovery of the duty and the fine.

Every person who draws up or receives instruments or writings subject to the fiscal stamp duty on the occasion of his carrying on a commercial or industrial activity, a liberal profession, or any other permanent work, shall retain such of those instruments and writings as remain with him or devolve upon him for a period of five years starting from the date of their drawing up or the end of the legal bond or the creditor-debtor relationship which they create; however, with respect to institutions subject to the mandatory periodic payment method and institutions that apply for the stamping of their instruments and writings or use stamping machines, the retention period shall begin starting from the date of the end of the time limit prescribed for the payment of the duty into the Treasury fund, unless they are of the kind that creates a legal bond or a creditor-debtor relationship, in which case the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply thereto.
Every taxpayer is entitled to object to the duty and the fine imposed on him pursuant to the provisions of this Legislative Decree if he finds therein an error, unfairness, or a violation of the law.

The objection shall be submitted to the competent financial office within a time limit of one month starting from the date of notification of the taxpayer in accordance with the procedures prescribed in Article 65 of this Legislative Decree. However, if the objection concerns a purely material error relating exclusively to the entry of figures or names, or to the performance of arithmetical operations, or to double assessment, or to an assessment not originally due, the time limit shall be extended until 31 December of the year following the year in which the duty and the fine were imposed.

If it appears to the competent financial office that the objection submitted in accordance with the preceding Article satisfies the formal conditions and that the grounds contained therein are well-founded wholly or in part in fact and in law, it shall proceed to correct the assessment objected to and shall notify the person concerned thereof in accordance with the procedures.

However, if it considers that the objection is unfounded, it shall inform the party concerned thereof and refer the objection, accompanied by its opinion, to the Head of the Revenue Department, who is entitled, if he finds that its opinion is unfounded, to return the objection to it and request the correction of the assessment on his own responsibility; otherwise, he shall refer the objection together with the opinion of the competent office to the committee provided for in the following Article 103 to examine it and adjudicate thereon.

There shall be formed by decree, upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, the committee for examining objections to the fiscal stamp duty as follows:

- A judge chosen by the Minister of Justice, as Chairman.

- An official of the third category in the Revenue Department.

- A representative of the Merchants Association or the Industrialists Association, as two members, or the Association of Banks, chosen by the Minister of Finance.

- The Head of the Indirect Taxes Office, as Rapporteur.

The secretariat of the committee shall be assumed by one of the tax controllers in the Revenue Department (Indirect Taxes Office) in the capacity of clerk.

The appointment of the clerk shall be effected by decision of the Director General of Finance.

Both the Head of the Revenue Department and the taxpayer concerned are entitled to appeal before the State Council against the decision of the Objections Committee within a time limit of one month starting from the date of being notified of the decision.
The procedures for the recovery of direct taxes and similar duties shall apply to the recovery of the fiscal stamp duty.
The details of execution of this Legislative Decree shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.
Legislative Decree No. 130/L dated 20/12/1933 and all its amendments and all texts relating to stamp duties are repealed.
Article three of the Law of 30/5/1945 relating to the Army stamp duty and the fifth paragraph of Article 12 of the Law of 9/4/1956 and its amendments relating to the reconstruction tax are repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The purpose of this Decree is to define the conditions of application of certain provisions of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12 June of the year 1959 relating to the organisation of Public Administrations and the conditions of liaison between their various bodies.

The tasks mentioned in Article Five of the aforementioned Legislative Decree shall include:

1 - Accounting works.

2 - Personnel affairs.

3 - Supplies.

4 - Legal studies.

5 - Gathering statistical information.

6 - Clerical works.

7 - Inquiries and complaints.

8 - Publications and external relations.

9 - Other tasks determined in the regulations of each Ministry.

Accounting works shall include:

- Preparing the draft budget on the basis of the proposals of the competent units.

- Drawing up draft expenditure commitments on the basis of the requests of the heads of the competent units.

- Drawing up schedules of salaries, wages, allowances, bonuses, and grants. And ensuring the payment of what falls due thereof on time.

- Carrying out liquidation transactions.

- Keeping budget accounts and, in general, transactions relating to preparing the budget, executing it, and keeping its accounts, including materials accounts.

Personnel affairs shall include:

- Participating, where necessary, with the Civil Service Board in preparing competitive examinations and examinations.

- Preparing transactions specific to everything relating to the personal affairs of employees.

- Organising the personal files of employees.

- Preparing advancement schedules on the basis of the proposals of the competent departments and, in general, all transactions relating to the personnel regulations.

Supplies shall include:

- Furniture, clothing, office equipment, printed matter and the like, keeping their records, and taking care of them.

- Maintaining buildings and securing their needs.

- Ensuring the guarding and cleanliness of buildings.

Legal studies shall include:

- Attending to lawsuits and giving opinions on settlement contracts.

- Drafting the texts of agreements in their legal form.

- Providing legal advice.

- Conducting regulatory studies.
Statistical information shall include numerical data and statistics received from the various bodies of the Ministry and required to be sent to the Central Statistical Service.

Clerical works shall include:

- Registering incoming and outgoing mail, and ensuring its distribution.

- Drafting and translation works.

- Archives.

Inquiries and complaints shall include:

- Receiving concerned parties and providing the information and clarifications they need regarding the administrative channels and procedures relating to their transactions and the stages they have reached, and assisting them in completing them.

- Receiving the inquiries and complaints of interested parties, referring them to the competent authorities, and following up on their outcomes.

- Submitting the register of inquiries and complaints at least once a month to the head of the administration and to the competent administrative inspector for review and initialling.

- Notifying concerned parties, where necessary, of the outcomes resulting from their inquiries and complaints.

Publications shall include:

- Managing the bulletins and journals issued by the administration.

- Managing the library.

- Supplying the competent administrations with publicity materials.

- Drafting statements, communiqués, announcements and notices.

External relations shall include:

- Ensuring liaison with the international and foreign body in accordance with the provisions set forth below:

- Preparing the means of participation in international conferences, and contributing to the preparation of international and regional conferences, meetings, and lectures held in Lebanon in agreement with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

The Diwan shall exercise the tasks mentioned in the preceding Articles if the Ministry consists of a single Directorate General. In a Ministry that comprises more than one Directorate General, these tasks shall be distributed between the Diwan and a joint administrative unit directly attached to the Minister, and in a Ministry that consists of a single Directorate General together with other administrations directly attached to the Minister, the Diwan of the Directorate General may be entrusted with exercising the tasks of the joint administrative service.

The joint administrative unit shall carry out the homogeneous administrative works common to the various bodies of the Ministry, in particular the tasks mentioned in paragraphs 1 to 5 of Article Two, and it may also be entrusted with other joint tasks determined by a decision of the competent Minister, whereas the remaining tasks shall be undertaken by the Diwan in each Directorate General or the Secretariat in the other administrations.

The Diwan shall be headed by an employee of at least Category Three who shall be accountable to the Director General, and the joint administrative unit shall be headed by an employee of at least the same Category who shall be accountable to the Minister.

The Diwan and the joint administrative unit shall exchange correspondence with the other bodies of the Ministry in everything relating to the performance of their task, and each of them shall verify the administrative works and documents falling within its competence and received by it from the central administrations in the Ministry, the regional departments, and the public institutions subject to the tutelage or supervision of the Ministry.

The Minister shall delegate, by a decision from him, from among the employees of his Ministry, one employee, or two where necessary, to carry out the works of his private secretariat, provided that the delegation decision includes assigning someone to replace them in carrying out the tasks of their original post.

The task of the secretariat shall be restricted to organising the Minister's interviews, private invitations, and appointments, securing telephone communications, and conducting personal follow-ups. The period of delegation of the employees of the private secretariat shall end upon the end of the period of the Minister's assumption of the affairs of the Ministry.
The Minister's secretariat shall be attached to the joint administrative unit where it exists, and otherwise to the Diwan.

There shall be established in each Ministry that consists of more than one Directorate General, or a Directorate or Service directly attached to the Minister, an advisory committee whose task is to coordinate work between these various units. This committee shall consist of the heads of the aforementioned administrations and shall be chaired by the highest-ranking among them, and in case of equality of rank, by the most senior of them therein.

The Coordination Committee shall study the joint matters among the various units mentioned in the preceding Article that are referred to it by the Minister, including:

- Internal organisation.

- The draft budget and requests for additional appropriations.

- Purchasing and works programmes.

- Personnel matters that presuppose a selection, such as matters of advancement, specialisation, or training.

- Matters of distribution of appropriations for works and supplies.

- Difficulties that may arise between the various bodies of the Ministry.
The proposals of the Coordination Committee shall be submitted to the Minister for decision thereon.

An employee with the rank of Head of Section shall be attached to the Administrative Department in each Governorate to undertake, under the supervision of the Governor and in cooperation with the various Public Administrations represented in the Governorate, the following administrative tasks common to these administrations:

- Executing the part of the budget pertaining to the Governorate.

- Personnel affairs.

- Supplies.

- Managing advance funds.

- Inquiries and complaints.

- And in general, unifying all administrative matters that require handling by the Governor or referral by him, and the Head of Section shall likewise undertake the verification of the administrative works and documents falling within his competence and received by him from the representatives of the administrations in the Governorate.

The Head of Section and the heads of the administrations represented in the Governorate shall exchange all information necessary for the execution of their tasks.

The provisions of Article (31) of this Decree shall apply to the correspondence exchanged between the Head of Section and the administrations represented in the Governorate.

If it appears to the Head of Section, during the execution of his tasks, that it is necessary to take certain measures to coordinate work or to reconsider the transaction he is handling, he shall submit a proposal in this regard either to the Governor or to the competent administration under the supervision of the Governor.

In each district, a civil servant of the fourth category belonging to one of the administrations represented therein shall be entrusted with exercising the powers vested in the head of the governorate section, or some of them.
Communications between Lebanese administrations and international or foreign bodies shall take place in accordance with the following Articles:
Every new relationship between the administrations and the bodies mentioned in the preceding Article shall be established through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

Every Lebanese administration approached by an international or foreign body regarding a new matter shall seek the opinion of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants on the matter or submit the reply through it.

When approached by an international or foreign body regarding a matter relating to a Lebanese administration, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall seek the opinion of this administration on the matter before submitting the reply, and shall then inform it of the reply given.

If the matter relates to foreign assistance of any kind requested by a Lebanese administration or offered by an international or foreign body, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall refer the papers to the Ministry of General Planning to deal with the matter after seeking the opinion of the competent Lebanese administrations thereon. The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply to study or training scholarships offered by international or foreign bodies to civil servants or to non-civil servants who undertake to serve the State where necessary. The Ministry of General Planning shall inform the competent Lebanese administrations of the results achieved in matters of foreign assistance.

Lebanese administrations may not communicate directly with international or foreign bodies except in the following cases:

- Execution of agreements previously concluded or matters previously dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Articles.

- Ensuring ordinary communications with international organisations of which Lebanon is a member.

- Ensuring communications of the Army and the Internal Security Forces with foreign armies through military attachés within the scope of the general policy of the Government.

If, during these direct communications, a matter arises that exceeds the scope of the agreements concluded or the decisions of principle previously taken, the Lebanese administrations shall refer the matter to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and, where necessary, the Ministry of General Planning.

The departments of the district shall exchange correspondence with the departments of the governorate directly, and the departments of the governorate shall exchange correspondence with their central administration:

1 - Through the Governor and accompanied by his opinion if the correspondence is of a nature of principle or of a general character.

2 - Directly if the correspondence relates to ordinary current business or is of a purely in technical nature.
Correspondence exchanged by public administrations shall indicate the unit to which the correspondence must be referred directly to be dealt with.

Each of the director, the head of service, or the heads of other units shall sign all transactions and correspondence falling within his competence unless they affect a general principle, without the need for a special delegation.

In the event of the absence of the director or the head of unit, his highest-ranking subordinate shall deputise for him in all of his duties that do not have a decision-making character or a personal character vested in him by law, following the approval of the immediate superior of the absent civil servant.

For the purpose of applying the provisions of paragraph 7 of Article 7 of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12 June 1959, the director may either resort to the Central Inspection Administration or assign civil servants subordinate to him to inspect the departments covered by his authority.
General and special provisions contrary to the provisions of this Decree or inconsistent with its content are repealed.
This Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette and notified where needed.

The proposed Law concerning the Duties of Dentists, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, has been approved.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
All dentists registered with (the two Dental Associations in Lebanon) shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

A dentist, who works in the service of the individual and of public health, shall practise his profession under the rules of respect for life and for the human person.

It shall be among his duties to support the efforts of the competent authorities in protecting public health and raising its standard.

a - Every dentist shall refrain from practising any profession other than the profession of dentistry. He shall likewise refrain from anything that conflicts with the dignity of this profession or demeans its standing.

b - A dentist shall equip his clinic with the technical means that enable him to treat his patients in a manner that guarantees them prevention and safety.

c - He shall be prohibited, save in limited exceptional cases, from providing treatments, issuing prescriptions, and performing acts that exceed the scope of his professional speciality or surpass the material resources available to him.
A dentist shall, save in cases of force majeure rendering it impossible, provide the necessary first aid and other assistance, where possible, to a patient in danger.

a - A dentist, his collaborators, and his assistants are all bound to respect professional secrecy, subject to cases relating to public safety and to regulations and laws.

Professional secrecy encompasses everything that comes to the knowledge of the dentist during or in the course of the practice of his profession, such as information confided to him by the patient or resulting from his examination of him.

b - In order to preserve professional secrecy, a dentist shall not disclose the personal cards of his patients or the documents or computerised files relating to his clinic, save in judicial cases.

c - When making use of his medical observations in scientific publications, he shall be required to use them in a manner that does not reveal the identity of the patients.

a - A dentist shall be exempted from the duty of professional secrecy when called upon by the judiciary as an expert to examine a patient or to study his file, within the limits of the mission assigned to him.

b - A dentist referred to the Disciplinary Council of the Association shall not be entitled to invoke professional secrecy.

c - Where a dentist is prosecuted in an action brought against him by a patient or his family, he shall be entitled to disclose the facts necessary to establish the truth in self-defence.

d - A dentist shall report to the health authorities every contagious disease where such disease, according to his diagnosis, is included on the list of diseases required by law to be reported.

a - The traditional principles of the dental profession shall apply to all dentists, save in cases where their wording conflicts with a statutory provision.

These principles are:

- The absolute freedom of the patient to choose the dentist.

- The freedom of the dentist to choose the most appropriate treatment for his patient and to issue prescriptions.

- The fees of the dentist shall be agreed upon directly between the dentist and the patient pursuant to a fee agreement issued by the Association. Provided that they shall not be less than the minimum tariff issued by the Dental Association in Lebanon.

- The payment of fees shall be made directly between the doctor and the patient.

b - Insuring institutions shall pay the dentist his fees in full. The Association shall undertake the settlement of any dispute that may arise in this regard.

A dentist shall treat all his patients with the same care and with the same technique, regardless of their origin, customs, family status, or affiliation with a race, nationality, religion, or party, and whatever their state of health, their reputation, and his feelings towards them.
A dentist may not abandon his patients in the event of a public danger unless an official decision is issued by the competent authorities.
It is prohibited to draw up a false report or to issue a certificate of convenience.

A dentist shall broaden the scope of his knowledge and improve it, in particular through participation in continuing education courses organised by the Scientific Committee of the Association and the Continuing Education Committee.

The dental profession may not be exploited for a commercial purpose.

In particular, the following are prohibited:

a - Recourse to direct or indirect advertising means in order to mislead, with the exception of announcing, for a period of one month at most, the commencement of his practice, the transfer of his clinic, the date of his departure on travel, or the date of his return.

b - Publishing articles in publications directed to the public that refer to his work as a dentist and contain his name and address. He shall be entitled to participate, following the approval of the Council of the Association, in scientific discussions specific to dentistry. Provided that he shall be liable to prosecution if, during his participation, he commits a breach of medical ethics.

A dentist shall not be entitled to include on his private professional stationery, in particular on his prescriptions, fee statements, and professional cards, any information other than the following:

a - His given name, surname, and address. His telephone and fax numbers and electronic mail. The days and hours of consultations.

b - The registration number with the Association. His capacity and his speciality recognised by the Ministry of Public Health and registered with the Association.

c - Titles and functions recognised by the Association, provided that such information is stated in a manner devoid of publicity.

d - Honorary distinctions recognised by the Lebanese authorities.

e - Reference to his membership in an accredited scientific society recognised by the Association.

A dentist shall not be entitled to include in a directory anything other than the following:

a - His given name, surname, and address. His telephone numbers. Fax and electronic mail. The days and hours of consultations.

b - The registration number and his speciality.

The names of joint clinics may be included.

A dentist shall not be entitled to include on the sign of his clinic placed at the entrance of the clinic or the entrance of the building in which it is situated, anything other than his given name, surname, capacity, and speciality recognised by the Ministry of Public Health and registered with the Association. Provided that he may add the institution from which he obtained his degree, the days and hours of consultations, the floor on which the clinic is situated, and the telephone number.

This information shall be displayed with discretion in accordance with the customs of the profession. He is prohibited from mentioning anything that might suggest that it is a speciality. Given that every speciality must be registered with the Association.

The usurpation of titles is prohibited. It is likewise prohibited to use a title not recognised by the Association. Particularly where the inclusion of such titles aims to mislead, notably through the use of unpermitted abbreviations.

A dentist is prohibited from:

a - Performing any act from which he derives an unjustified or unlawful material benefit for any patient whatsoever.

b - Granting a cash or in-kind discount to a patient or reducing the fee for the purpose of competition below the minimum tariff for medical acts set by the Dental Association.

c - Exchanging or sharing sums of money between dentists or with a third party.

d - Paying a commission to any person whatsoever.
It is prohibited to grant facilities to anyone who practises the dental profession unlawfully.

A dentist is prohibited from conducting consultations, even free of charge, in commercial or craft premises or in their annexes, in which drugs, articles, or instruments prescribed by a dentist or any other doctor are displayed or sold.
Collusion between a dentist and any other doctor, pharmacist, medical assistants, and other persons, whosoever they may be, is prohibited.

A dentist shall avoid, in his writings and statements or during his participation in conferences, prejudicing the honour of the profession or its members.

He is prohibited from advertising or engaging in publicity for himself or for others.

Any premature disclosure within dental circles or elsewhere of a new method of diagnosis or treatment whose efficacy has not been proven shall constitute a punishable offence unless the physician making the disclosure points out the potential risks.

Deceiving patients by practising physicians through presenting a method whose efficacy has not been wholly proven as a salutary, risk-free method shall constitute gross misconduct exposing its perpetrator to all liabilities.
A dentist who holds an administrative public office is prohibited from exploiting his office to gain new clients.

a - A dentist shall issue, within the scope of the practice of his profession, certificates, attestations and documents which the regulations require to be issued.

b - Prescriptions, certificates and attestations shall be drawn up in the official Arabic language and may be drawn up in the French and English languages.

c - It is the duty of the dentist to take all necessary preventive measures so that none other than those entitled thereto gain access to the drugs which he uses in treatment.

A dentist may, except in cases of emergency or where he would be in breach of a humanitarian duty, refuse to provide treatment for personal or professional reasons, provided that:

a - He does no harm to his patient.

b - He ensures the continuity of treatment. And he gives all necessary instructions for this purpose.

- A dentist may not exercise this right except in compliance with the rule laid down in Article Eight of this

Law.

A dentist who has agreed to treat a patient shall be bound to:

a - Provide clear treatment consistent with scientific and professional principles in the event of calling upon the assistance of a colleague of his in any medical speciality whatsoever.

b - Deal at all times with the patient with integrity and propriety.

c - Accept the request of the President of the Association to conduct an attempt at conciliation between him and the patient where necessary.
A dentist shall enable the patient to obtain his rights to social benefits.
A dentist is prohibited from prescribing, for the purpose of experimentation, treatments capable of harming the patient or exposing him to danger.

a - Where a dentist notices that one of his patients is subjected to ill-treatment or deprivation, he must use the most appropriate means to protect him and inform the competent authorities when necessary.

b - Where it is impossible to obtain the consent of the legal representative of a minor or an incapacitated person, the dentist must, in cases of extreme emergency, provide the treatment which he deems appropriate.

With the exception of the cases referred to in Paragraph (a) of Article Twenty-Nine, a dentist working in a hospital in which the inpatient consultation system applies must inform the legal representative of the patient in the event of a serious ailment. He must accept consultation with the physician chosen by the patient or his legal representative, or consult him whenever necessary.

A dentist shall be free to issue the prescriptions which he deems most appropriate according to each case. Provided that he limits his prescriptions and acts to what is necessary to ensure the quality and efficacy of the treatment.

A dentist may withhold from the patient the results of a grave diagnosis for legitimate reasons of conscience. Where it is unavoidable to inform him, this shall be done with great circumspection.

Where the patient has requested in advance that a grave diagnosis not be disclosed, or where he has named the person or persons whom he wishes to have informed thereof, his request must be complied with.

a - A dentist shall fix his fees equitably in accordance with the schedule of tariffs approved by the Association.

b - He is not entitled to reduce his fees with the aim of attracting clients. Provided that he retains the right to provide treatment free of charge.

c - A dentist must explain the reasons for fixing his fees if the patient so requests.

d - He is not entitled to request an advance payment unless the importance of the treatment justifies this. The physician must, in any case, abide by the dictates of the customs and traditions of the profession. Provided that he agrees directly with the patient on the method of payment.
The attending dentist is entitled to additional fees if the treatment requires the consultation of another dentist.
The attending dentist who attends a surgical operation may charge additional fees if the patient or his family requested his attendance. Or if they agreed to such attendance.

Fee-splitting between dentists and other physicians, whatever their speciality, is prohibited. Every physician must claim his own fees.

Fee-splitting - whether requested, offered or accepted - shall constitute gross professional misconduct, even if it has not been carried out.

a - Every dentist must keep in his clinic a medical file for each of his patients, for the preservation of which he shall be responsible.

The dentist must deliver a copy of the file to the patient when requested to do so, provided that the file contains all the information necessary to complete the diagnosis or to continue the treatment.

b - Where the files are the result of the work of several dentists and are confined to a single institution, none other than the attending dentists and researchers are entitled to inspect them.

c - The investigating judge, or the judicial police if necessary, has the right to search a dentist's clinic or a dental department and to seize medical documents, provided that this takes place in his presence and in the presence of the President of the Association or a member of the Council of the Association delegated by him. The dentist may not, in that event, oppose the search procedures.
A dentist must cooperate with the competent authorities with a view to preserving public health.
A dentist must not contravene the provisions of Article Thirty-One by reason of the existence of a third-party guarantor, such as private or public insurance.

A dentist is required to sign the fee agreement approved by the Association for the party whom he undertakes to treat, whatever that party may be. Where the other party is an administration or an institution, the model contract issued by the Council of the Association shall be adopted.

Where a dentist receives fees, such fees may not be calculated on the basis of criteria of productivity and yield, because this affects the quality of the treatment, in addition to infringing the principle of the professional independence of the dentist.

The Council of the Association shall ensure that the provisions of the contract respect the principles laid down by the law in general and by the present Law in particular.

A dentist who provides a preventive programme on behalf of a given community is not entitled to undertake treatment therein, except in cases of emergency, subject to compliance with the legislative or regulatory provisions governing medical and social occupational services.

He must, in such a case, refer the sick person to his attending physician.

Where the patient does not have an attending dentist, he shall be given the freedom to choose one of the physicians.

This consideration shall apply to a dentist who conducts a general examination for the detection of diseases, provided that it remains open to him to provide treatment:

a - To patients subject to the inpatient consultation system in a hospital in which he works as a dentist.

b - To patients affiliated with associations, hospitals or institutions that have obtained an authorisation in this regard from the Minister of Public Health, after hearing the opinion of the Council of the Association.

A dentist who practises, alongside his profession, preventive dentistry in a given community or conducts a general examination for the detection of diseases is prohibited from exploiting this function to increase his clientele.

Except in cases of emergency, no one may be, at the same time, a dentist entrusted with a mission of supervision or expertise and an attending dentist. This prohibition extends to the members of the patient's family who live with him. A dentist may not accept to perform a mission of expertise in which the interests of one of his patients, friends, relatives, partners, or a group with which he works, are connected closely or remotely with such expertise, except in the event of the agreement of the parties concerned.

A supervising dentist must not interfere in the treatment. However, where a divergence of views with his colleague appears during the conduct of an examination, or where he becomes aware of an element useful for completing the treatment, he must inform the attending physician thereof, in confidence.

The inspecting dentist shall inform the patient subject to his inspection that he is examining him in his capacity as an inspecting dentist. He shall, in this case, be circumspect in his statements and refrain from expressing a personal opinion to the patient.

The inspecting dentist is bound to respect professional secrecy towards the administration or body that requests his services.

He shall confine his conclusions to the administrative aspect without mentioning the medical reasons upon which he relied.

No persons from outside the medical corps or from another administration may be apprised of the medical information contained in the files prepared by the dentist.

An expert dentist ought, prior to commencing the expert work, whatever it may be, to inform the person concerned of the nature of his mission.

He shall refrain from making any comment whatsoever during the examination.

An expert dentist shall recuse himself when a mission is entrusted to him, if he considers that the questions put to him bear no relation to dentistry.

The expert dentist shall draw up his report in strict adherence to the questions put to him by the decision appointing him as an expert.

He shall keep confidential whatever comes to his knowledge in the course of performing his mission or on the occasion thereof.

Dentists shall preserve relations of fellowship and the ethics thereof.

In the event of a professional disagreement among them arising from practice, the parties shall accept an attempt at conciliation undertaken by the President of the Order.

A dentist is prohibited from attributing to himself, particularly in any publication, the credit for a scientific discovery, unless such discovery is registered in accordance with the regulations and laws.

Dentists shall at all times exchange moral support. Dentists are entitled to charge fees among themselves, if they so wish.

It is prohibited to spread news about a colleague that harms his reputation or to circulate statements that may prejudice him in the course of practising his profession.
It is prohibited to solicit the clients of another dentist or to attempt to solicit them.

Dentists are required, when requested to give testimony in disciplinary cases, to disclose all useful information that has come to their knowledge, subject to the principle of respecting professional secrecy.

A dentist may receive in his clinic, even in non-emergency cases, all patients concerned with his specialty, whoever their treating dentist may be.

If the patient expresses his wish to change his dentist, the latter shall provide him with the information necessary to complete the treatment and ensure its quality.

If the treating dentist is absent, the patient is entitled to have recourse to a substitute dentist. Provided that the substitute shall, with the consent of the patient, give the treating dentist, upon his return, all necessary information.

If the patient's family requests a dentist for consultation, it is preferable that the treating dentist accept this. He shall then name the dentist whom he prefers, leaving the choice to the patient's family, making the interest of this patient a condition for his consent.

The treating dentist and the consulting dentist shall take care that neither of them discredits the other in the eyes of the patient and his family.

The consulting dentist shall cease providing the treatment required by the patient's condition if it falls within the specialty of the treating dentist, unless the patient expressly requests otherwise of him.

If, during the consultation, a major and irrevocable divergence of views appears, the treating dentist is entitled to refuse to assume any liability and to refuse to apply the treatment proposed by the consulting dentist.

The dentist may cease providing treatments if the patient consents to the proposed treatment.

Dentists may form joint clinics among themselves, provided that they send to the Council of the Order an application signed by all participants in which they specify:

A - The names of all the dentists participating in the clinic and their registration numbers on the roll of the Order.

B - The address of the premises of the joint clinic.

C - The name of the clinic and the registration of the name on the roll of the Order in order to prevent the duplication of names.

The registration application shall be submitted by registered letter to the Secretariat, and the Council shall rule on the application within a period not exceeding one month from the date of registration of the application.

D - The Order shall levy an annual fee approved by the General Assembly upon the proposal of the Council of the Order.

Dentists participating in a joint clinic shall place a professional plaque at the entrance of the building or on the outer door of the clinic, bearing the names of all participants. The provisions of Articles 13, 14, 15 and 16 of this Law shall apply to them.

In the event of the withdrawal or death of one of the dentists participating in joint clinics, or in the event of the affiliation of a new dentist, or the liquidation of the joint clinic, the Order shall be notified thereof.

No association in the practice of the profession may take place without concluding a written contract submitted to the Council of the Order and respecting the professional independence of each dentist.

Contracts or annexed amendments shall be submitted to the Council of the Order, which shall verify their compliance with the principles of this Law, as well as with the clauses of the standard contracts drawn up by the Council.

The Council of the Order shall be apprised of every agreement, partnership contract or annexed amendments of a professional nature that may arise between a dentist and third parties so that it may verify the contract's compliance with the laws in force and with the Code of Professional Ethics, particularly with respect to the independence of dentists.

The Council of the Order shall be notified of draft agreements, contracts or annexed amendments agreed upon pursuant to this clause, provided that the Council of the Order gives its observations thereon within a period of one month.

The dentist shall sign a declaration which he deposits with the Council of the Order, in which he declares, upon his honour and integrity, that he has not executed a counter-deed relating to the contract submitted to the Council of the Order.

Subject to the application of Articles 7, 40 and 41 of this Law, every dentist who wishes to practise his profession in an individual capacity or within a partnership, of whatever kind, is required to benefit directly or through a joint clinic from:

A - The right to enjoy, pursuant to legal documents, professional premises, furniture and sufficient equipment to receive and treat patients.

B - The Order shall prepare a schedule of the technical equipment required to be present in clinics to ensure the safety of patients.

C - The ownership of the documents containing all information particular to the patients.

It rests with the Council of the Order to verify, at any time whatsoever, compliance with the conditions of paragraphs (A) and (B) of this Article. In all cases, a good quality of services in complete confidentiality shall be ensured while taking care to ensure the safety of patients.

The installation of technical equipment and the disposal of waste resulting from the practice of this profession shall also be subject to the rules of hygiene.

The practice of the profession of dentistry is prohibited without special fixed equipment complying with the provisions laid down by this Law.

The Order may nevertheless grant a special authorisation to dentists who assist organisations that meet:

- The need for prevention.

- Or emergency cases.

- Or permanent needs to receive treatment at home.

The Order shall verify, in cooperation with the competent authorities, that these activities comply with the general principles laid down in this Law.

Dentists are required to respect, in their professional relations with members of other medical and paramedical professions, the independence of the latter, and to avoid, as far as possible, offending anyone connected with the medical field.

A dentist shall, upon his registration with the Order, take an oath to abide by the provisions of this Law. The President of the Order shall draw up a record thereof, which the dentist shall sign with him and which shall be kept in the latter's file.
Every contravention of the provisions of this Law shall render its perpetrator liable to referral to the Disciplinary Council.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Second: Taxpayers against whom assessment rolls, collection orders, or urgent assessments have been or are issued up to and including 30/09/2000 shall benefit from the exemption provided for in Article /55/ of the General Budget Law for the year 1999 and its amendments.

Third: Taxpayers subject to transfer duty who have previously had the duty accrued on them paid in instalments, as well as the surcharges and fines attached thereto, shall also benefit from the exemption provided for in Article /55/ referred to above, in the event that they pay /20/ twenty percent of the balance of the payable duty within a period of two months before 01/10/2000, provided that the balance is paid in instalments in accordance with the instalment rules applicable to the transfer duty.

Instalment applications for this duty that were previously submitted outside the legal time limits, as well as new instalment applications concerning it, shall also be accepted during this period and shall be exempted from the fines and surcharges mentioned above, provided that their holders pay the first instalment thereof before 01/10/2000.

Inadmissibility of the monthly allowances of contractors falling below those of their counterparts in the position

The following new paragraph shall be added to Item Second of Article Six of Law No. 717 dated 05/11/1998:

G - The monthly allowances of contractors that are considered a salary or wage may not fall below the salary of the parallel or closest step in the salary scale of the position identical or similar to their duties after their conversion in accordance with the attached tables.

Multiplication of fines for violating the Labour Law

The value of the fines specified pursuant to Articles Two and Four of the Law issued on 17 September 1962 relating to the repeal of Articles 107 and 108 of the Labour Law issued on 23 September 1946 shall be multiplied twenty-fivefold.

Benefit of female employees affiliated with the Civil Servants Cooperative

The Single Article of Law No. 149 issued on 30 October 1999 has been amended to read as follows:

1 - Notwithstanding any other text, a female employee affiliated with the Civil Servants Cooperative shall benefit from all the benefits from which a male employee affiliated with the Cooperative benefits and which are provided for by the regulations of the Cooperative, and at the same rates, within the conditions set out below.

2 - In the event that both the husband and the wife are affiliated with the Cooperative and each of them is entitled to benefit from it for the same case, the assistance or grant for that case shall only be given to the one of them who first submitted an application fulfilling the conditions to benefit therefrom, and in accordance with the amounts and rates to which he is entitled pursuant to the regulations of the Cooperative.

3 - In the event that one of the spouses is affiliated with the Cooperative, and the other is not affiliated with it and benefits from another official authority, the spouse affiliated with the Cooperative shall not be entitled to benefit on behalf of his spouse from its benefits.

4 - In the event that one of the spouses is affiliated with the Cooperative, and the other is not affiliated with it, does not engage in paid work, and benefits from an insurance company for medical and hospitalisation cases, the spouse affiliated with the Cooperative shall benefit from the difference, if any, between what the Cooperative provides and what the insurance company has provided. In this case, certified true copies of the medical or hospitalisation documents may be adopted, provided that they are signed by the medical or hospitalisation authority by which the treatment was carried out, and stamped with the seal of the insurance company as being in conformity with the original kept with the latter. Practitioners of liberal professions and commercial and industrial professions, including partners who assume management duties of a company even if it is a civil company, shall not benefit from the provisions of this paragraph.

5 - Neither of the spouses shall be entitled to benefit from the Cooperative on behalf of his foreign spouse, as well as on behalf of foreign children, except on condition of reciprocity on the part of the State to which the foreign husband or wife or the foreign children belong.

Exemption from the entry fee to the precincts of the airport and maritime ports

Lebanese workers shall be exempted from the annual entry permit fee to the precincts of the airport and maritime ports set forth in Table No. 9 of Law No. 280 dated 15/12/1993 (the 1993 Budget). And in Table No. 9 of Law No. 107 dated 23/07/1999 (the 1999 Budget).

2 - The value of the fines set forth in Articles 14 and 15 of Law No. 11/68 dated 08/01/1968 (regulation of Lebanese passports).

3 - The value of the fine set forth in Article 10 of the Law issued on 27/11/1947 (subjection of all cinematographic films to censorship by General Security).

Half the tariff shall be adopted for children aged eighteen and under and for disabled persons, in tourist archaeological sites and museums and in public transport means belonging to the Railways and Public Transport Authority.

The following Regulations pertaining to the State Employees' Cooperative annexed to this Decree are hereby ratified:

a- The Regulations of the Employees of the Cooperative.

b - The Regulations of the Executive Management.

c- The Regulations on the Manner of Appointing the Board of Directors of the Cooperative and Determining its Powers.

d- The Regulations of Benefits and Services.

e- The Regulations on the Manner of Tutelage by the Civil Service Board and Supervision by the Ministry of Finance over the Cooperative.

f- The Financial Regulations.

g- The Regulations on the Manner of Transmitting the Accounts of the Cooperative and the Documents and Information Pertaining Thereto to the Court of Accounts.

h- The Regulations Determining the Scope and Rules of Supervision by the Court of Accounts over the Cooperative.
