This Decree shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Gazette.

In these Regulations:

- The word Cooperative means: the State Employees' Cooperative

- The word Board means: the Board of Directors of the Cooperative.

- The word Regulations means: the Regulations of the Employees of the Cooperative.

- The words Director General mean: the Director General of the Cooperative.

Scope of Application:

These Regulations shall apply to all employees of the Cooperative.

Employees, Contractors, and Wage-Earners:

1- Employees are divided into permanent employees and temporary employees:

a - A permanent employee is a person appointed to a permanent job in a position provided for in the permanent cadre of the Cooperative.

b - A temporary employee is a person appointed to a position created for a specific period or for casual work.

2- Every person in the service of the Cooperative who does not belong to either of the two categories set forth in paragraphs a and b of this Article shall be deemed a wage-earner.

3- Contractors are Lebanese or foreign nationals with whom the Cooperative contracts for a limited period to perform a specific work requiring special knowledge and qualifications, within the limits of the number and appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget of the Cooperative.

The permanent cadre of the Cooperative shall be composed in accordance with Table No. 1 annexed to these Regulations. This cadre may be composed of one or more corps.

Permanent positions are divided into categories, categories into ranks, and ranks into grades.

A temporary cadre may be created by a decision of the Board after the approval of the tutelage authority.

Provided that it includes the number of positions and the conditions of appointment, advancement by step, promotion, the salary scale, dismissal from service, and all other personnel matters.

a- That he has been a Lebanese national for more than ten years.

b - That he has completed twenty years of age.

c - That he has not exceeded thirty-five years of age if he is applying for a position in the fifth and fourth categories; however, if he is applying for a position in a higher category or a technical position of any category whatsoever, the difference between his age and the age of dismissal from service for reaching the legal age must not be less than fifteen

years.

d- That he produces a certificate from the Medical Committee of the Cooperative proving that he is free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from performing the duties of his position.

e - That he produces a copy of his judicial record proving that he enjoys his civil rights and has not been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour. The following shall be deemed a disgraceful misdemeanour: theft, fraud, breach of trust, issuing a cheque without provision, embezzlement, bribery, extortion, blackmail, forgery, use of forged documents, false testimony, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code, and offences relating to the cultivation of or trafficking in narcotic substances.

These provisions shall apply to persons who have been rehabilitated and have benefited from an amnesty.

f - That he holds the required academic degrees, and successfully passes the competitive examination or qualifying examination for appointment in all cases where the Regulations require passing the competitive examination or qualifying examination.

g - That he has not been previously removed or dismissed for a disciplinary reason from the service of the Cooperative or from a position in the State or in one of the municipalities, autonomous agencies, or public institutions attached to the State.

Age Requirement:

1- The age of employees in the Cooperative and their years of service shall be calculated on the basis of the Gregorian calendar

2- The minimum and maximum age limits required for appointment shall be calculated from the date of birth until the date fixed for the commencement of the competitive examination or the qualifying examination, or on the first of January of the year in which the appointment takes place with respect to employees whom the Regulations permit to be appointed without a competitive examination or a qualifying examination.

3- The age of the new employee shall be stated in the instrument of appointment on the basis of a certified true copy of his entry in the personal status registers, and if the day of birth is unknown, the employee shall be deemed born on the first day of the month of July of the year of his birth.

4- No rectification occurring after the issuance of the instrument of appointment shall be taken into account in determining the age of employees, whether the rectification is issued through non-contentious jurisdiction or through contentious jurisdiction.

Conditions of Appointment in the First and Second Categories:

(As amended by Decisions of the Board of Directors of the Employees' Cooperative No. 1255

dated 18/1/75 and No. 1275 dated 25/2/1975 and Decision 104 d. 12/12/90 .

First: The Director General of the Cooperative.

The Director General shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the tutelage authority and in accordance with the following conditions:

1- That he is an employee in one of the three upper grades of the second category in the permanent cadre of the Cooperative.

Or that he is an employee in the permanent cadre of the State of the second category at least.

2- That his age is not less than thirty-five years, of which he has spent at least ten years in actual service in the cadre of the State or the cadre of the Cooperative.

3- In the event that there is no employee in the Cooperative who meets the conditions set forth in paragraphs 1 and 2 above, the Director General of the Cooperative may be appointed from among the employees of the permanent cadre of the State of the second category at least, provided that he is placed outside the cadre of his administration in accordance with the provisions of the State Employees' Regulations.

Second- The Head of the Financial Department.

The Head of the Financial Department shall be appointed in accordance with the following conditions:

1- That his age is not less than twenty-five years.

2- That he holds a university degree (Licence) in Lebanese law, or in financial, economic, or commercial affairs, or the equivalent thereof, provided that he obtained the degree after the second part of the Lebanese Baccalaureate or the equivalent thereof.

3- That he has at least three years of experience in financial or commercial affairs.

4- That he passes the qualifying competitive examination for this position, conducted by the Civil Service Board.

This post may be filled by selection from among the employees of the first and second grades of the third category in the cadres of the State, after placing him outside the cadre.

This post may also be filled by selection from among the employees of the Cooperative who have reached the first and second grades in the third category, provided that the candidate for filling the post by selection meets the special conditions required for participating in the competitive examination.

The regulations of the qualifying competitive examination for this position may provide for granting additional marks not exceeding 15 % of the total marks to candidates who hold degrees higher than the minimum required, and ten percent to employees of the Cooperative and employees of public administrations who have three years or more in service, provided that these marks are given, when ranking the order of success, to those who pass the competitive examination.

It shall be specifically required for appointment to the position of driver that the candidate hold a public driving licence valid for work in Lebanon.

Employees of the Fifth Category shall be appointed by a decision of the Director General of the Cooperative following the approval of the Civil Service Board.

Employees of the Fourth, Third, and Second Categories shall be appointed by a decision of the Director General following the approval of the Civil Service Board, from the list of successful candidates in competitive examinations, provided that this list shall remain valid for a period of one year.

Vacant positions in the Cooperative may be filled, upon the proposal of the Director General and the approval of the Civil Service Board, from among the employees of the permanent cadres in the administrations of the State who occupy positions of the same category, by way of placing them outside the cadre, and the administration of the Cooperative shall be entitled to grant the employee placed outside the cadre for the purpose of attaching him to the Cooperative an exceptional advancement step.

Conditions of Probation:

- Those appointed to the positions of the Cooperative shall remain probationers for a period of one year in the step in which they were appointed, and no employee shall be exempted from probation regardless of his category.

- The authority vested with the right to appoint them shall confirm the probationers as permanent, and the effect of confirmation shall be deemed valid starting from the date of expiry of the probation period.

- Probationers may be dismissed from service before the expiry of the probation period or at the end thereof upon the proposal of the Director General and following the approval of the Civil Service Board, and the dismissed person in this case shall not be entitled to any compensation for the period he spent in the service of the Cooperative. The effect of dismissal shall be deemed valid starting from the date of his notification thereof or from the date of actual cessation of work if that occurred before the notification.

- The probation period shall be included in the count of years of actual service.

- If confirmation or dismissal is not decided at the end of the probation period, the probationer must request his confirmation within a time limit of one month, and the administration of the Cooperative must decide on his request within a time limit of another month, failing which he shall be deemed confirmed by operation of law since the expiry of his probation period.

- The provisions of this Article shall not apply to the appointment of the Director General.

The Government shall notify the Chamber of Deputies of any amounts of issued Treasury bonds that exceed the limits of the actual deficit realised in the execution of the budget, including the total appropriations carried over to the year 2000 and the supplementary appropriations, pursuant to quarterly reports stating the explanatory reasons for such excess.

2 - Within the framework of restructuring the public debt, the Government is authorised to issue Treasury bonds in foreign currency within the limits of a value of one billion US dollars, provided that the funds borrowed pursuant to this authorisation are used to refinance the maturities of external debts and/or to convert the equivalent of their value of the public debt in Lebanese pounds into foreign currencies. The entirety of these issued bonds must be finally repaid within a period not exceeding thirty years from the date of commencement of their issuance, and the interest rates on these bonds shall be determined in accordance with the prevailing rates in the international market for similar bonds abroad, and this shall be effected by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Loan Accounts

Special Treasury accounts shall be opened for loans, to which the value received from these loans shall be credited and to which the values paid in settlement of matured instalments and bonds shall be debited.

Manner of Repayment of Loans

The Government is authorised, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, to open, where necessary, annual appropriations in the General Budget and the annexed budgets for the purpose of repaying loan instalments that fall due (principal, interest and supplementary expenditures) and to determine the sources of their coverage.

Application of the Provisions of External Loan Agreements to the Entire Expenditure Pertaining to Externally Financed Projects.

In the expenditure of external loan and grant agreements concluded with various public administrations, public institutions and municipalities, the regulatory provisions adopted by the lending party shall apply, whether such expenditure is from the local component or from the foreign component, provided that they are subject to the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts.

Opening of Extraordinary Appropriations

Execution of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if unforeseen circumstances necessitate urgent expenditures, adopt a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, to open extraordinary or supplementary appropriations or to transfer appropriations in the General Budget for the year 2000, provided that these appropriations do not exceed thirty-five billion pounds, and these measures must be submitted to the Chamber of Deputies for approval at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Carry-over of Appropriations and Transfer of Carried-over Appropriations

It is authorised to transfer to the remaining titles of the budget the appropriations allocated in previous budgets and carried over to the budget of the year 2000 under Title 31 Debts Due for Payment in the following paragraphs:

16 Settlement of the increases imposed by the Rent Law.

18 Settlement of the deficit of the Fuels Fund. The transfer shall be effected in accordance with the rules provided for in Article 26 of the Public Accounting Law. It is also authorised to carry over the appropriations of Title 31 Debts Due for Payment before or after their transfer to the remaining titles of the budget until the obligations arising therefrom are settled due to the attachment of third-party rights thereto. It is also authorised, where necessary, to carry over the appropriations allocated under Title 32 Budget Reserve Items 12, 13, 14, 16 and 18, and it is also authorised to transfer within this title from one item to another by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment. The carry-over shall be effected in accordance with the rules determined in Article 114 of the Public Accounting Law.

Opening of Appropriations to Subsidise Interest on Development Loans

The Government is authorised annually and according to need to provide in the budget reserve for the appropriations required to cover the interest on development loans (agricultural, industrial, touristic) in accordance with the special regulations established by the Minister of Finance and the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon for this purpose.

Health Treatment Appropriations

The appropriations allocated on a lump-sum basis under the various titles of the General Budget designated for treatment in private institutions and hospitals and contracts with physicians in the private sector shall be distributed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the joint proposal of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance.

Authorisation to Transfer Appropriations of the Title of the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports to the Remaining Titles

It is authorised to transfer the appropriations provided for in the budget of the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports for the year 2000 under Chapter Two and Chapter Three, Item 13, to the corresponding item under the remaining titles of the General Budget and the annexed budgets by a joint decision issued by the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports and the Minister of Finance, after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment, in order to secure the salaries required for the execution of Law No. 454 dated 17/08/1995 (Transfer of Primary School Teachers, Intermediate School Teachers and Secondary School Professors to the Cadres of Public Administrations), the application of which was extended pursuant to Article Five, Item 9 of Law No. 717 dated 05/11/1998 (Conversion of Salary Scales).

Appropriations of Social Centres

Notwithstanding any other text, the value of the appropriations designated for social centres directly linked to the Ministry of Social Affairs in the 2000 budget shall, after their disbursement, be deposited in the special accounts opened at the Bank of Lebanon, and the obligations incurred by these centres shall be paid therefrom.

Authorisation to Pay Expropriations and Contractors' Statements of Account Pertaining to the Year 1999 from the Balance of Law 95

It is authorised to pay expropriation compensations, contractors' statements of account, medical and hospitalisation expenditures, and compensations for martyrs and wounded of the Israeli aggressions that were incurred before 31/12/1998 and for which decisions, statements of account or invoices were issued during the year 1999, pursuant to special bonds out of the balance of the amount of 1242 billion determined in Law No. 95 dated 18/06/1999.

Other Allowances:

As amended pursuant to Decision 39 dated 9/9/67 and Decision 468 dated 16/5/70

1- The employees of the Cooperative may be granted all other allowances and bonuses, including the special allowance, the allowance for overtime work, the travel allowance, transportation fares, and various other allowances, within the scope of the special conditions and the allowance for overtime work prescribed for civil servants, provided that the allowances requiring the issuance by a decree in respect of civil servants shall be determined by a decision of the Board of Directors of the Cooperative upon the proposal of the Director General and after the approval of the supervisory authority with respect to the employees of the Cooperative.

2- The total of the allowances and bonuses of whatever kind and the remuneration received by an employee from the budget of the Cooperative or from the budgets of the State or of public and private institutions and services during a single financial year may not exceed seventy-five per cent of the total of his monthly salaries in the same year.

3- The special allowance, the travel allowance, transportation expenses, family allowances, the acting allowance, and remuneration for teaching hours outside official working hours shall not be included in the calculation of this total.

Material Losses:

1- An employee may be granted compensation for a material loss sustained by him while performing an official mission if it resulted from circumstances of force majeure to which he was exposed by reason of the office.

2- If the loss arises from negligence or fault on the part of the employee, compensation shall not be granted in such case except upon the opinion of a committee appointed by the Director General to examine the matter and determine the extent of the employee's liability.

3- The injured employee must submit an application for compensation within fifteen days from the date of the occurrence of the damage. Where circumstances of force majeure prevent the submission of the application within this time limit, it must be submitted immediately upon the cessation of such circumstances, and the employee's right to compensation shall lapse if he fails to comply with these conditions.

4- The compensation shall be granted by a decision of the Director General.

The employees of the Cooperative shall be deemed affiliated thereto by operation of law, and they shall pay to the fund of the Cooperative the monthly compulsory contribution imposed on affiliated members, and they shall be entitled to benefit from all the services and assistance of the Cooperative in accordance with the regulations in force.

- A special appropriation shall be provided for in the budget of the Cooperative representing the assistance of the Cooperative to its employees, at the same rate as the assistance provided by the State to its employees.

Advancement by Step:

1- Every employee who has spent two years in a single step or in an equivalent step from the date on which he assumed duty after his appointment or the date on which he obtained an increase in his salary shall acquire one step within the category by operation of law.

2- An employee who has reached the top of his category shall continue to benefit, by operation of law and in accordance with the provisions governing advancement by step, from an increase in his salary equivalent to one step in accordance with the scale of steps of the cadre to which he belongs.

He shall also benefit from the provisions of Article 25 of these Regulations, provided that he remains in his category in both cases and that he does not benefit from more than six steps.

3- Only the period of actual service for which the employee received his full salary shall be included in the calculation of the period for advancement by step.

Accelerated Advancement:

1- Accelerated advancement shall bring forward the due date of advancement by step by six months.

2- Prior to the end of the month of June of each year, the Director General shall draw up a list of the names of the employees whom he proposes for accelerated advancement, provided that their number does not exceed ten per cent of the total of the employees of the Cooperative whose advancement by step falls due in the following financial year, and that this number is distributed, as far as possible, among the various categories according to the percentage.

3- The list shall be accompanied by a statement of the grades and the explanatory reasons for the accelerated advancement in accordance with the forms adopted by the Personnel Department at the Civil Service Board.

4- The list shall be submitted to the Civil Service Board for approval in accordance with the prescribed rules.

5- The accelerated advancement shall take effect as from the date of approval by the Civil Service Board of the list of accelerated advancement.

6- Where it is not possible to disburse the accelerated advancements from the appropriations allocated therefor in the budget, they shall be disbursed from the surplus realized in the salary appropriations, if any; otherwise, a new appropriation shall be opened in accordance with the prescribed rules.

Promotion:

1- It is the transfer of an employee from one rank to a higher rank within the same category and from one category to another category.

2- An employee shall not be promoted from one rank to another rank unless he is in the first step of his rank and his name is entered on the promotion roster.

3- The Director General of the Cooperative shall draw up a promotion roster which he shall send to the Civil Service Board prior to the first of October of each year, and he shall include therein the names of the employees whom he nominates for transfer from one rank to another rank in the same category or from one category to another category, and he shall accompany the roster with the explanatory reasons.

The Civil Service Board must issue a final decision on this roster prior to the end of the first of January; if it fails to take its decision within the specified time limit, the roster shall be deemed effective as received from the Cooperative.

Administrative Leave:

1- An employee shall be entitled, after the expiration of one year from his appointment, and in each subsequent year spent by him in actual service, to benefit from an annual leave on full salary for a period of twenty days.

2- Leave may be accumulated for a maximum period of three years.

3- The Director General shall schedule the dates of employees' leave in a manner that ensures the continuity of work in the Cooperative.

4- Dismissal from service shall not take effect until after the expiration of the period of administrative leave to which the employee is entitled.

Family Leave:

An employee shall be entitled, in addition to his annual leave, to be absent with permission and on full salary for a period of one week at most, in the event of his marriage or the death of his spouse or one of his ascendants, descendants, brothers or sisters.

Leave Without Pay:

An employee may be granted, for private reasons and upon his request, a leave without pay not exceeding three months, which may be extended for another three months, provided that the total of private leaves does not exceed six months during five consecutive years.

As amended pursuant to Decision 1310 dated 27/3/75 and Decision 211 dated 3/11/92

See: Amendment of maternity leave in the Civil Servants Regulations pursuant to Article 1 of Law 266/2014

Maternity Leave:

A pregnant female employee shall be granted a leave on full salary called "maternity leave" for a maximum period of sixty days, and maternity leave shall not be included in the calculation of administrative leave nor in the calculation of sick leave.

1- Maternity leave shall be granted all at once without division when the applicant therefor is about to give birth.

2- In order to be granted maternity leave, the female employee must submit a special application:

a- The start date of the leave and the end date thereof.

b- The approximate date of delivery according to the physician's report.

3- A female employee who has been granted maternity leave shall not be entitled to submit medical sick reports during the period of the maternity leave, nor shall she be entitled to divide this leave.

Sick Leave:

1- An employee who is absent for health reasons shall be entitled to receive his full salary for a period of one month at most, provided that he immediately informs his superior of his current address and the reasons calling for the absence, and sends him a medical report stating the nature of the illness and specifying the approximate duration of the absence.

If the employee refrains from sending the medical report, he shall be subject to disciplinary penalties, and the Administration shall have the right to send a physician to examine him at his own expense. If the duration of the absence exceeds ten days, the immediate superior must request the Cooperative's physician to examine the absent employee and draw up a report on him.

2- If the absence exceeds one uninterrupted month, or one month over several stages within three months, leave with full salary shall only be granted pursuant to the report of the Medical Committee in the Cooperative and for a maximum period of three renewable months, provided that the total leaves do not exceed nine months within a full year or eighteen months within five consecutive years.

3- If the absence exceeds a period of nine months within a year or eighteen months within five consecutive years, the employee shall be referred at the end of

the period to the Medical Committee referred to in the preceding paragraph to consider his case. If he is curable within a period of two years, he shall be granted leave at half salary for a period of one year at most, and then placed on availability without salary for another year, and he shall not thereafter be reinstated to his work except pursuant to the opinion of the said Medical Committee.

If he is not curable within a period of two years, or if the Medical Committee deems during or at the end of this period that he is unable to resume his work, he shall be dismissed from service in accordance with the regulations in force.

4- If the absence results from the employee contracting an illness or an infirmity arising from the performance of his duty, he shall receive his full salary until his incapacity to continue service is established and he is dismissed as a result thereof.

5- An employee who is legally absent from Lebanon shall be entitled to obtain sick leave or request the extension of a previous sick leave, within the conditions referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article, on the basis of medical reports certified by the head of the Lebanese diplomatic or consular mission, or certified by the local health departments where there is no Lebanese mission.

As amended by Decision 269 dated 7/12/68:

The Authority Vested with the Right to Grant Leaves and Appoint the Employee Replacing the Employee on Leave or Absent on a Mission:

1- Leaves, whatever their duration and types, shall be granted by a decision of the Director General, and the leave decision must state the name of the employee who shall replace the employee on leave throughout the duration of his absence and act on his behalf in all his powers and responsibilities.

2- As for the leaves of the Director General, they shall be granted, whatever their duration and types, by a decision of the Chairman of the Board of Directors, stating the name of the employee who shall replace the Director General on leave throughout the duration of his absence and act on his behalf in all his powers and responsibilities.

3- In the event of the absence of the Director General or one of the employees of the Cooperative on a mission, the rules set forth in paragraphs 1 and 2 above shall apply with respect to the employee who replaces the employee absent on a mission.

Transfer from One Post to Another:

1- An employee may be transferred from one post to another after the approval of the Civil Service Board if he meets all the conditions for appointment to the post to which he is to be transferred, including the condition of a competitive examination.

2- The transfer shall be effected by a decision issued by the authority vested with the right of appointment.

3- It shall be required for a transfer that the post to which the employee is to be transferred be vacant in the cadre and have a special appropriation allocated to it in the budget.

4- The transferred employee shall retain the seniority acquired in his previous corps unless his transfer results in an increase in his salary equivalent to at least one step.

Transfer from One Duty Station to Another:

An employee may be transferred from one duty station to another by a decision of the Director General, provided that the transfer is based on considerations derived from the interest of the service.

Conditions for the Appointment of an Acting Officer:

1- An acting officer is an employee temporarily assigned to occupy a post other than his original post.

2- The authority that appoints the incumbent shall appoint the acting officer, and it may temporarily exempt him from the duties of his original post or keep him therein.

3- An acting officer may only be appointed to a vacant post or to a post from which the incumbent is absent.

4- The acting officer must belong to the corps of the incumbent, and if that is not possible, he may be appointed in another corps.

5- The acting officer must meet the conditions prescribed for appointment to the vacant post, with the exception of the conditions of age and competitive examination.

6- An acting officer may not be appointed for a period exceeding one year.

Rights and Duties of the Acting Officer:

1- The acting officer shall exercise all the powers of the incumbent and shall be bound to fulfill all his responsibilities and duties.

2- The acting officer shall receive the permanent allowances allocated to the post which he occupies in an acting capacity. If he has permanent allowances in his original post, he shall receive the higher allowance.

3- The acting officer shall have no acquired right to be appointed to the post which he occupies in an acting capacity.

4- The acting officer shall receive an acting allowance equivalent to half the difference between his salary and the salary of the lowest step of the category of the post which he occupies in an acting capacity. However, if his salary is equal to or exceeds the salary of this step, he shall not be entitled to any acting allowance. The allowance shall fall due ipso jure even if it is not expressly mentioned in the instrument of appointment.

5- The acting allowance shall be disbursed from the appropriations allocated for salaries or from the appropriations allocated for miscellaneous allowances.

6- An employee who is appointed as an acting officer outside his place of residence shall receive the relocation allowance provided for in Article Twenty-One of these Regulations.

Secondment of an Employee:

- An employee of the Cooperative may be seconded to specialize in one of the branches that it needs, and his secondment shall be subject to the provisions of the specialization regulations applicable to State employees.

- The post of the seconded employee shall remain vacant in the cadre of the Cooperative, and he shall return to it immediately upon the expiry of the period of his secondment.

Temporary Placement Outside the Cadre:

Employees of the Cooperative may be placed temporarily outside the cadre in accordance with the provisions applicable to State employees.

Conditions of Availability:

1- An employee shall be placed on availability ex officio or at his request, whereupon his salary shall be suspended and he shall lose his right to advancement throughout the period he spends on availability.

2- An employee shall be placed on availability by a decision of the authority vested with the right of appointment.

3- An employee may be placed on availability at his request if he suffers a grave accident, or in the event of the illness of his spouse or one of his descendants, or for the purpose of undertaking studies from which the Cooperative seeks a public expenditure, provided that the period of availability does not exceed one year renewable twice.

4- An employee may be placed on availability ex officio in the cases provided for by the Regulations.

5- The Cooperative must verify that the employee placed on availability at his request does not violate the purpose for which he was placed on availability, and it may at any time revoke its decision approving the request for availability.

Termination of Availability:

An employee on availability shall be reinstated to his post if it is still vacant. If it is not vacant, he shall be assigned a post equivalent to it in his category, or offered a lower post while retaining his original salary; if he refuses this latter post, he shall be dismissed from service. However, if the employee was placed on availability for the purpose of undertaking studies from which the Cooperative seeks a public benefit, his post shall remain vacant and he shall mandatorily be reinstated to it upon the termination of his placement on availability.

Disciplinary Liability

An employee shall be deemed liable from the disciplinary standpoint and shall be subject to disciplinary penalties if he intentionally or negligently breaches the duties imposed upon him by the laws and regulations, and in particular the duties provided for in Articles 13 and 14 of these Regulations. Disciplinary prosecution shall not preclude the prosecution of this employee, where applicable, before the competent civil or criminal courts.

Disciplinary Sanctions:

Disciplinary sanctions are of two degrees:

First Degree:

1- Reprimand.

2- Deduction of salary for a period of fifteen days at most.

3- Deferment of step advancement for a period of six months at most.

Second Degree:

1- Deferment of step advancement for a period of twenty-four months at most.

2- Suspension from work without salary for a period not exceeding six months.

3- Reduction by one or more steps within the same rank.

4- Reduction of rank.

5- Termination of service.

6- Dismissal.

As amended pursuant to Decision 434 dated 7/2/1970

The authority vested with the right to impose disciplinary sanctions

1- The Head of Department has the right to impose the sanction of reprimand and the sanction of deduction of salary for a period not exceeding three days.

2- The Head of Service has the right to impose the sanction of reprimand and the sanction of deduction of salary for a period not exceeding six days upon the proposal of the immediate superior of the employee.

3- The Director General of the Cooperative has the right to directly impose upon the employee any sanction of the first degree, provided that the third sanction thereof. shall not be imposed except after addressing two consecutive reprimands to the employee and after the approval of the supervisory authority.

The General Disciplinary Council:

Method of referral - Effect of decisions issued by the Disciplinary Council The employees of the Cooperative shall be subject to the General Disciplinary Council established by Law No. 54/65 dated 2/10/1965, and the legal and regulatory provisions relating to this Council shall apply to them.

Method of referral:

1- An employee of the Cooperative shall be referred to the General Disciplinary Council by a decision of the authority vested with the right to appoint him. He shall also be referred by a decision of the Central Inspection Board.

2- The decision ordering the referral to the General Disciplinary Council may provide for the suspension of the employee from work. The employee shall remain suspended until the General Disciplinary Council rules on his case or the authority that referred him to discipline revokes the referral decision.

3- The Director General has the right to suspend the employees of the Cooperative from work prior to their referral to the General Disciplinary Council for a period not exceeding 15 days.

If they are not referred to the General Disciplinary Council at the end of this period, their salaries shall be restored to them in full.

Effect of decisions issued by the Disciplinary Council:

1- The sanctions imposed by the General Disciplinary Council shall be executed immediately upon notification of the Council's decision to the employee.

2- An employee sentenced to termination of service or dismissal may not be reinstated to service in any department of the Cooperative.

Criminal Liability:

1- An employee of the Cooperative shall be referred to the judiciary where it appears that the acts attributed to him constitute an offence punishable under the Penal Code and other laws in force.

2- The public prosecution action is independent of the disciplinary action, and the institution of the public prosecution action shall not preclude the institution of the disciplinary action, proceeding therewith, and rendering judgment therein.

Civil Liability:

If an employee of the Cooperative commits an act harmful to a third party during the exercise of his function or by reason of his exercise thereof, the Cooperative shall be liable towards the third party for the act of the employee.

In the event that damages are awarded against it, the Cooperative shall have a right of recourse against the employee if it appears to it that he committed a gross fault that could easily have been avoided.

Cases in which service terminates:

The service of an employee of the Cooperative shall terminate and he shall permanently leave the cadre in each of the following cases:

1- Resignation

2- Termination of service

3- Dismissal

4- Death

Resignation upon the request of the employee:

1- An employee may submit his resignation in writing to the Cooperative, and he must continue to perform his function until a decision is made on his request.

2- The authority vested with the right of appointment shall decide on the resignation request. And if

the resignation is not rejected within two months from the date of its submission, it shall be deemed accepted by operation of law.

3- The instrument ordering the acceptance of the resignation may not be revoked or amended after its issuance.

4- A resigning employee shall not benefit from his rights to severance indemnity if his period of service is less than ten years. He shall receive half of the severance indemnity if the period of service ranges between ten years and fifteen years, and he shall receive his full indemnity if his period of service exceeds fifteen years.

The indemnity shall be liquidated in accordance with the provisions of Article 60 of these Regulations.

5- A resigning employee may not be reinstated to service unless he fulfills all the conditions of appointment with the exception of the condition of age, and in such case he shall be reinstated to his former rank and step, provided that he refunds in a single lump sum to the fund of the Cooperative the full amounts he received pursuant to the preceding paragraph.

Cases in which an employee is deemed to have resigned:

1- The following shall be deemed to have resigned:

a- An appointed or transferred employee who fails to assume his function without a legitimate reason within fifteen days from the date of his notification of the instrument ordering his appointment or transfer.

b- An employee who absents himself from his work without regular leave and fails to resume his work after the expiry of fifteen days from the date of his absence from work.

c- An employee who fails to resume his work after the expiry of fifteen days from the date of the end of his leave.

d- An employee who goes on strike from work or incites to strike.

2- Resignation in the aforementioned cases shall be confirmed by a decision of the authority vested with the right of appointment.

3- The provisions of paragraphs 3, 4, and 5 of the preceding Article shall apply to the employee deemed to have resigned.

Termination of Service:

1- Termination of service is the ending of the service of the employee and his permanent removal from the cadre, provided that he is granted a severance indemnity.

2- An employee shall be terminated from service by a decision of the authority vested with the right of appointment.

His service shall be deemed terminated by operation of law upon his reaching the legal age, or on the day following his notification of the decision of termination, or from the date of his actual cessation of work if it ended prior to his reaching the age limit.

3- An employee may not be reinstated to service in the Cooperative, even on a temporary basis, if he was terminated by a judgment of the General Disciplinary Council for reaching the legal age. He may be reinstated in other cases provided that he fulfills the conditions of appointment with the exception of the condition of age, in which case he shall be reinstated to his former rank and step. If he has received a severance indemnity, his former services shall not be added to his new services unless he refunds the severance indemnity, in a single lump sum, to the fund of the Cooperative prior to assuming his new function.

Grounds for Termination of Service:

An employee shall be terminated from service in the cases provided for by the Regulations, or by a decision of the General Disciplinary Council, or in each of the following cases:

- Reaching the legal age.

- Abolition of the post.

- Professional incompetence.

- Reorganization of the departments of the Cooperative.

Compulsory termination of service by operation of law due to reaching the age limit:

1- Every employee who has completed the sixty-fourth year of his age shall be terminated from service by operation of law.

2- As for those who perform work requiring extraordinary physical efforts, they shall be terminated from service by operation of law upon their completion of the sixtieth year of age, and these posts shall be determined by a decision of the Board of Directors upon the proposal of the Director General after the approval of the Civil Service Board.

Optional termination of service due to age and seniority:

1- The service of an employee who has completed the fifty-fifth year of his age and whose period of actual service in the permanent cadre of the Cooperative has reached thirty full years may be terminated, by a decision of the Director General, for his incompetence, his unfitness, or his medical incapacity, provided that the Civil Service Board approves this measure.

2- Severance indemnities in the preceding case shall be liquidated in accordance with the provisions of Article 60 of these Regulations.

Abolition of the Post:

If a post in the establishment of the Cooperative is abolished and the appropriations allocated thereto in the budget are deleted, the employee who occupied it shall be transferred to another vacant post in his corps, rank, and salary, provided that he fulfils the conditions of appointment with the exception of the conditions of competitive examination and age; if there is no vacant post in his corps and rank or if he does not fulfil the conditions of appointment therein, a lower post in his corps shall be offered to him, and if he accepts it, he shall retain his salary and the right of priority for appointment to a post of his rank. If he does not accept it, or if there is no vacant post in his corps, he shall be dismissed from service.

Professional Incompetence:

1- The Cooperative shall verify the professional competence of its employees pursuant to an investigation conducted by a special committee formed by the Civil Service Board.

2- Every employee whom the committee proves does not possess the basic knowledge indispensable for him to perform his duties properly shall be dismissed from service.

3- Dismissal from service shall be decided by the authority vested with the power of appointment.

Reorganisation of Departments:

- The Board of Directors maytask a special committee to examine the reorganisation of the departments of the Cooperative, provided that it defines its mission by a reasoned decision issued by it and coupled with the approval of the supervisory authority.

- This committee shall draw up a report on the mission entrusted to it containing its proposals.

- The report shall be submitted to the Board for decision thereon, provided that its decision is coupled with the approval of the supervisory authority.

- If the reorganisation of the departments necessitates the dismissal of one or more employees, his severance indemnity shall be liquidated in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.

- Dismissal in this case shall be decided by the Director General after the approval of the Civil Service Board.

Death:

- Service shall terminate ipso jure upon the death of the employee, and his severance indemnity shall be liquidated in accordance with the provisions of Article 60 of these Regulations.

- The severance indemnity shall be granted to the rightful claimants in accordance with the provisions applicable in this case to civil servants of the State.

As amended pursuant to Decision 63 dated 14/5/91 and Decision 227 dated 1/12/92

Determination of the Severance Indemnity

1- The severance indemnity shall be determined on the basis of one month's salary for each year of actual service up to the tenth, two months' salary for each year of actual service after the tenth and up to the thirtieth, and three months' salary for each year of actual service after the thirtieth.

2- For the purpose of calculating the severance indemnity, and notwithstanding any other text, the following percentages shall be added to the last basic monthly salary that the employee was receiving on the date of termination of his service:

40% for employees of the Fourth and Fifth Categories.

60% for employees of the Second and Third Categories.

75% for employees of the First Category.

- A proportion of one twenty-fourth of the value of the last step for each month that the employee has spent in actual service after his last advancement in step.

Removal from Office:

1- An employee shall be removed from office by a decision of the General Disciplinary Board if he commits a breach of one of his professional duties defined in the laws and regulations, and in particular in Articles 13 and 14 of these Regulations.

2- An employee removed from office shall forfeit his right to the severance indemnity.

3- Under no circumstances may an employee removed from office be reinstated into service in any permanent or temporary post of the Cooperative, the State, public institutions, or municipalities.

1- Temporary posts shall be created by a reasoned decision of the Board of Directors upon the proposal of the Director General within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget of the Cooperative, and after the approval of the supervisory authority.

2- When the Director General sees a necessity to create temporary posts, he shall draw up a statement of these posts comprising their number, the salary of each of them, the justifying reasons for creating them, and the draft regulations and establishment to which they must be subject.

Rights and Duties of the Temporary Employee

The temporary employee shall be subject to the provisions of the special regulations applicable to him.

Termination of Employment:

The temporary employee shall be terminated by a decision of the authority vested with the power of appointment at any time whatsoever.

The Director General shall contract with Lebanese nationals or foreigners for a specified period and to perform a specific work requiring special knowledge and qualifications, within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget of the Cooperative and within the scope of the number fixed therefor.
The contract shall not be renewed tacitly.

Contracted persons shall be granted, upon the expiry of the term of the contract, a severance indemnity in accordance with the bases adopted for granting the severance indemnity to temporary employees of the State.
The Director General may request the approval of public administrations to assign one of their employees to perform overtime work outside official working hours.
The Cooperative shall employ wage-earners in accordance with special regulations drawn up by the Board of Directors upon the proposal of the Director General and approved by the Civil Service Board.

Physiotherapy is an art and a science in the field of treatment whose aim is the rehabilitation of the limbs of the physically disabled and the massaging of human muscles with a view to strengthening the weak among them and restoring their natural activity and strength.
The practice of the profession of physiotherapy shall be subject to a licence from the Ministry of Public Health.

The licence to practise the profession of physiotherapy shall be granted to Lebanese persons who fulfil the following conditions: 1- That the applicant for the licence holds the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, Second Part, or its equivalent. 2- That he holds a specialisation certificate in physiotherapy issued by official or officially recognised institutes or establishments. 3- That he has not been convicted of a felony or a disgraceful offence. 4- That he passes a colloquium examination in the same manner as the other branches of the medical professions in accordance with the regulations in force.

Non-Lebanese persons may be granted a licence to practise the profession of physiotherapy in Lebanon if they fulfil the conditions provided for in the preceding Article, provided that they belong to countries that permit Lebanese nationals to practise this profession on their territories. And provided that reciprocity is applied on the basis of the inverse numerical proportion of the population.
The Ministry of Public Health may, exceptionally and temporarily, grant a licence to foreign missions to teach or practise the profession of physiotherapy free of charge.

A person licensed to practise the profession of physiotherapy is prohibited from employing persons to perform acts of treatment who are not licensed to practise the profession in due form, and he is also prohibited from treating any patient except pursuant to a physician's prescription and on his responsibility, which shall be kept in the patient's file.
Physiotherapists shall not be entitled to use misleading advertisements and medical titles, but they may announce only their name, the type of their specialisation, and their working hours.
Physiotherapy premises must fulfil the sanitary conditions, and anyone who wishes to open and operate a physiotherapy premises must obtain a prior licence from the Ministry of Public Health.
The practitioner of the profession of physiotherapy and all those working with him must abide by professional secrecy.
The Minister of Public Health shall, where necessary, issue decisions relating to the implementation of the provisions of this Law.

The provisions of the Third Article shall not apply to persons who obtained a licence to practise the profession of medical massage before the date of entry into force of this Law. Likewise, those who held before the date of 1/1/1970 an officially recognised medical massage certificate and who apply for a licence to practise the profession within a period of two years from the date of the entry into force of this Law shall be exempted from the provisions of items: (1), (2), and (4) of the Third Article of this Law.
The Minister of Public Health shall be entitled to close any physiotherapy premises whose owner does not hold an official licence to practise this profession.
Holders of physiotherapy certificates issued by the Ministry of National Education shall be exempted from the colloquium examination.
Anyone who unlawfully practises the profession of physiotherapy shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Article 393 of the Lebanese Penal Code.

With the exception of the provisions relating to the regulation of the profession of cosmetology, the provisions of the draft law put into force by virtue of Decree No. 9827 dated 22/6/962 and all other provisions contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content are repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

There shall be established in Lebanon a council for wild hunting called the "Higher Council for Wild Hunting", hereinafter referred to by the term "the Council".

The Council shall be composed of one representative from the following ministries and public institutions: Justice, Agriculture, Environment, Interior and Municipalities, National Defence, Finance, the National Council for Scientific Research, the Association of the National Council for Wild Hunting, an environmental specialist in ornithology and mammalogy, a representative of the Syndicate of Dealers in Hunting Weapons and Ammunition Therefor, a representative of the Lebanese Shooting and Hunting Federation, and a representative of environmental associations.

All members of the Council shall be volunteers who work free of charge.

a - The representatives mentioned in Article One of this Law shall be appointed, for a non-renewable term of three years, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers on the basis of the nomination of the ministries and administrations concerned specified in Article One.

b - The Council shall commence its work immediately upon the issuance of the decree necessary therefor.

c - The internal regulations of the Council shall be issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment.

d - The Council shall be linked to the Minister of Environment in his capacity as the tutelage authority.

e - The Council shall be subject to the ex post audit of the Court of Accounts.

The Minister of Environment shall determine the date of opening and closing of the hunting season and the times during which hunting is permitted, upon the proposal of the Council, provided that the application of the principle of sustainability of the natural heritage stipulated in the concluded international conventions is observed, such that hunting shall be prohibited during the breeding season of animals and birds, and during their passage towards their breeding grounds or while caring for their young.

a - The Minister of Tutelage shall determine, after consulting the Council, the game classified as hunting game and permitted to be hunted at specific times and shall determine those times. With the exception of the game determined in accordance with the preceding paragraph, all resident and migratory wild birds and animals shall be considered protected throughout the year and their hunting shall be prohibited.

b - The Minister of Tutelage shall take the necessary decisions to prohibit, temporarily or permanently, the hunting of every bird or animal that appears to be beneficial to agriculture or to the ecological balance or for the purpose of propagating its species due to the scarcity of its numbers locally or due to its inclusion on the lists of globally endangered birds and animals set forth in the international conventions concluded with Lebanon and those set forth in the Red Data Book of the International Union (I.U.C.N), and he shall designate the areas and periods in which hunting is prohibited during the year, upon the proposal of the Council.

c - The Council shall propose to the Minister of Tutelage the taking of decisions regarding:

1 - The times during which the hunting of transboundary birds and animals is permitted.

2 - The birds and animals harmful to agriculture or to the ecological balance which may be hunted at any time he deems appropriate.

3 - The birds and animals the hunting of which is strictly prohibited, and the lands in which hunting is prohibited upon the request of their owners or exploiters, including municipalities.

4 - The Minister of Tutelage shall, upon the proposal of the Council, determine the conditions and criteria as well as the private clubs to conduct the examination to which every applicant for a hunting licence for the first time after the issuance of this Law shall mandatorily be subject.

5 - The establishment of centres for breeding various species of wild animals and birds, provided that they are of local species or species that pass through Lebanon naturally, and especially those threatened with extinction, for the purpose of increasing their number and releasing them subsequently, in preservation of biological diversity and ecological balance, and the associations concerned with this matter shall be commissioned.

The Director General of the Ministry of Environment shall perform the duties of the Government Commissioner to the Council and shall attend its sessions and participate in the discussion without the right to vote, and through him all minutes of sessions and decisions shall be submitted to the Minister of Environment and shall also be notified through him to all public administrations concerned with the practice of hunting and to the Court of Accounts.

It is prohibited for anyone to hunt outside the times during which hunting is permitted.

And the hunter must hold a hunting licence from the Ministry of Environment based on:

a - A legal licence to carry weapons from the Ministry of National Defence for weapons of the fourth category (for hunting furred game), and from the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities for weapons of the fifth category (for hunting wild birds).

b - A third-party liability insurance policy, that is, specific to guaranteeing damages that may be inflicted on third parties as a result of the practice of hunting, to be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

Wild birds and animals in Lebanon, whatever their species or origin, shall not be considered the property of anyone.

The owner of a real property or the holder of any right therein may prohibit hunting on his real properties by placing signs at the entrances of these real properties announcing the prohibition in accordance with the rules in force.

Hunting is strictly prohibited in cities, villages, picnic areas, public parks, nature reserves and places classified as heritage sites, at a distance of not less than 500 metres from residential places, places of worship, and public and private installations, even if carried out by means of air pressure or compressed gas weapons, and displaying hunted game outside cars and on public roads is also prohibited.

Hunting is strictly prohibited by means of owls, birdlime, nets, traps, snares, artificial and natural floating birds, bait, captive game and searchlights, and it is also prohibited by means of poisons, gas, smoke and electrical devices.

Hunting shall not be permitted except by means of firearms licensed for hunting, and the crossbow, and it shall be permitted by means of dogs, falcons, hawks and eagles.

Lying in wait for partridges and deceiving any species of game by attracting it through the use of recording devices that emit sounds similar to the sounds of birds and animals is strictly prohibited.

Chasing all species of game by means of a car or aircraft is also prohibited. And likewise hunting in mountainous areas when they are completely covered with snow.

It is prohibited in all seasons of the year to remove nests or to take, destroy, sell, buy, transport, capture or harm the eggs, chicks or young of wild animals and birds. It is also prohibited to export the eggs or chicks of all species of wild birds and animals (with the exception of birds and eggs of wild birds and animals bred on farms) and the young of furred animals, and the caging of wild partridges is also prohibited.
It is prohibited to export hunted game without a licence issued by the Ministry of Environment.

The manufacture and importation of birdlime (Cordia myxa) and adhesive substances used for catching birds, or their sale, possession, circulation, use or hunting therewith, is strictly prohibited.

And the sale, display or use of devices that emit sounds similar to the sounds of birds or animals (calling devices) is strictly prohibited.

Promoting them through advertising is also prohibited, and their temporary passage within Lebanese territory (transit) is prohibited.

The hunting licence shall be considered personal, annual, and shall be granted by the Ministry of Environment exclusively to the hunter in accordance with Article Six of this Law, provided that he fulfils all the conditions stipulated in the said Article.

There shall be stated on the licence the name and address of its holder, his distinguishing marks, his signature or fingerprint, and the species of game which he is entitled to hunt, and this licence shall be granted after the collection of the fee determined pursuant to the laws and regulations in force on the date of granting the licence.

While practising hunting, the hunter must mandatorily carry a licence to carry the weapon used, the hunting licence, and the insurance policy specific to hunting.

As for scientific researchers, they may capture animals and birds for the purpose of scientific research, provided that they are released alive without causing harm to them, and they may also collect eggs to conduct research thereon, and such persons shall obtain a special permit from the Ministry of Environment on the basis of an application submitted to the National Council for Scientific Research.

Shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one month and by a fine equivalent to five hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties, and by the withdrawal of the hunting licence for a period of one to three years, any person apprehended:

1 - Whilst practising hunting outside the season or the times during which hunting is permitted.

2 - In possession of game hunted outside the hunting seasons and times.

3 - Whilst hunting on the lands of others without the consent of their owners or the holders of rights over them, or in places where there are crops or tree saplings whose yield is still upon them or which are surrounded by a closed fence preventing their connection with neighbouring lands, or despite the presence of the sign provided for in Article Seven of this Law.

Shall be punished by the imprisonment and the fine provided for in the preceding Article, or by either of these two penalties, and in all cases by the permanent confiscation of the weapon used and, where applicable, by the destruction of the devices, materials, instruments and means prohibited pursuant to the provisions of this Law, any person apprehended:

1 - Whilst hunting without a licence.

2 - Whilst hunting by means of instruments or materials and devices or any other means the use of which is prohibited under this Law.

3 - Having hunted useful birds or birds the hunting of which is prohibited.

In the event of recidivism, the penalty of the fine shall be doubled without the penalty of imprisonment. The penalty for recidivism shall apply to any person who violates the provisions of Article Ten of this Law or has hunted species threatened with the danger of extinction.

Shall be deemed a recidivist any person who has been referred to the court pursuant to this Law during the twenty-four months preceding his commission of the last offence.

The guards of natural reserves shall have the right to draw up offence reports against offenders within the perimeter of the reserves, and the report drawn up by them shall have the effect of a report drawn up by an assistant of the judicial police.

With the exception of members of the Internal Security Forces and the forest and hunting guards affiliated with the Ministry of Agriculture, the members mentioned below shall be granted, on an exceptional basis and solely for the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, the right to draw up offence reports against offenders and refer them to the competent authorities:

- Guards of natural reserves, provided that they hold a qualification certificate issued by "the Council".

Any hunter apprehended committing one of the offences provided for in this Law whilst disguised or masked, or who refuses to disclose his identity, or who has no known place of residence, shall be brought immediately before the criminal judge having jurisdiction over the place of the offence.

In this case, the maximum penalty prescribed for the offence shall be applied against him.

The fee for a licence to carry and possess a weapon of the Fourth Category (bullet hunting weapon) and the ammunition pertaining thereto is fixed at an amount of two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds /200000/ L.L. for each piece of weaponry, paid once upon the issuance of the permit.

- The fee for a licence to carry and possess a weapon of the Fifth Category (hunting weapon) and the ammunition pertaining thereto is fixed as follows:

1. Licensing fee for a single-shot, single-barrel hunting weapon 2.300.000 L.L.

2. Licensing fee for a two-shot, double-barrel (side-by-side/over-under) hunting weapon 4.600.000 L.L.

3. Licensing fee for a three-shot, semi-automatic hunting weapon 9.200.000 L.L.

4. Licensing fee for a multi-barrel hunting weapon, (one or more of these barrels being for bullets) 9.200.000 L.L.

The fee for the terrestrial hunting licence shall be fixed by the Ministry of Finance upon the proposal of the supervising Minister.

This fee shall be collected by means of a special stamp called the "Terrestrial Hunting Stamp" issued by the Ministry of Finance in accordance with the details and elements adopted by the Council and approved by the Ministers of Finance and of the Environment.

All laws and texts contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its provisions are repealed, in particular the Terrestrial Hunting Regulations issued on 18 June 1952 and the amendments thereto (Articles 81 et seq.), with the exception of the laws and decrees relating to the Association of the National Council for Terrestrial Hunting in all that is not inconsistent with the provisions of this Law.
The details of implementation of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by implementing decrees.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Articles 27 and 28 of Decision No. 1130/M/2001 dated 10/9/2001 are repealed and replaced with the following text:

A member of the teaching staff shall be assigned the duties of supervision by a decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education, after consulting the opinion of the competent Director of Education and upon the proposal of the Director General of Education.

Anyone who assumes the duties of supervision and various administrative duties shall be required to satisfy the following:

1 - Not to have been sentenced:

a - To a penalty of the second degree under the Civil Servants Regulations.

b - Or to the last two penalties (of the penalties of the first degree) at their maximum limit, or twice to either of them at its maximum limit.

c - The effect of the penalties precluding the right to assignment shall lapse after the passage of five years from the date of completion of the execution of the last penalty thereof.

2 - To be of good conduct in the school and in society.

3 - To be of educational and administrative experience.

4 - To have spent more than five years of teaching in the permanent cadre.

5 - To submit, through the administrative hierarchy, a written application containing his desire to assume the tasks of supervision or various administrative duties, under penalty of rejection of non-compliant applications.

There shall be exempted from the duties of supervision and other administrative duties anyone who:

- Is proven to have failed in performing the tasks entrusted to him, pursuant to established evidence (written replies - letters of warning, etc....).

- Has lost one of the conditions mentioned in Article Two of this Decision.

- Has submitted a reasoned personal application for exemption.

The number of supervisors in the school shall be determined as follows:

- One supervisor for each school whose number of pupils is less than one hundred and fifty pupils.

- Two supervisors for each school whose number of pupils exceeds one hundred and fifty pupils.

- Three supervisors for each school whose number of pupils exceeds three hundred pupils.

- Four supervisors for each school whose number of pupils exceeds four hundred and fifty pupils.

- Five supervisors for each school whose number of pupils exceeds six hundred pupils.

- Six supervisors for each school whose number of pupils exceeds eight hundred pupils.

The number of supervisors may be modified in each school whose rooms are distributed over more than one building or more than two floors, pursuant to a reasoned letter from the Director General of Education.

Notwithstanding any other text, a member of the teaching staff shall be assigned to perform various administrative tasks (librarianship and otherwise) by a decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education, after consulting the opinion of the competent Director of Education and upon the proposal of the Director General of Education.
This Decision shall be communicated to whom it may concern and wherever needed.
