Mandatory Nature of the Permit:

The construction, conversion, restoration and renovation of buildings of all kinds shall be subject to obtaining a prior permit granted in accordance with the provisions in force and on the basis of the approval of the competent technical administrations based on a technical inspection conducted by them for this purpose. The application for the prior permit and the building plans must be signed by the responsible engineer in accordance with the regulations governing the practice of the profession in the two Orders of Engineers, and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut or Tripoli according to the registration of the responsible engineer and in accordance with the Law Regulating the Engineering Profession.

The prior permit is mandatory for all buildings, even those belonging to public administrations, public institutions and municipalities, with the exception of military public buildings which are determined by a decision of the Council of Ministers, provided that they comply with the indicated conditions specified in this Law and the regulations in force.

The prior permit shall be granted, on the basis of the technical inspection issued by the competent technical administration, by:

- The head of the executive authority in the competent municipality for buildings intended to be constructed within the municipal boundaries.

- The Muhafiz or the Qaimaqam for buildings intended to be constructed outside the municipal boundaries.

Works Exempted from the Permit:

The application for a prior permit shall be replaced by a written declaration signed by a responsible engineer and certified by one of the two Orders of Engineers in the following works:

- External maintenance works (whitewashing, joinery, etc..).

- Construction of boundary walls.

- All restoration works, in buildings or parts of buildings that exist legally or that have been regularised.

- Cladding works.

- Retaining walls and demolition works.

- Levelling of natural ground in the light of the building permit plans (with the obligation to comply with the provisions of the last paragraph of Article Four).

- Internal modifications within a residential unit or an independent right, which do not affect the structural elements and the common parts and which do not affect the legality of the residential unit.

Strengthening works that involve the main structure of the building or the replacement of roofs and balconies shall only be permitted in buildings or parts of buildings that exist legally or that have been regularised.

Receipts for declarations of all kinds and certificates of legality of the building shall be granted by the competent authorities that grant the building permit in accordance with the provisions of Article Four of this Law.

The details of the works covered by the written declaration and the exemption of certain works from the declaration shall be determined by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

The declaration for works exempted from the permit shall be valid for a period of one year.

Conditions and Documents of the Permit Application:

The conditions that must be met in the application for a prior permit or the written declaration, the documents that must be attached thereto, the conditions for keeping the registers of building permits and declarations, and the methods of notifying them to the concerned administrations and bodies and the interested parties shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport upon the proposal of the Director General of Urban Planning.

Effect and consequences of appointment:

1- No person shall be appointed except to a vacant post on the establishment of the Cooperative for which a special appropriation has been allocated in the budget and in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the regulations of the Cooperative.

2- Appointment shall be made at the last step of the category.

However, if the employee has been drawn from the establishments of the State, public institutions or municipalities and his salary exceeds the salary of the last step, he shall be appointed at the step the salary of which equals his salary on his original establishment.

3- The appointment shall take effect from the date of assumption of duties, and it shall not be permissible for it to produce any retroactive effect.

4- Instruments of appointment shall be notified to the Civil Service Board and the Central Inspection Administration.

5- If the appointment is made to a post that is not vacant on the establishment or to a post for which no special appropriation has been allocated in the budget, both the liquidator and the payment-ordering officer shall be prohibited from liquidating the expenditure resulting therefrom and disbursing it even if a written order to that effect is received by them, and the payment-ordering officer shall notify the matter to the Board of Directors and to the supervisory authority in order to take action to cancel the instrument of appointment.

6- If the appointment is contrary to the regulatory procedures, it shall be deemed ineffective and no vested right shall accrue to the person concerned as a result thereof until he obtains from the competent judicial authority a final and binding decision as to its legality.

An employee shall, in general:

1- Be guided in his work by the public interest alone, and ensure the application of the laws and regulations in force, without overlooking any infringement or negligence.

2- Submit to his immediate superior and execute his orders and instructions unless such orders and instructions are clearly contrary to the regulations.

In this case, the employee shall draw the attention of his superior in writing to the infringement occurring and shall not be bound to execute such orders and instructions unless the superior confirms them in writing, and he may send copies of the correspondence to the Central Inspection Administration.

3- Bear personal responsibility for the orders and instructions which he gives to his subordinates.

4- Complete the transactions of interested parties with speed, accuracy and fidelity within the limits of his competence.

Prohibited acts:

An employee is prohibited from performing any act forbidden by the laws and regulations in force, and in particular:

1- To engage in political affairs, or join political parties, or wear the badge of any party, or deliver or publish, without written permission from the Director General, speeches, articles, statements or books on any matters.

2- To join professional organizations or syndicates.

3- To go on strike from work or incite others to strike.

4- To practise any commercial or industrial profession or any other remunerated profession or trade, except in the cases expressly provided for by special laws and regulations, or to be a member of the board of directors of a joint-stock company or a partnership limited by shares, or to have a direct material interest or an interest through a third party in an enterprise subject to his supervision or to the supervision of the administration of the Cooperative, or in work executed by the Cooperative.

5- To combine his post with parliamentary, municipal and mukhtar elective offices as set forth in the special laws relating to such offices.

6- To perform any remunerated work that detracts from the dignity of the post or is connected therewith.

7- To solicit or accept any recommendation, or to solicit or accept, directly or indirectly by reason of the post which he occupies, gifts, gratuities or grants of any kind whatsoever.

8- To disclose official information of which he has become cognizant during the performance of his post, even after the termination of his period of service, unless the Director General authorizes him in writing to do so.

1- Salaries in the Cooperative shall be fixed in accordance with the salary scale set out in Schedule No. 2 annexed to these Regulations.

2- Salaries and their accessories shall be liquidated on a monthly basis and all months without exception shall be calculated as thirty days with effect from the first day thereof.

3- Salaries shall be paid at the beginning of each month.

4- No advance on salaries may be made before they fall due.

5- No person may receive the salary of a post unless he is regularly appointed thereto and is actually performing the duties thereof, subject to the special cases provided for in the Regulations. Immediate superiors shall be deemed personally responsible for the payment of the salaries of employees who do not actually perform the duties of their posts.

6- It shall not be permissible to combine two salaries.

Conditions of entitlement to salary:

1- The salary of a new employee shall fall due with effect from the date of his assumption of duties.

2- The new salary of an employee advanced in step shall fall due with effect from the first day of the month following the month in which the advancement took place.

3- The new salary of an employee promoted from one category to another category shall fall due with effect from the date of issuance of the instrument providing for his promotion.

4- The new salary of an employee who is sentenced to reduction of rank or step shall fall due with effect from the date on which the judgment becomes final.

Cases in which half salary is paid:

1- An employee suspended from work shall receive half of his salary with effect from the day following the date of his notification of the instrument providing for his suspension from work.

And with effect from the date of his actual cessation of work if he had ceased work prior to being notified of the instrument. The other half shall not be paid to him unless the General Disciplinary Board acquits him or sentences him to a penalty of the first degree

or if the Cooperative refrains from referring him to the General Disciplinary Board after the expiry of fifteen days from the date of his suspension from work.

2- An employee placed under preventative judicial detention shall receive half of his salary. The other half shall not be paid to him unless his trial is barred, or he is acquitted, or he is sentenced to a penalty other than the penalty of imprisonment.

Cases in which salary is withheld:

1- Salary shall be withheld from an employee placed outside the establishment or on availability, and from an employee suspended from work by judgment of the General Disciplinary Board or dismissed from service, or who has resigned or been removed from office, with effect from the day following the date of his notification of the instrument or from the date of his cessation of work if that occurred prior to the effecting of notification.

2- Salary shall be withheld from an employee who is deemed to have resigned pursuant to the provisions of these Regulations starting from the day on which he ought to have returned to his post.

3- Salary shall be withheld from an employee who has reached the legal age, with effect from the day following his reaching that age, even if no instrument has been issued providing for his termination of service.

Special cases:

1- An employee transferred to a post the seat of which is in a place other than his place of residence shall be entitled to continue receiving his salaries without interruption, provided that he complies

with the written instructions issued by his superiors regarding his travel.

2- An employee shall not receive a salary for the period which he spends in prison

in execution of a judicial penalty unless he was sentenced for an unintentional misdemeanor.

3- If an employee disappears, or news of him is cut off as a result of an act connected with the post, his salaries shall be disbursed to the beneficiaries provided for in the Regulations for a period of one year at most, and this period shall be deemed to be included in

actual service. The employee shall be deemed dismissed from service after the expiry of the year. The rights of his heirs shall be liquidated provisionally in accordance with the provisions of the Regulations.

4- If an employee whose service has ended is required to carry out the formality of handing over and taking over, he shall receive an allowance equivalent to his salary for the period which he spends in carrying out the operation of handing over and taking over, provided that the period required for the handing over as well as the amount of the allowance shall be fixed by a decision of the Director General, and provided that the allowance shall not exceed two months' salary in any case whatsoever.

Family allowance:

An employee in the Cooperative who receives a monthly salary shall be granted a family allowance in respect of his spouse and children in accordance with all the conditions and rules applicable to employees of the State.

On the execution of the permit:

In principle, the permit shall be limited to the matters contained therein, and every amendment sought to be introduced to the permitted and unexecuted building, which is capable of altering the external projection of the building or its internal partitioning or its height in a manner that affects the line of sight or the envelopes or increases the permitted areas, must be declared by submitting amending plans registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers. In such case, the fee shall be imposed on that which exceeds the permitted basic areas on the basis of the unit fee resulting from the assessment in accordance with the prevailing price on the date of the granting of the basic building permit, and an supplementary amending permit shall be granted, the validity of which shall expire upon the expiry of the validity of the basic permit.

If the permitted building under execution includes internal amendments without a fundamental alteration in the external projection of the building or the height, the concerned party may continue the works under the responsibility of the engineer until the submission of the occupancy permit application.

A copy of the prior permit granted and a copy of the order to commence shall be displayed prominently at the construction site prior to commencing the works, throughout the duration of the works, and until obtaining the final works (occupancy) permit for all parts of the building.

Upon obtaining a permit or a declaration receipt and upon commencing the work, the owner of the real property shall have the right to use the sidewalk up to a maximum of two metres, provided that a pedestrian passage is secured within the sidewalk having a width of not less than eighty centimetres (80 cm) throughout the duration of the work.

The permit shall be granted to the owner of the real property or to whoever legally succeeds him, without prejudice to the rights of third parties, and the owner or whoever succeeds him, the engineers, and the contractors shall be responsible, each with respect to that which concerns him, and they must take the necessary arrangements prior to and during the commencement of the work to secure the maintenance, safety, and stability of public and private structures, the safety of persons, and the non-obstruction of traffic.

The technical conditions for the right to use the sidewalk and the particulars of the responsibilities of each of the owner or whoever succeeds him, the engineers, and the contractors shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

If all the works that are the subject of the permit or declaration are not executed within the legal time limits, the unexecuted works or parts thereof shall be deemed unpermitted, and the execution thereof shall be subject to obtaining a new permit or submitting a new declaration according to their nature and to the payment of the fees due thereon.

Upon the expiry of the permit time limit, the building works shall be deemed not to require the payment of new permit fees as soon as its load-bearing parts (foundations, load-bearing walls, all external walls, columns beams, roofs) are completed. As for the remaining internal and external works, they shall be deemed complementary works that require obtaining a declaration receipt.

After the expiry of the validity of the permit and in the event of non-completion of the external facades of the building, the owner of the real property must finish the complementary works for the facades within a time limit of one year from the date of expiry of the permit time limit, failing which fines shall be imposed on the unexecuted works for the facades equal to (15%) fifteen percent of the value of the permit fees according to the prevailing assessment for each year, and they shall be registered on the real folio of the real property as a privileged debt.

The municipalities must execute what is mentioned above after conducting an assessment for the permit in accordance with the rules and notifying the competent departments.

Existing buildings the permit validity of which has expired, and the structure of which has been completed while their facades have not yet been completed, shall be subject to the provisions of the paragraph above with respect to delay fines. The assessment of the fees shall be carried out and the fines shall take effect one year after the date of issuance of this Law.

This item shall apply to violating buildings with respect to removing the violations and completing the facades or demolishing the building in its entirety. The unexecuted internal works and external complementary works shall be subject to obtaining a declaration receipt or a restoration permit in accordance with the type of the unexecuted works, and obtaining the declaration or the restoration permit shall not exempt the owner of the real property from the fines imposed for the period prior to the date of the declaration in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

Upon the expiry of the permit time limit, the building works shall be deemed not to require the payment of new permit fees as soon as its load-bearing parts (foundations, load-bearing walls, all external walls, columns beams, roofs) are completed. As for the remaining internal and external works, they shall be deemed complementary works that require obtaining a declaration receipt.

After the expiry of the validity of the permit and in the event of non-completion of the external facades of the building, the owner of the real property must finish the complementary works for the facades within a time limit of one year from the date of expiry of the permit time limit, failing which fines shall be imposed on the unexecuted works for the facades equal to (15%) fifteen percent of the value of the permit fees according to the prevailing assessment for each year, and they shall be registered on the real folio of the real property as a privileged debt.

The municipalities must execute what is mentioned above after conducting an assessment for the permit in accordance with the rules and notifying the competent departments.

Existing buildings the permit validity of which has expired, and the structure of which has been completed while their facades have not yet been completed, shall be subject to the provisions of the paragraph above with respect to delay fines. The assessment of the fees shall be carried out and the fines shall take effect one year after the date of issuance of this Law.

This item shall apply to violating buildings with respect to removing the violations and completing the facades or demolishing the building in its entirety. The unexecuted internal works and external complementary works shall be subject to obtaining a declaration receipt or a restoration permit in accordance with the type of the unexecuted works, and obtaining the declaration or the restoration permit shall not exempt the owner of the real property from the fines imposed for the period prior to the date of the declaration in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

First: The occupancy permit: its types and the procedure for granting it:

Upon completion of the licensed building, including the external facades, the owner shall submit to the competent technical administration an application to obtain an occupancy (habitation) permit accompanied by the required documents and the plans of the executed works registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers showing that the execution took place under the supervision of the engineers signing the plans, each according to his specialisation, in accordance with the regulations in force and in accordance with the licence or the executed amendment and pursuant to the regulations of the two Orders of Engineers, subject to compliance with the following:

- Final occupancy permits shall be granted for the entirety of the licensed works, or granted for each building or block separately (an independent staircase and lift) provided that the common parts from which this block benefits are completed.

- A partial occupancy permit shall be granted for a part of a building, provided that the works of the facades of the building and its common parts are completed.

Upon the granting of the final occupancy permit for all the licensed works, the building permit shall be deemed terminated by operation of law even if its period of validity has not yet expired. The authority that granted the prior permit for building shall grant the occupancy (habitation) permit on the basis of the approval of the competent technical administrations.

The conditions for completion of the licensed building and the documents required for granting a complete or partial final occupancy permit or a complete or partial temporary occupancy permit shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning. The conditions for submitting this application and keeping the registers and receipts relating thereto shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works upon the proposal of the Directorate General of Urban Planning.

Second: Amendments to the licensed building:

Where there are amendments to the licence, plans showing the state of the building after execution signed by the responsible engineer must be submitted, and in the event that there is an increase in the licensed area or a fundamental amendment to the design of the building, these amending plans shall be registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut and Tripoli.

If it appears that the building conforms to the designs on the basis of which the permit was granted, or differs therefrom yet remained in conformity with the texts in force when the licence was granted and with the special provisions specified in the building permit, if any, the occupancy (habitation) permit shall be granted after the approval of the competent technical administrations, and after all fees and fines due, where applicable, have been paid in accordance with the prevailing price on the date of granting the original building permit for the additional areas executed without a licence.

In the event that the building or any part thereof does not conform to the texts in force, the owner shall carry out, under the supervision of the responsible engineer who signed the permit application, the works necessary for the building to become conforming, and he shall thereafter notify the administration and submit new plans, where applicable, signed by the responsible engineer and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut and Tripoli.

Third: On time-limits

The occupancy permit must be granted or refused within one month at most from the date of submission of the application. In the event of refusal, the reasons therefor must be stated once only and the nature and location of the infringement must be specified. If the aforementioned time-limit expires and no decision has been taken on the application by way of approval or refusal, the applicant for the permit may consider himself licensed by operation of law for occupancy on his own responsibility and notify the administration in writing thereof, provided that the constructions are in conformity with the licence and with the texts in force, and that he pays the legal fees in the event that there are lawful increases to the areas set out in the original licence within two months at most from the date of expiry of the time-limit specified above.

Subdivision of the building:

Subject to the provisions of Article 26 of Law No. 539 dated 24/7/1996, the Land Registry and Cadastre Offices are prohibited from finally subdividing the building into different rights unless the person concerned produces a duly issued occupancy (habitation) permit and certificates issued by the competent administrations proving that the building has been connected to the public electricity and water network.

The occupancy permit may be replaced by one of the following documents:

1 - A certificate based on official records issued by the head of the executive authority in the municipality, or by the Governor (Muhafiz) or the District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) in the absence of a municipality, and if that is not possible for lack of proof, reliance may be placed on a certificate issued by the competent financial departments in the governorates proving that the building was completed before the date of 13/9/1971

2 - A certificate from the competent technical administration proving that no decision has been taken on the occupancy permit application by way of approval or refusal within the period provided for in Article Six above, accompanied by a certificate from the responsible engineer (the signatory to the permit application) proving the conformity of the building with the granted permit.

Remnants of public and private domain:

The purchase of a remnant of public or private domain belonging to the State or to the municipalities resulting from the execution of an alignment plan or an expropriation shall only take place after the approval of the entity owning the remnant on the basis of a recommendation of the competent technical administration.

As for the purchase of remnants of private domain, it shall take place in accordance with the provisions of the Urban Planning Law, and it is not mandatory for granting the licence. The granting of the building permit in this case shall be conditional upon the payment of a deposit by the owner equivalent to the price of the remnant estimated on the basis of the assessment adopted for the real property for the imposition of the building fee, provided that the formalities of decommissioning, demarcation and annexation are subsequently carried out at the expense of the applicant for purchase.

The remnant in this case shall be deemed annexed to the original real property if the conditions for annexation provided for in the land laws are met therein; otherwise, the remnant shall be deemed a unit of two properties with the original real property.

The time-limits for granting the building licence referred to in Article Four of this Law shall run after the payment of the deposit referred to above. The price of the remnant shall be finally determined by the committee specified in Article 80 of Decision No. 275/26 in accordance with the prevailing price on the date of payment of the deposit, and in the event of a dispute over the price, the competent Appellate Expropriation Committees shall adjudicate thereon on the same bases within one year from the date of payment of the deposit, and after the lapse of this period, the deposit paid shall be deemed the price for this remnant and the Land Registry Offices must within this remnant to the original real property.

The operation of annexing the remnant to the real property is not mandatory for the administration if it declares its allocation for public use.

The envelope:

The building envelope is the volume within which the building must remain, and it consists of vertical and inclined planes and lines without the possibility of exceeding the maximum height specified in the regulations of the zone in which the real property is located.

This envelope and the methods of its application shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

Projection beyond the Envelope:

1 - Projections beyond the envelope line erected on the road side:

Projection beyond the envelope line erected on the road side shall be permitted only for open, unenclosed balconies, canopies, staircase and elevator shafts, sunbreakers (Brise Soleil), cornices, means of decoration and beautification, flower boxes, advertisements, pitched tile roofs, parapets, and walls erected above the roof of the top floor to conceal staircase and elevator shafts, water tanks, and technical installations, as well as for thermal insulation and waterproofing works whose height does not exceed fifty centimetres /50 cm/ above the roof of the top floor.

2 - Projection beyond the envelope line erected on the open spaces side:

Projection beyond the envelope line erected on the open spaces side shall be permitted for staircase and elevator shafts, cornices, means of decoration and beautification, flower boxes, sunbreakers, pitched tile roofs, and for parapets and walls erected above the roof of the top floor to conceal staircase and elevator shafts, water tanks, and technical installations, as well as for thermal insulation and waterproofing works whose height does not exceed fifty centimetres /50 cm/ above the roof of the top floor, under the same conditions permitted for projections beyond the envelope line erected on the street side.

The conditions and specifications of the projections that are the subject of items (1) and (2) of this Article shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

3 - Exceptional projection:

By a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council for Urban Planning, projection beyond the envelope line may be permitted for certain parts of industrial buildings and places of worship if the nature of their structure and allocation so requires, provided that there are no reasons preventing this projection, such as aviation safety.

Line of Sight:

The line of sight is the distance between the vertical line erected tangent to the facade at the axis of the opening that lights and ventilates the room and the vertical line erected on the boundary of the real property or another vertical line.

This distance shall be measured within the field of the line of sight and along the axis of the opening (window, glass door, or glass facade), from the most prominent point of the building structure opposite the opening.

The line of sight may extend across the boundary of another real property if easements and rights to that effect are registered in the title register of the two real properties concerned.

Rooms intended for habitation or for daytime or day-and-night occupancy must have at least one line of sight onto open spaces or onto roads, the specifications and conditions of which shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

The following shall not be considered rooms requiring a line of sight:

1-

- Stairwells - bathrooms - lavatories - entrances of residential apartments, provided that their area does not exceed ten percent of the area of the apartment.

- Waiting rooms for commercial offices and for liberal professions, provided that their area does not exceed twenty percent of the area of the office with a maximum of thirty square metres (30m2) - corridors - lobbies - pantries - ironing rooms - larders - servants' rooms - laundry rooms and kitchens, provided that the area of the kitchen, laundry room, ironing room, larder, or maid's room does not exceed eight square metres and that the rooms mentioned in this item are independent of one another - lecture and sports halls - cinema halls - exhibition halls - lobbies of hotels, banks, and private and public institutions - nightclubs, restaurants, and cafes - laboratories - developing, photography, X-ray, operating, and examination rooms - machine rooms - factories (their industrial sections) - hangars - warehouses - poultry and animal farming buildings - commercial shops - offices pertaining to these halls, salons, and rooms - offices in hotels and hospitals.

2 - Rooms resulting from the partitioning of halls by glass partitions shall not be considered rooms requiring a line of sight, provided that the transparent area thereof is not less than sixty percent (60%).

3 - The aforementioned sections in items (1) and (2) and the rooms of buildings similar in terms of use to the rooms and sections listed above and which do not by their nature require the provision of a view, the manner of their ventilation shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Setback of Buildings:

Subject to the setback easements imposed and which may be imposed subsequently pursuant to regulations enacted by decrees in the Council of Ministers, buildings must be erected:

1 - Along the sides of international, main, secondary, and local roads: in accordance with the setback imposed pursuant to their special setback decree.

2 - Along the sides of internal roads: in accordance with the setback imposed from the boundary of the real property pursuant to the zoning regulations in zoned areas, provided that it is not less than four and a half metres from the axis of a road whose width is less than six metres, and three metres in unzoned areas.

3 - Along the sides of railways: behind a line situated at least three metres from the boundaries of railway property.

4 - Along the sides of "enclosed" canals: in accordance with the setback imposed from the boundary of the real property pursuant to the zoning regulations, with a minimum of two metres from the boundary of the real property.

5 - Along the sides of natural winter watercourses: behind a line situated four and a half metres from the boundary of the watercourse.

6 - Along the sides of rivers: behind a line situated ten metres /10m/ from the boundary of the riverbed, unless the special regulations of the zone provide otherwise.

7 - From the boundaries of other public domain properties: behind a line situated at least three metres /3m/ outside the boundaries of the City of Beirut and two metres within them from the boundaries of the public domain.

Special easements:

First - Special conditions relating to the rights of persons with disabilities:

All buildings shall be required to comply with the provisions of Law No. 220 dated 29/5/2000 relating to the rights of persons with disabilities and with all implementing decrees issued pursuant thereto.

Related text: Application of the provisions of Law No. 220 dated 29/5/2000 relating to the rights of persons with disabilities

Second - Special easements relating to public safety, health and architectural vistas:

1- By decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, conditions and principles may be imposed for studying the structural soundness of buildings and for the use of various building materials, and special conditions may be imposed for protecting buildings from fire hazards or for the building to withstand the effects of natural factors such as earthquakes and others, and the use of certain materials in construction may be prohibited or additional conditions may be imposed regarding the possibility of using them if they pose a danger to public safety and health. Until the issuance of the public safety decrees and their inclusion of special specifications for earthquakes, it is mandatory, with respect to buildings whose number of floors exceeds three or whose height exceeds ten metres above ground level, to adopt an earthquake-resistant design, such that the seismic factor (Zone Perimeter Seismic) used in the analysis and design is not less than /2,0/ or the equivalent of ( Zone 2 B) of the U.B.C. A decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, shall determine the types of projects that require a technical audit office, the conditions and stages that must be adopted for technical audit offices, and the powers of these offices. A decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport and the competent Minister shall also determine the setbacks imposed on the types of public projects linked to public safety (power transmission lines...).

2 - Additional special conditions relating to public safety, health, architectural vistas and Lebanese technical specifications, as well as the provision of additional facilities proportionate to the importance of the building, shall be imposed on certain buildings.

The buildings and the special conditions mentioned above shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

The stages of construction of the building and its occupancy, and its demolition if necessary, must observe the rules of environmental protection and the sustainability of its natural resources (water, air, land and living organisms) as defined by Law No. 444/2002 (Protection of the Environment).

3 - The building permit may be granted subject to compliance with special provisions, and it may be refused if the buildings, in view of their locations, volumes and external appearances, and the structures intended to be erected or altered, are likely to harm public health and safety, natural vistas, the environment or architectural vistas, or if such buildings require public authorities to carry out new public facilities.

4 - The applicant for the permit may be required, when granted the permit, pursuant to the special provisions mentioned in the preceding paragraphs, to carry out various works, and in particular a road network, a water network and connecting it to the public network or constructing a tank to collect winter rainwater for domestic use, wastewater disposal (connecting the building to the public sewage network if it exists, or constructing a septic tank of a design and size suitable for the needs of the building, or constructing a treatment plant in accordance with the conditions and specifications determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning), lighting, arranging and equipping spaces designated for playgrounds, parking lots, and open or wooded spaces or planting new trees, a contribution either in cash or by providing land free of charge for the execution of public facilities related to the needs of the buildings intended to be erected, and which become necessary by the mere erection of these buildings. These special provisions shall be specified in the building permit and expressly mentioned in the decision granting it, and the occupancy (habitation) permit shall not be delivered until the permit holder has executed the imposed obligations.

Where the authority entrusted with granting the building permit considers that such permit must be subjected to special provisions not specified by the technical approval, or considers that the special provisions that were specified are inappropriate, the authority entrusted with granting the permit shall be bound by the decision taken by the Higher Council for Urban Planning in this regard.

Planning studies and building conditions, in zoned and unzoned areas, which are approved by a decision of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, shall become binding on the authority entrusted with granting the building permit, in all matters exceeding the conditions of the approved regulations, provided that the regulatory decree is issued within three years from the date of issuance of the decision.

5 - The building permit may be refused or granted only under conditions specified in the technical approval of the permit if the properties that are the subject of the application are located in areas where the building and its occupants are exposed to danger such as floods or land prone to landslides or collapses.

These areas shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and no compensation of any kind shall be due to the permit applicant in the event of its refusal or as a result of the imposition of conditions resulting in additional costs for the beneficiary.

6 - When the building permit is refused or when it is granted subject to compliance with special provisions pursuant to items /3/ and /4/, the permit applicant, if he considers that the special provisions are unlawful, excessive or inappropriate, may submit the matter to the Minister of Public Works and Transport within three months from the date he is notified of the decision.

The Minister of Public Works and Transport shall adjudicate the matter after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and this shall not preclude judicial remedies to which the permit applicant and the authorities entrusted with granting the building permit are entitled to have recourse.

Rules for granting a building permit and its effects:

First: The regulations that must be complied with in granting building permits:

In granting a prior permit, compliance must be observed with the alignments and regulations in force on the date of granting the permit, particularly those relating to urban planning, health and public safety.

As for properties affected by an approved unexecuted alignment, whether expropriated or not expropriated, the approved alignment shall be adopted in all its particulars with respect to determining the manner of entry and exit of vehicles to and from the property, and the extent of the view and the envelope, provided that the setback from the boundaries of the property prior to the alignment shall not be less than four and a half metres.

Upon submitting the building permit application, the owner is given the choice between paying the fees in lieu of the vehicle parking spaces that must be provided on the property in accordance with the permit plans and pursuant to the laws and regulations in force, or maintaining the vehicle parking spaces in kind.

The renewal of a building permit shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and to the building regulations and easements in force on the date of granting the renewal of the permit, with the exception of the right that the permit holder has acquired by virtue of executing the load-bearing parts of the permitted building: (foundations, load-bearing walls, columns, beams and ceilings).

The permit shall not be granted except after the approval of the competent technical administration and the payment of all fees due thereon.

Second: On time limits:

The approval of the competent technical administrations must be granted or refused with a statement of all the reasoned grounds for refusal, once only, within the time limits set out below, provided that they are calculated as from the date of registration of the application with these administrations:

1 - Within a time limit of two months at most if the property that is the subject of the permit application is situated on an executed road or along the sides of an approved alignment.

- Within a time limit of six months at most if the property is affected by or adjacent to a draft alignment or a modification of an alignment or a general master plan referred for approval, or if the application requires seeking the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning or other concerned public administrations (the Directorate General of Antiquities or the Directorate General of Civil Aviation or others...).

2 - The other competent departments (Civil Defence - Electricité du Liban - classified establishments... etc.) must each grant approval or refusal with a statement of all the reasoned grounds, once only, within fifteen days from the date of their receipt of the referral to that effect, failing which the application shall be deemed tacitly approved by the aforementioned departments.

3 - The competent technical departments must, under pain of liability, take their decision whether by approval or refusal and notify it within the aforementioned time limits to the concerned party, and if they do not take any decision, the latter may submit to the competent authority for granting the permit, directly or through a notary public, within a time limit of six months from the date of expiry of the time limits specified in Item Second, Paragraph /1/ of this Article, a letter in which he deems himself tacitly permitted to build, accompanied by the amount of the fees due, provided that he undertakes to comply with the contents of the permit file and with the laws and regulations in force.

4 - The competent authority must deliver to the concerned party, within a period of one month from the date of registration of the permit application, a certified true copy of the adopted assessed value of the land of the property in force on the date of the application. In the event that the competent authority abstains from delivering the assessed value to the concerned party, the latter may pay what he believes to be due by way of fees on his own responsibility, provided that the settlement of accounts takes place prior to obtaining the occupancy permit.

It shall appertain to the Higher Council for Urban Planning, within a period of one month at most, to decide on any technical dispute arising between the concerned parties and the administration and to give an opinion on the proper application of the provisions of this Law.

Third: Effects of the building permit:

It is not permissible to commence building works, demolition works, earthworks preparatory to building, or works exempted from a permit except after obtaining the permit or declaration in accordance with the legal rules and paying all the fees due. Provided that this is carried out, where applicable, under the supervision of an engineer and in accordance with the following conditions:

- The owner of the property who holds the permit and his contractors must not commence the execution of the contents of the permit before obtaining an order to commence execution signed by the responsible engineer and registered with the Order of Engineers.

- The permit holder and his contractors must not pour any slab or ceiling for any floor except after obtaining a pouring permit signed by the responsible engineer, and on his responsibility.

- The concerned Order of Engineers shall undertake coordination with the various competent authorities to ensure proper execution.

A building permit application may include restoration works, the construction of boundary walls and retaining walls, the final grading of the land of the property, and demolition at the same time; however, if the application is limited to works for grading the land of the property (excavation or backfilling), the declaration application must include plans of the natural ground signed by a surveying engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers and registered with one of the two Orders, or a licensed topographer and registered with the Syndicate of Licensed Topographers, together with photographs thereof prior to commencing the work, and the final plans required to be executed.

In the event that the total underground area subject to fees and for which a permit is requested exceeds a certain area, the owner may, under the supervision of a responsible engineer, commence excavation and shoring works pursuant to a special permit and to the submitted permit plans within conditions to be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after seeking the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

The permit shall be valid for a period of six years, renewable once only for a period of two years from the date of expiry of the validity of the original permit, exempted from fees if no increase has occurred in the permitted area or in the absence of a legal impediment, provided that the renewal application is submitted to the technical departments within a maximum period of six months from the date of expiry of the validity of the original permit, and provided that this time limit is calculated as part of the permit renewal period without the owner being able to complete the execution of the building during this period unless he obtains the renewal of the permit, and the competent technical administrations must decide on the renewal application within a time limit of one month from the date of submitting the renewal application.

In the event that the area of the property or group of contiguous properties that is the subject of the permit application exceeds 20000 m2, the permit may be divided into phases on the basis of the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning of the master plan of the project and the areas that are the subject of the permit.

The approval of the Urban Planning shall remain in force with respect to the design and the approved areas regardless of any amendments that may occur to the zoning regulations in force, for a period of twelve years (12 years), and subject to compliance with the following conditions:

- That the project be integrated.

- That the permit be subject to the provisions of Article Sixteen of this Law (Large Complexes).

- In the event that the property or group of properties that is the subject of the permit application is located within an unzoned area, and in order to benefit from the provisions mentioned above, the building conditions on the property shall be determined after the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, particularly the surface exploitation factor and the total exploitation factor, heights, envelopes, and regulatory and aesthetic conditions, without these conditions exceeding those in force pursuant to the provisions of Article Seventeen of this Law with respect to the total exploitation factor.

Any modification to the approved plan must be coupled with the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning without this entailing any extension of the time limit referred to above.

Constructions permitted to be erected within the legally mandated setback:

First - Within the setback from the boundaries or the alignment of roads and from public property:

It is prohibited to erect underground, ground-level, or upper constructions of any materials whatsoever, whether roofed or unroofed, or enclosed or unenclosed, and it is prohibited to place vehicles and trailers used for a purpose other than transport, with the exception of concierge rooms, the boundary wall, eaves, balconies, and retaining and supporting walls, the conditions of which shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Second - Within the setback from the boundaries of adjoining properties:

Subject to the regulations and easements imposed in the zones, it is permitted to erect underground floors the ceiling level (concrete) of which does not exceed a height of one metre above the level of the natural or levelled ground.

It is permitted to erect retaining walls for the natural ground whatever their height may reach, and supporting walls for legal backfill the height of which does not exceed two metres, and it is permitted to project certain constructions pertaining to protection, decoration, and beautification, the conditions of which shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Large Complexes:

Shall be considered large complexes, within the meaning of this Law, building projects in which the following conditions are met:

1 - That they be designed on a property the area of which is not less than ten times the minimum limit for subdivision in the zone, with a minimum of four thousand square metres /4000m2/ in the centres of Governorates and twenty thousand square metres /20000m2/ outside them.

2 - That a proportion of not less than twenty-five percent / 25%/ of the area of the property be allocated, equipped, and used as gardens or sports playgrounds, and a proportion of ten percent /10%/ of the area of the property shall be deducted when calculating the general exploitation factor when its area exceeds

ten thousand square metres /10000/m2.

3 - That they be subject to a volumetric plan submitted for the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, and to special conditions relating to setbacks, architectural perspectives, public health and safety, the submission of a natural and environmental impact study, and the provision of special installations (electricity, telephone, water..) commensurate with the importance of the project. All of them shall be determined by a decree issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

The construction of large complexes to which the conditions specified above apply may be exempted from the application of the envelope lines provided for in this Law and from the surface exploitation, the number of floors, and the height imposed in the regulations of the zone, if that results in distinctive architectural specifications for the project itself and for the zone in which the property is located.

Regulated Zones and Unregulated Zones:

Regulated zones for which easements for the surface and general exploitation ratio and factor and for the height or the number of floors are specified, shall be subject to their own special regulations, subject to the provisions of Article Thirteen of this Law. As for unregulated zones, pending their regulation, they shall be subject to building regulations in accordance with their nature (summer resort, inhabited, un-

inhabited agricultural, valleys...) to be determined by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

It is permitted to establish non-nuisance and non-harmful classified establishments of the second and third categories within unregulated zones after the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

Appearance and Structural Soundness of Buildings:

1 - Insurance to be applied progressively shall be imposed against the risk of collapse of the whole or part of a building or its manifest impending collapse, in respect of all buildings subject to compulsory technical inspection in accordance with the conditions for ensuring safety in buildings, provided that the insurance shall be valid for a period of ten years from the date on which the technical inspector draws up a final report certifying that the building or structure has been properly completed without fundamental reservations.

2 - The nature of the projects subject to compulsory technical inspection, their conditions, and the stages to be adopted to obtain insurance to guarantee the safety of the building shall be determined by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

3 - Building permit applications must be accompanied by a soil bearing capacity study issued by a specialized soil investigation office in accordance with the regulations of the Order of Engineers in this regard, as approved by the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

4 - The construction of bridge-shaped buildings over roads is prohibited unless the approved zoning regulations so provide, or in exceptional cases justified by architectural and aesthetic perspectives, provided that the exception is granted by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

5 - The shape and colours of facades and boundary walls must be in harmony with the surroundings, and the competent technical authorities shall have the right to assess this when granting the permit.

6 - Owners may be required to enclose their properties with boundary walls along the road, and if they refuse, the municipality shall have the right, after serving notice upon them, to erect the said boundary wall at their expense.

7 - Owners must maintain the cleanliness of the facades of their buildings and their other parts and must, where necessary, paint, plaster, whitewash, or restore them, and if they refuse, the municipality shall have the right, after serving notice upon them, to carry out the said work at their expense.

8 - The owner must constantly watch over the maintenance of his built properties and ensure the necessary stability and structural soundness thereof in order to preserve the safety of occupants and the neighbourhood. Whenever the need arises, or at the request of the municipality based on the consultation of the competent technical authorities, he must commission one or more engineers to inspect the building, verify it by appropriate technical means, and submit a detailed report on the condition of the building.

If it appears to the engineer that the building or parts thereof show signs of weakness, he must state in his report the cause of this weakness and its probable consequences and propose the works to be carried out, indicating their degree of urgency. If it is established as a result of the engineer's report that the stability or structural soundness of the building is impaired, the owner must carry out, under the supervision of an engineer through an assignment registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers, the necessary temporary construction and shoring works, and inform the municipality, or the Governor (Mohafez) or District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) outside the municipal area, of what he has done. Thereafter, he must take the necessary measures, after agreement with the occupants of the building or by applying to the Summary Proceedings Court, if necessary, to carry out the final strengthening works after obtaining a permit in due form. Upon completion of the work, the engineer shall draw up a report on the works he has carried out, indicating therein the new condition of the building.

9 - When a risk of collapse appears in the building, the owner shall be obliged to carry out the necessary shoring without delay at his own expense and responsibility and to immediately inform the municipality, or the Governorate or the District Commissioner where there is no municipality, thereof, which in turn shall inform the competent technical authorities of the matter.

10 - When a building, walls, or otherwise threatens to collapse and its continued existence constitutes a danger, and the owner does not take the initiative to perform his duties either because he is unable to carry out the necessary strengthening works or because he refuses to do so, it must be demolished within a period of not less than fifteen days and not more than two months, and the concerned municipality may evacuate the building of its occupants.

If it is impossible to notify the owner, or if he refuses to receive the demolition notice, a record of the facts must be drawn up by the municipal employees, or the Mayor (Mukhtar) where there is no municipality. In this case, a copy of the demolition notice shall be posted on the building required to be demolished and another copy on the door of the municipal headquarters, or on the door of the headquarters of the Governorate or the District Administration (Qaimaqamiya) outside the municipal area.

The period for demolition shall run from the date of notification or posting of the demolition notice. If the period expires and the owner has not executed the orders of the administration, the municipality shall proceed to carry out the demolition at his expense, and the municipality may sell the rubble resulting from the demolition to recover the expenses. In the event of extreme necessity to demolish a building pursuant to a report of the technical departments, which must be based on the report of a sworn expert engineer, the notice period may be reduced to one day, in which case the provisions of this paragraph must be mentioned in the demolition notice.

11 - Special conditions regarding the shape of the building, its external appearance, and the materials used may be imposed in respect of building and restoration permits in certain areas by a decree passed upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport and after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

12 - The creation of covered passages and arcades within buildings for public use may be imposed, the conditions and specifications of which shall be determined by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

On the clear height under the ceiling:

The minimum and maximum clear height under the ceiling for the various types of rooms and buildings, according to their intended use, shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

It shall not be permissible to alter the intended use of the garage specified upon licensing for any reason whatsoever.

However, in the event of altering the intended use of the building, wholly or partially, to another intended use permitted in the zone, and if the new intended use requires a garage larger than the area allocated as a garage for the original intended use, the owner shall be required either to provide the additional garage or to pay the fee in lieu for the part for which a garage is not provided, in an amount equal to the actual costs of its construction, provided that it is calculated in accordance with Article Nineteen above, and that the alteration of the intended use of the building and everything resulting therefrom shall be deemed null and void in the event of failure to provide the required additional garage or to pay the fee in lieu.

If building violations occur that necessitate removal during the period between the date of licensing and the date of obtaining the occupancy (habitation) permit, the responsible engineer shall withdraw his undertaking immediately upon the occurrence of the violation and notify the owners of the property or their legal representatives and the Order of Engineers thereof, provided that he serves notice upon the owner to demolish the violation in the event of refusal.

The President of the Order of Engineers shall notify the competent technical administration and the municipalities concerned of the matter by registered letters with acknowledgment of receipt:

1 - If the responsible engineer who signed the permit fails to withdraw his undertaking and notify the Order of Engineers concerned, the Directorate of Urban

Planning, the Governor of the region, or the head of the executive authority in the municipality concerned shall report the first violation within a period of one month from the date of the violation, or the President of the Order of Engineers concerned, to whom it falls, as a minimum, to address a warning to the engineer and/or take disciplinary measures and penalties in accordance with the provisions of the Practice of the Profession Law No. 636/97.

2 - In the event of repetition and after the President of the Order has been notified as stated in the preceding paragraph (1), it shall fall to the President of the Order to order the suspension of all technical transactions pertaining to the engineer at the Order for a period ranging between three months and six months according to the gravity of the violation and/or to take disciplinary measures and penalties in accordance with the provisions of the Practice of the Profession Law No. 636/97, within one month from the date the President of the Order is notified of the repetition of the violation.

3 - In the event of repetition for the third time, the engineer shall be excluded, by a decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport upon the request of the Director General of Urban Planning, the Governor of the region, or the head of the executive authority in the municipality concerned, from all contracts concluded by public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities, in addition to the administrative measures that may be taken against him before State departments and which may be included in this decision, within a period of one month from the receipt of the request by the Minister of Public Works and Transport. In this case, it shall fall to the Disciplinary Council at the Order of Engineers concerned to order the taking of maximum measures where necessary, within a maximum period of three months from the date of its notification of the violation by the Director General of Urban Planning, the Governor of the region, or the mayor of the municipality concerned, accompanied by a report from the head of the administration that grants the technical approval for the permit.

The execution contractor (builder) shall be subject to the confiscation of equipment and to the penalties to which the violating owner is subject, and shall also be excluded temporarily or permanently

from all contracts concluded by public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport upon the request of the Director General of Urban Planning, the Governor of the region, or the mayor of the municipality concerned.

The investigation carried out on the permit application and on the building designs, as well as the supervision carried out by the administration during the execution of the permit, shall not bind the latter where liability exists.

Any excavation of foundations, construction, restoration, or alteration commenced without a permit or declaration, depending on whether the work is subject to a permit or

to a declaration, or carried out in violation of the permit or the declaration receipt, shall be compulsorily stopped, and an infringement report shall be drawn up against the owner and the person responsible for execution for the violation, and the person concerned shall apply without delay for a permit or make a declaration, as the case may be.

If it appears that the constructions do not conflict with the alignment plan or with the legal conditions, the permit or the declaration receipt shall be granted with the imposition of a fine equivalent to double the value of all fees due for the part that has been completed. Every building whose ceiling has been cast shall be deemed completed.

The fine and fees shall be deemed a privileged debt on the property, and no municipal clearance certificate shall be granted until after they have been collected and the status of the violation has been regularized.

The owner of constructions that conflict with the alignment plan or that violate the building laws and regulations in force must demolish them, and if he fails to do so, the administration shall undertake the demolition at his expense and responsibility and the costs shall be recovered from him in the manner of collecting State and municipal fees. The building violation infringement report must specify the location of the violation, its nature, and the date of its occurrence accurately, and the stage reached by the violator on the date the infringement report was drawn up.

The violation shall be registered, upon the request of the municipality or the competent technical administration, on the real property folio of the property and shall not be struck off until after its status has been regularized or it has been removed.

The responsible person who violates the provisions of this Law and the texts adopted for its implementation shall be punished by a fine from /2000000/ (two million Lebanese Pounds) to /100000000/ (one hundred million Lebanese Pounds).

The violator who continues the work after it has been stopped shall be punished by a fine from /4000000/ (four million Lebanese Pounds) to /200000000/ (two hundred million Lebanese Pounds) and by imprisonment from one week to 15 days, or by either of these two penalties, provided that this shall not preclude the removal of the violation where necessary.

Subject to the provisions of Article Eleven of this Law regarding the extension of the line of sight, the provisions of the Building Law shall apply within the boundaries of each property individually or a group of contiguous properties not legally amenable to amalgamation, provided that an annotation has been entered on the real property folio of each of the properties of which it is composed, stating that they constitute an indivisible real property unit. However, if the contiguous properties are legally amenable to amalgamation, they must be amalgamated to become a single property.

The Building Law promulgated by Legislative Decree No. 148 dated 16/9/1983 and Legislative Decree No. 45 dated 23/3/1985 are hereby repealed, and all general and special texts that conflict with the provisions of this Law are likewise repealed.

The implementing decrees and decisions annexed to the Building Law No. 148/83 dated 16/9/83, repealed pursuant to this Article, shall remain in force until the issuance of the implementing decrees and decisions annexed to this Law, in all matters not conflicting with the content of this Law.

The holder of a permit granted prior to the issuance of this Law shall have the option between executing it or amending it in accordance with the provisions of this Law or the laws in force on the date of obtaining the permit.

Within six months from the effective date of this Law, and with the exception of what isstipulated to be issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, all implementing texts, including detailed drawings, shall be issued pursuant to decrees adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

An implementing decree for this Law
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
