A draft law aiming to amend certain provisions of the law establishing the Ministry of Social Affairs. - The proposed law aiming at appointment to the permanent cadre of all public institutions, councils, bodies, funds and all persons of public law pursuant to a competitive examination conducted by the Civil Service Board. - A proposed law aiming to pay the entitlements specified in Law No. 717 dated 5/11/1998 - A proposed law aiming to amend Article One of Law No. 344 dated 6/8/2001 relating to granting equity to holders of the teaching licence (Ijaza) and competency certificate (Kafa'a) who entered the cadre of public primary and intermediate education. - The draft law on the Mediator of the Republic (Ombudsman). - A draft law aiming to grant the Minister of Interior and Municipalities the competence to appoint committees and determine their allowances. - A proposed law aiming to amend the third paragraph of Article 98 of the Civil Servants Regulations. - A proposed law aiming to amend the third Article of Law No. 525 dated 6/6/1996 providing for the amendment of the cadre of the Ministry of Public Health. - A proposed law containing special provisions for workers in the State Employees' Cooperative. - The proposed law aiming to lay down special provisions for the missing civil servant. - A draft law aiming to amend Article /50/ of the Civil Servants Regulations. - A proposed law aiming to amend certain provisions of Legislative Decree No. 82/83 dated 16/9/1983 (Organisation of the Court of Accounts). - A proposed law aiming to amend Law No. 441 dated 29/7/2002 with respect to the provisions relating to the appointment of successful candidates in the restricted competitive examination conducted pursuant to the provisions of the aforementioned law. - The proposed law aiming to amend Article 87 of the Civil Servants Regulations with respect to subjecting contracting in public administrations to a competitive examination conducted by the Civil Service Board in accordance with the rules. - The Public Food draft law. - A draft law aiming to amend the organisation of the Ministry of Economy and Trade. - A proposed law aiming to exempt successful candidates in the competitive examination held in the year 1987 for the admission of students to the Faculty of Pedagogy to prepare for the competency certificate (Kafa'a) from the two conditions of age and competitive examination. - A draft law aiming to amend the Law issued on 23/7/1962 relating to the establishment of the Lebanese Standards Institution. - A draft law aiming to amend Law No. 642 dated 2/6/1997 (Establishment of the Ministry of Industry). - 1 - Serious accident: In the case concerning the request to render an opinion on the concept of a serious accident provided for in paragraph 3 of Article 52 of the Civil Servants Regulations concerning the conditions for placement on leave without pay (disponibilité), the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3531 dated 27/12/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as follows: Whereas paragraph 3 of Article 52 of the Civil Servants Regulations and the amendments thereto provides as follows: "A civil servant may be placed [on leave without pay] in the event of a serious accident, or in the event of the illness of his spouse or one of his descendants, or for the purpose of undertaking studies from which the Administration seeks a public benefit, provided that the duration of the leave without pay does not exceed one year renewable twice". And whereas it appears that paragraph 3 of Article 52 mentioned above has provided for three cases in which a civil servant may be placed on leave without pay at his request, among which is the case of his suffering a serious accident. And whereas the interpretation of the concept of a serious accident must be made within the limits of the purpose intended by the legislator through permitting the civil servant to request his placement on leave without pay, which lies in allowing him to be absent from work for a maximum period of one year renewable twice in cases not governed by the provisions that permit granting the civil servant sick leaves, such as his exposure to an accident or a sudden affliction that causes him harm without this situation allowing him to benefit from sick leave or from placement ex officio on leave without pay due to the non-fulfilment of the conditions provided for in this regard in Article 39 of the Civil Servants Regulations. And whereas what reinforces this interpretation is that absence for health reasons requires that the civil servant meet the reasons and conditions provided for in the aforementioned Article 39, including the requirement that this absence be justified by medical reports proving that the concerned civil servant suffers from a health condition that requires rest and prevents him from going to his workplace and performing the duties of his post. And whereas there are certain health conditions that do not prevent the civil servant from performing the duties of his post and therefore cannot be accompanied by medical reports, which does not allow the civil servant to benefit from sick leave pursuant to Article 39 mentioned above, and consequently renders it impossible for the civil servant to benefit from the provisions of placement on leave without pay ex officio provided for in Article 39, considering that this must be preceded by a number of measures such as exhausting the balance of his health leaves on full salary and his benefiting from a health leave on half salary for a period of one year. And whereas we see fit to review some examples of the cases referred to above, such as a civil servant suffering an accident that creates a visible disfigurement in his body without causing a disability in his physical faculties that impedes his movement and the pursuit of his daily activity, yet this disfigurement affects the injured person who is keen not to appear in his social environment throughout the period required to undergo one or several surgical operations which may take some time, or the civil servant may suffer a health affliction resulting in a partial disability in his hand or leg without diminishing his ability to practice his work, yet the treatment of this disability requires undergoing daily sessions or travelling abroad, which compels the injured civil servant to cease work in order to pursue treatment. And whereas the contention that a serious accident is not restricted to the physical and material element but extends to the moral element, such as the person concerned being exposed to a death threat that forces him to leave the country to move away from and avert danger or to forced residence outside the country, cannot be relied upon in the presence of the security institutions and agencies whose task is to maintain order and security across all Lebanese territory in a manner that guarantees the safety of all citizens, especially since any threat to a citizen's life is considered one of the crimes punishable by law and exposes its perpetrators to the imposition of the appropriate penalties against them. Therefore, the Civil Service Board considered that the expression "serious accident" contained in paragraph 3 of Article 52 mentioned above is restricted to the cases not covered by the provisions set forth in Article 39 of the Civil Servants Regulations, and it is an accident whose material consequences exceed the limits of normal and customary burdens that can be borne, and leads to an acute deficiency in physical, mental or physiological capacities, and it remains incumbent upon the concerned Administration to ascertain the extent of the damage that has befallen the civil servant once its causes are established. As for the legal status entailed for the civil servant placed on leave without pay at his request due to his suffering a serious accident, pursuant to the provisions of paragraph /1/ of the aforementioned Article /52/, his salary is suspended and he loses his right to step advancement and pension computation throughout the period he spends on leave without pay.

2 - Tourist hostess - renewal of a tourist guide licence: In the case concerning the request of tourist hostesses on the establishment of the Ministry of Tourism to renew a tourist guide licence for each of them, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3386 dated 18/11/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Tourism as follows: It appeared from the documents of the transaction that each of the concerned parties held a tourist guide licence and practiced the profession of tourist guide prior to her appointment to the post of tourist host pursuant to Decree No. 7619 dated 14/3/2002. It appeared that item No. (4) of Decree No. 11576 issued on 27/12/1997 (amending Annex No. - 7 - of Decree No. 15598 dated 21/9/1970 concerning the determination of the general conditions for the establishment and operation of tourist establishments) provides as follows: "The Ministry of Tourism grants the licence to practice the profession of accompanying or local tourist guide in accordance with the rules and conditions specified for this profession, and this licence is considered personal and may not be assigned at all". Item No. (5) of the aforementioned Decree also provided as follows: "The licence is renewed at the end of each year subject to compliance with the provisions of item No. (17) of these Regulations". And it appeared that item No. (17) mentioned above provides in paragraph (1) thereof that after the lapse of four years from his licensing, the licensed guide shall be subject to follow-up training courses conducted by the Institute of Guides affiliated with the Ministry of Tourism for his rehabilitation. Based on the foregoing, we consider the following: Whereas Decree No. 13179 dated 8/10/1998 and the amendments thereto (amending the conditions of appointment to the establishment of the Directorate General of Tourist Affairs in the Ministry of Tourism) requires a candidate for the post of tourist host to hold the Technical Superior Certificate (TS) in Tourist Sciences or a tourist guide licence issued by the Ministry of Tourism. And whereas holding a "tourist guide licence" is one of the conditions required for appointment to the post of tourist host and was met by each of the concerned parties upon submitting her application to participate in the competitive examination conducted by the Civil Service Board for appointment to the aforementioned post, consequently, the assumption by the concerned parties of their post does not prevent each of them from proceeding to renew this licence annually throughout the duration of her service in the post of tourist host, provided that she does not practice the profession of tourist guide outside the scope of her post so that this does not conflict with the provisions of item (4) of Article 15 of the Civil Servants Regulations.

2 - Tourist Hostess - Renewal of a Tourist Guide Licence: In the case concerning the application of tourist hostesses on the establishment of the Ministry of Tourism for the renewal of a tourist guide licence for each of them, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 3386 dated 18/11/ 2004 addressed to the Ministry of Tourism as follows: It appeared from the documents of the transaction that each of the concerned parties held a tourist guide licence and practised the profession of tourist guide prior to her appointment to the post of tourist host pursuant to Decree No. 7619 dated 14/3/2002. It appeared that Item No. (4) of Decree No. 11576 issued on 27/12/1997 (amending Annex No. - 7 - of Decree No. 15598 dated 21/9/1970 concerning the determination of the general conditions for establishing and operating tourist establishments) provides as follows: "The Ministry of Tourism shall grant a licence to practise the profession of accompanying or local tourist guide in accordance with the rules and conditions specified for this profession, and this licence shall be deemed personal and may not be assigned at all". Item No. (5) of the aforementioned Decree also provided as follows: "The licence shall be renewed at the end of each year, subject to compliance with the provisions of Item No. (17) of these Regulations". And it appeared that Item No. (17) mentioned above provides in Paragraph (1) thereof that after the lapse of four years from his licence, the licensed guide shall be subject to follow-up training courses conducted by the Institute of Guides affiliated with the Ministry of Tourism in order to rehabilitate him. Based on the foregoing, we are of the opinion as follows: Whereas Decree No. 13179 dated 8/10/1998 and its amendments (amending the conditions of appointment to the establishment of the Directorate General of Tourist Affairs in the Ministry of Tourism) requires a candidate for the post of tourist host to hold the Technical Excellence Certificate (TS) in Tourist Sciences or a tourist guide licence issued by the Ministry of Tourism. And whereas holding a "tourist guide licence" is one of the required conditions for appointment to the post of tourist host and was fulfilled by each of the concerned parties when she submitted the application to participate in the competitive examination conducted by the Civil Service Board for appointment to the aforementioned post, consequently, the assumption by the concerned parties of their post does not prevent each of them from working on renewing this licence annually throughout the duration of her service in the post of tourist host, provided that she does not practise the profession of tourist guide outside the scope of her post so that this does not conflict with the provisions of Item (4) of Article 15 of the Civil Servants Regulations.

4 - Criminal Judgments - Loss of Conditions of Employment - Liquidation of End-of-Service Indemnity: In the case concerning the status of civil servants sentenced to criminal judgments and the manner of liquidating their end-of-service rights, particularly as regards the right of the concerned parties to salary starting from the date of their resumption of work after the execution of the judgments rendered against them and until the cessation of the liquidation and disbursement of these salaries, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 204 dated 19/2/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Finance as follows: Whereas it is required of every applicant for a public office, in accordance with the text of Paragraph (e) of Item (1) of Article (4) of the Civil Servants Regulations and its amendments, that he enjoy his civil rights and not be sentenced for a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or for a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour. And whereas the condition mentioned above must be fulfilled by the civil servant throughout the duration of his performance of the duties of the public office, and his loss of this condition during office is deemed an impediment to continuing therein and withholds from him the right to remain in service. And whereas the Civil Service Board has found that certain teachers against whom judgments were rendered by the Military Court convicting them pursuant to certain articles of the Penal Code have lost one of the conditions that entitle them to continue working, and that action must be taken to issue the necessary text to terminate their services. And whereas the concerned parties - in view of the issuance of judgments convicting them of criminal acts provided for in Paragraph (e) of Item (1) of Article (4) referred to above, which are a bar to appointment and to remaining in service - have lost their functional eligibility, and there is no longer any legal justification for their remaining in service, considering that each of them has become, on the date of issuance of the judgment against him, outside the office by operation of law, and no authority has the competence to permit keeping a civil servant in service after his loss of one of the general conditions of employment, as this pertains to public policy. And whereas it appeared from the letter of the Ministry of Finance that some of the concerned parties resumed their work in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education after the execution of the judgment rendered against them and continued to receive their salaries until the Directorate of Expenditures requested the Accounting Department in the aforementioned Ministry to cease the liquidation of these salaries or until the date of issuance of the decree terminating his service, without legal justification, considering that each of them lost the capacity of civil servant starting from the date of issuance of the judgment against him. And whereas the period subsequent to the date of issuance of the judgments against the concerned teachers, during which some of them attended their workplaces, even though it was not based on a legal status, it is nevertheless improper to deprive them of their remuneration therefor due to the inadmissibility of unjust enrichment of the Administration at the expense of the concerned parties. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board found that the end-of-service rights of each of the concerned parties must be liquidated starting from the date

of his entry into service and until the date of the judgment rendered against him, provided that whatever he may have received during the period subsequent to the date of the aforementioned judgment shall be deemed as remuneration for services he performed for the benefit of the Administration and consequently shall not be included in the calculation of his actual services in the permanent establishments.

5 - Payment of travel expenses - Mother of an ambassador: In the case relating to the extent to which the claim of the Ambassador Mr. (- -) for the payment of the travel expenses of his mother who accompanied him on his travel returning from Sofia to Beirut may be granted, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 3367 dated 4/11/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants as follows: Whereas Article (35) of Decree No. 1306 dated 18/6 /1971 (Regulations of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and the Determination of its Numerical Cadres) provides as follows: "The Government shall cover the expenses of round-trip travel to Lebanon for employees on leave and for the members of their families. a - Once every two years for anyone entitled to two months' leave annually. b - Once every three years for anyone entitled to one month's leave annually. The family shall include the wife and those whose maintenance is at the expense of the employee from among the sons who have not exceeded the eighteenth year of their age or who are pursuing their studies at educational institutes up to the twenty-fifth year of their age, and from among the unmarried daughters, ascendants and sisters who are unable to support themselves.". Whereas it appears from the contents of the file of the transaction that the mother of the Ambassador (- -) resides with him - in the same house and is dependent upon him - in accordance with the certificate dated 7/7/1999 issued by the Mukhtar of Zahle - Mar Elias, as well as in accordance with the statement signed by the person concerned on 31/8/2004 wherein it appears that he is her sole breadwinner. Whereas it appears from the certificate dated 16/10/2004 issued by the Health and Social Affairs Department at the State Employees' Cooperative that "the mother of Mr. (- -), affiliation number (- -), is under his dependency at the State Employees' Cooperative, pursuant to dependency application number (- -), which signifies that she is unable to support herself in accordance with the conditions relating to dependents provided for in Paragraph (b) - Item 2 of Article (4) of the Hospitalization Regulations of the Cooperative. And whereas the inability of the mother of the Ambassador (- -) to support herself places her in the position of a beneficiary of the provisions of Article (35) of Decree No. 1306 dated 186/1971 mentioned above. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that the claim of the Ambassador Mr. (- -) for the payment of the travel expenses of his mother is legally sound, provided that this is within the limits provided for in Items (a) and (b) of Article (35) of Decree No. 1306/1971 referred to above.

6 - Salary deduction - Repeal of a penalty - Lapse of ten years - Withdrawal: In the case relating to the permissibility of repealing a penalty after the lapse of ten years from its imposition, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 126 dated 22/4/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Telecommunications as follows: It appeared that on 18/5/1994 the former Minister of Telecommunications issued Decision No. 1564/1/W relating to the deduction of the salary of certain employees for a period of fifteen days for their breach of the duties of office. It appeared that the First Investigating Judge in North Lebanon, by his Decision No. 138/96 dated 25/11/1996, barred the trial of the persons concerned for lack of evidence. It appeared that after the lapse of more than ten years from the date of imposition of the penalty mentioned above, the former Minister of Telecommunications issued anew Decision No. 1169/A dated 30/8/2000, which ordered the repeal of the penalty against the persons concerned in light of the issuance of the decision of the First Investigating Judge mentioned above. Accordingly, whereas administrative doctrine and case law are settled that where individual administrative decisions creating a right are lawful or not contrary to the law, they may not be revoked after their signature unless there is an explicit legislative text to the contrary (1). This category of decisions cannot be the subject of withdrawal by the competent administrative authority, neither ex officio nor pursuant to a non-contentious administrative petition (Recours Gracieux) (2). Case law considers that the revocation of an individual administrative act creating a right constitutes an abuse of power and consequently leads to the annulment of the decision of revocation or withdrawal, and the rules that govern the revocation of these decisions apply also to their amendment, in accordance with what case law has held(3). And State Council of Lebanon, 17 April, Fakih, A.R., 1974, p. 187. And whereas a disciplinary administrative penalty may create a right: - towards the employee concerned thereby, on the one hand, in that the administrative authority cannot revoke such a penalty, whether lawful or unlawful and final, in order to replace it with a more severe penalty(4). - towards third parties, on the other hand, in that the competent administrative authority cannot exercise its right to withdraw the penalty decision on the ground of inexpediency if that would result (for example) in dismissing another employee from the post to which he was appointed, considering that this measure infringes upon his acquired rights(5). "la dite autorite ne peut user de cette faculte (retrait de sanction inopportune) dans le cas ou le retrait aurait pour effet d'entrainer l'exclusion d'un autre fonctionnaire de l'emploi auquel celui-ci avait ete nomme et de porter ainsi atteinte a ses droits acquis"

And whereas repeal is decided in principle for acts that are continuous in time, such that their legal effects are subsisting on the date of repeal, particularly with respect to regulatory decisions or individual decisions creating a right, which does not apply to decisions relating to penalties, as they commence and produce their legal effects simultaneously, and do not have continuous effects, and consequently repeal in those cases is without object. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that it is not permissible to repeal the penalty under consideration for the reasons set forth above. (1) State Council of Lebanon, 7 November 1966, Jean Farah and his colleagues, Decision No. 1676. And State Council of Lebanon, 22 March 1979, Wassef Nassar, S.C.D., Vol. 2, p. 658. (2) Council of State of France, 23 July 1984 Min. de l'interieur/Gray, Collection, p. 442. (3) For example: Council of State of France, 21 Nov. 1947, Delle Ingrand, Collection, p. 430, etc.,... (4) Council of State of France, 4 May 1949, "Demangeot", Collection, p. 550. (5) Council of State of France, 4 May 1919, "Mounier", Collection, p. 196. (See to this effect: General Administrative Judiciary - Part One - Youssef Saadallah El-Khoury - Pages 425 - 426).

7 - Abolition of a Post - Operation of the Public Utility - Promotion: In the case concerning the promotion of an employee to a post that no longer exists by operation of law, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1525 dated 7/8/2004 addressed to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers with the following: Whereas Article (17) of Law No. 481 dated 12/12/2002 (Management of the Civil Aviation Sector) stipulated the repeal of the final paragraph of Item (1) of the Fourth Article of Law No. 247 dated 7/8/2000 relating to the merger, abolition, and establishment of ministries and councils, and its replacement with the following text: "The Directorate General of Civil Aviation shall be abolished, and a Government Commissariat to the General Authority of Civil Aviation shall be established within the Ministry of Public Works and Transport..."). And whereas Paragraph (2) of the aforementioned Article (17) stipulated that the phrase "Directorate General of Civil Aviation" wherever it occurs shall be replaced by the phrase "General Authority of Civil Aviation". And whereas the regulatory decrees defining the cadres of the Government Commissariat to the Authority and relating to the manner of attaching employees and workers of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation and the Civil Aviation Safety Centre who meet the statutory requirements and transferring them to the new cadres of the Government Commissariat, have been issued and published on 24/6/2004 in Issue 34 of the Official Gazette. And whereas the post to which the appointment is proposed is a technical post provided for solely in the cadre of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (abolished) and consequently no longer exists by operation of law, from which it is inferred that the proposed appointment is contrary to the general principles of appointment and to the Personnel Regulations, in particular Article 13 thereof, given that the appointment must be made to a post provided for in the cadre and for which a specific appropriation is allocated in the budget. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that it is not possible to approve the proposed promotion, given that the posts of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation into the cadre of which the promotion is proposed no longer exist by operation of law, and that the duties carried out by the said Directorate General fall under the operation of the public utility.

8 - Acting Capacity: In the case concerning the request for an opinion on who shall perform in an acting capacity the duties of a post from which the titular employee is absent, in light of the provisions of Article /34/ of Decree No. 2894 dated 16/12/1959, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1000 dated 3/6/2004 addressed to the Central Administration of Statistics with the following: Whereas Article /34/ of Decree No. 2894 dated 16/12/1959 (defining the conditions for applying certain provisions of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12/6/1959 relating to the organisation of public administrations and the conditions of linkage among their various bodies) stipulated that "In the event of the absence of the Director or the Head of Unit, his subordinate who is highest in rank shall deputise for him in all matters of his duties that do not have a decision-making character or a personal character vested in him by law, following the approval of the immediate superior of the absent employee". And whereas Article /3/ of the Personnel Regulations stipulated in its first paragraph the following: "1 - Permanent posts are divided into categories, categories into ranks, and ranks into grades", and it is consequently required to distinguish between the rank of the employee and his grade defined in the salary scale of his post. And whereas Article /34/ referred to above clearly mentioned the subordinate highest in rank to deputise for the absent employee, following the approval of the immediate superior of the absent employee. And whereas the said Article, by stipulating "highest in rank", has adopted the rank as the criterion for acting capacity and not the grade. And whereas it appears that Mr. (-- --) is from the third administrative category, which does not include ranks, and it is consequently required to consider him as being of the same rank. And whereas it appears that the aforementioned legal provisions have granted the immediate superior of the employee absent from his post the authority to approve the designation of the employee who performs the duties of the said post in an acting capacity, which obliges this superior, while observing the conditions provided for in these provisions and when exercising his powers of selection, to take into consideration the proper functioning of the work in the utility that he manages and supervises. And whereas it falls to the Director General, who in the present case is the immediate superior concerned by Article /34/ mentioned above, to assess and accept the reasons put forward by Mr. (-- --) for excusing himself from performing the duties of the head of the Bureau Service in an acting capacity, given that an employee must comply with the instructions given to him by his immediate superiors, just as it falls to him, in the event that he accepts these reasons, and in light of ensuring the continuity of work in the Bureau Service at the Central Administration of Statistics - in the present case - to choose from among the previously mentioned employees (the Head of the Administrative Department or the Head of the Accounting Department) to perform the acting duties, the employee whom he deems more qualified in terms of competence to manage the said Service in accordance with the provisions of the aforementioned Article /34/, given that this assignment is temporary pending the appointment of a titular employee for the Service concerned; furthermore, it is permissible, and this falls to the said immediate superior, to include the factor of seniority in the category among the factors adopted for testing, and in the event of equality in this seniority, to adopt the seniority in the cadre defined by the grade in the salary scale of the post and the due date of the next step advancement for each of those concerned, in the event of equality in the qualification of both the Head of the Administrative Department and the Head of the Accounting Department in assuming the duties under consideration.

9 - Administrative Leave - Cash Compensation - Death - Right of the Heirs: In the case concerning the request for an opinion regarding the granting of cash compensation for administrative leave to the heirs of the late Ambassador (-- --), who passed away on 17/5/2004 while present in Lebanon on administrative leave after having benefited from sick leave based on medical reports certified by the Official Medical Committee, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1914 dated 15/7/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants with the following: Whereas Article (35) of the Personnel Regulations granted the employee the right to benefit from annual leave on full salary for a period of twenty days, with the possibility of accumulating it for a maximum period of three years. And whereas the opinion of this Board is settled on the right of the employee to benefit from financial compensation equivalent to his salary for the period of administrative leave of which he was deprived, if the reason for his deprivation is attributable to the administration, such as where the employee requests to be granted the leave due to him and the administration refuses his request, which obliges the administration, such being the case, to pay cash compensation for the damage incurred by the employee as a result of depriving him of the administrative leave due to him. And whereas it did not appear from the facts of the case at hand that Ambassador (-- --) had requested to be granted administrative leave for the days due to him and that the administration had refused to grant the person concerned the requested leave. And whereas administrative leave is one of the rights exclusively attached to the person of the employee, and he cannot delegate this right or assign it to another, as the enjoyment thereof belongs exclusively to him, and consequently this right lapses upon the occurrence of an event such as death; accordingly, the claim of the heirs in this case for financial compensation is neither consistent nor in harmony with the spirit of the legal text except upon the occurrence of damage caused by the administration by its refusal to grant the employee concerned his administrative leaves, which is not met in the present case. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board decided not to approve granting the heirs of the deceased employee, the late Ambassador (-- --), financial compensation for the remaining period of his administrative leave.

10 - Calculation of Administrative Leaves - Night Shift: In the matter relating to the extent of the possibility of determining the duration of calculation of the administrative leave for shift employees in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation by the number of actual hours required, estimated at six hours of actual work, the Civil Service Board responded by its Letter No. 1394 dated 24/6/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Public Works for Civil Aviation requesting approval to enable it to grant administrative leave for a period of one day and calculate it by the number of actual hours required from employees working under the shift system, provided that the concept of administrative leave when granted for consecutive days remains in conformity with the text of Article 35 of the Employees Regulations. Accordingly, whereas it appears that the Central Inspection had previously, by its Letter No. 1884/S2/2000 dated 18/5/2000, requested the Civil Service Board to express its opinion on several matters relating to certain functional statuses of employees in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, including: 1 - Is the concerned technical employee (i.e., subject to the shift system) who benefits from an administrative leave during the day entitled to return to night or overtime work on the same day? 2 - Can the administrative leave be divided into hours, so that the employee may return and benefit from the remaining hours of leave on another day? And whereas it appears that this Board, by its Letter No. 2337 dated 9/8/2000, expressed its opinion on the questions raised in the letter of the Central Inspection above, according to the following: - With regard to the first question: Whereas Clause (1) of Article /35/ of the Employees Regulations stipulates that the employee is entitled, after the expiration of one year from his appointment and in every subsequent year spent in actual service, to benefit from an annual leave with full salary for a period of twenty days. And whereas a day is (24) full hours, which means the employee benefits for a single day by virtue of his administrative leave from a period extending up to 24 hours preceding the time of commencement of his working hours on the following day, i.e., from twenty hundred hours in the evening until twenty hundred hours in the evening of the following day, as a day of leave. And whereas, by way of digression, it is inferred from the phrase ".... in a manner that guarantees the continuity of work therein..." (i.e., in his administration) contained in Paragraph (3) of Article (35) mentioned above, that the holder of this leave is not able to return to work outside official working hours, because the timing of granting the administrative leave is supposed to have taken place in a manner that guarantees the continuity of work in the administration so that the need for the concerned employee to report to his workplace while benefiting from his leaves is negated (tantaqi). This Board concluded that the employee is not entitled, during his administrative leave, to return to work in order to benefit from night or overtime working hours, because by doing so he violates the content of the decision granting him the said leave and contradicts the purpose of granting it, and consequently the employee who performs night work or overtime work during his administrative leave is not entitled to any compensation for these works and they shall be considered as a donation on his part. - With regard to the second question: This Board deemed that, pursuant to the text of Article /35/ of the Employees Regulations, the administrative leave from which the employee benefits in a single year is fixed at twenty days and is granted for a single day (i.e., 24 hours) or for several days, such that the administration, when granting this leave to the employee during the period of the year, must time it by days, and it cannot be divided into designated hours in a single day because that violates the legal text set forth above, especially since the employee who benefits from the administrative leave retains his full salary during this leave.

11 - Administrative Leave - Financial Compensation: In the matter relating to the extent of the possibility of granting financial compensation in lieu of administrative leave on the grounds that the administration's refusal to grant the leave to the employee stems from the necessity of the continuity of the operation of the public utility and avoiding causing a disruption in the affairs of the registry and accounting, which would cause material and moral damages far exceeding the financial compensation decided to be granted in lieu of the administrative leave due to him for the year 2001, the Civil Service Board responded by its Letter No. 1019 dated 17/6/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Culture with the following: Whereas Article 35 of the Employees Regulations granted the employee the right to benefit from an annual administrative leave with full salary for a period of twenty days with the possibility of accumulating it for a maximum period of three years. And whereas Paragraph (4) of the aforementioned Article preserved the employee's right to the balance of his accumulated leaves, and stipulated that he must be allowed to benefit from them prior to his dismissal from service or his referral to retirement. And whereas the opinion of the Civil Service Board has settled in more than one letter issued by it on the right of the employee to benefit from financial compensation equivalent to his salary for the duration of the administrative leave of which he was deprived, if the reason for his deprivation is attributable to the administration, such as when the employee requests to be granted the leave due to him and the administration refuses his request. And whereas the Ministry of Culture refused to grant the administrative leave to the concerned party after he submitted a request to benefit from it, due to the need for his services in securing the continuity of the operation of the public utility represented by the regularity of work in the Directorate General of Antiquities. And whereas the Circular of His Excellency the President of the Council of Ministers No. 15/2002 dated 17/5/2002 stipulated the inadmissibility of granting cash allowances for administrative leaves that have not lapsed by prescription except in compelling cases in which the employee is deprived of benefiting from his administrative leave by the act of the administration, provided that these cases are determined exclusively and linked to the continuity of the operation of the public utility and securing the public interest and in accordance with criteria assessed solely by the supreme head in the administration. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board deemed that it rests with the supreme head of the administration, who is the Minister of Culture, to state the criteria and assess the facts on the basis of which the granting of administrative leave to the concerned employees is refused, provided that this is done in compelling cases linked to the operation of the public utility, with the necessity of adhering to the provisions of the Circular of His Excellency the President of the Council of Ministers No. 15/2002 referred to.

12 - Probationary Employee - Confirmation of Appointment - Administrative Leave: In the case concerning the extent of the possibility for probationary employees to benefit from the balance of their administrative leaves accrued to them during the first year of probation, the Civil Service Board replied in its Letter No. 2451 dated 16/9/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Finance as follows: Whereas Article (4) of Decree No. 2500 dated 18/12/1971 (Amendment of the Cadre of the Directorate General of Finance and Amendment of Certain Conditions of Appointment and Training of Tax Controllers and Collection and Levy Employees Therein) stipulated the following: "Successful candidates in the competitive examinations designated for the position of Tax Controller (Second Rank) Tax Controller (First Rank) - Collection Controller - Paymaster - Accountant - Chief Tax Controller - Assessment Controller - Head of Accounting shall be subject to the following provisions: - These employees shall be appointed as probationers for a period of at least one year and at most two years. - The Administration must organize for them during this period a compulsory training course specific to the position, concluding with a proficiency examination. The rules and conditions of the course shall be determined by the Ministry of Finance in agreement with the Civil Service Board. - Those who succeed in this course shall each be confirmed in the position to which they were appointed, and an unsuccessful candidate who is not an employee shall be deemed dismissed ipso jure from service from the date of announcement of the result and without the need to issue any other text. - As for an unsuccessful candidate who is an employee, he shall be returned to his original position if it is still vacant; if it is not vacant, he shall be assigned a position of an equivalent category or offered a position lower than it while retaining his original salary. If he refuses this latter position, he shall be dismissed from service." And whereas Items (1-2 and 4) of Article (10) of the Civil Servants' Regulations and the amendments thereto stipulated the following: "1 - Those appointed in each of the Fourth and Third Categories shall remain probationers for a period of one year in the grade to which they were appointed...". "2 - Each Ministry shall undertake the training of the probationers affiliated to it in accordance with the general principles determined by the Department of Preparation and Training in the Civil Service Board." "4 - The authority vested with the right to appoint them shall dismiss probationers before the expiry of the probationary period or at its end, following the approval of the Central Inspection Department; in this case, the probationer shall not be entitled to any dismissal indemnity for the period he spent in service, and the effect of the dismissal shall be deemed operative starting from the date of his notification thereof or from the date of actual cessation of work if that occurred before notification." And whereas Article (35) of the Civil Servants' Regulations stipulated the right of the employee, after the expiry of one year from his appointment, and in every subsequent year he spends in actual service, to benefit from an annual leave on full salary for a period of twenty days, provided that each department schedules the dates of leaves of the employees affiliated to it in a manner that ensures the continuity of work therein, and that the leave decision states the name of the employee who replaces the employee on leave throughout the period of his absence and deputizes for him in all his powers and responsibilities, and that the effect of dismissal from service or placement on retirement shall not become operative until after the end of the period of administrative leaves to which the employee is entitled. And whereas what is understood from the phrase "after the expiry of one year from his appointment" set forth in Article 35 of the Civil Servants' Regulations is the expiry of one year of actual service from the appointment of the employee occurring for the first time in the general administrative cadre, such that the employee is entitled after the expiry of this year and in every subsequent year to benefit from his administrative leaves; consequently, in the event that this employee is transferred and appointed to a new position in the general administrative cadre, even if in the capacity of a probationer, as is the case in the present matter, that does not preclude him from benefiting from his administrative leaves previously accrued to him. Furthermore, holding otherwise would lead to the forfeiture of part of the accumulated leave balance of the concerned parties, which was formed and constituted one of their acquired rights that cannot be divested except by an explicit legal text.

13 - Maternity Leave - Adopted Son: In the case concerning the extent of the possibility for a female teacher to benefit from maternity leave in order to care for her adopted son, the Civil Service Board replied in its Letter No. 669 dated 23/3/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as follows: Whereas Article 38 of the Civil Servants' Regulations and the amendments thereto stipulates the following: "A pregnant female employee shall be granted a leave on full salary called 'maternity leave' for a maximum period of sixty days. Maternity leave shall not be included in the calculation of administrative leaves nor in the calculation of sick leaves. 1 - Maternity leave shall be granted all at once without division when the applicant therefor is about to give birth. 2 - In order for maternity leave to be granted, the female employee must submit a special application containing: a - The start date of the leave and its end date. b - The approximate date of delivery according to the physician's report. 3 - A female employee who has been granted maternity leave is not entitled to submit medical sick reports during the period of maternity leave, nor is she entitled to divide this leave." And whereas maternity leave - regardless of the purpose justifying its grant - does not accrue to a female employee unless the grounds and conditions of entitlement thereto are met in accordance with the rules clearly defined in Article 38 referred to above. And whereas it is evident from the provisions set forth in Article 38 referred to above that maternity leave applies only to a pregnant female employee, who must submit a special application in this regard accompanied by the necessary documents. And whereas the purpose of maternity leave is to take into consideration the circumstances of the female employee during the period of delivery, together with what this period and the state immediately following it require in terms of the mother's personal need for rest, on the one hand, and the child's need, on the other hand, for care, attention, and looking after by his mother. And whereas it is evident from the presented case that the aspect relating to the mother's personal need for rest is not met, given that Mrs. (- -) did not give birth to a newborn, but rather came to have an adopted son, and consequently there remains only the other aspect relating to the need of her adopted child, whose age has not exceeded two weeks, for his mother's care. And whereas Article 38 of the Civil Servants' Regulations, in fixing maternity leave at a maximum period of sixty days, did not separate the period that the mother needs for rest after delivery from the period during which the child needs care by his mother, but rather considered it an indivisible whole. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board - pursuant to the provisions of Article 38 of the Civil Servants' Regulations - found that it is not possible for Mrs. (- -) to benefit from the maternity leave provided for in the aforementioned Article, in light of the possibility for the concerned party to request to benefit from a special leave without to request to benefit from a special leave without

salary in accordance with the rules, in order to care for her adopted child.

14 - Maternity leave - Calculation of the duration - Placement outside the cadre: In the matter concerning the request for information on the date that may be adopted to begin calculating the duration of maternity leave, the Civil Service Board replied in its Letter No. 571 dated 7/4/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Agriculture as follows: Whereas Article (38) of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Personnel Regulations) provides as follows: "A pregnant female employee shall be granted leave with full salary called 'maternity leave' for a maximum period of sixty days. Maternity leave shall neither be included in the calculation of administrative leaves nor in the calculation of sick leaves. 1 - Maternity leave shall be granted all at once without division when the applicant therefor is about to give birth. 2 - In order to be granted maternity leave, the female employee must submit a special application including: a - The start date of the leave and its end date. b - The approximate date of delivery according to the physician's report...". And whereas Article (40) of the Personnel Regulations concerning the authority vested with the right to grant leaves, has provided that maternity leaves shall be granted by a decision of the Director General. And whereas, in order to grant Mrs. (-- --) maternity leave, it is required that she have been reinstated to the general administrative cadre in accordance with the rules, after having been placed outside the cadre. And whereas the person concerned was reinstated to her original position in the cadre of the Ministry of Agriculture pursuant to Decision No. 3/1T dated 4/2/2004, therefore the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that the running of the remaining period of the maternity leave due to Mrs. (-- --) begins as of the date of issuance of the aforementioned decision reinstating her to the general administrative cadre and her notification thereof in accordance with the rules, and consequently the competent administrative authority must issue the necessary decision in this regard, considering that during the period prior to the date of her notification of the decision reinstating her to the cadre, she was administratively and disciplinarily subordinate to the regional organisation to which she was attached after her placement outside the cadre.

15 - Compensation - Deductions - Tourism offices abroad: In the matter concerning the request to give an opinion on the following two subjects: First: May it be considered that the compensation determined by Decree No. 4123 dated 17/10/2000, concerning the operating regulations of tourism offices abroad, in Article Six thereof, is the net compensation that must be paid to the Head of the Office, or must the deductions due on the salary in the French host State be deducted therefrom, such as sickness, old-age and end-of-service indemnities... which is what the Ministry currently bears, leaving the Head of the Office to bear the payment of the income tax which he declares personally at the end of each year to the French State? And is it consequently possible to reconcile Lebanese law and French law in respect of this matter? Second: The validity of fixing the compensation of Mr. Serge Akl, Head of the Office in Paris, in accordance with the exchange rate of the Dollar against the Euro on the date of issuance of Decree No. 4123 dated 17/10/2000? The Civil Service Board replied in its Letter No. 1393 dated 3/6/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Tourism as follows: a - With respect to the first question: Whereas Article Six of Decree No. 4123/2000 provides as follows: "The Head of the Office shall receive a lump-sum compensation in accordance with what is specified in Table No. 16 attached to Law No. 717 dated 5/11/1998, and an expatriation allowance shall also be paid to him in addition to the monthly family allowance set forth in Decree No. 1053 dated 5/8/1999 and the housing allowance amended by Decree No. 1087 dated 9/8/1999". Whereas it appears from your Letter No. 2038/1 mentioned in the reference above that the Ministry of Tourism bears all the deductions due on the salary in the host State such as sickness, old-age and end-of-service indemnities..., and the Head of the Office bears only the income tax which he declares personally at the end of each year to the French State, considering that the said office is treated towards the French State as a private institution in accordance with what was indicated in your aforementioned letter. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that there is nothing that prevents the continuation of the situation as it is in this respect, unless a contrary legal situation arises that requires adopting other bases. b - With respect to the second question: Whereas the Ministry of Finance had previously, in its Letter No. 563/S1 addressed to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers on 1/4/2004, considered that Law No. 717 dated 5/11/1998 (Raising the minimum salaries and wages and converting the salary scales of employees of the general administrative cadre...) had anticipated fluctuations in the exchange rate of the US Dollar in relation to other currencies and thus determined the bases for addressing these fluctuations in a manner that guarantees to the salary of a Foreign Service employee working abroad the same purchasing power that it had on the date of fixing this salary, namely on 1/1/99, and consequently there is no need for any legislative or regulatory text to address the apparent decline in the purchasing power of the salaries of Foreign Service employees in the Sterling, Euro and Swiss Franc zones because this addressing is carried out by an administrative measure on the part of the Ministry of Finance. And whereas Decree No. 4123 dated 17/10/2000, when determining the lump-sum compensation for the Head of the Tourism Office abroad, cross-referenced the salary scales of Foreign Service employees of the Third Category working abroad shown in Table No. 16 attached to Law No. 717 dated 5/11/1998, therefore the Board of the Civil Service Board decided to approve what was expressed by the Ministry of Finance in its aforementioned Letter No. 563/S1, which also governs the presented issue concerning the compensation of the Head of the Tourism Office in Paris.

18 - Additional compensation of 50% of the salary - technical employees in Civil Aviation: In the case relating to the request of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (formerly) to approve the granting of an additional monthly compensation equivalent to 50 % of the value of the monthly salary to the technical employees and the special corps working in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation as a result of working conditions and the continuous decline this measure until the commencement of the work of the General Authority of Civil Aviation, the Civil Service Board replied in its letter No. 2683 dated 29/9/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport with the following: Whereas Item (Second) of the second Article of Law No. 717 dated 5/11/1998 and its amendments (raising the minimum of salaries and wages...) repealed all compensations, allowances, bonuses, salary accessories and supplements, whatever their kind, designation, form or nature, from which the employees concerned by the provisions of Law No. 717/98 benefit, enumerating the compensations exempted from repeal. And whereas the compensation proposed to be given to the technical employees and the special corps working in the technical departments in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (formerly) is considered - by its nature - among the compensations accessory to the salary that were repealed pursuant to Law No. 717/98 in accordance with what is set out above, and that giving such a compensation requires the issuance of a text at the level of a law. And whereas the primary reason relied upon by the Ministry of Public Works and Transport to propose such a compensation, represented by the existence of a shortage in the number of technical employees in the technical departments, does not constitute a sufficient argument to proceed with the aforementioned proposal, because that will lead to similar demands from the rest of the employees who are in a similar position or by other public administrations that suffer from a shortage in their human staff for various reasons, and that is bound to enter the Government into a vortex of similar demands that do not end in order to address matters that have an exceptional and partial character. And whereas it appears or the salaries of technicians and the special corps in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation have been allocated special scales distinct from the salary scales of positions similar to them in category and rank, with a difference reaching in some of them up to three steps, considering that the nature of the work of those concerned differs from other positions similar to them in category and rank, whether in terms of working hours or responsibility. Furthermore, Law No. 717/98, in converting the salary scales of technicians and the special corps in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation after merging the compensations, distinguished, in addition to the steps mentioned above, these scales with an increase equivalent to the value of four steps over the salary scales of positions similar to their positions in category and rank, a matter from which it is inferred that those concerned have benefited from non-negligible increases in their salaries over the employees in the general administrative cadre who are similar to them in category and rank. And whereas the issue of the abstention of technical employees from working outside official working hours, to which the Ministry of Public Works and Transport referred in its letter No. 499/S dated 21/7/2004 mentioned above, cannot be accepted, considering that this constitutes a breach of the functional duties incumbent upon them in accordance with the laws and regulations in force and conflicts with the public interest which the employee must, in accordance with the law, seek to achieve; furthermore, the technical employees working in the technical departments in Civil Aviation are obliged to work continuously during official working hours and outside them according to the nature of the work governed by the relevant regulations and which were taken into consideration when converting their salary scales; furthermore, they are entitled to benefit from compensation for overtime hours to which they are assigned in accordance with the regulations applied to them and the provisions of Decree No. 3379 dated 11/7/2000 and its amendments (Overtime Regulations) and from the compensation allowance for night working hours as provided for in Decree No. 4357 dated 12/11/ 1993 (determining the compensation for night working hours in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport), and consequently, in return for performing their work outside the working hours specified for them, they receive compensation in accordance with what is set out above, a matter which indicates the absence of the need to give them the proposed additional monthly compensation. And whereas this Board must point out that granting a lump-sum additional monthly compensation to the technical employees and the special corps, and before the General Authority of Civil Aviation commences its work, opens the way for the possibility of a demand by an employee who requests the termination of his service in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph (3) of Item (First) of Article (18 ) of Law No. 481 dated 12/12/2002 (Management of the Civil Aviation Sector) to include the said compensation within the last salary he received for the purpose of calculating the additional compensation provided for in the aforementioned Paragraph (3). And whereas it is required, in order to address the problems faced by the technical departments in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (formerly), to take the initiative with the necessary speed to adopt the measures aimed at enabling the General Authority of Civil Aviation to commence its work, whereby it in turn takes the measures that would organize the work of the civil aviation sector and advance it, pursuant to the powers vested in it. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board saw fit not to approve giving the technical employees and the special corps working in the technical departments affiliated with the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (formerly) a lump-sum monthly additional compensation equivalent to 50% of the value of the monthly basic salary of the employee.

19 - Demands of the air traffic controllers at Beirut International Airport: In the case relating to the demands of the air traffic controllers in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation regarding the following matters: 1 - Considering the draft of the new organizational structure for air navigation as the primary demand. 2 - Pending the organizational structure draft, repealing Council of Ministers Decision No. 35 dated 27/9/2001 3 - Including all compensations, including night and overtime work, in the calculation of the end-of-service indemnity. 4 - Paying the differences of the scale of ranks and salaries and what ensues therefrom for the years 1996 - 1997 - 1998 The Civil Service Board replied in its letter No. 1042 dated 15/4/ 2004 addressed to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers with the following:

First: Regarding the first demand relating to the draft of the new organisational structure for air navigation: Whereas on 12/12/2002 Law No. 481 relating to the administration of the civil aviation sector was issued, wherein Article Two thereof provided for the establishment of a public institution called the "General Authority of Civil Aviation". And whereas Article (17) of the aforementioned Law No. 481/2002 provided for the repeal of the final paragraph of Item (1) of Article Four of Law No. 247 dated 7/8/2000 relating to the merger, abolition, and establishment of ministries and councils, and its replacement with the following text: "The Directorate General of Civil Aviation shall be abolished, and a Government Commissariat to the General Authority of Civil Aviation shall be established within the Ministry of Public Works and Transport". And whereas Item - 1 - of Paragraph (First) of Article (18) of

the Law referred to above provided that, within a period of three months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, the Ministry of Public Works and Transport shall cause to be issued the regulatory decrees determining the cadres of the Government Commissariat therein, and the employees and workers at the Directorate General of Civil Aviation and the Civil Aviation Safety Centre who meet the statutory requirements shall be attached and transferred to the new cadres of the Government Commissariat in accordance with the provisions set forth in the said regulatory decrees. And whereas Law No. 481/2002 was published in Issue No. 69 of the Official Gazette dated 19/12/2002, and consequently there is no longer any scope for reconsidering the organisational structure of any of the units affiliated with the Directorate General of Civil Aviation save in the light of the provisions contained in the said Law. And whereas the General Authority of Civil Aviation is not subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board pursuant to Item (2) of Article Ten of Law No. 481/2002, and whereas the Council of Ministers approved, by its Decision No. 20 dated 14/ 8/2003, five draft decrees relating to the General Authority of Civil Aviation, among which are drafts relating to the Government Commissariat, to the staff regulations, and to the organisational structure pertaining thereto. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Council considers that the subject of the new organisational structure for air navigation falls outside the powers of this Council, and it rests with the concerned authorities to complete the procedures aimed at causing the necessary regulatory texts to be issued in implementation of Law No. 481/2002

Second: Regarding the second demand relating to the repeal of Decision of the Council of Ministers No. 35 dated 27/9/2001: Whereas Decision of the Council of Ministers No. 35 dated 27/9/2001 ordered, contrary to the opinion of this Council, the settlement of the allowances pertaining to the employees working in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation for the year 2000 for one final time, provided that the concerned parties waive any demand or right of whatever kind relating to this subject. And whereas the air traffic controllers are requesting the repeal of Decision No. 35/ 2001 with the aim of recalculating night hours as actual working hours according to the method that was previously followed and paying the retroactive effect for the years 2001 - 2002 - 2003 And whereas the air traffic controllers, in implementation of Decision of the Council of Ministers No. 35/2001, signed settlement agreements in which they undertook not to claim any allowance of whatever kind with respect to overtime remuneration for night working hours starting from 1/1/ 2001 because the right to this allowance does not legally exist, and consequently their request to repeal Decision No. 35/2001 does not achieve the purpose behind which they are concealing themselves after the said Decision has been executed, a matter which necessitates not repealing it. And whereas it appears from the attached documents that the technical employees working in the Air Navigation Department in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation perform their work continuously on the basis of three shifts rotating over 24 hours for each of them, and resting for 48 hours, so that each shift works 10 times in a single month, resulting in 240 actual working hours (night - day) per month distributed as follows: - Number of official working hours = 32 hours weekly × 4 = 128 hours per month. - Number of night working hours = 10 working days in a single month × 10 night working hours daily = 100 night working hours monthly. Thus the difference (i.e. 240 - 228) is the maximum number of hours for which an additional allowance is due (i.e. 12 hours per month). And whereas the Civil Service Board, by its Letter No. 4754 addressed to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport on 28/10/2000, in the course of expressing its opinion regarding the payment of remuneration for additional monthly night hours to employees in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation - Air Navigation Department, considered, in the light of the rule set out above, that the hours for which an additional allowance is due to the said employees are 12 hours per month. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Council states that it still maintains its opinion set out in its Letter No. 4754/2000, because to hold otherwise would lead to granting remuneration for overtime work twice, considering that the night hours performed outside official working hours are overtime working hours governed by different regulations with respect to calculating the allowance therefor, and consequently granting the remuneration in accordance with the said demand comes in violation of the provisions of the laws and regulations in force and of the general principles of law.

Third: Regarding the third demand relating to the inclusion of all allowances received by the air traffic controllers, including night and overtime work, in the calculation of end-of-service indemnity: Whereas the said demand relates to the rules and principles provided for in Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 19/6/1983 (Retirement and Dismissal from Service Regulations) which are adopted in determining the end-of-service indemnity, and which are applied not only to air traffic controllers but to all employees in the public administrations. And whereas any demand that deals with amending a general and comprehensive text in order to meet the interests of a specific category of employees to the exclusion of others will breach the principle of equality and lead to similar demands pursuant to the said principle. And whereas the opinion of the Civil Service Board has settled on not approving partial solutions relating to the demands of a category of persons to the exclusion of others, especially those who are in a similar situation. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Council decided not to approve the request of the air traffic controllers to include all allowances that they receive, including night and overtime work, in the calculation of the end-of-service indemnity, considering that the said request is of a fundamental and comprehensive nature and its effect reflects upon the rest of the employees, and consequently it will enter the Government into a spiral of endless demands.

Fourth: With regard to the fourth demand relating to the payment of the differences of the scale of ranks and salaries and what accrues therefrom for the years 96 - 97 - 98: Whereas Article Fourteen of Law No. 717 dated 8/11/1998 (Raising the minimum limit of salaries and wages...) provided that "when resources become available at the Treasury, the Government shall refer to the Chamber of Deputies draft laws aimed at opening the necessary appropriations in order to settle the retroactive effect due as of 1/1/1996 to the beneficiaries of the provisions of this Law". And whereas the disbursement of the retroactive effect due to the members of the teaching staff in pre-university education for the differences of their salaries as of 1/1/1996 for more than five years has violated the two principles of justice and equality between one category and another of employees in public administrations, which has rightfully led and continues to lead to demands of a financial nature from numerous categories of employees, amongst which fall the demands of air traffic controllers. And whereas several draft legal texts relating to the manner of settling the dues provided for in the aforementioned Article Fourteen have previously been submitted to the Civil Service Board, and this Board has expressed its opinion approving them, the last of which was by its Letter No. 507 addressed to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers on 11/3/2004 in the course of expressing its opinion on the proposed law aimed at settling the said dues in five annual instalments as of the year 2005, and whereas securing the necessary appropriations in order to settle the retroactive effect due as of 1/1/96 to the beneficiaries thereof falls within the general policy of the State. Therefore, the Committee of the Civil Service Board deemed that it pertains to the Council of Ministers to decide the appropriate manner that secures the right of all concerned persons to receive the differences due to them, including the air traffic controllers, in a manner consistent with the right of the persons concerned therewith in accordance with the objective intended by the legislator in granting them these differences, and the general policy of the State in this regard. 20 - Retirement pension - Civil Defence - wage earner - death: In the case relating to a former wage earner in the General Directorate of Civil Defence who died as a martyr on 26/9/2002, with a view to allocating a retirement pension to his family pursuant to Law No. 136 dated 26/10/1999 after the end-of-service indemnity of the person concerned as a wage earner had been liquidated pursuant to Articles 50 and 51 of the Social Security Law, and in which an opinion is requested on the category, rank and grade that may be adopted in order to allocate a retirement pension to his family, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 21 dated 31/3/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Finance as follows: Whereas Article One of Law No. 136 dated 26/10/1999 (Granting special financial assistance to the families of firefighters and Civil Defence personnel upon their martyrdom while performing their duty) provided as follows:

Article One: The family of the civil servant, wage earner, or contractor in the Civil Defence Directorate, as well as the family of the firefighter in municipalities, federations of municipalities, and civil aviation, who dies as a result of an assault suffered during the performance of his duty or as a result of performing a selfless act to save the life or property of others, shall be granted the financial grant provided for in paragraph (a) of item (1) of Article 95 of Legislative Decree No. 102 dated 16/9/1983 (National Defence Law), and his children shall also be admitted to schools at the expense of the State within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget, in addition to the other rights established in the event of death pursuant to special provisions.” Whereas a paragraph was added to the end of the aforementioned Article One pursuant to Law No. 425 dated 6/6/2002 providing as follows: “In addition thereto, the family shall be entitled to the retirement pension provided for in item (2) of Article (94) of the aforementioned Legislative Decree (i.e., Legislative Decree No. 102 dated 16/9/1983) or a dismissal indemnity in the determination of which the same bases set forth in item (1) of the said Article shall be observed, unless the application of the special provisions governing the civil servant, wage earner, contractor, or optional volunteer in the Civil Defence Directorate or the firefighter concerned confers better rights upon his family, in which case the family shall be granted such rights.” Whereas Article 94 of Legislative Decree No. 102 dated 16/9/1983 (National Defence Law) provided as follows: “Retirement pensions and dismissal indemnities shall pass to the families of volunteers in accordance with the general regime for retirement and dismissal from service: 1 - If the volunteer is killed by bullets or by any other weapon during an armed clash with the enemy in time of war, or during internal security maintenance operations within the country in times of peace and war, or in an ordered aviation accident, his family shall be granted a retirement pension equivalent to the basic salary subject to retirement deductions and allocated to the highest step of the rank immediately superior to his rank, including the steps above the ceiling, provided that the salary of the rank superior to his rank exceeds by at least one step the salary to which he is entitled for his rank...”. Whereas the laws and regulations in force have not defined an establishment and conditions for the appointment of Civil Defence personnel, nor has a scale of ranks and salaries been defined for them whether they are civil servants, wage earners, or contractors; however, the schedules attached to Decree No. 7563 dated 8/9/1961 (Organisation of Civil Defence) provided for certain administrative and technical positions in the Civil Defence and defined their duties as well as the responsibilities and rights of those entrusted therewith without any reference to what pertains to Civil Defence personnel entrusted with carrying out first aid operations and other duties mentioned in Legislative Decree No. 50 dated 5/8/1967 and its amendments relating to the statute and organisation of the Civil Defence. Whereas, pursuant to Decree No. 4082 dated 14/10/2000 (Organisation of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities), the General Directorate of Civil Defence was organised in implementation of the provisions of Law No. 247 dated 7/8/2000 relating to the merger, abolition, and establishment of ministries and councils. Whereas Article (81) of the aforementioned Decree No. 4082/2000 defined the conditions and procedures for filling the positions of the Second, Third, Fourth, and Fifth Categories that remain vacant after the completion of the process of classifying civil servants, from among the permanent civil servants, contractors, wage earners, and workers in the Ministry on the effective date of this Decree, in accordance with the bases defined by the said Article. Whereas it appears that the Civil Service Board approved, by its Decision No. 99 dated 22/1/2002, a draft decree aimed at classifying all civil servants of the General Directorate of Civil Defence and filling the vacant posts from among its contractors and wage earners, including Mr. (- -), where it was proposed to appoint him to the position of Civil Defence member in the first step of the salary scale of the said position; however, the said draft has not been issued to date. And since the person concerned was, on the date of his martyrdom, still a wage earner in the General Directorate of Civil Defence and his end-of-service indemnity was liquidated on the basis of the provisions of Articles 50 and 51 of the Social Security Law. And since the issue raised in the present case relates to one of the wage earners in the General Directorate of Civil Defence who was martyred before any change took place in his employment status, given that the decree appointing him to the position of Civil Defence member in the first step of the salary scale of the said position was not issued. Therefore, the Civil Service Board deemed that it is not possible to determine the category, rank, and salary that can be relied upon to calculate the value of the retirement pension for the beneficiaries, and that it falls to the Ministry of Finance to deal with the martyr Mr. (- -) as a wage earner, and consequently it falls to it to determine the financial rights to which his family is entitled in light of the legal texts referred to above and the provisions governing wage earners in the General Directorate of Civil Defence.
