21 - Public Establishments - Placement at Disposal - Benefiting from a Lump-Sum Allowance: In the matter concerning the extent of the possibility for the former Director General of the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment to benefit from the provisions of Decree No. 12351 dated 23/4/2004 providing for granting each of the Chairman of the Board of Directors - Director General, employees, wage earners, and contractors working in each of the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment and the National Authority for the Litani River a monthly lump-sum allowance in the amount of one hundred and twenty-five thousand Lebanese pounds deemed to be part of the core salary, wage, and allowance and an integral part thereof, in addition to one advancement step for each employee, wage earner, or contractor, in lieu of the reduced tariff for electrical energy repealed pursuant to Article 75 of the General Budget Law for the year 2001, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 2007 dated 22/7/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas Article (46) of Decree No. 4517 dated 13/12/1972 ( the General Regulations of Public Establishments) provides as follows: "The Director General or the Director covered by Article (45) of this Decree shall retain his rank and salary in his previous position, and shall maintain his right to advancement in accordance with the scale of steps and salaries pertaining to that position and the provisions relating thereto, and to benefit from all other benefits and services from which the employees in the public establishment to which he belonged benefit, with the exception of those specifically allocated to his previous position." And whereas the Civil Service Board had opined by its Letter No. 6127 dated 8/4/2000 that the person concerned, placed at the disposal of the Minister of Energy and Water (Minister of Hydraulic and Electrical Resources) at

the time, by Decree No. 73/99, retains his rank and salary in his previous position, and maintains his right to advancement in accordance with the scale of steps and salaries pertaining to that position and to benefit from all other benefits and services from which the employees in the public establishment to which he belonged benefit, in accordance with what is provided for in Article (46) of the General Regulations of Public Establishments. Therefore, the Panel of the Civil Service Board opined that the employees in the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment benefit, pursuant to the provisions of the aforementioned Decree No. 12351/2004, from a monthly lump-sum allowance and an advancement step, which entails granting the person concerned the entitlement to benefit from the benefits of the said Decree on an equal footing with all other employees of the Establishment. And in the alternative, whereas Article 45 of Decree No. 4517/ 72 provides that "By a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, the Director of the public establishment may be relieved of the duties of his position in order to perform one of the duties specified hereinafter, and his position in this case shall be deemed vacant: a - Chairmanship or membership of the board of directors of a public establishment. b - Placement at the disposal of the supervisory minister or the Prime Minister and the other ministers for a period of two years: and if he is not returned to a position of the positions of his category during this period, or if one of the duties mentioned in Paragraph (a) of this Article is not entrusted to him, a position lower than the positions of his category in one of the public establishments shall be offered to him upon its expiry; if he accepts it, he shall retain his salary, and if he does not accept it, he shall be dismissed from service, and his rights to dismissal indemnity shall be liquidated in accordance with the texts in force." And whereas the two-year period of the placement of the person concerned at the disposal of the Minister of Energy and Water expired on 13/1/2001, it is necessary to recommend to the Ministry of Energy and Water to work towards applying the provisions of the General Regulations of Public Establishments, in particular the said Article 45, to the person concerned and to all other employees in public establishments among directors and directors general who were previously relieved of the duties of their position and placed at disposal for more than two years and who remain in the same status to date. 22 - Placement at Disposal - Expiry of the Two-Year Period - Continuation of Salary Disbursement: In the matter concerning the continuation of the disbursement of the salaries of two civil servants placed at the disposal of the President of the Council of Ministers after the expiry of the period of their placement at disposal, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 948 dated 7/4/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Finance as follows: Whereas Article 45 of the aforementioned Decree No. 4517/72 provided as follows: "By a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, the Director General or Director of the public establishment may be relieved of the duties of his position in order to perform one of the duties specified hereinafter. And his position in this case shall be deemed vacant: a - Chairmanship or membership of the board of directors of a public establishment. b - Placement at the disposal of the supervisory minister or the Prime Minister and the other ministers for a period of two years. And if he is not returned to a position of the positions of his category during this period, or if one of the duties mentioned in Paragraph (a) of this Article is not entrusted to him, a position lower than the positions of his category, in one of the public establishments, shall be offered to him upon its expiry; if he accepts it, he shall retain his salary, and if he does not accept it, he shall be dismissed from service. And his rights to dismissal indemnity shall be liquidated in accordance with the texts in force." And whereas Article 46 of Decree No. 4517/72 referred to above provided that "The Director General or the Director covered by the provisions of Article 45 of this Decree shall retain his rank and salary in his previous position, and shall maintain his right to advancement in accordance with the scale of steps and salaries pertaining to that position and the provisions relating thereto, and to benefit from all other benefits and services from which the employees in the public establishment to which he belonged benefit, with the exception of those specifically designated for his previous position." And whereas Article (45) mentioned above specified in Paragraph (b) thereof the measures and procedures that must be followed and observed during or upon the expiry of the two-year period of the placement of the Director General or Director of the public establishment at disposal. And whereas the salary is one of the rights of the civil servant which may not be infringed except in accordance with the cases expressly provided for by the law.

And whereas it is not permissible, such being the case, to resort to the measure of cutting off the salary from the Director General relieved of the duties of his position and placed at disposal merely due to the lapse of a period of two years from his placement at disposal unless the procedures expressly provided for in Paragraph (b) of Article (45) referred to above have been exhausted. And since the two-year period of the placement of Messrs. (- -) and (- -) at disposal specified pursuant to Decrees No. 7035/2002 and No. 7311/2002 has expired without any of the measures and procedures provided for in Paragraph (b) of the aforementioned Article (45) having been taken in their regard, which entails in the present case (civilization) the continuation of the disbursement of the salaries of the two persons concerned. 23 - Half Salary - Judicial Detention - Annulment of Prosecution: In the matter concerning the payment of half-salaries of certain employees in the Water Authority of Zahle and its Environs who were previously judicially detained and returned and rejoined their positions after a judgment was issued in their regard ordering the annulment of the prosecution, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 3658/2003 dated 28/8/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas the raised matter relates to the repayment of half-salaries to the employees in the Water Authority of Zahle and its Environs for the period of their preventive detention and does not relate to the matter of paying the full salary to the employee after resuming his work after the period of his preventive detention has ended. And whereas Paragraph 2 of Article 18 of the General Regulations for Employees of the Water Authority of Zahle and its Environs provides that: "An employee who is judicially detained on a preventive basis shall receive half of his salary, and the other half shall not be paid to him unless his trial is barred, or he is acquitted, or he is sentenced to a penalty other than the penalty of imprisonment." And whereas it is inferred from the foregoing that the cases in which half-salaries are repaid to the employees who were previously judicially detained are exhaustively limited to three cases, which are the barring of trial (which is issued by the investigating judge or by the Indictment Chamber due to the absence of evidence or the absence of criminal elements or due to doubt"), acquittal (that is, upon the absence of evidence or its insufficiency), or sentencing to a penalty other than the penalty of imprisonment (sentencing to a fine). And whereas the Criminal Court of Bekaa in the raised matter annulled the prosecution against the persons concerned due to the failure to obtain the authorization to prosecute them from the competent administrative authority. And whereas the cases in which the court rules for acquittal, or barring of trial, or a penalty other than the penalty of imprisonment relate to the extent to which the criminal acts are proven or not proven against the accused, whereas the Court of Bekaa in its Decision No. 373/2000, the subject of the present matter, did not adjudicate the offences attributed to the persons concerned, but rather annulled the prosecution pursuant to the existence of a procedural plea. And since, in principle, the release of the appointed civil servant and his return to his position in a normal manner entails granting him the right to receive his full salary without the need to await the adjudication of the lawsuit brought against him and without the continued existence of that lawsuit constituting any delay to his right to receive his full salary...". - And in all cases, the annulment of prosecution or the annulment of proceedings was not mentioned among the cases exhaustively specified in Paragraph /2/ of Article /18/ of the General Regulations for Employees of the Water Authority of Zahle and its Environs mentioned above. Therefore, the Panel of the Civil Service Board opined that the half-salaries under consideration cannot be paid, on the grounds that the annulment of prosecution against the accused concerned does not fall among the cases exhaustively enumerated in Paragraph -2- of Article 18 of the General Regulations for Employees of the Water Authority of Zahle and its Environs, which permit, if fulfilled, the repayment of the other half of the salary to the employee judicially detained on a preventive basis. 24 - Family Allowance - End-of-Service Indemnity - Elements of Calculation of the Dismissal Indemnity: In the matter concerning the calculation of the family allowance within the dismissal from service indemnity for a former employee in the Water Authority of Tyre and its Dependencies, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1359 dated 22/7/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas the National Social Security Fund - End-of-Service Indemnity Branch - covers within its scope persons affiliated with it compulsorily, or optionally who entered employment before 1/5/1965, and whereas it appears that the person concerned worked in the Water Authority of Tyre and its Dependencies starting from the year 1960 and did not opt to affiliate with the National Social Security Fund - End-of-Service Indemnity Branch, and received his dismissal from service indemnity from the fund of the said Authority without the family allowance being calculated within it. And whereas Item (1) of Article (5) of Decree No. 2448 dated 11/2/2000 (conversion of the salary scales of employees in the Water Authorities with the exception of the Beirut Water Authority and amendment of the bases for calculating dismissal from service indemnities) provides that "The dismissal from service indemnity for employees shall remain subject to the legal and regulatory provisions applicable thereto prior to the enforcement of this Decree....". And whereas Item (d) of Article (45) of the General Regulations for Employees of the Water Authority of Tyre and its Dependencies provides that: "d: 1 - The calculation of the dismissal from service indemnity shall be carried out on the basis of: a - One month's salary for each year of actual service up to ten years of service. b - Two months' salary for each year of actual service after ten years and up to thirty years of service. c - Three months' salary for each year of actual service after thirty years of service. 2 - A rate of (3%) three percent shall be deducted from the employee's monthly salary as a contribution to bearing the cost resulting from these provisions. 3 - These deductions shall be transferred to the end-of-service indemnity reserve in the Authority and shall be allocated to pay the end-of-service indemnity to its employees who are compulsorily or optionally affiliated with the End-of-Service Indemnity Branch in the National Social Security Fund and to cover the end-of-service indemnities for those among them who are not affiliated with this Branch....". And whereas the opinion of the Civil Service Board is settled that the indemnities of employees in public establishments who are not affiliated with the National Social Security Fund shall be disbursed in accordance with what is provided for by the special regulations of each public establishment, proceeding from the principle of financial and administrative autonomy of these public establishments and in accordance with the bases applied in calculating dismissal from service indemnities in this Fund. And whereas this Board had previously, by its two Letters No. 1742/2001 mentioned above and No. 1830 dated 13/8/1002 - in the course of examining the issue of calculating the family allowance among the elements entering into the calculation of dismissal from service indemnities for employees not affiliated with the National Social Security Fund in each of the Barouk Water Authority and the Sidon Water Authority, opined that the family allowance may be calculated among the elements entering into the calculation of the dismissal from service indemnity for the said employees on the grounds that there is no text in the employees' regulations of each of the Barouk Water Authority and the Sidon Water Authority that provides for the elements entering into the calculation of this indemnity. And whereas it is necessary, consequently, to consider the family allowance paid directly from the fund of the Authority concerned as being among the fixed allowances and benefits added to the salary upon liquidating the dismissal from service indemnity for employees not affiliated with the National Social Security Fund. And whereas the legal provisions in the Water Authority of Tyre and its Dependencies governing the dismissal from service indemnity did not specify the elements added to the salary which enter into the calculation of the said indemnity. Therefore, the Panel of the Civil Service Board opined that the Water Authority of Tyre and its Dependencies may calculate the family allowance among the elements entering into the calculation of the dismissal from service indemnity for employees not affiliated with the National Social Security Fund. 25 - Difference in Dismissal Indemnity: In the matter concerning the extent of the possibility for two former employees at the Jabal Amel Water Authority to benefit from the difference in the dismissal indemnity due to each of them from the Authority's fund, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 2967 dated 13/10/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas Article 42 of the Employees' Regulations in the Jabal Amel Water Authority - amended pursuant to Decision No. 6 dated 17/4/2002 in accordance with the provisions of Article Five of Decree No. 2448 dated 11 /2/2000 (conversion of the salary scales of employees in the Water Authorities with the exception of the Beirut Water Authority...) - provided in Paragraph (a) thereof that "Dismissal from service is the termination of the service of the employee and his final removal from the cadre, provided that he is given the dismissal indemnity", and also provided in the Sixth Item of Paragraph (d) thereof as follows: "The employee shall receive the dismissal from service indemnity from the National Social Security Fund in accordance with the provisions of social security. As for the difference between the dismissal indemnity due to him by virtue of this Decision and the indemnity he received from the Fund, it shall be paid from the budget of the Authority." And whereas the services of each of the two persons concerned ended upon his reaching the legal age, and the two persons concerned were finally removed from the cadre of the aforementioned Authority. Therefore, the Panel of the Civil Service Board opined that each of the two persons concerned shall benefit from the difference in the dismissal from service indemnity due to him from the fund of the Jabal Amel Water Authority, in application of the provisions of Article 42 of the Employees' Regulations in the said Authority amended pursuant to Decision No. 6 dated 17/4/2002 26 - Collection Proceeds - Dismissal Indemnity: In the matter concerning the inclusion of collection proceeds in the dismissal from service indemnity in the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 989 dated 10/6/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas Administrative Memorandum No. 357 dated 24/10/1967 issued by the Director General of the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment provided that the said Establishment had decided - in application of the Board of Directors Decision No. 2 dated 3/7/ 1967 - to include certain elements that are granted to the employee on a regular and continuous basis within the calculation of the dismissal from service indemnity (production bonus, cost of living increase, gratuity, shift allowance, car allowance, overtime allowance, housing allowance...). And whereas the Board of Directors of the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment approved by its Decision No. 108-11/2004 dated 24/2/2004 the inclusion of collection proceeds in the dismissal indemnity or end-of-service indemnity whenever they fulfill the condition of continuity in receiving them during the twelve months preceding the entitlement to this indemnity and on the basis of one-twelfth of the total amounts of collection proceeds received therein in accordance with what is provided for by the Labor Law, the Social Security Law, and the judicial rulings issued in this regard, provided that this Decision is submitted for the approval of each of the Civil Service Board and the supervisory authority. And whereas Paragraph 4 of Article 5 of Decree No. 2444 dated 11/2/2000 (conversion of the salary scales of employees of the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment...) provides that "The employee shall receive the dismissal from service indemnity from the National Social Security Fund in accordance with the provisions of the Social Security Law....". And whereas Paragraph (1) of Article /68/ of the Draft Law put into force by Decree No. 13955 dated 26/ 9/1963 (the Social Security Law) provides "that the earnings taken as a basis for the calculation of contributions shall include the total income resulting from work, including all elements and accessories...". And whereas Article 57 of the Labor Law provides that the wage adopted for the calculation of indemnities is the basic wage which the wage earner receives on the basis of time, together with the increases, allowances, and commissions that were added to this wage. And whereas the jurisprudence of the Labor Arbitration Board is settled on considering collection proceeds as part of the wage that must be adopted for calculating the dismissal from service indemnity, on the grounds that they are given to the employee in return for his work for a long period and are characterized by generality, continuity, and stability, and are among the accessories provided for in Article 57 of the Labor Law and in Article 68 of the Social Security Law referred to. Therefore, the Panel of the Civil Service Board opined that there is nothing to prevent the inclusion of collection proceeds in the dismissal from service indemnity in the Electricity of Lebanon Establishment in accordance with what is set forth in the Decision of the Board of Directors of the said Establishment No. 108/11/2004 dated 24/2/ 2004, on the grounds that this matter is in accordance with the jurisprudence of the Labor Arbitration Board in this respect. 27 - Public Establishments - Granting Administrative Leaves - Competence of the Governor: In the matter concerning the extent of the competence of the Governor of Bekaa to grant leaves to the civil servants of the Housing Office in the Governorate of Bekaa affiliated with the Public Establishment for Housing, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 403 dated 22/4/2004 addressed to the Governorate of Bekaa as follows: It appeared that the Governor of Bekaa states by his letter mentioned in the reference above that he sometimes receives certain leave applications pertaining to the persons concerned by referral from the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Public Establishment for Housing - Director General, containing the approval of the latter of the requested leave with an attached statement of the balance of administrative leaves pertaining to the civil servant applying for leave, and that the Governor has issued certain decisions relating to leaves on the basis of the said approval. Accordingly, whereas Article (3) of Law No. 539 dated 24/7/1996 (Establishment of the Public Establishment for Housing) provided that "The Establishment shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and to the provisions of the Housing Law that do not conflict with its provisions, and the Establishment shall have special administrative and financial regulations drawn up by the Board and approved by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister. The cadres of the Establishment and the categories of its employees and their ranks, salaries, and allowances shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister." And whereas Law No. 247 dated 7/8/2000 attached to the Public Establishment for Housing all workers in the Autonomous Housing Fund and gave the civil servants of the (abolished) Directorate General of Housing the right to choose to transfer to the Public Establishment for Housing or to vacancies in the cadres of public administrations. And whereas the cadre of the Public Establishment for Housing and the determination of the positions of this cadre have not been issued to date, from which it is inferred that no appointment could have been made from among the civil servants of the (abolished) Directorate General of Housing to the cadre of the Public Establishment. And whereas the legal texts governing housing affairs permitted the creation of regional offices concerned with housing affairs in the regions, and it is consequently necessary that these offices have become affiliated with the Public Establishment for Housing in implementation of the provisions of Law No. 247/2000. And whereas the Governor of Bekaa, by his letter mentioned in the reference above, stated that the persons concerned are among the civil servants of the Housing Office in Zahle affiliated with the Public Establishment for Housing, which requires that they be among the employees of the abolished Autonomous Housing Fund, and it is consequently necessary that the legal provisions in force in the Public Establishment for Housing be applied to them. And whereas Paragraph (5) of Article Five of the Administrative Regulations of the Public Establishment for Housing approved by Decree No. 10451 dated 19/6/1997 provided that granting leaves of whatever kind is within the competence of the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Public Establishment for Housing - Director General. And whereas the powers of the Governor, in accordance with what is provided for in Legislative Decree No. 116 dated 12/6/1959 (Administrative Organization), are general and comprehensive powers covering all departments and bodies with the exception of the Ministries of Justice and National Defense, and they also include overseeing the implementation of laws, regulations, and general instructions in the Governorate, and consider him responsible for their proper application, and he may for this purpose take all measures that lead to coordinating work among the various departments and ensuring its proper functioning and execution. And whereas the Law of Establishment of the Public Establishment for Housing and the regulations issued in application thereof did not give the Governor the competence to grant leaves to the workers affiliated with the said Public Establishment. And whereas Legislative Decree No. 116/59 gave the Governor the competence to grant leaves to the civil servants of the ministries present within the scope of his Governorate, yet it did not provide for the exercise of this competence over the bodies of public establishments. However, this Board must point out that the General Regulations of Public Establishments issued by Decree No. 4517 dated 13/ 12/1972 provided in Article /36/ as follows: "Subject to the provisions relating to supervision and the oversight authority, the Governor or the Qaimaqam, each within the scope of his competences, shall supervise the public establishment or its departments located within the scope of the Governorate or the District, with the exception of the Governorate of the City of Beirut. The details of the application of the preceding paragraph shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the supervisory minister and the Minister of the Interior." Therefore, the Panel of the Civil Service Board opined that it is necessary for the competent authorities to take the initiative to work in accordance with the rules towards preparing and issuing the said decree, which determines, within the scope of the competences of each of the Governor and the Qaimaqam, the details of his supervision over public establishments and their departments located within the scope of the Governorate or the District, and that under the currently existing legal texts, the competences to grant leaves of various kinds to the persons concerned are, in accordance with what has been set forth above, within the competences of the Chairman of the Board of Directors - Director General of the Public Establishment for Housing. 28 - Overtime - /13th/ Month - Calculation of Dismissal Indemnity: In the matter concerning a request for an opinion on the extent to which overtime hours and the thirteenth month are considered part of the dismissal from service indemnity for an employee working in the Koura Potable Water Authority, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 871 dated 23/9/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows:

First: With regard to overtime compensation: Whereas paragraph - 4 - of Article Five of Decree No. 2448 dated 11/2/2000 (conversion of the salary scales of employees in the Water Authorities....) provides that "the employee shall receive the end-of-service indemnity from the National Social Security Fund in accordance with the provisions of the Social Security Law; as for the difference between the end-of-service indemnity due to him by virtue of this Decree and the indemnity that he received from the Fund, it shall be paid from the budget of the Authority". And whereas paragraph (1 - a) of Article 51 of the draft law put into effect by Decree No. 13955 dated 26/ 9/1963 (the Social Security Law) provides as follows: "... If the wage is calculated wholly or partially on the basis of commission (commission), the amount of the indemnity shall equal, for each year of service, one-twelfth of the total sums received by the person concerned during the twelve months preceding the date referred to above (that is, the date on which the right to the indemnity arose)... In all cases, the wage taken as the basis for calculating the indemnity is that determined in Article 68, paragraph (1), of this Law". And whereas paragraph (1) of Article 68 of the draft law put into effect by the aforementioned Decree No. 13955/1963 provides as follows: "The earnings taken as the basis for calculating contributions shall include the total income resulting from work, including all elements and ancillaries, and in particular the compensation for overtime hours paid on a customary basis...". And whereas items 1 and 3 of Article 57 of the General Regulations for Employees and Contractors of the Koura Potable Water Authority provide as follows: "1 - The end-of-service indemnity for the employee shall be determined at one month's salary for each year of actual service and on the basis of the last salary

received by him together with its fixed supplements. 3 - Fixed salary supplements are designated as: a - Cost of living increase. b - Production bonus. c - The thirteenth-month proportion. d - Specialization allowance. e - Compensation for overtime hours granted to the employee in return for additional work performed by him on a customary, regular, and continuous basis, excluding the compensation given to the employee on an exceptional basis in return for additional work performed by him on an incidental, emergency, and non-fixed basis. f - Family allowance....". And whereas it appears that both the General Regulations for Employees and Contractors of the Koura Potable Water Authority and the Social Security Law have stipulated, for the inclusion of overtime hours in the end-of-service indemnity, that such hours be regular, customary, and continuous. And whereas it appears from the letter of the Director General of Exploitation by substitution No. 175/6 S addressed to the Civil Service Board on 21/2/ 1998 that the Directorate General of Exploitation had deemed at the time that compensation for overtime hours should be included in the end-of-service indemnity provided that such hours had been granted on a regular basis for a period of at least three years, on the basis of 1/12 of the average received by the employee during these last three years. And whereas the Civil Service Board - in reply to the letter of the Ministry of Energy and Water No. 175/6 S dated 21/2/1998 - considered in its letter No. 714 dated 11/4/1998 that compensations for overtime hours enter into the calculation of the end-of-service indemnity provided that they are disbursed in accordance with the bases adopted in the National Social Security Fund, that is, the equivalent for each year of 1/12 of the total paid to the employee as an allowance for hours for the entire last year of service. And whereas this Board considers that, in order for overtime hours to be characterized by regularity and continuity, it is required that the employee has performed them on a customary and continuous basis for a period of three years, so that they may thereafter be calculated in accordance with the bases adopted in Social Security, that is, the equivalent of 1/12 of the total paid to the employee as an allowance for hours for the entire last year of service.

Second: With regard to the thirteenth month: Whereas the thirteenth-month proportion is considered one of the fixed salary supplements that enter into the composition of the salary adopted in calculating the end-of-service indemnity for the employee in the Koura Potable Water Authority. And whereas the Council of Ministers, by its Decision No. 7 dated 9/12/1970, approved the calculation of the thirteenth-month salary in accordance with the proposal of the Ministry of Hydraulic and Electric Resources (formerly), such that the calculation of this salary includes all its supplements, among which is the family allowance. And whereas the Ministry of Finance considered in its letter No. 411/S16 dated 10/2/2004, with regard to the matter under consideration, that the thirteenth month must be calculated without adding the family allowance, whereas it had previously expressed in its letter No. 1950/S16 dated 16/12/2002 a contrary opinion through its approval of the decision of the Board of Directors of the North Lebanon Water Establishment No. 8/22 dated 24/10/2002 aimed at securing the necessary appropriations to pay the thirteenth-month differences to the employees and wage-earners of the Koura Potable Water Authority in application of Decision of the Council of Ministers No. 7 dated 9/12/1970 And whereas it does not appear from the file of the transaction that a decision was issued by the Council of Ministers amending or repealing its aforementioned Decision No. 7/1970. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considers, with regard to the calculation of the thirteenth month, that what was contained in the aforementioned decision of the Council of Ministers must be adhered to. 29 - Temporary transport allowance - guards: In the matter concerning the request for an opinion on the letter of the Public Establishment for Consumer Markets relating to the manner of calculating the temporary transport allowance for the guards working for it, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3795 dated 27/12/2004 addressed to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers as follows: Whereas paragraph (a) of Article One of Law No. 266 dated 23/10/1993 provided for the granting of a temporary transport allowance paid monthly to all workers in public administrations, including permanent and temporary civil servants regardless of their positions and cadres, and contractors.... and members of the teaching staff regardless of the types and stages of public and private education...... with the exception of military personnel regardless of their categories, as well as those who benefit from in-kind transport benefits whatever their positions and cadres........, and paragraph (b) of the aforementioned Article One provided that the said allowance falls due for each day of actual attendance at the rate of 2% of the minimum wage in force at any time, and whereas Decree No. 7723 dated 5/4/2002 determined the amount of the temporary transport allowance provided for in Law No. 266/93 at the sum of six thousand Lebanese pounds for workers in public establishments for each day of actual attendance at work, and whereas it is inferred from the legal texts referred to above that the temporary transport allowance falls due to the employee (and the contractor) for each day of actual attendance at his place of work, since the legal and regulatory provisions governing the rules for payment of this allowance presume that the beneficiary thereof has incurred expenses when travelling to his place of work, and consequently the said allowance is an allowance in return for an expense. And whereas, in the event that the civil servant, employee, or contractor remains at his place of work throughout the day until the following day, he is only entitled to a transport allowance paid to him once, given that this allowance is in return for the expense incurred by him to attend his place of work, and in the present case he has only incurred this expense once.

30 - Secondary school teachers attached to the Central Administration - Return to original workstations - Summer vacation: In the matter concerning the extent of the right of members of the teaching staff attached to the Central Administration and the Educational Regions to assist administrative employees, to return to their original workstations for the purpose of benefiting from the summer vacation and consequently receiving the salaries for this vacation, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 746 dated 15/5/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as follows: Whereas the assignment of members of the teaching staff to assist administrative employees in the various directorates and services affiliated with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education is effected for a specific period (which is often for a period of one year) and in accordance with the rules stipulated in Decree 5257 dated 10/8 /1966, including its conjunction with the approval of the Civil Service Board. And whereas it appears from the reports issued by the competent authorities in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education that there is a surplus of secondary school teachers and primary school teachers in the teaching corps. And whereas the aforementioned assignment is originally effected from among the surplus members of the teaching staff in the teaching corps in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, in order to assist the administrative employees in the various administrative units in the said Ministry in light of the need of these units based on an investigation conducted by the Central Inspection's Department of Research and Guidance in this regard. And whereas it is incumbent upon the members of the teaching staff assigned to assist the administrative employees in accordance with the bases set out above, to continue with what is required of them in order to achieve the desired purpose of this assignment throughout the period specified in the assignment decision. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that it is not permissible to return those persons to their workstations in the public education cadre before the expiry of the period of their assignment due to its conflict with the public interest, considering that it ultimately leads to an increase in the number of employees in a corps that suffers from a surplus, and to a decrease in this number in administrative units in need of their services.

31 - Electing to remain in the Administration - Return to the teaching corps: In the matter concerning the extent of the permissibility of returning to the teaching corps after electing to remain in the administrative corps, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3018 dated 16/9/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Culture as follows: Whereas Law No. 454/95 stipulated that the members of the teaching staff concerned thereby shall submit a written application containing their election to remain in the public administrations or to return to the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, to be submitted to this Ministry, and whereas it appears from the facts set forth above that Mrs. (- -) and Mr. (- -) elected to remain in the general administrative cadre and confirmed this election pursuant to the provisions of Laws No. 454/95 and No. 717/98 and whereas the position of the Civil Service Board has been settled in more than one letter issued by it that the time limit for submitting applications is a forfeiture time limit such that whoever exercised his right of election within the legal time limit cannot retract his choice after the expiry of this time limit for any reason whatsoever. And whereas Law No. 454/95 did not include provisions permitting whoever elected to remain in the public administrations to return to the teaching cadre, but rather stipulated that in the event of the absence of vacant positions in the administration in which the person concerned by the election works, his appointment shall then take place in the vacancies of the cadres of other public administrations, and not his return to his former corps, and since the return of Mrs. (- -) and Mr. (- -) to the teaching cadre in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education falls in violation of the legal provisions in force which regulate the status of the members of the teaching staff attached to the public administrations who elected to remain in these administrations, and since the Council of Ministers issued Decision No. 36 dated 11/ 10/2001 which included the request to the concerned Ministers, in implementation of the principle of ministerial solidarity, to prepare draft texts tending to transfer the members of the teaching staff who elected to remain in the public administrations and refer them to the Civil Service Board in accordance with the rules, which is the procedure that must be applied to the cases of the two concerned parties, therefore the Board of the Civil Service Board considered the return of the two concerned parties to the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education to be unlawful, and it is consequently required to return them to their workstations in which they elected to remain in the general administrative cadre in accordance with the rules.

32 - Aggregation of services - Actual service - Higher Teachers' Training Institute: In the matter relating to the extent to which the years of study at the Higher Teachers' Training Institute at the Lebanese University for secondary education teachers are considered to constitute actual services, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1117 dated 16/8/2004 addressed to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers as follows: Whereas reliance cannot be placed on the decisions issued by the State Council ruling to declare the right of an employee to aggregate his services for the years he spent at the Faculty of Pedagogy - formerly the Higher Teachers' Training Institute (prior to the issuance of the Draft Law put into force by Decree No. 3736/80) with his subsequent services in the secondary education cadre and to regularise his status on this basis, given that the decisions of the State Council are characterised by relative authority of res judicata and bind only the litigating parties therein, and consequently their effect is relative and is confined to the relationship between the parties in the lawsuit in which the judgment was rendered. Whereas the Civil Service Board, by several previous letters and in the course of applying the legal texts relating to the aggregation of services performed by an employee prior to his entry into the permanent cadre subject to the pension system, has established criteria and foundations on the manner of such aggregation and determined the beneficiaries thereof in accordance with the legal provisions stipulated by the relevant laws. Whereas the primary legal text for the aggregation of services upon which the decisions of the State Council were based and to which the Ministry of Education and Higher Education reverted in order to justify its request set out in its letter mentioned above is Article Nine of Law No. 717/98, which provides as follows: "Article Nine: First: Subject to the provisions of the Personnel Regulations, an employee who was appointed or is appointed to the permanent cadres subject to the pension system shall have the right to aggregate his services prior to such appointment in the public administrations or at the Lebanese University or the Chamber of Deputies, whatever their nature may be: temporary, contractual or daily, with his subsequent services in these cadres under the following conditions: 1 - That he be in actual service on the date of issuance of this Law or after that date. 2 - That he have been previously and duly appointed, prior to appointment to the permanent cadre, in one of the public administrations or the Lebanese University or the Chamber of Deputies. 3 -.........................". Whereas Article One of Law No. 1/72 dated 13/1 /1972 (Appointment of graduates of the Faculty of Pedagogy at the Lebanese University) provided as follows: "Article One: Graduates of the Faculty of Pedagogy at the Lebanese University holding the Teaching Diploma for Secondary Education and benefiting from a subsistence grant in accordance with the laws in force at the Faculty of Pedagogy shall be appointed without a competitive examination, at the rank and salary of a trainee secondary education teacher of the second rank - sixth grade - provided that they have obtained the teaching licence as a result of pursuing studies at the said Faculty...". Whereas it appears that Item (First) of Article /9/ mentioned above has stipulated services which the beneficiary employee must have performed prior to his appointment to the permanent cadre subject to the pension system in accordance with the rules governing employment in the administrations concerned, subject to the Personnel Regulations, by stipulating in paragraph (2) of the said Item (First) "that he have been previously and duly appointed, prior to appointment to the permanent cadre.........". Whereas the laws and regulations in force governing appointment or employment in the public service, in particular the Personnel Regulations in the public administrations and the equivalent thereof in the public institutions concerned by Article Nine referred to above, have defined the workers in the public administrations concerned who are actually performing service in accordance with the rules as follows: the permanent, temporary, or contractual employee, or the wage earner, and consequently, in order to determine the capacity of any person or to consider that he is performing service outside the cases mentioned, the law must expressly provide therefor. Whereas capacity is one of the essential elements in determining the beneficiaries of a legal text in accordance with the logical and objective interpretation of that text. Whereas the laws and regulations that governed the status of students at the Higher Teachers' Training Institute, in particular the Draft Law issued by Decree No. 2883 dated 16/12/1959 (Organisation of the Lebanese University) and Decree No. 16489 dated 29/5/ 1964 (Organisation of the Higher Teachers' Training Institute), did not provide for the status of the employee-student who was admitted to the Institute during the years he spent therein and whether those years are considered actual service in the manner provided for by the Draft Law issued by Decree No. 3736/80 regarding the possibility of aggregating them with his subsequent services by operation of law after his graduation from the said Institute and his appointment as a secondary education teacher in the permanent cadre. Whereas the phrase "whatever their nature may be" contained in Item (First) mentioned above cannot be invoked in order to consider the period spent by secondary education teachers at the Higher Teachers' Training Institute as covered by the provisions of Article Nine of Law No. 717/98, since the enumeration of the nature of these services as set out in the said Item was exhaustive and was not by way of enumeration or example, on the basis of what has been set forth above. Whereas this Board considers that the purpose of aggregating the services concerned is those services which the employee has performed prior to his entry into the permanent cadre for the first time, considering that Article Nine of Law No. 717/98 provided that the Personnel Regulations must be observed, and consequently an employee who enters the permanent cadre has become subject to the laws and regulations in force governing the status of employees pursuant to the provisions of Article Two of the Personnel Regulations, from which it is inferred that the services performed by the employee after his entry into the permanent cadre are subject to the Personnel Regulations and consequently the provisions of Article Nine of Law No. 717/98 regarding the aggregation of services cannot apply to him. Whereas to maintain otherwise leads to rendering inoperative certain legal texts governing the affairs of workers in the public administrations, in particular those governing the situations in which an employee is outside his post or is in a state of not performing a specific post provided for in the cadres, such as pursuing his academic attainment or his training, we observe that the law has expressly provided that the period during which the employee is in the said situations shall either be considered part of the actual service subject to pension deductions or shall not be counted as part of the actual service. Whereas the status in which the interested parties found themselves prior to their entry

into the Higher Teachers' Training Institute or the Faculty of Pedagogy before the year 1980 was that of employees, and consequently they cannot be considered as concerned by the provisions of Article Nine of Law No. 717/98, but rather they are subject to the special legal provisions that were in force at the Lebanese University and in the Personnel Regulations. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that the employees concerned by the transaction under consideration are the employees who were admitted to the Higher Teachers' Training Institute at the Lebanese University and graduated therefrom as secondary education teachers prior to the issuance of the Draft Law put into force by Decree No. 3736/80 mentioned above, from which it is inferred that the years during which they were students at the Higher Teachers' Training Institute formerly or at the Faculty of Pedagogy cannot be considered years of actual service and the provisions of Article Nine of Law No. 717/98 cannot be applied

33 - Financial allowance - Integration into the basic salary - Assisting administrative employees: In the case concerning the request for an opinion on the matter of the entitlement of teachers of the Second and Third Categories, assigned to administrative duties in the Central Administration of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education or in public technical institutes and schools pursuant to memoranda issued by the higher authorities in the Administration, to benefit from the financial allowance provided for in Law No. 250 dated 14/8/2000, as well as secondary school teachers assigned to the same duties pursuant to the aforementioned memoranda, from the financial allowance provided for in Law No. 148 dated 29/10/1999 and consequently integrating it into the basic salary in application of Law No. 551 dated 20/10/ 2003, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1887 dated 13/8/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as follows: Whereas Paragraphs (d) and (e) of Article 3 of Law No. 250/2000 provide as follows: "d - Teachers of the Second and Third Categories duly assigned to administrative duties in public institutes and schools affiliated with the Ministry of Vocational and Technical Education (formerly) or its Central Administration shall benefit from the provisions of this Law, e - Secondary school teachers duly assigned to administrative duties in the Central Administration of the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports (formerly), or in public secondary schools, or in public technical institutes or schools, or in teacher training colleges, or in the Lebanese University shall benefit from the provisions of Law 148 issued on 29/ 10/1999, and secondary school teachers assigned to guidance and counselling work in the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports (formerly) shall also benefit from the provisions of Law No. 148 issued on 29/ 10/1999". And whereas Article 1 of Law No. 551 dated 20/10 /2003 (Integration of the financial allowance granted under Laws No. 148/99 and 250/2000 into the basic salary) provided as follows: "By integrating the financial allowance granted under the provisions of Laws No. 148 dated 29/10/1999 and No. 250 dated 14/8/ 2000 into the basic salary, the beneficiary of the integration of the financial allowance shall be classified in the step closest to his salary in the salary scale of members of the teaching staff, provided that his advancement is accelerated or delayed in proportion to the increase or decrease incurred by his salary". And whereas, for the purpose of integrating the financial allowance granted to members of the teaching staff under the provisions of Laws No. 148/99 and No. 250/2000 into their basic salary, it is required that each of them fulfil the conditions required for granting him this allowance in the light of the provisions of the two aforementioned Laws and according to each case separately. And whereas the issue at hand relates to the extent to which teachers of the Second and Third Categories assigned to administrative duties in the Central Administration of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education or in public technical institutes and schools pursuant to memoranda issued by the higher authorities in the Administration benefit from the financial allowance referred to above, as well as secondary school teachers assigned to the same duties pursuant to memoranda. And whereas it is inferred from the provisions of Paragraphs (d) and (e) of Article 3 of Law No. 250/2000 that the teachers who benefit from the provisions of Laws No. 250/2000 and No. 148/ 99 with respect to integrating the financial allowance into their basic salary are those duly assigned to administrative duties, and whereas the assignment of members of the teaching staff to assist administrative employees, whether in the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education or in the public technical schools and institutes affiliated therewith, is regulated and governed, each within its respective scope, by the provisions of Articles 29 and 30 of Decree No. 8349 dated 2/5/1996 concerning the organisation of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education and the provisions of Decree No. 9193 dated 18/1/1968 and its amendments (Administrative Organisation of Vocational and Technical Education Schools). And whereas the assignment of teachers pursuant to memoranda to perform administrative duties, whether in the Central Administration of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education or in the public technical institutes and schools affiliated therewith, which do not observe the legal provisions stipulated in the two aforementioned Decrees, is considered a violation of the required due process stipulated by both Laws No. 250/2000 and No. 148/99, and consequently no legal effects result from these memoranda and no right accrues to those concerned therewith to claim it, and whereas the argument that this assignment is due to the need for their services does not confer the right for them to benefit from the provisions of Laws No. 250/2000 and No. 148/99, given that the concerned authorities in the Administration may proceed to assign teachers to perform administrative duties in accordance with the due process specified in the legal texts governing this matter and referred to above. And whereas Paragraphs (d) and (e) of Article 3 referred to above have clearly provided that the person who benefits from the provisions of Laws No. 250/2000 and No. 148/99 is the one who has been duly assigned to administrative duties, that is, in accordance with the due process stipulated by the two aforementioned Decrees, therefore the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that teachers assigned to administrative duties pursuant to memoranda issued by the higher authorities in the Administration are not entitled to benefit from the provisions of Laws No. 250/2000 and No. 148/99, and consequently are not entitled to have the financial allowance integrated into their basic salary.

34 - Remuneration for Services - Loss of Conditions of Employment - Medical Committee: In the case concerning the request for an opinion regarding the amounts received by an employee whose services were terminated on 31/1/2004, during the period extending from the date of issuance of the Medical Committee's decision deeming him incurable within two years until 3/12/2003, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 2131 dated 9/8/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Finance as follows: Whereas Decree No. 11841 terminated the service of the person concerned with effect from 24/9/ 2002 on the basis of the decision of the Official Medical Committee in Beirut No. 108/L.T. dated 24/9/2002 stating that the person concerned is incurable within a period of two years and is consequently unfit for service. And whereas Mr. (- -) lost, with effect from the date of issuance of the aforementioned decision of the Medical Committee, the condition stipulated in paragraph (d) of item (1) of Article (4) of the Civil Servants Regulations, which provides that every applicant for a public office is required to submit a certificate from the Official Health Committee proving that he is free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from performing the duties of his office. And whereas the aforementioned condition is a preclusive condition for appointment and for remaining in service, and Mr. (- -) became, with effect from the date of issuance of the decision of the Official Medical Committee, lacking in functional capacity and

there is no longer any legal justification for his remaining in service given that he became on the said date outside the office by operation of law, and no authority has the competence to authorize keeping an employee in service after he has lost one of the general conditions of employment as that pertains to public policy. And whereas it appears that the Ministry of Education and Higher Education continued to disburse the monthly salaries of Mr. (- -) during the period extending from 1/1/2002 until 3/12/2003, and it also appeared that Mr. (- -) attended regularly and without interruption or absence until the end of the 2002 - 2003 academic year pursuant to the certificate that was attached at the time and issued by the principal of (- -) Official Secondary School No. 141/2003 dated 29/7/2003, and whereas the Civil Service Board had previously - in the course of expressing its opinion on the liquidation of the end-of-service entitlements of teachers against whom judgments were issued by the Military Court - opined that the period subsequent to the date of issuance of the judgments against the teachers concerned, during which some of them attended at their workplaces, although not based on a legal status, it is nevertheless improper to deprive them of their remuneration for services in respect thereof due to the inadmissibility of unjust enrichment by the Administration at the expense of the persons concerned. And whereas there applies to the period subsequent to the date of issuance of the decision of the Official Committee referred to above, during which Mr. (- -) attended at his workplace, the same status pertaining to the period subsequent to the date of issuance of the judgments against the teachers during which they attended at their workplaces. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board opined that the end-of-service entitlements of Mr. (- -) must be liquidated with effect from the date of his entry into service until the date of 24/9/2002, provided that whatever he may have received during the period subsequent to the said date shall be deemed as remuneration for services that he performed for the benefit of the Administration and shall consequently not be included in the count of his actual services in the permanent cadres.

35 - Notification - Article /65/ of the Civil Servants Regulations - Failure to Assume Duties for the First Time - Lapse of 10 Years - Confirmation and Insistence: In the case concerning the approval of a draft decision aimed at confirming a probationary technical education teacher in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education - cadre of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education with effect from the date of 22/9/2003, after he had assumed his duties ten years after the issuance of his decree of appointment, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3345 dated 9/8/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as follows: Whereas paragraph (a) of item (1) of Article 65 of the Civil Servants Regulations provides that an appointed or transferred employee who fails to assume his office without a legitimate reason within fifteen days from the date of his notification of the decree or decision providing for his appointment or transfer shall be deemed to have resigned from service. And whereas the issuance of Decree No. 2070 dated 30 /12 1991 providing for the appointment of the person concerned to the office of probationary technical education teacher in the cadre of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education entails the subjection of the latter to all laws and regulations governing the public office, including the obligation to report to his workplace within fifteen days from the date of his notification or his certain knowledge of his aforementioned decree of appointment. And whereas Mr. (- -) invoked in his petition dated 29/ 7/2002 compelling reasons to justify his occurred absence without clarifying the nature of these reasons. And whereas what the person concerned invoked cannot be accepted given that it was couched in general and vague terms, especially since it was submitted ten years and seven months after the issuance of his decree of appointment, whereas he was under an obligation to inquire about his decree of appointment by all means available to him. And whereas this Board had previously, in more than one letter issued by it in similar cases, opined that it is not possible to accommodate an employee in his personal circumstances and make the office contingent upon his conditions, such that its doors remain wide open for him awaiting the completion of his private projects to enter it whenever he wishes, because that would disable the provisions contained in the Civil Servants Regulations - particularly with regard to the time limits specified therein - and render them of no consequence. And whereas it appears that the decision assigning Mr. (- -) to the Bir Hassan Technical School No. 1017/M/2002 dated 12/8/2002 was based in its final recital on the approval, confirmation, and insistence of His Excellency the Minister dated 30/7/2002 enabling the person concerned to assume his duties. And whereas the Council of Ministers, by its Decision No. 2 dated 27/12/ 1989, requested the Ministers not to confirm and insist on the execution of orders and instructions to which their subordinate draws their attention in writing as being explicitly and clearly in violation of the laws and regulations in force pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (2) of Article (14) of the Civil Servants Regulations except after submitting the matter to the Council of Ministers. And whereas the Minister, by his aforementioned insistence and confirmation, did not observe the content of the aforementioned decision of the Council of Ministers. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board opined that it is not possible to approve the confirmation of Mr. (- -) in the office to which he was appointed in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education - Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, and to submit the case to the authority of the said Council to decide what is appropriate regarding it.

36 - Justification of absence - travel - marriage: In the case relating to the examination of the employment status of a female teacher who resumed her work after her unjustified interruption thereof, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 1138 dated 7/8/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as follows: Whereas the Civil Service Board, in more than one letter issued by it, has opined - in the course of clarifying the matter of assessing the legitimacy of absence and its justification - that no excuse is deemed a legitimate excuse under the Personnel Regulations other than the excuse provided for in the said Regulations, such as absence in the event of illness or in the event of the death of a spouse or one of the ascendants or descendants, or in the event of judicial or disciplinary detention, or in general the cases in which it is impossible for the employee to attend his place of work and perform what is required of him, due to exceptional, compelling, and sudden reasons beyond his free and conscious will. And whereas the absence of the concerned party from her work as from 13/5 /1993 until 9/10/1995 has no legal basis, and the security and family reasons put forward by the concerned party cannot be accepted because they do not conform to reality and to the attached documents, particularly with regard to her statement that she was compelled in the year 1996 to travel to Australia due to family and security circumstances, knowing that security was established at that time, in addition to the fact that she did not attach to the transaction any official medical report duly certified from abroad showing the condition of her son. And whereas the competent employee at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education stated that the approval of His Excellency the Minister No. 7610/M dated 5/10/ 1995 for the resumption of work by the concerned party is not found at the Ministry because the file of Decision No. 748 dated 26/10/ 1995 was lost either before he assumed his duties or during the process of transferring the Ministry from UNESCO to Chiyah. And whereas the loss of the aforementioned file is considered a dereliction and negligence on the part of the employee responsible for keeping official files, documents, and records during their presence at the offices of the Ministry or during their transfer to the new Ministry building, a matter which requires conducting the necessary investigation in this regard and imposing disciplinary penalties against him where applicable. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board opined that the interruption of the concerned party from her place of work from 13/5/1993 until 9/10/ 1995 is not based on legal or factual grounds capable of justifying her absence, which places her in an irregular status during the aforementioned period, with all the consequences resulting from this status relating to the employment relationship of the concerned party with the Administration as regards the application of the legal provisions in force in this respect, a matter which requires working to include the name of Mrs. (- -) within the list that this Board requested the Ministry of Education and Higher Education to prepare and submit to the Council of Ministers to take a final and comprehensive decision in such cases.

37 - Examination of a petition - stay of execution - participation in a competitive examination: In the case relating to the request to examine the petition submitted by Miss (- -) through her legal counsel, seeking to stay the execution of Decision No. 222/2 dated 7/6/2004 relating to the organisation of a competitive examination restricted to hourly contractors in public secondary schools and to those seconded to these secondary schools from among the instructors and teachers in primary and intermediate education for appointment to the post of secondary education teacher in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 2393 dated 29/7/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Justice as follows: It appeared that Law No. 441 dated 29/7/2002 (Rules of Appointment to the Post of Secondary Education Teacher) provided in items (1) and (2) of Article Two thereof as follows: "Article Two: 1 - The Civil Service Board shall conduct, for one time only, a competitive examination restricted to hourly contractors in secondary schools and to those seconded to these secondary schools from among the instructors and teachers in primary and intermediate education who hold teaching and university degrees, provided that they fulfill the conditions of appointment to the cadre of secondary education teacher in accordance with the number specified in the schedule annexed to this Law. 2 - It is required for participation in the competitive examination that the contractor fulfill the general and special conditions of employment provided for in the laws and regulations in force, with the exception of the age requirement, and that the contractor has been contracted with in accordance with the rules". And it appeared that Decree No. 12321 dated 23/4/2004 (Application of Certain Provisions of Law No. 441 dated 29/7/2002), in turn provided in Article Two thereof as follows: "Article Two: The seconded person meant by Law No. 441/ 2002 shall mean the teacher or instructor in general education who was temporarily attached pursuant to any instrument or approval from the Director General of Education to public secondary schools to perform teaching duties, administrative duties, or non-teaching duties of whatever kind". And it appeared that the Civil Service Board, after seeking clarification from the Ministry of Education and Higher Education regarding the import of the word "seconded" contained in Law No. 441/2002, and pursuant to its Letter No. 4838/3 dated 7/6/2004 regarding the seconded (attached) instructors in public secondary schools, [was informed of] the following: "The seconded (attached) instructors are those who were seconded (attached) in accordance with the rules to public secondary schools for teaching or for any other duty since the academic year 2001 - 2002 and prior thereto and who are still seconded (attached) up to the date of entry into force of Law No. 441 dated 29/7/2002". And it appeared that, pursuant thereto, the Acting Head of the Personnel Department at the Civil Service Board issued Decision No. 222/2 dated 7/6/2004 (Organisation of a competitive examination restricted to hourly

contractors...), which provided in Articles One, Two, and Three thereof as follows: "Article One: The Personnel Department at the Civil Service Board shall conduct, starting from Tuesday 27/7/2004, a competitive examination restricted to hourly contractors in public secondary schools and to those seconded to these secondary schools from among the instructors and teachers in primary and intermediate education for appointment to the post of secondary education teacher in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education in the following specialisations (......). Article Two: Conditions for participation in the competitive examination: 1 -... 2 -... 3 -... 4 -.... 5 - Contracted intermittently or continuously with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education for hourly teaching in public secondary schools pursuant to an annual contract drawn up in accordance with the rules and conditions contained in Decree No. 1360/71 and its amendments for the academic year 2001 - 2002 or prior thereto. Or a teacher or instructor in general education (primary and intermediate: the kindergarten and basic education stages) temporarily attached to a public secondary school on a full-time or part-time basis for the academic year 2001 - 2002 or prior thereto, provided that his attachment continued for the academic year 2001 - 2002 pursuant to an instrument issued by the Minister of Education and Higher Education or by the Director General of Education, or pursuant to an approval from the said Director General to perform teaching duties, administrative duties, or non-teaching duties of whatever kind. Article Three: Documents and time limit for submitting applications: 1 -... 2 -... 3 -... 4 -.... 5 - With respect to those seconded for teaching: - A certified copy of the instrument of attachment to the public secondary school issued by the Minister of Education and Higher Education or the Director General of Education for the academic year 2001 - 2002 or prior thereto. - A certificate issued by the principal of the secondary school to which the seconded person is attached, certified by the Directorate of Secondary Education, clearly stating: the subject or subjects which he taught or the tasks which were assigned to him during the period of attachment, and that his attachment to the secondary school continued for the academic year 2001 - 2002". Based on the foregoing, whereas Law No. 441/2002 relating to the restricted competitive examination is fundamentally an exceptional law constituting a departure from the general rules of employment expressed by the open competitive examination available to all citizens wishing to enter the public service on the basis of competition and equality of opportunity, as the competitive examination is considered the best means to select the most deserving and most competent, and this is expressly affirmed by the Lebanese Constitution in Articles /7/ and / 12/ thereof, which state verbatim: "- All Lebanese are equal before the law, and they equally enjoy civil and political rights and are bound by public obligations and duties without any distinction among them. - Every Lebanese has the right to hold public office, with no preference of one over another except in terms of merit and competence". And whereas the petitioning party elaborated at length in explaining the academic qualifications and practical experience she holds, and in presenting certain political aspects, commenting on the "contracting policy", and delving into matters unrelated to the substance of the case. And whereas Law No. 441/2004 issued on 29/7/ 2002 aimed in letter and spirit at addressing the worsening problem of contractors and seconded persons, by conducting a competitive examination restricted to them for one time only in order to resolve that issue radically, and it fundamentally did not legislate for the future, as it relates to granting a right to a specific and defined category of Lebanese, and was not characterised by comprehensiveness and generality so as to validly claim that its provisions extend to the future; rather, it is merely an exceptional and special law addressing the case of a specific category in their contractual or statutory capacity on the date of its issuance, which precludes the possibility of expanding the interpretation of this exception to cover other persons. And whereas "capacity" is one of the essential elements in determining the beneficiaries of a special and exceptional legal text, in accordance with the logical and objective interpretation of this text. And whereas it is required, for the acceptance of an application for candidacy by the Competitive Examinations Section at the Civil Service Board, that the applicant be among the beneficiaries of the provisions of the said Law, and specifically that he hold, with respect to the case at hand, the capacity of a seconded person on the date of issuance of Law No. 441/2002, and whereas, by way of digression, capacity is a necessary condition for the admissibility of the action. And whereas expanding the interpretation of the word "seconded" and generalising it as claimed by the concerned party in her interpretation of the word contained in Decree No. 12321/2004 in this respect, would allow all teachers and instructors to benefit from the provisions of Law No. 441/ 2002 after its issuance, by obtaining secondment decisions subsequent to the Law, and would also allow persons who were seconded prior to its issuance to benefit therefrom even though they did not hold the capacity of a seconded person on the date of its entry into force, because had the purpose been to include those seconded persons in the competitive examination, the implementing decree of Law No. 441/2002 issued under No. 12321/2004 would have provided for that clearly and expressly, just as it did with respect to hourly contractors, where it provided that the contracting must have been concluded with them in the academic year 2001 - 2002 or prior thereto. And holding contrary to the foregoing constitutes a distortion of the legislator's intent, an excess of power, a discrimination in their favour, and a compounded inequality towards other citizens holding university degrees in the specialisations required for appointment to the post of secondary education teacher. And whereas the conditions of secondment laid down by the Civil Service Board in the regulatory decision for the competitive examination No. 222/2 are not new additional conditions, but rather an application of the letter and spirit of Law No. 441 /2002 and the implementing decree pertaining thereto, and by virtue of its competence to organise the competitive examination pursuant to the provisions of Article /8/ of the Personnel Regulations. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board decided to dismiss the action for lack of a sound legal basis.

38 - Exceptional steps - Redress for holders of licences: In the matter concerning the extent of the entitlement of a former female teacher in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education holding the equivalence to the teaching licence, to the four exceptional steps provided for in Article One of Law No. 344 dated 6/8/2001 (Redress for holders of the licence and the competency who entered the cadre of public education), the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3932 dated 3/6/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as follows: Whereas Article /13/ of Legislative Decree No. 134 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Conditions of appointment in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education) provided for the following: "The appointment of teachers shall be subject to the following provisions: 1 - Holders of the Second Teaching Certificate or its equivalent shall be appointed without a competitive examination. 2 - There shall be appointed after them the successful candidates in a competitive examination organised for this purpose in which participate holders of the First Teaching Certificate who have practised teaching for three years at least, and holders of the Lebanese Baccalaureate Part Two or its equivalent who have practised teaching for five years at least. These teachers shall be appointed by decree as probationers for a period of one year at least and two years at most, at the end of which they shall be confirmed in their posts or dismissed from the service". And whereas it appears from the aforementioned legal provisions that the Second Teaching Certificate or its equivalent is one of the additional special conditions of appointment to the post of teacher in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education. Moreover, the candidate for the post of teacher may be an instructor in the teaching cadre in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education holding the First Teaching Certificate and having experience in teaching of three years at least or holding the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate or its equivalent with experience of five years at least in teaching, from which it is inferred that there are among the members of the teaching staff appointed to the post of teacher in the teaching cadre persons who do not hold the Second Teaching Certificate or its equivalent.
