Article 1: The section of the real estate area of Baasir (District of Chouf) shown on the attached map drawn at a scale of 1/4000 has been subjected to the following building regulations: - Surface exploitation ratio: 30% (thirty per cent). - Total exploitation factor: 60% (sixty per cent). - Number of storeys: 2 (two storeys) - Maximum height: 9.5 m (nine and a half metres). - Setback from roads: in accordance with the alignment and setback decree. - Lateral and rear setbacks: 5 m. (five metres). - Minimum area for subdivision 1200 m2 (one thousand two hundred square metres). Minimum frontage and minimum depth: 25 m. (twenty-five metres). - Existing plots suitable for building: * Minimum area after alignment: 500 m2 (five hundred square metres). * Minimum frontage and minimum depth: 15 m. (fifteen metres). * The construction of one basement storey is permitted provided that its area does not exceed the horizontal projection of the largest upper storey whatever its intended use may be, with the exception of underground passages to garages on condition that the width of such passages does not exceed the legal width.
Article 2: All previous texts of decrees, regulations, and decisions contrary to or inconsistent with the content of this Decree are repealed.
Article 3: This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

Surface exploitation rate and general exploitation factor:

First - Definition:

The surface exploitation rate is the ratio between the area of the horizontal projection of the building and the area of the real property, whereas the general exploitation factor is the ratio between the area of the building across all its floors calculated in the exploitation and the area of the real property.

The surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor shall be calculated:

1 - On the basis of the area of the real property after deducting the area affected by the approved alignment plan. In the event that the alignment plan divides the real property into several sections, each section shall be deemed as an independent real property for the calculation of the two exploitation factors.

2 - On the basis of the area of the real property including the section affected by the planned alignment plan (which has not been coupled with final approval), while complying with the setbacks from the alignment plan.

3 - Regardless of the existence of easements for the benefit of neighbouring real properties.

4 - In the event of the exhaustion of the exploitation factors in a given real property, it shall not be permissible to build on any section deducted therefrom, whatever the reasons for this deduction, even if it is in execution of an approved alignment plan.

Second - Parts of buildings whose area is not included in the calculation of the two exploitation factors and the number of floors:

1 - Balconies, verandas, loggias, roofed open spaces, and unenclosed roofs

1 - a) The area of unenclosed balconies, verandas, and loggias, and unenclosed roofed open spaces shall not be included in the calculation of the two exploitation factors to the extent that their total area does not exceed 20% (twenty percent) of the designed general exploitation area, provided that the area of balconies on any floor does not exceed 25% (twenty-five percent) of its designed area across all buildings, with the exception of industrial buildings in which the area of balconies must not exceed a proportion of 5% (five percent) of the area of each floor.

By designed general exploitation is meant the area requested to be licensed and which enters into the general exploitation factor.

The area of balconies, verandas, and loggias shall be calculated once, regardless of the height of their ceiling.

Within the meaning of this Decree, the following shall be deemed as:

* Balcony: The horizontal part projecting from the body of the building, connected to it from one side or two sides at most, and unenclosed.

* Veranda: The horizontal part projecting from the body of the building, connected to it from at least one side, resting on its other sides on columns resting on the natural ground, and unenclosed.

* Loggia: The horizontal part recessed into the body of the building, connected to it from three sides, and unenclosed from at least one side, provided that the width of the loggia is not less than its depth towards the inside of the building. The loggia may be connected to the body of the building on its unenclosed facade for a distance not exceeding one-third of the width of the facade, provided that it does not exceed one and a half metres.

* Paragraph added pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007 O.G. 50

By the glass curtains referred to in Article Twelve of Law No. 646 dated 11/12/2004 is meant all movable transparent glass panels, including those fitted with coloured aluminium frames.

The quality and colours of the glass curtains must be uniform on the facades overlooking the roads in the buildings that are licensed after the issuance of this Decree, provided that the specifications of these curtains are registered in the ownership regulations of the building.

1 - b) Within the meaning of this Decree, the following shall be deemed as:

* Roof: An unroofed horizontal area (pertaining to a common right).

* Terrace (Terrasse): An unroofed horizontal area appurtenant to a floor or an apartment (distinct right).

The area of terraces (Terrasses) and roofs shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor, and shall not be included in the calculation of the area of balconies, verandas, and loggias.

(See Drawings No. 56 and 57)

1 - c) The following shall be calculated within the area of the balconies referred to above:

* Technical areas for the floor, provided that these areas are connected to the common parts of the building and that their area does not exceed eight square metres.

* Corridors for access exclusively to the maid's room, the laundry room, and the pantry room, provided that the area of each of these rooms does not exceed eight square metres, and provided that these corridors do not lead to any other sections of the residential apartment, do not separate the various sections pertaining to this apartment, and their area does not exceed the area of the rooms to which they lead.

(See Drawing No. 58)

* Roofed corridors for access between the various buildings in the project, provided that the following conditions are met:

- That their clear width does not exceed 2.50 m (two and a half metres).

- That their height does not exceed the height of the floor and is not less than 2.20 m (two metres and twenty centimetres).

- That the number of corridors connecting two blocks does not exceed two, one of them on the ground or first floor and the other on one of the upper floors, subject to the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning with respect to the upper corridor.

- That these corridors secure communication between the common parts of the buildings and are registered within the common parts upon the subdivision of the real property.

The corridors referred to above shall not preclude the buildings from being deemed independent within the meaning of Item "Second" of Article Eleven of this Decree.

(See Drawings No. 59, 60 and 61)

1 - d) Unenclosed balconies, verandas, loggias, and roofed open spaces that are used for access to offices or apartments shall be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor.

2 - Basements:

2 - a - Backfilled basements:

2 - a - 1: In zones where the height and number of floors are specified

A floor shall be deemed a backfilled basement where it meets the following conditions:

* That the height of any section of its ceiling (concrete) does not exceed one metre above:

- The level of the natural or reclaimed (levelled) ground from all internal sides, with the exception of garage entrances that do not exceed the minimum width required to secure access to the garage.

(See Drawing No. 62)

- The line with which it intersects horizontally and which connects any two opposite points of the ground level of the real property after levelling alongside the facade of the building.

(See Drawings No. 63 and 64)

* The level of the line parallel to the road or the pavement, where it exists, and which rises above it by one metre for the front facades.

(See Drawing No. 65)

* If the basement is supported on one or more sides by backfill, the height of the backfill must not exceed three and a half metres above the natural ground, and its width must not be less than two metres.

(See Drawing No. 66)

* That the backfill results from the levelling of the sloping ground of the real property and is not an artificial backfill aimed at converting the floor in question into a basement in an artificial manner.

(See Drawing No. 67)

In certain cases necessitated by the requirement to secure the conditions of this Article, the Administration may impose certain levellings in the ground of the real property, in order to prevent the alteration of the intended use of the floors deemed to be basements.

The two-metre width of the backfill shall be measured from the external wall of the basement regardless of the positioning of the ground floor above it.

* When the ceiling of the basement steps into several levels, it is required:

- That the depth of the ceiling of any section of the basement be not less than twice the clear height of the said section, provided that the difference between the two levels does not exceed one metre. The depth of the ceiling shall be measured perpendicularly in the direction of the stepping.

(See Drawing No. 68)

- That the ceiling level of any of the sections of the basement remains between the levels of the two sections adjacent to it on two opposite sides.

(See Drawings No. 69 and 70)

* The erection of basements is permitted across the entire remaining area of the real property outside the mandatory setback from the road boundary or from the road alignment plan (unless special regulations provide otherwise) within the following conditions:

- If the natural ground level of the real property is higher than the ground level of the neighbouring real property, the height of the upper surface of the ceiling of the basement contiguous to the neighbouring real property must not exceed one metre above the natural ground level of this real property.

The following shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor:

* Backfilled basements or sections of basements in accordance with the above conditions, whatever their area, if they are allocated for use as car garages, storerooms for the service of the building, or for machinery pertaining to the service of the building such as heating and cooling.

* Basements or sections of basements allocated for uses other than the three preceding uses whose total area does not exceed (50%) of the general exploitation factor permitted in the zone, and anything in excess thereof shall be included in the general exploitation factor, with the exception of hotels, hospitals, and tourist establishments which by their nature require a basement area greater than that in all of the following cases:

- Hotels and tourist establishments, if the area of these sections of the basements is allocated for service uses and does not enter into the core area allocated for tourist exploitation.

- Hospitals, if the area of these sections of the basements is used for radiology (imaging or therapy), operating theatres, pharmacy, laboratories, cold rooms, archives, or electrical power transformer stations.

In the event of the existence of areas similar in their intended use to the areas specified above, approval for their exemption may be granted by a decision of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

Areas in the basements of these buildings allocated for uses other than those mentioned above shall be calculated within the fifty percent proportion of the general exploitation factor in the real property specified for these uses in the basements.

* The area of mezzanines erected within basements allocated for commercial uses shall be exempted from the proportion specified above if they meet the conditions for mezzanines referred to in Item "Third" - 3 below.

2 - a - 2: In zones where the number of floors is not specified:

In zones where the number of floors is not specified, and in addition to the basements that meet the conditions of the paragraph above, exposed floors shall be deemed basements, without taking into consideration the elevation of the ground of the neighbouring real properties, provided:

* That the number of basements exposed towards the neighbour's side does not exceed two.

* That the external height of the exposed section does not exceed 5 m (five metres) from the lowest point of the natural or levelled ground of the real property. This height shall be calculated within the maximum height of the building in the event that the approved regulations in the zone specify the maximum height of buildings.

* That the exposed sections of the basement remain outside the limits of the setbacks from the neighbouring real properties.

The fourth paragraph of Item Second 2 - a - 2 was repealed pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007 O.G. 50

Drawing 71 and the paragraph preceding it were moved to become 2 - a - 3 pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 / 2007

2-a - 3 - In the event that the ceiling level of the basement is lower than the ground level of the neighbouring real property, permission may be granted outside the projection of the building to reconstitute the natural or reclaimed ground by way of backfilling above the ceiling of the highest basement (first basement), provided that the height of the backfill does not exceed one metre above the ceiling of the basement.

(See Drawing No. 71)

2 - b - The exposed basement:

2 - b - 1 - In zones where the number of floors or the maximum height is specified:

The area of the exposed basement erected within the maximum permitted surface exploitation shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor in accordance with the following conditions:

* That the projection of the building for the exposed basement and the floors above it complies with the maximum permitted surface exploitation.

* That its height from the outside, including the thickness of the ceiling (concrete), does not exceed three and a half metres (3.50 m) from the level of the lowest point of the adopted ground of the real property in contact with any of its facades, provided that the width of the horizontal distance of the natural ground or the backfill of the levelled ground in contact with the facade is not less than two metres.

* That the height of its ceiling from the outside does not exceed one metre (1.00 m.) from the level of the lowest point of the adopted ground of the real property in contact with one of its facades, whether it is a rear or side facade. In this case, the backfill must cover the entire width of the facade and not be limited only to a part thereof.

* That its clear height does not exceed 3.50 m (three and a half metres).

(See Drawing No. 73)

* That the width of the entire backfilled facade is not less than 60% of the depth of the exposed section of the additional floor.

(See Drawing No. 74)

* That the difference between the ground levels in contact with the facades of the floor results from the slope of the natural ground at the building site and does not result from artificial and imported backfill to convert the ordinary ground floor into a backfilled floor on one of its facades.

* Balconies appurtenant to the exposed basement that do not exceed 20% of its area shall not be calculated within the two exploitation factors.

* The height of the exposed basement shall be calculated within the total height of the building.

* Hotel buildings exempted from the height and number of floors pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 402 dated 12/1/1995 and its extensions shall not benefit from this paragraph.

2 - b - 2 - In zones where the number of floors and the maximum height are not specified:

In the event of the erection of basements that are backfilled on at least one side and exposed on one or more sides, whatever their number, an area equivalent to a depth of four times its height on each floor for each exposed side shall be included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor in accordance with the following conditions:

* That the projection of the building for the exposed basement and the floors above it complies with the maximum permitted surface exploitation.

* That the exposed basement complies with the mandatory setback from the boundaries of the real properties.

* In the event that the side facades are partially exposed, an area equivalent to a depth of four times the height of the floor towards the side of the backfilled section of the facade shall be included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor.

(See Drawing No. 75)

In the event of a variation in the clear height of the sections of the basement calculated in the exploitation, the maximum clear height shall be adopted.

(See Drawing No. 76)

* Large complexes and hotel buildings exempted from the height and number of floors pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 402 dated 12/1/1995 and its extensions shall benefit from this paragraph.

3 - Projections intended for decoration and crowning, sunshades, cornices, canopies, and cladding thickness

The following shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor within the conditions specified for them in Article Eight of this Decree:

3 - a - Canopies (auvents) on the ground floor.

Provided that they do not project more than four metres from the body of the building.

3 - b - Sunshades Brise Soleil, cornices, means of decoration and beautification, and the cladding of the external facade walls of the building with natural stone, wood, or metals, provided that the thickness of the cladding does not exceed fifteen centimetres (15 cm) at most.

3 - c - Flower boxes

3 - c - 1 - Contiguous to balconies, loggias, or verandas):

60 cm of their width shall be calculated as a flower box and the remaining section shall be calculated within the balconies.

If the flower box is contiguous to the smaller side of the balcony and the level of its floor rises at least 50 cm above the level of the balcony, 120 cm of its width shall be calculated as a flower box and the remaining section shall be calculated within the balconies.

3 - c - 2 - Contiguous to rooms:

If the floor of the flower box is at the level of the floor of the room and its height does not exceed 1.00 m above this level, it shall not be included within the balconies provided that its width does not exceed 60 cm (sixty centimetres).

(See Drawings No. 77, 78 and 79)

4 - Rooms allocated for electrical power transformer stations:

Rooms allocated for electrical power transformer stations shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate, the general exploitation factor, and the number of floors, provided that they are not taken from the area intended for the garage, that they conform to the plan approved by the competent electricity authority, that they are located outside the limits of the setbacks imposed by law, with the exception of the access hatch to the room, and that they do not obstruct a right of way, car parking spaces, or the field of view. However, if the area of a single room exceeds the approved model, it shall be calculated in its entirety within the two exploitation factors.

5 - Sections of pitched tiled roofs and insulation works:

5 - 1 - Sections of pitched tiled roofs

Pitched tiled roofs shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate, the general exploitation factor, the number of floors, and the maximum height:

a - In zones whose special building regulations require the construction of a pitched tiled roof, provided that it complies with the conditions pertaining to it as provided for by these special regulations.

b - In zones whose regulations require the construction of a pitched tiled roof without specifying its technical conditions, and in zones whose special building regulations do not require the construction of a pitched tiled roof (provided that the number of floors of the building does not exceed four, excluding floors that are not included in the calculation of the exploitation factors and the number of floors), provided that the following conditions are complied with:

* That the height of the parapet wall erected above the roof of the top floor upon which the pitched tiled roof rests does not exceed one metre.

* That the slope of the pitched tiled roof relative to the horizontal plane is not less than 25 degrees, and that its maximum height does not exceed three metres. Sections of the pitched tiled roof whose height exceeds three metres shall be calculated within the general exploitation factor only.

* It is prohibited to subdivide the pitched tiled roof into distinct sections, and it shall be registered among the common parts of the building, even if the section whose height exceeds 3 m is included within the exploitation.

* That the proportion of ventilation and beautification openings does not exceed 10% (ten percent) of the length of the facade of the pitched tiled roof, without the width of each opening exceeding one metre and twenty centimetres.

(See Drawings No. 80 and 81)

Pitched tiled roofs that do not meet the conditions above with respect to the height of the parapet wall, the intended use, or the degree of slope shall be calculated in their entirety within the number of floors and the two exploitation factors.

5 - 2 - Waterproofing and thermal insulation works

Waterproofing and thermal insulation works whose height does not exceed fifty centimetres /50 cm/ above the roof of the top floor shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate, the general exploitation factor, the number of floors, and the maximum height.

(See Drawing No. 82)

6 - Area of transparent ceilings for open spaces:

The area of transparent ceilings for open spaces that meet the following conditions shall not be calculated within the surface exploitation rate and shall be calculated once in the general exploitation factor regardless of their height:

* That the entirety of the open spaces over which the field of view for the sections of the building is secured, in addition to the field of view for all sections lit via the open space, remain either uncovered or covered with transparent ceilings; consequently, it is prohibited to cover statutory open spaces and fields of view with any concrete or iron materials or any other non-transparent materials, with the exception of the load-bearing parts of the transparent ceiling.

* Licensing for the construction of transparent ceilings for open spaces is permitted in tourist, commercial, and distinctive residential buildings or sections of buildings, and others, following the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning in light of the submitted project and the reasonableness of the need for these ceilings, their height, and their uses.

The provisions of Article Seven and Article Nine of this Decree shall apply with respect to the envelope and the conditions for securing the field of view in the building, regardless of the transparent ceilings where they exist.

(See Drawing No. 83)

7 - Area of external walls:

In the event of the existence of a double wall for insulation, the area of the external walls (including the thickness of the insulation where it exists and the parts of columns located within the external walls) whose thickness ranges between twenty-two centimetres /22 cm/ and thirty-five centimetres /35 cm/ shall not be included within the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor, and anything in excess thereof shall be included in the calculation of the surface and general exploitation factors.

It is required that the width of the cavity separating the two walls be not less than 3 cm (three centimetres) and that the thickness of the external wall be not less than ten centimetres (10 cm). The width of the cavity separating the two walls may be reduced to 2 cm (two centimetres) for buildings licensed prior to the issuance of this Decree.

It is also required that the cavity (Z) between the double wall contain a thermally insulating material in the event that the real property is located at an altitude of more than 700 m above sea level.

In the event of benefiting from the provisions above, the glass in the external doors and windows must be of the double-glazed type.

In buildings subject to mandatory technical audit to secure public safety requirements, the commissioned technical audit offices shall remain responsible for verifying the execution of the double walls in accordance with the licensing plans.

The width of the double wall shall not include the thickness of the cladding that meets the conditions of Item 3 - b where it exists.

(See Drawing No. 84)

Paragraph added pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007

* The proportion of the area of the double wall compared to the area of the double glazing is unspecified and is subject to the wish of the party concerned.

To measure the thickness of the double glazing, the thickness of the wall containing the glass from both sides, or from the top (lintel) or from the bottom (sill), where it exists, shall be adopted.

8 - Staircase and lift

The internal area excluding the walls of the main staircase and the lift for each building or block shall not be calculated within the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor, provided:

* The clear width of the main staircase must not be less than 1.10 m (one metre and ten centimetres) and the clear width of the corridor leading from the lift to the apartments must not be less than 1.40 m (one metre and forty centimetres), provided that public safety conditions are met therein with respect to commercial and special buildings and large complexes; buildings licensed prior to the issuance of this Decree shall be exempted from the conditions of this paragraph.

* That their internal area excluding the walls does not exceed /20 m2/ twenty square metres, and anything in excess thereof shall be included in the calculation of the two exploitation factors.

* To the area specified above shall be added /6 m2/ six square metres for each additional lift, and anything in excess thereof shall be included in the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor.

(See Drawing No. 85) (Drawing 85 was replaced by a new one which must be inserted pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007)

* The area of staircases connecting the different levels in an independent unit (villa or duplex) shall be calculated within the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor.

* It is prohibited to subdivide the staircase and the lift into distinct sections; rather, they shall be registered among the common parts of the building, failing which their area shall be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor of the building.

* (This paragraph was repealed pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007 O.G. 50)

Third - Parts of buildings that are not included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor and the number of floors:

1 - Stairwells, lift shafts, and water tanks erected above the top roof

1 - a - It is required for stairwells, lift shafts, and water tanks erected above the top roof, in order that their area not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor, that the height of these structures not exceed:

* Three metres above the roof in buildings whose height does not exceed fifteen metres, unless their special regulations provide otherwise.

* Four and a half metres above the roof in other buildings, and that their area does not exceed thirty-five square metres for each unit composed of one stairwell and one lift, and fifteen square metres shall be added for each additional lift.

1 - b - There shall also not be included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor the area of the special tank required to be secured in accordance with the conditions for securing public safety in buildings, as well as ventilation, heating, and cooling machinery, solar energy collectors and the water tanks pertaining to them, and prefabricated water tanks pertaining to the apartments and floors of the building placed on the roof of the top floor, provided that their height above the roof does not exceed the height specified in paragraph 1 - a - above.

2 - Area of the janitor's quarters:

Up to thirty-five square metres /35 m2/ on the ground floor or the pilotis floor or between the ground and first floors for each block, whatever the nature of the other structures therein, provided that it remains within the common parts in the event of the subdivision of the building.

3 - Area of mezzanines:

Mezzanines shall not be included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor and the number of floors:

* Whose clear height does not exceed 1.90 m, erected above laundry rooms - ironing rooms - pantry rooms - servants' rooms - bathrooms - water closets - pantries (office) - internal corridors - apartment entrances - kitchens.

* - Whose clear height does not exceed 2.20 m, erected within shops and showrooms on the ground and first floors and storerooms in the basements, provided that their area does not exceed two-thirds of the area of these units including the staircase leading to them, and that they do not have any external entrance.

4 - Floors and parts of floors allocated for technical structures

The following shall not be included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor and the number of floors:

4 - a - The floor or the part of a floor that is used as a technical floor etage technique:

Provided that their clear height does not exceed one hundred and ninety centimetres (190 cm), and that only in buildings characterised by special specifications such as hospitals, hotels, and public buildings, and buildings in which the area of structures calculated in the exploitation factor exceeds 4000 m2 (four thousand square metres), or those in which the number of their floors calculated in the count of floors equals or exceeds eight above ground level excluding the pilotis floor.

More than one technical floor may be erected in buildings whose height exceeds 50 metres and whose number of floors exceeds twelve floors including the ground floor, at the rate of one technical floor for every eight additional floors, provided that there is attached to the building permit application file the technical engineering study that justifies the increase in the number of technical floors, and that it is verified prior to the granting of the occupancy permit that these floors contain the extensions of the various technical networks (sanitary, water, electricity, telephone, etc...) that necessitated their erection.

In the event that the building permit includes more than one technical floor, the permit shall be subject to the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

4 - b - Areas used for technical installations:

Within lightwells, as well as corridors and staircases within lightwells that contain technical installations while observing public safety conditions, and provided that the clear area of the lightwell free of any structures is not less than the minimum area required to secure ventilation or lighting for the units connected to the lightwell in accordance with Item Third of Article Nine of this Decree.

(See Drawing No. 86)

It is prohibited to subdivide the floors and parts of floors allocated for technical structures, and in the event of the subdivision of the building, these structures shall remain within the common parts of the building.

5 - Area of a pilotis floor:

5 - a - Erected within the horizontal projection of the largest upper floor

Permission may be granted for the erection of a single pilotis floor in the building within the horizontal projection of the largest upper floor including balconies, verandas, loggias, and internal lightwells:

1 - Either above the backfilled basements.

2 - Or directly above the natural ground.

3 - Or at the level of the road contiguous or adjacent to the building overlooking it, within a tolerance of one metre at most above or below the level of the road, provided that no structures are erected between the building and the road.

By the road contiguous or adjacent to the building, within the meaning of paragraph - 3 - above, is meant a vehicular road defined as follows:

* A public road (public domain).

* A private road defined and numbered on the cadastral map, from which the real property on which the building is erected benefits.

* A right of way established on the cadastral map, from which the real property on which the building is erected benefits.

If the facade of the building is located on a sloping road:

* The level of the road shall be taken at the midpoint of the entire facade of the building on the road to calculate the tolerance set out in paragraph - 3 - above.

(See Drawing No. 87)

* However, if the facade of the building is located on a sloping road and the length of the facade exceeds thirty metres, the pilotis floor may be in the form of successive steps, provided that the length of the facade of each step towards the side of the road is thirty metres at most, and the average level of this step shall be taken relative to the level of the road, while observing the number of floors and the maximum height imposed within the regulations of the zone.

(See Drawing No. 88)

Within the pilotis floor, in an area not exceeding 5% (five percent) of the general exploitation rate, there are permitted the main entrance of the building, a stairwell and lift shaft, electricity and water meter rooms, a waiting corner, a meeting hall for the occupants of the building, a small storeroom for the service of the building whose area does not exceed four square metres (4 m2), an information room, water tanks, a bathroom, as well as a main staircase, a generator room, and an electrical power transformer room; anything in excess thereof shall be calculated in the general exploitation factor without calculating it in the number of floors if the floor does not include any other uses.

The area of the janitor's quarters referred to in the Item above shall be included within the proportion specified for the structures permitted on the pilotis floor, even if it is located between the ground and first floors.

It is prohibited to subdivide the contents of these sections of the pilotis floor into distinct private sections; rather, they shall be registered among the common parts of the building.

The enclosed structures within the pilotis floor must remain within the projection of the external perimeter of the largest upper floor, including enclosed balconies, verandas, loggias, and internal lightwells.

The pilotis floor shall be included in the calculation of the total height of the building, provided that its clear height does not exceed three and a half metres, and this height may be exceeded up to /4.5 m/ four and a half metres only in buildings that meet the conditions for the erection of a technical floor without benefiting from the said floor.

This height may be raised following the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning in accordance with what is required by the design of the following buildings:

* Entrances of hospital buildings.

* Entrances of hotel buildings.

* Entrances of public buildings.

* Entrances of opera, theatre, and conference buildings.

* Exposed columns (Pilotis) within the base (Galette) of high-rise buildings whose height exceeds 50 metres in accordance with Item Fifth of Article Ten of this Decree.

The pilotis floor may exceed the projection of the upper building without exceeding the surface exploitation rate, provided that the sections thereof located outside the projection of the upper building are allocated as a mandatory car garage, that they are located towards the rear side of the building, and that its clear height does not exceed two metres and thirty centimetres (2.30 m), and it is also required that its roof not be used for any purpose.

(See Drawings No. 89 and 90)

Fourth - The provisions of the Article above shall apply to all new buildings, namely those not holding an occupancy permit

However, in the event of an application for a permit to add an additional building area to an existing building holding an occupancy permit, the provisions of the Article above shall apply to the added parts. A permit for the construction of mezzanines pertaining to shops, showrooms, and storerooms shall be deemed as a new permit even if the shop, showroom, or storeroom holds a habitation permit.

Maternity Leave:

A pregnant female employee shall be granted leave with full salary called maternity leave, the maximum duration of which is forty days, and maternity leave shall not be included in the calculation of administrative leave nor in the calculation of sick leave. The provisions of the local labour and social security law shall apply to a female employee affiliated with the local social security and benefiting from its full benefits.

1 - Maternity leave shall be granted all at once without division when the applicant therefor is about to give birth.

2 - In order to be granted maternity leave, the female employee must submit a special application containing the following:

a - The start and end dates of the leave.

b - The approximate date of delivery according to the physician's report. A female employee who has been granted maternity leave shall not be entitled to submit medical sick reports during the maternity leave, nor shall she be entitled to divide this leave.

Health Leave:

An employee shall be entitled to be absent for health reasons, provided that he informs the Head of the Mission immediately of his current address and of the reasons calling for the absence, and deposits with the Mission a medical report stating the nature of the illness and specifying the duration of the absence, and the Head of the Mission shall be entitled to delegate a physician to examine the person concerned and draw up a report on him. An employee absent for health reasons shall receive full salary for the first month and half salary for the second month, and his salary shall cease entirely if his absence exceeds a period of two months during a year.

In the event that the health leave exceeds a period of two months, the Head of the Mission may appoint a temporary replacement employee for him, and his right to return to service before the expiry of one year from the start date of the health leave shall be preserved.

The provisions of the labour and social security law relating to health leave shall apply to an employee affiliated with the local social security and benefiting from its full benefits.

The Authority Vested with the Right to Grant Leave

a - Administrative and family leave: The Head of the Mission shall have the right to decide on the matter of administrative and family leave in accordance with the requirements of work, provided that the Administration is notified with copies of the decisions relating to this matter.

b - Leave without pay, and health leave: The Head of the Mission shall prepare a draft decision in this regard and deposit it with the Central Administration, and the decision shall not become effective until it is coupled with the approval of the Director of Administrative and Financial Affairs.

Enrolment of Local Employees in Social Security:

Employees shall be subject to the local social security system, the prescribed percentage shall be deducted monthly from their salaries, and the Mission shall pay on their behalf the obligations imposed on employers under the following conditions:

1 - The Central Administration shall be notified, prior to enrolling the employees in the social security, with a copy of the social security system in force locally.

2 - That the Mission obtains the prior approval of the Secretary-General.

3 - In the event of approval of the principle of enrolling employees in the social security in any Mission, no employee may be exempted from subscription unless local laws prohibit that.

4 - An employee affiliated with the social security shall not be entitled to receive dismissal compensation from the Mission's fund if the social security grants him this compensation or if it entitles him to a retirement pension.

5 - An employee shall not be entitled to receive compensation or salary for leave of whatever kind if such leave is paid for by the social security.

6 - An employee not affiliated with the social security for the reasons mentioned above shall receive a monthly allowance amounting to 7% of his salary as a social allowance, and this allowance shall not be included in the calculation of the end-of-service indemnity.

7 - The amounts due as a result of enrolling employees in the social security or from paying the lump-sum monthly allowance shall be paid from the item of salaries of local employees.

Transitional Provisions:

The Mission must notify the Ministry of the laws or regulations issued in the host country relating to the regularisation of the status of violators of the provisions of social security regulations, the possibility of benefiting therefrom, and the expected cost resulting from putting them into effect.

Termination of Service The service of a local employee shall terminate in the following two cases:

- Resignation.

- Dismissal from service.

Resignation at the Request of the Employee:

1 - An employee may submit a written resignation to the Head of the Mission, and he must continue to perform his duties until the Head of the Mission decides on his application after the approval of the Secretary-General. The appointment of a replacement employee prior to being notified of the Ministry's approval of the draft dismissal decision shall be the responsibility of the Head of the Mission.

2 - If the resignation is not rejected within two months from the date of its submission, it shall be deemed accepted by operation of law.

3 - An employee whose resignation is accepted in accordance with the conditions mentioned above shall benefit from the dismissal compensation.

4 - A resigned employee may not be reinstated in service unless he fulfils all the conditions of appointment except for the age requirement, and in this case he shall be reinstated in his former rank and step if a full year has not elapsed since he left work, and his advancement in step shall be delayed in proportion to the period during which he was absent from work. In the event that more than one year has elapsed since his resignation, he may be reappointed in the lowest step of his category, provided that he fulfils all the conditions of appointment as of the date of his reinstatement in service, except for the age requirement.

Cases in Which an Employee is Deemed to Have Resigned:

1 - The following shall be deemed to have resigned:

a - An appointed employee who fails to assume his duties without a legitimate reason within fifteen days from the date of being notified of the decision of his appointment.

b - An employee who absents himself from his work without legal leave and fails to resume his work within ten days from the date of his absence from work.

c - An employee who fails to resume his work after the expiry of ten days from the end date of his leave.

2 - An employee shall be deemed to have resigned by a decision of the Head of the Mission after the approval of the Secretary-General.

3 - No dismissal compensation shall be due to an employee deemed to have resigned.

4 - In exceptional cases and after examining the file of the employee deemed to have resigned, he may be reinstated in service if he fulfils all the conditions of appointment.

An employee deemed to have resigned and reinstated in service shall be appointed in the same category and step if more than one year has not elapsed since his resignation, and his advancement in step shall be delayed in proportion to the period during which he was absent from work.

And he shall be reappointed in the lowest step of his category after the lapse of one year from his leaving work.

Dismissal from Service A local employee shall be dismissed from service in the following cases:

- Attainment of the legal age.

- Professional incompetence.

- Gross breach of one of his professional duties.

Termination of an Employee's Service by Operation of Law Due to Attainment of Age:

1 - An employee affiliated with the local social security who has completed the age prescribed for cessation of work in accordance with the local law in the host State, which has a mandatory character for workers in foreign missions, shall be dismissed from service. In the event that this age is below sixty-four, the service of employees may be extended year by year, up to the age of sixty-four, pursuant to reasoned decisions by the Head of the Mission, provided that the local law does not prohibit keeping them in service, and after the approval of the Secretary-General.

2 - The service of each of a cook, a driver, and a servant may be extended year by year up to the age of seventy if he still enjoys the physical and mental ability to continue working, provided that local laws do not prohibit that.

Professional Incompetence:

1 - An employee shall be dismissed from service if it is proven to the Head of the Mission that he does not possess the basic knowledge indispensable for the proper performance of his duties, or if he is afflicted with an infirmity or illness that prevents him from performing his duties.

2 - An employee who has been dismissed for professional incompetence may not be reinstated in service, nor may he be appointed in another Lebanese mission.

3 - An employee dismissed for professional incompetence shall receive the dismissal compensation provided for in these Regulations.

Disciplinary Responsibility and Disciplinary Penalties:

1 - The Head of Mission may take measures against the employee in the event of a breach by him of the conditions of work, provided that the measure taken is commensurate with the nature and ruling of the violation, in accordance with the following provisions:

a - Disciplinary Responsibility:

The employee shall be deemed responsible from the disciplinary standpoint and shall be subject to disciplinary penalties if he breaches, intentionally or through negligence, the duties stipulated in the Ninth Article.

b - Disciplinary Penalties:

- Reprimand.

- Salary deduction from one day to fifteen days by a reasoned decision approved by the Secretary-General.

- Delay of advancement for a period of three months at most.

- Dismissal from service. These penalties shall apply to anyone who violates the provisions of the Ninth and Tenth Articles of these Regulations.

2 - Each time a violation occurs, the Head of Mission shall address to the employee a written warning setting out the violations therein, the receipt of which the employee shall sign; in the event that he refuses to sign, the assistant accountant and another employee shall declare this on the warning sheet as proof of the employee's failure to sign after having taken cognisance of the warning. A copy of the warning shall be notified to the Central Administration.

3 - An employee dismissed in accordance with the last penalty mentioned in this Article shall forfeit his right to dismissal compensation, and under no circumstances may he be reinstated to service in any of the Lebanese missions abroad.

The service of the employee shall be terminated by a decision of the Head of Mission after the approval of the Secretary-General in any of the cases of termination of service mentioned in these Regulations.

Dismissal Compensation:

1 - Dismissal compensation shall be due to the employee if he has completed at least twelve months of actual service.

2 - Dismissal compensation shall be liquidated on the basis of one month's salary for each year of actual service, and a month shall be calculated as one-twelfth of a year, and a day as one-thirtieth of a month.

3 - In liquidating the compensation, the salary of the last month shall be adopted, provided that it does not exceed the salary of the first step of the employee's category, and in this case the salary of the first step of his category shall be adopted regardless of the amount of his salary.

4 - The value of the compensation due to a deceased employee shall be disbursed in the name of the heirs after obtaining a judgment of determination of heirs.

1 - The mission must observe the mandatory local labour regulations that form part of the public order of the host State, and it may, where necessary, draw up employment contracts for its local employees, each of which shall be signed by the Head of Mission, on behalf of the mission, and the local employee concerned.

2 - The employment contract shall include all the provisions of the Regulations for Local Employees in Lebanese Missions Abroad that do not conflict with the mandatory local labour regulations, on the one hand, and the provisions of the mandatory local labour regulations adopted in the host State, on the other hand.

3 - In missions that will draw up employment contracts for their local employees, the Head of Mission shall prepare a model contract in the local and Arabic languages, deposit it with the Central Administration, and attach thereto the texts of the mandatory local labour regulations, for the purpose of studying it and introducing the necessary amendments thereto, after which it shall be returned to the mission accompanied by the approval of the Secretary-General thereon. The mission shall adopt this model contract in all employment contracts with its employees.

4 - The Head of Mission shall deposit with the Central Administration the draft decisions for the appointment of local employees in accordance with the provisions of the Sixth Article of these Regulations, and shall attach thereto their employment contracts signed by them and by him, in order to obtain the approval of the Secretary-General thereon.

5 - Employment contracts drawn up in accordance with the provisions of this Article shall be deemed effective after the approval of the Secretary-General of the draft appointment decisions.

Transitional Provisions :

Employees currently working in the missions shall retain their statuses and the positions to which they were appointed until the termination of their services, provided that the status of those who meet the conditions is regularised so as to conform with the provisions of the new establishment in each mission.

Final Provisions:

Decision No. 9/14 issued on 11/3/1996 (Regulations for Local Employees in Lebanese Missions Abroad) and Decision No. 153/14 dated 20/9/2001 (Amending Decision 9/14 dated 11/3/1996) and every text contrary to the provisions of these Regulations are hereby repealed.
This Decision shall be published and notified where needed and shall enter into force as of 1/9/2006.
