This Decree regulates the operations of importation, exportation, sale, manufacturing, filling and packaging of dietary supplements and natural products having health benefits, the formation of the committee concerned with the entry of natural medicinal products and dietary supplements, and the determination of the remuneration for its sittings.

There shall be formed, by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of Health, the concerned Committee, composed of:

- The Director General of the Ministry of Public Health - Chairman.

- The Head of the Sanitary Engineering Department - Member.

- The Head of the Chemistry Branch in the Directorate of Health Laboratories - Member.

- The Head of the Drug Importation and Exportation Section at the Ministry of Public Health - Member.

- A representative of the Fanar Laboratory - Member (proposed by the Agricultural Research Institute).

- A licensed pharmacist representing the Order of Pharmacists - Member.

- A physician specialised in nutrition representing the Order of Physicians - Member.

- A nutrition specialist practising at one of the university hospitals (selected by the Minister of Public Health) - Member.

- A pharmacology specialist (selected by the Minister of Public Health from among holders of a doctoral degree) - Member.

- A lecturing nutrition specialist representing one of the major universities (by rotation) - Member.

The naming of the representatives of the Orders and universities shall take place on the basis of a list proposed by the concerned body containing 3 to 5 names fulfilling the conditions specified in this Decree, one of whom shall be selected by the Minister of Public Health. The decision shall also appoint a rapporteur for the Committee who shall attend its sittings and assume the receipt of applications from the concerned parties, the verification of their documents, the preparation of the minutes of the sittings, and the provision of the printing of resolutions, their notification to the concerned parties, and their filing in due form.
Decisions in the Committee shall be taken by a majority, and in the event of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

The Committee shall hold its meetings periodically within or outside official working hours, and each of the Chairman, members and rapporteur of the Committee shall receive an attendance allowance in the amount of 80.000 L.L. (eighty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for each sitting, provided that the attendance allowance is paid at a maximum rate of four sittings per month, and the civil servants among them shall not receive any remuneration for sittings held during official working hours.

Before commencing the examination of the files submitted to it, the Committee shall determine the bases and criteria for classifying the preparations and placing them in the following categories:

- Dietary items.

- Vitamins and minerals.

- Concentrated foods.

- Foods for athletes.

- Non-drug stimulants and energy drinks.

- Natural plants and herbs having health benefits.

The Committee shall lay down the maximum safe permissible limits in addition to the technical conditions for permitting the preparation to be sold by free sale, imposing its sale in pharmacies, or considering it outside the scope of this Decree and rejecting the application, and shall also follow up on updating these conditions, provided that this classification does not conflict with the laws in force.

The Committee shall issue its proposals or the required updates in order that they be adopted pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry of Public Health.

The tasks of the Committee in regulating the activities provided for in the Second Article of this Decree shall be determined in accordance with the following:

- Examining applications submitted to the Ministry of Public Health to permit the importation and sale of dietary supplements and natural products having health benefits, and taking the appropriate decision thereon.

- Examining applications submitted to the Ministry of Public Health to permit the filling and packaging of dietary supplements and natural products having health benefits, and taking the appropriate decision thereon.

- Examining applications submitted to the Ministry of Public Health to permit the manufacturing of dietary supplements and natural products having health benefits, and taking the appropriate decision thereon.

- Examining applications submitted to the Ministry of Public Health to permit the exportation of dietary supplements and natural products having health benefits, and taking the appropriate decision thereon.

- Examining applications submitted to the Ministry of Public Health to permit the advertising of dietary supplements and natural products having health benefits across all advertising media, whether audio, visual, written, electronic or leaflets, and taking the appropriate decision thereon.

- Drawing up a list of substances the circulation of which is prohibited internationally, and renewing it whenever the need arises.

The application for an importation licence shall be submitted to the Ministry of Public Health - Directorate General, accompanied by the following documents:

1 - A written application stating the name, address and telephone number of the licence applicant, or the name of the company or establishment, its address, and the name of the person authorised to sign on its behalf and his telephone number.

2 - An individual civil status extract or a copy of the identity card of the applicant.

3 - A recent judicial record of the applicant proving that its holder has not been convicted of a felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour.

4 - A certificate of registration with the Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

5 - A certificate of registration of a commercial establishment or company.

6 - A commercial circular.

7 - Proof of ownership, lease or right of exploitation of the warehouse or premises in which storage is requested.

8 - An undertaking to advance the expenses of the necessary studies, research and tests.

9 - A certificate of Good Manufacturing Practice for the producing factory issued by the competent official authority in the country of the factory.

10 - An introductory letter regarding the manufacturing company or the holder of the marketing authorisation stating its name, its commercial form, the date of its establishment, the persons authorised to sign on its behalf, its address, a list of the preparations that it markets, and the countries in which these preparations are marketed. The following documents shall also be submitted for each preparation:

11 - A certificate from the manufacturing company or the holder of the marketing authorisation regarding the contents of the preparation, the proportion of each of these contents therein, and the shelf life.

12 - A certificate of analysis with the methods of analysis.

13 - A certificate from the manufacturing company or the holder of the marketing authorisation regarding the countries to which the preparation has been authorised to be exported.

14 - A certificate of free sale in the country of the manufacturing company or the country of the holder of the marketing authorisation, issued by the competent official authorities.

15 - Two samples of the requested preparation.

The required documents shall be duly legalised by the competent official authority and by the Embassy or Consulate of Lebanon in the country from which they are issued. The Committee shall be entitled to request any additional document that it deems necessary.

Preparations manufactured, filled or packaged locally shall be exempted from the documents required under items 9 - 10 - 12 - 14 of the Seventh Article, which shall be replaced by the following documents:

1 - A list of the substances used in the composition of the preparation.

2 - A certificate of origin for the raw materials used, duly legalised.

3 - A certificate from the company producing the raw materials regarding the shelf life of these materials, duly legalised.

4 - A certificate of analysis and methods of analysis issued by an officially recognised laboratory.
The factory where the operation of manufacturing, filling or packaging takes place must be legally licensed.

The conditions of Good Manufacturing Practice must be met at the factory in accordance with the provisions of the decision determining the rules of Good Manufacturing Practice for drugs.

The application of these conditions shall be confirmed pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Public Health on the basis of an inspection carried out by the Sanitary Engineering Department, and shall be renewed annually in the event that the application of the conditions continues.

It is prohibited to bring in, manufacture or sell any of the preparations concerned by this Decree in the Lebanese markets except after obtaining a prior licence from the Minister of Public Health based on the decision of the competent Committee.

Entry permits shall be endorsed by the Head of the Sanitary Engineering Department at the Ministry of Public Health.

Advertising and publicity across all advertising media for the preparations that are the subject of this Decree are prohibited except after obtaining a prior licence from the Minister of Public Health based on the decision of the competent Committee.

The Committee shall decide on every application submitted to it within a period of three months, failing which the Minister shall be entitled to authorize importation, marketing and manufacturing by the applicant pending the Committee's decision on the application, and in the event of rejection of the preparation, reasons must be stated therefor.

The applicant shall be entitled to lodge an objection before the Committee within a time limit of 4 weeks from his notification of the rejection, and he shall also be entitled to submit a reasoned application for reconsideration after the lapse of more than 6 months from his notification of the rejection.

Import licences granted in accordance with Decree No. 11710 dated 22/1/1998 shall remain in force except in the event that the Committee established pursuant to this Decree requests the reconsideration thereof due to new or supervening data.
Decree No. 11710 dated 22/1/1998 is hereby repealed.
This Decree shall be published and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Decree No. 14293 dated 11/3/2005 is amended to read as follows:

On Definitions:

For the application of the provisions of this Decree, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

1 - Technical Audit: is the inspection, review and examination of the design and execution of structures, materials and equipment elements used within the framework of the construction operation on the basis of the technical specifications required to be adopted in this operation and the expression of the appropriate opinions in this regard with a view to contributing to the prevention of risks.

2 - Technical Auditor: is the natural or legal person accredited by the public authority and requested by the employer to carry out technical audit assignments.

3 - Technical Audit Assignment: is that which is defined by virtue of its nature or the fields of its intervention. The nature of this assignment is characterised by the selection of the technical risks that must be avoided. The fields of intervention cover the entirety of the structures and equipment elements that are the subject of the assignment.

4 - Construction Operation: the design and execution of new buildings or the execution of civil engineering structures or new works on existing buildings or structures.

5 - Employer: is the natural or legal person for whose benefit the construction operation is carried out.

6 - Builder: is the employer and anyone who carries out design and execution works, including an engineer, a technical engineering office, a contractor, a technician, or any person bound to the employer by a contract for works.

7 - Manufacturer: is every natural or legal person who manufactures parts of structures, equipment elements, structures or materials for the purpose of installing them in a given building.

8 - Insured: is the policyholder, the employer, or the successive owners of the structure for whose benefit the insurance is concluded. Or the person duly authorised by them.

9 - Total Area: is the sum of the areas of the basement floors, the ground floor and all upper floors after deducting the area of parking garages.

10 - Approved Standards and Specifications: are the mandatory national standards and specifications. And in the absence thereof. They shall be the standards and specifications approved in the Member States of the European Union. The United States of America or Canada.

11 - Rules of the Profession: are the rules, regulations and technical provisions established by professional bodies representing the sectors concerned.

12 - Structure: is in general the building or any civil engineering structure (ouvrage de genie civil) the execution of which is requested by the employer within the framework of a given construction operation.

13 - Equipment Elements That Do Not Form an Integral Part of the Structure: are the equipment elements that can be removed, dismantled or replaced without damaging the structure or removing any of its materials.

14 - Equipment Elements That Form an Integral Part of the Structure: are the equipment elements that cannot be removed, dismantled or replaced without damaging the structure or removing any of its materials.

15 - Existing Buildings and Structures: those that are existing or that are under construction.

16 - Adjoining Buildings and Structures: those contiguous to the structure that is the subject of the construction operation or the structures designated by name in the technical audit contract.

17 - Responsible Engineer: is the engineer referred to in the Building Law and its amendments. The limits of his liability shall be in accordance with the legal rules and the regulations in force.

Public Safety Requirements in the Construction Sector:

The public safety requirements in construction operations include all measures and procedures that must be provided. To ensure the structural soundness of buildings and structures and the safety of their occupants and users, for the three basic assignments set forth in Chapter Two of Annex No. (1) attached to this Decree.

Technical Standards and Specifications Relating to Ensuring Public Safety Requirements in Buildings and Structures:

The technical standards and specifications adopted shall be those set forth in the definition of Approved Standards and Specifications in accordance with Article One (Item Ten) of this Decree. All of them shall be mandatory in nature, provided that a single source is adopted for each subject of the public safety subjects.

With regard to the subject of earthquake resistance, a horizontal acceleration factor (Acceleration horizontale) of at least 0.25g shall be adopted, and in the event that this acceleration is used within the American specifications, the seismic-resistant design conditions and details approved for moderate seismic risk zones (Moderate Seismic Risk) may be adopted as a minimum.

On Application:

1 - In New Buildings and Structures: the provisions of this Decree shall apply to all public and private building projects that have not yet obtained a building permit on the date of issuance of this Decree, including the modification of or addition of a building to existing buildings or the modification of the intended use of a building or a part thereof even if the modification does not include an increase in areas. They shall also apply to all new public and private structures. - The adoption of soil investigation (core drilling) shall be mandatory when preparing structural studies for the erection of all structures subject to mandatory technical audit, bridges and dams.

2 - In Existing Buildings and Structures or Those Under Construction:

A - The public safety provisions for lift installations shall apply in existing buildings and structures in accordance with what is specified in Annex No. 3 attached to this Decree.

B - Prior to the expiry of the time limits referred to in Annex No. 2., the owners of buildings and structures subject to the provisions of this Article must submit to the municipality concerned a certificate issued by an accredited technical audit office confirming compliance with the provisions of this Article, with the exception of lift installations subject to Paragraph (A) above.

3 - The employer may not commence the execution of any licensed building or structure except after obtaining an order to commence execution from the Responsible Engineer registered with the Order of Engineers and Architects so as to enable the latter to carry out his responsibilities in supervising and monitoring execution in due form. Provided that the owner of the real property submits at least the contracting agreement for the building's structural framework to the municipality concerned prior to the actual commencement of the execution of the works.

4 - The owner (or the association of owners), shall be deemed responsible for applying the public safety requirements in buildings and structures. Particularly with respect to the structural soundness of the building and the periodic maintenance of the buildings and their installations, in accordance with the provisions of the Building Law.

5 - In the event of the addition of a building to an existing building or a modification in the intended use of the building, the owner (or the association of owners), the Responsible Engineer, the contractor and the manufacturer shall be deemed responsible, each in so far as he is concerned, for applying the public safety requirements in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article, especially with respect to the safety of persons, earthquake resistance, the structural soundness of the building, its capacity to bear the required modification or addition, and its observance of the conditions of the new intended use.

6 - In the event of the addition of a building to an existing building or a modification in the intended use, and if it proves impossible to obtain a certificate of conformity from a technical audit office for some of the fire prevention provisions, the employer may seek the assistance of a Category One technical audit office to express an opinion and provide the appropriate solutions, provided that these solutions are submitted to the Auditors Accreditation Committee concerned in this Decree, and it shall be for this Committee to give the final opinion, whether by rejecting or accepting the exemption.

Objective This Decree aims to determine the procedures governing the environmental impact assessment of public and private projects in order to avoid significant environmental consequences likely to occur during the construction, operation, and decommissioning of the said projects.

Definitions:

The following words and expressions, wherever they appear in this Decree, shall have the meanings assigned to each of them:

Environment: The natural (i.e. physical, chemical, and biological) and social surroundings in which all living organisms live, and the systems of interaction within the surroundings, within the organisms, and between the surroundings and the organisms.

Environmental Impact Assessment: Identifying, estimating, and assessing the impacts of a project intended to be constructed on the environment, and designating the necessary measures to mitigate negative impacts and increase positive impacts on the environment and natural resources, prior to giving the decision to approve or reject the project (Environmental Impact Assessment)

Environmental Consequences: The repercussions of the project on the environment during its construction, operation, and decommissioning.

Initial Environmental Examination: A preliminary study aimed at identifying the potential environmental impacts of a project in order to determine the necessity of conducting an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study for the project. (initial Environmemtal Examination)

Environmental Management Plan: The set of mitigative measures, monitoring and control means, and institutional procedures taken during the construction, operation, or decommissioning of the project which would eliminate negative environmental impacts or reduce them to locally acceptable levels, if any, and otherwise in accordance with United Nations standards. The "Environmental Management Plan" shall be considered an integral part of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report and the "Initial Environmental Examination" report (Environmental Management Plan).

Environmental Impact Assessment Scoping: The process of communication between the project proponent, the competent official administrations, and the concerned public with the aim of determining (1) the boundaries of the environmental impact assessment study, (2) the significant issues, (3) the information necessary for preparing the report, (4) the significant impacts that must be studied (EIA Scoping).

Project: - The execution of construction works or other installations which may have significant impacts on the environment.

- Any intervention in the natural surroundings, including those involving the extraction or addition of natural resources, which may have significant impacts on the environment as a result of its construction, operation, or decommissioning.

Significant Impact: To determine the significance of the impact, the following elements shall be taken into consideration: the type of impact, its magnitude, its nature, its extent, its timing, its duration, the probability of its occurrence, and its reversibility.

Project Proponent: - The natural or legal person from the private sector who applies for a permit to establish his project.

- The official administration that initiates a specific project.

Permit: The fundamental decision given by the competent official administrations and/or the receipt of declaration which authorises a project proponent to commence the construction or operation of his proposed project.

Official Administration: Public administrations and/or public institutions and/or municipalities and/or unions of municipalities.

Annex No. 1: List of projects that mandatorily require an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study.

Annex No. 2: List of projects that mandatorily require: an "Initial Environmental Examination", with the exception of projects located within an area specified in Annex No. 3 or that may have a significant impact on such an area, whereby these projects shall be subject to an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study.

Annex No. 3: List of Lebanese areas considered environmentally sensitive with respect to any project.

Annex No. 4: The screening form for "Environmental Impact Assessment" which must be filled out by the project proponent and pursuant to which the Ministry of Environment classifies the project.

Annex No. 5: List of potential stakeholders.

Annex No. 6: List of information required in the "Initial Environmental Examination" report.

Annex No. 7: List of information required in the report relating to the scoping of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" (Scoping Report).

Annex No. 8: List of information required in the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report.

Annex No. 9: Flow chart of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" system.

Scope of the Project:

(1) It is prohibited to submit the project before the competent official administrations in stages in a manner that prevents its accurate classification, and in this case, the "Initial Environmental Examination" or the "Environmental Impact Assessment" study submitted for a fragmented project shall be considered null and void.

(2) Any modification, addition, expansion, rehabilitation, or decommissioning of an existing project, or one holding a permit if it is a private project, or approved if it is a public project, which may result in significant environmental impacts, shall be subject to the provisions of this Decree.

Procedures for Requesting Approval of the Environmental Impact Assessment:

(1) The private project proponent shall submit to the competent official administration an application to be informed of the classification of his project in accordance with the approved form set out in Annex No. 4, together with the supporting documents required by the Ministry of Environment. The competent official administration shall, after registering the application with it, refer it to the Ministry of Environment, with the exception of what falls within the scope of work of the industrial licensing committees at the Ministry of Industry and the health councils in the governorates, where the applicable procedures shall apply.

(2) The official administration shall submit to the Ministry of Environment an application to be informed of the classification of its project or a project executed on its behalf in accordance with the approved form set out in Annex No. 4, together with the supporting documents required by the Ministry of Environment.

Classification of the Project:

(1) The Ministry of Environment, taking into consideration what is stated in Paragraph (1) of Article Four of this Decree, upon receiving the classification application for a proposed project in accordance with the approved form with its documents, shall verify whether the project is listed in Annex No. 1 or No. 2, or is located in an area set out in Annex No. 3, or has the possibility of having a significant impact on such an area.

(2) The Ministry of Environment shall notify the competent official administration and the project proponent of the classification decision within a period of fifteen days from the registration of the classification application in its registry:

a - If it appears that the proposed project is listed in Annex No. 1, the project shall mandatorily be subject to an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study in accordance with the information set out in Annex No. 8 .

b - If it appears that the proposed project is listed in Annex No. 2, the project shall mandatorily be subject to an "Initial Environmental Examination" in accordance with the information set out in Annex No. 6 .

c - If the proposed project classified under Item (b) of this Paragraph is located in an area set out in Annex No. 3 or may have a significant impact on such an area, the project shall be subject to an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study.

d - If it appears that the project is not listed in Annex No. 1 or No. 2 and it is located in an area built in Annex No. 3 or may have a significant impact on such an area, this project shall be subject to an "Initial Environmental Examination".

e - In the event that no reply is given by the Ministry of Environment within the specified time limit, the project proponent and the competent official administration shall have the right to complete the project file, provided that this does not contradict Items (a), (b), (c), and (d) of this Paragraph.

(3) The Minister of Environment shall have the right, based on a reasoned opinion, and within the period specified above, to request an "Initial Environmental Examination" report or an "Environmental Impact Assessment" report for the project regardless of the classification of this project according to Paragraphs (1) and (2) of this Article.

Verification of the Ensuring of Public Safety Requirements in Buildings and Installations - Mandatory Technical Inspection:

1 - The verification of the ensuring of public safety requirements in buildings and installations shall be carried out by means of technical inspection in accordance with the provisions of this Decree.

2 - Technical inspection of the measures taken to ensure public safety shall be mandatory for buildings and installations in accordance with Chapter Two of Annex No. 2 attached to this Decree.

3 - Where technical inspection is mandatory in accordance with the provisions of this Decree, the approval of an accredited technical inspection office must be obtained for the following documents:

a - The preliminary design drawings attached to the building permit application.

b - The execution and/or detailed drawings attached to the application for permission to commence execution.

c - Any modification to the execution and/or detailed drawings during execution.

d - The occupancy permit application attached to the final report of the technical inspector and the handover minutes between at least the responsible engineer and the building structure contractor, with the approval of the property owner.

4 - The mandatory technical inspection that is the subject of this Article shall be subject to all the provisions of Annex No. (1) and Annex No. (2) attached to this Decree.
All the annexes attached to this Decree shall be deemed an integral part thereof (3) annexes.

- Decrees No. 11264 dated 11/11/1997 (Regulatory Conditions Specific to Public Safety and Fire Prevention in Buildings),

- and No. 11266 dated 11/11/1997 (Conditions and Rules to be Applied in the Design and Construction of Installations Against Earthquakes).

- and No. 11267 dated 11/11/1997 (Determination of the Technical and Preventive Conditions Specific to Public Safety Requirements in Lift Equipment), are hereby repealed,

- and Item "First" and Paragraph (5) of Item "Second" of Article (8) of Decree No. 2791 dated 15/10/1992 (Amendment of the Implementing Decree of the Building Law) are hereby repealed,

All provisions that conflict with this Decree or are inconsistent with its content are also hereby repealed.

This Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette with respect to the mandatory application of public safety requirements. The date of commencement of the mandatory technical inspection for new buildings shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport in the light of the decisions accrediting technical inspection offices and their categories and taking into consideration the transitional provisions below:

1 - The First Phase: The mandatory nature of technical inspection shall be applied only to new buildings falling within the limits of the First Category in Table No. 3 - 2 set forth in Chapter Two of Annex No. 2 attached to this Decree.

2 - The Second Phase: After the lapse of two years from the item on the application of the First Phase, the mandatory nature of the application of technical inspection shall be added to new buildings falling within the limits of the Second Category in the aforementioned Table.

3 - The Third Phase: After the lapse of four years from the commencement of the application of the First Phase, the mandatory nature of the application of technical inspection shall be added to new buildings falling within the limits of the Third Category in the Table above.

As for existing buildings, the date of commencement of the mandatory technical inspection shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport following the issuance of a supplementary decree based on the proposal of the same Minister providing for the adoption of special and appropriate standards and specifications based on the specifications and standards adopted for new buildings and installations defined in Item No. 10 of Article One of this Decree.
Every interpretation or clarification of the content of this Decree shall be issued pursuant to a decision by the Minister of Public Works and Transport.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

Position of the Ministry of Environment on the Environmental Impact Assessment Report:

(1) Following review of the final version of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report, the Ministry of Environment shall state its position on the said report, which shall be either approval, conditional approval, or reasoned refusal.

(2) The position shall be notified to the project owner in addition to the competent official administration where the project is a private project, and the public and all concerned parties may inspect the position at the Ministry of Environment, provided that such right of inspection shall not encompass any information that infringes intellectual or industrial property rights or any details relating to the finances of the project. The said position shall also be notified to the competent municipality for posting on the notice board within a period of fifteen days.

(3) The competent official administration shall issue a licence for a private project in light of the Ministry of Environment stating its position with respect to the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report for the said project, with the exception of the cases referred to in paragraph (2) of Article Nine of this Decree.

(4) Every official administration shall refrain from commencing the construction or operation of its proposed project before the Ministry of Environment states its position with respect to the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report for the said project, with the exception of the cases referred to in paragraph (2) of Article Nine of this Decree.

Environmental Management of the Project and Subsequent Monitoring Following Commencement of Construction of the Project:

(1) The project owner shall comply with the mechanism of the "Environmental Management Plan" during construction, operation, and decommissioning works.

(2) The Ministry of Environment shall undertake the monitoring of the implementation of the mechanism of the "Environmental Management Plan" for the project during construction, operation, and decommissioning works.

(3) The project owner shall be responsible for addressing, within the provisions of this Decree, any environmental impact not mentioned in the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report or erroneously assessed, the existence of which is ascertained during construction, operation, and decommissioning works.

Publication of Information:

The public and concerned parties shall have the right to inspect the final report of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" or the "Initial Environmental Examination" and the relevant report of the Ministry of Environment at the Ministry, provided that such right of inspection shall not encompass any information that infringes intellectual or industrial property rights or any details relating to the finances of the project.

Validity Period of the Report:

The report issued by the Ministry of Environment regarding the "Environmental Impact Assessment" and/or "Initial Environmental Examination" study shall be deemed valid for a period of two years where execution of the project has not commenced. Upon expiry of the time limit, the project owner shall notify the Ministry of Environment of his desire to proceed with the project, whereupon the Ministry shall verify whether or not new elements have arisen that require conducting an "Environmental Impact Assessment" or "Initial Environmental Examination" study anew.

Objections and Applications for Review:

(1) The project owner, concerned parties, right holders, and the general public shall have the right to submit written objections to the positions of the Ministry of Environment specified in Article Ten. Such objections shall be accepted at the Ministry of Environment within a period of fifteen days from the date of issuance of the position, and the Ministry shall decide upon such objections within a period of fifteen days from the date of registration of the objections at its registry. Objections received after the time limit specified in this paragraph shall not be accepted. Where the objector is not notified of the position of the Ministry with respect to his objections within the time limit specified above, such objections shall be deemed rejected by the Ministry.

(2) Where an official administration objects to the positions of the Ministry of Environment provided for in Articles Six, Seven, Ten, and Fifteen of this Decree, the objections shall be referred to the Council of Ministers for adjudication.

Infractions and Fines:

(1) In the event of violation of the provisions of this Decree, the provisions of Title Six, and in particular Article Fifty-Eight, of Law No. 444 dated 8/8/2002 (Protection of the Environment) shall apply to the project owner.

(2) The application of the provisions of Title Six of Law No. 444 dated 8/8/2002 (Protection of the Environment) shall not preclude compelling the project owner, where he has not commenced execution of his project, to prepare an "Environmental Impact Assessment" or "Initial Environmental Examination" study for the said project, or, where he has commenced execution of his project, to prepare, at a minimum, the "Environmental Management Plan" for the said project, in accordance with the provisions of this Decree.

Cost of Reviewing the Environmental Impact Assessment Study and the Initial Environmental Examination:

(1) Pursuant to the provisions of Article Twenty-Three of Law No. 444 dated 8/8/2002 (Protection of the Environment), the project owner shall pay a fee in the amount of /250.000 L.L./ two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds for projects requiring an "Initial Environmental Examination" report and /500.000 L.L./ five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds for projects requiring an "Environmental Impact Assessment" report, immediately upon the project owner being notified of the screening decision for his project.

(2) Pursuant to the provisions of Article Twenty-Three of Law No. 444 dated 8/8/2002 (Protection of the Environment), the owner of a private project whose project requires an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study shall deposit a cash sum by way of security with the Ministry of Environment in an initial amount of 0.05 % of the value of the project according to the value submitted by the project owner in Annex No. 4, immediately upon commencing the scoping of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" for his project. Such security shall cover the cost of reviewing the "Environmental Impact Assessment" study if the Ministry requires a specialised expert to perform the same. The security shall be refunded in accordance with the conditions of refund, pursuant to a reasoned decision issued by the Ministry of Environment.

(3) With respect to projects submitted by official administrations that require an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study, such administrations shall be bound to make provision within the budget of the project to cover and pay the cost of reviewing the study.

(4) Theremunerations of the employees of the Ministry of Environment assigned to review "Initial Environmental Examination" reports and "Environmental Impact Assessment" reports in accordance with Article Six and Article Nine of this Decree, in consideration of their overtime work, shall be determined in accordance with the laws in force.

Transitional Provisions:

Where public administrations or public institutions have environmental impact assessment studies prepared by them with the approval of recognised international authorities or prepared by such recognised international authorities, these studies shall be referred to the Ministry of Environment to state its position in accordance with the tenth Article of this Decree.

Annex No. 6: Information Required in the Initial Environmental Examination Report

The «Initial Environmental Examination» report shall include the following information (not necessarily according to the sequence noted);

1 - Executive summary

2 - Table of contents

3 - Introduction:

Identification of the project, specification of its proponent and the person or office carrying out the «Initial Environmental Examination», and a brief explanation of the nature, size, and location of the project.

4 - Policy, legal, and administrative frameworks:

An investigation into the applicable regulations and the principles and standards in force in the environment sector locally and nationally, and identification of the legislation governing the sector under which the project falls. This information must address the identification of the competent official administration and its capacities at the local and national levels.

5 - Description of the proposed project:

A description of the parts of the project and an indication of the maps relating thereto at the appropriate scale and photographs, showing the information pertaining to the project site, the overall design, size, capacity, work programme, services, duration of operation, etc.

6 - Description of the environment surrounding the project:

Collection and assessment of the main information regarding the environmental characteristics of the study site (the physical, chemical, biological, social, and economic environment), taking into consideration any expected modifications prior to the commencement of the project or any potential future changes.

7 - Potential environmental impacts of the project:

Identification, estimation, and assessment of all potential impacts of the project on the environment (physical, chemical, biological, social, and economic), whether positive or negative, direct or indirect, in the short or long term.

8 - Environmental Management Plan:

This paragraph summarises the set of mitigation measures, monitoring and supervision means,

and institutional procedures that shall be taken during the construction, operation, and decommissioning of the project, which would eliminate negative environmental impacts or mitigate them to locally acceptable levels, or in the absence thereof, internationally acceptable levels. This paragraph must also show the approximate cost of the «Environmental Management Plan».

9 - Conclusion

10 - Annexes:

. A summary of the documents related to the project

. Tables and data of information

. A list of the scientific and non-scientific references used

. A list of the names of the preparers of the «Initial Environmental Examination» report (individuals and institutions).

Note: The environmental Ministry shall have the right to amend the points required in this Annex in accordance with the environmental requirements applicable to the specifications and tasks of the project, whilst ensuring the application of the twelfth Article relating to the publication of information.

Annex No. 7: Information Required in the Report Relating to the Scoping of the Environmental Impact Assessment

1 - Introduction:

This paragraph specifies the objective of the report relating to the scoping of the «Environmental Impact Assessment», identifies the project under study, and explains the executive measures for the «Environmental Impact Assessment».

2 - Background information:

This paragraph includes the relevant information regarding the potential parties who may conduct the «Environmental Impact Assessment» study, a brief investigation of the basic contents of the proposed project, a statement on the necessity of and need for the project and the objectives it seeks, the executing office, and a summary of the history of the project including the alternatives studied and the projects related thereto. Reference shall be made to any projects under execution or planned in the same area that may compete with the project under study with respect to the resource unit.

3 - Objectives:

This paragraph defines the scope of the «Environmental Impact Assessment» and discusses its timing in relation to the stages of project preparation, design, and execution.

4 - Environmental Impact Assessment requirements:

This paragraph identifies any regulations and directives governing the conduct of the «Environmental Impact Assessment» or defining the content of the report relating to the scoping of the «Environmental Impact Assessment».

5 - Study area:

This paragraph defines the boundaries of the area covered by the study for the purposes of the «Environmental Impact Assessment». If there is any adjacent or distant area that must be studied in relation to the potential impacts of the execution or management of this project, it must be included in the report relating to the scoping of the «Environmental Impact Assessment».

6 - Scope of work:

In some cases, the tasks that the project proponent must carry out can be clearly known in a manner that allows them to be fully specified in the report relating to the scoping of the «Environmental Impact Assessment». However, in other cases, the need arises to conduct specialised field studies or develop models in order to assess the impacts that may result from the proposed project; in such event, the project proponent is required to specify these particular tasks in greater detail, and the scope of work shall include the following points:

6 - 1) Policy, legal, and administrative frameworks:

An investigation into the applicable regulations and the principles and standards in force in the environment sector locally and nationally (the study specifies the known considerations and the project proponent is required to verify the existence of other considerations) and identification of the legislation governing the sector under which the project falls. This information must address the identification of the competent official administration and its capacities at the local and national levels.

6 - 2) Assistance in coordination among official administrations and public participation:

Assistance in coordinating the study with official administrations and in obtaining the opinion of local non-governmental organisations and groups affected by the proposed project, and in keeping minutes of meetings and all other activities, communications, comments, and the manner of dealing with them (and the report relating to the scoping of the «Environmental Impact Assessment» specifies the types of activities such as a scoping meeting in which concerned parties participate, informational sessions in the environment sector for project staff, support for consultants in the environment sector, public seminars, etc.).

6 - 3) Description of the proposed project:

A description of the parts of the project and an indication of the maps relating thereto at the appropriate scale and photographs, showing the information pertaining to the project site, the overall design, size, capacity, work programme, services, duration of operation, etc.

6 - 4) Description of the environment surrounding the project:

Collection and assessment of the main information regarding the environmental characteristics of the study site (the physical, chemical, biological, social, and economic environment), taking into consideration any expected modifications prior to the commencement of the project and any potential future changes.

6 - 5) Potential environmental impacts of the project:

A distinction must be made between positive impacts and negative impacts, direct impacts and indirect impacts, short-term impacts and long-term impacts. Permanent impacts that cannot be avoided must be identified, and global and transboundary impacts must be identified. The project proponent shall describe the estimation means and techniques used to assess the impacts of the project on the environment. The scope and quality of the available information shall be specified, explaining significant gaps in information and any unknown probabilities regarding the possibility of

estimating the potential impacts of the proposed project. It is advisable to present the terms of reference for certain studies intended to be conducted for the purpose of obtaining the missing information. This paragraph must show the possible mitigation measures for each impact and suggest the most effective and least costly measures.

6 - 6) Analysis of project alternatives:

A general preliminary description of the alternatives studied during the preparation of the proposed project and a mention of those other alternatives that may achieve the same objectives. The concept of these alternatives generally includes the selection of the project site, its designs, its specific technology, construction methods with the specification of its stages, and procedures for its operation and maintenance. A general preliminary comparison of these alternatives shall also be made in terms of potential environmental impacts, their capital and operating costs, their suitability to local conditions, and institutional, training, and monitoring and supervision requirements. To the extent possible, a general preliminary determination of the cost and returns of all alternatives must be made, in addition to the estimated cost of mitigation measures. The alternative of not constructing the project must also be included, in order to clarify the environmental conditions as they are without the project.

6 - 7) Environmental Management Plan:

Mitigation measures for negative impacts

- Monitoring and supervision plan

- Institutional capacity-building plan to implement the recommendations included in the «Environmental Impact Assessment».

The project proponent shall prepare a detailed environmental management plan that includes mitigation measures for all negative impacts, a monitoring and supervision programme, and the needs of personnel and institutions to apply these measures. The cost of this plan must also be specified, including compensation for those harmed as a result of unmitigable impacts.

7 - The Report:

The «Environmental Impact Assessment» report must be concise and limited to basic environmental issues. The main text shall be based on the results of the investigations, the conclusion, and practical recommendations supported by summaries of the collected information and a reference to any recognised references to explain and interpret this information. Detailed or unclarified information is considered inappropriate in the main text and must be presented in the annexes or in a separate document; the same applies to unpublished documents used in the «Environmental Impact Assessment» study with respect to compiling them in an annex.

The «Environmental Impact Assessment» report shall mandatorily include the following:

- Executive summary

- Table of contents

- Introduction

- Policy, legal, and administrative frameworks

- Public participation

- Description of the proposed project

- Description of the environment surrounding the project

- Potential environmental impacts of the project

- Analysis of project alternatives

- Environmental Management Plan

- Conclusion

- Annexes: - Minutes of public participation

- A summary of the documents related to the project

- Tables and data of information

- A list of relevant reports

- A list of the scientific and non-scientific references used

- A list of the names of the preparers of the «Environmental Impact Assessment» report (individuals and institutions)

Note: The Ministry of Environment shall have the right to amend the points required in this Annex in accordance with the environmental requirements applicable to the specifications and tasks of the project, whilst ensuring the application of the twelfth Article relating to the publication of information.

Annex No. 8: Information Required in the Environmental Impact Assessment Report

The «Environmental Impact Assessment» report must include the following points (not necessarily according to the sequence noted below):

1 - Executive summary

2 - Table of contents

3 - Introduction

. Objective and justification of the project:

- Identification of the project and the project proponent

5 - Public participation:

. Official agencies

. Non-governmental organisations

. Groups affected by the project

6 - Description of the proposed project:

. Type of project

. Project location: maps indicating the project location and the extent of its impact

. Size of the project, including the associated activities required by or for it

. Proposed programme for construction and operation

7 - Description of the environment surrounding the project:

7 - 1) Physical and chemical environment:

. Land topography, land geology, and a study of the impact of earthquakes or other hazards

. Study of surface water and groundwater

. Marine and coastal parameters

. Existing means for discharging polluted water and water quality

. Ambient air quality and existing sources of air pollution

. Climate and meteorological monitoring

. Noise

7 - 2) Biological environment:

. Flora and fauna

. Fish and aquatic living organisms

. Rare or endangered species

. Sensitive areas (forests - nature reserves - natural parks - etc.)

7 - 3) Social and economic environment:

. Demographic element (population - social fabric - employment - income distribution - customs and traditions - aspirations of the population - etc.)

. Development activities (infrastructure - industry - agriculture - institutions - tourism - recreation - etc.)

. Land use

. Traffic movement

. Public health

. Archaeological and historical heritage

. Aesthetic values

. Civilisational and cultural values (customs, traditions, and aspirations)

8 - Potential environmental impacts of the project:

8 - 1) Physical and chemical environment

8 - 2) Biological environment

8 - 3) Social and economic environmental

9 - General preliminary analysis of alternatives to the project:

. In the event of not constructing the project

. Alternative projects with the same objectives

. The same project with alternative technologies

. Comparison of the different possibilities economically and environmentally

10 - Environmental Management Plan:

10 - 1) Negative impacts mitigation programme:

. A summary of the significant environmental impacts

. Technical detail for each of the mitigation measures (to which impact it is applied and what are the conditions of its application - its designs - equipment details - operating procedures)

. Potential environmental impacts of these measures

. Linkage of these measures to other mitigation programmes

. Cost of the negative impacts mitigation programme

10 - 2) Monitoring and supervision programme:

. Specific technical detail of the supervision means (parameters subject to supervision - supervision methods - required frequency of supervision - supervision locations - conducting measurements - keeping and analysing information - emergency procedures)

. Reporting procedures

. A detailed budget and programme for acquiring the necessary equipment and supplies

. Cost of the monitoring and supervision programme

10 - 3) Institutional capacity-strengthening programme:

. A detailed description of the institutional measures necessary to carry out the mentioned environmental procedures (responsibility for carrying out mitigation measures, supervision procedures, etc.)

. Technical assistance programmes

. Acquisition of equipment and supplies

. Organisational amendments

. Cost of the institutional capacity-strengthening programme

11 - Conclusion:

. The general net benefit that justifies the application of the project

. Explanation of how negative impacts are mitigated

. Prior preparations for follow-up supervision

12 - Annexes:

. Minutes of public participation

. A summary of the documents related to the project

. Tables and data of information

. A list of relevant reports

. A list of the scientific and non-scientific references used

. A list of the names of the preparers of the «Environmental Impact Assessment» report (individuals and institutions)

Note: The Ministry of Environment shall have the right to amend the points required in this Annex in accordance with the environmental requirements applicable to the specifications and tasks of the legislator, whilst ensuring the application of the twelfth Article relating to the publication of information.

This Decree shall be published and notified wherever needed.

Subject Matter of the Decree

1 - 1 The provisions of this Decree shall regulate advertisements of all kinds, with the exception of advertisements via radio, television, newspapers and magazines, which shall remain subject to the laws and regulations governing them.

1 - 2 An advertisement means any board, writing, sign, poster, flyer, raised letters, mark, picture, inscription, three-dimensional model, balloon, signal or drawing aimed at indicating, publicising or promoting an establishment, name, shop, goods, trade, profession, service or any other activity, and this includes an advertisement illuminated by energy of all kinds, whether permanent or intermittent, including an electronic advertisement, and a fixed, moving or mobile advertisement.

1 - 3 The content of the advertisement shall observe the preservation of national sentiment, public safety and morals, the environment, natural landscapes, and archaeological and historical buildings.

Locations for the Placement of Advertisements

The placement of advertisements shall be permitted in the following locations:

2 - 1 Inside sports stadiums of all types, provided that the height of the sign does not exceed the height of the built wall or fence such that the advertising sign is not

directed outwards, and on the facades of the buildings of sports clubs of all types.

2 - 2 Inside public and private car parks, with the exception of the car parks of buildings, and subject to observing the setbacks provided for in item /2 - 14/ of this Article.

2 - 3 Inside public and private transport stations and on the kiosks of public transport stops, provided that their dimensions do not exceed the limits of the protective structure of such kiosks.

2 - 4 Inside tourist complexes, subject to observing the maximum height limit of /200/ cm from the ground surface.

2 - 5 Inside the real property on which construction sites are established, and it shall also be permissible to cover a building under construction or restoration and the scaffolding with an advertising sign, provided that it is removed upon obtaining the occupancy permit.

2 - 6 Within the entrances of buildings to identify the names and professions of the occupants of these buildings and their floors, provided that these advertisements shall not be subject to the licensing requirement provided for in Chapter Two of this Decree.

2 - 7 On blind building facades (Wall Murals) (Mur Pignon), provided that the area of the sign does not exceed 80% of the area of the blind facade, and provided that the building is occupied in all its floors, with the exception of the ground floor and the basement floors, by a single occupant, and that this advertisement indicates the name and function of the occupant.

2 - 8 On blind building facades (Mur Pignon) outside cities (which with respect to the City of Beirut means the municipal area of the Municipality of Beirut), provided that only one sign is placed and that the area of the sign does not exceed 80% of the area of the blind facade and subject to the approval of 75% of the owners of the various sections in the building, provided that a distance of /500/ metres is left between one advertisement and another in the same direction. Exempted from these conditions are advertisements on the facades of the buildings of sports clubs of all types provided for in item /2 - 1/ of this Article, as well as advertisements on the facades of cracked and completely abandoned buildings.

2 - 9 On the rooftops of buildings (Rooftop) that have not exhausted the general exploitation factor (with respect to vertical extension) and after the approval of 75% of the owners of the various sections

in the building, within the limits of the facades of the building, provided that the area of the sign does not exceed /16/ metres (horizontally) X /8/ metres (vertically) and that a distance of at least one metre is left between the advertisement and the parapet of the building, and that the projection of the advertisement from the facade or from the rooftop does not exceed the projections permitted under the Building Law and the regulations relating thereto, provided that a distance of /75/ metres is left between one advertisement and another in the same direction.

The structure of the advertisement may be designed for placing a double-sided advertisement facing oncoming and outgoing traffic such that it is fixed in accordance with the specifications of the rooftop, and it shall also be permissible to modify the structure or install a second structure in order to be able to install the outgoing face of the sign in accordance with acceptable technical specifications.

No licence may be granted for placing a wall sign (Wall Mural) and a rooftop sign (Rooftop Sing) on the same building, nor may a licence be granted for placing more than one sign on the rooftop of a building.

2 - 10 On the facades of shops, offices and establishments located on the ground floor, provided that the projection of the advertisement from the facade does not exceed /30/ cm and that it is restricted to the name of the shop, office or establishment and the description of the activity.

It shall be prohibited to convert the signs of commercial and industrial shops, including cafés and pharmacies, into advertising signs.

2 - 11 Establishments and shops may place one advertising sign dedicated exclusively to indicating their name and/or activity in the outdoor area falling within their private property and subject to observing the setbacks provided for in item /2 - 14/ of this Article, and the height of the sign from the ground surface may not exceed four metres and the total area of the sign may not exceed /8/ m2 on motorways and international roads; as for other roads, the height of the sign from the ground surface may not exceed two metres and the area of the sign /3/ m2 .

2 - 12 Inside ports, harbours and airports after the approval of the competent administration, provided that they shall be subject to special conditions proposed by this administration with due regard to the provisions of this Decree and approved by the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities.

2 - 13 Within the precincts of fuel distribution stations, provided that the height of the sign from the ground surface does not exceed ten metres and its width /250/ cm, and provided that the sign is dedicated to indicating the name of the station, the name of the fuel distribution company and the prices of petroleum derivatives, and subject to compliance with the setbacks imposed pursuant to this Decree.

It shall also be permitted to install a maximum of two advertising signs inside the station, and not on its facade or rooftops, of any of Categories (A), (B) or (C) solely to promote its goods

or similar goods, subject to compliance with the provisions of Chapter Two of this Decree.

2 - 14 Outside the minimum setback from the edge of the asphalt for the following roads:

-Motorway--------1.5/m-

-International road------1,5/m-

-Main road-----1.5/m-

-Secondary road-------1/m-

-Local road-----1/m-

-Internal road----1/m-

Notwithstanding the setbacks provided for in item /2 - 14/ of this Article, signs of Category (A) may be installed on pavements whose width is not less than /3.50/ metres, provided that the edge of the sign is at a distance of not less than /30/ cm from the edge of the pavement, and that a pedestrian walkway of not less than two metres is left and in a manner that does not obstruct visibility and traffic movement.

Notwithstanding the setbacks provided for in item /2 - 14/ of this Article, and with respect to the other categories of advertising signs (with the exception of signs of Category (D), the installation of which on the pavement is prohibited), the base of the sign shall be fixed on pavements whose width is less than /6/ metres on the pavement in a manner that leaves the widest possible walkway for pedestrians and in a manner that does not obstruct visibility and traffic movement.

2 - 15 In central and side islands of roads, provided that the width of the island exceeds five metres starting from the edge of the pavement and/or the asphalt of the road and the verge, and subject to observing the setbacks provided for in item /2 - 14/ of this Article from the edge of the island on each side. In all cases, the advertising signs must be of one category only within the single island, and a distance of /75/ metres shall be left between one advertisement and another in the same direction for signs of Categories (A) and (B), a distance of /100/ metres between one advertisement and another in the same direction for signs of Category (C), and a distance of /500/ metres between one advertisement and another in the same direction for signs of Category (D).

For the purposes of this Decree, an island means any unbuilt plot of land of the public domain bordered on every side by a road used by motor vehicles.

2 - 16 On bridges dedicated to the passage of motor vehicles and on pedestrian bridges, provided that the sign does not exceed the limits of the concrete, and that there are no official announcements or signs placed thereon to indicate the directions of cities and villages.

2 - 17 Inside commercial centres, provided that the licence application is signed by the owner of the commercial centre and by the operator, if any, after presenting the operating contract duly registered.

2 - 18 On vehicles and machinery, subject to observing the Traffic Law, and in accordance with the following:

Advertisements on vehicles shall be divided into three categories:

-Vehicles and machinery dedicated to public transport;

-Vehicles and machinery belonging to companies that use them for their own activity; and

-Vehicles and machinery dedicated to advertising.

Category One: Vehicles and machinery dedicated to public transport. This category comprises taxis (Taxi) and passenger transport buses:

-Taxis (Taxi): the placement of the advertisement shall be permitted on the doors only;

-Passenger transport buses: the placement of the advertisement shall be permitted on the three sides of the bus, but when it is placed on the side or rear glass, special vinyl material (See Through) that does not obstruct visibility from the inside to the outside must be used;

Category Two: Vehicles and machinery belonging to companies that use them for their own activity:

-The placement of the name and number of the company and/or the goods it sells shall be permitted on the body of the car;

-It shall also be permitted to place an advertisement solely about itself or about its goods, in which case --the advertisement fee for the remaining categories of vehicles shall apply;

Category Three: Vehicles and machinery dedicated to advertising:

-The placement of the advertisement shall be permitted on all parts of the vehicle except the front windscreen;

-Vehicles and machinery dedicated to advertising shall be prohibited from parking in the public domain, driving in convoys at a speed below 50 km, and obstructing traffic;

-It shall be prohibited to operate a digital device on any vehicle or machinery roaming on public roads, whatever its type.

Placing Advertisements in Public Streets, Squares and Gardens

3 - 1 Banners shall be placed and decorations erected above and along the sides of public streets, squares

and gardens on the occasion of official religious and national holidays for a period of one month at most, and their size and location must not affect natural scenery or traffic safety and must not disfigure nature, in agreement with the concerned municipality or with the Governor or the Qaemقام outside the municipal area.

3 - 2 Banners shall be placed and decorations erected above and along the sides of public streets, squares

and gardens upon the holding of celebrations, festivals or sports activities of all kinds for a period of fifteen days at most, after obtaining the necessary licences from the concerned administrations, and their size and location must not affect natural scenery or traffic safety and must not disfigure nature, and a deposit equal to four times the minimum wage must be lodged to be used in the event that the concerned parties fail to remove the advertisements and clear the remains of the decorations.

3 - 3 The concerned administration may allow an establishment or a company, at the expense of the latter, to plant with trees, illuminate, beautify and maintain public squares and gardens, provided that the concerned administration allows it to place its name or the name of one of its products on a board fixed in the ground of the square or garden, and the size of the board must not or exceed 1.80 (vertically)X

1.20 metres (horizontally).

Places Where the Placing of Advertisements and Advertising Boards is Prohibited

The placing of advertisements and advertising boards of all kinds is prohibited in the following places:

4 - 1 On the buildings of public administrations, public institutions and municipalities and inside these places.

4 - 2 In archaeological and tourist places and on archaeological and tourist buildings and within a radius of /100/ metres thereof.

4 - 3 On places of worship and their appurtenances and on cemeteries and their walls and within a radius of /50/ metres thereof.

4 - 4 On lighting, electricity and telephone poles and trees.

4 - 5 Above bridges and at the entrances and exits of tunnels.

4 - 6 On boards bearing the names of cities and villages and boards of tourist and archaeological places and at a distance of /50/ metres and in a manner that does not obstruct visibility and traffic movement.

4 - 7 On traffic signs and at a distance of /10/ metres and in a manner that does not obstruct visibility and traffic movement.

4 - 8 On traffic lights and within a distance that does not obstruct visibility and traffic movement.

4 - 9 On road parapets and walls and inside roundabouts and at intersections and bends devoid of traffic lights on each side up to the limits of visibility for a distance of /50/ metres and in a manner that does not obstruct visibility and traffic movement.

4 - 10 On the walls of public gardens and inside these gardens, subject to the provisions of Article Three of this Decree.

4 - 11 On the roofs, walls and balconies of houses, buildings, establishments and shops of all kinds, subject to the provisions of Items /2 - 7/, /2 - 8/, /2 - 9/ and /2 - 10/ of Article Two of this Decree.

4 - 12 Towards the sea, lakes and rivers if the distance between the advertising board and these sites is less than /50/ metres, provided that the distance requirement shall not apply to the Beirut River.

4 - 13 It is prohibited to place boards and signs that direct traffic to economic, industrial, social, residential, medical, professional or educational centres, with the exception of what is placed or permitted to be installed by the concerned municipality or the Governor or the Qaemقام outside the municipal area, subject to the provisions of this Decree and provided that their size and location do not affect traffic safety, and provided that they contain only on the name of the centre and the distance to reach it.

4 - 14 Above the roofs of stairwells, elevators, water tanks, cooling machines and other structures erected above the roofs of buildings.

4 - 15 On a building that is wholly in violation.

Measurement of Boards

6 - 1 With the exception of other cases and measurements expressly provided for in this Decree, the measurement of advertising boards along the sides of roads is unified within the following categories:

(See attached file)

6 - 2 The distance between a board of Category (B) and a board of Category (C) must not be less than /100/ metres.

6 - 3 It is permitted to install two boards of Category (C) measuring /4/ metres horizontally

and /3/ metres vertically only, one adjacent to the other (side by side), subject to compliance with what is stated in Item /2 - 14/ of Article Two of this Decree.

6 - 4 It is permitted to convert two boards of Category (C) only into a single board measuring /8/ metres (horizontally) , X/ 3 / metres (vertically) outside cities (and with respect to the City of Beirut, this means the municipal area of the Municipality of Beirut) such that it is prohibited to install it vertically (that is, measuring /8/ metres vertically and /3/ metres horizontally), and provided that the distance between two consecutive boards measuring /8/ metres (horizontally) X /3/ metres (vertically) is not less than /200/ metres.

6 - 5 When a property is located on two streets, the calculation of distances shall be on the basis of each street, that is, it is permitted to install two boards on the single property from Categories (A), (B) or (C) only.

Examination of the Application and Granting of the Licence

8 - 1 The administration concerned with licensing shall refer the file within three days from the date of its registration with it to the Technical Department in the municipality or the Engineering Body in the Federation of Municipalities in the event that the municipality is part of a federation, or to the Technical Department in the Directorate General of Urban Planning in the governorate or the district in the absence of the Technical Department or the Engineering Body referred to above, in order to examine it, give the technical opinion and return it to the administration competent to grant the licence within a period of fifteen days from the date of its receipt.

The concerned administration must, within the three-day time limit mentioned above, inquire in writing with the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities regarding the existence of any standing violation committed by the licence applicant of which he was notified pursuant to the provisions of the sixteenth Article of this Decree. The silence of the Ministry after the expiry of five days from the date of its receipt of the letter of inquiry shall be deemed to signify the absence of a violation.

8 - 2 The concerned administration must, within three days from its receipt of the approval of the Technical Department, deliver to the applicant a notice of the amount of the fees due or send the notice to him by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt, and he must pay the fees due in accordance with Chapter Three of Law 60/88 dated 12/8/1988 (Municipal Fees) within a week from his receipt of the payment order, under penalty of dismissal of the licence application.

8 - 3 The concerned administration must decide on the licence application within a maximum time limit of one week from the date of attaching the payment receipt to the licensing file. In the event of failure to decide on the licence application within a maximum time limit of one week from the date of attaching the payment receipt to the licensing file, the advertising sign that is the subject of the application shall be deemed licensed ipso jure.

8 - 4 The licence holder must comply with the content of item /1 - 3/ of the first Article of this Decree under penalty of removal of the advertising sign at his expense and under his responsibility. In the event of repetition of the violation, the licence shall be revoked without its holder having the right to claim any compensation.

8 - 5 Subject to the provisions of the eleventh and eighteenth Articles of this Decree, priority in licensing for the first time shall be given to the petitioner who held the last lawful licence upon the issuance of this Decree and installed a lawfully licensed sign in the same location.

Renewal of the Licence

9 - 1 The party concerned who wishes to renew the licence must submit a written application to the Competent Administration within a period of one month from the date of expiry of the term of his licence; otherwise, his right to renewal shall lapse and the advertising board shall be removed at his expense and under his responsibility.

9 - 2 The application for renewal of the licence shall include a detailed list of the sites with the dimensions of the board and the identification number of each board.

9 - 3 The Competent Administration must, within the three-day time limit mentioned above, inquire in writing with the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities as to the existence of any standing infringement committed by the licence applicant of which he was notified pursuant to the provisions of Article Sixteen of this Decree. The silence of the Ministry after the expiry of five days from the date of its receipt of the letter of inquiry shall be deemed to signify the non-existence of an infringement.

9 - 4 The Competent Administration shall decide upon the renewal application within a maximum time limit of one month from the date of submission of the application after verifying the fulfilment of all legal conditions.

9 - 5 In the event of approval of the renewal of the licence, the procedures provided

for in Clause /8 - 2/ of Article Eight of this Decree shall be adopted; otherwise, the party concerned shall be deemed to have defaulted on submitting the application in accordance with what is stated in Clause /9 - 1/ of this Article.

9 - 6 Renewal of the licence shall be withheld from the applicant therefor in the event that it appears that he owns any board in infringement of the provisions of this Decree.

The Bank Guarantee

10 - 1 As a guarantee for good performance, every licence applicant or licence holder within the meaning of this Decree must attach to his application or submit within the three-month time limit granted pursuant to Article Eighteen of this Decree, an on-demand bank guarantee in favour of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities in the amount of /30 000 000/ L.L. (thirty million Lebanese Pounds) which shall be renewed automatically and shall neither be cancelled nor recovered except in the event of the removal of all advertisements belonging to the company concerned.

10 - 2 Each company shall submit one bank guarantee to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities regardless of the number of boards that it wishes to license in all municipalities.

Determination of the Advertiser's Quota of Advertising Boards

No advertiser shall be permitted to obtain in a single municipal area more than ten per cent of the legal and permitted number of advertising boards, and companies belonging to a single advertiser or those in which the same advertiser or his spouse or one of his minor children holds shares shall be deemed to constitute a single company.

Awareness Campaigns and Others

12 - 1 Any of the public administrations may use free of charge a proportion not exceeding ten per cent of the total licensed boards in a given real estate area when launching campaigns for awareness and guidance, provided that it is for a maximum period of seven days in each locality and provided that the total days do not exceed thirty during a single year.

12 - 2 Each company must draw up a schedule of its contributions to the campaigns of these administrations.

12 - 3 Any of the public administrations may use free of charge one of the two faces of urban furniture boards (Category (A)) to place maps of the city or advertisements belonging to the city or town.

Indication of the Name of the Owner of the Board and the Number and Date of the Licence

13 - 1 There must be affixed to one of the corners of the advertising board, under pain of dismantling the infringing board under the responsibility and at the expense of its owner:

-The name of the owner of the board;

-The number and date of the licence;

-A different serial identification number for each company, provided that each company sends its list to the municipality; this number shall consist of at least three digits.
