1- A driver who is preparing to leave a road in order to take another road situated on his right shall keep to the right edge of the carriageway and shall, in all cases, execute the necessary turn at a moderate speed, and after ensuring that this can be done without any danger or inconvenience to others. 2- And a driver who is preparing to leave a road in order to take another road situated to his left shall bear to his left without crossing the centreline of the carriageway.
In the event that two drivers approach a road intersection coming from two different roads, the driver coming from the left must give way to the passage of the other driver.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding Article, a driver coming from a road of ordinary traffic onto a road of major traffic shall give way to vehicles travelling on the second road. - Roads of major traffic are designated: 1- In built-up areas : by decision of the competent municipality. 2- Outside built-up areas : by decision of the Minister of Interior after consulting the Ministry of Public Works and Transport. In the absence of classification of roads by decision of the competent authority, all of them are considered to be of the same degree of importance and thereupon the provisions of Article (26) shall apply.

Upon reaching road junctions or intersections, a user shall: 1- Comply with electric traffic signals where present. For this purpose, the red colour is adopted for stopping, the orange colour for readiness, and the green colour for proceeding. 2- Or comply with the signal of the security officer charged with directing traffic where present. 3- Or where a special sign requiring a stop is present, stop for the time necessary to enable others to pass safely.

1- A driver shall, in all cases, give the right of way to vehicles of the Army, the Security Forces, the Fire Brigade, and the Ambulance Service that give warning of their approach by using the devices set forth in Articles (95) and (219) of this Law. 2- And a driver shall also give the right of priority of passage to school pupils when they are entering or leaving their schools.

1- Where a railway track exists on the road, whether across or along it, priority of passage belongs to the rolling stock that ordinarily runs on the track. Every user of the road shall clear the railway track immediately upon the approach of the aforementioned rolling stock, giving way for its passage. 2- If a railway crossing on the road is not equipped with a barrier or is unguarded, a road user must, upon seeing the regulatory sign indicating the presence of the crossing, not enter it except after ensuring that it is possible to pass safely and that there is nothing indicating the approach of a train towards it. 3- If the crossing is equipped with barriers or is guarded, a road user must comply with the instructions of the crossing guard.

It is prohibited to stop or park on sections of the road occupied or crossed by railway tracks, and it is also prohibited to leave vehicles or animals standing thereon, or to use railway tracks for running vehicles foreign thereto.
Audible warning devices shall not be used except for giving necessary warnings to other users.
The use of multi-tone horns, sirens, and whistles is prohibited.

Audible warning devices shall not be used inside built-up areas except in cases of extreme necessity and under the following conditions: 1- That the warning devices meet the conditions specified in Article (94) of this Law. 2- That the warning signal be intermittent, short, and very moderate. At night, warnings shall be given by means of light signals, and audible warning devices shall not be used except in case of extreme necessity.
The competent local authorities may restrict the use of audible warning devices inside built-up areas, or prohibit them except in cases of imminent danger.

The provisions of Articles (33), (34), and (35) shall not apply to drivers of vehicles of the Army, the Security Forces, the Fire Brigade, and the Ambulance Service when carrying out a mission that requires their rapid intervention.

Article 37: It is prohibited: 1- To stop or leave a vehicle or an animal on the public road if doing so constitutes an abuse of the use of the road. 2- For the driver to move away from the parking place of his vehicle without taking the necessary precautions to forestall any accident that may result from his absence. 3- For a passenger of a vehicle to alight from it or to board it or to open any of its exits before verifying in advance the possibility of doing so without any hazard.

Article 38: 1- The parking of a vehicle, or an animal, on the road must take place in a manner that does not result in any hindrance to traffic movement, or obstruction of entry to neighbouring properties. 2- The vehicle or animal must in all cases be stopped at the extreme right edge of the road, so as to leave clear the largest possible part of the carriageway, unless this side is designated for special traffic or the condition of the ground does not permit this. 3- Parking is prohibited: a - In places indicated by a no-parking sign. b - In places located less than ten metres from stops for electric buses and other vehicles intended for public transport. c - At a bend, the crest of a road, or a road junction, or when visibility is insufficient. d - In places where parking obstructs the departure of another parked vehicle. e - On bridges, pedestrian crossings, and the entrances and exits of garages, public gardens, places of worship, and schools. f - In front of the entrances of roads leading to official or private public buildings. g - On pavements intended for pedestrian traffic, on railway tracks, and on lanes intended for fast traffic. 4- On roads where places for picking up passengers are designated, taxis are prohibited from stopping elsewhere than in these places for the same purpose. 5- The parking of any vehicle in a parking place designated for a category of vehicles other than the category to which it belongs is prohibited. 6- The display or parking of vehicles intended for sale for the purpose of trade, whether new or used, on public roads is prohibited even in places where parking is permitted.

Article 39: It is prohibited to leave vehicles neglected on the public road. Vehicles or wrecks of vehicles neglected on the public road and remaining in this condition for a period of thirty days from the date of drawing up a record by the authorities charged with the suppression of traffic contraventions shall be deemed abandoned by their owner, in which record shall be established: - The description of the vehicle or the wrecks. - The place where it is lying. - The period during which it was seen lying in the same place. - The name of its owner if known or the registration number of the vehicle if the registration plates are still affixed to it. - All other surrounding circumstances. The record shall be submitted to the President of the Municipal Council if the public road falls within the municipal area, and otherwise it shall be submitted to the Qaemقام (District Commissioner). The President of the Municipal Council or the Qaemقام must address a formal notice to the owner of the vehicle to remove it within a period of ten days from the date of service of the notice, which must be served on the owner in person if his place of residence is known, and otherwise it shall be served by affixing it to the vehicle itself.

Article 40: If the vehicle or the wrecks are not removed within the period of ten days granted pursuant to the formal notice provided for in the preceding Article, the President of the Municipal Council or the Qaemقام must then decide either to destroy the vehicle or the wrecks that are the subject of the record, or to remove and place them in a special place, or to sell them for the account of their owner by public auction. All fees and expenses due thereon or incurred as a result of this operation shall be deducted from the sale price. As for the balance, if any remains, it shall be kept in trust for the account of the owner of the vehicle or the wrecks for a period of one year starting from the date of the sale. Upon the expiry of this period, the kept amount shall become the property of the municipality or of the State, depending on whether the sale was effected by the President of the Municipal Council or the Qaemقام. However, if the sale value is insufficient to cover the fees and expenses, the difference shall be collected from the owner in accordance with the method of collection of direct taxes.

Article 41: 1- At night, and during the day when necessary, particularly in time of fog, a driver proceeding on a road equipped or not equipped with public lighting must switch on the position lights or the driving lights, or the passing lights, or the lamps specified in this Law. 2- The driver must switch on the marker lights if the vehicle is equipped with them in accordance with the provisions of Article (86) of this Law. 3- He must use the passing lights, instead of the driving lights, and instead of the fog lamps, in all circumstances that require this in order to avoid dazzling the eyes of other drivers. 4- The responsible authorities may regulate the use of driving lights and passing lights on roads equipped with sufficient public lighting.

Article 42: 1- At night, and during the day when necessary, particularly in time of fog, every vehicle standing on a road not equipped with public lighting - or equipped with insufficient public lighting - subject to the application of the special provisions of Chapters (3), (4), (5) and (6) of this Law - must be indicated either by a position light or a rear red light, or by a parking light, on the side opposite the pavement or the side of the road. 2- If the length of the vehicle or combination of vehicles exceeds six metres, or its width exceeds two metres, it must be indicated, while standing, by two position lights and two red lights. 3- If, as a result of force majeure, it is impossible to stop the vehicle within the conditions specified in Article (38), or if the load of the vehicle or part thereof falls onto the road and cannot be removed immediately, the driver must, if visibility is insufficient, and especially at night, take all necessary measures to indicate the existing obstacles. 4- In all cases of parking at night on the public road outside towns and inhabited areas, the driver of a goods transport vehicle must place on the carriageway behind his vehicle and in line with its left side, and at a sufficient distance from it, a triangular light-reflecting sign.

Article 43: 1- It is prohibited to equip vehicles, with the exception of vehicles that may be used for special transport and for which a special regulation is established, with lighting or signalling devices other than those specified in this Law. 2- These provisions do not apply to the interior lighting devices in the vehicle, provided that these devices do not disturb other drivers. 3- Vehicles are prohibited from using any illuminated or light-reflecting sign intended for advertising.
Article 44: Road users, except in cases of force majeure, must confine their movement to the carriageways, crossings, and pavements designated for the traffic of the category to which they belong.

Article 45: The form of the signs and markings that must be used to inform the public of traffic measures shall be those adopted in the International Convention concluded in Geneva in the year 1949, and set out in the Annex to this Law. The forms of the additional and local signs and markings referred to in the said Convention shall be determined by a decision of the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of the Interior.
Article 46: Everyone is prohibited from causing any damage to traffic markings and signs, or affixing advertisements or notices onto them, or altering their features, positions, or directions.

Article 47: 1- The Minister of the Interior, after consulting the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, may take all measures he deems necessary to ensure the safety of traffic on bridges, and in tunnels. 2- Special signs announcing the instructions that must be followed to preserve them or to ensure the safety of traffic must be placed at the entrances and exits of bridges and tunnels.

Article 85: Rear Red Lights: 1- The motor vehicle or trailer shall be equipped at the rear with two lights emitting to the rear a non-dazzling red light visible at night, in clear weather, at a distance of one hundred and fifty metres. 2- The illumination of the position lights, the driving lights, or the passing lights shall result in the illumination of the rear red lights.

Article 86: Clearance Lights: 1- Every motor vehicle or every combination of vehicles the length of which exceeds six metres, or the width of which, including the load, exceeds two metres, shall be equipped at the front with two clearance lights emitting forward a white or yellow light and at the rear with two lights emitting to the rear a red light, provided that such lights are non-dazzling. 2- These lights shall be mounted on both sides of the vehicle at the limits of the outer width, and these lights may substitute for the position lights at the front and the red lights at the rear.

Article 87: Rear Registration Plate Lighting Device: 1- The motor vehicle or trailer shall be equipped with a device that illuminates at night, in clear weather, and at a distance of at least twenty metres, the number recorded on the registration plate placed at the rear. 2- The illumination of the position lights, the driving lights, or the passing lights shall result in the illumination of the aforementioned device.

Article 88: Slowing Down Signal: 1- The motor vehicle or trailer shall be equipped at the rear with one or two slowing down signals emitting to the rear a non-dazzling orange or red light, which shall illuminate as soon as the driver begins to apply the main brake. 2- If the signal emits a red light, such light shall be of greater intensity than the light emitted by the rear red light when the signal is grouped with or incorporated into the rear light, provided that such light remains in all cases non-dazzling. 3- The mounting of this signal shall not be required on trailers or semi-trailers if their dimensions do not obscure from a driver approaching from the rear the slowing down signal mounted on the towing vehicle.
Article 89: Direction Indicator Signals: Every motor vehicle shall be fitted with flashing lights visible from the front and rear sides of the motor vehicle when changing direction.

Article 90: Parking Lights: A vehicle may be equipped on both its sides with parking lights emitting forward and to the rear the same lights as those emitted by the position lights and the rear red lights.

Article 91: Dirigible Lights: The use of a searchlight (projector) for the purpose of illuminating the road is absolutely prohibited, with the exception of motor vehicles of the Army, the Security Forces, the Fire Brigade, and the Ambulance Service.

Article 92: Special Lights and Signals: 1- Overtaking signal: The Minister of Interior may require, by a decision issued by him, that certain motor vehicles be equipped with a signal emitting a non-dazzling light allowing its driver to give, by night and by day, a signal indicating that he has received the warning of the driver preparing to overtake him. 2- Fog lights: A motor vehicle may be equipped with special lights called (fog lights). 3- Reversing lights: A motor vehicle may be fitted with lights placed at its rear to facilitate visibility to the rear, provided that they operate solely upon engaging the reversing gear, that their light does not extend over the carriageway beyond ten metres, and that they are non-dazzling. 4- Every motor vehicle intended for the transport of goods shall be fitted with a triangular-shaped signal, the specifications of which shall conform to the specifications set out in the International Convention concluded at Geneva in the year 1949, to be used in accordance with what is set out in Article (42), fourth paragraph, of this Law. 5- Transport of trees and objects of continuous length: Subject to the provisions of Article (67) of this Law, vehicles transporting trees or objects of continuous length shall be subject to the following conditions: 1- That by day there be placed at the rear of the load a flag of a crimson red colour measuring not less than 30X20 centimetres. 2- That by night there be placed at the rear of the load a lamp emitting a clear, non-dazzling red light.

Article 93: General Provisions Relating to Lighting and Signalling: 1- Where there is a balance or two devices signifying the same thing and capable of being used at the same time, they shall be mounted at the extremities of the vehicle symmetrically and in relation to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle, and they shall emit or reflect luminous rays of the same colour and the same intensity. 2- The intensity of the lights and signals shall not be variable, with the exception of the lights of signals relating to changing direction.

Article 94: A motor vehicle shall be fitted with two warning devices, the sound intensity of each of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior. The device with a soft sound shall be designated for use within towns and populated areas, and the other outside these places.
Article 95: Vehicles of the Army, the Security Forces, and the Fire Brigade may be equipped with special warning devices in addition to the ordinary warning devices.
Article 96: Vehicles for the transport of patients may be equipped with warning instruments having a special sound in addition to the ordinary warning devices.

Article 97: 1- Every motor vehicle shall bear a plate known as the /manufacturer's plate/ on which are clearly stated the make of the motor vehicle, its model, and the serial number of the model therein, and the manufacturer shall undertake the affixing of this plate to the motor vehicle. 2- In addition to this plate, the serial number of the model shall be stamped by the manufacturer on the chassis or body of the motor vehicle; otherwise, it shall be stamped by means of cold stamping by the competent administration. 3- The engine of the motor vehicle shall bear a serial number engraved thereon; otherwise, it shall be stamped by the competent administration. 4- The manufacturer of the motor vehicle and his agent in Lebanon, as well as the owner of every vehicle, shall be jointly and severally liable for the accuracy of the particulars mentioned in this Article.

Article 98: Every motor vehicle intended for the transport of goods shall bear on its right side a visible plate clearly containing its unladen weight and its authorised gross weight, or such weights shall be clearly written on its body.

Article 99: 1- Every motor vehicle shall be fitted with two plates known as the /registration plates/ bearing the registration number assigned to the motor vehicle pursuant to the provisions of Article 117 of this Law, provided that one of them is affixed at the front and the second at the rear in a manner that renders them permanently visible to the eye and does not permit their removal, and that they are stamped with the stamp of the competent department. 2- Every public motor vehicle for the transport of passengers shall be fitted on the inside with a plate bearing the name of its owner, its registration number, and the other particulars which, together with the form of the plate and the place of its installation, shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior. 3- The owner of the motor vehicle shall maintain these plates so that they remain clean and intact, and he is prohibited from affixing beside them or upon them any letters, numbers, or signs other than what is authorised pursuant to a decision of the Minister of Interior, and it is likewise prohibited to install plates other than those authorised by the competent department. Exempted from the provisions of this paragraph are the special badges of judges, lawyers, doctors, pharmacists, and journalists, provided that such badges remain separate from the registration plates and not attached thereto.

Article 100: Every trailer and every semi-trailer shall have affixed at its rear a registration plate bearing the same registration number belonging to the towing vehicle, and this plate shall be stamped with the stamp of the competent department.

Article 101: The competent department shall undertake the provision of registration plates for the vehicles and trailers the registration of which falls within its competence; as for the vehicles the registration of which is undertaken by the municipalities, the competent municipality shall provide their plates, provided that they conform to the contents of Article (107) of this Law.

Every motor car or combination of vehicles that has not yet been used and is intended to be driven on the road for the purpose of testing must be equipped with two trial plates, the first placed at the front and the second at the rear. A vehicle equipped with two trial plates may not be driven except on the sections of roads designated for that purpose by a decision of the Minister of the Interior, who shall also determine the conditions of circulation. While driving the vehicle, the driver must carry the circulation permit relating to its plates and an authorisation from the customs authorities to remove the motor car from its customs warehouse in order to test it, or a declaration from the said authorities certifying the payment of the customs duties due thereon, or a declaration from approved motor car dealers certifying on their responsibility that the customs receipt (with a statement of its number and date) pertaining to it is in their possession.

Every motor car or combination of vehicles that has not yet been registered and is intended for export abroad must be equipped with two transit plates, the first placed at its front and the second at its rear. While the vehicle is proceeding on the road, the driver must carry the legal customs declarations relating to it, and a transit permit drawn up by the competent department stating the name of the agent of the motor car company or the holder of the transit plate, his place of residence, the make and model of the vehicle, the serial chassis number, the engine number, the destination, the route of the roads to be followed, and the period of validity of the permit.

1- Approved agents of motor car companies in Lebanon, concessionary companies, and United Nations organisations shall be granted a number of trial and transit plates for use when needed. 2- These plates shall be granted for a renewable period of one year, provided that the competent department determines their number in proportion to the importance of the business of each of them. 3- Public institutions may be granted trial plates for a renewable period of one year, where necessary, upon the request of the competent Minister.

The competent department may permit, where necessary and on an exceptional basis, the delivery of trial and transit plates to individuals, provided that they are used once only and for a period not exceeding three days.

If the motor car intended to be tested or exported is accompanied by a trailer or semi-trailer, the two trial or transit plates must be placed, one at the front of the motor car and the second at the rear of the trailer or semi-trailer.

The Minister of the Interior may determine, by a decision issued by him, the models of registration, trial, transit, and temporary admission plates, registration plates for motor cars intended for hire by non-residents, and registration plates for motor cars intended for external transport, as well as the manner of their numbering, their distribution to vehicles, and the method of their fitting. Special plates and numbers shall be allocated solely to the motor cars of the Presidency of the State, the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies, the Presidency of the Government and its members, the members of the Chamber of Deputies, and the members of the diplomatic and consular corps accredited in Lebanon. The profession of manufacturing registration plates may not be practised except under a licence from the Minister of the Interior, and licensees must comply with the models and specifications of plates defined in the decision provided for in this Article and must keep a register with "numbered" pages, certified as to their number by the local Internal Security Forces station, in which they shall record the number of the plates manufactured, the date of their delivery, and the names of their recipients.

If the authorised gross weight of the trailer exceeds 750 kilograms or half the unladen weight of the towing vehicle, the trailer must be equipped, - in addition to the main coupling which ensures its towing and steering, with an auxiliary coupling which may consist - of chains or metal cables capable, in the event of failure of the main coupling, of towing the trailer and preventing it from deviating from its normal direction. In the event that the main coupling breaks or snaps, the auxiliary coupling may only be used temporarily to complete the journey to the nearest repair centre, provided that the vehicle proceeds in such a case at a very moderate speed. - The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply in the event of the use of an auxiliary coupling consisting of ropes or other materials the use of which is dictated by extreme necessity, and such couplings may only be used for a single coupling if the towing vehicle is towing several vehicles, and the couplings must remain visible by night and by day to facilitate their inspection.

Every motor car, motor vehicle, trailer, or semi-trailer intended to be put into circulation must be constructed and equipped in a manner that limits, in the event of collision, the risks of bodily injury both to its users and to other road users. Every tanker motor car intended for the transport of flammable materials must be equipped with a fire extinguisher.

The Minister of the Interior shall determine, by a decision issued by him, the conditions that must be met in all types of motor cars, vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers, whether with respect to the manufacture of bodies or the internal and external dimensions, or for the purpose of ensuring the safety and comfort of passengers and securing the transported load.

1- Every motor car, every trailer, and every semi-trailer presented for registration for the first time, or for which re-registration is requested after its withdrawal from circulation, must be inspected by the competent department to verify that all the conditions imposed thereon in this Law are met in it. 2- Every motor car that undergoes a substantial modification to the engine, chassis, or body must be re-inspected by the competent department, and the significant modifications that require presenting the motor car for a new inspection shall be determined for the Minister of the Interior.

If it appears to the competent department that the motor vehicle, trailer, or semi-trailer that it has inspected satisfies all the imposed conditions, it shall draw up a reception report for it, which shall be relied upon for registration and the issuance of the circulation permit.

Motor cars and trailers whose weight or dimensions exceed the statutory limits, and whose circulation conforms to Article 49 of this Law, shall be subject to a mechanical inspection, and a temporary reception report shall be drawn up for them, which shall be relied upon to issue a temporary circulation permit for a maximum of five renewable days.

The following shall be subject to a mechanical inspection by the competent department: 1- Private passenger motor cars after the lapse of five years from their being put into circulation for the first time in Lebanon or abroad, and after this period they shall be subject to mechanical inspection once every year. 2- Private motor cars provided for in the second paragraph of item (First) of Article (122), private motor cars intended for the transport of loads, and all other motor cars, trailers, and semi-trailers, once every six months. 3- All types of motor cars, vehicles, and trailers, while circulating on the roads, shall be subject to a mechanical inspection conducted at any time whatsoever by the competent department to verify that all the conditions imposed thereon are met.

A permanent committee, one of whose members shall be an engineer specialised in motor car mechanics, shall be formed by a decision of the Minister of the Interior to adjudicate upon appeals relating to the refusal of the competent department to draw up reception reports or inspection reports.

Every owner of a motor car, trailer, or semi-trailer who wishes to put it into circulation for the first time and return it to circulation after its withdrawal therefrom must submit to the competent department a declaration drawn up by him in accordance with the model determined by this department, and must attach to this declaration the customs documents and all the legal instruments proving ownership. Officially accredited agents of motor car and motorcycle manufacturers in Lebanon may be commissioned to carry out the registration formalities for new motorcycles and private passenger motor cars put into circulation for the first time, under conditions to be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of the Interior and of Finance.

The competent department shall deliver to the owner of the vehicle a circulation licence which it shall draw up on the basis of the contents of the receipt record and in which it shall enter the following specifications: - The first name, surname and place of residence of its owner. - The type of vehicle, and the purpose of its use. - Its make and model. - The chassis and engine number. - The number of cylinders and the power of the engine. - Its shape, its colour and the specifications of its body. - Its unladen weight and its net and gross load capacity if the motor vehicle is intended for the transport of loads. - The registration number authorised for it. - The date on which it was put into circulation for the first time. - Special endorsements and remarks. - The number of passengers authorised to be transported and the manner of their distribution. Two children, each aged ten years or under, shall be considered as one passenger. The driver of the vehicle must carry this licence while in circulation and abide by its contents.

The owner of every private vehicle registered in Lebanon who permanently transfers his place of residence abroad must submit to the competent department a written declaration to that effect, to which he shall attach the circulation licence and the registration plates pertaining to the vehicle. Motor vehicles registered under the temporary admission regime shall be exempted from surrendering the plates and the circulation licence, provided that their registration records are settled upon their exit from Lebanese territory, and their circulation thereafter shall be subject to the regime of the International Convention concluded in Geneva on 19 September of the year 1949.

The owner of any registered vehicle must declare to the competent department every modification that occurs to his vehicle with respect to the engine, the chassis, the body or the colour, and must present the vehicle to it together with the circulation licence in order for the necessary corrections to be made thereon.

The owner of any registered private vehicle who wishes to destroy it or withdraw it from circulation, temporarily or permanently, must submit to the competent department a declaration to that effect to which he shall attach the vehicle's circulation licence and its registration plates, and the declaration alone shall suffice in the event that the loss of the licence and the plates as a result of force majeure is proven.
Any person who loses the circulation licence may obtain a copy thereof from the competent department, which must verify that the licence is not impounded.

Motor vehicles shall be divided into five categories: First: Passenger motor vehicles: There shall fall within this category every motor vehicle intended for the transport of persons and the number of whose seats, excluding the driver, is eight or fewer, as well as every motor vehicle equipped with household furniture fixed in its body. It shall be permitted to register as private passenger motor vehicles, motor vehicles the number of whose seats, excluding the driver, is eleven seats or fewer, in favour of schools, airline companies and travel and tourism agencies, on condition that these motor vehicles are designed by their factory as passenger motor vehicles. Second: Autobus motor vehicles: Subject to the provisions of the preceding item, there shall fall within this category every motor vehicle intended for the transport of persons and the number of whose seats, excluding the driver's seat, exceeds eight, as well as every motor vehicle of this type intended for the transport of passengers and goods together. Third: Goods motor vehicles: There shall fall within this category every motor vehicle intended for the transport of loads or goods, as well as every motor vehicle of this type containing refrigerated bodies. Fourth: Passenger and transport motor vehicles: There shall fall within this category every passenger motor vehicle intended at times for the transport of persons and at other times for the transport of loads, as well as every passenger motor vehicle intended for the transport of persons and loads at the same time. Fifth: Special-use motor vehicles: There shall fall within this category every motor vehicle not intended for the transport of loads or persons, but equipped with mechanical machinery for special use, including motor vehicles equipped with weight-lifting machinery, with machinery for prospecting for water, minerals and liquid combustible materials, or with drilling machinery, or with a pump for emptying wells and the like, as well as every motor vehicle equipped with machinery and equipment for photography, cinema and television, mobile repair garages and the like of these motor vehicles, such as motor vehicles for the transport of latrine sediment, motor vehicles equipped with a concrete mixer and motor vehicles equipped with mobile restaurants.
Motor vehicles shall be registered as private or public.

1- A passenger motor vehicle shall be registered as private in the name of its owner (whether a natural or legal person) when transport therein takes place without consideration of whatever kind. 2- Registration as private of passenger motor vehicles the number of whose seats, excluding the driver, exceeds five shall be authorised: - In the name of schools for the purpose of transporting their pupils and their teachers from their homes to the school and vice versa, or for the purpose of transporting pupils on group excursions. - In the name of airline companies and travel and tourism agencies for the purpose of transporting their passengers and their baggage and their workers and their employees, from their headquarters to the airport or to the port and vice versa, without consideration. - In the name of factories and establishments the number of whose employees and workers exceeds twenty-five for the purpose of transporting them without consideration, with the right to transport the tools and parts necessary for carrying out their work. 3- Subject to the provisions of this article, it shall be permitted to register private passenger motor vehicles in the name of Lebanese establishments that represent or are represented by international establishments abroad, provided that they have branches in at least ten foreign countries whose specialty is hiring out private motor vehicles to tourists, on condition that the latter drive the motor vehicles themselves and provided that these motor vehicles have special plates of their own distinguishing them from others. The rules for implementing these provisions shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior, and in all cases these motor vehicles must be insured against all risks, and the supplementary fees specified in the schedule annexed to this Law must be paid. 4- Registration of passenger motor vehicles as private shall be authorised in the name of driving instructors licensed as such, for the purpose of transporting their students to the places of instruction and examination and training them thereon. The competent department shall determine the itinerary for these motor vehicles, which must be distinguished by visible writing on both their sides indicating the purpose of their use, and these motor vehicles must be insured against third-party liability for an amount of not less than twenty-five thousand pounds. 5- It is prohibited to use these motor vehicles for a purpose other than that for which they are authorised.

The vehicle circulation permit shall specify the route that must be followed by the private goods vehicle and the private passenger vehicle indicated in the first paragraph of Article (132) when carrying goods, the types of goods that may be carried, and the number of persons whom it is permitted to carry.

There shall be registered in the category of private passenger vehicles: ambulances belonging to hospitals, official and health institutions, charitable associations, and private institutions whose number of workers exceeds twenty-five workers, as well as vehicles fitted for the transport of the dead. It is prohibited to use these vehicles for other than the purpose for which they are fitted.

A passenger vehicle shall be registered as public if the applicant for registration submits the plates of a passenger vehicle registered as public that is intended to be withdrawn from public circulation. A public plate may not be transferred from one name to another unless the beneficiary of the transfer presents a vehicle to which the transferred plate is to be allocated.

1- A bus vehicle shall be registered as public if the applicant for registration submits the plates of a bus vehicle registered as public that is intended to be withdrawn from public circulation. 2- If the number of seats of the bus vehicle requested to be registered exceeds the number of seats in the vehicle to which the submitted registration plates belong, the applicant for registration must pay for each missing seat an amount of one thousand Lebanese pounds. 3- If the registration holder submits the plates of a bus vehicle whose number of seats exceeds the seats of the vehicle intended to be registered, the excess seats submitted shall be deemed cancelled ipso jure. 4- In all cases, it is not permissible to subdivide or merge plates, nor is it permissible to transfer a public plate from one name to another unless the beneficiary of the transfer presents a vehicle to which the transferred plate is to be allocated.

A vehicle shall always be deemed a bus vehicle if it is originally of this category, even though it is fitted at the same time for the transport of persons and goods, and the conditions imposed in the preceding Article shall apply to its registration as public, provided that at least half of it remains dedicated to the transport of passengers and that the net load of the goods that it can carry is determined on the basis of 70 kilograms for each seat that it lacks, provided that the gross load does not exceed the technically licensed load.

1- A goods vehicle shall be registered if the applicant for registration submits the plates of a goods vehicle registered as public that is intended to be withdrawn from public circulation. 2- If the goods vehicle requested to be registered as public has a net load exceeding the net load of the vehicle intended to be withdrawn from circulation, the applicant for registration must pay, in consideration of the difference in net load, one hundred Lebanese pounds for every one hundred kilograms or fraction of one hundred kilograms. 3- And if the applicant for registration submits the plates of a goods vehicle whose net load exceeds the load of the vehicle intended to be registered, the excess load shall be deemed cancelled ipso jure. 4- In all cases, it is not permissible to subdivide or merge plates, nor is it permissible to transfer a public plate from one name to another unless the beneficiary of the transfer presents a vehicle to which the transferred plate is to be allocated.

Plates of public vehicles shall not be surrendered on a temporary basis except for the purpose of withdrawing them from circulation with a view to registering other public vehicles, provided that in all cases the duration of their surrender does not exceed one week of working days.

The vehicle or combination of vehicles mentioned in the fifth paragraph of Article (122) of this Law may be registered as private in the name of its owner. And it shall be subject to the fees specified in the schedule annexed to this Law.

The provisions of this Second Section relating to registration shall not apply: First: To vehicles subject to the regime of the International Convention on International Transport concluded in Geneva on 19 September 1949, or registered in contiguous countries with which a special agreement has been concluded, provided that their circulation permits are in order. Second: To vehicles of foreign tourists and summer visitors; these persons shall be granted a temporary admission permit by the Customs, provided that the vehicle circulation permit is legal in the country of its registration, that the period of the Customs authorisation does not exceed the period of validity of the circulation permit, and that the vehicle is insured against third parties. Third: To vehicles bearing trial or transit plates provided for in Articles (102) and (103) of this Law. Fourth: To vehicles of the Army and the Security Forces registered in special categories.

No one may drive a motor car or motor vehicle without holding a driving licence issued by the competent department for the class of motor car or motor vehicle that he drives. And the driver must carry this licence while driving the vehicle.

Driving licences shall be divided into the following categories: First: A driving licence for motorcycles. Second: Driving licences for passenger vehicles or for transport vehicles whose gross weight does not exceed 3500 kilograms. Third: Driving licences for transport vehicles whose gross weight exceeds 3500 kilograms and does not exceed 10000 kilograms. Fourth: Driving licences for transport vehicles whose gross weight exceeds 10000 kilograms, and for the vehicles provided for in paragraph (5) of Article (123), and vehicles with a tractor, trailer, and semi-trailer. Fifth: Driving licences for agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment. Sixth: Driving licences for private passenger vehicles and motorcycles fitted for the transport of persons and driven by persons with physical disabilities, provided that the motor car or motorcycle is specially fitted for them in accordance with their conditions.
There shall be stated in the driving licence the category or categories of vehicles licensed to be driven.

The minimum age for applicants for driving licences shall be determined as follows: First: Eighteen full years for applicants for driving licences for private passenger vehicles and motorcycles. Second: Twenty-one full years for applicants for driving licences for public passenger vehicles and goods vehicles whose gross weight does not exceed 3500 kilograms. Third: Twenty-five full years for applicants for driving licences for goods vehicles whose gross weight exceeds 3500 kilograms and bus vehicles.

Drivers of vehicles with electric motors shall be exempted from the driving licence if the power of their motor does not exceed one kilowatt, and the competent department must verify, where necessary, the power of these motors.

The Motor Car and Vehicle Registration Service in the Ministry of the Interior shall issue driving licences for agricultural machinery and public works equipment, and the Service may, when conducting an examination for the issuance of these licences, seek the assistance of employees from the Central Garage in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport.
A driving licence shall be issued only to a person who has actual residence in Lebanon.
Driving licences, in respect of passenger vehicles, shall be divided into two types: First: Private driving licences. Second: Public driving licences.

A private driving licence shall entitle its holder to drive a private passenger vehicle, provided that he is not hired by third parties, and a public driving licence shall entitle its holder to drive a public or private passenger vehicle for remuneration.

Article 152: A driving licence of whatever kind shall not be granted: First: Until after the lapse of two years from the date of completion of the execution of the sentence for any person sentenced to imprisonment for a period exceeding three months for having committed serious driving accidents without holding a driving licence. Second: Until after the lapse of one year from the aforementioned date for any person sentenced for the same reason to imprisonment for a period not exceeding three months. Third: To any person addicted to intoxicants (for this purpose, any person who is a recidivist shall be deemed addicted). Fourth: To any person who consumes, uses, manufactures, prepares, possesses, transports, trades in, imports, exports, or brokers narcotics, or performs any act whatsoever relating to narcotics. Every driver who is sentenced for one of these offences shall be punished, in addition to the penalties provided for in the Law on Narcotics, by the withdrawal of his licence for a period of three months the first time, and permanently the second time; the period of withdrawal of the licence shall commence from the date of completion of the execution of the penalty of imprisonment.

Article 153: A driving licence shall only be granted to Lebanese nationals, and after the rehabilitation of any person who has been convicted of a felony or one of the following offences: Theft - Fraud - Breach of trust - Cheque without provision - Embezzlement Rape - Blackmail - Forgery - Use of a forged instrument - Offences offending public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code - Offences relating to trading with the enemy or transporting passengers or goods to and from its territory. A judgment may be passed cancelling every public driving licence whose holder becomes the subject of a final judgment for having committed one of the offences set forth above.

Article 154: 1- Every person who wishes to obtain a driving licence must submit an application to that effect to the competent department, stating therein: - His given name and surname. - His place of residence. - His place and date of birth. - The category or categories of the licence which he wishes to obtain. - The type of licence: public or private. 2- He must attach to the application: - His identity card or his passport. - An extract of the judicial record dating back less than three months. - Five copies of his photograph measuring 4x44 centimetres - A medical certificate dating back less than three months proving that his state of health allows him to drive the category or categories of vehicles for which the driving licence is requested. - A receipt from the Treasury chest proving that he has paid the fee due for the examination. 3- The Minister of the Interior, after taking the opinion of the Ministry of Health, shall determine the physical disabilities that are incompatible with the conditions for obtaining a driving licence, and the physical disabilities whose bearers may be granted a driving licence under specific conditions. 4- The competent department shall appoint the date and place of the examination. 5- The conditions of the examination relating to the driving of motor vehicles, with the exception of public works vehicles and their equipment, shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior, whereas the conditions of the examination relating thereto shall be determined by a decision of the Ministers of the Interior and of Public Works and Transport.

Article 155: A driving licence shall only be granted if the applicant therefor passes, before a committee appointed by the Minister of the Interior, a technical test to verify his ability in driving and operating a motor car, and his knowledge of the Traffic Law and its regulations. An applicant for a public driving licence must also prove that he is conversant with the structure of the engine, the brakes, the transmission, the steering, and the lighting, and that he has a thorough knowledge of the Traffic Law and its regulations. A licence to drive public passenger cars shall only be granted to a person who holds a private driving licence, and a licence to drive goods vehicles and buses shall only be granted to a person who holds a licence to drive public passenger cars.

Article 156: If an applicant for a licence fails the test mentioned in the preceding Article, he shall be prohibited from sitting a new test before the lapse of a period of: - Fifteen days from the date of the first test. - One month from the date of the second test and the tests following it.

Article 157: A - The test shall be deemed null and void ipso jure if the applicant for a licence sits it: First: During one of the periods mentioned in the preceding Article. Second: During the period in which the driver is not entitled to drive a vehicle following the issuance of an administrative order or a judicial judgment withdrawing his previous licence. Third: If the applicant submits false particulars relating to his identity or if he substitutes one person for another for the test or attempts to substitute him. B - Every driving licence obtained by the applicant in one of the cases mentioned above shall be immediately withdrawn administratively, without prejudice to the necessary criminal prosecutions against him.

Article 158: If the result of the test is satisfactory, the committee shall draw up a record thereof which shall be referred to the Motor Vehicles and Machinery Registration Service, entitling the applicant for the licence to obtain a driving licence of the category or categories mentioned in his application.
Article 159: The holder of a driving licence for a specific category of vehicles may not use it to drive a vehicle of another category.

Article 160: Every applicant for a licence who fails to appear for the test or the examination on the day and at the hour appointed for him for any reason whatsoever shall forfeit the amount of the fee which he has paid.
Article 161: No fee shall be refunded, even in part, to an applicant for a licence who fails the test.

Article 162: The driving licence shall be dated and numbered in accordance with the order in which it is granted and registered, and the category or categories of motor cars and vehicles which the driver is permitted to drive shall be recorded in the registration and in the licence. It must bear: - A photograph of the licensed driver. - The driver's given name, surname, his mother's name, and his place of residence. - His date and place of birth. - A stamp to the value of five pounds.

Article 163: Licences to drive private passenger cars and motorcycles shall be subject to a renewal endorsement, extending their validity, every five years, after the holder thereof reaches the age of fifty. All remaining licences shall be subject to a renewal endorsement extending their validity, every five years until the holder thereof reaches the age of fifty, and every three years after this age. The renewal endorsement shall only be granted if the holder of the licence submits a new medical certificate in accordance with the rules set forth in paragraph (2) of Article (154) of this Law, in addition to a copy of his judicial record. The Speaker and members of the Chamber of Deputies, the President and members of the Council of Ministers, judges, civil and military State employees, and members of the diplomatic and consular corps shall be exempted from submitting a copy of the judicial record.

Article 164: 1- The period of validity of a driving licence may be limited if it appears that the applicant therefor is afflicted with a disability that does not currently prevent him from driving, but which may worsen later. 2- If it appears, after the delivery of the licence, that the holder thereof is afflicted with a temporary or permanent infirmity that is incompatible with the conditions prescribed for obtaining the licence, the Minister of the Interior shall have the right to decide to cancel it permanently or to limit the period of its validity.
Article 165: The disabilities referred to in Article (154) of this Law shall subject the bearer thereof to the provisions of the second paragraph of the preceding Article (164)
Article 166: If a driving licence is lost, its owner may obtain a duplicate thereof, after an investigation conducted by the Administration.

The provisions of this Section shall not apply to: First: Drivers holding international driving licences for the category of motor vehicles indicated in their licences. Second: Drivers holding driving licences of the model set forth in the Ninth Annex to the International Convention on Road Traffic concluded in Geneva on 19 September 1949, and within the period of validity of the licence. Third: Drivers of Army and Security Forces motor vehicles who must carry driving permits granted to them by the said authorities, provided that such permits shall be valid only for driving Army and Security Forces motor vehicles. Fourth: Persons who enter Lebanon for the purpose of tourism and summering and carry driving licences other than those indicated in the preceding first and second paragraphs, which they have obtained from the authorities of the countries to which they belong, provided that they obtain, by way of exception, from the competent department an endorsement on their licences authorising them to use them within Lebanese territory for a period of six months renewable once only for another six months, if the validity of the licence so permits. Fifth: Drivers who carry driving licences granted to them by countries with which a special agreement has been concluded.

Foreign driving licences may be exchanged for Lebanese driving licences, if the licence requested to be exchanged is an international licence or a licence of the model set forth in the Ninth Annex to the International Convention on Road Traffic concluded in Geneva on 19 September 1949, provided that such exchange is effected within the period of validity of the licence specified therein only

Military driving permits granted by the higher authorities in the Army and the Internal Security Forces to officers may be exchanged for private driving licences for the category of vehicles indicated in their permits without subjecting them to the examination mentioned in Article (155) of this Law

1- Subject to the provisions of Article (138) of this Law, it is strictly prohibited to transport animals or goods inside motor buses. 2- Motor vehicles are prohibited from circulating without doors or without a bonnet for the engine compartment or mudguards (fenders) for the rear wheels, and goods motor vehicles are also prohibited from leaving the rear door of their body hanging down while in motion, or transporting any load outside their bodies. 3- It is permitted to transport passengers' suitcases and luggage on the roof of motor buses and touring motor vehicles provided that their height does not exceed one metre for motor buses, and half a metre for touring motor vehicles, and that they do not in any case project beyond the exterior contour of the motor vehicle.

1- Goods motor vehicles are licensed to transport two persons beside the driver provided that the length of the seat is not less than the dimensions determined by the Minister of the Interior 2- Goods motor vehicles are licensed to transport up to three workers in their body, with or without a load, provided that they are equipped with the necessary seats.

The driver of a motor vehicle or a combination of vehicles must produce upon every request addressed to him by an officer of the competent authorities: 1- The driving licence. 2- The circulation licence of the motor vehicle or combination which he is driving. 3- All other documents required by this Law or any subsequent traffic regulations

The provisions of Title One and the provisions of this Title shall apply to the following vehicles: A - Agricultural vehicles and equipment, which are defined as follows: 1- Agricultural tractor: a self-propelled vehicle specially manufactured to tow or operate equipment intended for agricultural exploitation, and not equipped with tracks. 2- Mobile agricultural machine: a machine capable of circulating by its own means intended for agricultural exploitation. 3- Agricultural trailers and semi-trailers: vehicles coupled to an agricultural tractor used to transport crops, materials and equipment necessary for agriculture to or from an agricultural enterprise and used, where necessary, to transport the workers of such enterprise. B - Public works vehicles: a self-propelled vehicle specially manufactured for a public works enterprise or to tow or operate equipment intended for public works, not equipped with tracks, and not used to transport materials and goods on roads. C - Public works equipment: equipment specially manufactured for a public works enterprise and not used to transport goods, materials and persons on roads. The Minister of the Interior shall determine public works vehicles and equipment pursuant to special schedules.

The provisions of Articles (55) to (59) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and to their trailers and semi-trailers, and the provisions of Articles (52) and (53) shall also apply to trailers and semi-trailers.

If the agricultural vehicles and equipment are not equipped with pneumatic tyres, their pressure on the ground may not exceed at any time one hundred and fifty kilograms per single centimetre of the width of the tyre.

The Minister of the Interior shall determine the characteristics and specifications that must be met in the metallic tyres with which agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment are equipped, and the grip chains used where necessary and on their pneumatic tyres.
Equipment and tractors equipped with tracks may not be put into circulation on public roads.
The provisions of Articles (62) and (63) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment only when they are in motion on public roads.
The provisions of Article (64) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment only when they are in motion on public roads.
Movable or easily detachable parts of the vehicles or equipment mentioned in this Title shall be folded inwards while in motion on the public road.

The provisions of Articles (65) to (68) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment - however, public works equipment shall be exempted from the provisions of Article (66) if the width of its load does not exceed, in any case, the width of the towing vehicle.
The provisions of Article (69) of this Law shall apply to agricultural tractors, mobile agricultural machines and public works equipment.

If the driver's field of vision in every direction is not sufficient to enable him to drive in complete safety, another person must guide him to proceed safely. The provisions of Articles (74) to (76) of this Law shall apply to mobile tractors and public works equipment. However, the rear-view mirror mentioned in Article (76) is unnecessary in vehicles and equipment not equipped with a closed cabin for the driver. Agricultural tractors shall be subject to the provisions of Article (75), and if one of these vehicles is equipped with a windscreen, it must be fitted with a windscreen wiper.
The provisions of Articles (79) and (81) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment.

The provisions of Articles (82) to (87) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment when they are in motion or stationary on roads at night and during fog.

The provisions of Article (85) of this Law shall apply to towed agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment when they are in motion or stationary on roads at night and during fog. And if such vehicles and equipment do not meet the conditions provided for in Article (85), they may be operated by means of a lamp with a red light placed on their left side.

Where the width of self-propelled agricultural machines or of towed agricultural machines or equipment, or the width of self-propelled or towed public works equipment, exceeds two and a half metres, the towing vehicle shall bear at the top of its front end a square plate illuminated at night and visible from the front and from the rear of the vehicle up to a distance of one hundred and fifty metres without being dazzling, and displaying in white on a black background the word "Danger" with a height of at least twenty centimetres. Where the plate is not visible from the rear of the vehicle or combination, the last towed vehicle shall bear at its rear end a retro-reflective device displaying, in white on a black background, the word "Danger" with the same dimensions mentioned above.

Agricultural vehicles or equipment or public works equipment may, in order to facilitate their work at night, be fitted with lighting devices other than the devices mentioned in this Section, and such devices may not be used on roads.

The Minister of the Interior shall determine by a decision issued by him the characteristics that must be met by the lighting and signalling devices fitted to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment and, where necessary, their position and the conditions for their installation so as to conform to the provisions of this Section, and he may prohibit the use of devices that do not conform to the prescribed devices.

Self-propelled agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment shall be fitted with an audible warning device the sound power of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior.
The provisions of Article (97) of this Law shall apply to motor vehicles assigned to agriculture and public works.

The provisions of Article (99) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment, provided that only one registration plate is affixed at the rear; whereas animal-drawn carts and hand-drawn equipment shall be fitted with one registration plate which the municipalities shall undertake to install and stamp.

Agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment shall be fitted with an identification plate called an "operating plate" indicating the nature of the work they perform, which shall be affixed at the rear end of the vehicle in a visible and non-removable manner.
The Minister of the Interior shall determine the models of this plate and the manner of its installation.
The Minister of the Interior shall determine the conditions for the application of this Section to public works equipment where necessary.

The provisions of Article (108) of this Law shall apply to agricultural trailers, towed agricultural machines and equipment, and towed public works equipment when their total weight, including the authorised load, exceeds one and a half tonnes.
The maximum speed of agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment on public roads shall be fixed at thirty kilometres per hour.
The provisions of Articles 111, 112, 113 and 115 of this Law shall apply to agricultural and public works vehicles and equipment.

Agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles, their equipment and their trailers shall, while travelling on roads, be subject to an unscheduled mechanical inspection carried out by the competent department.

Agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment shall be subject to the provisions of Articles 116 to 121 of this Law and shall be registered as private, provided that the provisions of Articles 131 and 134 of this Law shall apply to them when they tow a trailer.
The provisions of Articles 102 to 107 shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment intended for testing or for export abroad.

The Minister of the Interior may exempt from the provisions of Article 200 of this Law certain agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment owned by the State, municipalities and public institutions.
The Minister of the Interior may subject to certain provisions of this Title certain special equipment the speed of which, by construction, does not exceed twenty-five kilometres per hour.

1- No person may drive an agricultural vehicle or public works equipment on public roads without holding a driving licence issued by the competent department and valid for the category of vehicle he is driving. 2- The minimum age for an applicant for a licence of this category shall be fixed at eighteen completed years.

The issue of the driving licences set out in this Section shall be subject to the provisions of Articles 152 and 154 to 163 of this Law, and such licences shall entitle their holders to be employed for remuneration by third parties provided that they are Lebanese.

The driver of agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment shall produce to traffic inspectors and upon every request by the competent authorities a driving licence, the vehicle circulation permit and all other documents required by this Law or any subsequent traffic regulations.

Every two-wheeled or three-wheeled motor vehicle equipped with a thermal engine and the unladen weight of which does not exceed four hundred kilograms, as well as every vehicle of this kind having four wheels specially constructed to be driven by persons with physical disabilities, shall be deemed a motorcycle.
The provisions of Articles (60) and (61) of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Title.

The provisions of Article 65 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Title, and the dimensions of the load are prohibited in any case from exceeding, in width or in length, the perimeter of the body of the vehicle, and drivers of cycles of all kinds are prohibited from carrying articles likely to impede driving or to constitute a danger to traffic. However, two-wheeled motorcycles fitted by their manufacturer with a seat behind the driver, footrests and a handhold are permitted to carry one person on that seat.
The provisions of Articles 69 and 71 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Title.
The provisions of Articles 72, 73, 76 and 78 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Title.

The provisions of Articles 79 and 81 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Part; however, if the motorcycle is not designed for the transport of loads, there shall be no need for the brake therein to remain engaged during the absence of the driver.

1- Motorcycles must be equipped at the front with one or two position lights, a driving light, and a passing light fulfilling the conditions stipulated in Articles 82 to 84 of this Law. 2- These vehicles must be equipped at the rear with one or two lights fulfilling the conditions stipulated in Articles 85 and 87 of this Law. If the motorcycle is fitted with a sidecar, it must be equipped at the front with a position light and at the rear with a red light.

1- The vehicles mentioned in this Part may be equipped with the lights set forth in Article 90 of this Law. 2- If two-wheeled motorcycles are without a sidecar, they may be parked without being lit, alongside the pavement or on the edge of the road.
The vehicles mentioned in this Part must be fitted with a light-reflecting device
The vehicles mentioned in this Part may be fitted with the devices set forth in Articles 88 and 89.
The provisions of Article 93 shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Part.
The vehicles mentioned in this Part must be equipped with a warning device the sound power of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior.
Vehicles of the Army, the Security Forces, and the Fire Brigade may be equipped with special warning devices in addition to the ordinary warning devices.
The provisions of Articles 97, 99, and 107 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Part. A single registration plate affixed to the rear of the vehicle shall suffice
The provisions of Articles 111, 112, and 115 and the third paragraph of Article 114 shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Part.
The provisions of Articles 116 to 121 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Part.
Three-wheeled motorcycles shall be registered as private for their use in the transport of goods, provided that such registration is subject to the provisions of Articles 131 and 134 of this Law.
The provisions of Articles 143, 144, 146, 149, 152, and 154 to 166 of this Law shall apply to motorcycles.
The driver of a motorcycle must present to traffic inspectors, and upon every request from the competent authority, a driving licence and the vehicle circulation permit.
Every vehicle having two, three, or four wheels and not equipped with an engine, but propelled by the power of its rider, shall be considered an ordinary bicycle.
Riders of ordinary bicycles are prohibited from riding side by side except in the case of overtaking, and they must permanently keep to the extreme right of the carriageway and in a straight line.
When a section of the road is designated for the circulation of ordinary bicycles, riders of these bicycles must keep to this section.

Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (7) of the sixth Article of this Law, two-wheeled ordinary bicycles shall be permitted to proceed on pavements if their riders are leading them by hand while walking. Provided that the width of the pavements allows for this.

Two-wheeled ordinary bicycles may proceed on pavements and pathways designated for pedestrians on paved roads that are under repair, and located outside inhabited areas. In this case, riders must proceed at a moderate pace when encountering pedestrians, and near houses.

Riders of two-wheeled ordinary bicycles are prohibited from carrying a second person with them; however, ordinary bicycles are permitted to be equipped with a basket designed to carry certain items the weight of which does not exceed 25 kilograms.
An ordinary bicycle must be equipped with two effective brakes.

At night and during the day, if circumstances so require, an ordinary bicycle must be equipped at the front with a single light emitting forward a non-dazzling light and at the rear with a red light visible from behind. Ordinary bicycles may be operated on public roads without a light if they are led by hand, and in this case those leading them must comply with the regulations imposed on pedestrians.
An ordinary bicycle must be equipped, day and night, at the rear with a device that reflects or emits backward a non-dazzling red light.
If the ordinary bicycle has three wheels and includes a "side basket" designated for carrying certain items, the outermost edge of the basket must be equipped with a non-dazzling red marker light.
An ordinary bicycle must be equipped with a warning device (a bell) or a "rotary chime" audible at a distance of at least 25 metres, and the use of any other warning device is prohibited.

Pedestrians must use the pavements or passages reserved for them where they exist, and if it is impossible for them to do so, they must not go beyond the boundaries of the pavements and passages except after verifying that they are able to do so without any danger.

Pedestrians walking on the carriageway must keep to its edges, and they must move to the furthest edge nearest to them upon hearing the warning of any vehicle or animals approaching them, as well as on bends, road junctions, and the tops of slopes and upon approaching these locations, and in general in every place where visibility is insufficient.

Pedestrians must not cross the carriageway except after verifying that they are able to do so without any danger, and they must cross it at the locations designated for this purpose where they exist, and in this latter case they shall have priority of passage in the absence of an electric light signal or a security officer to direct traffic.

The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to formations of the Army and Security Forces, nor to pedestrian processions marching in an organised manner or funeral processions. However, these formations and processions must keep to one side of the carriageway so as to leave the other side thereof free as far as possible for the passage of at least one vehicle. Where they consist of several detachments, they must leave between one detachment and the next a space sufficient for vehicles to pass one another.

The driving of herds and of single or grouped animals walking on the road must be ensured in such a manner as not to result in any obstruction to public traffic and to allow them to be overtaken or passed under satisfactory conditions.

Drovers of herds or of single or grouped animals must indicate them, especially at their rear, by a light carried in the hand, which is clearly visible at night, outside built-up areas whose roads are lit. These provisions shall not apply to horsemen or to drovers of animals walking on roads not used by motor-equipped vehicles.
It is prohibited to leave any animal on public roads, and it is prohibited to halt herds on the carriageway.

Motor cars, motorcycles, agricultural tractors, public works equipment, and in general all motor vehicles shall be registered in special registers or cards with the Motor Vehicles and Machinery Registration Department, whereas ordinary bicycles, animal-drawn carts, and hand-drawn vehicles and equipment shall be registered at municipal offices.
The registers mentioned in the preceding Article shall be numbered and stamped by the head of the competent department, and their contents shall be acted upon unless their forgery is proved.

With the exception of the cases provided for in the Law issued on 20 May 1935, concerning the sale of motor cars and by instalment, it shall not be permissible to sell or mortgage motor cars, motorcycles, agricultural tractors, and all motor vehicles subject to registration pursuant to Article 269 except at the Registration Department and through the commissioned officer. Any sale or mortgage taking place outside this Department shall have no effect against a third party or before the State, and anyone who participates in violating the provisions of this Article shall be deemed an accomplice in liability.

In the case of a mortgage of motor cars, motorcycles, agricultural tractors, and all motor vehicles subject to registration pursuant to Article 269, the mortgaged object may remain in the possession of the debtor, provided that the mortgage contract expressly stipulates this.

The officials entrusted with keeping the registers or entrusted with hearing all kinds of contracts relating to vehicles shall take, before the court in whose jurisdiction their place of work is located and prior to commencing this work, the following oath: "I swear to perform my duty with honesty and fidelity". These officials may hear contracts in private sittings upon an application submitted by one of the contracting parties to the competent head of unit, in return for a travel allowance determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior, to be provided by the person concerned together with the means of transport.

A - If an accident occurs, the driver must stop his vehicle immediately; if the damage is purely material, he must stop and not resume his journey until after he has declared to the injured party the number of his vehicle, his name, and his address, together with the name and address of the owner of the vehicle. If any person is injured and the wounds of the injured person render him unable to move, the driver of the vehicle must transport him in his vehicle to the nearest place in order to provide him with the necessary medical first aid. Where necessary, the driver must go in person and fetch a doctor, and return the injured person to his home, and it shall not be permissible to go in person and fetch a doctor, and return the injured person to his home, and it shall not be permissible for the driver to leave the scene of the accident permanently before he has been questioned by officers of the public force. If the driver is exposed to any danger to his person or his vehicle as a result of remaining at the scene of the accident, he may leave the place heading for the nearest post of the public force to report the matter to it and return in its company to the scene of the accident. In this case, he shall not be punished on account of this flight of his. B - Owners of motor cars and motor vehicles shall be obliged to take out insurance on their motor cars and motor vehicles against civil liability towards third parties. The rules and conditions for the application of the provisions of this insurance shall be determined by a subsequent law.
The fees required to be collected for everything relating to vehicles of all kinds are set out in the Schedule annexed to this Law.
The following penalties shall apply to traffic contraventions in addition to the penalties provided for in the Penal Code.

Contraventions of the provisions of this Law shall be classified, with respect to the penalties entailed thereby, into three categories as follows: A - Category One contraventions: which are those set out in Contraventions Schedule No. (1) annexed to this Law, punishable by imprisonment for up to two months and by a fine ranging between /35/ pounds and /100/ Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties. B - Category Two contraventions: which are those set out in Contraventions Schedule No. (2) annexed to this Law, punishable by imprisonment for up to one month, and by a fine ranging between /15/ pounds and /100/ Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties. C - Category Three contraventions: which are those set out in Contraventions Schedule No. (3) annexed to this Law, punishable by up to ten days' imprisonment and by a pecuniary fine ranging between five pounds and /25/ Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, with the exception of pedestrian traffic contraventions, which shall be punishable only by a pecuniary fine in the amount of two pounds.
