1- Contraventions not listed in the three Schedules mentioned in the preceding Article shall be deemed Category Three contraventions. 2- Contraventions of the provisions of decisions issued by the administrative and municipal authorities in execution of the provisions of this Law shall also be deemed Category Three contraventions if they are not punishable under another text.

The public prosecution action shall be deemed extinguished in respect of contraventions if the offender pays, within ten days from the date of being notified of the record, the equivalent of the amount of the fine provided for in Article 296 concerning the immediate fine.

Certain judicial penalties shall be accompanied by measures requiring the impoundment of the vehicle or the withdrawal of the driving and circulation licences, or either of them, as set out in the Schedules annexed to this Law. The duration of impoundment decided by the judge shall range between five days and three months and may reach six months in the event of recidivism.

The conditions for carrying out the seizure of motor vehicles and vehicles of all kinds, or their impoundment, custody, guardianship, the duration of impoundment, and the lifting thereof, shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and the Interior. This decree shall also include the conditions for selling seized and impounded motor vehicles and vehicles of all kinds in the event that their owner fails to claim them within a specified period and fails to pay the fees and expenses incurred thereon. This article shall apply to all motor vehicles and vehicles under seizure or impoundment on the date this Law is put into effect.

A motor vehicle may be seized in the possession of its owner in special cases determined in the decree provided for in the preceding article. Driving a motor vehicle seized in the possession of its owner shall be deemed an infraction of the first category, and this shall result in its seizure in the possession of a third party and the withdrawal of the driving licence from its owner for a period of six months.

Custodians of seized motor vehicles shall be deemed judicial receivers with all the legal consequences arising therefrom, and in return therefor they shall receive a daily allowance borne by the owner of the motor vehicle, the value of which shall be determined by the decree referred to in Article 281, and the conditions required to be met by the judicial receiver shall be determined in the same decree.

1- Infractions of the provisions of this Law shall be established by offence reports drawn up by: - Members of the Internal Security Forces. - Members of the Municipal Police. - Sworn employees of the Motor Vehicle and Mechanised Equipment Registration Service commissioned by a decision of the Minister of the Interior, in respect of infractions of a mechanical nature and excess load infractions. 2- The reports shall be drawn up in a number of copies equal to the number of competent administrations to which they will be sent, in addition to one copy to be delivered to the perpetrator of the infraction. 3- When drawing up an offence report for an infraction against the registration number of a vehicle, the descriptions of this vehicle must be established in the report as far as possible (such as its colour, type or make, etc.). 4- These reports shall be deemed authentic until the contrary is proven.

All infractions of the provisions of this Law shall be subject to the procedures provided for in Articles 182-190 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. However, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, in the event that the objection is dismissed, the penalty imposed may not be increased, by a reasoned decision.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 186 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the service of judgments issued in traffic cases that include a pecuniary penalty only shall be effected by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt to the address declared by the perpetrator of the infraction to the issuer of the offence report or with the Motor Vehicle and Mechanised Equipment Registration Service.

The registered letter shall be delivered to the offender or to one of the adult members of his family residing with him in a single dwelling, and service shall be deemed effected if the addressee refuses to receive the letter or if the postman does not find him on the third delivery round.

An infraction shall be deemed a single infraction between the point of departure of the vehicle and the point to which it is heading, unless it was possible to remedy the same infraction along the way.

The infractions provided for in this Law shall be adjudicated by single judges, each within his district. The Minister of Justice may commission additional single judges whose jurisdiction shall be to hear traffic cases only, in centres where such cases are numerous. When adjudicating the infraction report, judges must take into consideration the judgments that preceded it.

There shall be established alongside the headquarters of the Motor Vehicle and Mechanised Equipment Registration Service, and in each of its branches in the governorates, an office that shall undertake the functions of the judicial record for traffic infractions in respect of which final judgments have been issued and the execution of these judgments, and this office shall be subordinate to the Internal Security Forces. The competent courts shall send to these offices the final judgments issued in respect of these infractions. The completion of transactions in the Motor Vehicle and Mechanised Equipment Registration Service and its branches shall be contingent upon the person concerned presenting a clearance certificate from the competent office proving payment of the fines imposed, provided that the date of this clearance does not go back more than one month.

1- For every infraction of the third category and every infraction punishable under Article 770 of the Penal Code, the perpetrator thereof shall be punished by double the penalty prescribed therefor if a judgment has been issued against him within one year for the same infraction. In the event of repeating this infraction for the second time within the said period, the offender shall be punished as though he had committed an infraction of the second category. 2- For every infraction of the second category, the perpetrator thereof shall be punished by double the penalty prescribed by law if a final judgment has been issued against him less than one year prior for the same infraction. In the event of repeating the same infraction for the second time within the said period, the offender shall be punished as though he had committed an infraction of the first category. 3- For every infraction of the first category, the perpetrator thereof shall be punished by double the penalty prescribed by law if a final judgment has been issued against him less than one year prior for the same infraction. In the event of repeating the same infraction for the second time within the said period, the offender shall be punished by at least the maximum penalty prescribed therefor. 4- In addition to the penalties set out in paragraph three above, upon the commission of the infraction committed for the second time, a sentence shall be passed withdrawing the driving permit for a minimum period of one month. For an infraction committed for the third time, a sentence shall be passed withdrawing the driving permit for a period of at least six months, as well as for every subsequent infraction of the first category. The provisions of Article 254 of the Penal Code relating to mitigating causes shall not apply to the pecuniary penalties provided for in this Law. In cases where drawing up the report constitutes an impediment to traffic flow, the Minister of the Interior may, exceptionally and by a decision from him, authorise members of the security forces to administratively withdraw the driving licence for a period not exceeding twenty-four hours, in addition to the penalties provided for in this Law.

In addition to the penalties imposed by the courts in traffic accidents, the judge may order the withdrawal of the licence for a period he determines according to the circumstances of the case. The permanent withdrawal of the licence may be ordered in the case of repeated grave faults.

1- By a decision of the Minister of the Interior, members of the Internal Security Forces shall be appointed and authorised to collect immediate fines for traffic infractions. 2- The infractions for which immediate fines are collected shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior. The procedures for recording these infractions shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior. 3- Any person commissioned to record infractions and collect immediate fines therefor shall have the capacity of a public accountant. He shall be subject to the regulations relating to public accountants, with the exception of the obligation to provide a guarantee.

1- By a decision of the Minister of the Interior, after consulting the opinion of the Minister of Finance, the conditions for collecting immediate fines and the methods of paying them to the Treasury shall be determined. 2- Twenty per cent of the proceeds of fines collected immediately shall be allocated in favour of the Reserve Fund of the Internal Security Forces. 3- Twenty per cent of the proceeds of the total fines collected for traffic infractions shall also be allocated in favour of the municipalities, and these allocations shall be distributed among the municipalities in accordance with the principles adopted in distributing the allocations of municipalities from common fees.

If the perpetrator of one of the infractions provided for in Article 293 refuses to pay the fine immediately, an ordinary offence report shall be drawn up against him, and the general procedures shall apply to him.
This Law determines the rules for the preparation of the State budget, its execution, the settlement of its accounts, and the administration of public funds and funds deposited in the Treasury.
The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 14315 dated 4/11/1963 is hereby put into effect, the text of which is as follows:
Public funds are the funds of the State, municipalities, public institutions attached to the State or municipalities, and the funds of all other legal persons of a public nature.
This Decree shall be published and notified wherever required.
The budget is a legislative instrument in which the expenditures and revenues of the State are estimated for a coming year, and pursuant to which collection and expenditure are authorised.
The budget consists of the law of the summary and detailed schedules annexed thereto.

The budget law is the text containing the approval by the legislative authority of the draft budget.

This law contains basic provisions stipulating the estimation of expenditures and revenues, the authorisation of collection, and the opening of credits necessary for expenditure, as well as special provisions limited to matters directly related to the execution of the budget.

The State budget consists of the general budget, annexed budgets, and extraordinary budgets.

Annexed budgets and extraordinary budgets are established by special laws, and the provisions of this Law apply to them, unless the special provisions governing them contain contrary texts.
The budget is drawn up for a financial year commencing on the first of January and ending on 31 December.
Revenues and expenditures shall be recorded in the budget accounts of the year during which they were actually collected or paid.

Material errors and errors in imputation may be corrected by a decision of the Minister of Finance issued at the request of the competent administration up to the fifteenth of March of the following year.

The time limit for the correction of material errors in imputations provided for in this Article is extended for up to three months

The budget is divided into two parts:

1- The expenditures part, which includes the credits opened to meet these expenditures.

2- The revenues part, which includes the revenues allocated to cover these credits.

Credits are of two types:

- Basic, which are those opened pursuant to the budget law.

- Additional, which are those added to the basic credits after the publication of the budget. Additional credits are of two types:

- Supplementary, which are those opened to meet a shortfall in a specific item.

- Extraordinary, which are those opened to meet an expenditure for which no credit was originally allocated in the budget.

Credits shall only be opened within the scope of the budgets mentioned in Article 6.

However, it is exceptionally permissible to open a credit in a budget prior to its ratification, provided that it is recorded therein.

Each minister shall draw up, before the end of the month of May of the year, a draft of the expenditures of his ministry for the following year, and send it to the Minister of Finance accompanied by the documents, statistics, and clarifications necessary to justify each of the requested credits, and that in accordance with rules determined by the Minister of Finance.

Exceptionally, and in view of the delay in the issuance of the budget for the year 1999, the time limit provided for in Article 13 of the Public Accounting Law for drawing up the draft budget for the year 2000 is extended until the end of the month of June instead of the month of May (and that pursuant to Law 107 dated 23/7/99)

The Minister of Finance estimates the revenues on the basis of the assessments of his ministry and the assessments of the ministers who undertake the assessment or collection of certain revenues for his account.

The revenues of the new year are estimated on the basis of the following two elements:

A- The collections of the last year for which the draft settlement of accounts has been completed.

B - The collections of the elapsed months of the current year.

The Minister of Finance may amend the estimate on the basis of circumstances he adopts, provided that he justifies the reasons therefor.

The Minister of Finance compiles the estimates of expenditures, compares them with the estimates of revenues, and draws up the draft budget after securing the balance between its two parts. If the requested credits exceed the estimated revenues, the Minister of Finance must secure the balance by proposing such of the following measures as he deems necessary:

A- Reducing expenditures.

B - Covering the difference by withdrawals from the reserve fund, if that is possible.

C- Finding new resources.

The Minister of Finance submits the draft budget to the Council of Ministers before the first of September, accompanied by a report in which he analyses the requested credits and the significant differences between the figures of the draft and the figures of the budget of the current year.

The Council of Ministers approves the draft budget in its final form and lodges it with the legislative authority within the time limit specified in the Constitution.

The Minister of Finance submits to the legislative authority, before the first of November, a detailed report on the economic and financial situation in the country, and on the principles adopted by the Government in the draft budget.

No increase may be introduced to the draft budget, or to drafts of additional credits, during the discussion thereof in the competent parliamentary committee and in the Chamber of Deputies, except after obtaining the written opinion of the Ministry of Finance and the approval of the Council of Ministers.

The expenditures budget is divided into two parts:

- Part One: which contains ordinary expenditures.

- Part Two: which contains equipment and construction expenditures and the State's developmental contributions

The concept of the expenditures of each of the two aforementioned parts is determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.
Each of the two aforementioned parts of the expenditures section is distributed into titles, and the number of titles of each part is determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

A title is divided into chapters, each of which pertains to a single administration or a group of administrations, or to a single project or a group of projects. A chapter is divided into items, each of which pertains to expenditures of a single type or similar expenditures, and an item is divided, where necessary, into paragraphs.

In the division of credits, a standard schedule determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance shall be adopted.

There shall be shown in the salaries item:

1- With respect to permanent and temporary employees:

- The total number of employees by category, with the total of their salaries and accessories.

2- With respect to contracted personnel:

- Their number, with the total of their salaries and accessories.

3- With respect to wage-earners:

A- For permanent wage-earners: their number, with the total of their wages and accessories.

B - For non-permanent wage-earners: the total of their wages and accessories.

Appropriations for similar works may be distributed into paragraphs within a single item. In such a case, the following provisions shall apply:

1- The appropriation allocated for each project shall be deemed an independent paragraph.

2- A transfer may be made from the appropriation allocated for one project to another project:

a- After the awarding of the works, provided that at least fifteen percent of the amount of the original appropriation is retained.

b - After the completion of the project and the liquidation of the contract.

3- No transfer shall be permitted except to a project similar to the first project and located in the same region.

1- In each title of the expenditures division, a chapter shall be set aside from which the value of pecuniary judgments rendered against the State and the settlements concluded by it shall be disbursed, whenever no appropriations are available for these expenditures in the relevant items.

This chapter shall be funded by way of transfer from the overall appropriation allocated in the title of the budget reserve in accordance with the provisions of the following Article 26:

2- (Repealed by the 1977 Budget Law and replaced by the following text):

- Amounts collected by the Treasury in error or without right shall be refunded by deducting them from the budget revenues account in which they were originally recorded, that is, by recording them on the debit side of the revenues account, and no appropriation shall be opened in the budget for this purpose.

Only the balances of the revenue accounts shall be recorded in the column of collected amounts in the final settlement of the budget account.

3- In each title of the expenditures division, during a transitional period ending in the year 1966, a chapter called Expenditures of Previous Years shall be set aside, from which shall be taken the amounts that accrued in favor of third parties in the years prior to the year 1963 and which were not disbursed during them.

No appropriation shall be allocated in the said chapter upon preparing the budget; rather, the expenditures disbursed therefrom shall be covered by drawings from the reserve fund to be approved by the Law on the Final Settlement of the Account.

1- There shall be allocated in the title of the budget reserve:

a- Reserve appropriations for common expenditures among several ministries, such as sickness and death grants, pecuniary judgments, settlements, etc...

b - A reserve appropriation for unforeseen expenditures, to be used to fund budget items whose appropriations have been exhausted, or to open extraordinary appropriations, provided that this reserve appropriation is not less than one percent of the total appropriations of the first and second parts of the budget.

2- In the event of exhaustion of the appropriations allocated for pecuniary judgments and settlements, the Government may open, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, the necessary supplementary appropriations and cover these appropriations by drawings from the reserve fund to be approved by the Law on the Final Settlement of the Account. The provisions of this paragraph shall also apply in the event of exhaustion of the appropriations allocated for retirement pensions and end-of-service indemnities.

3- No expenditure shall be disbursed directly from the appropriations of this title; rather, these appropriations shall be transferred, when necessary, to the other items of the budget in the following manner:

- By a decision of the Minister of Finance, upon the proposal of the competent administration, and after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment, with respect to the appropriations mentioned in sub-paragraph "a" of the preceding paragraph.

- By a decree issued upon the proposal of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance, with respect to the appropriations mentioned in sub-paragraph "b " of the preceding paragraph.

1- Subject to the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution and Article 26 of this Law, additional appropriations shall only be opened by a law.

These appropriations shall be covered by way of transfer from other items, or from the title of the budget reserve, or by drawing from the reserve fund, or by new resources.

2- Subject to the provisions of Article 26 of this Law, appropriations shall only be transferred from one item to another by a law.

3- Subject to Article 114 of this Law, appropriations shall only be carried over from the budget of a given year to the budget of the following year by a law.

1- Subject to the provisions of Article 24 of this Law, appropriations shall be transferred from one paragraph to another within a single item by a decision of the competent minister after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

A transfer may be made in the same manner to a new paragraph if such paragraph is of the type of expenditures to which the item relates.

2- Appropriations allocated in the two titles of debts due for payment and the budget reserve shall be transferred from one paragraph to another within a single item by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

3- A transfer from one paragraph to another in the budget of a given year may be effected up to the 31st of January of the following year.

The revenues division in the budget shall consist of two parts:

The First: Contains the ordinary revenues assigned to cover the expenditures of the first and second parts of the expenditures division.

The Second: Contains the revenues assigned to cover the expenditures of the third part of the expenditures division.

The latter revenues shall consist of:

1- Drawings from the reserve fund.

2- Revenues assigned or created by special laws.

Each part of the revenues division shall be distributed into titles, and each title shall be divided into chapters, each of which pertains to a category of revenues, and each chapter shall be divided into items, each of which pertains to a specific revenue.

In each part, a special chapter shall be set aside in which shall be recorded the funds paid by the Treasury in error or without right and subsequently recovered by it. A standard schedule determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance shall be adopted in the division of revenues.

In each part of the revenues division, a special title with a single chapter shall be set aside for drawings from the reserve fund.

This chapter shall be divided into items in accordance with the standard schedule mentioned in the preceding Article.
The following rules shall apply to the assessment of taxes and fees unless the law provides otherwise.

The assessment of direct taxes collected pursuant to assessment rolls shall be undertaken by the competent central financial department or the competent financial department in the governorate, and the Director of Revenues shall confer executory force upon these rolls.

The assessment of other taxes and fees shall be undertaken by the head of the financial department or the competent unit in each governorate pursuant to collection orders issued by him.

- Any concealment or deficiency in the assessment of direct and indirect taxes and fees may be remedied up to the end of the third year following the year in which the assessment should have taken place, pursuant to additional assessment rolls or collection orders for concealed assessments, and pursuant to supplementary assessment rolls or collection orders for deficient assessments.

In addition to the period of remedy referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, the competent financial departments shall enjoy another exceptional period to remedy the right of the Treasury to impose the tax or fee on any profit, income, revenue, or instrument disclosed by a judicial judgment, an arbitral award, the liquidation of an estate, or an amicable agreement, as well as to rectify any assessment for which a decision of annulment has been issued.

This exceptional period shall expire on the date of 31 December of the year following the year in which the annulment was decided or in which the profit, income, revenue, or instrument subject to assessment was disclosed.

The placing of the basic assessment rolls into collection shall be announced through the Official Gazette, the radio, and local newspapers. Where necessary, notices to this effect shall be posted in the offices of the accountants, and in meeting places and public squares. The notice shall state the time limits fixed for payment, for benefiting from the statutory discount, and for objection, and the commencement date of each of them.

The time limit for filing an objection against taxes levied pursuant to principal assessment rolls shall commence on the day following the date of publication of the notice relating thereto in the Official Gazette.

The time limit for filing an objection against taxes levied pursuant to additional or supplementary assessment rolls, and against taxes and fees levied pursuant to collection orders, shall commence on the day following the date of service of such documents upon the taxpayer. Such service shall be effected by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt. Where the taxpayer is absent or refuses receipt, service shall be effected through the competent administration in accordance with the service provisions laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure. The time limit for filing an objection shall be set at two months for direct taxes assessed pursuant to assessment rolls, and at one month for other taxes and fees.

1- The rules governing objections against the various taxes and fees and the time limits for deciding thereon by the administration and the objection committees shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Justice within three months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

2- The rules and time limits determined in the said decree shall supersede all special provisions relating to objections contained in the various laws governing taxes and fees.

Notwithstanding any other provision, the tax departments at the Directorate General of Finance may not decide to cancel or reduce tax and fee assessments except with the approval of the Head of the Revenue Department, save where they relate to a material error or to an amount not exceeding 50 percent of the value of the assessment, provided that under no circumstances does it exceed /500/ L.L. for each assessment.

Supervision over the various operations of assessing taxes and fees managed by the Directorate General of Finance shall be carried out by an assessment control body whose powers and manner of performing its duties shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

No tax or fee may be collected unless the legislative authority has authorized the same pursuant to the Budget Law or any other law. Any offender shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Article 361 of the Penal Code.

Taxes and fees shall be collected on the basis of the assessment rolls or collection orders pursuant to which they were assessed, unless they are of a kind paid directly by the taxpayer by affixing stamps or similar papers. None other than public accountants and their assistants may undertake the collection of taxes, fees, and other public revenues.

All taxes and fees of every kind shall be extinguished in respect of taxpayers by prescription on 31 December of the fourth year following the year in which the assessment took place. Prescription shall be interrupted by the mere initiation of the individual enforcement proceedings provided for by law.

A formal notice to pay shall be deemed an initiation of enforcement proceedings, provided that it is served in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 147 dated 12/6/1959.

Where necessary, the formal notice to pay shall be renewed before the expiry of four years from the date of its service upon the person concerned.

Assessment rolls shall be retained for a period of ten years, and collection orders shall be retained for a period of five years, unless the Court of Accounts decides, before the expiry of the retention period, to discharge those responsible for collection.

Supervision over the operations of collecting taxes and fees managed by the Directorate General of Finance shall be carried out by a collection control body whose powers and manner of performing its duties shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

In the liquidation and collection of State debts and other revenues other than taxes and fees, the specific provisions applicable to each of them shall be observed. As for debts and revenues for which the laws in force have not designated the methods of liquidation, collection, and enforcement proceedings, they shall be liquidated pursuant to recovery orders issued by the head of the competent administration and collected in accordance with the rules followed in the collection of direct taxes and fees similar thereto. An objection against a recovery order may be filed before the competent judicial court at the place of residence of the objector within two months from the date of service upon the debtor in person or at his place of residence. An objection shall not stay the execution of the recovery order unless the court decides otherwise, in whole or in part.
The immovable property of the State shall be sold in accordance with the provisions specific thereto.

The movable property of the State shall be sold:

1 - By mutual agreement, if its appraised value does not exceed 3000000 L.L. (three million Lebanese pounds).

2 - By invitation to tender, if its appraised value does not exceed 6000000 L.L. (six million Lebanese pounds).

3- By public auction and by sealed envelope, if its appraised value exceeds 6,000,000 six million Lebanese pounds. Unless the law provides otherwise, the provisions applicable to supply and works contracts shall apply to sale by mutual agreement, by invitation to tender, and by public auction.

Contracts for the sale of movable property shall be decided upon:

1 - In the central administration:

- By the competent Director, if the value of the contract does not exceed 150000 L.L.

- By the competent Director General, if the value of the contract exceeds 150000 L.L. and does not exceed 600000 L.L.

- By the competent Minister, if the value of the contract exceeds 600000 L.L.

2 - In the governorates and districts:

- By the Qaemaqam, if the value of the contract does not exceed 150000 L.L.

- By the Governor, if the value of the contract exceeds 150000 L.L. and does not exceed 600000 L.L.

- By the competent Minister, if the value of the contract exceeds 600000 L.L.
Movable property shall be appraised by a committee formed in each administration by a decision of the authority competent to decide upon the contract.
Sale transactions subject to the audit of the Court of Accounts shall be submitted to it by the authority competent to decide upon the contract.
Collected revenues shall be entered in their entirety in the revenues section of the budget.

1- Cash and in-kind donations offered to the State by legal and natural persons shall be accepted by a decree issued upon the proposal of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance, if their value does not exceed 250.000.000 Lebanese pounds.

2- Cash and/or in-kind donations offered to the State by legal and natural persons shall be accepted by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, if their value exceeds 250.000.000 Lebanese pounds.

3- Cash donations received by the Lebanese Treasury shall be entered in the revenues section of the budget, and if such donations are assigned to a specific expenditure purpose, appropriations equal to their value shall be opened for them in the expenditures section in accordance with the rules.

4- The Ministry of Finance shall prepare a quarterly schedule of the donations referred to in items (1) and (2) and received by the Lebanese Treasury, and shall submit it to the Council of Ministers for information.

The Ministry of Finance shall keep, for each type of budget revenue and for each year separately, an independent account showing:

- The arrears of previous years, for each year separately.

- The total revenues assessed pursuant to assessment rolls and collection orders issued during the year.

- The total collections up to 31 December of the year, distributed between the current year and each of the previous years.

- The statutory deductions from which taxpayers benefited.

- The uncollected arrears at the end of the year.

Each ministry shall keep a detailed account of the revenues it manages, for each year separately, on the basis of the collection or recovery orders that it issues or that are issued at its request.

The stages of execution of an expenditure are four:

1- Commitment.

2- Liquidation.

3- Payment order.

4- Payment.
Commitment of an expenditure is the performance of an act capable of creating a debt against the State.
The competent Minister commits the expenditure, unless the law provides otherwise.
No expenditure shall be committed unless an appropriation is available for it in the budget. An appropriation may not be used for a purpose other than that for which it was allocated.

Expenditures paid out of the principal of the advance shall be settled by payment orders issued in the name of the custodian.

The advance shall be renewed in the amount of the sums disbursed pursuant to these payment orders, without the need to issue any new decision.

The custodian of the advance shall undertake:

- Collecting the advance and the settlement payment orders.

- Effecting payments.

- Gathering the supporting documents for the expenditure and submitting them regularly to the competent authority for the issuance of payment orders at the end of every month.

- Keeping an account for the advance, the rules of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

Ordinary liquidation and disbursement transactions shall be carried out on the basis of the supporting documents submitted by the custodian.

If it appears to the Disbursements Department that some of the supporting documents are irregular, it shall proceed to issue the payment order in the amount of the valid documents, and to return the other documents to the competent administration within a period of five days at most.

In the latter case, the value of the advance may be increased by the amount of the documents the disbursement of which is suspended.

Permanent advances the amount of which exceeds a limit to be assessed by the Minister of Finance must be deposited in the name of the custodian in one of the State funds designated by the decision granting the advance.
The rules of payment by means of permanent advances shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

An emergency advance shall be granted by a decision of the Director of Finance after the endorsement of the Controller of Expenditure Commitments, in which decision shall be specified:

- The amount of the advance.

- The purpose of the expenditure.

- The person in whose name the advance is granted.

- The maximum time limit for submitting the supporting documents for the final settlement of the advance, provided that this does not exceed 31 January of the following year at the latest.

Paragraph added pursuant to Law 107 dated 23/7/99 Official Gazette 37 dated 30/7/99

It shall be permitted to carry over appropriations reserved for permanent or emergency financial advances granted during a given year to fulfil obligations the execution of which extends beyond the year (opening documentary credits to execute agreements with foreign governments or foreign and local companies or paying the expenses of medical treatment abroad) to the budgets of subsequent financial years
An emergency advance shall be paid pursuant to a payment order drawn up by the authority competent to issue payment orders on the basis of the decision granting the advance.
The settlement payment order shall be drawn up in the name of the person who was granted the advance.
The advance shall not be used for anything other than the purpose for which it was granted. The legal provisions governing the regulation of public funds shall be observed in its use.

The advance shall be settled either in cash by returning its value to the Treasury, or by supporting documents for the expenditure, or by both methods together, within the time limit specified in the decision granting it.

The custodian of the advance shall be personally liable on his private property for its value. He must justify upon every request its presence in his possession either in cash or by supporting documents for what he has spent out of its principal.

The Head of the Treasury Department must ensure the auditing of the accounts of advances at least once every six months. He shall have the right to deduct directly from the salary and allowances of the custodian of the advance the sums the use of which he does not prove, or in the spending of which he exceeds the amount of expenditures due, or which he does not settle within the specified time limits, and he may also execute automatically against him any other legal measure that ensures the recovery of these sums.

If an expenditure is committed in accordance with the provisions of the law before obtaining the endorsement of the Controller of Expenditure Commitments, and there is a corresponding appropriation for it, it shall be disbursed by way of regularisation, provided that those responsible are prosecuted before the Court of Accounts.

The Minister shall be personally liable on his private property for every expenditure he commits in excess of the appropriations opened for his ministry with his knowledge of such excess, as well as for every measure that leads to an increase in the expenditures disbursed from the said appropriations if such measure does not result from prior legislative provisions. This liability shall not preclude the prosecution before the Court of Accounts of the civil servants who intervened in the commitment, liquidation, and disbursement of the expenditure, unless they produce a written order that absolves them from liability.

The Controller of Expenditure Commitments, and other authorities where applicable, each within his competence, must inform the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts of the violations set out in the two preceding articles.

1- Appropriations of Part One of the budget that have not been committed by 31 December of the year shall be cancelled, with the exception of appropriations pertaining to allocations of the General Treasury.

2 - Appropriations of Part Two that have not been committed by 31 December shall be carried over for one year, with the exception of appropriations of programme laws.

3 - Appropriations allocated in Parts One and Two of the budget that have been committed and not disbursed by 31 December of the year shall be carried over to the budget of the following year, if a right of a third party attaches to them.

4 - The carry-over shall take place by a decision of the Minister of Finance issued upon the request of the competent administration before the first of March of the following year in accordance with the texts in force.

5 - This text shall take effect starting from the budget of the year 2017 .

Debts that have not been liquidated or have not been disbursed or have not been paid up to 31 December of the fourth year following the financial year in which the debt arose shall lapse automatically by prescription, and shall be definitively extinguished in favour of the State, unless the delay results from the administration or from litigation before the courts.

1- Expenditures of previous years that have not lapsed by prescription shall be disbursed

from the appropriations carried over for this purpose to the budget of the current year.

It shall also be possible, if the state of the appropriations so permits, for these

expenditures to be disbursed from the appropriations of the budget of the current year.

2- Subject to the provisions of the first paragraph of this article, expenditures

of previous years pertaining to the period prior to the year 1963 and which have not

lapsed by prescription shall be disbursed from the chapter designated for expenditures of previous years in the budget of the current year in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 25.

Sums paid by the Treasury in error or without right and recovered by it during the financial year in which they were disbursed may be added to the appropriation of the relevant item by a decision of the Minister of Finance. The competent minister must submit a request in this regard to the Minister of Finance within a maximum period ending on 31 December of the same year.

The Minister of Finance may, if he finds it necessary, propose to the Council of Ministers the suspension of the use of certain appropriations allocated in the budget. The Council of Ministers may decide to approve the proposal if current circumstances justify taking such a measure.

The Ministry of Finance shall keep separate accounts for expenditures that are committed, disbursed, and paid.

The competent administrations shall keep corresponding accounts for their expenditures that they commit and liquidate and that are disbursed.

Expenditures for supplies, works, and services shall be executed either by means of contracts concluded by the administration with third parties, or by the administration directly, that is, by direct labour.

Contracts for supplies, works, and services shall be concluded by public tender. However, in the cases set out below, contracts may be concluded by restricted tender, or request for proposals, or mutual agreement, or pursuant to a statement or invoice.
Public and restricted tenders shall be conducted on the basis of a general annual programme announced on dates that may not go beyond the second month following the publication of the budget.
A contract may not be divided unless the authority competent to commit the expenditure considers that the nature of the works, supplies, or services to be contracted justifies this.

A public tender (hereinafter referred to by the word "tender") shall be conducted either on the basis of a price offered by the bidder, or on the basis of a percentage reduction from the prices of the estimated statement set forth in Article 126 of this Law.

For contracts concluded by tender, model general books of specifications shall be drawn up, ratified by decrees and published in the Official Gazette.

For each such contract, a special book of specifications shall be drawn up, prepared by the Administration concerned and signed by the authority competent to decide upon the contract.

The special book of specifications shall set forth the following information:

- The types of supplies, works or services to be contracted out and their descriptions.

- The qualifications and special conditions that must be met by anyone wishing to participate in the tender.

- The elements of comparison, whenever the Administration intends not to be bound by the lowest price, provided that such elements are stated clearly and in detail,

and that a special coefficient is established for each of them where necessary.

- The basis adopted for conducting the tender in accordance with the provisions of Article 124.

- The special conditions of performance.

- The time limit for delivery.

- The amount of the guarantee that must be furnished to participate in the tender and to ensure the proper performance by the contractor of his obligations.

There shall be annexed to the book of special specifications, whenever possible:

- An estimated statement of quantities and prices.

- Price schedules containing a description of each type of supplies, works or services to be contracted out, and fixing for each type a price

stated in words and figures.

The price set by the Administration shall be deemed the maximum limit for a contract conducted on the basis of a percentage reduction, and the Administration shall announce the maximum

limit of the reduction that may be accepted, and such reduction shall be deemed the minimum limit for the contract.

The guarantee shall be:

1- Either in cash, the value of which is paid directly to one of the Treasury funds, or to the fund of the competent Administration where one exists, against a receipt attached to the bid, provided that its value in the second case is transferred to the Central Finance Fund immediately upon the award of the contract.

2- Or a bank guarantee issued by an approved bank and drawn up in the name of the competent Administration or in the name of the State Treasury.

Every tender shall be announced in the Official Gazette and in at least three daily newspapers, at least 15 days prior to the date fixed for the award. The period may be reduced to at least five days when re-conducting the tender, or in case of necessity, provided that the reduction is subject to the prior approval of the authority competent to commit the expenditure. Every amendment made to the book of specifications after the publication of the tender announcement shall also be announced in accordance with the same rules.
Tenders shall be conducted by committees formed specifically for this purpose.

The contract shall be provisionally awarded to the party who submitted the lowest prices or to the party who submitted the best bids if the book of specifications requires adopting elements of comparison other than price, provided that bids submitted for goods manufactured in Lebanon shall be given a preference of 10 percent over bids submitted for foreign goods, on condition that national goods and the conditions that must be met therein in order to benefit from this preference are determined by decrees passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Economy

"As for contracts conducted on the basis of a percentage reduction, the tender committee shall provisionally award the contract to the party who submitted the lowest prices within the two estimated prices".

If the bids are equal after giving Lebanese goods the preference of 10 percent

mentioned in Article 131 above, the tender shall be repeated by way of sealed envelope among their submitters exclusively in the same session; if they refuse to submit new bids or if their bids remain equal, the provisional contractor shall be appointed by drawing lots among the submitters of the equal bids.

"As for contracts conducted on the basis of a percentage reduction, if the bids are equal, the provisional contractor shall be appointed by drawing lots among the equal bids".

The contract shall be decided upon by:

- The competent Director, or the Head of Service in the absence of a Director, if its value does not exceed 10,000,000 L.L.

- The Director General if its value exceeds 10,000,000 L.L. and does not exceed 35,000,000 L.L.

- The Minister in other cases

2- The contract shall not become final until the ratification is notified to the contractor through administrative channels

(This Article was amended pursuant to Decree Rendered Enforceable ipso jure No. 977/2007, Article 35, and the amendment was not adopted)

In principle, works contracts may not be concluded until after the completion of all legal procedures enabling the Administration to take possession of the work sites; however, contracting formalities may be initiated before the completion of these procedures, provided that the contract is neither ratified nor notified to the contractor until after possession of the said sites has been taken.

If any sum becomes due from the contractor in the course of performance, in application of the provisions of the book of specifications, the Administration shall have the right to deduct such sum from the guarantee and call upon the contractor to replenish it within a specified period. If he fails to do so, he shall be deemed in default, and the Administration shall proceed either to re-conduct the tender or to perform the contract by direct execution.

If the new tender or the performance by direct execution results in a saving in costs, the saving shall accrue to the Treasury.

And if it results in an increase in costs, the Administration shall have recourse against the defaulting contractor for the excess.

In all cases, the guarantee shall be provisionally confiscated until the contract is liquidated in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

The contract between the Administration and a contractor who is declared bankrupt shall be rescinded ipso jure, and the following procedures shall immediately be followed:

1- The guarantee shall be provisionally issued to the account of the Treasury.

2- The Administration shall take an inventory of the works, supplies and services performed or the materials stored prior to the date of the declaration of bankruptcy, and shall draw up a statement thereof, the value of which shall be provisionally disbursed on trust in the name of the Treasury.

3- The works, supplies or services, or whatever remains thereof, shall be placed under direct execution or re-contracted out.

If the new tender or the performance by direct execution results in a saving in costs, the saving shall accrue to the Treasury, and the guarantee and the value of the statement set forth in the preceding paragraph shall be paid to the bankruptcy trustee.

And if it results in an increase in costs, the excess shall be deducted from the guarantee and the value of the said statement, and the balance shall be paid to the bankruptcy trustee. If that is insufficient to cover the excess in full, seizure of the guarantee and the value of the statement shall suffice.

The value of the contract shall not be paid until after its performance.

However, the Minister of Finance may, upon the request of the competent Minister, grant contractors advances against bank guarantees. Where it is impossible to obtain such guarantees, the granting of an advance without a guarantee shall be subject to the ratification of the Council of Ministers.

The advance may not exceed 25 percent of the value of the contract, provided that it does not exceed 30.000.000 L.L.

However, in exceptional cases, derogation from the preceding provisions may be made by a decision of the Council of Ministers.

Where the book of specifications so provides, payments on account not exceeding nine tenths of the amount due may be made against completed services, and the tenth shall remain retained in the Treasury until final acceptance takes place. These retentions shall be refunded upon final acceptance if the book of specifications does not fix a guarantee period for the supplies or works, after the contractor has settled the liabilities that may have been incurred by him in application of the provisions of the book of specifications. The Administration may cease deducting the ten-percent retentions when it deems that they have reached the limit necessary for the guarantee.

Supplies, works and services in each ministry shall be received by a committee appointed by a decision of the Director General, provided that it comprises three employees, one of whom belongs to the unit for whose benefit the contracting took place, and the other two are from outside it.

If the contractor, in executing the transaction, violates the book of conditions or some of its provisions, the competent Administration shall serve him with an official warning of the necessity to abide by all of his obligations, within a specific time limit the estimation of which is left to it. And if the specified time limit expires without the contractor executing what was requested of him, the Administration shall have the right, subject to the provisions of the general book of conditions, to consider him a defaulter and to apply against him the provisions of Article 135 of this Law. And in the event of repeating the tender, the defaulting contractor shall not have the right to participate in it again.

However, if the acceptance committee sees that the transaction has been executed in general in accordance with the provisions of the book of conditions with the presence of some minor deficiencies or defects that do not prevent conducting the acceptance, it may proceed with the acceptance in accordance with conditions determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

The guarantee shall be returned to the contractor pursuant to a memorandum from the competent Administration at most one month after the date of final acceptance. However, the Administration may, before the expiry of the execution time limit, or after the provisional acceptance if the state of the works allows that, return to the contractor, upon his request, the whole of this guarantee or a part thereof.

The contractor whose works are placed under direct management or are re-awarded at his expense in application of the provisions of this Law or the provisions of the general book of conditions shall be excluded from tenders:

- For a period of three months when these measures are applied to him for the first time.

- For a period of one full year when they are applied to him a second time within twelve months.

- Permanently when they are applied to him a third time within five years.

The time limits mentioned above shall commence from the date of the first decision ordering the placement of the works under direct management or their re-awarding at the expense of the contractor.

The Administration may, if the nature of the supplies, works, or services does not allow opening the door of competition to everyone, restrict the tender to a limited category of tenderers who possess the required financial, technical, and professional qualifications.

These qualifications shall be determined in detail in the special book of conditions, and all other guarantees that must be possessed by the tenderers, and the specifications that must characterize the required works or materials, shall also be determined therein.
All provisions relating to public tenders shall apply to the restricted tender.

Transactions may be concluded by way of solicitation of offers:

A- If their value does not exceed /100000000/ Pounds.

B - If their value exceeds /100000000/ Pounds and they relate to:

1- Works carried out by the Administration by way of experiment or study, provided that the competent Minister decides that.

2- Things, materials, and produce that must be purchased at the place of their production in view of their special nature.

3- Freight, transport, and insurance.

4- Supplies, works, and services in respect of which no price was submitted in the tender, or in respect of which unacceptable prices were submitted.

5- Supplies, works, and services which certain urgent cases arising from unforeseen circumstances do not allow to be put out to tender, provided that the competent Minister decides that.

6- Technical supplies, works, and services the nature of which does not allow them to be put out to public tender, provided that the competent Minister decides that.

(This Article was amended pursuant to Decree Enforced Lockstep No. 977/2007 Article 35 and the amendment was not adopted)

The texts relating to public tenders shall apply to the solicitation of offers, subject to the following provisions:

1- The advertisement may be replaced by communicating the necessary information in a rapid and guaranteed manner to the merchants of the category or the masters of the profession in whom the Administration sees a capability to execute the transaction.

2- A special committee appointed in each public administration, by a decision of the Minister, shall conduct the solicitation of offers for a transaction the value of which does not exceed /100000000/ Pounds, and the tenders committee shall conduct the other transactions.

(This Article was amended pursuant to Decree Enforced Lockstep No. 977/2007 Article 35 and the amendment was not adopted)

Agreements by mutual consent may be concluded, whatever the value of the transaction, if they relate to:

1- Supplies, works, and services that cannot be placed in a tender, either due to the necessity of their remaining secret, or because the requirements of safety prevent that, provided that the competent Minister decides that.

2- Additional supplies, works, and services that must be entrusted to the original contractor lest their execution be delayed, or not proceed well if a new contractor were brought in during the execution of the transaction, and that is permissible:

- If the supplies, works, and services were unforeseen when conducting the first awarding, and are considered among its accessories, and constitute an integral part thereof.

- If the supplies, works, and services must be saved [executed] by means of special machines and equipment used by the contractor at the place of work, provided that they are unforeseen when conducting the awarding, and that they constitute an integral part thereof.

3- Things the right of manufacture of which is restricted to the holder of the patents of their invention.

4- Things that are owned by only one person.

5- Technical supplies, works, and services the execution of which can only be entrusted to artists, specialists, craftsmen, or industrialists whose competence has been demonstrated by experience.

6- Supplies and works manufactured by needy persons with disabilities licensed to work by the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, provided that their prices do not exceed the prevailing prices in the market.

7- Hospitality and protocol expenses: and similar representation expenses.

8- Supplies, works, and services for the sake of which were conducted:

- Two consecutive tenders.

- Or a solicitation of offers on two consecutive occasions.

- Or a tender followed by a solicitation of offers. And that is without these operations resulting in a positive outcome. And in this case, the agreement by mutual consent must not result in a price exceeding the most suitable prices offered during the awarding operations, except in exceptional cases justified by the Administration in a reasoned report.

9- Supplies, works, and services that may be entrusted to public institutions or municipalities.

10- Supplies and services secured by the Administration through international organizations.

11- Supplies, works, and services that may be entrusted, with the approval of the Council of Ministers, to foreign governments or institutions supervised by these governments. And the Government in such a case shall have the right to exempt the party with which it contracts from the conditions relating to the place of residence, the guarantee, the fines, and the necessity of delivery before payment.

12- Supplies, works, and services which the Council of Ministers decides to secure by mutual consent upon the proposal of the competent Minister.

The agreement by mutual consent shall be concluded by:

- The Director, or the Head of Service in the event of the absence of a Director, if the value of the transaction does not exceed 10,000,000 L.L.

- The Director General if the value of the transaction exceeds 10,000,000 L.L. and does not exceed 35,000,000 L.L.

- The Minister in other cases.

And contracting shall take place by one of the following methods:

1- Pursuant to a contract between the competent authority and the concerned party.

2- Pursuant to an undertaking which the concerned party appends to the special book of conditions.

3- Pursuant to an offer from the concerned party approved by the competent authority.

4- Pursuant to an exchange of correspondence between the concerned party and the competent authority, in accordance with commercial custom.

(This Article was amended pursuant to Decree Enforced Lockstep No. 977/2007 Article 35 and the amendment was not adopted)

Agreements by mutual consent shall be subject to the provisions of the general book of conditions, and a special book of conditions shall be drawn up for them where necessary.

And in addition to the provisions of the two preceding Articles, the provisions of Articles 137 to 141 of this Law shall apply to agreements by mutual consent.

Contracts for technical services (studies, preparation of terms of reference, supervision of the execution of works and projects, etc.) may be concluded by mutual agreement regardless of their value if they exceed the capabilities of the Administration.

The following provisions shall apply to such contracts:

1- Contracting may only be effected with persons who possess the requisite technical qualifications, provided that such qualifications are set out in detail in a study prepared by the Administration prior to concluding the contract.

2- The agreement may, where necessary, be concluded following a competition held among those who possess the said qualifications.

3- Such contracts shall be subject to the other provisions relating to agreements by mutual agreement.

Contracts may be concluded by way of a statement or invoice:

1- If their value does not exceed three million Lebanese pounds; this procedure shall apply to the execution of the budget of the Lebanese University without the need to issue another text.

2- If the prices of the materials to be purchased are fixed in a tariff issued by the Administration or a recognised international body and it is impossible to obtain a lower price therefor.

3- If the contract relates to the hiring of public works machinery pursuant to a general tariff fixed by a decision of the competent Minister.

The contract shall be concluded by the head of the competent unit, and delivery shall be effected by the committee provided for in Article 139.

The heads of the competent units authorised to conclude contracts shall be designated by a decision of the competent Minister in public administrations and by a decision of the head of the executive authority in public institutions and municipalities subject to the Public Accounting Law.

(This Article was amended pursuant to Decree Enforced by Law No. 977/2007, Article 35, and the amendment was not adopted)
Works by direct labour are works which the Administration undertakes to execute by itself.

Works by direct labour shall be authorised by:

- The competent head of unit if their value does not exceed 3.000.000 L.L.

- The Director, or the Head of Service in the absence of a Director, if their value exceeds 3.000.000 L.L. and does not exceed 10.000.000 L.L.

- The Director General if their value exceeds 10.000.000 L.L. and does not exceed 35.000.000 L.L.

- The Minister if their value exceeds 35.000.000 L.L. and does not exceed 150.000.000 L.L.

- The Council of Ministers in other cases.

The ordinary procedures shall apply to the purchase of the materials necessary for the execution of these works.

(This Article was amended pursuant to Decree Enforced by Law No. 977/2007, Article 35, and the amendment was not adopted)

There shall be appointed in every administration that undertakes the execution of works by direct labour a special body whose mission is to supervise the execution of these works by direct labour. This body shall report directly to the head of the administration and shall not undertake any act of execution.

The head of the unit that undertook the execution of the works by direct labour shall submit to his administration upon the completion of the works a detailed statement of the quantities executed and the costs paid of all kinds.

The supervisory body shall audit this statement and refer it, appended with its opinion, to the Central Inspection Administration.

The Caimacam shall exercise within his Casa the powers vested by the provisions of this Chapter in the Director.

The Mohafez shall exercise within his Mohafazat the powers vested by the provisions of this Chapter in the Director General, in respect of contracts for supplies, works, and services concluded in the Casa or the Mohafazat.

The details for the application of the provisions of this Law relating to contracts for supplies, works, and services, and in particular the conditions for the classification of contractors and their admission to participate in tenders, shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.
The State Treasury shall undertake all collection and payment operations required for the execution of the State budget, and the management of accounts opened outside the budget.

Collection and payment operations for the account of the Treasury shall be performed by officials each of whom is called an Public Accountant; however, the Public Accountant may delegate some of his powers to one of the accountants subordinate to him with the approval of the Head of the Treasury Service.

Public Accountants are of two categories: central and local.

1- The Central Public Accountant is the one who is answerable for budget revenues and expenditures, and for operations outside the scope of the budget.

2- The Local Public Accountant is the one who is answerable for operations outside the scope of the budget, and who locally performs the collection of budget revenues and the payment of its expenditures for the account of the Central Public Accountant to whom he is subordinate.

3- In certain public administrations, their Central Public Accountant may be charged with consolidating all the operations of the Local Public Accountants subordinate to him, whether such operations pertain to the budget or fall outside its scope.

4- Where a public administration has a single Public Accountant, such Public Accountant shall be deemed to be a Central Public Accountant for the purposes of the application of this Law.

The Central Public Accountants are:

- The Central Finance Public Accountant.

- The Central Customs Public Accountant.

- The Central Posts and Telegraphs Public Accountant.

- The Central Public Accountant in each administration with an annexed budget.

- Every official vested with this capacity by decree.

The Local Public Accountants are:

- The Finance Public Accountants.

- The Customs Public Accountants.

- The Posts and Telegraphs Public Accountants.

- The Public Accountants of administrations with an annexed budget.

- Every official vested with this capacity by decree.

The operations performed by the Public Accountant shall be recorded in accounts kept by him in accordance with a general chart of accounts approved by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The accounts of public funds shall be kept by the Central Public Accountants and the General Accounting Service on the basis of the double-entry method, and by the Local Public Accountants on the basis of the single-entry method.

Entries shall mandatorily be kept in ink, and may not at all be kept in pencil; nor is it permissible to scratch out, interlineate, erase, or overwrite in papers, schedules, documents, entries, and registers; rather, it is permissible to correct any error that may occur therein, provided that the correction is made visibly in figures and words spelled out in full, and in ink of a colour different from the colour used in the original, and that the correction is appended with the date and the signature of its author.

The Public Accountants shall undertake:

- To receive assessment rolls, collection orders, and recovery orders deposited with them by the competent authorities and to ensure their recovery.

- To ensure collections, of whatever kind.

- To ensure payments, either pursuant to payment orders or disbursement orders issued by the competent authority or, in certain cases, pursuant to disbursement orders issued directly by them.

- To preserve the supporting vouchers pertaining to these operations and the accounting documents.

- To keep the accounts of the accounting office which they manage.

The Central Finance Public Accountant shall undertake, in addition to the foregoing, the consolidation of revenue and expenditure operations relating to the general budget performed by the other Central Public Accountants. He shall also undertake the management of the State Treasury account at the Central Bank.

The office of Public Accountant may not be combined with any office connected with the assessment of revenues, or any office connected with the commitment, liquidation, or payment-ordering of expenditures.

Before assuming the duties of his office, the Public Accountant must furnish a legal security the value of which shall be fixed by a decision of the Minister of Finance, and take the oath before the Court of Accounts.

Securities shall be furnished either in cash, or by bank guarantees issued by approved banks, or by a mortgage of real property registered in the Land Registry offices. The receipts and documents relating to the securities furnished shall be kept with the General Accounting Service at the Ministry of Finance together with a copy of the instrument appointing the Public Accountant.

The Public Accountant may not personally perform the collection or payment of funds the management of which he supervises, but shall undertake the same through a cashier or collectors subordinate to him, except in the cases determined by a special decree.
The Public Accountant must supervise the acts of the cashiers and collectors subordinate to him, and must hold them accountable for every violation or delay in their work.

The public accountant shall be liable with his personal assets for every operation of receipt or payment carried out in the accounting office which he manages in violation of the provisions of the law, in addition to any disciplinary or penal sanctions to which he may be subject.
The public accountant shall be answerable only for his personal management.

The mission of the public accountant shall include all the operations which he carries out in his accounting office from the first of January until 31 December of each year, or during the period in which he assumed his post, if such period is less than one year.

Central public accountants as well as local public accountants provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 160 must submit, in their name and on their responsibility, the accounts of their mission to the Court of Accounts.

Local public accountants provided for in paragraph 3 of Article 160 must submit, in their name and on their responsibility, to the central public accountant to whom they are subordinate, the accounts of their mission within conditions and time limits to be determined by a subsequent decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Upon the termination of the mission of the public accountant, a handover and takeover operation shall take place between him and his successor pursuant to a record signed by both of them, and in the presence of a financial inspector with respect to central public accountants, and an employee delegated by the competent administration with respect to local public accountants. A copy of the record in both cases shall be sent to the Financial Inspectorate. A balance of accounts closed as at the date of conducting the handover and takeover operation must mandatorily be annexed to this record.

In the event of the death of the public accountant, or his inability to perform the role of handover and takeover, the succeeding public accountant shall draw up the account of the mission of the preceding public accountant under the supervision of a financial inspector.

The security bond shall be refunded after the public accountant obtains a discharge from the Court of Accounts, and it shall be refunded ipso jure after the lapse of three years from the public accountant leaving his mission, if the Court delays issuing its decision beyond this period.

1- Local public accountants and collectors shall be financially liable jointly and severally among themselves for direct taxes and all other funds entrusted to them for collection.

2- The head of the Beirut collection department shall be financially liable for direct taxes and all other funds entrusted to him for collection, and he shall be bound to provide the security bond required of public accountants.

3- The extent of the liability of the employees mentioned in the first and second paragraphs of this Article, and the procedures to be followed to mitigate their liability or discharge them, shall be determined by a subsequent decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Every person who interferes in the management of public funds without holding the capacity of a public accountant shall be deemed a public accountant liable for his acts, like an official public accountant, and subject to the obligations of the latter.
The right to handle and possess funds in every accounting office shall be restricted to cashiers and collectors, except in the cases determined in the decree provided for in Article 171 of this Law.
Cashiers shall be liable for the custody of funds in the accounting office in which they exercise their functions.

Collectors shall be liable for the custody of the funds which they collect. They must pay them periodically into the chest of the accounting office to which they belong, in accordance with conditions determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance. They shall also be financially liable, jointly and severally with the public accountant to whom they are subordinate, for the collection of direct taxes in accordance with the provisions of Article 180 of this Law. Collectors are absolutely prohibited from paying any expenditure of whatever kind.
Cashiers and collectors shall be subject to the security bond regime in the same manner as public accountants.
The cashier must verify on his responsibility before payment the identity of the owner of the funds and the authenticity of his signature.

If the amount is due to a deceased person, the cashier must request from the rightful claimants the official documents proving their capacity. A certificate from the mukhtar of the locality shall suffice if the amount is less than 500 pounds.

If the owner of the funds is illiterate, or unable to sign, a thumbprint shall take the place of the signature, provided that the cashier and two witnesses certify the print if the value of the payment order does not exceed one thousand pounds. In other cases, the cashier may request certification of the print by the notary public.

Against every amount received by cashiers and collectors, a receipt shall be given the form and manner of drawing up of which shall be determined for each administration or unit by the General Accounting Service in the Ministry of Finance.

Any alteration in a receipt issued by a cashier or collector, or in one of its copies, whatever its cause, shall be considered as proceeding from bad faith, and the penalties provided for in Articles 461 and 462 of the Penal Code shall be imposed upon its perpetrator, unless such alteration caused no damage to public funds.
A regular receipt must be given for every amount received from public funds. Whoever receives public funds and does not give a regular receipt therefor shall be deemed an embezzler.

The head of the General Accounting Service in the Ministry of Finance, upon the proposal of the competent central public accountant, shall determine the maximum limit of balances which cashiers may retain, provided that they pay whatever exceeds these balances to the banks or post offices designated for them.

Administrations which collect certain revenues in cash must assign one of their employees, with the approval of the General Accounting Service, to receive these funds and keep their accounts. This Service may also approve the manner of receiving and paying in the said funds, and the models of the registers that must be kept.

The said employee shall pay in the funds which he has received at least once every month, either to the central finance public accountant or to the local finance public accountant, pursuant to a schedule showing the value received and the type of revenue collected. This employee may be assisted in receipt operations, where necessary, by one or more assistant cashiers.

This employee and whoever assists him in receiving funds shall be subject to the obligations of cashiers and in particular to the provisions of Articles 185 and 189 to 192.
The General Accounting Service shall audit the operations of public accountants and administrative accountants and shall consolidate them.

The General Accounting Service shall draw up every year:

- The final settlement of the budget account, which must be submitted to the Court of Accounts before 15 August of the year following the budget year.

- The general mission account, which must be submitted to the Court of Accounts before the first of September of the year following the account year.

- The drawing up of the general mission account shall commence starting from the account of the year in which the implementation of the general chart of accounts envisaged in Article 163 of this Law begins.

If the final settlement of the budget account results in an excess of revenues, this excess shall be transferred pursuant to the settlement law to the "Reserve Fund" account, and if it results in an excess of expenditures, the said law shall authorize covering the deficit from the Reserve Fund.

If the Reserve Fund is insufficient, the deficit shall be entered in the advances account, provided that it is mandatorily settled from the first subsequent budget in which a surplus appears, and if this surplus is insufficient, from the surplus of the following years successively.
The Government must refer the draft law on the final settlement of the budget account to the Chamber of Deputies before the first of November of the year following the budget year.

The reserve fund shall consist of the excess of budget revenues over its expenditures. The Central Finance Accountant shall undertake the keeping of this account under the supervision of the General Accounting Department.

The reserve fund shall be used:

- To cover the expenditures of previous years during the transitional period provided for in Article 25 of this Law.

- To cover carried-over appropriations.
